# Build: A/B Layer Ping-Pong

A double buffer for DOM content. Incoming content is written into whichever of two absolutely-positioned layers is currently invisible, then the two swap opacity. Because the outgoing content is still on screen, every change is a real crossfade rather than a swap with a fade bolted on — and running two of these at different durations is how a hover preview gets its lag between thumbnail and full-bleed background.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Two stacked layers alternate so any change crossfades, however fast you move between rows.

- Category: transition
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. Two absolutely positioned layers share a stacking context. A `front` slot (`"a"` or `"b"`) records which one is currently visible; the other is always at opacity 0.
2. When `contentKey` changes, the new children are written into the BACK slot and `front` flips. The back layer is already transparent, so the new content mounts invisibly — writing into the front layer instead would replace the outgoing content before it had faded.
3. `gsap.killTweensOf([inEl, outEl])` runs before every transition. Moving across a list faster than the duration otherwise leaves an unfinished fade-out driving the same node a fade-in is now driving up, and the layers flicker.
4. Two symmetric tweens — `opacity: 1` on the incoming layer, `opacity: 0` on the outgoing — with `power2.inOut`, which keeps the midpoint of the fade at roughly equal luminance instead of dipping through a visible trough.
5. The first commit is a `gsap.set`, not a tween, so the initial content is simply present; only subsequent key changes animate.
6. The last `contentKey` acted on is held in a ref, so a parent re-rendering with the same key (new inline children, a hover on the row that is already active) does not restart the fade.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `duration (background) = 1`
  Seconds. A full-bleed area needs a long fade or the whole frame appears to jump brightness; at 0.5s a large gradient change reads as a cut.
- `duration (thumbnail) = 0.6`
  The small element under the cursor answers first. Both at 1s and the interface feels unresponsive; both at 0.6s and the background flickers on fast passes. The 0.4s difference is the effect.
- `ease = 'power2.inOut'`
  Symmetric ease on both halves keeps their crossover near 50/50. With `power2.out` on the way in and `power2.in` on the way out, both layers are dim at the midpoint and the panel visibly darkens mid-fade.

## API

```ts
function ABLayerCrossfade(props: { contentKey: string; children: ReactNode; duration?: number; ease?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `contentKey: string`
  Identity of the current content. A change starts a crossfade.
- `children: ReactNode`
  Content for the current key. Captured into a layer at the moment the key changes.
- `duration: number` — default `1`
  Crossfade length in seconds. Use a shorter one for the smaller element in a pair.
- `ease: string` — default `'power2.inOut'`
  GSAP ease applied to both halves.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the positioned wrapper. Give it a size — the layers are absolute.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function ABLayerCrossfade({
  contentKey,
  children,
  duration = 1,
  ease = 'power2.inOut',
  className,
}: ABLayerCrossfadeProps) {
  const aRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const bRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  const [front, setFront] = useState<Slot>('a');
  const [layers, setLayers] = useState<{ a: ReactNode; b: ReactNode }>({
    a: children,
    b: null,
  });

  const shownKey = useRef(contentKey);
  const frontRef = useRef<Slot>('a');
  const first = useRef(true);

  // Write into the BACK layer, then flip. The back layer is already at
  // opacity 0, so the new content mounts invisibly — no flash of it at full
  // strength before the tween starts.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (shownKey.current === contentKey) return;
    shownKey.current = contentKey;
    const next: Slot = frontRef.current === 'a' ? 'b' : 'a';
    frontRef.current = next;
    setLayers((l) => ({ ...l, [next]: children }));
    setFront(next);
  }, [contentKey, children]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const inEl = front === 'a' ? aRef.current : bRef.current;
    const outEl = front === 'a' ? bRef.current : aRef.current;
    if (!inEl || !outEl) return;

    if (first.current) {
      first.current = false;
      gsap.set(inEl, { opacity: 1 });
      gsap.set(outEl, { opacity: 0 });
      return;
    }

    // Kill first, always. Two rapid changes otherwise leave an old fade-out
    // running on the layer the new fade-in is driving up.
    gsap.killTweensOf([inEl, outEl]);

    if (reduced) {
      gsap.set(inEl, { opacity: 1 });
      gsap.set(outEl, { opacity: 0 });
      return;
    }

    gsap.to(inEl, { opacity: 1, duration, ease });
    gsap.to(outEl, { opacity: 0, duration, ease });
  }, [front, duration, ease, reduced]);

  useEffect(
    () => () => {
      gsap.killTweensOf([aRef.current, bRef.current]);
    },
    [],
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** An unmount effect calls `gsap.killTweensOf` on both layer elements, so an in-flight fade cannot write opacity to a detached node after React has removed it.

**Reduced motion.** The layers still ping-pong, but the swap is a `gsap.set` rather than a tween: content changes instantly with no fade. The double-buffer structure is unchanged, so nothing else in the component behaves differently.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Crossfading one element by swapping its content at opacity 0. There is nothing to fade out of, so it reads as a blink; the two-layer buffer is the whole point.
- Writing incoming content into the front layer. The old content is replaced before it has faded, which is a hard cut with a pointless fade on top.
- Skipping `killTweensOf`. Hovering four rows in a second stacks eight opacity tweens across two nodes, and the layers end up at whatever the last-finishing pair leaves behind — usually both partly transparent.
- Giving both layers the same duration in a paired preview. The lag between the small element and the full-bleed one is what makes the interaction feel like it is answering you; without it the whole frame changes at once and reads as a page change.
- Restarting the fade when the parent re-renders. Any inline `children` array is a new object every render, so the effect must compare `contentKey`, not identity, or a hover crossfades continuously.
- Leaving tweens running past unmount. They keep writing opacity onto detached nodes; the unmount cleanup kills both layers.

## Notes

- Layers hold whatever you give them — a gradient, a canvas, a `<video>`, an image. Nothing here is image-specific.
- Content is captured per key, so if the same key needs to show new children you must change the key. That is deliberate: it is the only way to know when a transition is warranted.
- App Router wiring: pass `contentKey={usePathname()}` and render the route content as children for a whole-page crossfade with no layout thrash.

## Definition of done

Move down a list at a normal pace and each change is a smooth blend with no dip in brightness at the midpoint. Sweep the cursor across every row as fast as you can and the layers never flicker or settle half-faded. In a paired setup, the small preview visibly finishes before the background does.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Accent Swatch Picker

The colour row under a composer preview: round, glossy swatches with an iridescent first option, chosen like radio buttons. `AccentScope` is the other half: it writes the chosen colour to one custom property, `--accent`, derives the kit's whole accent ramp from it with color-mix, and re-declares the tokens that read that ramp, so primary buttons, switches, focus rings and the swatch outline inside it all change colour together. The demo wires it to the kit Composer Loader, whose light band follows the swatch.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Glossy colour spheres in one keyboard radio group; the pick becomes one --accent property that re-tints kit controls in its scope.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Render a react-aria `RadioGroup` (`orientation="horizontal"`) whose `Radio`s are the swatches: one Tab stop, arrow keys move and select, `aria-label` names each colour. Each radio sets `--swatch` to its colour in inline style.
2. Paint the sphere as a stacked background: a white radial highlight at 32% 26% fading out by 42%, over a radial body that runs from the colour mixed 70% with white, to the colour at 52%, to the colour mixed 72% with black at the rim. A swatch with `fill` (the iridescent one) swaps the body for its own conic gradient. An inset shadow made from the colour darkens the bottom edge.
3. Show state on the sphere itself: a 2px outline at 2px offset is transparent until `data-selected`, then takes `var(--swatch)`; focus-visible switches it to `text-primary` so keyboard focus is never the same colour as the selection; hover scales to 1.05 and press to 0.95 over 150ms.
4. `AccentScope` puts `--accent: <colour>` on a div and, through arbitrary-property classes, sets `--color-accent-50…400` as color-mix toward white (8, 16, 32, 52, 78%), `500` to the accent, and `600…950` toward black (86, 70, 56, 42, 28%).
5. Because the kit's semantic tokens (`--gradient-button-primary-*`, `--color-border-focus-ring`, `--color-switch-on-chip-*`, `--color-button-ghost-*`, `--color-badge-new-*`) are resolved at :root, the scope re-declares each one with the same formula as the theme, with `dark:` variants where dark mode maps the ramp differently.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `sphere sizes = sm 24px · md 36px · lg 36px, 48px from 640px`
  The compact pill matches the floating 24px row; lg drops to 36px on phones so seven spheres still fit one line at 360px.
- `ramp mixes = 50→400: 8/16/32/52/78% accent in white; 600→950: 86/70/56/42/28% accent in black`
  Roughly tracks Tailwind's blue ramp lightness, so swapping the hue keeps the kit's contrast (ghost text on ghost fill, white on the button gradient).
- `selection outline = 2px at 2px offset (1px offset at sm)`
  A gap between sphere and ring reads as "selected" on any colour, including the iridescent one, without a check mark.

## API

```ts
function AccentSwatchPicker(props: { swatches?: AccentSwatch[]; value?: string; defaultValue?: string; onChange?: (id: string) => void; size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg"; variant?: "plain" | "pill"; label?: string; isDisabled?: boolean; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function AccentScope(props: { color: string; children?: ReactNode; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type AccentSwatch = { id: string; label: string; color: string; fill?: string }
```

- `swatches: AccentSwatch[]` — default `DEFAULT_ACCENT_SWATCHES`
  Iridescent, blue, violet, pink, red, green, orange: id, label, CSS colour and optional sphere fill.
- `value: string`
  Controlled selected swatch id.
- `defaultValue: string` — default `swatches[0].id`
  Initial id when uncontrolled.
- `onChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called with the newly selected id.
- `size: "sm" | "md" | "lg"` — default `"md"`
  Sphere size: 24px, 36px, or 36px rising to 48px from the sm breakpoint.
- `variant: "plain" | "pill"` — default `"plain"`
  `pill` places the row on a floating rounded surface with a border and shadow.
- `label: string` — default `"Accent colour"`
  Accessible name of the radio group.
- `isDisabled: boolean`
  Disables every swatch.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the group.
- `AccentScope.color: string`
  Any CSS colour; written to `--accent` and expanded into the accent ramp for the subtree.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * The ramp: 50–400 mix the accent toward white, 600–950 toward black, 500 is
 * the accent itself. Then every semantic token that reads the ramp is
 * re-declared here so it resolves against the scoped ramp (dark mode keeps
 * the kit's own dark mapping for the ghost button and NEW badge).
 */
export const accentScopeClassName = [
  "[--color-accent-50:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--accent)_8%,white)]",
  "[--color-accent-100:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--accent)_16%,white)]",
  "[--color-accent-200:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--accent)_32%,white)]",
  "[--color-accent-300:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--accent)_52%,white)]",
  "[--color-accent-400:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--accent)_78%,white)]",
  "[--color-accent-500:var(--accent)]",
  "[--color-accent-600:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--accent)_86%,black)]",
  "[--color-accent-700:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--accent)_70%,black)]",
  "[--color-accent-800:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--accent)_56%,black)]",
  "[--color-accent-900:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--accent)_42%,black)]",
  "[--color-accent-950:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--accent)_28%,black)]",
  "[--color-border-focus-ring:var(--color-accent-500)]",
  "[--gradient-button-primary-default:linear-gradient(180deg,var(--color-accent-500)_0%,var(--color-accent-600)_100%)]",
  "[--gradient-button-primary-hover:linear-gradient(180deg,var(--color-accent-400)_0%,var(--color-accent-500)_100%)]",
  "[--gradient-button-primary-active:linear-gradient(180deg,var(--color-accent-600)_0%,var(--color-accent-700)_100%)]",
  "[--color-switch-on-chip-start:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--color-accent-500)_63%,var(--color-accent-600))]",
  "[--color-switch-on-chip-end:color-mix(in_oklab,var(--color-accent-600)_16%,var(--color-accent-700))]",
  "[--color-button-ghost-background:var(--color-accent-100)] dark:[--color-button-ghost-background:var(--color-accent-900)]",
  "[--color-button-ghost-hover:var(--color-accent-200)] dark:[--color-button-ghost-hover:var(--color-accent-800)]",
  "[--color-button-ghost-active:var(--color-accent-300)] dark:[--color-button-ghost-active:var(--color-accent-700)]",
  "[--color-button-ghost-foreground:var(--color-accent-700)] dark:[--color-button-ghost-foreground:var(--color-accent-300)]",
  "[--color-badge-new-background:var(--color-accent-100)] dark:[--color-badge-new-background:color-mix(in_srgb,var(--color-accent-950)_50%,transparent)]",
  "[--color-badge-new-text:var(--color-accent-600)] dark:[--color-badge-new-text:var(--color-accent-400)]",
].join(" ");

export interface AccentScopeProps {
  /** Any CSS colour: a palette variable, hex, oklch()… */
  color: string;
  children?: ReactNode;
  className?: string;
}

/** Re-tints every kit control inside it from one `--accent` value. */
export function AccentScope({ color, children, className }: AccentScopeProps) {
  return (
    <div style={{ "--accent": color } as CSSProperties} className={cx(accentScopeClassName, className)}>
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

/** Glossy sphere: a light spot up-left, the colour, a darker rim. */
function sphereBackground(s: AccentSwatch) {
  const gloss =
    "radial-gradient(circle at 32% 26%, color-mix(in oklab, white 85%, transparent) 0%, color-mix(in oklab, white 0%, transparent) 42%)";
  if (s.fill) return `${gloss}, ${s.fill}`;
  return `${gloss}, radial-gradient(circle at 40% 35%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--swatch) 70%, white) 0%, var(--swatch) 52%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--swatch) 72%, black) 100%)`;
}

export function AccentSwatchPicker({
  swatches = DEFAULT_ACCENT_SWATCHES,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onChange,
  size = "md",
  variant = "plain",
  label = "Accent colour",
  isDisabled,
  className,
}: AccentSwatchPickerProps) {
  return (
    <RadioGroup
      aria-label={label}
      orientation="horizontal"
      value={value}
      defaultValue={value === undefined ? (defaultValue ?? swatches[0]?.id) : undefined}
      onChange={onChange}
      isDisabled={isDisabled}
      className={cx(
        "flex w-fit flex-wrap items-center justify-center",
        GAP[size],
        variant === "pill" &&
          "rounded-full border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default p-1.5 shadow-md",
        className,
      )}
    >
      {swatches.map((s) => (
        <Radio
          key={s.id}
          value={s.id}
          aria-label={s.label}
          style={{ "--swatch": s.color } as CSSProperties}
          className={cx(
            "group relative shrink-0 cursor-pointer rounded-full outline-none",
            "data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:opacity-50",
          )}
        >
          <span
            aria-hidden
            style={{ background: sphereBackground(s) }}
            className={cx(
              "block rounded-full",
              SPHERE[size],
              "shadow-[inset_0_-2px_4px_color-mix(in_oklab,var(--swatch)_55%,black),0_1px_2px_color-mix(in_oklab,var(--swatch)_30%,transparent)]",
              "outline-2 outline-offset-2 outline-transparent",
              "transition-[scale,outline-color] duration-150 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
              "group-data-hovered:scale-105 group-data-pressed:scale-95",
              "group-data-selected:outline-(--swatch)",
              "group-data-focus-visible:outline-text-primary",
              size === "sm" && "outline-offset-1",
            )}
          />
        </Radio>
      ))}
    </RadioGroup>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up: no timers, listeners or observers; state is the selected id.

**Reduced motion.** The only motion is the 150ms hover/press scale and outline colour change on each sphere; it carries `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so selection snaps. The re-tint itself is instant.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Overriding only `--color-accent-500` on a wrapper. Tokens like the primary-button gradient were already resolved from the root ramp, so nothing inside changes until they are re-declared in the scope.
- Using the focus-ring token for the swatch focus state inside a scope: it now equals the selected colour, so focus becomes invisible. Use a neutral (text-primary) outline for focus.
- Making each swatch its own button with aria-pressed. A single choice is a radio group; that gives roving focus and arrow keys for free.

## Notes

- Swatch colours default to kit palette variables (`var(--color-violet-500)`…), so they follow the theme file; any CSS colour works.
- Composer Loader takes hex stops for its SVG band, so the demo keeps a four-stop band per swatch next to the picker.
- Two pickers can share one state, as the demo's big row and compact pill do.

## Definition of done

The iridescent sphere starts selected with an outline. Clicking "Violet" outlines it, turns the send button gradient and the "Agent working" switch violet, and the caption reads "Violet · --accent: var(--color-violet-500)"; the compact pill shows the same selection. With focus on the group, ArrowRight selects the next sphere. Toggling the switch off fades the composer light and swaps the Stop button for Send.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Accordion

Stacked sections for FAQs, settings groups and order details. `Accordion` is React Aria's `DisclosureGroup` and each `AccordionItem` is a `Disclosure`, so every header is a real button inside a heading with `aria-expanded`, and a collapsed panel stays searchable by find-in-page. Opening is pure CSS: React Aria measures the panel into `--disclosure-panel-height`, the panel eases to that height over 300ms while the body fades in, drops 4px and sharpens from a 4px blur, and the indicator turns with it. Three looks share the code: hairline-divided rows, the landing FAQ's tray of rounded cards, and one bordered card per item.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Sections that expand in place in divided, contained and separated styles, with an eased height and a blur-in body, on React Aria.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `Accordion` renders `AriaDisclosureGroup` with all props passed through (`defaultExpandedKeys`, `expandedKeys`, `allowsMultipleExpanded`, `onExpandedChange`) and puts `{ variant, indicator }` in a context, so items style themselves without prop drilling.
2. `AccordionItem` renders `AriaDisclosure` with `group/item`, then an `AriaHeading` (level 3 by default) holding an `AriaButton slot="trigger"`: optional icon, title in `text-headline-medium`, optional description, and the indicator icon. Keyboard focus shows an inset 2px focus ring.
3. The indicator is `RiArrowDownSLine` or `RiAddLine`. On `group-data-[expanded]/item` it rotates 180deg (chevron) or 45deg (plus turns into a close) and darkens from tertiary to primary icon colour, over 300ms.
4. `AriaDisclosurePanel` gets `h-(--disclosure-panel-height) overflow-clip transition-[height] duration-300`. React Aria's `useDisclosure` writes the measured content height into that custom property, so the height eases between 0 and the real size.
5. The body inside starts at `opacity-0` and, when motion is allowed, `-translate-y-1 blur-[4px]`. On expand it goes to `opacity-100 translate-y-0 blur-[0px]` with the same 300ms curve.
6. Variant classes come from a `sortCx` map: `divided` uses `divide-y divide-separator-border`; `contained` is a `rounded-[26px]` tray with 3px gaps holding `rounded-[23px]` cards (surfaces swap in dark mode); `separated` is `gap-2` between `rounded-2xl` bordered cards with `shadow-xs`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `EASE = cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), 300ms`
  A fast-out, soft-landing curve shared with the agent limits card and Tree View, used on the height, the body fade and the indicator turn so they move as one.
- `body entrance = opacity 0 → 1, translate-y -4px → 0, blur 4px → 0`
  The text settles into place as the panel opens instead of being revealed by the clip edge alone.
- `contained radii = tray rounded-[26px] p-[3px]; card rounded-[23px]`
  The card radius is the tray radius minus its 3px padding, so the curves stay concentric.
- `indicator turn = chevron rotate-180; plus rotate-45`
  A chevron points back up; a plus rotated 45deg reads as a close mark.

## API

```ts
type AccordionVariant = "divided" | "contained" | "separated"
interface AccordionProps extends Omit<DisclosureGroupProps, "className" | "children"> { variant?: AccordionVariant; indicator?: "chevron" | "plus"; className?: string; children: ReactNode }
interface AccordionItemProps extends Omit<DisclosureProps, "className" | "children"> { title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; icon?: ComponentType<{ className?: string }>; headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6; className?: string; children: ReactNode }
function Accordion(props: AccordionProps): JSX.Element
function AccordionItem(props: AccordionItemProps): JSX.Element
```

- `variant: "divided" | "contained" | "separated"` — default `"divided"`
  Accordion: hairline rows, a tray of cards, or one bordered card per item.
- `indicator: "chevron" | "plus"` — default `"chevron"`
  Accordion: chevron that flips, or plus that turns into a close.
- `defaultExpandedKeys / expandedKeys: Iterable<Key>`
  Accordion: uncontrolled or controlled open items (React Aria).
- `allowsMultipleExpanded: boolean` — default `false`
  Accordion: let several items stay open (React Aria).
- `id: Key`
  AccordionItem: key matched by the expanded keys.
- `title: ReactNode`
  AccordionItem: header text inside the trigger button.
- `description: ReactNode`
  AccordionItem: supporting line under the title.
- `icon: ComponentType`
  AccordionItem: Remix Icon shown before the title.
- `headingLevel: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` — default `3`
  AccordionItem: heading level wrapping the trigger.
- `isDisabled: boolean`
  AccordionItem: dims to 50% and blocks toggling (React Aria).

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function AccordionItem({
  title,
  description,
  icon: Icon,
  headingLevel = 3,
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: AccordionItemProps) {
  const { variant, indicator } = useContext(AccordionContext);
  const Indicator = indicator === "plus" ? RiAddLine : RiArrowDownSLine;

  return (
    <AriaDisclosure
      {...props}
      className={cx("group/item data-[disabled]:opacity-50", styles.item[variant], className)}
    >
      <AriaHeading level={headingLevel} className="flex">
        <AriaButton
          slot="trigger"
          className={({ isFocusVisible }) =>
            cx(
              "group/trigger flex w-full cursor-pointer items-center gap-3 text-start outline-none",
              "disabled:cursor-not-allowed",
              isFocusVisible && "ring-2 ring-border-focus-ring ring-inset",
              styles.trigger[variant],
            )
          }
        >
          {Icon ? <Icon className="size-5 shrink-0 text-foreground-icon-secondary" aria-hidden /> : null}
          <span className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-0.5">
            <span className="text-headline-medium text-text-primary">{title}</span>
            {description ? <span className="text-body-regular text-text-secondary">{description}</span> : null}
          </span>
          <Indicator
            aria-hidden
            className={cx(
              "size-5 shrink-0 text-foreground-icon-tertiary transition-[rotate,color] duration-300 motion-reduce:transition-none",
              EASE,
              "group-hover/trigger:text-foreground-icon-secondary group-data-[expanded]/item:text-foreground-icon-primary",
              indicator === "plus" ? "group-data-[expanded]/item:rotate-45" : "group-data-[expanded]/item:rotate-180",
            )}
          />
        </AriaButton>
      </AriaHeading>
      <AriaDisclosurePanel
        className={cx("h-(--disclosure-panel-height) overflow-clip transition-[height] duration-300 motion-reduce:transition-none", EASE)}
      >
        <div
          className={cx(
            "text-body-regular text-text-secondary",
            "opacity-0 transition-[opacity,translate,filter] duration-300 motion-reduce:transition-none",
            "motion-safe:-translate-y-1 motion-safe:blur-[4px]",
            "group-data-[expanded]/item:translate-y-0 group-data-[expanded]/item:opacity-100 group-data-[expanded]/item:blur-[0px]",
            EASE,
            styles.content[variant],
          )}
        >
          {children}
        </div>
      </AriaDisclosurePanel>
    </AriaDisclosure>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. React Aria owns the expanded state and the panel measurement; the component adds no listeners or timers.

**Reduced motion.** Every transition carries `motion-reduce:transition-none`, and the body's 4px drop and blur are applied only under `motion-safe:`. With reduced motion the panel snaps open, the text appears in place, and the indicator jumps to its turned angle.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Give every `AccordionItem` a stable `id`. `defaultExpandedKeys` and `expandedKeys` match on it.
- Do not animate the panel with `max-height` or JS. The height comes from `--disclosure-panel-height`, which React Aria keeps up to date when the content changes.
- The group allows one open item at a time by default. Pass `allowsMultipleExpanded` for settings groups where several can stay open.
- Pick `headingLevel` to fit the page outline; the default h3 is wrong under an h1-only page.
- Do not put interactive controls inside `title` or `description`. They render inside the trigger button.

## Notes

- A collapsed panel uses `hidden="until-found"` (set by React Aria's `useDisclosure`), so the browser's find-in-page can reach hidden text and expand its section.
- The `separated` card uses `bg-background-full` (the modal ground) rather than the card surface, so inputs and switch tracks inside keep an edge in dark mode.

## Definition of done

A contained accordion with `indicator="plus"` and `defaultExpandedKeys={["billing"]}` shows three rounded cards on a tray with the first open and its plus turned into a close. Clicking the second header closes the first and opens the second: its height eases over about 300ms and its text fades in from a slight blur while dropping 4px. Each header is a button with `aria-expanded` inside an h3, Enter and Space toggle it, and find-in-page for text in a closed panel opens that panel. With reduced motion everything snaps.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Activity Rings Card

A grey dashboard card with one value tile per goal (Move, Exercise, Running by default) above a stack of concentric SVG progress rings. Each ring starts at twelve o'clock and sweeps clockwise to its share of the goal over a tinted track, the outer ring first. Hovering or focusing a ring or its tile dims the others and puts the percentage in the centre, and clicking a tile pins that focus. Under reduced motion the rings are simply there at their final length.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Watch-style concentric goal rings in SVG with value tiles: the rings draw in on mount, and hovering a ring or tile focuses it.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Each ring is a pair of circles rotated by -90° so the path starts at twelve o'clock: a track and a progress stroke. The track colour is the ring colour mixed 22% into `--color-chart-track` with `color-mix(in oklab, …)`, so it reads as a pale tint in light mode and a dark tint in dark mode.
2. The progress circle has `pathLength={100}`, so the dash maths is in percent regardless of radius: `stroke-dasharray: 100 100` and `stroke-dashoffset: 100 - pct` leave exactly pct percent of the lap visible, with round caps on both ends. Progress is clamped to 0–100 for the arc.
3. Radii step inward: the outer ring sits half a stroke inside the edge and each next one moves in by one 18px band plus a 4px gap, which leaves a 60px hole at the default 184px size. More than three rings get thinner bands so they still fit.
4. On mount every offset is 100 (nothing drawn). Two `requestAnimationFrame`s later `drawn` flips to true and the offsets move to their targets through a CSS `transition-[stroke-dashoffset]` of 1100ms with an expo-out curve, delayed 140ms per ring from the outside in. A remount (the demo's Replay) draws them again.
5. Focus is `preview ?? pinned`. Pointer enter on a ring group (hit-tested on the stroke only, so the gaps do not count) or on a tile sets the preview; leaving clears it; clicking a tile toggles the pinned ring, which can also be controlled with `focused` and `onFocusedChange`. Unfocused rings fade to 30% and unfocused tiles to 50%.
6. The centre readout is a polite live region that shows the focused ring's percentage and label, keyed by ring so `.animate-number-fade` replays on each change. The SVG itself carries an `aria-label` listing every ring's percentage.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `STROKE / RING_GAP = 18px / 4px at 184px`
  Fat bands with a hairline of card between them read as separate rings at a glance; both scale with `size`.
- `draw = 1100ms, cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`
  The expo-out curve spends most of the time near the end, so the rings sweep in fast and settle gently on the exact value.
- `STAGGER_MS = 140ms`
  Enough to see the rings draw one after another from the outside in without making the last one feel late.
- `track mix = 22%`
  Keeps the unfinished part of the lap visibly the ring's colour but much lighter than the stroke, in both themes.

## API

```ts
function ActivityRingsCard(props?: ActivityRingsCardProps): JSX.Element
type ActivityRing = { id: string; label: string; value: number; goal: number; display?: string; color: string }
const ACTIVITY_RINGS: ActivityRing[]
```

- `title: string` — default `"Activity"`
  Header label.
- `caption: string`
  Right-hand header text, such as the selected day.
- `rings: ActivityRing[]` — default `ACTIVITY_RINGS`
  Rings from the outside in, each with its value, goal, display text and colour.
- `size: number` — default `184`
  Diameter of the ring stack in px; stroke and gap scale with it.
- `focused: string | null`
  Controlled pinned ring id.
- `onFocusedChange: (id: string | null) => void`
  Called when a tile click pins or unpins a ring.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Each ring is a circle with pathLength 100, so a dash of p units is p percent of the lap.
// The outer radius leaves half a stroke of room; each inner ring steps in by one band plus the gap.
const stroke = rings.length > 3 ? Math.max(8, (size / 2 - 20) / rings.length - RING_GAP) : (STROKE * size) / SIZE;
const geometry = rings.map((ring, i) => {
  const r = size / 2 - stroke / 2 - i * (stroke + RING_GAP);
  const pct = ring.goal > 0 ? (ring.value / ring.goal) * 100 : 0;
  const shown = drawn || reduced ? Math.min(100, Math.max(0, pct)) : 0;
  return { ring, r, pct, offset: 100 - shown, delay: i * STAGGER_MS };
});
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The mount effect cancels both pending animation frames on unmount. Everything else is CSS transitions and React event props.

**Reduced motion.** With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `useReducedMotion` renders the rings at their final offsets from the start and `motion-reduce:transition-none` removes the draw transition, so nothing sweeps. The focus fades and the centre readout fade are also instant.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Animating `stroke-dasharray` or computing `2πr` per ring. `pathLength={100}` makes every ring use the same 0–100 numbers, so one transition rule covers them all.
- Starting the transition in the same frame as the first paint. Setting `drawn` straight from `useEffect` can be batched with the initial render and the rings appear without animating; waiting two animation frames guarantees the browser has painted the empty state first.
- Letting progress past 100% wrap the dash. The arc is clamped to a full lap; the centre readout still shows the real percentage, such as 112%.

## Notes

- `ACTIVITY_RINGS` and the `ActivityRing` type are exported. A ring is `{ id, label, value, goal, display?, color }`.
- Pass `caption` to show the day on show at the top right; the Most Active Days Card demo uses this to pair the two cards.

## Definition of done

The default card reads "Activity" with three tiles, Move 1,592 kcal (pink), Exercise 1h 45m (lime) and Running 5.2 km (sky), and three rings that draw clockwise from the top to about 88%, 81% and 76%. Hovering the Exercise ring or tile dims the other rings and tiles and shows "81%" and "Exercise" in the centre; leaving restores them. Replay draws the rings again.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Agent Chat

The chat starter's home screen: the dashboard sidebar, a rounded chat card with an overlaid header, a streaming transcript and a pill composer, and a 260px rail of past chats. Messages go through the AI SDK's `useChat` to `/api/chat`, or to a scripted `DemoTransport` when the runtime has no key or `offline` is set. Assistant replies soften in a paragraph at a time, and threads are kept in localStorage, so history survives a reload without a database.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A full AI chat screen on the AI SDK: sidebar, a chat card whose replies blur in line by line, and a local thread history rail.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @ai-sdk/react@^4.0.166, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, ai@^7.0.162, motion@^12.43.0

## How it works

1. A single transport is created in a `useState` initializer so its identity never changes: `new SwitchingTransport(new DefaultChatTransport({ api: "/api/chat" }), new DemoTransport())`. `useChat({ transport })` drives `messages`, `status`, `sendMessage`, `stop` and `setMessages`. `submit` trims the input, stamps `activeUpdatedAt` with `Date.now()` and calls `sendMessage({ text }, { body: { demo: demoActive } })`. `SwitchingTransport.sendMessages` reads `body.demo` and hands the call to the canned transport when it is true, otherwise to the live one; `reconnectToStream` always goes live.
2. On mount the screen probes the runtime with `fetch("/api/chat", { method: "GET" })`. Only an explicit `configured: false` marks it "unconfigured"; a failed or unreadable probe counts as "ready" so a network fault never hides the composer. The probe's `providerLabel` and `model` feed the composer's status row. With no key, no messages and no demo flag, `SetupNotice` replaces the transcript with the AI_API_KEY steps and a "Skip, show me the demo" button that sets `demo` and stores `"on"` under `kinetic:agent-chat-demo`. `offline` skips the probe entirely and forces `demoActive`, so nothing touches the network.
3. `DemoTransport.sendMessages` picks a reply with `pickDemoAnswer` (five regex-matched answers and a fallback) and returns a `ReadableStream<UIMessageChunk>`. It enqueues `start` and `start-step`, waits 700ms, sends `text-start`, splits the reply with `/(?<=\s)/` so each word keeps its trailing space, and enqueues one `text-delta` every 28ms before `text-end`, `finish-step` and `finish`. The waits listen to the `AbortSignal`, so `stop()` clears the pending timer and the stream ends with an `abort` chunk.
4. `busy` is `status === "submitted" || status === "streaming"`. `AgentThinking variant="wave"` shows while `busy` and the last assistant message has no text yet, rather than only while `submitted`, because reasoning models flip the status to `streaming` on their first non-text chunk.
5. `AgentMessage` renders the user turn as a right-aligned `max-w-[75%] rounded-2xl` bubble. The assistant turn goes through `StreamedText`, which splits on `"\n"` and renders each line as a memoised `motion.p` that animates once from `{ opacity: 0, filter: "blur(5px)", y: 4 }` to `{ opacity: 1, filter: "blur(0px)", y: 0 }` over 0.42s with ease `[0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1]`. Lines are keyed by index, so a line mounts once and then only grows. Copy, read-aloud (`speechSynthesis`) and a relative timestamp sit under the reply and stay hidden while it streams.
6. Threads live in component state and localStorage under `kinetic:agent-chat-threads`. A mount effect assigns a fresh thread id (`crypto.randomUUID()` with a fallback) and restores up to 30 stored threads. The open thread is derived with `useMemo` (its title is the first user message cut at 48 characters plus "..."), merged into the list and sorted by `updatedAt`. The list is written back only once `restored` is true and the stream is idle. `messageAt` records when each message id first appeared, for the hover timestamps.
7. The header is `absolute` and 48px tall (`h-12`) over the scroll area, and the column starts at `pt-[72px]`. A `ResizeObserver` on the scroller checks whether `title.right + 16 > column.left`. Only when the transcript is scrolled and the title would clash does the header show its border and frost to `bg-white/20 backdrop-blur-[20px]` (`dark:bg-black/20`). Each change to `messages` or `busy` scrolls the transcript to `scrollHeight` with `behavior: "smooth"`.
8. The root is `flex gap-4 p-3 bg-background-full`, `h-dvh` by default or `h-[var(--template-preview-height)]` when `contained`. `DashboardSidebar` with `starterNav(useStarterBase())` is `hidden lg:flex`; below `lg` a menu button opens it as an overlay drawer (`absolute` when contained, else `fixed`). `AgentChatHistory` is a 260px card, `hidden xl:flex`, with "New chat", rename, mark-unread and delete on each row, an account menu and a JSON export.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `THINK_MS / WORD_MS = 700ms, then 28ms per word`
  The demo stream pauses long enough for the thinking indicator to read as a real wait, then releases whole words on a steady tick so the line-level blur-in looks like a live model rather than a paste.
- `LINE_TRANSITION = { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1] }, from blur(5px), opacity 0, y 4`
  Animating once per line instead of per token avoids the stutter of a fragment blurring in and then mutating into a finished word. The objects sit at module scope so Motion gets a stable target on every token re-render.
- `MAX_THREADS = 30`
  Enough history to be useful without letting localStorage grow unbounded. `orderThreads` sorts newest first and slices to this count on every merge.
- `header and column offset = header h-12 (48px) absolute, column pt-[72px]`
  The header overlays the transcript instead of stacking above it, so text runs up to the card's rounded top. The 72px top padding (48px header plus 24px) clears the title when nothing is scrolled.
- `clash buffer = 16px (title.right + 16 > column.left)`
  On a wide screen the centred column never reaches a short title, so the border and frost only appear when the measured geometry says the text would actually run under the title.
- `title cut = 48 characters plus "..."`
  A derived title has to fit the header and a 260px rail row. Renaming sets `activeTitle`, so the derived title cannot overwrite a chosen name.
- `composer pill = h-[52px] rounded-full p-2 gap-2.5, 36px (size-9) controls`
  Matches the Pro composer's geometry, so 8px padding seats the 36px circles flush inside a 52px pill and the starter reads as the same product.
- `feedback reset = 1600ms`
  How long the share and copy buttons show their check before reverting. Both timers are cleared if the state changes or the button unmounts.

## API

```ts
function AgentChat({ className, contained = false, offline = false }: { className?: string; contained?: boolean; offline?: boolean })
class DemoTransport implements ChatTransport<UIMessage>
class SwitchingTransport implements ChatTransport<UIMessage> { constructor(live: ChatTransport<UIMessage>, canned: ChatTransport<UIMessage>) }
function pickDemoAnswer(prompt: string): string
```

- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root with tailwind-merge. Pass `h-full` to fill a host instead of the viewport.
- `contained: boolean` — default `false`
  Fill `--template-preview-height` instead of `h-dvh`, and keep the phone nav drawer `absolute` inside the frame.
- `offline: boolean` — default `false`
  Skip the `/api/chat` probe and answer every message from the scripted `DemoTransport`. No network requests.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Demo mode: the visitor skipped the key notice. Only meaningful while the
// runtime reports no key; the moment a key exists, the real route answers.
const [demo, setDemo] = useState(false);
const demoActive = offline || (demo && probe.status === "unconfigured");
const [transport] = useState(
  () => new SwitchingTransport(new DefaultChatTransport({ api: ENDPOINT }), new DemoTransport()),
);
useEffect(() => {
  try {
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/set-state-in-effect -- restoring from localStorage after mount; there is no render-time source for it
    setDemo(window.localStorage.getItem(DEMO_KEY) === "on");
  } catch {
    // Storage can be blocked; the notice simply shows again.
  }
}, []);
const enterDemo = () => {
  setDemo(true);
  try {
    window.localStorage.setItem(DEMO_KEY, "on");
  } catch {
    // Nothing to remember without storage.
  }
};

const { messages, sendMessage, setMessages, status, stop, error } = useChat({
  transport,
});

const busy = status === "submitted" || status === "streaming";

// Reasoning models stream their thinking before any text, and the SDK flips
// status to "streaming" on that first non-text chunk. Gating the indicator on
// "submitted" alone therefore hides it seconds before a word appears, leaving
// an empty transcript. It stays up until real text exists.
const streamedText = useMemo(() => {
  const last = messages[messages.length - 1];
  if (!last || last.role !== "assistant") return "";
  return last.parts
    .filter((part) => part.type === "text")
    .map((part) => part.text)
    .join("");
}, [messages]);
const showThinking = busy && streamedText.length === 0;

/** The open chat as plain text, for the share control. */
const transcript = useMemo(
  () =>
    messages
      .map((message) => `${message.role === "user" ? "You" : "Assistant"}: ${messageText(message)}`)
      .filter((line) => !line.endsWith(": "))
      .join("\n\n"),
  [messages],
);

// Ask the runtime what it has before the first message, so a deployment with
// no key renders setup steps instead of letting someone type into a dead box.
useEffect(() => {
  if (offline) return;
  let cancelled = false;
  fetch(ENDPOINT, { method: "GET" })
    .then((res) => (res.ok ? res.json() : null))
    .then((data: { configured?: boolean; provider?: string; providerLabel?: string; model?: string } | null) => {
      if (cancelled) return;
      // Only an explicit `configured: false` means "no key". A failed or
      // unreadable probe says nothing about the key, and treating it as
      // missing would hide the composer behind setup steps for a fault that
      // has nothing to do with configuration.
      setProbe({
        status: data && data.configured === false ? "unconfigured" : "ready",
        provider: data?.provider ?? null,
        label: data?.providerLabel ?? null,
        model: data?.model ?? null,
      });
    })
    .catch(() => {
      // A failed probe shouldn't lock the composer — let the send attempt
      // surface the real error rather than guessing the cause here.
      if (!cancelled) setProbe({ status: "ready", provider: null, label: null, model: null });
    });
  return () => {
    cancelled = true;
  };
}, [offline]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The probe effect sets a `cancelled` flag so a late response never sets state. The header `ResizeObserver` is disconnected. The 1600ms copy and share timers are cleared, and `speechSynthesis.cancel()` runs when a message unmounts. Calling `stop()` aborts the demo stream's pending wait. The export blob URL is revoked a tick after the download starts, and the React Aria menus remove their portals when they close.

**Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `StreamedText` passes `initial={false}`, so each line appears settled with no blur, fade or rise. `AgentThinking` falls back to static rendering on its own. The smooth auto-scroll to the newest message is not gated.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Generating the thread id during render. It would differ between server and client and break hydration, which is why `activeId` starts as "" and the mount effect assigns it.
- Persisting before the restore has run. On the first render `threads` is empty, and writing that would erase stored history on every load. The writer waits for `restored` and for the stream to go idle.
- Constructing the transport inline. A new `SwitchingTransport` per render hands `useChat` a new transport each time. Keep it in a `useState` initializer.
- Treating a failed probe as "no key". Only an explicit `configured: false` shows the setup notice. Anything else lets the send attempt surface the real error.
- Gating the thinking indicator on `status === "submitted"` alone. Reasoning models switch to `streaming` before any text arrives, which leaves an empty transcript for seconds.
- Animating each word of the reply. Tokens arrive as fragments and the blur-in plays on a fragment that then changes, which reads as a stutter. Animate whole lines and memoise them.
- Revoking the export blob URL in the same turn as `click()`. The browser may not have read it yet; the URL is revoked on a `setTimeout(..., 0)`.

## Notes

- The route handlers live in `registry/lib/agent-chat-route.ts` and no file of this item imports them. A host must re-export them from `app/api/chat/route.ts` and declare `export const maxDuration = 30` there, because Next reads route config only from the route file.
- `offline` is a Kinetic addition for previews. It skips the GET probe and routes every send to `DemoTransport`, so the status row reads "Demo mode" and the empty state says the answers are scripted.
- Sidebar links come from `starterNav(useStarterBase())` in `app-shell`. Wrap the screen in `StarterBaseContext.Provider value={STARTER_SITE_PREFIX}` to point them into the hosted starter.
- Every subcomponent returns its JSX through `useTemplateCopy()`, which is the identity without a `TemplateCopyProvider`.

## Definition of done

The screen shows the sidebar, a chat card reading "What can I help with?" with three suggestion chips, and the history rail. Clicking "Explain what this starter does" adds a right-aligned user bubble, shows the wave "Thinking" indicator for about 700ms, then streams a scripted reply word by word with each paragraph blurring in. The header title becomes the prompt, the composer row reads "Demo mode" and "2 messages", and the thread appears under "Recent" in the rail.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Agent Creator

An agent setup card. The top half is a paper-cut avatar ringed by sixteen face options, with nine shapes on an arc underneath that rotates to bring the chosen one into its socket, and a colour pill that recolours every piece of paper. Below it, grouped fields collect the name, label, description, model, tools, language, notifications, voice and playback speed. Create validates the draft, awaits onCreate, and swaps to a created summary with Edit details and Create another.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A create-an-agent card: paper avatar with a face ring and shape arc, colour pill, profile, tools and voice fields, then a created summary.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: motion@^12.43.0, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Faces sit on a circle of radius 104px around the avatar at 22.5° steps; shapes sit on a 162px arc below it, each tile placed by its wrapped offset k from the selected index (θ = 90° − 24°·k), so picking a shape slides the arc with a CSS transform transition.
2. Faces, shapes and colours are radiogroups with a roving tabindex: arrow keys and Home/End move the selection and focus together, so a keyboard user can turn the arc without a pointer.
3. The avatar is SVG paper: the silhouette drawn twice (a 28% darker copy offset 2.5/3.5 units for the cut edge), a feTurbulence speckle filter clipped to the shape alpha for grain, and ink features drawn in a fixed dark tone because they sit on paper, not on the page.
4. validateAgent(draft) returns per-field errors. They appear only after the first Create, update live while typing, and the first invalid field receives focus; a footer line counts what is left to fix.
5. Submit sets a submitting state, awaits onCreate, and guards against unmount with a mounted ref; a rejection keeps the form and shows its message, success swaps to the summary and focuses its heading.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `FACE_R = 104`
  Clears the 136px avatar with room for 32px face discs without touching the shape arc.
- `SHAPE_R = 162`
  Hangs the arc under the face ring; five visible tiles span about 270px, inside the 320px stage.
- `SHAPE_STEP_DEG = 24`
  Spacing between neighbouring shapes on the arc; wider steps push the outer tiles off the card.
- `SHAPE_VISIBLE = 2`
  Tiles with |k| greater than 2 fade out and stop taking pointer input.

## API

```ts

```

- `value: AgentDraft`
  Controlled draft. Pair with onChange.
- `defaultValue: Partial<AgentDraft>`
  Uncontrolled starting draft merged over DEFAULT_AGENT_DRAFT; Reset restores it.
- `onChange: (draft: AgentDraft) => void`
  Called on every field, face, shape or colour change.
- `onCreate: (draft: AgentDraft) => void | Promise<void>`
  Called with a valid draft. A promise shows the creating state; a rejection shows its message.

  Called after Reset or Create another.

  Option lists for the selects, tool chips and speed control.

  Preset paper colours; a custom colour input sits at the end.

  Primary button text.

  Classes on the card, e.g. a fixed height so the body scrolls.

## Reference implementation of the core

```tsx
/** Field-level problems with a draft; an empty object means it can be created. */
export function validateAgent(draft: AgentDraft): AgentErrors {
  const errors: AgentErrors = {};
  const name = draft.name.trim();
  if (!name) errors.name = "Give the agent a name.";
  else if (name.length < 2) errors.name = "Use at least 2 characters.";
  else if (name.length > 40) errors.name = "Keep the name under 40 characters.";
  const label = draft.label.trim();
  if (!label) errors.label = "Add a short label.";
  else if (label.length > 16) errors.label = "Labels fit 16 characters.";
  if (draft.description.trim().length < 12) errors.description = "Say what it helps with (12+ characters).";
  if (draft.tools.length === 0) errors.tools = "Pick at least one tool.";
  return errors;
}

/** Place shape `index` on the arc relative to the selected one; k wraps to -n/2..n/2. */
function arcSlot(index: number, selected: number, count: number) {
  let k = (index - selected + count) % count;
  if (k > count / 2) k -= count;
  const theta = ((90 - k * SHAPE_STEP_DEG) * Math.PI) / 180;
  const visible = Math.abs(k) <= SHAPE_VISIBLE;
  return {
    k,
    visible,
    x: CX + SHAPE_R * Math.cos(theta) - TILE / 2,
    y: CY + SHAPE_R * Math.sin(theta) - TILE / 2,
    scale: k === 0 ? 1 : visible ? 0.86 : 0.5,
  };
}

/** Roving-tabindex arrow handling shared by the face ring and shape arc. */
function rovingIndex(event: KeyboardEvent, index: number, count: number): number | null {
  switch (event.key) {
    case "ArrowRight":
    case "ArrowDown":
      return (index + 1) % count;
    case "ArrowLeft":
    case "ArrowUp":
      return (index - 1 + count) % count;
    case "Home":
      return 0;
    case "End":
      return count - 1;
    default:
      return null;
  }
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The only async work is the awaited onCreate; a mounted ref drops its result after unmount. Motion loops stop with their elements. The demo clears its pending save timers on unmount.

**Reduced motion.** The avatar stops floating and blinking, the pop on pick is skipped, the shape arc and face hover snap without transitions, and the created summary appears without its rise.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Ink stays dark in both themes on purpose; it is drawn on the coloured paper, not on the page background.
- Each PaperAvatar builds its grain filter id from useId, stripped of colons, so several avatars on one page never share a filter.
- The shape arc wraps: a tile moving from k = −4 to k = 4 crosses the arc while invisible, so only visible tiles take pointer input.

- Pass value + onChange to drive the draft yourself; defaultValue seeds the uncontrolled draft and is what Reset returns to.
- Export validateAgent to run the same checks on the server.

Clearing the name and pressing Create shows "Give the agent a name." and focuses the field; a valid draft shows Creating… then "<name> is ready"; Create another restores the starting draft; arrow keys on the face ring and shape arc change the avatar.

# Build: Agent Detail Panel

The side panel of a multi-agent workspace for the agent you picked: avatar and name, a live status pill, the task it is working on, a progress rail with "n of m" steps, optional stat tiles and a vertical step log. The footer drives the run: Pause turns into Resume, Stop asks for confirmation, and a finished, failed or stopped run offers Run again. The step log re-reads itself from the run status, so a paused run shows a paused step and a stopped run strikes out what will never happen.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Selected-agent panel: status pill, task, progress, step log and Pause / Resume / Stop actions that change the run state.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. useAgentRunStatus keeps the run status controlled (status) or uncontrolled (defaultStatus) and returns a dispatcher: pause → paused, resume and restart → running, stop → stopped; every change calls onStatusChange(next, action), and restart also calls onRestart so the owner can reset its steps.
2. stepLook(stepState, runStatus) folds the run status into each step: the active step renders a spinner while running, a pause chip when paused, a question chip when waiting, a stop chip when stopped and an error chip when failed; pending steps become "Skipped" (struck through, detail hidden) once the run is stopped or failed.
3. The progress rail is the kit ProgressTrack at doneCount / steps.length, recoloured through its text colour: accent while running, orange paused, neutral stopped, red failed, green done.
4. The footer swaps between three layouts: Pause or Resume plus Stop while live, an inline "Stop this run?" group with Keep running / Stop run when confirmStop is on, and a status line with Run again once the run is terminal.
5. When the active step id changes and followActive is on, an effect measures that row inside the scrolling body (offsetTop against the relative body) and, only if it is out of view, scrolls the body so its bottom sits 16px above the fold; the page itself never scrolls.
6. The status pill has role="status" so the new label ("Paused", "Stopped") is announced; every step carries an sr-only state word next to its title.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `step chip = 20px circle, 12px icon`
  Wide enough for the 16px kit spinner glyph so the working step does not shift when it turns into a check.
- `connector = 1px at start-2.5, from top-6 to bottom-1`
  Centres the rail under the 20px chip and leaves a gap above the next chip.
- `follow margin = 16px`
  Leaves a sliver of the next pending step visible under the live one, so the log reads as continuing.
- `stats grid = 3 columns`
  Three short metrics (elapsed, files, tokens) fit a 360px-wide panel without wrapping.

## API

```ts

```

- `name: string`
  Agent name in the header.
- `subtitle: string`
  Role or label under the name.
- `avatar: ReactNode`
  40px avatar; defaults to a seeded monogram.
- `task: ReactNode`
  The instruction the agent is working on.
- `steps: AgentStep[]`
  { id, title, detail?, time?, state: "done" | "active" | "pending" | "failed" }.
- `stats: { label: string; value: ReactNode }[]`
  Optional stat tiles under the progress rail.
- `status: "running" | "waiting" | "paused" | "done" | "stopped" | "error"`
  Controlled run status.
- `defaultStatus: AgentRunStatus` — default `"running"`
  Initial status when uncontrolled.
- `onStatusChange: (status, action: "pause" | "resume" | "stop" | "restart") => void`

  Shows Run again on terminal runs; reset your steps here.
- `onClose: () => void`
  Shows the header close button.
- `confirmStop: boolean` — default `true`
  Ask before stopping.
- `followActive: boolean` — default `true`
  Scroll the panel body to keep the active step in view.
- `className: string`
  Classes for the panel surface (width, height).

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function stepLook(step: AgentStepState, run: AgentRunStatus): StepLook {
  if (step === "done") return "done";
  if (step === "failed") return "failed";
  if (step === "active") {
    if (run === "running") return "working";
    if (run === "waiting") return "waiting";
    if (run === "paused") return "paused";
    if (run === "error") return "failed";
    if (run === "done") return "done";
    return "stopped";
  }
  return run === "stopped" || run === "error" ? "skipped" : "pending";
}

export function nextRunStatus(action: AgentRunAction): AgentRunStatus {
  if (action === "pause") return "paused";
  if (action === "stop") return "stopped";
  return "running";
}

/** Controlled-or-uncontrolled run status plus the action dispatcher behind the footer buttons. */
export function useAgentRunStatus({
  status,
  defaultStatus = "running",
  onStatusChange,
  onRestart,
}: Pick<AgentDetailPanelProps, "status" | "defaultStatus" | "onStatusChange" | "onRestart">) {
  const [innerStatus, setInnerStatus] = useState<AgentRunStatus>(defaultStatus);
  const run = status ?? innerStatus;
  const act = (action: AgentRunAction) => {
    const next = nextRunStatus(action);
    if (status === undefined) setInnerStatus(next);
    onStatusChange?.(next, action);
    if (action === "restart") onRestart?.();
  };
  return [run, act] as const;
}
```

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is

**Reduced motion.** The running ping on the status dot is hidden, colour and confirm-row transitions use motion-reduce:transition-none, and the kit spinner slows to a 2.4s turn instead of stopping, and following the active step jumps (behavior auto) instead of smooth-scrolling; state changes are instant.

`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Restart only resets the status; reset your steps in onRestart or the log still shows the old run as finished.
- In controlled mode the panel never changes its own status: update status from onStatusChange or the buttons appear dead.

## Notes

- Set the panel height through className; the body scrolls while the header and footer stay put.
- The panel is a size container: below 22rem wide the status pill collapses to its coloured dot and keeps the label for screen readers, so the name has room.

# Build: Agent Limits Card

A usage card for an agent session. The top row reads used / capacity with a percent, over a thin bar split into one coloured segment per token bucket. Opening the row grows the card to list each bucket with its tokens and share, free space, deferred buckets that do not count, and collapsible member lists. Below it, each plan limit shows its reset time, percent used and a progress bar, and the plan heading links to plan settings.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

An agent budget card: a context window bar split by token bucket, an expandable breakdown, and plan limits with reset times.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. summarizeContext sums only non-deferred buckets, so deferred tools are listed with a dash but never move the bar, the total or free space; segment widths divide by max(capacity, used) so an overflowing window still ends at the bar edge.
2. Bucket colours come from the chart tokens in a fixed order (blue, purple, pink, yellow, green, sky, teal, lime, indigo); the counter skips deferred buckets, which take the neutral chart colour, and a bucket can pass its own colour.
3. The breakdown and every group list open with a grid-template-rows 0fr → 1fr transition on a wrapper with min-h-0 overflow-hidden, so the card grows to its natural height without measuring; closed content is inert and turns visibility-hidden once the close transition ends.
4. Hovering a bar segment or a breakdown row fades every other segment and row, linking the two views.
5. Each limit is a role="meter" with aria-valuetext carrying the reset copy; its bar switches to the warning tone at 75% and the error tone at 90%.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `WARN_AT = 0.75`
  A limit three-quarters used is worth a glance; the bar turns the warning colour.
- `DANGER_AT = 0.9`
  Past 90% the bar and the percent switch to the error colour.
- `BUCKET_PALETTE = chart-6, 5, 3, 8, 7, 4, 1, 2, 9`
  Neighbouring buckets get colours far apart on the wheel, so thin segments stay distinguishable.

## API

```ts
<AgentLimitsCard context={{ capacity: 1_000_000, buckets, groups }} plan="Max (5x)" limits={[{ label: "5-hour limit", used: 0.38, resets: "Resets in 2 hr 46 min" }]} planHref="/settings/plan" />
```

- `context: { capacity: number; buckets: ContextBucket[]; groups?: ContextGroup[] }`
  Window size, token buckets ({ label, tokens, color?, deferred? }) and collapsible member groups.
- `plan: string`
  Plan name shown after the limits title.
- `limits: PlanLimit[]` — default `[]`
  Rows of { label, used (0–1), resets }.
- `planHref: string`
  Makes the plan heading a link.
- `onManagePlan: () => void`
  Makes the plan heading a button when there is no planHref.
- `expanded / defaultExpanded / onExpandedChange: boolean / boolean / (open: boolean) => void` — default `false`
  Controlled or uncontrolled breakdown.
- `maxBreakdownHeight: number`
  Caps the breakdown height in px; longer lists scroll inside the card.
- `contextTitle / limitsTitle: string` — default `"Context window" / "Plan usage limits"`
  Section headings.
- `className: string`
  Classes on the card.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * Splits the window into what counts and what does not. Deferred buckets are
 * listed but never summed, so they cannot push the bar past the window. If
 * the counted tokens overflow the capacity, segment widths scale by the
 * larger number so the bar still ends at its right edge.
 */
export function summarizeContext({ capacity, buckets }: ContextUsage) {
  const safeCap = Math.max(1, capacity);
  let used = 0;
  for (const bucket of buckets) if (!bucket.deferred) used += Math.max(0, bucket.tokens);
  const scale = Math.max(safeCap, used);
  let paletteIndex = 0;
  const views: BucketView[] = buckets.map((bucket) => {
    const auto = bucket.deferred ? DEFERRED_COLOR : BUCKET_PALETTE[paletteIndex++ % BUCKET_PALETTE.length]!;
    const tokens = Math.max(0, bucket.tokens);
    return {
      ...bucket,
      color: bucket.color ?? auto,
      share: bucket.deferred ? null : (tokens / safeCap) * 100,
      width: bucket.deferred ? 0 : (tokens / scale) * 100,
    };
  });
  const free = Math.max(0, safeCap - used);
  return { views, used, free, percent: Math.round((used / safeCap) * 100) };
}

/** Clamps a limit share and picks its tone. */
export function limitTone(used: number) {
  const value = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, used));
  const tone = value >= DANGER_AT ? "danger" : value >= WARN_AT ? "warning" : "normal";
  return { value, tone } as const;
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers, listeners or observers; all motion is CSS transitions on state changes.

**Reduced motion.** The breakdown and group lists open and close instantly, chevrons snap, and bar segments and limit fills jump to their new widths without transitions.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Deferred buckets are excluded from the used total; pass them for the listing only, not as part of the capacity maths.
- With maxBreakdownHeight the breakdown scrolls, so focus rings inside it are inset to avoid being clipped.
- Share percentages use the capacity even when the window overflows, so they can add up past 100%.

## Notes

- Pass planHref for a link or onManagePlan for a button; with neither, the plan heading is plain text.
- formatTokens and summarizeContext are exported for use in tooltips or server summaries.

The header reads 820k / 1M (82%); clicking it reveals Messages 520k 52.0%, the deferred rows with a dash and Free space 180k 18.0%; opening MCP tools lists its four members; the plan heading calls onManagePlan; sending a message widens the Messages segment and raises the 5-hour limit.

# Build: Agent List Panel

The left rail of a multi-agent workspace: a pill toolbar (search, optional extra buttons, a blue "+"), a three-way All / Running / Done filter with live counts, and a list of agents. Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —

Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Agent sidebar list with avatar, live status dot, last message and time, single selection, search and All/Running/Done tabs.

- Category: navigation
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Counts for every tab are computed once per agents array with matchesAgentFilter: Running covers status running or waiting, Done covers done, All covers everything.
2. The visible list is the agents array filtered by the active tab and by the search query (case-insensitive match on name or last message), memoised on agents, filter and query.
3. The filter is a React Aria ToggleButtonGroup with selectionMode="single" and disallowEmptySelection, so one tab is always pressed; filter/defaultFilter/onFilterChange make it controlled or uncontrolled.
4. The list is a React Aria ListBox (single selection, disallowEmptySelection): arrow keys, Home/End and typeahead move focus, Enter/Space or a click select, and handleSelection maps the key back to the agent before calling onSelect.
5. The search pill toggles an autofocused input under the toolbar; Escape or the pill (now an X) clears the query and closes it.
6. Avatars default to AgentMonogram, a 32px rounded tile whose tint is picked by hashSeed(name) from five calendar-event palettes, so a name always keeps its colour; any node can replace it per agent.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `avatar = 32px tile, 10px radius`
  Matches the reference rows; the status dot (10px with a 2px ring) sits on its bottom corner without covering the initials.
- `toolbar pills = h-8, rounded-full, flex-1`
  Search, extra buttons and "+" share the width evenly like the reference toolbar.
- `filter rule = running = running | waiting; done = done`
  An agent waiting on your input is still in progress; failed and idle agents only appear under All.
- `tones = 5 (lime, blue, pink, purple, emerald)`

```tsx
const counts = useMemo(() => {
  const out: Record<AgentFilter, number> = { all: 0, running: 0, done: 0 };
  for (const a of agents) {
    out.all += 1;
    if (matchesAgentFilter(a.status, "running")) out.running += 1;
    if (matchesAgentFilter(a.status, "done")) out.done += 1;
  }
  return out;
}, [agents]);

const visible = useMemo(() => {
  const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();
  return agents.filter(
    (a) =>
      matchesAgentFilter(a.status, activeFilter) &&
      (!q || a.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || (a.lastMessage ?? "").toLowerCase().includes(q)),
  );
}, [agents, activeFilter, query]);

const setFilter = (next: AgentFilter) => {
  if (filter === undefined) setInnerFilter(next);
  onFilterChange?.(next);
};

const handleSelection = (keys: Selection) => {
  if (keys === "all") return;
  const [first] = keys as Set<Key>;
  if (first === undefined) return;
  const id = String(first);
  const agent = agents.find((a) => a.id === id);
  if (!agent || id === activeId) return;
  if (selectedId === undefined) setInnerSelected(id);
  onSelect?.(id, agent);
};

const closeSearch = () => {
  setQuery("");
  setSearchOpen(false);
};
```
