# Build: Announcement

An onboarding or "what's new" card sized for the 260px sidebar footer: a 20px icon, a title, an optional description and an optional full-width secondary button. Dismissal is managed inside the card. The close button plays a 250ms blur, fade and scale-down exit, then the card unmounts and `onClose` fires. An opt-in `introDelay` plays the reverse as an entrance once the surrounding UI has settled.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A compact sidebar card with an icon, title, note and full-width call to action that blurs and shrinks away when dismissed.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, motion@^12.43.0

## How it works

1. The card is a `motion.div` inside `AnimatePresence`, rendered while a local `dismissed` flag is false. The close button sets the flag, `AnimatePresence` keeps the node mounted for its `exit` animation, and `onExitComplete={onClose}` calls the consumer only after the card has actually left.
2. The exit animates `opacity: 0`, `scale: 0.85` and `filter: "blur(6px)"` over 0.25s with `easeInOut`. Blur together with scale reads as the card receding rather than being cut out.
3. `introDelay` turns on the entrance. With it set, `initial` is `{ opacity: 0, y: 15, scale: 0.85, filter: "blur(6px)" }` and `animate` returns everything to rest over 0.25s `easeOut`, starting after `introDelay` seconds. Without it, `initial={false}` and `animate={undefined}`, so the card renders in its final state on the first frame with no animation work.
4. The layout follows the Figma frame: a `flex-col gap-3 p-3` card with `rounded-xl`, a 1px `border-border-button-default` and `bg-background-primary-default`, and no shadow. Inside it a `gap-1` column holds the 20px icon (`text-foreground-icon-secondary`) and a `gap-0.5` text block with the title in `text-body-medium text-text-primary` and the description in `text-body-2-medium text-text-secondary`. That totals 150px with every part present.
5. The close control is the kit's `CloseButton` at `size="xs"` (a 20px round button), absolutely placed at `end-3 top-3` so it mirrors in RTL. It takes `aria-label={closeLabel}`, which defaults to "Dismiss".
6. The action is a `Button` with `variant="secondary"`, `size="small"` and `className="w-full"`, rendered only when `actionLabel` is set. It calls `onAction` directly and does not dismiss the card. Leaving out `description`, `actionLabel` or `dismissible` removes that part and the card shrinks to fit.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `exit = scale 0.85, blur 6px, opacity 0 over 0.25s easeInOut`
  The card leaves visibly without dragging. At 0.85 the shrink reads as dismissal rather than a glitch, and the 6px blur hides the hard edge as it fades so the card never looks clipped.
- `entrance = y 15px, scale 0.85, blur 6px → rest over 0.25s easeOut, after introDelay`
  The mirror of the exit plus a small rise from below, so the card arrives from where the eye is not looking yet. `easeOut` lands it softly. The delay lets the sidebar settle first so the card draws attention on its own.
- `card metrics = p-3, gap-3, rounded-xl, 20px icon, 150px tall`
  Taken 1:1 from the Figma "Event card": 12 + 20 + 4 + (20 + 2 + 36) + 12 + 32 + 12 = 150. It fills its container (236px inside the 260px sidebar) instead of fixing a width.

## API

```ts
function Announcement(props: Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "title" | "onDrag" | "onDragStart" | "onDragEnd" | "onAnimationStart" | "onAnimationEnd"> & { title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; icon?: IconComponent; actionLabel?: ReactNode; onAction?: () => void; dismissible?: boolean; onClose?: () => void; closeLabel?: string; introDelay?: number; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
```

- `title: ReactNode`
  Required headline, set in Body 1 Medium (14/20).
- `description: ReactNode`
  Supporting line in Body 2 Medium (13/18). Omit for a title-only card.
- `icon: ComponentType<{ className?: string }>` — default `RiShieldStarFill`
  Leading icon component, drawn at 20px.
- `actionLabel: ReactNode`
  Label for the full-width secondary button. No button is rendered without it.
- `onAction: () => void`
  Click handler for the action button. Does not dismiss the card.
- `dismissible: boolean` — default `false`
  Shows the 20px close button in the top-end corner.
- `onClose: () => void`
  Called once, after the exit animation finishes.
- `closeLabel: string` — default `"Dismiss"`
  Accessible name of the close button.
- `introDelay: number`
  Seconds before the entrance plays. Leave it out to skip the entrance.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function Announcement({
  title,
  description,
  icon: Icon = RiShieldStarFill,
  actionLabel,
  onAction,
  dismissible = false,
  onClose,
  closeLabel = "Dismiss",
  introDelay,
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: AnnouncementProps) {
  const [dismissed, setDismissed] = useState(false);
  const hasIntro = introDelay !== undefined;

  return (
    <AnimatePresence onExitComplete={onClose}>
      {!dismissed && (
        <motion.div
          ref={ref}
          initial={hasIntro ? { opacity: 0, y: 15, scale: 0.85, filter: "blur(6px)" } : false}
          animate={
            hasIntro
              ? {
                  opacity: 1,
                  y: 0,
                  scale: 1,
                  filter: "blur(0px)",
                  transition: { duration: 0.25, ease: "easeOut", delay: introDelay },
                }
              : undefined
          }
          exit={{
            opacity: 0,
            scale: 0.85,
            filter: "blur(6px)",
            transition: { duration: 0.25, ease: "easeInOut" },
          }}
          className={cx(styles.card, className)}
          {...props}
        >
          <div className={styles.content}>
            <Icon className={styles.icon} aria-hidden />

            {dismissible ? (
              <CloseButton
                size="xs"
                aria-label={closeLabel}
                onClick={() => setDismissed(true)}
                className={styles.close}
              />
            ) : null}

            <div className={styles.text}>
              <p className={styles.title}>{title}</p>
              {description ? <p className={styles.description}>{description}</p> : null}
            </div>
          </div>

          {actionLabel ? (
            <Button
              variant="secondary"
              size="small"
              onClick={onAction}
              className="w-full"
            >
              {actionLabel}
            </Button>
          ) : null}
        </motion.div>
      )}
    </AnimatePresence>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to release by hand. Motion stops any running entrance or exit animation when the card unmounts, and the component adds no listeners or timers of its own.

**Reduced motion.** There is no reduced-motion branch in the component, and Motion's default `reducedMotion` is `"never"`, so the 250ms exit (and the entrance, when enabled) plays as written. Under `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">` Motion removes the scale and `y` transforms and keeps the short opacity and blur fades.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Unmounting the card yourself on close. The card owns its `dismissed` state. If the parent removes it immediately, `AnimatePresence` goes with it and the exit never plays. Listen to `onClose`, which fires after the exit finishes.
- Passing an icon element (`icon={<RiSparklingFill />}`). The prop takes the component and renders it at `size-5` with `aria-hidden`.
- Expecting the action button to dismiss the card. `onAction` only runs your handler. Hide the card from `onAction` yourself, for example by changing its `key` or rendering it conditionally after your own exit.
- Setting `introDelay={0}` and expecting no animation. Any number, including 0, turns the entrance on. Leave the prop out entirely for a card that simply appears.

## Notes

- The card is uncontrolled. To show it again after a dismissal, remount it with a new `key`.
- The component does not read the reduced-motion preference itself. In an app wrapped in `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">`, Motion drops the scale and `y` transforms and keeps the opacity and blur fades.

## Definition of done

Inside a 260px sidebar the card fills the column, shows the icon, title, description and a full-width "See what's new" button, and with a two-line description it is 150px tall. Clicking the close button blurs and shrinks the card away in about a quarter of a second, and `onClose` fires once the card is gone. Clicking the action runs `onAction` and leaves the card in place. A remount with `introDelay={0.1}` rises in from 15px below while un-blurring.

# Build: Anti-Aliased Point Discs

A point sprite is a square; this is the pair of shader tricks that makes it a dot. The fragment shader carves a disc with one smoothstep across the outer few percent of the sprite and discards everything below a visibility threshold, and the vertex shader clamps the point size to the hardware floor and then divides the alpha by the area that clamp invented. The field is laid out as a phyllotaxis spiral with a size ramp so both ends of the problem — sub-pixel dots and twenty-pixel dots — are on screen at once.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A phyllotaxis field of dots that stay the same weight at every pixel ratio, with no MSAA and no texture.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1

## How it works

1. Dots are placed by golden-angle phyllotaxis: `t = sqrt((i + 0.5) / count)` for the normalised radius and `i * 137.507°` for the angle, so spacing is even rather than crowded at the centre. A seeded jitter of ±0.06 rad is added to break the moiré a pure spiral shows at small radii.
2. The vertex shader rotates differentially — `angle + uElapsed * uSpin * (0.6 + t)` — so the rim turns 1.6x faster than the core and the arms shear instead of the field spinning rigidly.
3. Point size ramps as `mix(uMinRadius, uMaxRadius, t * t)`, quadratic so most of the field stays small and the large discs are confined to the rim where the anti-aliasing is easiest to inspect.
4. The size is then clamped: `clamped = max(2.0, radius * 2.0 * uPixelRatio)` against `unclamped = max(1.0, …)`, and `vAlphaScale = unclamped² / clamped²` is passed to the fragment shader. A dot the driver forced to be twice as wide comes out four times fainter, so total emitted light is unchanged.
5. The fragment shader computes `d = length(gl_PointCoord - 0.5)` and `disc = 1.0 - smoothstep(uEdgeInner, 0.5, d)` where `uEdgeInner = 0.5 - softness`, so the falloff always ends exactly at the sprite edge and the disc stays inscribed in its square.
6. Anything whose final alpha lands below 0.003 is discarded rather than blended, which removes a framebuffer read-modify-write per pixel across the sparse outer field.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `GOLDEN_ANGLE = Math.PI * (3 - Math.sqrt(5)) ≈ 2.39996 rad`
  The only angle whose successive multiples never repeat a rational fraction of a turn. Any nearby value produces visible spokes within a few hundred points.
- `softness = 0.07`
  Anti-aliased band as a fraction of the sprite radius, giving `smoothstep(0.43, 0.5, d)`. Below ~0.05 a 2px dot aliases back into a square; above ~0.15 every dot reads as blurred rather than small.
- `MIN_POINT_SIZE = 2.0`
  Hardware floor in device pixels. Below roughly 1px most GPUs rasterise nothing, so the smallest dots would be absent on some machines and present on others.
- `ALPHA_EPSILON = 0.003`
  Discard threshold, just under 1/255. Anything fainter cannot be shown by an 8-bit framebuffer, so blending it is pure fill cost.
- `radius ramp exponent = t * t`
  Quadratic rather than linear. Linear puts mid-size discs everywhere and the field turns into a solid disc; quadratic keeps the interesting large sprites at the rim.
- `count = 4000`
  One buffer, one draw call, and about 4000 sprites of up to 20px — roughly the point where fill rate rather than vertex count starts to dominate on integrated graphics.
- `differential spin factor = (0.6 + 1.0 * t)`
  Rim-to-core angular speed ratio of 1.6. At 1.0 the field spins rigidly and reads as a rotating image; past ~2.5 the arms wind into a solid ring within a minute.

## API

```ts
function AntialiasedDiscFragment(props: { count?: number; minRadius?: number; maxRadius?: number; fieldRadius?: number; spin?: number; softness?: number; opacity?: number; colorInner?: string; colorOuter?: string; seed?: number | string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `count: number` — default `4000`
  Number of discs. One draw call regardless.
- `minRadius: number` — default `0.5`
  Disc radius in CSS pixels at the centre — deliberately sub-pixel at DPR 1.
- `maxRadius: number` — default `10`
  Disc radius in CSS pixels at the rim.
- `fieldRadius: number` — default `0.92`
  Field diameter as a fraction of the container short side.
- `spin: number` — default `0.08`
  Base angular speed in radians per second; the rim runs 1.6x faster.
- `softness: number` — default `0.07`
  Anti-aliased band width as a fraction of the sprite radius.
- `opacity: number` — default `1`
  Multiplier applied before the area compensation.
- `colorInner: string` — default `'#ffffff'`
  Tint at the centre of the field.
- `colorOuter: string` — default `'#6f7680'`
  Tint at the rim.
- `seed: number | string` — default `'antialiased-disc-fragment'`
  Seeds the angular jitter so the layout is stable across reloads and matches on the server.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the host element via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function AntialiasedDiscFragment({
  count = 4000,
  minRadius = 0.5,
  maxRadius = 10,
  fieldRadius = 0.92,
  spin = 0.08,
  softness = 0.07,
  opacity = 1,
  colorInner = '#ffffff',
  colorOuter = '#6f7680',
  seed = 'antialiased-disc-fragment',
  className,
}: AntialiasedDiscFragmentProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);
  const [unsupported, setUnsupported] = useState(false);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const size = useRef({ width, height });
  size.current = { width, height };

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const ready = width > 0 && height > 0;

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready) return;

    if (!hasWebGL()) {
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }

    let renderer: THREE.WebGLRenderer;
    try {
      renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: false, alpha: true });
    } catch {
      // A context can still be refused between the probe and the construction —
      // the tab may have hit the browser's live-context ceiling in between. three
      // throws rather than returning null, and an uncaught throw here takes the
      // page with it.
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }
    renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio());
    renderer.setClearAlpha(0);

    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const camera = new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0.1, 10);
    camera.position.z = 1;

    const rng = createRng(seed);
    const positions = new Float32Array(count * 3); // all zeros; the shader places them
    const disc = new Float32Array(count * 2);

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
      // sqrt spacing, not linear: linear spacing crowds the centre, which is
      // exactly where the sub-pixel dots are and where crowding is least
      // forgiving.
      const t = Math.sqrt((i + 0.5) / count);
      // A little seeded angular jitter breaks the moiré that a pure golden
      // spiral shows at small radii on a low-DPR screen.
      disc[i * 2] = t;
      disc[i * 2 + 1] = i * GOLDEN_ANGLE + (rng() - 0.5) * 0.12;
    }

    const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
    geometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(positions, 3));
    geometry.setAttribute('aDisc', new THREE.BufferAttribute(disc, 2));

    const uniforms: Uniforms = {
      uElapsed: { value: 0 },
      uExtent: { value: 1 },
      uPixelRatio: { value: renderer.getPixelRatio() },
      uSpin: { value: spin },
      uFieldRadius: { value: fieldRadius },
      uMinRadius: { value: minRadius },
      uMaxRadius: { value: maxRadius },
      uOpacity: { value: opacity },
      uColorInner: { value: new THREE.Color(colorInner) },
      uColorOuter: { value: new THREE.Color(colorOuter) },
      // The band always ENDS at 0.5 — the sprite's own edge. Softening inward
      // keeps the disc inscribed in the sprite; softening outward would clip
      // the falloff square at the corners.
      uEdgeInner: { value: 0.5 - softness },
    };

    const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader: ANTIALIASED_DISC_VERT,
      fragmentShader: ANTIALIASED_DISC_FRAG,
      uniforms,
      transparent: true,
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
      // Additive would blow the overlapping core to white. Normal blending
      // with a discard keeps the density readable where the dots overlap.
      blending: THREE.NormalBlending,
    });

    const points = new THREE.Points(geometry, material);
    points.frustumCulled = false;
    scene.add(points);

    el.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
    renderer.domElement.style.display = 'block';
    renderer.domElement.style.width = '100%';
    renderer.domElement.style.height = '100%';

    const resize = (w: number, h: number) => {
      renderer.setSize(w, h, false);
      camera.left = -w / 2;
      camera.right = w / 2;
      camera.top = h / 2;
      camera.bottom = -h / 2;
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
      uniforms.uExtent.value = Math.min(w, h);
      // Re-read rather than assume: moving a window between a retina and a
      // non-retina display changes devicePixelRatio without changing the
      // canvas size, and a stale value breaks the whole compensation.
      uniforms.uPixelRatio.value = renderer.getPixelRatio();
    };

    const draw = (elapsed: number) => {
      uniforms.uElapsed.value = elapsed;
      renderer.render(scene, camera);
    };

    resize(size.current.width, size.current.height);
    stage.current = { resize, draw };
    draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      disposeObject(scene);
      material.dispose();
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      renderer.domElement.remove();
    };
  }, [
    ready,
    count,
    minRadius,
    maxRadius,
    fieldRadius,
    spin,
    softness,
    opacity,
    colorInner,
    colorOuter,
    seed,
  ]);

  useEffect(() => {
    stage.current?.resize(width, height);
    if (reduced) stage.current?.draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);
  }, [width, height, reduced]);

  useRaf((_dt, elapsed) => stage.current?.draw(elapsed), ready && !reduced && !unsupported);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nulls the stage ref, disposes the geometry and material via `disposeObject` plus an explicit `material.dispose()`, calls `disposeRenderer` for `dispose` + `forceContextLoss` + a zeroed drawing buffer, then removes the canvas. `useRaf` releases the frame subscription itself.

**Reduced motion.** No rAF subscription is opened. A single frame is drawn at `uElapsed = 6`, which is far enough into the rotation that the arms are already sheared, so the composition is the interesting one rather than the unrotated starting pose. The field is fully visible; only the spin stops.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Softening the disc outward from 0.5 instead of inward to it. The sprite has no pixels past 0.5, so the outer half of the falloff is clipped by the sprite boundary and the dot shows four square corners.
- Clamping `gl_PointSize` and leaving the alpha alone. The clamp does nothing at DPR 3 and doubles the covered area at DPR 1, so the identical component looks twice as heavy on a non-retina monitor — a bug that is invisible on the machine most people develop on.
- Caching the pixel ratio at construction. Dragging the window from a retina to a non-retina display changes `devicePixelRatio` without changing the canvas size, so the compensation silently goes stale; it is re-read on every resize.
- Reaching for `antialias: true` when the dots look jagged. MSAA allocates a multisample buffer the size of the canvas and does not help a point sprite whose edge is defined by alpha — the smoothstep is the fix.
- Blending fully transparent fragments instead of discarding them. At 4000 sprites with a 20px radius the outer field is mostly empty pixels, and each one still costs a read-modify-write of the framebuffer.
- Linear radial spacing instead of `sqrt`. It crowds the centre, which is precisely where the sub-pixel dots live, and the core turns into an undifferentiated smear.

## Notes

- The camera is orthographic and 1:1 with CSS pixels, so `uMinRadius` and `uMaxRadius` are literal pixel radii rather than scene units.
- The same two tricks apply to any `THREE.Points` material. The spiral is only a way to show the whole size range at once.

## Definition of done

A spiral of dots that grows from barely-visible at the centre to clearly round discs at the rim, with soft edges and no square corners at any size. Zoom the browser between 100% and 200% and the field keeps the same apparent weight instead of getting denser or lighter. Nothing shimmers along the arms as they turn. With reduced motion the spiral renders in full and holds still.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: App Shell

The page standard every BoardUI template follows: a full-height frame with the dashboard sidebar on large screens (an overlay drawer below `lg`), and a main column of at most 1300px holding a breadcrumb trail, the page heading with its actions, and the page content sitting directly on the page background. The starter's navigation is generated from one base path read off the URL, so the sidebar only links to pages the app has. The default header actions are a notification bell with an unread badge that opens the notification center in a popover, plus Filters and Create ticket buttons.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Page frame for the chat starter: sidebar, phone drawer, breadcrumb and heading over a 1300px column, with a notification bell.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `AppShell` renders a `relative flex h-dvh w-full gap-4 overflow-hidden bg-background-full p-3` row: `DashboardSidebar` (hidden below `lg`) and a `<main>` that is the only scroller (`flex-1 overflow-y-auto overflow-x-hidden`, `sm:pt-3`) centring a `max-w-[1300px] flex-col gap-2.5` column. `columnClassName` overrides the column width.
2. Navigation comes from `starterNav(base)`: Chat, Dashboard, Components and Blocks, Sign in, Sign up, each `href` prefixed with `base`. `useStarterBase()` returns a pinned base from `StarterBaseContext` when a host provides one, else matches `pathname` against `/templates/chat-starter` (with an optional language prefix) and falls back to "" in a deployed copy. `useStarterSelected()` maps the rest of the path to "dashboard", "components" or "chat".
3. Below `lg`, an `IconButton` beside the heading toggles `navOpen`; when true a `fixed inset-0 z-50 lg:hidden` layer renders a full-bleed `<button aria-label="Close navigation">` backdrop (`bg-black/40`) and the sidebar in `mobile` mode with `onClose`. The toggle swaps its glyph between `RiMenuLine` and `RiCloseLine`.
4. The header is a `Breadcrumb` (team avatar, member avatar, then the current page with `icon`) over a wrapping row: the `h1` (`text-title-2-medium`, `heading` defaulting to `title`) on the left and the actions on the right. `actions` undefined renders the defaults; `null` renders none.
5. `NotificationBell` owns `isOpen` and two refs: an `IconButton` trigger with `aria-expanded` / `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and a React Aria `Popover` (`placement="bottom end"`, `offset={8}`, `isNonModal`, `w-[440px] max-w-[calc(100vw-24px)]`) holding a `Dialog` with `NotificationCenter`. Outside presses close it via `useDismissOnOutsidePress`. The unread count (items with `unread`) shows in a 16px red badge at `top-0.5 start-[18px]` that loses its 1.5px ring on hover and press.
6. Both the shell and the bell run their JSX through `useTemplateCopy()`'s `localize`, so localized templates translate the fixed copy without the components taking strings as props.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `content column = max-w-[1300px]`
  The width every BoardUI template page uses, so cards and tables line up across pages; the catalogue overrides it (e.g. `max-w-[964px]`) through `columnClassName`.
- `sidebar breakpoint = lg (1024px)`
  Below it the sidebar would squeeze the content column, so it becomes an overlay drawer opened from the header.
- `notification popover = 440px wide, max-w-[calc(100vw-24px)], bottom end, offset 8`
  Wide enough for a notification row with inline actions; end alignment keeps it under the bell at the right of the header.
- `STARTER_SITE_PREFIX = "/templates/chat-starter"`
  Where the starter lives on the hosted site; reading it off the URL lets the same files run hosted or deployed at the root untouched.

## API

```ts

```

- `title: string`
  The page's name, shown as the current breadcrumb item.
- `heading: string` — default `title`
  The `h1` over the content.

  Icon on the current breadcrumb item.
- `actions: ReactNode` — default `bell + Filters + Create ticket`
  Header actions on the right; `null` for none.
- `className: string`
  Classes on the outer frame, e.g. `h-full` instead of `h-dvh` inside a host.
- `columnClassName: string`
  Overrides the 1300px content column.
- `NotificationBell.notifications: NotificationCenterItem[]` — default `STARTER_NOTIFICATIONS`
  The inbox shown in the popover; unread items drive the badge.

```tsx
/**
 * The page standard every BoardUI template follows, free or Pro: content sits
 * directly on the page background inside a 1300px column, so cards and tables
 * carry their own surfaces; above it a breadcrumb trail (team, member, page)
 * and the page heading. Pages pass what differs and get the rest.
 */
export function AppShell({
  title,
  heading = title,
  icon: Icon = RiDashboardLine,
  actions,
  children,
  className,
  columnClassName,
}: {
  /** The page's name, shown as the current breadcrumb item. */
  title: string;
  /** The heading over the content. Defaults to the title. */
  heading?: string;
  /** Icon on the current breadcrumb item. */
  icon?: IconComponent;
  /** Header actions on the right; the Pro dashboard's set by default, `null` for none. */
  actions?: ReactNode;
  children: ReactNode;
  className?: string;
  /** Overrides the 1300px content column, e.g. `max-w-[964px]` for the catalogue's grids. */
  columnClassName?: string;
}) {
  const localize = useTemplateCopy();
  const [navOpen, setNavOpen] = useState(false);
  const items = starterNav(useStarterBase());
  const selected = useStarterSelected();

  return localize((
    <div
      className={cx(
        "relative flex h-dvh w-full gap-4 overflow-hidden bg-background-full p-3",
        className,
      )}
    >
      <DashboardSidebar items={items} selected={selected} className="hidden lg:flex" />

      {/* Below lg the sidebar rides in as an overlay drawer. */}
      {navOpen && (
        <div className="fixed inset-0 z-50 flex lg:hidden">
          <button
            type="button"
            aria-label="Close navigation"
            onClick={() => setNavOpen(false)}
            className="absolute inset-0 cursor-pointer bg-black/40"
          />
          <div className="relative flex h-full p-3">
            <DashboardSidebar
              mobile
              items={items}
              selected={selected}
              onClose={() => setNavOpen(false)}
              className="flex"
            />
          </div>
        </div>
      )}

      <main className="relative flex min-h-0 min-w-0 flex-1 justify-center overflow-x-hidden overflow-y-auto bg-background-full sm:pt-3">
        <div className={cx("flex w-full max-w-[1300px] flex-col gap-2.5", columnClassName)}>
          <header className="flex w-full flex-col gap-2">
            <Breadcrumb>
              <BreadcrumbItem href="#">
                <Avatar size="xs" color="blue" initials="A" />
                Acme team
              </BreadcrumbItem>
              <BreadcrumbItem href="#">
                <Avatar size="xs" color="neutral" initials="J" />
                Jordan
              </BreadcrumbItem>
              <BreadcrumbItem current icon={Icon}>
                {title}
              </BreadcrumbItem>
            </Breadcrumb>
            <div className="flex w-full flex-wrap items-end justify-between gap-2">
              <div className="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-1.5">
                <IconButton
                  icon={navOpen ? RiCloseLine : RiMenuLine}
                  size="medium"
                  aria-label="Open navigation"
                  onClick={() => setNavOpen((open) => !open)}
                  className="lg:hidden"
                />
                <h1 className="px-1 text-title-2-medium whitespace-nowrap text-text-primary">
                  {heading}
                </h1>
              </div>
              <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-end gap-2.5">
                {actions !== undefined ? actions : (
                  <>
                    <NotificationBell />
                    <Button variant="secondary" size="medium" leadingIcon={RiFilter3Fill}>
                      Filters
                    </Button>
                    <Button variant="primary" size="medium" leadingIcon={RiAddFill}>
                      Create ticket
                    </Button>
                  </>
                )}
              </div>
            </div>
          </header>
          <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-4 pb-4">{children}</div>
        </div>
      </main>
    </div>
  ));
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The bell's capture-phase outside-press listener exists only while its popover is open and is removed on close or unmount. The shell holds only `navOpen` state; nothing else to release.

**Reduced motion.** The shell itself has no motion: the phone drawer appears and disappears without a transition. Motion inside it (the notification center, buttons) follows those components' own reduced-motion rules.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not configure the base path in two places. It is read off the URL (or pinned with `StarterBaseContext` by a host whose path has no prefix), so the sidebar never links to a page the app lacks.
- Do not let the whole frame scroll. The outer row is `h-dvh overflow-hidden` and only `<main>` scrolls, so the sidebar stays put.
- Do not make the bell popover modal to get outside dismissal; it is `isNonModal` and closed by `useDismissOnOutsidePress`, so opening it does not lock page scroll.
- Do not pass `actions={undefined}` expecting no actions. `undefined` means "use the defaults"; pass `null` to render none.

## Notes

- `STARTER_NOTIFICATIONS` is the sample inbox: five items over Today and Yesterday, three unread, matching the sidebar badge and the bell. `STARTER_UNREAD_COUNT` is derived from it.
- The shell's sample breadcrumb (Acme team, Jordan) is fixed copy; real apps replace it with their own trail.

## Definition of done

At 1280px wide the sidebar sits on the left with "Dashboard" selected, and the main column shows the breadcrumb, the heading and the bell, Filters and Create ticket buttons. The bell shows a red 3; pressing it opens the notification list below it, and pressing outside closes it. Only the main column scrolls. Below 1024px the sidebar is gone and a menu button beside the heading opens it as an overlay drawer; pressing the dimmed backdrop closes it.

# Build: Appointments List Card

A patient's upcoming appointments in the medical profile's grey card: a label, a big count of visits that are not cancelled, then one white tile per visit with a month/day/weekday chip, the visit type, its time window and mode, the doctor's initials and a status chip. Reschedule opens a menu of open slots and moves the visit, Cancel strikes it through and swaps the actions for an Undo that restores the status it had.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Upcoming visits as inner tiles: date chip, time window, mode, doctor initials and status, with reschedule slots, cancel and undo.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @internationalized/date@^3.12.4, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The list is controlled (`appointments`) or uncontrolled (`defaultAppointments`); every change goes through `commit`, which updates internal state only when uncontrolled and always calls `onAppointmentsChange` with the whole list. Tiles render sorted by the `date`T`time` string, so a moved visit slides to its new place.
2. Dates are parsed with `parseDate` / `parseDateTime` from @internationalized/date and printed with `DateFormatter` in the `locale` (en-US by default) on `toDate("UTC")` with `timeZone: "UTC"`, so the chip and the "9:30 AM – 10:00 AM" window never shift with the viewer's timezone. The end time adds `durationMinutes` (default 30) with `.add({ minutes })`.
3. Reschedule is a kit `Dropdown` whose open state is held per card (`openMenu` = the visit id), because `DropdownItem` does not close the menu itself. Its items come from `getSlots`, which defaults to `defaultSlots`: the next three weekdays after the visit (`getDayOfWeek` skips Saturday and Sunday) at the same time, 14:30 and 10:00. Picking one patches `date`, `time` and `status: "rescheduled"`, closes the menu and calls `onReschedule`.
4. Cancel stores the current status in `previousStatus` keyed by id, then sets `status: "cancelled"`; the tile dims to 60% with a line-through and shows Undo, which restores the stored status (or "confirmed") and calls `onRestore`.
5. The count and the date chip are keyed by their value (`active` count, `date`T`time`), so the kit `animate-number-fade` keyframe replays when a visit is cancelled, restored or moved. A visually hidden `aria-live="polite"` line announces each change.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `default duration = 30 minutes`
  Most outpatient visits; the end of the time window is start + durationMinutes.
- `default slots = next 3 weekdays at same time, 14:30, 10:00`
  Gives a morning and an afternoon option without a scheduling backend.
- `cancelled opacity = 60%`
  Keeps the cancelled visit readable for the Undo while clearly out of the schedule.
- `date chip width = 48px`
  Fits a three-letter month, a two-digit day and a weekday at caption size.

## API

```ts
export function AppointmentsListCard({ appointments, defaultAppointments = [], onAppointmentsChange, onReschedule, onCancel, onRestore, getSlots = defaultSlots, title = "Upcoming appointments", countLabel = "scheduled", locale = "en-US", className }: AppointmentsListCardProps): JSX.Element
```

- `appointments: Appointment[]`
  Controlled list of visits.
- `defaultAppointments: Appointment[]` — default `[]`
  Initial list when uncontrolled.
- `onAppointmentsChange: (appointments: Appointment[]) => void`
  Called with the whole list after a reschedule, cancel or undo.
- `onReschedule: (appointment: Appointment, slot: AppointmentSlot) => void`
  Called when a slot is picked, with the visit before the move.
- `onCancel: (appointment: Appointment) => void`
  Called when a visit is cancelled.
- `onRestore: (appointment: Appointment) => void`
  Called when Undo restores a cancelled visit.
- `getSlots: (appointment: Appointment) => AppointmentSlot[]` — default `defaultSlots`
  Open slots offered in the Reschedule menu.
- `title: string` — default `"Upcoming appointments"`
  Card label and accessible name.
- `countLabel: string` — default `"scheduled"`
  Words after the count of visits that are not cancelled.
- `locale: string` — default `"en-US"`
  Locale for month, weekday and time formatting.
- `className: string`
  Classes on the card.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function AppointmentsListCard({
  appointments,
  defaultAppointments = [],
  onAppointmentsChange,
  onReschedule,
  onCancel,
  onRestore,
  getSlots = defaultSlots,
  title = "Upcoming appointments",
  countLabel = "scheduled",
  locale = "en-US",
  className,
}: AppointmentsListCardProps) {
  const [inner, setInner] = useState<Appointment[]>(defaultAppointments);
  const [previousStatus, setPreviousStatus] = useState<Record<string, AppointmentStatus>>({});
  const [openMenu, setOpenMenu] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [announcement, setAnnouncement] = useState("");

  const list = appointments ?? inner;
  const sorted = [...list].sort(byStart);
  const active = list.filter((a) => a.status !== "cancelled").length;
  const f = makeFormatters(locale);

  const toDate = (date: string) => parseDate(date).toDate("UTC");
  const toTime = (date: string, time: string, minutes = 0) =>
    f.time.format(parseDateTime(`${date}T${time}`).add({ minutes }).toDate("UTC"));
  const slotLabel = (slot: AppointmentSlot) => `${f.slotDay.format(toDate(slot.date))} · ${toTime(slot.date, slot.time)}`;

  const commit = (next: Appointment[]) => {
    if (appointments === undefined) setInner(next);
    onAppointmentsChange?.(next);
  };
  const patch = (id: string, change: Partial<Appointment>) =>
    commit(list.map((a) => (a.id === id ? { ...a, ...change } : a)));

  const reschedule = (appointment: Appointment, slot: AppointmentSlot) => {
    patch(appointment.id, { ...slot, status: "rescheduled" });
    setOpenMenu(null);
    setAnnouncement(`${appointment.type} moved to ${slotLabel(slot)}`);
    onReschedule?.(appointment, slot);
  };

  const cancel = (appointment: Appointment) => {
    setPreviousStatus((prev) => ({ ...prev, [appointment.id]: appointment.status }));
    patch(appointment.id, { status: "cancelled" });
    setAnnouncement(`${appointment.type} cancelled`);
    onCancel?.(appointment);
  };

  const restore = (appointment: Appointment) => {
    const status = previousStatus[appointment.id] ?? "confirmed";
    patch(appointment.id, { status });
    setAnnouncement(`${appointment.type} restored`);
    onRestore?.(appointment);
  };

  return (
    <section
      aria-label={title}
      className={cx(
        "flex w-full min-w-0 flex-col gap-3 rounded-[20px] bg-background-secondary-default px-2.5 pt-4 pb-2.5",
        className,
      )}
    >
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-0.5 px-1.5">
        <h3 className="text-body-medium text-text-secondary">{title}</h3>
        <p className="flex items-baseline gap-1.5">
          <span
            key={active}
            className="animate-number-fade text-title-1-medium text-text-primary tabular-nums motion-reduce:animate-none"
            data-appointments-count=""
          >
            {active}
          </span>
          <span className="text-body-2-medium text-text-secondary">{countLabel}</span>
        </p>
      </div>

      {sorted.length === 0 ? (
        <p className="rounded-2lg bg-background-inner-default px-3 py-6 text-center text-body-regular text-text-secondary">
          No upcoming appointments
        </p>
      ) : (
        <ul aria-label={title} className="flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-2 overflow-y-auto">
          {sorted.map((a) => {
            const cancelled = a.status === "cancelled";
            const day = toDate(a.date);
            const mode = a.mode ? MODE[a.mode] : undefined;
            const status = STATUS[a.status];
            return (
              <li
                key={a.id}
                data-appointment={a.id}
                className="flex gap-3 rounded-2lg bg-background-inner-default p-2.5"
              >
                <div
                  key={startOf(a)}
                  aria-hidden
                  className={cx(
                    "flex w-12 shrink-0 animate-number-fade flex-col items-center justify-center self-start rounded-lg bg-background-secondary-default py-1.5 motion-reduce:animate-none",
                    cancelled && "opacity-60",
                  )}
                >
                  <span className="text-caption-2-semibold text-text-secondary uppercase">{f.month.format(day)}</span>
                  <span className={cx("text-title-2-medium text-text-primary tabular-nums", cancelled && "line-through")}>
                    {parseDate(a.date).day}
                  </span>
                  <span className="text-caption-2-medium text-text-tertiary">{f.weekday.format(day)}</span>
                </div>

                <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-2">
                  <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-2">
                    <div className={cx("flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-0.5", cancelled && "opacity-60")}>
                      <p className={cx("line-clamp-2 text-body-medium break-words text-text-primary", cancelled && "line-through")}>
                        {a.type}
                      </p>
                      <p className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-1.5 gap-y-0.5 text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary">
                        <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1 whitespace-nowrap tabular-nums" data-appointment-time="">
                          <RiTimeLine className="size-3.5 shrink-0" aria-hidden />
                          <span className="sr-only">{f.slotDay.format(day)}, </span>
                          {toTime(a.date, a.time)} – {toTime(a.date, a.time, a.durationMinutes ?? 30)}
                        </span>
                        {mode ? (
                          <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1">
                            <mode.icon className="size-3.5 shrink-0" aria-hidden />
                            {mode.label}
                          </span>
                        ) : null}
                      </p>
                    </div>
                    <Chip variant="caption" color={status.color} className="shrink-0" data-appointment-status="">
                      {status.label}
                    </Chip>
                  </div>

                  <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-2">
                    <span className={cx("flex min-w-0 items-center gap-1.5", cancelled && "opacity-60")}>
                      <Avatar size="sm" color={a.doctorColor} initials={a.doctorInitials ?? initialsOf(a.doctor)} aria-hidden />
                      <span className="truncate text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary">{a.doctor}</span>
                    </span>
                    <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center gap-1">
                      {cancelled ? (
                        <Button
                          variant="secondary"
                          size="xs"
                          leadingIcon={RiArrowGoBackLine}
                          aria-label={`Undo cancel ${a.type}`}
                          onClick={() => restore(a)}
                        >
                          Undo
                        </Button>
                      ) : (
                        <>
                          <Dropdown
                            isOpen={openMenu === a.id}
                            onOpenChange={(open) => setOpenMenu(open ? a.id : null)}
                          >
                            <DropdownTrigger
                              aria-label={`Reschedule ${a.type}`}
                              className={cx(
                                buttonStyles.base,
                                buttonStyles.size.xs,
                                buttonStyles.variant.ghost,
                                "gap-1",
                              )}
                            >
                              <RiCalendarScheduleLine className="size-3.5 shrink-0" aria-hidden />
                              Reschedule
                            </DropdownTrigger>
                            <DropdownPopover
                              aria-label={`New time for ${a.type}`}
                              placement="bottom end"
                              className="w-[232px]"
                            >
                              <DropdownGroup label="Open slots">
                                {getSlots(a).map((slot) => (
                                  <DropdownItem
                                    key={startOf(slot)}
                                    className="px-2 py-1.5 tabular-nums"
                                    onSelect={() => reschedule(a, slot)}
                                  >
                                    <RiCalendarScheduleLine className="size-4 shrink-0 text-text-secondary" aria-hidden />
                                    <span className="text-body-medium text-text-primary">{slotLabel(slot)}</span>
                                  </DropdownItem>
                                ))}
                              </DropdownGroup>
                            </DropdownPopover>
                          </Dropdown>
                          <Button
                            variant="secondary"
                            size="xs"
                            leadingIcon={RiCloseLine}
                            aria-label={`Cancel ${a.type}`}
                            onClick={() => cancel(a)}
                          >
                            Cancel
                          </Button>
                        </>
                      )}
                    </div>
                  </div>
                </div>
              </li>
            );
          })}
        </ul>
      )}
      <p className="sr-only" aria-live="polite">
        {announcement}
      </p>
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers, listeners or observers of its own; the kit Dropdown removes its outside-press listener when it closes.

**Reduced motion.** The count and date chip fades use motion-reduce:animate-none, so values swap instantly.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not format a `CalendarDate` through the viewer's local timezone: convert with `toDate("UTC")` and format with `timeZone: "UTC"`, or the chip can show the previous day west of UTC.
- Do not leave the Reschedule menu uncontrolled: kit `DropdownItem` only runs `onSelect`, so the menu would stay open over the moved tile.
- Do not key the tile by its date: the `li` keeps the id as key so focus and the menu survive a re-sort, and only the date chip is keyed by start time to replay the fade.

## Notes

- Status colours: confirmed lime, pending yellow, rescheduled blue, cancelled rose (kit `Chip` caption variant).
- Mode icons are Remix `RiHospitalLine` (in person), `RiVideoChatLine` (video call) and `RiPhoneLine` (phone).
- The tile list is a flex-1 `overflow-y-auto` column, so a `max-h-*` class on the card keeps it to a fixed height and scrolls the visits (the demo uses max-h-[500px]).
- Doctor initials come from `doctorInitials` or the first letters of the first two words after a "Dr." prefix.

## Definition of done

Picking a slot in a Reschedule menu closes it, moves the visit to that date and time with a blue Rescheduled chip; Cancel shows a rose Cancelled chip, lowers the count by one and offers Undo, which restores the previous status.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Area Chart Card

A grey dashboard card that charts monthly visitors by channel as gradient-filled Recharts areas, stacked by default. The header shows the period total with its change against the period before and a This year / Last year switch that swaps the whole data set. Hovering a month draws a dashed cursor, a pinging dot on each area and a tooltip with the split, while the headline counts to that month and the tiles under the chart show its per-channel values.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A dashboard card of stacked gradient areas with a period switch, a hover tooltip and tiles that follow the hovered month.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: recharts@^3.10.1

## How it works

1. Each series is an `Area` with a 2px stroke in its tone's `-active` colour and a fill of `url(#<id>-<key>)`: a vertical `linearGradient` in the chart `<defs>` from `--color-chart-N` at 0.55 opacity to 0.05. Ids are `useId()` plus the series key, so cards never share gradients.
2. `view` decides stacking. `stacked` gives every Area `stackId="total"`; `overlap` gives none, so each area starts at zero; `percent` keeps the stack and sets `stackOffset="expand"` on the chart, with the Y axis fixed to `[0, 1]` and ticks formatted as whole percents.
3. `onMouseMove` stores `state.activeTooltipIndex` in `hovered` when `isTooltipActive` is true and the index is finite, and `onMouseLeave` clears it. With a month hovered the headline is that month's sum across series against the month before (no chip for the first month); otherwise it is the period total against `previousTotal`.
4. The `Tooltip` keeps a dashed `--color-chart-cursor` cursor and renders `ChartTooltipCard` from `activeIndex` (mapped from `null` to -1 first): the month and its total, then one row per series from the top of the stack down, with each share in brackets in percent view.
5. Every Area's `activeDot` is the shared `PulseDot`, so each stacked band gets a ringed dot with a ping behind it at its own height.
6. `ChartStatTiles` lists the series under the chart with square colour keys. Each tile shows the hovered month's value or, with nothing hovered, the series total, so the tiles double as the legend.
7. Choosing a period clears `hovered`, updates internal state only when `period` is uncontrolled, and calls `onPeriodChange`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `area gradient = chart-N at stopOpacity 0.55 → 0.05`
  Stacked bands need more tint than a single area to stay distinct where they meet; keeping 0.05 at the bottom stops lower bands from looking empty.
- `plot height = 248px`
  The card height follows its content (header, plot, tiles). A fixed plot box gives `ResponsiveContainer` a real height without fixing the whole card.
- `axes = YAxis width 44, tickCount 4 (5 in percent view), XAxis preserveStartEnd, minTickGap 8`
  44px fits "13.5K" at 12px. The minimum gap lets Recharts drop month labels on phones instead of overlapping them.
- `tile columns = 3 series: grid-cols-2, grid-cols-3 from a 384px card (@sm); 2 series: grid-cols-2`
  Three tiles fit side by side at preview width; on narrow cards the third wraps instead of truncating the numbers.
- `motion = areas 450ms, tooltip 160ms, count-up 320ms, number-fade 220ms`
  Short enough to follow a pointer across twelve months; all of it is off under reduced motion.

## API

```ts
function AreaChartCard(props?: AreaChartCardProps): JSX.Element
type AreaChartCardProps = { title?: string; series?: AreaSeries[]; periods?: AreaPeriod[]; period?: string; defaultPeriod?: string; onPeriodChange?: (id: string) => void; view?: "stacked" | "overlap" | "percent"; shape?: "curved" | "sharp"; periodControl?: "segmented" | "select"; className?: string }
type AreaSeries = { key: string; label: string; tone: ChartTone }
type AreaPeriod = { id: string; label: string; data: AreaPoint[]; previousTotal?: number }
```

- `title: string` — default `"Visitors"`
  Header label; while hovering it becomes "Visitors · <month>".
- `series: AreaSeries[]` — default `AREA_SERIES`
  Categories from the bottom of the stack up; also the tile order.
- `periods: AreaPeriod[]` — default `AREA_PERIODS`
  Data sets the switch moves between; `previousTotal` feeds the headline chip.
- `period: string`
  Controlled period id.
- `defaultPeriod: string` — default `first period id`
  Initial period when uncontrolled.
- `onPeriodChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called with the chosen period id.
- `view: "stacked" | "overlap" | "percent"` — default `"stacked"`
  Stack the areas, draw each from zero, or stretch each month to 100%.
- `shape: "curved" | "sharp"` — default `"curved"`
  Monotone curves or straight segments.
- `periodControl: "segmented" | "select"` — default `"segmented"`
  Segmented switch, or a calendar pill that opens a listbox.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function AreaChartCard({
  title = "Visitors",
  series = AREA_SERIES,
  periods = AREA_PERIODS,
  period,
  defaultPeriod,
  onPeriodChange,
  view = "stacked",
  shape = "curved",
  periodControl = "segmented",
  className,
}: AreaChartCardProps = {}) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const gradientBase = useId();
  const [innerPeriod, setInnerPeriod] = useState(defaultPeriod ?? periods[0]?.id ?? "");
  const periodId = period ?? innerPeriod;
  const active = periods.find((p) => p.id === periodId) ?? periods[0];
  const data = active?.data ?? [];
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState<number | null>(null);

  const point = hovered !== null ? data[hovered] : undefined;
  const sumOf = (p: AreaPoint | undefined) => series.reduce((sum, s) => sum + valueAt(p, s.key), 0);
  const totals = series.map((s) => data.reduce((sum, p) => sum + valueAt(p, s.key), 0));
  const grandTotal = totals.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);

  const headline = point ? sumOf(point) : grandTotal;
  const delta = point
    ? hovered !== null && hovered > 0
      ? describeDelta(headline, sumOf(data[hovered - 1]))
      : null
    : describeDelta(grandTotal, active?.previousTotal);
  const curve = shape === "sharp" ? "linear" : "monotone";
  const percent = view === "percent";

  const selectPeriod = (id: string) => {
    setHovered(null);
    if (period === undefined) setInnerPeriod(id);
    onPeriodChange?.(id);
  };

  return (
    <section aria-label={`${title} chart`} className={cx(CHART_CARD_FRAME, "gap-3", className)}>
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 px-2 pt-2 @md:flex-row @md:items-start @md:justify-between">
        <ChartHeadline
          label={point ? `${title} · ${point.label}` : title}
          value={headline}
          delta={delta}
          swapKey={`${periodId}-${hovered ?? "total"}`}
          reducedMotion={reduced}
        />
        {periods.length > 1 ? (
          <ChartPeriodControl
            options={periods}
            value={periodId}
            onChange={selectPeriod}
            variant={periodControl}
            label={`${title} period`}
            className="self-start"
          />
        ) : null}
      </div>

      <div className="h-[248px] w-full pe-2">
        <ResponsiveContainer width="100%" height="100%" initialDimension={{ width: 520, height: 248 }}>
          <ComposedChart
            data={data}
            stackOffset={percent ? "expand" : "none"}
            margin={{ top: 8, right: 8, bottom: 0, left: 0 }}
            onMouseMove={(state) => {
              const next = Number(state?.activeTooltipIndex);
              if (state?.isTooltipActive && Number.isFinite(next)) setHovered(next);
            }}
            onMouseLeave={() => setHovered(null)}
          >
            <defs>
              {series.map((s) => (
                <linearGradient key={s.key} id={`${gradientBase}-${s.key}`} x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
                  <stop offset="0%" stopColor={toneColor(s.tone)} stopOpacity={0.55} />
                  <stop offset="100%" stopColor={toneColor(s.tone)} stopOpacity={0.05} />
                </linearGradient>
              ))}
            </defs>
            <CartesianGrid vertical={false} stroke={GRID_STROKE} strokeDasharray="4 4" />
            <YAxis
              width={44}
              domain={percent ? [0, 1] : [0, "auto"]}
              tickCount={percent ? 5 : 4}
              tickFormatter={(v: number) => (percent ? `${Math.round(v * 100)}%` : formatCompact(v))}
              tickLine={false}
              axisLine={false}
              tick={AXIS_TICK}
            />
            <XAxis
              dataKey="label"
              tickLine={false}
              axisLine={false}
              tickMargin={10}
              interval="preserveStartEnd"
              minTickGap={8}
              tick={AXIS_TICK}
            />
            <Tooltip
              cursor={CHART_CURSOR}
              offset={16}
              isAnimationActive={!reduced}
              animationDuration={160}
              wrapperStyle={{ outline: "none", zIndex: 10 }}
              content={({ active: isActive, activeIndex }) => {
                const at = data[activeIndex == null ? -1 : Number(activeIndex)];
                if (!isActive || !at) return null;
                const total = sumOf(at);
                return (
                  <ChartTooltipCard
                    title={`${at.label} · ${formatNumber(total)} total`}
                    rows={[...series].reverse().map((s) => {
                      const v = valueAt(at, s.key);
                      const share = total > 0 ? ` (${Math.round((v / total) * 100)}%)` : "";
                      return { key: s.key, label: s.label, tone: s.tone, value: `${formatNumber(v)}${percent ? share : ""}` };
                    })}
                  />
                );
              }}
            />
            {series.map((s) => (
              <Area
                key={s.key}
                type={curve}
                dataKey={s.key}
                name={s.label}
                stackId={view === "overlap" ? undefined : "total"}
                stroke={toneActiveColor(s.tone)}
                strokeWidth={2}
                fill={`url(#${gradientBase}-${s.key})`}
                activeDot={<PulseDot color={toneActiveColor(s.tone)} pulse={!reduced} />}
                isAnimationActive={!reduced}
                animationDuration={450}
              />
            ))}
          </ComposedChart>
        </ResponsiveContainer>
      </div>

      <ChartStatTiles
        columns={series.length === 2 ? 2 : "3-wrap"}
        tiles={series.map((s, i) => ({
          key: s.key,
          label: s.label,
          tone: s.tone,
          value: formatNumber(point ? valueAt(point, s.key) : (totals[i] ?? 0)),
        }))}
      />
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `useCountUp` cancels its animation frame on target change and unmount, `useReducedMotion` unsubscribes its media-query listener, and `ResponsiveContainer` disconnects its resize observer. The card adds no listeners or timers of its own.

**Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `useReducedMotion` turns off `isAnimationActive` on the Areas and the Tooltip, the headline shows its value without counting, the number fade is `motion-reduce:animate-none`, and the active dots drop their ping circle.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Sharing one gradient id across series. Each series needs its own `<linearGradient>` id, and ids must be unique per card; the id is `useId()` plus the series key.
- Using a Y domain of `[0, "auto"]` in percent view. With `stackOffset="expand"` the stacked values run 0 to 1, so the domain is pinned to `[0, 1]` and ticks are multiplied by 100.
- Comparing the hovered month with `undefined` for January. The first month has no month before it, so the chip is hidden rather than showing "New".
- Reading `activeIndex` with `Number()` directly. Recharts passes `null` when inactive and `Number(null)` is 0, which would pin the tooltip to January.

## Notes

- `AREA_SERIES`, `AREA_PERIODS` and the `AreaSeries`, `AreaPoint`, `AreaPeriod` and `AreaChartView` types are exported. This year adds up to 94,700 (Organic 50,500, Referral 25,900, Paid 18,300) against 87,520, shown as "+8.2%"; last year is 87,520 against 80,940, "+8.1%".
- The frame, headline, period switch, tooltip card, tiles and pulse dot come from `line-chart-card-parts.tsx`, so this card matches the line chart card beside it.
- BoardUI's preview shows the period as a calendar pill; `periodControl="select"` gives that pill and the default is a segmented switch.

## Definition of done

The card shows "Visitors", "94,700" and a lime "+8.2%" chip with This year selected, three stacked lime, blue and purple gradient areas over dashed rules, and tiles Organic 50,500, Referral 25,900, Paid 18,300. Hovering a month shows a tooltip with its total and each channel, a dot on every band, and the headline and tiles switch to that month. Choosing Last year shows "87,520" and "+8.1%".

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Asymmetric In/Out Staggers

A list whose entrance and exit are deliberately different animations. In: 24px up, 0.5s each, 0.06s apart, after a 0.25s hold that lets the outgoing view clear. Out: 16px up, 0.3s each, 0.03s apart, running from the last item back to the first. The exit is roughly half the total time of the entrance, which is what makes a view swap feel responsive without making the arrival feel rushed.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A list that arrives item by item after a hold and leaves twice as fast, from the last row backwards.

- Category: transition
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. Every direct child is wrapped in a `[data-stagger-item]` div, so the caller writes ordinary list markup and the component owns the animated node — no cloneElement, no required ref forwarding.
2. Entering runs `gsap.fromTo(items, { autoAlpha: 0, y: 24 }, { autoAlpha: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.out", stagger: 0.06, delay: 0.25 })`. The delay is not decoration: it is the window in which whatever this list replaces finishes leaving.
3. Leaving runs `gsap.to(items, { autoAlpha: 0, y: -16, duration: 0.3, ease: "power2.in", stagger: { each: 0.03, from: "end" } })`. Halving the stagger and reversing its origin is what stops the exit from reading as the entrance rewound.
4. `autoAlpha` rather than `opacity`: at zero it also writes `visibility: hidden`, so a faded row cannot swallow a click aimed at the view underneath it.
5. Both tweens carry `overwrite: "auto"`, and the whole thing lives in a `useGsap` context keyed on `show`, so toggling twice in quick succession cancels the in-flight direction instead of layering two opposing tweens on the same nodes.
6. A layout effect hides the items before first paint when the component mounts closed, and an internal `hasShown` flag makes sure `onExited` can only fire after a real entrance.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `inStagger = 0.06`
  Seconds between arriving items. Below ~0.04 a five-item list reads as one block; above ~0.1 the last row lands well after the eye has moved on and the list feels slow to load.
- `outStagger = 0.03`
  Half the entrance value. Exits are acknowledgement, not presentation — the wave still reads as a direction, but the whole list is gone in under 200ms.
- `inDelay = 0.25`
  Seconds of hold before the first item arrives. Sized to the outgoing view's own fade (~0.3-0.4s) so the two never overlap; at 0 both views are half-opaque at the same time and the frame looks like a rendering bug.
- `inDuration / outDuration = 0.5 / 0.3`
  Per-item. The exit is shorter for the same reason its stagger is: nobody is reading rows that are leaving.
- `inDistance / outDistance = 24 / 16`
  Pixels. The entrance comes up from below (from where the content is arriving); the exit continues upward and travels less, because a long exit path is time spent watching nothing.
- `stagger.from = 'end'`
  Reverses the exit wave. Same-direction staggers make the exit look like a backwards entrance; from the end it looks like the list is being pulled off the screen.

## API

```ts
function AsymmetricStagger(props: { children: ReactNode; show: boolean; inStagger?: number; outStagger?: number; inDelay?: number; inDuration?: number; outDuration?: number; inDistance?: number; outDistance?: number; onExited?: () => void; className?: string; itemClassName?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  List items. Each direct child is wrapped and animated on its own.
- `show: boolean`
  True enters, false exits. The component stays mounted through both.
- `inStagger: number` — default `0.06`
  Seconds between entering items.
- `outStagger: number` — default `0.03`
  Seconds between leaving items.
- `inDelay: number` — default `0.25`
  Hold before the entrance, sized to the outgoing view.
- `inDuration: number` — default `0.5`
  Per-item entrance length in seconds.
- `outDuration: number` — default `0.3`
  Per-item exit length in seconds.
- `inDistance: number` — default `24`
  Pixels travelled on the way in.
- `outDistance: number` — default `16`
  Pixels travelled on the way out.
- `onExited: () => void`
  Called once the last item has left. Safe place to unmount the data.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the flex column wrapper.
- `itemClassName: string`
  Merged onto every generated item wrapper.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function AsymmetricStagger({
  children,
  show,
  inStagger = 0.06,
  outStagger = 0.03,
  inDelay = 0.25,
  inDuration = 0.5,
  outDuration = 0.3,
  inDistance = 24,
  outDistance = 16,
  onExited,
  className,
  itemClassName,
}: AsymmetricStaggerProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  const exited = useRef(onExited);
  exited.current = onExited;

  const startedHidden = useRef(!show);
  /* An exit only makes sense after an entrance. Without this, mounting with
     `show={false}` plays an invisible exit and fires `onExited` — and under
     StrictMode the double-invoked effect fires it a second time. */
  const hasShown = useRef(show);
  /* One exit per hide. `reduced` is in the effect's dep list because the OS
     setting is live, so flipping it while the list is already hidden re-entered
     the exit branch and fired `onExited` a second time — at which point a
     parent that unmounts its data on that callback unmounts it twice. */
  const exitPlayed = useRef(false);

  // Before paint, not after. A passive effect can land on the far side of the
  // first frame, so a list that starts closed would flash its items once.
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = root.current;
    if (!el || !startedHidden.current) return;
    gsap.set(el.querySelectorAll('[data-stagger-item]'), { autoAlpha: 0 });
  }, []);

  useGsap(
    gsap,
    () => {
      const el = root.current;
      if (!el) return;
      const items = Array.from(el.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-stagger-item]'));
      if (items.length === 0) return;

      if (!show && !hasShown.current) return;

      // Re-entering the exit branch for a list that has already gone. The
      // `revert()` this hook runs before every re-execution has just undone the
      // exit tween's styles, so the list is visible again and has to be put
      // back — but it must not animate and must not report a second exit.
      if (!show && exitPlayed.current) {
        gsap.set(items, { autoAlpha: 0 });
        return;
      }

      if (reduced) {
        // No travel and no stagger, but the state change still has to happen
        // or the list is stuck in whichever position it was left in.
        gsap.set(items, { autoAlpha: show ? 1 : 0, y: 0 });
        if (show) {
          hasShown.current = true;
          exitPlayed.current = false;
        } else {
          exitPlayed.current = true;
          exited.current?.();
        }
        return;
      }

      if (show) {
        hasShown.current = true;
        exitPlayed.current = false;
        // autoAlpha, not opacity: at 0 it also sets visibility:hidden, so a
        // faded-out row cannot still swallow a click meant for what is
        // underneath it.
        gsap.fromTo(
          items,
          { autoAlpha: 0, y: inDistance },
          {
            autoAlpha: 1,
            y: 0,
            duration: inDuration,
            ease: 'power2.out',
            stagger: inStagger,
            delay: inDelay,
            overwrite: 'auto',
          },
        );
        return;
      }

      exitPlayed.current = true;
      // `fromTo`, not `to`, and the start state is stated rather than read off
      // the element. This hook reverts its context before every re-run, and
      // revert restores the inline styles that were on the node BEFORE the
      // entrance tween — which, for a list that mounted with `show={false}`,
      // are the `visibility: hidden; opacity: 0` written by the pre-paint set
      // above. A `to()` therefore tweened a list that was already invisible:
      // it vanished on the frame the hide was requested and `onExited` still
      // arrived `outDuration` later. Reaching here at all means the entrance
      // has run, so fully visible is the honest place to leave from.
      gsap.fromTo(
        items,
        { autoAlpha: 1, y: 0 },
        {
          autoAlpha: 0,
          y: -outDistance,
          duration: outDuration,
          ease: 'power2.in',
          // `from: 'end'` reverses the wave. Same-direction staggers on the way
          // out read as the list re-entering backwards.
          stagger: { each: outStagger, from: 'end' },
          overwrite: 'auto',
          onComplete: () => exited.current?.(),
        },
      );
    },
    root,
    [show, reduced],
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `useGsap` reverts the context on unmount and on every `show` change, killing both tweens and restoring the inline styles GSAP wrote. `onExited` is held in a ref so a completion callback cannot reach a stale closure after the parent has re-rendered.

**Reduced motion.** No travel and no stagger. Items are set to their visible or hidden state in one `gsap.set`, and `onExited` still fires, so the surrounding state machine behaves identically — only the choreography is dropped.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Reusing the entrance timeline with `reverse()`. That gives you power2.out played backwards (so it decelerates into nothing), the entrance delay stranded at the end, and the same stagger direction — three separate reasons the exit feels heavy.
- Unmounting the list when `show` flips false. React removes the nodes on the same frame, so the exit never runs; the component stays mounted and reports completion through `onExited`.
- Animating `opacity` alone. A finished row sits at opacity 0 with full hit area and eats clicks intended for the view underneath. `autoAlpha` writes `visibility: hidden` at zero.
- Omitting `overwrite: "auto"`. Toggling twice inside 300ms leaves the entrance tween running under the exit tween, and the rows settle at whatever opacity the two happen to agree on.
- Setting the initial hidden state in a passive effect. Mounting with `show={false}` paints the list once, then hides it — a visible flash of content that was never meant to be seen. It is set in `useLayoutEffect` instead.
- Firing `onExited` on mount. With `show={false}` at mount there is nothing to exit, and under StrictMode the double-invoked effect would call it twice; a `hasShown` flag gates it.

## Notes

- The same numbers apply outside lists — modals, drawers, route content. Any pair of entrance/exit values that are equal is worth questioning.
- App Router wiring: drive `show` from a pathname comparison in a layout, and do the actual `router.push` from `onExited` if you want the route to change only once the list has gone.

## Definition of done

Switch to the list: the previous view fades, a quarter-second of nothing, then rows arrive top to bottom. Switch back: the bottom row leaves first and the whole list is gone in about half the time it took to arrive. Toggle rapidly and rows never settle at a partial opacity.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
