# Build: Asymmetric Typewriter

A phrase erases itself and a new one is typed in its place, cycling forever. Deleting runs at exactly half the interval of typing, because backspacing is a held key with a mechanical auto-repeat while typing is composition — give both phases the same interval and the result reads as a ticker tape rather than as somebody at a keyboard. A quarter-second pause at the empty string turns the turnaround from a dropped frame into a decision.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Rotating phrases that delete at twice the speed they type, with a beat of nothing at the empty string.

- Category: text
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Timing is a chain of `setTimeout` calls, not a `setInterval`: the four phases (type, hold, delete, empty) each have their own interval, and the boundaries between them are pauses that a fixed interval cannot express without a counter and a modulo.
2. The state machine is four closures over a `text` local — `type` slices one more character off the target and reschedules at `typeMs`; on reaching full length it schedules `beginErase` at `holdMs`. `erase` slices one character off and reschedules at `deleteMs`; at length zero it schedules `advance` at `emptyMs`. `advance` moves the phrase index modulo the list length and re-enters `type`.
3. Typing slices the *target* string (`target.slice(0, text.length + 1)`) rather than concatenating a looked-up character. Under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` an index read is `string | undefined`, and slicing also means the visible text can never desync from the source phrase.
4. A single `timer` ref holds the one outstanding timeout id, so cleanup is a single `clearTimeout` regardless of which phase was in flight.
5. The effect is keyed on `phrases.join("\u0000")` rather than on the array itself. An array prop is a fresh reference every parent render, which would tear the machine down and restart it, pinning the typewriter to its first character forever. NUL is the delimiter because real phrases contain spaces and commas.
6. The caret is the `step-end-caret` component, driven with `paused={busy}`: while characters are being added or removed the caret holds solid, and it resumes blinking only during the hold and empty beats.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `TYPE_MS = 70`
  Milliseconds per character while typing. Around 14 characters a second — brisk human typing. Below ~45ms the reader cannot follow the word forming; above ~110ms the phrase takes longer to appear than anyone will wait for.
- `DELETE_MS = 35`
  Exactly half of `TYPE_MS`. This ratio is the whole component: deleting is a held key on auto-repeat, typing is composition. Equal intervals make both directions read as machine output.
- `HOLD_MS = 1500`
  How long a completed phrase stays up. It has to exceed the time to read four or five words. Under ~900ms the phrase is gone before it has been parsed and the component reads as flickering.
- `EMPTY_MS = 250`
  The beat at zero characters. Without it the string bottoms out and immediately rebounds, which the eye reads as a dropped frame rather than as a turnaround.
- `START_DELAY_MS = 1500`
  Longer than a normal hold, so the first phrase is legible while the rest of the page is still settling. Starting the erase immediately makes the component look like it is correcting a mistake.

## API

```ts
function AsymmetricTypewriter(props: { phrases: string[]; typeMs?: number; deleteMs?: number; holdMs?: number; emptyMs?: number; startDelayMs?: number; caret?: boolean; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `phrases: string[]`
  Cycled in order, forever. Index 0 is also the server-rendered string.
- `typeMs: number` — default `70`
  Milliseconds between characters while typing.
- `deleteMs: number` — default `35`
  Milliseconds between characters while deleting.
- `holdMs: number` — default `1500`
  Milliseconds a completed phrase is held.
- `emptyMs: number` — default `250`
  Milliseconds held at the empty string.
- `startDelayMs: number` — default `1500`
  Milliseconds before the very first deletion.
- `caret: boolean` — default `true`
  Render the blinking caret after the text.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the outer span via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const TYPE_MS = 70;
const DELETE_MS = 35;
const HOLD_MS = 1500;
const EMPTY_MS = 250;
const START_DELAY_MS = 1500;

export function AsymmetricTypewriter({
  phrases,
  typeMs = TYPE_MS,
  deleteMs = DELETE_MS,
  holdMs = HOLD_MS,
  emptyMs = EMPTY_MS,
  startDelayMs = START_DELAY_MS,
  caret = true,
  className,
}: AsymmetricTypewriterProps) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  // An array prop is a fresh reference on every parent render. Keying on the
  // joined string is what stops the effect tearing down and restarting each
  // time — which would pin the typewriter to its first character forever.
  // NUL is the delimiter because real phrases contain spaces and commas, and
  // a separator that occurs in the data silently splits one phrase into two.
  const key = phrases.join('\u0000');
  const list = useMemo(() => key.split('\u0000'), [key]);

  const [shown, setShown] = useState(() => list[0] ?? '');
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const timer = useRef(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    const first = list[0] ?? '';
    if (reduced || list.length < 2) {
      setShown(first);
      setBusy(false);
      return;
    }

    let index = 0;
    let text = first;
    setShown(text);

    const at = (fn: () => void, ms: number) => {
      timer.current = window.setTimeout(fn, ms);
    };

    const erase = () => {
      if (text.length === 0) {
        // The beat. Caret goes back to blinking because nothing is happening.
        setBusy(false);
        at(advance, emptyMs);
        return;
      }
      text = text.slice(0, -1);
      setShown(text);
      at(erase, deleteMs);
    };

    const advance = () => {
      index = (index + 1) % list.length;
      setBusy(true);
      at(type, typeMs);
    };

    const type = () => {
      const target = list[index] ?? '';
      if (text.length >= target.length) {
        setBusy(false);
        at(beginErase, holdMs);
        return;
      }
      // Slice the target rather than concatenating a looked-up character:
      // `target[i]` is `string | undefined` and the slice cannot desync from
      // the source string if the phrase list changes underneath.
      text = target.slice(0, text.length + 1);
      setShown(text);
      at(type, typeMs);
    };

    const beginErase = () => {
      setBusy(true);
      erase();
    };

    at(beginErase, startDelayMs);

    return () => {
      window.clearTimeout(timer.current);
    };
  }, [list, reduced, typeMs, deleteMs, holdMs, emptyMs, startDelayMs]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** A single `window.clearTimeout(timer.current)` in the effect teardown. Only one timeout is ever outstanding, so no phase can survive unmount and call `setState` on a dead component.

**Reduced motion.** The machine never starts. The first phrase is rendered in full and stays — the final text state, immediately, rather than an empty slot or a sped-up cycle. The caret is still rendered but its own reduced-motion rule holds it solid.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Driving the whole cycle from one `setInterval`. Hold and empty pauses then have to be faked with a frame counter, and every change to a phase length becomes an arithmetic edit rather than a constant.
- Depending on the `phrases` array identity in the effect. Every parent render gives a new array, the effect restarts, and the typewriter is stuck showing the first character of the first phrase.
- Joining phrases with a comma or a pipe as the effect key. Both occur in real copy, so one phrase silently becomes two.
- Letting the element size itself from the current string. It grows and shrinks by tens of pixels several times a second and drags every neighbouring element with it — a transparent copy of the longest phrase reserves the box instead.
- Using normal whitespace collapsing. A phrase erased back to "Product " loses its trailing space, so the caret jumps one character left and then right again on the next tick.
- Blinking the caret while characters are being typed. Real cursors hold solid during input; a caret blinking mid-word makes the text look like it is being deleted by something else.

## Notes

- No text-splitting library is involved: the component owns a single string in React state and never mutates the DOM. Adding a split dependency here would buy nothing, since there are no per-character targets to animate.
- React state at ~14 updates a second is a deliberate tradeoff. The subtree is one span, and holding the string in state is what keeps the server-rendered first phrase and the client in agreement.
- A list of fewer than two phrases renders the first one statically and never starts the machine.

## Definition of done

Watch one full cycle: the phrase erases visibly faster than the next one types — time it and the ratio is 2:1. At the empty string there is a perceptible pause before the next phrase starts. The caret holds solid while characters move and blinks while the phrase is held. Nothing to the right of the component moves at any point during the cycle. With reduced motion enabled the first phrase is present on first paint and never changes.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Auth Card

The shell around a sign-in screen. One card covers three steps: `signin` (email, password, remember me, forgot password), `signup` (name, email with a hint, password, terms line) and `verify` (OTP boxes and a resend action). Social providers always sit below the email form, behind an "or continue with" divider, in one of three layouts from the same `providers` array. Passing `media` turns it into an 880px split card with artwork on the right, and `AuthMediaCarousel` is the ready-made option: full-bleed images that shrink into cards and swing away on a drum.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Sign-in, sign-up and code-verify cards with social providers stacked, inline or in a grid, and an optional split layout with artwork.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. `mode` picks a copy set from `COPY` (title, description, CTA and footer line) and which fields render. `verify` swaps the email and password inputs for `InputOtp` (6 digits by default, split into two groups when the length is even), drops the providers, shows a mail icon as the mark and turns the footer link into a resend button.
2. The form is uncontrolled. On submit it calls `preventDefault` and hands `new FormData(form)` to `onSubmit`, with fields named `name`, `email`, `password` and `confirmPassword`, so it can be wired to any auth library.
3. Providers map to `SocialButton`s with the white appearance. `stacked` gives full-width labelled buttons in a column; `inline` gives icon-only squares in a wrapping, centred row; `grid` gives icon-only buttons in `grid-flow-col auto-cols-fr`, stretched with `w-full`, so a small set reads as one row of controls. Icon-only buttons get `aria-label="Continue with <Provider>"`.
4. Without `media` the card is a single 400px column. With it, the card becomes a two-column grid (`md:grid-cols-2`, max 880px) and the media cell is `hidden` below `md`, so a phone gets the form alone instead of a tall image above it. `footnote` renders small print centred below the card, outside its border.
5. `AuthMediaCarousel` runs a four-beat `setTimeout` state machine: `idle` for `interval` (3200ms), `shrink` to `scale(0.82)` with a 24px radius for 450ms plus a 200ms hold, `slide` for 700ms, then a 20ms `enter` frame before growing back to full bleed over 500ms.
6. Each slide is placed by `position = (slideIndex − index + count) % count`. During `slide` the current one moves to `translateX(−100%) translateZ(−220px) rotateY(−48deg)` inside an 850px perspective, while the next one travels from the mirrored spot (`translateX(100%)`, `rotateY(48deg)`) to the centre at `scale(0.8)`. Only the slides moving in a beat get a transition, so a slide wrapping from the left to the back of the queue jumps without streaking. The sign flips in RTL.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `card widths = 400px single, 880px split`
  A sign-in column stays narrow enough to scan; the split halves the wider card between form and art.
- `default providers = ["google", "apple", "github"]`
  Three is a full row in `grid` and a short stack in `stacked`.
- `CARD_SCALE / ENTER_SCALE / CARD_RADIUS = 0.82 / 0.8 / 24px`
  The image visibly detaches into a card before it moves, and the incoming card arrives slightly smaller so the grow reads as a separate beat.
- `PERSPECTIVE / DEPTH / TILT = 850px / 220px / 48deg`
  Cards bank away from the middle as if on a drum turning past the viewer, which gives the movement a front and a back.
- `SHRINK_MS / HOLD_MS / SLIDE_MS / GROW_MS = 450 / 200 / 700 / 500`
  The hold makes the shrink read as deliberate; the slide is the longest beat because it carries the most distance.
- `interval = 3200ms`
  Time at full bleed before each change: atmosphere, not a slideshow to watch.

## API

```ts
type AuthLayout = "stacked" | "inline" | "grid"
type AuthMode = "signin" | "signup" | "verify"
function AuthCard(props: { mode?: AuthMode; email?: string; codeLength?: number; onComplete?: (code: string) => void; onResend?: () => void; layout?: AuthLayout; providers?: SocialProvider[]; title?: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; media?: ReactNode; logo?: ReactNode; centered?: boolean; confirmPassword?: boolean; footnote?: ReactNode; onSubmit?: (data: FormData) => void; onProvider?: (provider: SocialProvider) => void; switchHref?: string; headingLevel?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function AuthMediaCarousel(props: { slides: { src: string; alt?: string }[]; interval?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `mode: "signin" | "signup" | "verify"` — default `"signin"`
  Which step the card shows.
- `layout: "stacked" | "inline" | "grid"` — default `"stacked"`
  How the provider buttons are arranged under the form.
- `providers: SocialProvider[]` — default `["google", "apple", "github"]`
  Provider keys from `SOCIAL_PROVIDERS`; an empty array hides the divider and buttons.
- `onSubmit: (data: FormData) => void`
  Called with the form's FormData on submit.
- `onProvider: (provider: SocialProvider) => void`
  Called when a provider button is pressed.
- `email: string`
  `verify` only: the address shown in the description.
- `codeLength: number` — default `6`
  `verify` only: how many OTP boxes.
- `onComplete / onResend: (code: string) => void / () => void`
  `verify` only: fires when the last box is filled, and the resend action.
- `media: ReactNode`
  Artwork for the right half; switches to the split layout.
- `logo: ReactNode`
  Mark above the title.
- `centered: boolean` — default `false`
  Centre the mark and heading.
- `confirmPassword: boolean` — default `false`
  Sign-up only: two password fields instead of name and password.
- `footnote: ReactNode`
  Small print below the card; also replaces the in-card terms line on sign-up.
- `title / description: ReactNode`
  Override the copy for the current mode.
- `switchHref: string` — default `"#"`
  Target of the footer link to the other mode.
- `headingLevel: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` — default `1`
  Heading element used for the title.
- `slides: AuthMediaSlide[]`
  AuthMediaCarousel: images to cycle; `alt` makes a slide non-decorative.
- `interval: number` — default `3200`
  AuthMediaCarousel: ms a slide rests at full bleed.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const social = (
  <div
    className={cx(
      layout === "stacked" && "flex flex-col gap-2.5",
      // Wraps rather than scrolls: six providers on a narrow card should
      // fall to a second row, not clip.
      layout === "inline" && "flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-2",
      // Equal columns that share the full width, so three providers read as
      // one row of controls rather than three loose squares.
      layout === "grid" && "grid grid-flow-col auto-cols-fr gap-2.5",
    )}
  >
    {providers.map((provider) => (
      <SocialButton
        key={provider}
        brand={provider}
        appearance="white"
        iconOnly={layout !== "stacked"}
        fullWidth={layout === "stacked"}
        // `iconOnly` fixes a square width; the grid needs it to stretch,
        // and `className` is last into `cx` so it wins.
        className={layout === "grid" ? "w-full" : undefined}
        aria-label={layout !== "stacked" ? `Continue with ${SOCIAL_PROVIDERS[provider].label}` : undefined}
        onClick={() => onProvider?.(provider)}
      >
        {`Continue with ${SOCIAL_PROVIDERS[provider].label}`}
      </SocialButton>
    ))}
  </div>
);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The carousel keeps exactly one pending `setTimeout`, cleared whenever the phase, slide count or interval changes and on unmount. The card adds no timers or listeners.

**Reduced motion.** The card itself has no motion beyond its controls' own hover and focus styles. `AuthMediaCarousel` checks `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` when its effect runs and, if set, never schedules a beat, so it holds on the first slide at full bleed. It also does nothing with fewer than two slides.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- `headingLevel` defaults to 1 because on a real sign-in screen the card is the page. Set it to 2 or lower wherever the card is embedded in a page that already has an `<h1>`.
- The "Remember me" checkbox is internal state with no `name`, and `InputOtp` has no `name` either, so neither appears in the submitted `FormData`. Read the code from `onComplete`.
- `confirmPassword` replaces the "Full name" field with a second password field rather than adding one, since the name input only renders for `signup && !confirmPassword`.
- "Forgot password?" is hard-coded to `href="#"` and `switchHref` defaults to `"#"`. Point them at real routes, or wrap the card and replace them.
- The signup description mentions "Acme" and the copy is in English. Pass `title` and `description`, or provide a `TemplateCopyProvider`, for your own product.
- `AuthMediaCarousel` is absolutely positioned (`absolute inset-0`) and keys slides by `src`. Give it a positioned parent with a height (the card's media cell already is one) and use distinct `src` values.

## Notes

- `auth-card` re-exports `AuthMediaCarousel` and `AuthMediaSlide`, so the carousel installs alongside the card even though the card never renders it itself.
- The carousel uses a plain `<img>` (first slide eager, the rest lazy) so it does not impose `next/image` on the installing project. Slides are decorative (`alt=""`, `aria-hidden`) unless you pass `alt`.
- The carousel has no controls on purpose: next to a sign-in form, artwork is atmosphere, and arrows would invite visitors away from the form.
- In dark mode both card variants switch to the secondary background.

## Definition of done

In `signin` the card shows the title, email and password fields, "Remember me" (checked) and "Forgot password?", a full-width "Sign in" button, the divider and the providers, and a "New here? Create an account" footer. `inline` shows icon-only squares that wrap; `grid` stretches them across one row; `stacked` labels each one. Submitting calls `onSubmit` with the form's FormData. `verify` shows OTP boxes in two groups of three, no providers and a "Send a new one" button. With `media`, the card splits in two at `md` and above and shows only the form below it. The carousel rests on an image for about 3.2s, shrinks it into a rounded card, swings it left into depth while the next card comes in from the right, then grows the new one back to full bleed.

# Build: Auto-Advance Filmstrip

Panels are a fixed number of container-width units wide and the whole track is one `translateX`. The active panel sits centred, its neighbours are dimmed and scaled down, and the strip steps every few seconds until you touch it. All motion is a CSS transition on a value React already recomputes when the index changes — there is no tween and no animation loop.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A centred strip that steps one panel every few seconds, neighbours dimmed and shrunk, on one CSS transition.

- Category: layout
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Every panel is `W` container-width units wide (`width: 46cqw`) and the track is translated to `(100 - W) / 2 - W * index` of the same unit. The first term centres one panel — `(100 - 46) / 2 = 27` — and the second steps exactly one panel per index. It is one expression with no measurement and no resize handler, because both terms are already relative to the container.
2. `cqw` rather than `vw`: the strip is sized against its own container, so it stays centred inside a card, a modal or a split layout instead of only when it happens to be full-bleed. The root sets `container-type: inline-size` to establish that container.
3. The transition is `transform 500ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` on the track. For a component where React already re-renders on index change, a CSS transition is fewer moving parts than a tween and it interpolates on the compositor.
4. Inactive panels get `opacity: 0.35` **and** `scale(0.8)`, transitioning on the same curve and duration as the track so the three properties land together.
5. Auto-advance is `setTimeout` re-armed on every index change, not `setInterval`. Manual navigation therefore restarts the dwell rather than inheriting whatever was left of the current tick.
6. The timer is gated on four conditions — `autoPlay`, not reduced-motion, `document.visibilityState === "visible"`, and not currently hovered or focused within — so it never advances behind the user's back or in a background tab.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `panelWidth = 46`
  Panel width in `cqw`. Under 50 means two neighbours are partly visible, which is what makes it a filmstrip rather than a slideshow. At 46 the centred panel leaves 27 units of peek on each side — enough to read the neighbour as a real panel, not a sliver.
- `interval = 3000`
  Milliseconds per panel. Below ~2500 a caption cannot be read before it leaves; above ~5000 the strip looks broken rather than paced on a page where nothing else is moving.
- `duration = 500`
  Slide transition. Roughly a sixth of the dwell, which keeps the strip reading as a series of held frames with a transition between them rather than as continuous motion.
- `EASE = cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`
  Expo-out. It covers about 80% of the distance in the first 30% of the duration, so the strip appears to arrive early and settle — the same reason it is the default curve for interface movement that should feel decided rather than mechanical.
- `inactiveOpacity / inactiveScale = 0.35 / 0.8`
  Both, together. 0.35 alone reads as a loading state; 0.8 alone reads as a layout bug. Applied together they read as depth, which is the only interpretation a viewer will land on.

## API

```ts
function AutoAdvanceFilmstrip(props: { children: ReactNode; panelWidth?: number; interval?: number; duration?: number; autoPlay?: boolean; inactiveOpacity?: number; inactiveScale?: number; className?: string; panelClassName?: string; 'aria-label'?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  One panel per child.
- `panelWidth: number` — default `46`
  Panel width in container-width units (`cqw`).
- `interval: number` — default `3000`
  Milliseconds a panel is held before the strip advances.
- `duration: number` — default `500`
  Slide transition duration in milliseconds.
- `autoPlay: boolean` — default `true`
  Whether the strip advances on its own.
- `inactiveOpacity: number` — default `0.35`
  Opacity applied to every panel that is not active.
- `inactiveScale: number` — default `0.8`
  Scale applied to every panel that is not active.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root, which is also the query container.
- `panelClassName: string`
  Merged onto each panel cell.
- `aria-label: string` — default `'Filmstrip'`
  Label for the carousel group.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// (100 - W) / 2 centres a panel of width W; W * index steps one panel per
// index. Both terms are in the same unit as the panel width, so the strip
// stays centred at every container size with no measurement at all.
const offset = (100 - panelWidth) / 2 - panelWidth * index;

const running = autoPlay && !reduced && visible && !held && count > 1;

useEffect(() => {
  if (!running) return;
  // setTimeout keyed on `index`, not setInterval: any manual navigation
  // re-arms a full dwell. With an interval, tapping "next" one tick before
  // it fires advances twice in a row.
  const id = window.setTimeout(() => {
    setIndex((current) => wrapIndex(current + 1, count));
  }, interval);
  return () => window.clearTimeout(id);
}, [running, index, interval, count]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The pending `setTimeout` is cleared by the effect's own teardown, which also runs on every index change and whenever the strip pauses. `useVisibility` and `useReducedMotion` unsubscribe their listeners. There is nothing else to release: all motion is CSS on nodes React owns.

**Reduced motion.** Auto-advance never starts, so nothing moves unless the user presses a control. When they do, `transition` is set to `none` on both the track and the panels, so the strip cuts to the new panel in one frame instead of sliding. The dot pager and arrows behave identically; only the interpolation is gone.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using a percentage in the track's `translateX`. Percentages on `transform` resolve against the *element's own* width, and the track is as wide as all its panels — so `translateX(-46%)` moves it by 46% of the whole strip, not of one panel. The arithmetic only works in a unit that refers to the container: `cqw` here, `vw` if the strip is genuinely full-bleed.
- Using `setInterval` for the auto-advance. Tap "next" a hundred milliseconds before the tick fires and the strip advances twice; the second jump has no cause the user can see. A `setTimeout` keyed on the index gives every panel a full dwell.
- Leaving the timer running while the tab is hidden. The user comes back to a strip that has silently walked eleven panels forward, and every intervening transition ran on a throttled timer.
- Not pausing on hover or focus. A pointer resting on a panel and a keyboard user tabbing into a control both mean "I am reading this"; advancing underneath either one is the single most common complaint about auto-advancing carousels.
- Only setting `containerType` on an ancestor that has no definite inline size. `cqw` then resolves against the viewport-sized fallback and the arithmetic silently reverts to the `vw` behaviour it was meant to replace.
- Fading inactive panels to `opacity: 0`. They are still in the layout and still hit-testable, so a click intended for the active panel can land on an invisible neighbour that happens to be under the cursor.

## Notes

- Cheapest of the three carousels here and the right default when the set is short and each panel needs a moment on screen. Unlike `wrapping-drum-carousel` it does not wrap continuously — it jumps from the last index back to the first, and that jump is a full-width slide, which is visible. Keep the set small enough that the loop point is rare.
- Every panel stays mounted and in the layout at all times. For twenty panels that is twenty subtrees painting; virtualise or switch technique past roughly a dozen.

## Definition of done

The strip steps one panel roughly every three seconds with the neighbours visible, dimmed and smaller on both sides. Hovering anywhere over it stops the advance and moving away resumes it with a full dwell. Switch tabs for ten seconds and come back: it is on the panel it was on, not ten further along. Resize the container from 320 px to full width and the active panel stays exactly centred.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Avatar

A circular `<span>` that shows a photo when `src` is set and centred initials on a tinted disc otherwise. Four sizes match the places the dashboard uses avatars (breadcrumb marks, table rows, sidebar cards, people cards), and each size carries its own initials type style so the letters always fit the disc.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Round photo or initials avatar in four sizes (20 to 36px) and four tints, with a lazy-loaded image that fills the disc.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Keep every class in a `sortCx` map. `base` is `inline-flex shrink-0 select-none items-center justify-center overflow-hidden rounded-full text-center align-middle`: a flex-centred disc that clips its photo and never shrinks inside a row.
2. Map `size` to a box and an initials style together: xs `size-5 text-[10px] leading-[15px] font-semibold`, sm `size-6 text-caption-1-semibold tracking-normal`, md `size-8 text-headline-semibold`, lg `size-9 text-[18px] leading-6 font-semibold`.
3. Map `color` to a fill and text pair: `neutral` uses the semantic `bg-avatar-neutral-background` with `text-text-secondary`; `blue`, `lime` and `pink` use fixed palette pairs (`bg-blue-300 text-blue-900`, `bg-lime-200 text-lime-700`, `bg-pink-200 text-pink-500`).
4. If `src` is set, render `<img className="size-full object-cover" loading="lazy" decoding="async">` with `alt ?? ""`; otherwise render `initials` as the span's text. A photo wins over initials.
5. Add `transition-[width,height,font-size] duration-200` to the base, so a list that switches density resizes its avatars smoothly instead of snapping.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `sizes = xs 20px, sm 24px, md 32px, lg 36px`
  One per Figma context: breadcrumb workspace marks, table rows, sidebar workspace / team cards and people cards. Lg matches the kit's 36px controls so an avatar sits level with a button.
- `initials type = 10/15, 12/16, 16/22, 18/24 px, all weight 600`
  Roughly half the disc diameter. A single size-agnostic style either overflows the 20px disc or looks lost in the 36px one.
- `neutral fill = light neutral-300, dark background-primary-default`
  The neutral tint is the only theme-aware one, because it is the default and appears on every surface; the coloured tints are fixed Figma pairs.

## API

```ts
interface AvatarProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement> { size?: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg"; color?: "neutral" | "blue" | "lime" | "pink"; src?: string; alt?: string; initials?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLSpanElement> }
function Avatar(props: AvatarProps): JSX.Element
```

- `size: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg"` — default `"md"`
  20, 24, 32 or 36px disc, each with its own initials type style.
- `color: "neutral" | "blue" | "lime" | "pink"` — default `"neutral"`
  Fill and initials colour when no photo is shown.
- `src: string`
  Photo URL. Rendered as a lazy, async-decoded `<img>` that covers the disc. Wins over `initials`.
- `alt: string` — default `""`
  Alt text for the photo.
- `initials: string`
  Fallback text shown when `src` is not set, e.g. "M".
- `className: string`
  Merged last through `tailwind-merge`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const styles = sortCx({
  base: "inline-flex shrink-0 select-none items-center justify-center overflow-hidden rounded-full text-center align-middle transition-[width,height,font-size] duration-200 ease",
  size: {
    xs: "size-5 text-[10px] leading-[15px] font-semibold",
    sm: "size-6 text-caption-1-semibold tracking-normal",
    md: "size-8 text-headline-semibold",
    lg: "size-9 text-[18px] leading-6 font-semibold",
  },
  color: {
    neutral: "bg-avatar-neutral-background text-text-secondary",
    blue: "bg-blue-300 text-blue-900",
    lime: "bg-lime-200 text-lime-700",
    pink: "bg-pink-200 text-pink-500",
  },
});

export function Avatar({
  size = "md",
  color = "neutral",
  src,
  alt,
  initials,
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: AvatarProps) {
  return (
    <span
      ref={ref}
      className={cx(styles.base, styles.size[size], styles.color[color], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {src ? (
        <img
          src={src}
          alt={alt ?? ""}
          loading="lazy"
          decoding="async"
          className="size-full object-cover"
        />
      ) : (
        initials
      )}
    </span>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component is stateless markup with no listeners, timers or effects.

**Reduced motion.** The component itself only has a 200ms size transition when its `size` prop changes. It is not gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`; any hover fan-out of a group belongs to the caller.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not drop `overflow-hidden` on the disc. Without it a non-square photo pokes out of the circle.
- Do not remove `shrink-0`. In a table cell or a flex row with long text, the avatar squeezes into an oval.
- Do not leave `alt` unset on a photo of a named person when no name sits next to it. The component falls back to `alt=""`, which marks the image decorative.
- Do not pass three or more letters as `initials`. The xs and sm discs only fit one or two characters.

## Notes

- Overlapping groups are composed outside the component: wrap each avatar in a `rounded-full ring-2 ring-background-primary-default` element and pull it left with a negative margin, so the ring cuts a gap against the previous avatar.
- The default is `size="md"` and `color="neutral"`.

## Definition of done

Without `src`, `<Avatar size="lg" color="blue" initials="M" />` renders a 36px blue-300 disc with an 18px semibold blue-900 "M" centred in it. The four sizes measure 20, 24, 32 and 36px and stay circular inside a flex row. With `src`, the photo fills and is clipped to the circle, and initials are not shown.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Avatar Stack

The assignee cluster from the project board cards: kit avatars overlap by a quarter of their width, each wearing a 2px ring in the surface colour so the stack reads as cut-outs. Past `max`, the remaining people collapse into a "+N" disc whose tooltip lists them. Every disc is a tab stop with a name tooltip, and the group announces everyone in its label.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Overlapping assignee discs with surface-coloured rings, a +N overflow disc and a name tooltip on every avatar.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. People render left to right as kit `Avatar`s with negative inline-start margins (`-ms-1.5` for xs/sm, `-ms-2` for md, `-ms-2.5` for lg) on every disc after the first. The root is `isolate`, so the hover/focus `z-10` lift stays inside the stack instead of leaking over neighbouring UI.
2. The ring is `ring-2` plus `ringClassName` (default `ring-background-primary-default`). Matching it to the surface underneath is what makes the overlap look like a cut-out rather than a border; pass the column colour when the stack sits on a non-white surface.
3. Overflow rule: with `limit = max(1, max)`, the stack only collapses when `people.length > limit + 1`. Replacing the last avatar with "+1" saves no space and hides a face, so four people at `max = 3` show all four, while five show three discs plus "+2".
4. Each disc is wrapped as `TooltipTrigger` (150ms delay) → RAC `Focusable` → `Avatar` with `role="img"` and `aria-label` set to the name. `Focusable` makes the disc keyboard reachable and wires hover/focus to the kit `Tooltip` (placement top, name plus optional `description` line). `tooltips={false}` drops the triggers, so discs stop being tab stops.
5. The "+N" disc is a `button` when `onOverflowPress` is set (e.g. to expand the list or open a member popover) and a `span role="img"` otherwise. Both carry `aria-label="N more: names"`; its tooltip lists the hidden names one per line.
6. Without an explicit `color`, a person's initial tint comes from a djb2 hash of the name over blue, lime, pink and neutral (`tintOf`), so the same person keeps the same colour on every card. `initialsOf` takes the first letters of the first two words.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `overlap = xs/sm 6px, md 8px, lg 10px`
  About a quarter of the disc width, matched by eye to the board card's 20–24px avatars. More overlap hides initials; less stops reading as one group.
- `ring = 2px, surface colour`
  Wide enough to separate two discs of the same tint, thin enough that the initials stay centred in the visible area.
- `collapse threshold = people.length > max + 1`
  Never shows "+1": a counter that hides one person takes the same room as that person's avatar.
- `tooltip delay = 150ms`
  Fast enough to scrub across the stack and read names, slow enough not to flash when the pointer crosses a card.
- `hover lift = -translate-y-0.5 over 150ms ease-out`
  A 2px nudge plus `z-10` brings the hovered face above its neighbour so its full disc is visible while its tooltip shows.

## API

```ts
function AvatarStack(props: Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "children"> & { people: readonly AvatarStackPerson[]; max?: number; size?: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg"; tooltips?: boolean; ringClassName?: string; label?: string; onOverflowPress?: () => void; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
interface AvatarStackPerson { id?: string; name: string; initials?: string; color?: AvatarProps["color"]; src?: string; description?: string }
function initialsOf(name: string): string
function tintOf(name: string): AvatarProps["color"]
```

- `people: readonly AvatarStackPerson[]`
  Who to show, in order. `id` is the key (falls back to `name`).
- `max: number` — default `3`
  Discs shown before the rest collapse into "+N". Collapses only when two or more would hide.
- `size: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg"` — default `"sm"`
  Kit avatar size; overlap and the "+N" disc scale with it.
- `tooltips: boolean` — default `true`
  Name tooltips on hover and focus. Off removes the tab stops too.
- `ringClassName: string` — default `"ring-background-primary-default"`
  Ring colour; set it to the surface the stack sits on.
- `label: string` — default `"Assignees"`
  Prefix of the group's accessible name, followed by every name.
- `onOverflowPress: () => void`
  Turns the "+N" disc into a button.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function AvatarStack({
  people,
  max = 3,
  size = "sm",
  tooltips = true,
  ringClassName = "ring-background-primary-default",
  label = "Assignees",
  onOverflowPress,
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: AvatarStackProps) {
  // Showing "+1" in place of the last avatar saves no room, so only collapse
  // when at least two people would hide.
  const limit = Math.max(1, max);
  const visibleCount = people.length > limit + 1 ? limit : people.length;
  const shown = people.slice(0, visibleCount);
  const hidden = people.slice(visibleCount);
  const names = people.map((p) => p.name);

  const discClass = (index: number) => cx(styles.disc, ringClassName, index > 0 && styles.overlap[size]);

  const overflowDisc = hidden.length > 0 && (
    <OverflowDisc
      count={hidden.length}
      names={hidden.map((p) => p.name)}
      className={cx(
        discClass(shown.length),
        styles.overflow[size],
        "inline-flex shrink-0 select-none items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-background-tertiary-default text-text-secondary",
      )}
      tooltips={tooltips}
      onPress={onOverflowPress}
    />
  );

  return (
    <div
      ref={ref}
      role="group"
      aria-label={people.length ? `${label}: ${names.join(", ")}` : `${label}: none`}
      className={cx("inline-flex shrink-0 items-center isolate", className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {shown.map((person, i) => {
        const disc = (
          <Avatar
            key={person.id ?? person.name}
            size={size}
            color={person.color ?? tintOf(person.name)}
            src={person.src}
            alt=""
            initials={person.initials ?? initialsOf(person.name)}
            role="img"
            aria-label={person.name}
            className={discClass(i)}
          />
        );
        if (!tooltips) return disc;
        return (
          <TooltipTrigger key={person.id ?? person.name} delay={150}>
            <Focusable>{disc}</Focusable>
            <Tooltip placement="top">
              <span className="block">{person.name}</span>
              {person.description && <span className="block text-text-secondary">{person.description}</span>}
            </Tooltip>
          </TooltipTrigger>
        );
      })}
      {overflowDisc}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No effects, timers or listeners of its own. Tooltip open/close timers belong to the kit Tooltip (React Aria) and are released when a trigger unmounts.

**Reduced motion.** The 2px hover lift and its transform transition are removed with `motion-reduce:transition-none` and `motion-reduce:hover:translate-y-0`; the z-index raise and tooltips still work.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Leaving the ring on its white default when the stack sits on a grey column or a dark tinted surface: the rings then read as white outlines. Pass `ringClassName` for that surface.
- Dropping `isolate` from the root. The raised `z-10` disc can then paint over sticky headers or popovers that share the stacking context.
- Using array indexes as keys. People join and leave cards; keys come from `id` and fall back to `name`.
- Hiding names behind colour only. Each disc keeps `role="img"` and its name as `aria-label`, and the group label lists everyone, so screen readers do not depend on the tooltip.

## Notes

- Kanban Card uses this for the top-right assignee cluster at `size="xs"` with `max={3}`.
- Photos work through `src`, but the demo uses initials only so it ships without remote images.
- Below 640px the demo shows only the ticket and its assignee list so it fits a phone screen; the Sizes panel joins it from `sm` up.

## Definition of done

Five assignees at max 3 render three overlapping discs plus "+2"; four render all four with no counter. Hovering or tabbing to a disc raises it and shows a tooltip with the name and role. In the demo, unchecking teammates shrinks the stack and updates "N assigned"; pressing "+N" expands the stack to show everyone and "Collapse" folds it back. Rings match the card in both light and dark themes.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Badge

A `<span>` with two colour tones and one fixed shape, 12px semibold type in a 4px-radius pill. It exists so every count in the kit (sidebar items, tab counts, unread totals) has the same metrics. The tone tracks the selection state of whatever holds it, not the meaning of the number.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

The small numeric counter on nav items and unread totals: a 16px pill in a selected (blue) or resting (neutral) tone.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The shape is one class string: `inline-flex` centred content, `px-1 py-px`, `rounded-sm` and the kit's `text-caption-1-semibold` type style (12px over a 16px line). With one pixel of vertical padding the pill is 18px tall, short enough to sit inside a 32px nav row without pushing its height.
2. `whitespace-nowrap` keeps "1,204" or "99+" on one line. Combined with `inline-flex` the pill grows with its content, and there is no fixed width that a three-digit count could overflow.
3. `primary` uses `bg-accent-400` with white text and is meant for a badge inside the selected nav item, where the row itself is tinted. `neutral` uses the `badge-neutral-background` token with secondary text for every other row. The neutral token is redefined in `.dark`, so the same class reads correctly on both themes.
4. All other attributes spread onto the `<span>`, so `aria-label="12 unread"` or a `title` pass straight through. `className` merges through `tailwind-merge`, so `rounded-full` replaces `rounded-sm` instead of both applying.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `padding = px-1 py-px (4px / 1px)`
  Figma's counter spec. Horizontal padding of 4px keeps a single digit almost square. Larger vertical padding makes the badge taller than the label text it sits beside, and the nav row starts to look uneven.
- `type = text-caption-1-semibold, tracking-normal`
  The smallest tier in the kit's type scale. `tracking-normal` overrides the negative tracking the scale applies at larger sizes, because tight tracking at 12px makes adjacent digits such as 11 merge into one shape.

## API

```ts
function Badge(props: HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement> & { color?: "primary" | "neutral"; ref?: Ref<HTMLSpanElement> }): JSX.Element
```

- `color: "primary" | "neutral"` — default `"neutral"`
  `primary` (blue fill, white text) inside a selected row; `neutral` everywhere else.
- `children: ReactNode`
  The count or short label. Keep it to a few characters.
- `className: string`
  Merged through `tailwind-merge`, so conflicting utilities replace the defaults.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const styles = sortCx({
  base: "inline-flex items-center justify-center rounded-sm px-1 py-px text-caption-1-semibold tracking-normal whitespace-nowrap",
  color: {
    primary: "bg-accent-400 text-white",
    neutral: "bg-badge-neutral-background text-text-secondary",
  },
});

export function Badge({ color = "neutral", className, ref, ...props }: BadgeProps) {
  return (
    <span
      ref={ref}
      className={cx(styles.base, styles.color[color], className)}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component renders a styled span with no state, effects or listeners.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing animates. The badge is static, so there is no motion to reduce.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Choosing the tone by meaning ("red for errors"). Badge has no status palette on purpose: its tone follows selection. For status use `Chip` or `StatusDot`, which do carry status colours.
- Using a bare number as the only label. A screen reader hears "12" with no context. Pass `aria-label` ("12 unread messages"), or make sure the surrounding link text explains the count.
- Giving the pill a fixed `w-*` so counts line up. Three digits then clip or wrap. Align the column with the parent's layout instead, for example `ms-auto` in a flex row.

## Notes

- The sidebar, tabs and notification centre all import this file, so changing its metrics changes every count in the kit at once. That shared source is the reason it is its own item.

## Definition of done

A neutral badge reads clearly on the page background in both light and dark themes, and a primary badge is legible white-on-blue inside a selected nav row. "7", "48" and "1,204" all sit on one line with even side padding, and the pill is no taller than the 16px label line beside it. A consumer `rounded-full` turns it into a full pill without leaving `rounded-sm` in the computed styles.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Banded Scrollspy Rail

A section rail that never flickers, because only one section can be "active" at a time by construction. The IntersectionObserver root is shrunk to a 7%-tall band across the middle of the scroller, so a section registers only while it crosses that line. The active tick grows from 16 to 32 pixels — a size change, legible in peripheral vision, rather than a tint change that is not. No animation library: one observer, one CSS width transition.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A tick rail whose active mark widens as a section crosses a 7% band through the middle of the screen.

- Category: scroll
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. One IntersectionObserver watches every `[data-scrollspy]` element with `rootMargin: "-38% 0px -55% 0px"`. Trimming 38% off the top and 55% off the bottom leaves a 7%-tall detection band (100 − 38 − 55), positioned just below centre so a section becomes active while you are reading it rather than while it is still arriving.
2. Entries maintain a `Set` of ids currently inside the band. The active id is resolved by scanning the authored `sections` order for the first member of that set — not by reading `entries[0]`, whose order depends on how the observer batched the callback and therefore on scroll direction.
3. When the set is empty — a gap between sections, or a header taller than the band — the previous answer is held rather than cleared, so the rail never blanks between sections.
4. A second observer watches the element named by `endId` with `rootMargin: "0px 0px -25% 0px"`, which makes "intersecting" mean exactly "its top has climbed above 75% of the root". That retires the whole rail, so it is not hovering over a footer with nothing left to navigate.
5. The indicator itself is a `<span>` whose inline `width` flips between 16 and 32 px with a 260 ms CSS transition. The only JavaScript per scroll event is a `Set` mutation and at most one `setState`.
6. Section elements are collected into an id → element `Map` by walking the attribute once, rather than running a `[data-scrollspy="id"]` selector per section — that form needs escaping for any id containing punctuation and silently matches nothing when the escaping is wrong.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `bandTop / bandBottom = 38 / 55`
  Leaves a 7% band. Widen it and two sections are inside at once on a tall screen, which is the flicker this design exists to remove. Narrow it below about 4% and a fast flick can jump the band entirely between two observer callbacks, leaving the rail on the previous section. The asymmetry (38 vs 55) puts the band below centre, where the eye is while reading.
- `ACTIVE_WIDTH / IDLE_WIDTH = 32 / 16`
  A 2x length change is detectable without looking directly at it. Equal widths with only a colour change is invisible in peripheral vision, which defeats the point of a rail you are not supposed to be looking at.
- `TRANSITION_MS = 260`
  Long enough that the width change reads as movement and draws the eye, short enough that it has finished before the next section can reach the band during normal scrolling.
- `hideAt = 0.75`
  Fraction of the root the end marker must pass before the rail retires. At 1.0 the rail is still on screen while the footer is being read; below about 0.6 it disappears while the last section is still active.

## API

```ts
function BandedScrollspyRail(props: { sections: { id: string; label: string }[]; rootRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; bandTop?: number; bandBottom?: number; endId?: string; hideAt?: number; attribute?: string; onActiveChange?: (id: string | null) => void; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `sections: { id: string; label: string }[]`
  Ordered list. Each `id` must match a `data-scrollspy` attribute inside the root.
- `rootRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>`
  The scroll container holding the sections. Omit for the document.
- `bandTop: number` — default `38`
  Percent of the root trimmed from the top to form the band.
- `bandBottom: number` — default `55`
  Percent trimmed from the bottom. The two must sum to under 100.
- `endId: string`
  Section after which the rail retires. Usually the footer.
- `hideAt: number` — default `0.75`
  Fraction down the root the end marker must pass before the rail hides.
- `attribute: string` — default `'data-scrollspy'`
  Attribute used to find sections inside the root.
- `onActiveChange: (id: string | null) => void`
  Fires once per active-section change. Held in a ref, so it needs no memo.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the nav element via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const ACTIVE_WIDTH = 32;
const IDLE_WIDTH = 16;
const TRANSITION_MS = 260;

export function BandedScrollspyRail({
  sections,
  rootRef,
  bandTop = 38,
  bandBottom = 55,
  endId,
  hideAt = 0.75,
  attribute = 'data-scrollspy',
  onActiveChange,
  className,
}: BandedScrollspyRailProps) {
  const [active, setActive] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [retired, setRetired] = useState(false);
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  // Held in refs so a new array literal or a fresh callback on every parent
  // render does not tear down and rebuild the observers.
  const sectionsRef = useRef(sections);
  sectionsRef.current = sections;
  const notify = useRef(onActiveChange);
  notify.current = onActiveChange;

  const order = sections.map((s) => s.id).join('|');

  useEffect(() => {
    const root = rootRef?.current ?? null;
    const scope: ParentNode = root ?? document;

    // Build id -> element by walking the attribute once, rather than running a
    // `[attr="id"]` selector per section: that needs escaping for any id with
    // punctuation in it, and silently matches nothing when the escaping is
    // wrong.
    const elements = new Map<string, Element>();
    for (const el of Array.from(scope.querySelectorAll(`[${attribute}]`))) {
      const id = el.getAttribute(attribute);
      if (id) elements.set(id, el);
    }
    if (elements.size === 0) return;

    const inBand = new Set<string>();

    const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
      (entries) => {
        for (const entry of entries) {
          const id = entry.target.getAttribute(attribute);
          if (!id) continue;
          if (entry.isIntersecting) inBand.add(id);
          else inBand.delete(id);
        }

        // Resolve in authored order, not entry order: callbacks arrive in
        // whatever order the observer batched them, so picking `entries[0]`
        // makes the active section depend on scroll direction.
        const next = sectionsRef.current.find((s) => inBand.has(s.id))?.id;

        // Nothing in the band — a gap between sections, or a header taller
        // than the band. Hold the last answer instead of blanking the rail,
        // which would read as the nav breaking.
        if (next === undefined) return;

        setActive((prev) => {
          if (prev === next) return prev;
          notify.current?.(next);
          return next;
        });
      },
      {
        root,
        // The band. 100 - bandTop - bandBottom percent of the root's height,
        // centred low enough that a section is "active" while you are reading
        // it rather than while it is still arriving.
        rootMargin: `-${bandTop}% 0px -${bandBottom}% 0px`,
        threshold: 0,
      },
    );

    for (const el of elements.values()) observer.observe(el);

    // Second observer: retire the rail once the end marker has climbed past
    // `hideAt`, so it is not hovering over a footer with nothing left to
    // navigate. Shrinking the bottom margin by (1 - hideAt) makes
    // "intersecting" mean exactly "its top is above hideAt of the root".
    let endObserver: IntersectionObserver | null = null;
    const endEl = endId === undefined ? undefined : elements.get(endId);
    if (endEl) {
      endObserver = new IntersectionObserver(
        (entries) => {
          const entry = entries[entries.length - 1];
          if (entry) setRetired(entry.isIntersecting);
        },
        { root, rootMargin: `0px 0px -${Math.round((1 - hideAt) * 100)}% 0px`, threshold: 0 },
      );
      endObserver.observe(endEl);
    }

    return () => {
      observer.disconnect();
      endObserver?.disconnect();
    };
  }, [rootRef, attribute, bandTop, bandBottom, endId, hideAt, order]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Both IntersectionObservers are disconnected on unmount and on any option change. An observer holds a strong reference to every element it watches, so skipping this pins the unmounted section tree in memory and keeps firing `setState` on a dead component.

**Reduced motion.** The rail still tracks the active section and still changes width — that is state, not decoration. Every `transition` is set to `none`, so the tick snaps between widths and the labels appear instantly, and click-to-navigate uses `behavior: "auto"` rather than a smooth scroll.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Observing with the default full-height root. Three sections intersect at once on a tall screen and the active tick flickers between them on every callback. Debouncing hides the symptom and adds lag; shrinking the root removes the ambiguity.
- Taking the active section from `entries[0]`. The callback batches entries in an order that depends on which boundaries were crossed, so the same scroll direction can yield a different winner between two frames. Resolve against the authored order instead.
- Clearing the active state when nothing is intersecting. Any gap taller than the band — a spacer, a full-bleed image, a header — blanks the rail mid-scroll and it reads as broken.
- Signalling the active section with colour only. On a hairline tick in the corner of the eye a tint change is imperceptible; a width change is not, and it also survives a monochrome or high-contrast rendering.
- Rebuilding the observers on every render. `sections` is usually a fresh array literal from the parent, so keying the effect on it disconnects and reconnects two observers on every keystroke elsewhere in the page. Key on the joined id list and read the array from a ref.
- Forgetting `observer.disconnect()`. IntersectionObserver keeps a strong reference to every observed element, so an undisconnected observer pins the whole unmounted section tree in memory and keeps calling `setState` on a dead component.
- Scrolling with `window.scrollTo` on click when the sections live in a container. `scrollIntoView` walks up and scrolls whichever ancestor actually holds the overflow, which is the only version that works in both cases.

## Notes

- No GSAP and no ScrollTrigger: the whole component is two IntersectionObservers and a CSS transition, which is why it is classed `css` cost and can be used dozens of times on a page.
- The labels are always in the DOM at `opacity: 0` and reveal on hover or keyboard focus, so the rail is operable and readable without a pointer.

## Definition of done

Scroll slowly: the active tick changes exactly once as each section crosses the middle of the screen, with no flicker at the boundary and no blank state in the gaps. The active tick is visibly twice as long as the others. Scroll to the end and the whole rail fades out. Hover it and the labels appear; tab into it and they appear too. With reduced motion on, the tick still moves but snaps rather than eases.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Bar List Card

An analytics breakdown card: each row is a label and icon sitting on a pale bar whose width is the item against the largest one, with the metric on the right. Underline tabs switch between lists, and the caption doubles as a switch between shares of the list total and raw counts. Lists longer than `limit` end in a faded peek row with a small chevron pill that unfolds the rest. Hovering a row brings in the other number.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Ranked analytics rows on proportional bars behind underline tabs, with a share / count switch and a pill that unfolds long lists.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Each list is filtered to finite values of 0 or more, then sorted high to low. Every item gets `share = value / total` and `width = value / max`, so the top row always spans the full bar and hidden rows never change the visible ones.
2. A bar is an absolutely positioned span behind the row content, `width: width × 100%` with an 8px minimum so a tiny item still shows a rounded nub. `useGrown` holds the width at 0 for two animation frames after a list mounts, then a 500ms ease-out width transition grows every bar to its size.
3. The kit `Tabs` render one `TabPanel` per list. Only the selected panel is mounted, so switching tabs mounts the new list and its bars grow in. The tab strip sits in a sideways scroller with a 24px fade on the right, and `-mb-px` lays the blue underline over the header divider.
4. Rows past `limit` live in a second list inside a clipping box. Collapsed, the box is 30px tall: a 4px gap plus 26px of the first hidden row, masked from opaque to transparent, and `inert` so the hidden rows are neither focusable nor announced.
5. The chevron pill toggles the box between that peek and `hidden rows × 40px + 26px`, over a 300ms height transition. The extra 26px leaves a band for the pill under the last row, and the chevron turns 180°. Only one list is open at a time, and switching tabs folds it again.
6. The caption button flips the metric between `share` and `value`; its % / # marker shows which is live. Each row's number is keyed by the metric, so it replays the kit's `animate-number-fade` on every switch. On row hover the other number (count or share) fades in beside it in tertiary text.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `row = 36px tall (h-9), 4px gap, 8px radius`
  Gives the 40px pitch of the preview and lets the unfold height be computed exactly instead of measured.
- `PEEK = 30px`
  Shows enough of the next row (its icon, label and number) to read as "there is more" under the fade, while the pill sits on top of it.
- `PILL_SPACE = 26px`
  Room under the last row for the 18px pill when the list is open, so the pill never covers a number.
- `BAR_MIN = 8px`
  One radius wide: a 1% item still shows a rounded nub instead of a hairline.
- `grow = 500ms ease-out width, after two animation frames`
  Two frames guarantee the zero width is painted before the transition starts, even when a click mounts the panel synchronously.
- `unfold = 300ms ease-out height`
  Fast enough to follow the click, long enough to show the list growing rather than jumping.

## API

```ts
function BarListCard(props: { tabs?: BarListTab[]; items?: BarListItem[]; title?: string; tab?: string; defaultTab?: string; onTabChange?: (id: string) => void; metricLabel?: string; metric?: "share" | "value"; defaultMetric?: "share" | "value"; onMetricChange?: (metric: "share" | "value") => void; metricToggle?: boolean; limit?: number; mono?: boolean; formatValue?: (value: number) => string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type BarListItem = { label: string; value: number; icon?: ReactNode }
type BarListTab = { id: string; label: string; items: BarListItem[] }
```

- `tabs: BarListTab[]` — default `TRAFFIC_TABS`
  Lists behind underline tabs. Ignored when `items` is set.
- `items: BarListItem[]`
  One list without tabs, headed by `title`.
- `title: string` — default `"Breakdown" (tabs) or `metricLabel` (items)`
  Header of a single list; the card's accessible name in both modes.
- `tab: string`
  Controlled tab id.
- `defaultTab: string` — default `first tab id`
  Initial tab when uncontrolled.
- `onTabChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called when a tab is selected.
- `metricLabel: string` — default `"Visitors"`
  Uppercase caption over the numbers.
- `metric: "share" | "value"`
  Controlled metric: share of the list total, or the raw value.
- `defaultMetric: "share" | "value"` — default `"share"`
  Initial metric when uncontrolled.
- `onMetricChange: (metric) => void`
  Called when the caption switch flips the metric.
- `metricToggle: boolean` — default `true`
  Turns the caption into a share / count switch with a % / # marker.
- `limit: number` — default `5`
  Rows shown before the rest fold behind the peek row and pill.
- `mono: boolean` — default `false`
  Grey chart-track bars instead of pale blue.
- `formatValue: (value: number) => string` — default `en-US integer`
  Formats counts in the rows and the hover detail.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
function BarRows({
  name,
  items,
  metric,
  metricLabel,
  limit,
  mono,
  expanded,
  onExpandedChange,
  formatValue,
}: RowsProps) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const grown = useGrown(reduced);
  const moreId = useId();
  const ranked = useMemo(() => rank(items), [items]);

  const cap = Math.max(1, Math.floor(limit));
  const shown = ranked.slice(0, cap);
  const rest = ranked.slice(cap);
  // Shares are of the tab's total and widths of its largest item, so hidden
  // rows never change the visible bars when they expand.
  const openHeight = rest.length * ROW_PITCH + PILL_SPACE;
  const row = (item: RankedItem) => (
    <BarRow
      key={item.label}
      item={item}
      metric={metric}
      metricLabel={metricLabel}
      mono={mono}
      grown={grown}
      formatValue={formatValue}
    />
  );

  if (ranked.length === 0) {
    return <p className="px-2.5 py-2 text-body-regular text-text-tertiary">No data yet</p>;
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col">
      <ul aria-label={`${name} by ${metricLabel.toLowerCase()}`} className="flex flex-col gap-1">
        {shown.map(row)}
      </ul>
      {rest.length > 0 && (
        <div className="relative">
          <div
            id={moreId}
            inert={!expanded}
            data-expanded={expanded || undefined}
            className="overflow-hidden transition-[height] duration-300 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none"
            style={{
              height: expanded ? openHeight : PEEK,
              maskImage: expanded ? undefined : 'linear-gradient(to bottom, black, transparent)',
              WebkitMaskImage: expanded ? undefined : 'linear-gradient(to bottom, black, transparent)',
            }}
          >
            <ul aria-label={`More ${name.toLowerCase()}`} className="flex flex-col gap-1 pt-1">
              {rest.map(row)}
            </ul>
          </div>
          <button
            type="button"
            aria-expanded={expanded}
            aria-controls={moreId}
            aria-label={expanded ? 'Show fewer' : `Show ${rest.length} more`}
            onClick={() => onExpandedChange(!expanded)}
            className="absolute bottom-1 left-1/2 flex h-4.5 w-9 -translate-x-1/2 items-center justify-center rounded-full border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default text-foreground-icon-primary shadow-xs outline-none transition-colors duration-150 ease-out after:absolute after:-inset-x-2 after:-inset-y-3 hover:bg-background-secondary-default focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring"
          >
            <RiArrowDownSLine
              aria-hidden
              className={cx(
                'size-3.5 transition-transform duration-300 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none',
                expanded && 'rotate-180',
              )}
            />
          </button>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `useGrown` cancels both of its animation frames on unmount, so switching tabs mid-grow leaves nothing running. Everything else is React state and CSS transitions; the kit `TabList` disconnects its own observers.

**Reduced motion.** `useGrown` is skipped, so the bars render at their final widths. The width, height, chevron, colour and fade transitions are removed with `motion-reduce:transition-none`, and the number fade with `motion-reduce:animate-none`. The list unfolds and folds at once.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Scaling bar widths to the list total. The top item of a flat list then stops halfway across, and every bar looks short. Widths are against the largest item; shares are against the total.
- Hiding folded rows with `display: none` or opacity alone. Neither gives the peek, and opacity leaves the rows focusable. A clipping box with a mask, plus `inert`, does both.
- Putting the tab underline inside a scroll container without the strip. The underline would stay put while the tabs scroll. The whole `TabList` (with its underline) scrolls together inside one wrapper.

## Notes

- `TRAFFIC_TABS`, `BarListItem`, `BarListTab` and `BarListMetric` are exported. With neither `tabs` nor `items`, the card shows the traffic sample.
- `icon` takes any 16px node. The sample countries use small text code chips rather than flag images, so the card works offline.
- Pass `metricToggle={false}` for a plain caption, or control `metric` from outside.

## Definition of done

The left card shows Devices, Browsers, Operating systems and Countries tabs and a "VISITORS % #" caption. Under Devices are Desktop 61%, Mobile 31% and Tablet 8%, with blue bars at full, about half and about an eighth of the width. Browsers shows four rows, then a faded Opera row under a chevron pill. Clicking the pill unfolds Opera, Samsung Internet and Other, and the chevron turns up. Back on Devices, clicking the caption changes Desktop to 3,120. Hovering a row shows the other number. The right card lists Pages in views: / 12,480, /pricing 6,210, /components 4,880, then /blog/launch peeking. Mono turns every bar grey.
