# Build: Breadcrumb

A `<nav>` holding an ordered list of ancestor pages, with a small chevron placed between items automatically. Each `BreadcrumbItem` decides its own element: a Next `Link` when it has `href`, a `<button>` when it has `onClick`, and a non-interactive `aria-current="page"` label when it is `current`. Ancestors are quiet tertiary text that lifts to secondary on a soft hover pill; the current page sits one step darker and never reacts.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Ancestor-page trail with auto-inserted chevrons; each item is a link, a button or the current page, with optional 16px icons.

- Category: navigation
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. `Breadcrumb` runs `Children.toArray(children).filter(isValidElement)`, which drops `null`, `false` and stray strings, so conditional items can be written inline. It maps the survivors into a `<Fragment key={item.key ?? index}>` and prepends a `ChevronRightSmall` (`size-3 shrink-0 text-text-tertiary`, `aria-hidden`) before every item except the first. Consumers never place separators by hand.
2. The wrapper is `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` (override with `aria-label`) set to `flex w-full items-center overflow-x-auto` with the scrollbar hidden (`[scrollbar-width:none]` plus `[&::-webkit-scrollbar]:hidden`). Inside, an `<ol>` lays items out with `gap-2.5` and `px-1`. A long trail scrolls sideways instead of wrapping, and every item is `whitespace-nowrap`.
3. `BreadcrumbItem` builds one `content` fragment: an optional `icon` component at `size-4 shrink-0` with `aria-hidden`, then `children`. The icon inherits the item colour.
4. With `current`, the item is an `<li aria-current="page">` in `text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary`, with no hover or focus styles.
5. Otherwise the `<li>` wraps a Next `Link` (when `href` is set) or a `<button type="button">` (when it is not) sharing one class string: `-mx-1 rounded-md px-1 py-0.5`, `text-caption-1-medium text-text-tertiary`, `hover:bg-background-primary-hover hover:text-text-secondary`, a 150ms colour transition and a `focus-visible:ring-2` focus ring. The `-mx-1` cancels the `px-1`, so the hover pill grows outward and the text stays exactly on the 10px rhythm.
6. The chevron gets `rtl:rotate-180` from the shared chevron helper, so the trail reads right-to-left with arrows pointing the right way without any prop.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `item gap = gap-2.5 (10px)`
  The Figma breadcrumb (node 3731:3011) spaces chevrons 10px from each label. The interactive items use `-mx-1 px-1` so their hover pill does not change this spacing.
- `chevron = size-3 (12px), 12×12 viewBox, 1.5px stroke`
  Small enough to read as punctuation rather than a control at the 12px caption type size. It uses `currentColor`, so `text-text-tertiary` sets its colour.
- `type style = text-caption-1-medium`
  Caption 1 Medium (12/16) is the Figma spec. A breadcrumb sits above a page title and must stay visually subordinate to it.
- `hover transition = 150ms transition-colors`
  Matches the kit's other ghost surfaces, so moving the pointer along the trail feels like the rest of the UI.

## API

```ts
function Breadcrumb(props: { children: ReactNode; "aria-label"?: string; className?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLElement> }): JSX.Element
function BreadcrumbItem(props: { children?: ReactNode; icon?: IconComponent; href?: string; onClick?: () => void; current?: boolean; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `Breadcrumb.aria-label: string` — default `"Breadcrumb"`
  Accessible name of the `<nav>` landmark.
- `BreadcrumbItem.href: string`
  Renders the item as a Next `Link`.
- `BreadcrumbItem.onClick: () => void`
  Used when there is no `href`: the item renders as a `<button type="button">`.
- `BreadcrumbItem.current: boolean` — default `false`
  Marks the active page with `aria-current="page"`. Not interactive, darker text.
- `BreadcrumbItem.icon: ComponentType<{ className?: string }>`
  16px leading icon component that inherits the item colour.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function Breadcrumb({
  children,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel = "Breadcrumb",
  className,
  ref,
}: BreadcrumbProps) {
  const items = Children.toArray(children).filter(isValidElement);

  return (
    <nav
      ref={ref}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      className={cx(
        "flex w-full items-center overflow-x-auto [scrollbar-width:none] [&::-webkit-scrollbar]:hidden",
        className,
      )}
    >
      <ol className="flex items-center gap-2.5 px-1">
        {items.map((item, index) => (
          <Fragment key={item.key ?? index}>
            {/* An <ol> may only hold <li>s; aria-hidden keeps the separator out of
                the item count screen readers announce. */}
            {index > 0 && (
              <li aria-hidden className="flex shrink-0">
                <ChevronRightSmall className="size-3 text-text-tertiary" />
              </li>
            )}
            {item}
          </Fragment>
        ))}
      </ol>
    </nav>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component is stateless markup with no listeners, timers or effects.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing moves. The only animation is a 150ms colour transition on hover, which is not motion and is left as is.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not put separators in the children. `Breadcrumb` inserts a chevron before every item after the first, so a hand-written "/" would show up as an extra crumb with a chevron in front of it.
- Do not mark the current page with an `href`. When `current` is true the item ignores `href` and `onClick`. That is intentional: a link to the page you are on is noise for screen-reader users.
- Do not wrap the trail to a second line. It is designed to scroll horizontally with a hidden scrollbar, so keep the `whitespace-nowrap` on items when restyling them.
- Do not pass an icon element (`icon={<RiHome5Line />}`). The prop takes the component so the item can size it to 16px.

## Notes

- An item with neither `href` nor `onClick` and without `current` still renders a `<button>` that does nothing. Use `current` for the active page.
- The file imports `next/link`. Outside Next, swap it for a plain `<a>` or your router's link.

## Definition of done

Three items render on one line with a chevron between each pair and none before the first. Hovering an ancestor darkens its text and shows a rounded tinted background without moving any text. The last item is darker, has `aria-current="page"` and does not react to hover or clicks. Tab reaches only the ancestor items, each showing a focus ring. In an RTL container the chevrons point left. A trail wider than its container scrolls sideways with no visible scrollbar.

# Build: Browser Chrome Frame

A title bar plus a content well, drawn entirely in CSS, wrapped around anything you want to present as a live site rather than a picture of one. The address pill copies the URL and confirms with a checkmark that draws along its own path and holds for 1600 ms. Every state change happens inside a fixed-width pill, so nothing in the bar ever reflows.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A macOS window frame with hover-revealed traffic lights and an address pill whose check draws itself on copy.

- Category: primitive
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The frame is a flex column: a `shrink-0` title bar and a `min-h-0 flex-1` content well. `min-h-0` is what lets the well actually shrink inside a flex parent — without it a tall child pushes the frame past its container and the rounded bottom corners leave the viewport.
2. The three window buttons are `11px` circles filled with the real macOS values (`#ff5f57`, `#febc2e`, `#28c840`) holding a `7px` SVG glyph at `opacity: 0`. The cluster is one Tailwind `group`, so hovering anywhere in the title bar fades all three glyphs in together — which is how the system chrome behaves, and hovering one button to reveal only that button is the tell of a reimplementation.
3. Copying goes through `navigator.clipboard?.writeText?.(url)`. That returns `undefined` outside a secure context and a rejecting promise when the document is not focused, so both branches resolve to an explicit `failed` state rather than a swallowed catch. A pill that silently does nothing reads as a broken button.
4. The confirmation checkmark carries `pathLength="1"` and `strokeDasharray="1"`, so `strokeDashoffset` moves between exactly `1` and `0` regardless of the path coordinates, and a single 320 ms `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` transition draws it. The link icon it replaces crossfades over 180 ms in an absolutely-positioned 12 px box, so the icon slot never changes size.
5. Both text labels — the URL and the confirmation — sit in the same CSS grid cell (`col-start-1 row-start-1`) and swap by opacity. The pill therefore cannot resize between states, so the URL never shifts sideways under the cursor that just clicked it.
6. A single `setTimeout` ref holds the return to idle. Every entry point clears it first, so clicking the pill three times in a row extends one confirmation rather than queuing three overlapping ones.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `COPIED_MS = 1600`
  How long the confirmed state holds. Deliberately long: at the 600-800 ms most implementations use, a user who looks back at the pill after moving their eyes to the clipboard target has already missed it, and clicks again. 1600 ms survives a glance away and back.
- `DRAW_MS = 320`
  Stroke-draw duration for the check. Below ~200 ms the draw is indistinguishable from a hard appear, which throws away the only cue that says "this just happened now"; past ~450 ms the confirmation is still arriving after the user has moved on.
- `FADE_MS = 180`
  Crossfade for the icon and label swap, and the traffic-light glyph reveal. Shorter than the draw on purpose — the check should finish last, so the eye lands on the completed mark rather than on a half-drawn one under settled text.
- `traffic light fills = #ff5f57 / #febc2e / #28c840`
  The actual macOS window-button values. This component reproduces a specific piece of system chrome, so these are content, not theme: recolouring them to the site palette turns the frame from "a browser" into "a diagram of a browser" and the recognition is gone.
- `dot size = 11px`
  Matches the system button diameter at 1x. At 8px the glyphs are unreadable; past ~14px the bar starts to read as a toy illustration rather than chrome.

## API

```ts
function BrowserChromeFrame(props: { url: string; children: ReactNode; label?: string; onCopy?: (url: string) => void; copiedDurationMs?: number; className?: string; bodyClassName?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `url: string`
  Shown in the address pill and written to the clipboard on click.
- `children: ReactNode`
  The framed content. Sized by the frame, not by itself.
- `label: string`
  Display text for the pill. Defaults to `url` with the scheme stripped, which is what a browser shows.
- `onCopy: (url: string) => void`
  Fires after a successful clipboard write, never on failure.
- `copiedDurationMs: number` — default `1600`
  How long the confirmed state holds before returning to idle.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the outer frame.
- `bodyClassName: string`
  Merged onto the content well below the title bar.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const COPIED_MS = 1600;
const DRAW_MS = 320;
const FADE_MS = 180;

type CopyState = 'idle' | 'copied' | 'failed';

export function BrowserChromeFrame({
  url,
  children,
  label,
  onCopy,
  copiedDurationMs = COPIED_MS,
  className,
  bodyClassName,
}: BrowserChromeFrameProps) {
  const [state, setState] = useState<CopyState>('idle');
  const timer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  const notify = useRef(onCopy);
  notify.current = onCopy;

  const reset = useCallback(() => {
    if (timer.current !== null) {
      clearTimeout(timer.current);
      timer.current = null;
    }
  }, []);

  // A pending timer outlives the component unless it is cleared. Left alone it
  // calls setState on an unmounted tree — React 19 no longer warns about that,
  // which makes it quieter, not less of a leak.
  useEffect(() => reset, [reset]);

  const copy = useCallback(() => {
    // `navigator.clipboard` is undefined outside a secure context and its
    // promise rejects when the document is not focused. Both are ordinary, so
    // the failure has a state of its own rather than a swallowed catch: a pill
    // that silently does nothing reads as a broken button.
    const write = navigator.clipboard?.writeText?.(url);
    if (!write) {
      reset();
      setState('failed');
      timer.current = setTimeout(() => setState('idle'), copiedDurationMs);
      return;
    }

    void write.then(
      () => {
        reset();
        setState('copied');
        notify.current?.(url);
        timer.current = setTimeout(() => setState('idle'), copiedDurationMs);
      },
      () => {
        reset();
        setState('failed');
        timer.current = setTimeout(() => setState('idle'), copiedDurationMs);
      },
    );
  }, [url, copiedDurationMs, reset]);

  const copied = state === 'copied';
  const failed = state === 'failed';

  // Reduced motion keeps the state change and drops only the tweening: the
  // check is already fully drawn on the frame it appears, and the two labels
  // hard-swap instead of crossfading. The confirmation is still legible for
  // the same 1600 ms — the information was never the animation.
  const drawMs = reduced ? 0 : DRAW_MS;
  const fadeMs = reduced ? 0 : FADE_MS;
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** One `clearTimeout` on the single pending reset timer, via an effect that returns the same `reset` callback every entry point already uses. There are no listeners, no rAF and no tweens — all motion is CSS transitions on mounted nodes, which the browser discards with the node.

**Reduced motion.** The state machine is untouched: clicking still copies, the check still replaces the link icon, and the confirmation still holds for the full 1600 ms. What goes to zero is `DRAW_MS` and `FADE_MS`, so the check appears already fully drawn and the labels hard-swap instead of crossfading. The traffic-light glyphs still reveal on hover, without the fade.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Swapping the icon element instead of stacking both. Replacing a link icon with a check changes the rendered width by a pixel or two, the flex row re-solves, and the URL text jumps sideways at the exact moment the user is reading the confirmation.
- Letting the label change the pill width. If the URL and "Copied" are the same node with different text, the pill resizes and the whole title bar reflows. Stacking them in one grid cell keeps the width pinned to the longer of the two, permanently.
- Hard-coding the measured path length for the dash animation. The first time anyone nudges a coordinate in the checkmark, the offset no longer matches the path and the stroke either starts partly drawn or never completes. `pathLength="1"` renormalises so the animation is coordinate-independent.
- Assuming `navigator.clipboard` exists. On `http://` origins and inside some embedded webviews it is `undefined`, and calling it throws a TypeError that takes the click handler down with it. On a secure origin it still rejects if the document is not focused — a case that happens constantly in dev tools.
- Not clearing the reset timer before starting a new one. Rapid clicks queue several timeouts and the confirmation flickers off at the first one's deadline rather than the last one's, so the state disappears while the user is still clicking.
- Leaving the timer pending on unmount. It fires into a disposed tree; React 19 no longer warns, which makes it quieter, not less of a leak.
- Reading the reduced-motion state and disabling the confirmation itself. The check is information, not decoration. Only the tweening is dropped.

## Notes

- The `group-hover` glyph reveal has no touch equivalent, and correctly so: there is no hover on touch, and firing the reveal on press would light up three buttons the user cannot click.
- The content well sets `overflow-hidden` and `bg-bg`, which is what gives the embed its edge. Framing exists as much to bound the content as to decorate it.

## Definition of done

Hover the title bar and all three glyphs fade in together. Click the pill: the link icon fades out, a checkmark draws itself left to right, "Copied" replaces the URL, the pill does not change width by a single pixel, and the state returns to the URL 1600 ms later. Click three times quickly and you get one confirmation that ends 1600 ms after the last click. On an `http://` origin the pill shows "Press to copy" instead of a silent no-op. With reduced motion the check is fully drawn on the first frame it appears.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Chord-Synced Particle Burst

A burst is N notes a fixed interval apart, each with a visual flare that has to appear on the same beat as its note. Audio is scheduled on `AudioContext.currentTime`, which is sample-accurate; the flares are driven by a rAF loop, which is not. This hook schedules both from one set of offsets and converts the audio times into wall-clock times via `getOutputTimestamp()`, so a flare is never more than one frame from its note however long the burst runs.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Fires an arpeggio and its visual flares off one schedule, so each flash lands on its own note.

- Category: primitive
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Notes are scheduled ahead of time on the audio clock: for step `i`, `at = ctx.currentTime + LEAD + step * i`, then `gain.setValueAtTime(peak, at)` and `gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, at + decay)`. Nothing is timed by `setTimeout`, so a busy main thread cannot skew a note.
2. `audibleAt(ctx, at)` converts that audio time into a `performance.now()` millisecond value. `ctx.getOutputTimestamp()` returns a matched pair — the sample frame currently leaving the output device and the wall-clock instant it left — so the mapping is `ts.performanceTime + (at - ts.contextTime) * 1000`. Hardware output latency is already inside that pair; adding `outputLatency` on top double-counts it.
3. When `getOutputTimestamp` is unavailable, or has not rendered a frame yet and returns `contextTime: 0`, the fallback is `performance.now() + (at - ctx.currentTime) * 1000 + min(outputLatency, 0.05) * 1000`. `currentTime` is the write head, not the speaker, so the latency has to be added back in this branch only.
4. Each step is pushed onto a queue sorted by wall-clock time, and a rAF loop pops every entry whose time has passed and calls `onStep(index, total)`. Overlapping bursts merge into one sorted queue rather than one loop per burst.
5. The loop is subscribed only while the queue is non-empty — `useRaf(tick, running)` — and unsubscribes itself on the frame it drains the last step, so an idle instrument holds no animation frame.
6. The `AudioContext` is constructed inside `fire()`, which the caller invokes from a click handler, and `resume()` is called if the browser still hands it back suspended. Constructing it at mount produces a suspended context whose scheduled notes are silently discarded.
7. `fire(steps)` caps at `chord.length` and returns the count actually scheduled, so a caller that has fewer flares available than the chord has notes hears exactly as many notes as it shows.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `step = 0.46`
  Seconds between notes, and the same number the visuals use. Around 130 bpm in eighths — fast enough to read as one gesture rather than four separate events, slow enough that each flare is individually visible. Below ~0.2s the flares smear into one flash; above ~0.7s the burst stops sounding like a chord and starts sounding like four taps.
- `gain = 0.15`
  Peak amplitude of a single sine. Four notes overlapping at 1.0 would sum past full scale and hard-clip the destination; 0.15 leaves headroom for the tails of earlier notes still decaying under later ones.
- `SILENCE = 0.001`
  -60 dB, the ramp target. `exponentialRampToValueAtTime` is mathematically undefined at 0 and throws; ramping to a literal 0 is the single most common Web Audio error. -60 dB is inaudible.
- `decay = 0.4`
  Seconds from peak to silence. Slightly shorter than the 0.46s step so a note has essentially finished before the next arrives — overlap past about 0.6s turns the arpeggio into a chord and the individual attacks stop being audible.
- `TAIL = 0.1`
  Extra seconds before `osc.stop()`. Stopping an oscillator exactly at the end of its ramp truncates the last samples and can produce a faint click; 0.1s of -60 dB signal costs nothing and guarantees the stop is inaudible.
- `LEAD = 0.02`
  Seconds of lead before the first note. One render quantum at 44.1 kHz is 128 samples, about 2.9 ms; 20 ms covers several quanta plus the jitter in getting from the click to the scheduling call. Scheduling at exactly `currentTime` means the first note is already partly in the past and its attack is clipped.
- `MAX_LATENCY = 0.05`
  Ceiling on the fallback latency compensation, in seconds. Bluetooth output can report 150-300 ms; delaying the visual by that much to match makes the click itself feel broken. Capping trades exact sync on pathological hardware for a UI that still responds.

## API

```ts
function useBurstAudioSync(options?: { chord?: readonly number[]; step?: number; gain?: number; decay?: number; onStep?: (index: number, total: number) => void; muted?: boolean }): { fire: (steps?: number) => number; unlocked: boolean }
```

- `chord: readonly number[]` — default `[261.63, 329.63, 392, 523.25]`
  One frequency in Hz per step. Caps how many notes a single `fire` can schedule.
- `step: number` — default `0.46`
  Seconds between steps. Shared by the audio schedule and the visual queue.
- `gain: number` — default `0.15`
  Peak gain of one note. Divided by the note count when the stagger collapses.
- `decay: number` — default `0.4`
  Seconds for the exponential ramp from `gain` down to -60 dB.
- `onStep: (index: number, total: number) => void`
  Called on the frame nearest each note. `index` is the position in the chord.
- `muted: boolean` — default `false`
  Skips audio entirely. Visual steps still fire on the same schedule, so the UI is unchanged.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** `exponentialRampToValueAtTime` is undefined at 0, so silence is -60 dB. */
const SILENCE = 0.001;
/** Seconds of dead air after the ramp before the oscillator is stopped. */
const TAIL = 0.1;
/** Seconds of lead before the first note. Absorbs one graph render quantum. */
const LEAD = 0.02;
/** Ceiling on latency compensation, in seconds. */
const MAX_LATENCY = 0.05;

/**
 * Wall-clock time at which a sample scheduled at `contextTime` is heard.
 *
 * The `getOutputTimestamp()` pair is measured *at the output device*, so the
 * hardware latency is already folded into it — adding `outputLatency` on top
 * would double-count it and push every flare late.
 */
function audibleAt(ctx: AudioContext, contextTime: number): number {
  if (typeof ctx.getOutputTimestamp === 'function') {
    const ts = ctx.getOutputTimestamp();
    // Before the graph has rendered anything both fields are 0. Trusting that
    // pair maps every future note to wall-clock zero, and the whole burst
    // flashes at once on the very next frame.
    if (
      ts.contextTime !== undefined &&
      ts.performanceTime !== undefined &&
      ts.contextTime > 0
    ) {
      return ts.performanceTime + (contextTime - ts.contextTime) * 1000;
    }
  }
  // Fallback. `currentTime` is the time of the sample being *written*, which
  // runs ahead of the speaker by roughly the output latency, so add it back.
  const reported = Number.isFinite(ctx.outputLatency)
    ? ctx.outputLatency
    : ctx.baseLatency;
  const latency = Number.isFinite(reported) ? Math.min(reported, MAX_LATENCY) : 0;
  return performance.now() + (contextTime - ctx.currentTime) * 1000 + latency * 1000;
}

export function useBurstAudioSync(options: UseBurstAudioSyncOptions = {}): BurstAudioSync {
  const { chord = C_MAJOR, step = 0.46, gain = 0.15, decay = 0.4 } = options;
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  const [unlocked, setUnlocked] = useState(false);
  const [running, setRunning] = useState(false);

  const ctxRef = useRef<AudioContext | null>(null);
  const queue = useRef<QueuedStep[]>([]);

  // Everything `fire` reads lives in one ref, so `fire` keeps a stable
  // identity and can be handed to a memoised child without re-binding it on
  // every render.
  const config = useRef({ chord, step, gain, decay, reduced, options });
  config.current = { chord, step, gain, decay, reduced, options };

  const fire = useCallback((steps?: number): number => {
    const cfg = config.current;
    const wanted = steps ?? cfg.chord.length;
    const total = Math.min(Math.max(Math.trunc(wanted), 0), cfg.chord.length);
    if (total === 0) return 0;

    // Reduced motion collapses the arpeggio into a single chord: the feedback
    // survives — it was asked for by a click, so it is not decoration — but
    // nothing travels across the screen.
    const stagger = cfg.reduced ? 0 : cfg.step;

    let ctx: AudioContext | null = null;
    if (!cfg.options.muted) {
      ctx = ctxRef.current;
      if (!ctx) {
        // Constructed here and only here: we are inside the gesture handler
        // that called `fire`, which is the one moment the autoplay policy
        // lets a context start.
        ctx = new AudioContext();
        ctxRef.current = ctx;
        setUnlocked(true);
      }
      if (ctx.state === 'suspended') void ctx.resume();
    }

    let baseMs = performance.now();

    if (ctx) {
      const start = ctx.currentTime + LEAD;
      // Four sines at full gain sum to 4x the peak and clip the destination.
      // They only ever overlap when the stagger is gone, so divide then.
      const peak = stagger === 0 ? cfg.gain / total : cfg.gain;

      for (let i = 0; i < total; i++) {
        const freq = cfg.chord[i];
        if (freq === undefined) continue;
        const at = start + stagger * i;

        const osc = ctx.createOscillator();
        const env = ctx.createGain();
        osc.type = 'sine';
        osc.frequency.value = freq;
        env.gain.setValueAtTime(peak, at);
        // `cfg.decay`, not the closed-over `decay`. This callback is memoised
        // with an empty dep array — deliberately, so a parent re-render never
        // changes its identity — which freezes every prop it closes over at
        // first render. Every other value here already comes through the ref;
        // these two lines read the prop directly, so changing `decay` after
        // mount left the envelope on whatever the first render happened to be.
        env.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(SILENCE, at + cfg.decay);
        osc.connect(env);
        env.connect(ctx.destination);
        osc.start(at);
        osc.stop(at + cfg.decay + TAIL);
        // Without this every burst leaves two live nodes attached to the
        // destination. A few hundred bursts and the graph audibly degrades.
        osc.onended = () => {
          osc.disconnect();
          env.disconnect();
        };
      }

      baseMs = audibleAt(ctx, start);
    }

    const q = queue.current;
    for (let i = 0; i < total; i++) {
      q.push({ at: baseMs + stagger * i * 1000, index: i, total });
    }
    // Two bursts can overlap; the drain below assumes the head is the
    // earliest step, so keep the queue sorted rather than scanning it.
    q.sort((a, b) => a.at - b.at);
    setRunning(true);

    return total;
  }, []);

  // The loop only exists while something is queued. An always-on rAF for a
  // widget that fires twice a minute keeps the browser's animation frame
  // pipeline alive for nothing.
  useRaf(() => {
    const q = queue.current;
    const now = performance.now();
    while (q.length > 0) {
      const head = q[0];
      if (head === undefined || head.at > now) break;
      q.shift();
      config.current.options.onStep?.(head.index, head.total);
    }
    if (q.length === 0) setRunning(false);
  }, running);

  useEffect(
    () => () => {
      queue.current.length = 0;
      const ctx = ctxRef.current;
      ctxRef.current = null;
      // close() stops every scheduled note and releases the hardware. Chrome
      // caps a document at ~6 live contexts and throws on the seventh.
      if (ctx && ctx.state !== 'closed') void ctx.close();
    },
    [],
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The unmount cleanup empties the pending-step queue and calls `ctx.close()`, which cancels every note still scheduled in the future and releases the hardware. The rAF subscription is owned by `useRaf` and released when `running` goes false or the component unmounts. Each oscillator disconnects itself and its gain node in `onended`.

**Reduced motion.** The stagger collapses to zero: all notes are scheduled at the same audio time and every `onStep` fires on one frame, so the burst is a chord rather than a sequence travelling across the screen. Audio is not muted — it is direct feedback for a click, not ambient motion — but the per-note gain is divided by the note count because the notes now overlap.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Constructing the `AudioContext` at mount. Outside a user gesture the browser hands back a `suspended` context; `osc.start(at)` on it neither throws nor plays, so the bug presents as "audio just does not work" with a clean console.
- Ramping the gain to 0. `exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0, t)` throws a `RangeError` — the target must be strictly positive. Ramp to 0.001 instead.
- Using `setTimeout` for the notes so audio and visuals share a timer. Both then inherit the main thread's jitter, and on a frame that takes 80 ms the note lands 80 ms late while the sample-accurate alternative would not have moved.
- Adding `outputLatency` on top of a `getOutputTimestamp()` mapping. That pair is measured at the output device and already contains the latency, so adding it again pushes every flare a full hardware buffer behind its note — the exact defect the conversion exists to prevent.
- Trusting `getOutputTimestamp()` immediately after construction. Before the graph has rendered a quantum both fields read 0, which maps every future note to wall-clock zero and dumps the entire burst onto the next frame.
- Never disconnecting the oscillator and gain. Both stay attached to the destination after the note ends; a few hundred bursts in one session and the graph is carrying hundreds of dead nodes, which shows up as rising CPU and eventually distortion.
- Keeping a rAF loop running so the flare queue can be polled. The queue is empty almost all the time — subscribe on `fire`, unsubscribe on the frame the last step drains.
- Letting the notes overlap at full gain when reduced motion collapses the stagger. Four sines at 0.15 sum to 0.6 and the summed peak clips; the per-note gain has to be divided by the note count in the collapsed case.
- Forgetting `ctx.close()` on unmount. Chrome allows roughly six live `AudioContext` objects per document and throws on the next one, so a page that mounts this in a list silently stops producing sound after the sixth item.

## Notes

- The hook deliberately exposes no `play()` that can be called from an effect. `fire` is the only entry point and its contract is "call me from a gesture handler" — encoding the autoplay policy in the API rather than in a comment.
- Two clocks, two policies. Reduced motion collapses the stagger but does not mute anything: the sound is feedback for a click the user made, not ambient decoration, and silencing it removes information.
- `chord` is any frequency list. A minor triad is `[261.63, 311.13, 392]`; a single frequency makes it a one-shot tick with the same scheduling guarantees.

## Definition of done

Click a string: four flares appear 0.46s apart and each one coincides with a note — watch the fourth flare and hear the fourth note land together, not a beat apart. Click a string at either end and only one flare appears and only one note sounds. Nothing plays before the first click. Toggle sound off and the flares keep exactly the same timing. With reduced motion on, all four strings light in the same frame and you hear a chord. Unmount mid-burst and the remaining notes do not play.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Button

A native `<button>` (and an `<a>` twin, `ButtonLink`) whose look is four style maps indexed by `variant` and `size`. The component draws its own icons from a component reference, so the consumer cannot pass the wrong icon size. The gradient fills of the primary and danger variants live in two `@utility` classes in the theme sheet, which fade a hover gradient in on a `::before` layer because CSS cannot interpolate `background-image`.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Primary, secondary, ghost and danger buttons in three sizes, with gradient fills that fade on hover and a soft press.

- Category: action
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Every class comes from one `sortCx` object: `base` (layout, focus ring, press motion), `size` (height, padding, radius and type style per tier), `iconOnlySize` (the square override), `icon` (glyph size per tier), `label` (inner padding) and `variant`. `cx` is a `tailwind-merge` instance extended with the kit's custom type scale, so a consumer `className` such as `h-10` replaces the size tier's `h-9` rather than both landing in the class list.
2. Icons are props that take a component (`leadingIcon={RiAddLine}`), not an element. The button renders it with the tier's size class — 20px at medium, 18px at small, 14px at xs — plus `aria-hidden`. Navigation glyphs (left/right arrows, sidebar fold) are listed in `directionalIconClass` and get `rtl:rotate-180`, so a "Next" arrow points the reading direction in Arabic or Hebrew without the caller knowing.
3. Primary and danger paint with `bg-button-primary` and `bg-button-danger`. Each sets the default gradient as `background-image`, then a `::before` with `inset: 0`, `z-index: -1` and `border-radius: inherit` holds the hover gradient at opacity 0. Hover fades that layer to 1 over `--button-transition-ms`. `isolation: isolate` on the button is what keeps the negative-z layer above the button's own background and below its label.
4. The press is `button-press-motion`: colours transition in 150ms while `transform` takes 420ms back to rest. `:active` scales to 0.98 and drops the transform duration to 220ms, so the button goes down fast and comes back slowly. Hover never touches `transform`, so hover colour changes never inherit the long press timing.
5. Disabled works for both `disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"`. The second matters when a disabled button must stay focusable so a tooltip can explain why. Every variant styles both selectors and the press motion turns itself off for both.
6. `type` defaults to `"button"`. A bare `<button>` inside a `<form>` is a submit button, so a Cancel or "Add row" button would otherwise submit the form it sits in.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `heights = 36 / 32 / 24 px (medium / small / xs)`
  Taken 1:1 from the Figma variant matrix. Medium matches the kit's inputs (also 36px), so a button next to a field lines up with no wrapper. Xs exists for dense surfaces such as calendar event cards and is the only tier that switches to the 12px caption type style.
- `small icon-only size = size-8 p-0`
  An 18px icon plus 8px padding on each side gives 34px, but Figma pins the small square at 32. Removing the padding and forcing the size keeps an icon button the same height as a small labelled button beside it. Medium needs no override because 8 + 20 + 8 is already 36.
- `--button-transition-ms = 150ms`
  Shared by the hover-gradient fade and the colour transitions, so the fill and the label change together. Much shorter and the gradient fade looks like a snap; much longer and fast pointer sweeps across a toolbar leave a trail of half-lit buttons.
- `press = scale(0.98), 220ms down / 420ms back`
  Two percent is enough to feel without visibly moving the label off its baseline. The asymmetric duration is the point: press feedback has to be immediate, and the return can be soft because nothing is waiting on it.

## API

```ts
function Button(props: ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> & { variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "danger"; size?: "medium" | "small" | "xs"; iconOnly?: boolean; leadingIcon?: IconComponent; trailingIcon?: IconComponent; ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement> }): JSX.Element
function ButtonLink(props: AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement> & { …same visual props }): JSX.Element
```

- `variant: "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "danger"` — default `"primary"`
  Gradient fill (primary, danger), bordered surface (secondary) or no surface until hovered (ghost).
- `size: "medium" | "small" | "xs"` — default `"medium"`
  36, 32 or 24px tall. Sets padding, radius, icon size and type style together.
- `iconOnly: boolean` — default `false`
  Square button showing only `leadingIcon`. Children and `trailingIcon` are ignored, so pass `aria-label`.
- `leadingIcon: ComponentType<{ className?: string }>`
  Icon component drawn before the label at the tier's size. Directional glyphs mirror in RTL.
- `trailingIcon: ComponentType<{ className?: string }>`
  Icon component drawn after the label.
- `type: "button" | "submit" | "reset"` — default `"button"`
  Native button type. Defaults to `button` so it never submits a surrounding form by accident.
- `className: string`
  Merged through `tailwind-merge`, so conflicting utilities replace the defaults instead of fighting them.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function Button({
  variant = "primary",
  size = "medium",
  iconOnly = false,
  leadingIcon: Leading,
  trailingIcon: Trailing,
  children,
  className,
  type = "button",
  ref,
  ...props
}: ButtonProps) {
  return (
    <button
      ref={ref}
      type={type}
      className={cx(
        styles.base,
        styles.size[size],
        styles.variant[variant],
        iconOnly && styles.iconOnlySize[size],
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      {Leading ? <Leading className={cx(styles.icon[size], directionalIconClass(Leading))} aria-hidden /> : null}
      {!iconOnly && children !== undefined && children !== null && (
        <span className={styles.label[size]}>{children}</span>
      )}
      {!iconOnly && Trailing ? (
        <Trailing className={cx(styles.icon[size], directionalIconClass(Trailing))} aria-hidden />
      ) : null}
    </button>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component is stateless markup with no listeners, timers or effects. All motion is CSS transitions that end on their own.

**Reduced motion.** The press scale and every transition on `button-press-motion` are removed under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, so states change instantly and the button never moves. The hover-gradient layer still swaps, because colour feedback carries meaning.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Swapping the gradient in `:hover` with another `background-image`. It snaps, because `background-image` does not interpolate. The fade only works because the hover gradient sits on its own layer and only its `opacity` changes.
- Removing `isolation: isolate` from the gradient utilities. The `::before` sits at `z-index: -1`, and without a new stacking context it slips behind the button's parent background, so the hover state disappears on any card with a fill.
- Passing an icon element (`leadingIcon={<RiAddLine />}`). The prop takes the component, so the button can size it. An element bypasses the size class and the glyph renders at Remix Icon's default 24px, which breaks the 36px height.
- Shipping an icon-only button without `aria-label`. The glyph is `aria-hidden` and there is no text, so screen readers announce just "button".
- Relying on the browser default `type`. Inside a form it is `submit`. The component defaults to `"button"`, so pass `type="submit"` explicitly on the button that should submit.
- Putting `transition-all` on a consumer `className`. It overrides the split timing of `button-press-motion` and gives hover colour changes the slow 420ms press-return curve.

## Notes

- The style maps are exported as `buttonStyles`, so another control (a toolbar toggle, a file input label) can share the exact variant classes without wrapping a `<button>` in a `<button>`.
- The kit's `IconButton`, `CloseButton` and `LinkButton` are separate items with their own shapes. `Button iconOnly` is the square form of a full button, with the same gradient and border.

## Definition of done

Four variants render side by side at the same height. Hover the primary button and its gradient fades smoothly to the lighter hover gradient (no snap). Press any button and it dips slightly, then eases back more slowly than it went down. Tab to a button and a 2px focus ring appears offset from the edge. Disabled buttons, including `aria-disabled` ones, show the muted palette, do not dip on press and show a not-allowed cursor. An icon-only small button is exactly as tall as a small labelled one. A button inside a form does not submit it unless `type="submit"`.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Button Group

A `role="group"` container that owns the border, radius and shadow, with plain `<button>` items inside it divided by 1px hairlines. Only the container is rounded; `overflow-hidden` clips the first and last items to its corners, so the items themselves stay square and never need first/last-child logic. A `selected` item keeps the hover fill and announces itself with `aria-pressed`, which makes the same markup work as an action row, a single-select range picker or a multi-select formatting bar.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Secondary buttons fused into one bordered strip with hairline dividers, for toolbars, range pickers and pressed toggles.

- Category: action
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The container carries every outer surface: `rounded-2lg` (10px), a 1px `border-border-button-group`, `shadow-xs` and the primary background. `divide-x divide-border-button-default` draws a left border on every item except the first, so the dividers come from the parent and adding or removing items never leaves a doubled or missing line.
2. `overflow-hidden` on the container is what rounds the outer items. A hover or pressed fill on the first item would otherwise paint square corners over the container's rounded border. Clipping at the container means the items carry no radius at all.
3. Item heights are 34px (medium) and 30px (small) because the container's 1px top and bottom border add 2px, so the whole strip lands on the kit's 36 / 32px button heights and lines up with a `Button` or input beside it.
4. Focus uses an inset ring (`ring-inset`) plus `focus-visible:relative z-10`. An outset ring would be clipped by the container's `overflow-hidden`, and without the z-index lift the next item's divider paints over the right edge of the ring. `isolate` on the container keeps that z-index local to the group.
5. `selected` maps to the hover fill (`bg-background-primary-hover`) and sets `aria-pressed={selected || undefined}`. Unselected items omit the attribute entirely, so a plain action row is not announced as a set of toggles.
6. Icons are component props rendered by the item at 20px (medium) or 18px (small) with `aria-hidden`; arrow and sidebar glyphs get `rtl:rotate-180` from `directionalIconClass`. With `iconOnly` the item becomes a 34 or 30px square and drops its label, so it needs an `aria-label`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `item height = 34px / 30px (medium / small)`
  The container border adds 1px above and below, so the visible strip is exactly 36 or 32px, matching Button's secondary sizes. Sizing items at 36px would make the group 2px taller than every control next to it.
- `horizontal padding = 12px / 10px`
  Same as Button's secondary tiers, so a labelled item and a standalone button with the same text are the same width.
- `transition = background-color, color 150ms ease`
  Only colour changes. Sweeping the pointer along a toolbar lights each item briefly without a trail, and no transform is involved, so items never shift inside the clipped strip.

## API

```ts
function ButtonGroup(props: { size?: "medium" | "small"; children: ReactNode; className?: string; "aria-label"?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function ButtonGroupItem(props: Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "children"> & { size?: "medium" | "small"; selected?: boolean; iconOnly?: boolean; leadingIcon?: IconComponent; trailingIcon?: IconComponent; children?: ReactNode; ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement> }): JSX.Element
```

- `size: "medium" | "small"` — default `"medium"`
  On `ButtonGroupItem`: 36 or 32px overall strip height, with 20 or 18px icons. Pass the same size to every item in a group.
- `selected: boolean` — default `false`
  On `ButtonGroupItem`: keeps the hover fill and sets `aria-pressed`. Drive it from state for single or multi select.
- `iconOnly: boolean` — default `false`
  On `ButtonGroupItem`: square item showing only `leadingIcon`. Needs `aria-label`.
- `leadingIcon: ComponentType<{ className?: string }>`
  Icon component drawn before the label at the tier's size.
- `trailingIcon: ComponentType<{ className?: string }>`
  Icon component drawn after the label. Ignored when `iconOnly`.
- `aria-label: string`
  On `ButtonGroup`: names the group for assistive tech, for example "Range".
- `className: string`
  Merged through `tailwind-merge` on either element.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const styles = sortCx({
  group: [
    "inline-flex items-stretch isolate",
    "rounded-2lg border border-border-button-group bg-background-primary-default shadow-xs",
    // Hairlines between items, outer corners rounded on the first/last item
    "divide-x divide-border-button-default overflow-hidden",
  ].join(" "),

  item: [
    "inline-flex items-center justify-center gap-1 whitespace-nowrap",
    "bg-background-primary-default text-text-primary font-sans select-none cursor-pointer",
    "transition-[background-color,color] duration-150 ease",
    "outline-none focus-visible:relative focus-visible:z-10 focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-inset focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
    "hover:bg-background-primary-hover active:bg-background-primary-active",
    "disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:bg-background-primary-disabled disabled:text-text-tertiary",
  ].join(" "),

  size: {
    medium: "h-[34px] px-3 text-body-medium",
    small: "h-[30px] px-2.5 text-body-medium",
  },

  iconOnlySize: {
    medium: "w-[34px] px-0",
    small: "w-[30px] px-0",
  },

  icon: {
    medium: "size-5 shrink-0",
    small: "size-[18px] shrink-0",
  },

  selected: "bg-background-primary-hover",
});
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. Both components are stateless markup with no listeners, timers or effects.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing moves. The only motion is a 150ms colour transition on hover, press and selection, which is not spatial and stays as is.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Giving items their own radius or border. The container already draws both, so you get a doubled outline and visible notches where the item corners do not match the 10px outer radius.
- Removing `overflow-hidden` from the container. The first and last items' hover and selected fills then paint square corners over the rounded border.
- Switching the focus ring to an outset `ring-offset`. The container clips it, so keyboard users see no focus indicator at all on the end items.
- Using `selected` without updating it from state. It is purely visual plus `aria-pressed`, so clicking an item does nothing until your handler moves the selection.
- Shipping an `iconOnly` item without `aria-label`. The glyph is `aria-hidden`, so the item is announced as an unnamed button.

## Notes

- For a single-choice switcher with an animated sliding thumb, use a segmented control instead. Button Group is for rows of equal actions where the selected state just stays lit.
- Pass `aria-label` on `ButtonGroup` (for example "Range" or "Text alignment") so screen readers announce what the group of buttons controls.

## Definition of done

Day, Week and Month render as one 36px strip with hairline dividers and rounded outer corners only. Clicking Month moves the lit fill from Week to Month and screen readers report it as pressed. Hovering the first item fills it right into the rounded corner without square edges poking out. Tabbing through shows an inset focus ring that is not clipped and not overlapped by the neighbouring divider. A small group is 32px tall, and icon-only items are square.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Calendar

The Calendar template as one working page. A Day / Week / Month switch and a stepper move through time; the month grid shows up to three chips a day with "+N more", the week and day views place timed events on a 24-hour grid with overlaps side by side and a now line, and pressing any event opens an anchored popover with guests, meeting code, RSVP, Join and Delete. Empty days and hours start a New event, and the inbox holds invitations to accept.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A full calendar page: Day, Week and Month views, anchored event popovers with guests and RSVP, new events, and an invitation inbox.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @internationalized/date@^3.12.4, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. All dates are `@internationalized/date` values. `monthWeeks(anchor)` starts at `startOfWeek(startOfMonth(anchor), "en-US")` and always returns six Sunday-first weeks so the grid keeps its height; `weekDays(anchor)` is the seven days from `startOfWeek(anchor)`. Today and the now line come from fixed constants, never the clock.
2. One `anchor` date drives every view. The stepper calls `stepAnchor(view, anchor, ±1)`, adding a month, a week or a day (month steps clamp 31 Aug to 30 Sep), and `rangeLabel` prints "August 2026", "16 – 22 Aug 2026" or "Thursday, 20 Aug 2026". The header title is always the anchor month.
3. `eventsOn(events, date)` keeps events whose start and end days bracket the date, all-day first and then by start time. A month cell shows them all when there are three or fewer, otherwise two plus a "+N more" button that opens that day.
4. `layoutDay` walks a day's timed events in start order, grouping chains of overlaps into clusters. Each event takes the first column whose last block has ended, and every event in a cluster shares the cluster's column count, so the 10:00 Roadmap review and the 10:30 Vendor call sit side by side at half width.
5. There is one standalone kit `Popover` for every event. Pressing a chip, block or agenda row stores that element in `anchorRef` and sets `openId`, and the popover anchors to it through `triggerRef`. Deleting closes the popover and toasts with Undo, which puts the event back.
6. Each month cell and each hour slot has a full-size background button (`tabIndex=-1`, labelled "New event on …") under pointer-transparent content, so clicking empty space opens New event pre-filled with that day and hour. The dialog remounts with a fresh `key` each time so its fields start from that draft.
7. Sidebar rows are `href="#"` links. One `onClickCapture` on the root maps the link's `aria-label` to a `DASHBOARD_NAV` key and switches the view in state, and any other key shows a placeholder with "Back to Calendar".

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `TODAY = 2026-08-20 (Thursday)`
  Fixed day for the today ring, the Today button and the default anchor, so renders never read the clock.
- `NOW = 10:40`
  Where the red now line sits in today's column in the Week and Day views.
- `HOUR_PX = 48px`
  A 30-minute event is 24px tall, enough for its title; the full day is 1152px and scrolls inside the grid, opening at 07:00.
- `MIN_BLOCK_MIN = 28 minutes`
  Shortest drawn block, so a 15-minute stand-up still shows its title. Overlap detection uses the drawn length too.
- `month rows = 6`
  Always six weeks, so stepping between months never makes the grid jump in height.

## API

```ts
function CalendarTemplate(props: { events?: CalendarEvent[]; invites?: CalendarInvite[]; defaultNotifications?: BellNotification[]; defaultCalendarView?: "day" | "week" | "month"; today?: CalendarDate; defaultView?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `events: CalendarEvent[]` — default `CALENDAR_EVENTS`
  Events on the calendar (28 samples, July to September 2026). Creating, accepting, RSVP and deleting change a local copy.
- `invites: CalendarInvite[]` — default `CALENDAR_INVITES`
  Pending invitations in the inbox. Accepting one adds its event.
- `defaultNotifications: BellNotification[]` — default `CALENDAR_NOTIFICATIONS`
  Initial bell contents; unread items drive the badge count.
- `defaultCalendarView: "day" | "week" | "month"` — default `"month"`
  View shown first.
- `today: CalendarDate` — default `TODAY (2026-08-20)`
  Day the calendar opens on and marks as today.
- `defaultView: string` — default `"calendar"`
  Sidebar key shown first. Any other key shows the placeholder view.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Sunday-first weeks, as the month grid and week view draw them. */
const LOCALE = "en-US";

/** Six full weeks starting on the Sunday on or before the 1st, so the grid never changes height. */
export function monthWeeks(anchor: CalendarDate): CalendarDate[][] {
  const first = startOfWeek(startOfMonth(anchor), LOCALE);
  return Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, w) => Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, d) => first.add({ days: w * 7 + d })));
}

export function weekDays(anchor: CalendarDate): CalendarDate[] {
  const first = startOfWeek(anchor, LOCALE);
  return Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, d) => first.add({ days: d }));
}

/** One step of the stepper. Month steps clamp the day (31 Aug -> 30 Sep). */
export function stepAnchor(view: CalendarView, anchor: CalendarDate, dir: 1 | -1): CalendarDate {
  if (view === "month") return anchor.add({ months: dir });
  if (view === "week") return anchor.add({ weeks: dir });
  return anchor.add({ days: dir });
}

/** "August 2026" · "16 – 22 Aug 2026" · "30 Aug – 5 Sep 2026" · "Thursday, 20 Aug 2026" */
export function rangeLabel(view: CalendarView, anchor: CalendarDate): string {
  if (view === "month") return `${monthName(anchor)} ${anchor.year}`;
  if (view === "day") return `${weekdayName(anchor)}, ${anchor.day} ${shortMonth(anchor)} ${anchor.year}`;
  const days = weekDays(anchor);
  const a = days[0] ?? anchor;
  const b = days[6] ?? anchor;
  if (a.year !== b.year) return `${a.day} ${shortMonth(a)} ${a.year} – ${b.day} ${shortMonth(b)} ${b.year}`;
  if (a.month !== b.month) return `${a.day} ${shortMonth(a)} – ${b.day} ${shortMonth(b)} ${b.year}`;
  return `${a.day} – ${b.day} ${shortMonth(b)} ${b.year}`;
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers, observers or global listeners. The time grid sets its scroll position once in an effect, and the popover anchor is a ref. Overlays and the Toaster clean up their own listeners.

**Reduced motion.** Hover tints on slots, stepper buttons and agenda rows carry `motion-reduce:transition-none`. The popover, modal and segmented control use the kit's own reduced-motion handling; nothing else animates.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Formatting dates with `Intl` in the host time zone. The labels here are built from the `CalendarDate` fields directly, and the chip times format in UTC, so the server and the browser print the same text.
- Laying out overlaps per pair instead of per cluster. A chain A–B–C where A and C do not touch still needs one shared column count, or the blocks have different widths and cover each other.
- Anchoring a popover to state captured at render time. The anchor element is stored in a ref at press time, so the popover follows the chip that was actually pressed, even in a scrolled time grid.
- A row button that unmounts when pressed (Accept or Decline in the inbox) leaves focus on the body, so Escape no longer reaches the popover. Focus moves to the dialog first.
- Leaving the mini calendar in the Day view on its first month. It is keyed by year and month so it follows the stepper.

## Notes

- Composed from kit items: `DashboardSidebar`, `DashboardPageHeader`, `NotificationBellBadge`, `SegmentedControl`, `CalendarEventChip`, `Popover`, `Modal`, `DatePicker`, `DateCalendar`, `Select`, `Input`, `Checkbox`, `Avatar` and `Toaster`. The grids, popover body, inbox and dialog are this item's own files.
- Week starts on Sunday (`en-US`) and times use a 24-hour clock, as in the preview.

## Definition of done

At 1280x800 the sidebar shows Calendar selected, the title reads "August 2026", the month grid starts on Sun 26 Jul and 20 Aug is ringed as today with Stand-up, Team lunch and "+2 more". Pressing Stand-up opens a popover with four guests, the meeting code and Join meeting. "+2 more" opens the Day view for Thursday, 20 Aug 2026 with a now line at 10:40. In Week view, Roadmap review and Vendor call on 18 Aug sit side by side. Next week reads "23 – 29 Aug 2026". New event with a title adds it and toasts. Accepting "Design system sync" in the inbox adds it on 21 Aug. Delete removes an event and Undo restores it. Clicking Finance in the sidebar shows the placeholder and "Back to Calendar" returns.

# Build: Calendar Event Chip

The event pill of the calendar template as a native button. Each colour is a background, title and time token triple, so light and dark come from the theme. The compact variant is a 22px line whose title truncates while the start time stays; the full variant is a block with a coloured start edge, a two-line title and the time range, made to fill an absolutely positioned slot in a week grid. The file also exports the shared `CalendarEvent` model and `formatEventTime`, which the other calendar pieces import.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Tinted calendar event pill in five colour tokens: one-line compact chip for month cells, block variant for time grids, selected ring.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @internationalized/date@^3.12.4

## How it works

1. `calendarEventColorStyles` maps each colour to complete class names (`bg-calendar-event-<c>-background`, `text-calendar-event-<c>-title`, `text-calendar-event-<c>-time`, plus border, ring and dot classes built from the title token), so Tailwind sees every class statically and nothing is concatenated at runtime.
2. Compact is a single flex row: the title span takes `min-w-0 flex-1 truncate` and the time span takes `shrink-0`, so a narrow month cell eats the title first and never the time. All-day chips omit the time.
3. Full is a column with `h-full w-full overflow-hidden`, a 3px logical start border in the title colour, `line-clamp-2` on the title and a truncated "start – end" line. The parent sets the height, so a 15-minute slot shows only the title and a 2-hour slot shows both lines.
4. `formatEventTime` formats a fixed UTC instant built from the wall-clock hour and minute with a cached `DateFormatter` (`hourCycle: "h23"` and 2-digit hours for 24h, `h12` for 12h). Server and client therefore print the same string whatever their time zones.
5. `selected` adds `ring-2` in the event colour and `data-selected`; keyboard focus uses the kit focus ring. Remaining button props are spread last, so the chip works as a `PopoverTrigger` child and accepts `aria-pressed`, handlers and refs.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `compact height = 22px`
  Three chips plus a "+N more" line fit under the day number of a ~120px month cell.
- `start border = 3px`
  Reads as the colour key of the block at a glance without eating the narrow width of a week column.
- `hover = brightness 0.97 light, 1.25 dark`
  The tinted backgrounds are light in light mode and deep in dark mode, so the hover nudge must go in opposite directions to stay visible.
- `time format = HH:mm (h23) by default`
  Matches the template and keeps every time the same width with `tabular-nums`.

## API

```ts
type CalendarEventColor = "blue" | "emerald" | "lime" | "pink" | "purple"
function formatEventTime(time: { hour: number; minute: number }, options?: { locale?: string; hourCycle?: 12 | 24 }): string
function CalendarEventChip(props: ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> & { title: string; color?: CalendarEventColor; start?: { hour: number; minute: number }; end?: { hour: number; minute: number }; allDay?: boolean; variant?: "compact" | "full"; selected?: boolean; locale?: string; hourCycle?: 12 | 24; ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement> }): JSX.Element
```

- `title: string`
  Event title; truncates (compact) or clamps to two lines (full).
- `color: CalendarEventColor` — default `"blue"`
  Token triple used for background, title and time.
- `start / end: { hour: number; minute: number }`
  Wall-clock times. Compact shows start; full shows the range.
- `allDay: boolean` — default `false`
  Hide the time.
- `variant: "compact" | "full"` — default `"compact"`
  One-line month chip or time-grid block.
- `selected: boolean` — default `false`
  Colour ring and `data-selected`.
- `hourCycle: 12 | 24` — default `24`
  "09:30" or "9:30 AM".
- `locale: string` — default `"en-US"`
  Locale for the time formatter.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function CalendarEventChip({
  title,
  color = "blue",
  start,
  end,
  allDay = false,
  variant = "compact",
  selected = false,
  locale = "en-US",
  hourCycle = 24,
  className,
  type = "button",
  ref,
  ...props
}: CalendarEventChipProps) {
  const c = calendarEventColorStyles[color];
  const startLabel = !allDay && start ? formatEventTime(start, { locale, hourCycle }) : null;
  const endLabel = !allDay && end ? formatEventTime(end, { locale, hourCycle }) : null;

  const base = cx(
    "relative min-w-0 cursor-pointer select-none text-start outline-none",
    "transition-[box-shadow,filter] duration-150 ease-out hover:brightness-[0.97] dark:hover:brightness-125",
    "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
    selected && cx("ring-2", c.ring),
    c.background,
  );

  if (variant === "full") {
    return (
      <button
        ref={ref}
        type={type}
        data-selected={selected || undefined}
        data-variant="full"
        className={cx(
          base,
          "flex h-full w-full flex-col items-start gap-0.5 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border-s-[3px] py-1 ps-1.5 pe-1",
          c.bar,
          className,
        )}
        {...props}
      >
        <span className={cx("line-clamp-2 w-full text-body-2-medium break-words", c.title)}>{title}</span>
        {startLabel ? (
          <span className={cx("w-full truncate text-caption-1-regular tabular-nums opacity-90", c.time)}>
            {startLabel}
            {endLabel ? ` – ${endLabel}` : null}
          </span>
        ) : null}
      </button>
    );
  }

  return (
    <button
      ref={ref}
      type={type}
      data-selected={selected || undefined}
      data-variant="compact"
      className={cx(base, "flex h-[22px] w-full items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md px-1.5", className)}
      {...props}
    >
      <span className={cx("min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-body-2-medium", c.title)}>{title}</span>
      {startLabel ? (
        <span className={cx("shrink-0 text-caption-1-regular tabular-nums opacity-90", c.time)}>{startLabel}</span>
      ) : null}
    </button>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up: no effects, timers or listeners. Formatters are cached in a module-level map.

**Reduced motion.** Only a 150ms colour/filter transition on hover; there is no movement. It is short and non-spatial, so it stays under reduced motion.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Building class names like `bg-calendar-event-${color}-background` at runtime. Tailwind only generates classes it can find in source; keep the full-name map.
- Formatting times with `toLocaleTimeString` on a local `Date`. The server and the browser can be in different zones and print different hours, which breaks hydration.
- Forgetting `min-w-0` on the compact title. Without it the flex item refuses to shrink and the time is pushed out of the cell instead of the title truncating.

## Notes

- Pass `aria-pressed` when the chip toggles a selection, or wrap it in the event detail popover trigger, which supplies `aria-expanded`.
- The shared `CalendarEvent` type stores `CalendarDateTime` start and end; pass `{ hour, minute }` objects (or the `CalendarDateTime` itself) as `start`/`end`.

In a 104px cell "Coffee with Lena" truncates with an ellipsis while "09:30" stays whole. Full blocks show the title and "13:00 – 14:00"; a 36px block shows only the title. Clicking a chip adds the colour ring and sets `data-selected`; clicking it again removes both. Both themes keep the title readable on the tinted background.
