# Build: Close Button

The small round "X" that dismisses announcements, toasts, modals and drawers. It ships its own glyph instead of taking an icon: each size draws its X as two round-capped lines in an SVG whose viewBox equals its pixel size, so `strokeWidth` is a literal CSS pixel value instead of a scaled approximation. The circle is a tertiary fill, and hover darkens only the glyph.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Circular dismiss button in four sizes whose X is redrawn per size, so the stroke is a true 1.6 to 2.5px at every scale.

- Category: action
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Three lookup tables keyed by size drive the glyph: `GLYPH_SIZE` (the X's bounding square in px), `STROKE_WIDTH` (line weight in px) and `GLYPH_INSET` (how far the line ends sit in from the square's corners).
2. The SVG is `width = height = glyph` with `viewBox="0 0 glyph glyph"`, so one user unit is one CSS pixel. The two diagonals go from `(inset, inset)` to `(glyph − inset, glyph − inset)` and mirrored, with `strokeLinecap="round"` so the caps add half a stroke beyond each end.
3. Scaling one shared icon would scale its stroke with it: a 2px line drawn for 20px becomes about 3.2px at 32px. Redrawing per size keeps 2px at xs and sm and lets md deliberately step up to 2.5px so it holds its own in a modal header.
4. The container is a `rounded-full` square (`size-4/5/6/8`) on `background-tertiary-default`. The glyph uses `currentColor`, so `hover:text-text-primary` darkens the X while the circle stays put, transitioning colour over 150ms.
5. `aria-label` is required by the props type and the SVG is `aria-hidden`. `type` defaults to `"button"` so a close button inside a form dialog does not submit it.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `GLYPH_SIZE = 2xs 6.8 / xs 10.8 / sm 12.6 / md 16.2 px`
  xs, sm and md are 90% of the natural 12 / 14 / 18px glyphs for 20, 24 and 32px circles; at full size the X crowds the circle edge, and 10% smaller reads as centred with breathing room. 2xs takes its 6.8px straight from the compact Figma variant.
- `STROKE_WIDTH = 2xs 1.6 / xs 2 / sm 2 / md 2.5 px`
  Literal pixel weights from Figma. md is bolder on purpose: a 2px X inside a 32px circle looks spindly next to a modal title.
- `GLYPH_INSET = 2xs 0.57 / others 2 px`
  Room for the round caps to stay inside the glyph box. The 2xs value comes from Figma's 8px bars rotated 45° inside a 6.8px square, which leaves about 0.57px at each corner when projected onto the diagonal.
- `container sizes = 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 px`
  2xs for compact floating chips, xs for the announcement corner, sm for toasts, md for modal and drawer headers.

## API

```ts
function CloseButton(props: Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "children"> & { size?: "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md"; "aria-label": string; ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement> }): JSX.Element
```

- `size: "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md"` — default `"xs"`
  16, 20, 24 or 32px circle, each with its own glyph size and stroke weight.
- `aria-label: string`
  Required. Names what the button dismisses.
- `type: "button" | "submit" | "reset"` — default `"button"`
  Defaults to `button` so it never submits a surrounding form.
- `className: string`
  Merged through `tailwind-merge`, for example to absolutely position it in a corner.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function CloseButton({
  size = "xs",
  className,
  type = "button",
  ref,
  ...props
}: CloseButtonProps) {
  const glyph = GLYPH_SIZE[size];
  const strokeWidth = STROKE_WIDTH[size];
  const inset = GLYPH_INSET[size];

  return (
    <button
      ref={ref}
      type={type}
      className={cx(styles.base, styles.container[size], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      <svg width={glyph} height={glyph} viewBox={`0 0 ${glyph} ${glyph}`} fill="none" aria-hidden>
        <path
          d={`M${inset} ${inset}L${glyph - inset} ${glyph - inset}`}
          stroke="currentColor"
          strokeWidth={strokeWidth}
          strokeLinecap="round"
        />
        <path
          d={`M${glyph - inset} ${inset}L${inset} ${glyph - inset}`}
          stroke="currentColor"
          strokeWidth={strokeWidth}
          strokeLinecap="round"
        />
      </svg>
    </button>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component is stateless markup with no listeners, timers or effects.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing moves. Hover only darkens the glyph colour over 150ms.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Replacing the hand-drawn SVG with an icon font or a single scaled icon. The stroke weight then drifts with size and the md X looks either hairline or blobby.
- Removing `aria-label`. The glyph is hidden from assistive tech, so the button announces as just "button" and nobody knows it closes something.
- Rounding the computed coordinates, for example `Math.round(glyph − inset)`. The sub-pixel values are what keep both diagonals the same length and the X optically centred.
- Placing it on a background that matches `background-tertiary-default`. The circle disappears and only the X remains, which reads as a smaller, unanchored target.

## Notes

- Label it after what it closes ("Dismiss announcement", "Close dialog") rather than a generic "Close" when several dismissible surfaces can be on screen at once.

## Definition of done

Four circles render at 16, 20, 24 and 32px, each with a centred X whose lines look equally crisp, and the 32px X is visibly a touch bolder. Hovering darkens the X but not the circle. Tabbing shows an offset focus ring around the circle. Inside the announcement card, clicking the xs button hides the card and a restore button brings it back.

# Build: Code Block

The snippet frame from a docs page: a grey shell holding a header row (filename or role chip on the left, wrap and copy icon buttons on the right) above a white, inset code panel. TSX is coloured by a small tokenizer that ships with the component, so there is no highlighter package, grammar file or WASM to load. Line numbers sit in a sticky gutter, long lines scroll sideways or soft-wrap on demand, and the copy button swaps its glyph for a check for 1.6 seconds.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Docs code block with a filename chip, sticky line numbers, a dependency-free TSX highlighter, wrap toggle and one-click copy.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. `tokenizeTsx` walks the source once with sticky (`/y`) regexes, trying whitespace, comments, strings, then mode-specific rules. A mode stack of `code`, `tag` and `text` entries is what separates `a < b` from `<Card>`: a `<` opens a tag only in expression position (start of input, after a keyword, or after punctuation other than `)` and `]`), and inside a tag every bare identifier is an attribute.
2. Tags manage the stack: `/>` pops the tag, `>` pops it and pushes a `text` entry for an opening tag or pops the enclosing `text` entry for a closing one. In `text` mode everything up to the next `<` or `{` is plain JSX text, so an apostrophe in copy never starts a string. `{` inside a tag or text pushes a fresh `code` entry with its own brace counter, and the matching `}` pops it.
3. Identifiers become `keyword` (from a fixed set), `number` (for `true`, `null` and other literals), `function` (when followed by `(` or a `<T>(` type argument) or `plain`. Adjacent tokens of the same kind merge, which keeps the span count low.
4. `splitLines` re-cuts the token stream at every newline so a multi-line comment or template string keeps its colour on each row. Each row is a flex line: an `aria-hidden`, `select-none` gutter cell that is `sticky start-0` with the panel background, then the code cell, which is `whitespace-pre` or `whitespace-pre-wrap break-words` depending on the wrap state.
5. The gutter width is `calc(<digits>ch + 2rem)`, computed from the line count, so numbers right-align without measuring. Without wrap the `<code>` element is `w-max min-w-full`, so long rows widen the scroll area while highlighted rows still span the panel.
6. Copy goes through `writeClipboard`: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` first, then a hidden read-only textarea with `execCommand("copy")`, and the previous focus is restored. `useCopyToClipboard` holds the `copied` flag and a reset timeout that restarts on each copy and is cleared on unmount.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `copied window = 1600 ms`
  Long enough to see the check after the pointer leaves the button, and short enough that a second copy a moment later still gets fresh feedback.
- `shell / panel radii = rounded-2xl outer, rounded-xl inner, p-1.5 gap`
  The inner panel sits 6px inside the shell, so a 16px outer radius and a 12px inner radius stay concentric.
- `code type = font-mono + text-body-regular (14 / 20 px)`
  Rows have `min-h-5` (20px) to match the line height, so empty lines keep their height without a placeholder character.
- `gutter width = calc(digits ch + 2rem)`
  16px of padding on each side of the widest number. Using `ch` keeps 9 to 10 and 99 to 100 from shifting the code column by a pixel or two.
- `icon swap = 200 ms opacity + scale 0.5 to 1`
  The copy and check glyphs are stacked absolutely and cross-faded, so the button never changes size.

## API

```ts
function CodeBlock(props: { code: string; filename?: string; chipTone?: "neutral" | "file"; language?: "tsx" | "plain"; showLineNumbers?: boolean; highlightLines?: number[]; wrap?: boolean; defaultWrap?: boolean; onWrapChange?: (wrap: boolean) => void; hideWrapToggle?: boolean; hideCopy?: boolean; maxHeight?: number; actions?: ReactNode; onCopied?: (code: string) => void; className?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLElement> }): JSX.Element
function tokenizeTsx(src: string): Token[]

```

- `code: string`
  Source to show and copy. Leading blank lines and trailing whitespace are trimmed.
- `filename: string`
  Header chip label: a filename or a role such as `usage`. Omit it for an empty chip slot.
- `chipTone: "neutral" | "file"` — default `"neutral"`
  White label chip, or the purple `docs-file-chip-*` chip with a code glyph.
- `language: "tsx" | "plain"` — default `"tsx"`
  Run the built-in TSX tokenizer or print the text as is.
- `showLineNumbers: boolean` — default `true`
  Sticky, unselectable line-number gutter.
- `highlightLines: number[]`
  1-based lines tinted with `background-secondary`, gutter included.
- `wrap / defaultWrap / onWrapChange: boolean / boolean / (wrap: boolean) => void` — default `uncontrolled, false`
  Soft-wrap state, controlled or uncontrolled. The header toggle is `aria-pressed`.
- `hideWrapToggle / hideCopy: boolean` — default `false`
  Drop either header action.
- `maxHeight: number`
  Pixel cap on the code panel. It scrolls past this.
- `actions: ReactNode`
  Extra header controls placed before wrap and copy.
- `onCopied: (code: string) => void`
  Called after a successful copy.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Tokenize once per source, then cut into rows so each line owns its gutter
// cell. The gutter is sticky, so numbers stay put while long lines scroll.
const lines = useMemo(
  () => splitLines(language === "tsx" ? tokenizeTsx(source) : plainTokens(source)),
  [source, language],
);
const highlighted = useMemo(() => new Set(highlightLines ?? []), [highlightLines]);
const gutterCh = String(lines.length).length;

const rows = lines.map((tokens, index) => {
  const lineNo = index + 1;
  const isHighlighted = highlighted.has(lineNo);
  return (
    <span
      key={lineNo}
      data-line={lineNo}
      data-highlighted={isHighlighted || undefined}
      className={cx("flex min-h-5", isHighlighted && "bg-background-secondary-default")}
    >
      {showLineNumbers && (
        <span
          aria-hidden
          className={cx(
            "sticky start-0 z-10 shrink-0 select-none ps-4 pe-4 text-end text-text-tertiary",
            isHighlighted ? "bg-background-secondary-default" : "bg-docs-code-background",
          )}
          style={{ width: `calc(${gutterCh}ch + 2rem)` }}
        >
          {lineNo}
        </span>
      )}
      <span
        className={cx(
          "min-w-0 flex-1 pe-5",
          !showLineNumbers && "ps-5",
          wrap ? "whitespace-pre-wrap break-words" : "whitespace-pre",
        )}
      >
        {tokens.map((token, t) => (
          <span key={t} className={TOKEN_CLASS[token.kind]}>
            {token.text}
          </span>
        ))}
        {"\n"}
      </span>
    </span>
  );
});
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The reset timeout in `useCopyToClipboard` is cleared on unmount and whenever a new copy restarts it. The fallback textarea is removed in the same tick it is created. There are no listeners or observers.

**Reduced motion.** The only motion is the 200ms copy-to-check cross-fade and the 150ms hover colour change. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the glyph swap has `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so the check appears at once. Nothing moves on scroll or load.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Treating every `<` as a tag. Generics (`useState<Period>`) and comparisons would light up green. The expression-position test on the last significant token is what prevents it.
- Rendering rows without the trailing `\n` inside each code cell. Selecting several lines and pressing Cmd+C would join them into one line, because flex rows carry no newline of their own.
- Letting line numbers be selectable or part of the copied text. The gutter is `select-none` and `aria-hidden`, and the copy button reads the trimmed `code` prop, never the DOM.
- Building the token classes dynamically (`text-${kind}`). Tailwind only compiles literal class names, so the colour map is a literal object.
- Calling `navigator.clipboard.writeText` with no fallback. It throws in insecure contexts and many embedded iframes, and the copy then silently does nothing.

## Notes

- `language="plain"` skips the tokenizer for shell output, JSON or anything else.
- `CopyButton`, `useCopyToClipboard` and `writeClipboard` are exported from `code-block-copy` for other docs pieces such as install commands and copy-page buttons.
- The tokenizer handles the TSX found in docs snippets. It does not understand regex literals or nested template literal expressions, which render as strings or punctuation.

## Definition of done

A TSX snippet renders with purple keywords, orange strings, grey comments and green JSX tag names, while `useState<Period>` and `a < b` stay uncoloured. Line numbers stay pinned while a long line scrolls sideways and are not included when the text is selected. Pressing the wrap toggle sets `aria-pressed="true"` and long lines wrap inside the panel. Pressing copy puts the exact `code` string on the clipboard, swaps the icon to a check, announces "Copied" and reverts after about 1.6s.

# Build: Code Diff Viewer

Give it the file before and after a change and it shows the difference the way a code review does: removed lines on red, added lines on green, each with its old and new line number, grouped into hunks with "@@ -a,b +c,d @@" headers. Long runs of unchanged code fold into a "Show N unchanged lines" bar; open one, or every one from the toolbar, to read the whole file. A Unified / Split switch moves between one column and old and new side by side. Long lines wrap instead of scrolling sideways.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Before / after line diff with old and new line numbers, hunk headers, a unified or split layout and folded unchanged lines.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. diffLines splits both texts into lines, trims the lines they share at the start and end, and fills a longest-common-subsequence table for the changed middle only. Walking the table gives unchanged, removed and added lines in order, each numbered against the old file, the new file or both. On a tie a removal goes first, so a replaced block reads "- old" then "+ new".
2. findFolds looks at every run of unchanged lines and keeps `context` lines (3 by default) next to each change. What is left becomes a fold if it hides at least 3 lines; runs at the very top or bottom keep no context on their outer side.
3. layoutDiff turns the closed folds into hunks: each visible stretch between closed folds gets a header with its old and new start and length, read from running line counts. A closed fold and the header of the hunk after it share one row; an opened fold keeps a slim "Hide N lines" row where it was, and the header of the surrounding hunk widens to include the lines it revealed.
4. Fold ids are the index where their unchanged run starts, which does not depend on `context`. Opened ids are stored together with the diff they belong to, so passing new code starts folded again without an effect.
5. The fold button keeps the same React key whether open or closed, so keyboard focus stays on it after you press it.
6. Split view pairs the rows of a change: the n-th removal sits beside the n-th addition, and a side with nothing to pair shows an empty grey cell. Unchanged lines show on both sides with their own numbers.
7. The table uses fixed layout with set gutter widths, so code cells wrap long lines (overflow-wrap anywhere) instead of widening the table. Below 28rem the gutters narrow, and below 32rem the folder part of the path hides.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `context = 3 lines`
  The same amount git shows by default; enough to see which block a change sits in.
- `MIN_HIDDEN = 3 lines`
  Folding one or two lines behind a bar that takes a row itself saves nothing.
- `gutter width = 2.75rem (2rem under 28rem)`
  Room for four-digit line numbers at caption size; narrower on phones so code keeps most of the width.
- `line tones = notification success / error background tokens`
  The same soft lime and rose fills as the Changes Diff Panel, readable in both themes.

## API

```ts
function CodeDiffViewer(props: { oldCode: string; newCode: string; fileName?: string; view?: "unified" | "split"; defaultView?: "unified" | "split"; onViewChange?: (view: "unified" | "split") => void; context?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `oldCode: string`
  The file before the change.
- `newCode: string`
  The file after the change.
- `fileName: string`
  Path shown in the toolbar and in the accessible name.
- `view: "unified" | "split"`
  Controlled layout.
- `defaultView: "unified" | "split"` — default `"unified"`
  Initial layout when uncontrolled.
- `onViewChange: (view: "unified" | "split") => void`
  Called when the Unified / Split switch changes.
- `context: number` — default `3`
  Unchanged lines kept beside each change before the rest folds.
- `className: string`
  Classes for the viewer surface (height, width).

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function diffLines(oldCode: string, newCode: string): DiffLine[] {
  const a = splitLines(oldCode);
  const b = splitLines(newCode);
  // Trim the shared head and tail first, so a typical edit only runs the table on the changed middle.
  let pre = 0;
  while (pre < a.length && pre < b.length && a[pre] === b[pre]) pre++;
  let suf = 0;
  while (suf < a.length - pre && suf < b.length - pre && a[a.length - 1 - suf] === b[b.length - 1 - suf]) suf++;
  const n = a.length - pre - suf;
  const m = b.length - pre - suf;
  const w = m + 1;
  // lcs[i * w + j] = longest common run of lines between a[pre + i..] and b[pre + j..]
  const lcs = new Uint32Array((n + 1) * w);
  for (let i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    for (let j = m - 1; j >= 0; j--) {
      lcs[i * w + j] =
        a[pre + i] === b[pre + j]
          ? (lcs[(i + 1) * w + j + 1] ?? 0) + 1
          : Math.max(lcs[(i + 1) * w + j] ?? 0, lcs[i * w + j + 1] ?? 0);
    }
  }
  const out: DiffLine[] = [];
  let oldNo = 1;
  let newNo = 1;
  const same = (text: string) => out.push({ kind: "ctx", text, oldNo: oldNo++, newNo: newNo++ });
  for (let k = 0; k < pre; k++) same(a[k] ?? "");
  let i = 0;
  let j = 0;
  while (i < n || j < m) {
    const x = a[pre + i] ?? "";
    const y = b[pre + j] ?? "";
    if (i < n && j < m && x === y) {
      same(x);
      i++;
      j++;
    } else if (i < n && (j >= m || (lcs[(i + 1) * w + j] ?? 0) >= (lcs[i * w + j + 1] ?? 0))) {
      // On a tie, removals go first so a replaced block reads "- old" then "+ new".
      out.push({ kind: "del", text: x, oldNo: oldNo++ });
      i++;
    } else {
      out.push({ kind: "add", text: y, newNo: newNo++ });
      j++;
    }
  }
  for (let k = a.length - suf; k < a.length; k++) same(a[k] ?? "");
  return out;
}

/** Every run of unchanged lines, minus `context` lines next to a change, is a fold candidate. */
function findFolds(lines: DiffLine[], context: number): Fold[] {
  const folds: Fold[] = [];
  let s = 0;
  while (s < lines.length) {
    if (lines[s]?.kind !== "ctx") {
      s++;
      continue;
    }
    let e = s;
    while (e < lines.length && lines[e]?.kind === "ctx") e++;
    const from = s === 0 ? 0 : s + context;
    const to = e === lines.length ? e : e - context;
    if (to - from >= MIN_HIDDEN) folds.push({ id: s, from, to });
    s = e;
  }
  return folds;
}

export function layoutDiff(lines: DiffLine[], context: number, openIds: ReadonlySet<number>) {
  const folds = findFolds(lines, context);
  const oldAt: number[] = [];
  const newAt: number[] = [];
  let o = 0;
  let nw = 0;
  for (const l of lines) {
    oldAt.push(o);
    newAt.push(nw);
    if (l.kind !== "add") o++;
    if (l.kind !== "del") nw++;
  }
  oldAt.push(o);
  newAt.push(nw);
  const span = (at: number[], from: number, to: number) => {
    const start = at[from] ?? 0;
    const len = (at[to] ?? 0) - start;
    return `${len ? start + 1 : start},${len}`;
  };
  const header = (from: number, to: number) => `@@ -${span(oldAt, from, to)} +${span(newAt, from, to)} @@`;
  const openAt = new Map(folds.filter((f) => openIds.has(f.id)).map((f) => [f.from, f]));

  const rows: Row[] = [];
  let cursor = 0;
  let pending: Fold | null = null;
  // A hunk is a visible stretch between closed folds; its header covers any opened folds inside it.
  const emit = (from: number, to: number, before: Fold | null) => {
    rows.push(
      before
        ? { t: "fold", fold: before, open: false, header: header(from, to) }
        : { t: "header", from, header: header(from, to) },
    );
    for (let i = from; i < to; i++) {
      const opened = openAt.get(i);
      if (opened) rows.push({ t: "fold", fold: opened, open: true, header: null });
      const line = lines[i];
      if (line) rows.push({ t: "line", i, line });
    }
  };
  for (const f of folds) {
    if (openIds.has(f.id)) continue;
    if (f.from > cursor) emit(cursor, f.from, pending);
    pending = f;
    cursor = f.to;
  }
  if (cursor < lines.length) emit(cursor, lines.length, pending);
  else if (pending) rows.push({ t: "fold", fold: pending, open: false, header: null });
  return { rows, foldIds: folds.map((f) => f.id) };
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers, listeners or observers. The diff and layout are memoised React values.

**Reduced motion.** Only the hover and selected colours of the layout switch and fold buttons transition, and they use motion-reduce:transition-none; folds open and close instantly in every mode.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- The line diff fills an old × new table for the changed middle, so it is meant for source files up to a few thousand lines. For whole generated files or huge diffs, compute the diff on a server or in a worker.
- Lines are compared exactly: a change in indentation or line endings counts as a change. Normalise "\r\n" to "\n" before passing text from Windows files.
- Code is plain text in a monospace table; add your own highlighter per line if you need token colours.

## Notes

- Uses DiffCounts from Changes Diff Panel for the +/− totals in the toolbar, so both read the same.
- diffLines and layoutDiff are exported for building other views, such as a commit summary or a minimap of changed lines.
- An unchanged file still renders: the whole file sits behind one "Show N unchanged lines" bar and the totals read +0 −0.

## Definition of done

The demo opens unified with three hunks and three "Show N unchanged lines" bars; the toolbar reads +7 −4. Pressing a bar reveals its lines and turns it into "Hide N lines" with focus still on it; "Show all lines" opens every fold and its label becomes "Fold unchanged". Split puts each removed line beside its replacement with old numbers on the left and new on the right. At 360px wide lines wrap and nothing scrolls sideways.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Color

A docs palette for the semantic layer of the kit theme. The tokens are grouped into Background, Text, Border, Status and Chart. Each group is a bordered table, and each row has a live swatch, the custom property name, the utility that consumes it, and what the token points to in the light and the dark theme. The light and dark columns are read from the loaded stylesheets, not typed in, so they stay correct when the theme changes. They show both themes whichever one the page is in. Clicking a token copies `--color-…` to the clipboard.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Semantic colour token palette: grouped swatch tables with light and dark values read from the theme, click a token to copy its variable.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. `COLOR_GROUPS` lists 74 tokens in five groups. Each token has its variable name and a display-only utility string (`bg-…`, `text-…`, `border-…`, `ring-…`, `fill-…`, `placeholder:text-…`).
2. On mount, `readThemeValues` walks `document.styleSheets`, recursing into `@import` and `@layer`/`@supports` blocks and skipping `@media`. It keeps only style rules whose selector list contains exactly `:root` (light) or `.dark` (dark), and reads each wanted custom property with `rule.style.getPropertyValue`. Cross-origin sheets throw on `cssRules` and are skipped. A token that `.dark` never overrides takes its light value.
3. `formatColorValue` turns the raw declarations into palette names: `var(--color-neutral-950)` becomes `neutral-950`, and `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-800) 60%, transparent)` becomes `neutral-800 / 60%`. The light and dark chips are painted with the raw value itself, so they resolve through the primitives and show the other theme correctly.
4. The main swatch in each row is painted with `var(<token>)`, so it follows whichever theme is active with no JS. Rows are a CSS grid with ARIA table roles. One template gives aligned columns: three columns on phones (the utility moves under the name and the light/dark labels become screen-reader text), and four from `lg`.
5. One `useCopyToClipboard` instance in `ColorPalette` serves every row. `lastCopied` records which token was clicked, so only that row shows the lime check for 1.4s. A `role="status"` span announces "Copied --color-…".

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `groups = background 14, text 10, border 13, status 16, chart 21`
  Every semantic colour that components consume. Primitives (`neutral-*`, `accent-*`) stay out, because components must never use them directly.
- `row grid = 1.4fr / 1fr / 9.5rem / 9.5rem from lg, 1fr / auto / auto (chips only) on phones`
  Fixed value columns keep the light and dark chips aligned across rows and fit "neutral-700 / 60%". On phones the names get almost the whole width and wrap instead of truncating.
- `swatch = 22px, rounded-md, 1px inset ring border-button-default`
  The inset ring keeps white and transparent swatches visible on a white card without changing their size.
- `copy reset = 1400 ms`
  Long enough to see the check, short enough for copying several tokens in a row.

## API

```ts
function ColorPalette(props: { groups?: readonly string[]; query?: string; headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4; onCopied?: (name: string) => void; className?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function ColorTokenTable(props: { group: ColorGroup; values: ReadonlyMap<string, ThemeValue>; copiedName?: string | null; onCopy: (name: string) => void; headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function readThemeValues(names: readonly string[]): Map<string, { light?: string; dark?: string }>
function formatColorValue(raw: string): string
const COLOR_GROUPS: readonly ColorGroup[]
```

- `groups: readonly string[]` — default `all five`
  Group ids to show: `background`, `text`, `border`, `status`, `chart`.
- `query: string` — default `""`
  Case-insensitive filter on variable and utility names. Groups with no matches are hidden.
- `headingLevel: 2 | 3 | 4` — default `3`
  Heading level of each group title.
- `onCopied: (name: string) => void`
  Called with the variable name after a successful copy.
- `className: string`
  Extra classes on the stack of groups.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
function collect(rules: CSSRuleList, names: ReadonlySet<string>, out: Map<string, ThemeValue>) {
  for (const rule of Array.from(rules)) {
    if (rule instanceof CSSImportRule) {
      if (rule.styleSheet) safeCollect(rule.styleSheet, names, out);
    } else if (rule instanceof CSSStyleRule) {
      // Only the two theme scopes count; `.dark[data-accent]` and friends are refinements.
      const selectors = rule.selectorText.split(",").map((s) => s.trim());
      const scope = selectors.includes(".dark") ? "dark" : selectors.includes(":root") ? "light" : null;
      if (!scope) continue;
      for (const name of names) {
        const value = rule.style.getPropertyValue(name).trim();
        if (value) out.set(name, { ...out.get(name), [scope]: value });
      }
    } else if (!(rule instanceof CSSMediaRule) && "cssRules" in rule) {
      // @layer / @supports blocks; @media is skipped so a colour-scheme query is never read as light.
      collect((rule as CSSGroupingRule).cssRules, names, out);
    }
  }
}

function safeCollect(sheet: CSSStyleSheet, names: ReadonlySet<string>, out: Map<string, ThemeValue>) {
  try {
    collect(sheet.cssRules, names, out);
  } catch {
    // Cross-origin sheets throw on cssRules; they never hold the kit theme.
  }
}

/**
 * Reads what each token is declared as in the light (`:root`) and dark
 * (`.dark`) scopes straight from the loaded stylesheets, so the table shows
 * both themes no matter which one the page is in. Client only.
 */
export function readThemeValues(names: readonly string[]): Map<string, ThemeValue> {
  const out = new Map<string, ThemeValue>();
  const wanted = new Set(names);
  for (const sheet of Array.from(document.styleSheets)) safeCollect(sheet, wanted, out);
  for (const [name, value] of out) if (!value.dark && value.light) out.set(name, { ...value, dark: value.light });
  return out;
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The stylesheet read runs once in a mount effect and adds no listeners or observers. The copied-state timeout belongs to `useCopyToClipboard` and is cleared on unmount.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing animates apart from the hover tint and the copy icon fade. Both use `motion-reduce:transition-none`.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Reading values with `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)`. That only returns the active theme, and only the resolved colour, so the light column shows dark values in dark mode and the primitive name is lost.
- Treating a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { … } }` block as light. That is why `@media` rules are skipped while walking.
- Painting the dark chip with `var(--token)`. On a light page that resolves to the light value. The chip has to use the declared `.dark` value, which references primitives that do not change with the theme.

## Notes

- `readThemeValues` and `formatColorValue` are exported, so a design-review tool can diff token declarations between two themes.
- Pass `groups={["status"]}` to put a single table on a badge or chip docs page, and `query` to wire a search field.

## Definition of done

In light mode the `--color-text-primary` row shows a near-black swatch, `text-text-primary`, Light `neutral-950` and Dark `neutral-50`. Switching the page to dark turns the swatch near-white while the Light and Dark columns stay the same. `--color-background-inner-default` shows Dark `neutral-800 / 60%`. Clicking a token puts exactly `--color-…` on the clipboard and shows a lime check on that row only. Filtering with "chart" leaves only the Chart group. At 360px each row shows the swatch, name, utility and two value chips with no horizontal scroll.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Color Picker

A compact colour editor on React Aria's colour components: a 3:2 saturation and brightness field, a hue rail, an optional opacity rail over a checkerboard, a swatch beside a hex field, and a row of presets. `ColorPicker` renders it inline; `ColorWell` is a 32px round swatch that opens the same editor in a popover. Thumbs are the kit slider's white embossed dot and grow slightly while dragged.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A saturation field, hue and opacity rails, a hex field and presets, inline or behind a round swatch that opens a popover.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Both exports wrap React Aria's `ColorPicker`, which owns the value and shares it through context, so every control inside binds to it with no props. `ColorPicker` renders the private `Editor` directly; `ColorWell` renders a `<button>` holding a `ColorSwatch` inside the kit `PopoverTrigger`, and the kit `Popover` (`w-[248px] rounded-3xl`, `p-1` dialog) holds the `Editor` at full width.
2. `Editor` is a `w-[228px] max-w-full` column with `gap-2.5`. First a `ColorArea` with `colorSpace="hsb"`, `xChannel="saturation"`, `yChannel="brightness"`, `aspect-[3/2]` and `rounded-2xl`; working in HSB means the hue survives dragging through grey. React Aria paints the gradient itself.
3. Under it a `ColorSlider` on `channel="hue"` with an `h-3` rounded `SliderTrack`, and with `showAlpha` a second slider on `channel="alpha"` whose track sits on a CHECKERBOARD div: a `repeating-conic-gradient` in 8px tiles, with darker tiles under `dark:`. Every surface gets an inset 1px `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.06)` hairline span so pale colours do not melt into the page.
4. All thumbs share one class: `size-4 rounded-full border border-white` with a two-part shadow (2px drop plus inset hairline), `data-[dragging]:scale-110` over 150ms, and a focus-visible ring. Rail thumbs add `top-1/2`.
5. The hex row is a 32px `ColorSwatch` and a `ColorField` with an `Input` (`dir="ltr"`, mono 13px uppercase, tertiary surface that turns primary with a focus ring). React Aria commits a colour field on blur only, so Enter is handled by blurring and immediately refocusing the input.
6. `swatches` renders a `ColorSwatchPicker` as a 7-column grid; each item is a `ColorSwatchPickerItem` that scales to 110% on hover. The selected ring is always rendered and fades in through `group-data-[selected]/swatch:opacity-100`: a 2px white inset inside a 1px dark inset, which reads on any colour.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `editor width = w-[228px] inline; w-full inside the w-[248px] popover`
  Seven presets at gap-1.5 come out at about 27px each, a comfortable hit target, and the 3:2 area is then 152px tall, enough vertical travel for brightness.
- `thumb = size-4, scale-110 while dragging, 150ms`
  Sixteen pixels is the kit slider's thumb, so colour rails and range sliders match. The grow confirms the grab without hiding the colour under the pointer.
- `rail height = h-3 (12px)`
  Thinner than the thumb, so the thumb visibly overhangs the rail and reads as draggable.
- `checkerboard tile = 8px, #e6e6e6 / #ffffff (dark: #3a3a3a / #262626)`
  Small enough to show partial opacity on a 12px rail; the dark pair keeps the rail from glaring in dark mode.
- `hairline = inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.06)`
  Separates white and near-white from the page background without drawing a visible border on saturated colours.

## API

```ts
function ColorPicker(props: Omit<AriaColorPickerProps, "children"> & { showAlpha?: boolean; swatches?: string[]; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function ColorWell(props: ColorPickerProps & { "aria-label"?: string; placement?: PopoverProps["placement"]; wellClassName?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `value / defaultValue: string | Color`
  Controlled or initial colour.
- `onChange: (value: Color) => void`
  Fires continuously while dragging and on hex commit.
- `showAlpha: boolean` — default `false`
  Adds the opacity rail over a checkerboard.
- `swatches: string[]`
  Preset CSS colours in a 7-column row under the editor.
- `className: string` — default `w-[228px]`
  Classes on the editor column, e.g. a width.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Color"`
  ColorWell only. Names the swatch button and its popover.
- `placement: PopoverProps["placement"]` — default `"bottom start"`
  ColorWell only. Where the popover opens.
- `wellClassName: string` — default `size-8`
  ColorWell only. Classes on the swatch button.

```tsx
function Editor({ showAlpha = false, swatches, className }: EditorProps) {
  const localize = useTemplateCopy();

  return (
    <div className={cx("flex w-[228px] max-w-full flex-col gap-2.5", className)}>
      <AriaColorArea
        colorSpace="hsb"
        xChannel="saturation"
        yChannel="brightness"
        className="relative aspect-[3/2] w-full shrink-0 cursor-crosshair rounded-2xl"
      >
        <span aria-hidden className={cx(HAIRLINE, "rounded-2xl")} />
        <AriaColorThumb className={THUMB} />
      </AriaColorArea>

      <AriaColorSlider colorSpace="hsb" channel="hue" className="w-full">
        <AriaSliderTrack className="relative h-3 w-full cursor-pointer rounded-full">
          <span aria-hidden className={cx(HAIRLINE, "rounded-full")} />
          <AriaColorThumb className={cx(THUMB, "top-1/2")} />
        </AriaSliderTrack>
      </AriaColorSlider>

      {showAlpha ? (
        <AriaColorSlider channel="alpha" className="w-full">
          <div className={cx("relative h-3 w-full rounded-full", CHECKERBOARD)}>
            <AriaSliderTrack className="relative h-3 w-full cursor-pointer rounded-full">
              <span aria-hidden className={cx(HAIRLINE, "rounded-full")} />
              <AriaColorThumb className={cx(THUMB, "top-1/2")} />
            </AriaSliderTrack>
          </div>
        </AriaColorSlider>
      ) : null}

      <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
        <AriaColorSwatch className="relative size-8 shrink-0 rounded-full shadow-[inset_0_0_0_1px_rgb(0_0_0/0.06)]" />
        <AriaColorField aria-label={localize("Hex color")} className="min-w-0 flex-1">
          <AriaInput
            dir="ltr"
            spellCheck={false}
            onKeyDown={(event) => {
              // React Aria commits the field on blur only; Enter commits it
              // too, and focus stays in the field.
              if (event.key !== "Enter") return;
              const input = event.currentTarget;
              input.blur();
              input.focus();
            }}
            className={cx(
              "h-8 w-full min-w-0 rounded-2lg bg-background-tertiary-default px-2.5 font-mono text-[13px] text-text-primary uppercase",
              "outline-none ring-2 ring-transparent ring-inset transition-[background-color,box-shadow] duration-150 ease",
              "focus:bg-background-primary-default focus:ring-border-focus-ring",
            )}
          />
        </AriaColorField>
      </div>

      {swatches?.length ? (
        <AriaColorSwatchPicker aria-label={localize("Presets")} className="grid grid-cols-7 gap-1.5 pt-0.5">
          {swatches.map((swatch) => (
            <AriaColorSwatchPickerItem
              key={swatch}
              color={swatch}
              className={cx(
                "group/swatch relative aspect-square w-full cursor-pointer rounded-full outline-none transition-[scale] duration-150 ease-out hover:scale-110",
                "data-[focus-visible]:ring-2 data-[focus-visible]:ring-border-focus-ring data-[focus-visible]:ring-offset-2",
              )}
            >
              <AriaColorSwatch className="size-full rounded-full shadow-[inset_0_0_0_1px_rgb(0_0_0/0.08)]" />
              {/* Selected: a white ring inside a dark hairline reads on any colour. */}
              <span
                aria-hidden
                className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 rounded-full opacity-0 shadow-[inset_0_0_0_2px_#fff,inset_0_0_0_3px_rgb(0_0_0/0.25)] transition-opacity duration-150 group-data-[selected]/swatch:opacity-100"
              />
            </AriaColorSwatchPickerItem>
          ))}
        </AriaColorSwatchPicker>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** React Aria releases its drag listeners when a drag ends or the control unmounts; the popover's overlay and focus management are torn down on close. No timers.

**Reduced motion.** Only 150ms scale on thumbs, swatches and the well plus opacity on the selection ring and the kit popover's entrance. The component does not branch on `prefers-reduced-motion`; the movements are a few pixels and colour updates are instant either way.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not keep the value in RGB or hex while dragging. Use `colorSpace="hsb"`; in RGB, dragging to grey loses the hue and the area snaps to red.
- Do not expect Enter to commit the hex field. React Aria commits on blur; the component blurs and refocuses on Enter, so keep that handler if you replace the input.
- Do not mount the selected ring only when selected. It is always present and fades on opacity, which is what makes the selection change smooth.
- Do not drop the hairline layers to "clean up" the markup. Without them white and pale presets vanish against a white card.
- Do not render `ColorWell` without a meaningful `aria-label`. The button contains only a swatch, so "Color" is all a screen reader would announce.

## Notes

- `value` / `defaultValue` take a CSS colour string or a React Aria `Color` (`parseColor("#6366F1")`); `onChange` hands back a `Color`, so call `toString("hex")` or `toString("css")` as needed.
- Every control is keyboard reachable: arrows nudge the area and rails, Shift or Page keys take bigger steps, and the hex field accepts any CSS colour.

## Definition of done

The inline picker shows a saturation field with a white thumb, a full-spectrum hue rail and a hex field reading the current colour. Dragging in the field updates the swatch and hex live; dragging the hue rail through any position keeps the saturation and brightness. Typing "#22C55E" in the hex field and pressing Enter applies it without leaving the field. Clicking a preset selects it with a white inner ring. A ColorWell opens the same editor in a popover from its round swatch; with `showAlpha`, the opacity rail sits on a checkerboard.

# Build: Combo Chart Card

A grey dashboard card that plots monthly sessions as rounded Recharts bars against a left axis and the conversion rate as a line with dots against a right percent axis. The header shows total sessions with their change on the period before, the session-weighted conversion rate, a legend and a "This year" calendar pill that swaps the data set. Hovering a month darkens its bar, dims the others, pops a pulsing dot on the line, opens a tooltip with both values and switches the headline and the two tiles to that month.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A dashboard card with bars on a left axis and a rate line on a right axis; hovering a month spotlights its bar and pops a dot on the line.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: recharts@^3.10.1

## How it works

1. A `ComposedChart` holds two `YAxis` components: `yAxisId="bars"` on the left with compact ticks ("3K", "6K") and `yAxisId="line"` with `orientation="right"` and percent ticks. The `Bar` and the `Line` each name their axis, so sessions and percentages scale independently on one plot.
2. The right axis domain is `[0, max => Math.max(3, Math.ceil(max * 1.2 / 3) * 3)]`: 20% headroom rounded up to a multiple of 3, so four ticks always land on whole percents (0%, 2%, 4%, 6% for the default data).
3. `onMouseMove` stores `state.activeTooltipIndex` in `hovered` when `isTooltipActive` is true and the index is finite; `onMouseLeave` clears it. Each bar is a `Cell`: the hovered one is filled with the tone's `-active` colour, the others keep the base colour at `fillOpacity` 0.45 with a 200ms `transition-[fill-opacity]`, and all return to full opacity when the pointer leaves.
4. The `Tooltip` has `cursor={false}` because the spotlighted bar already marks the month. Its content renders `ChartTooltipCard` from `activeIndex` (mapped from `null` to -1 first) with the bar value and the rate to one decimal.
5. The line has 3px dots ringed in the card colour, and its `activeDot` is the shared `PulseDot`, which pings while the month is hovered.
6. With nothing hovered the headline is the period total against `previousTotal` and the rate is the session-weighted average `Σ(bar × line) / Σ bar`. With a month hovered both switch to that month, the chip compares it with the month before (hidden for the first month), and the two tiles relabel from "total" / "average" to the month name.
7. The period switch is the kit `Select` as a calendar pill (or a segmented control with `periodControl="segmented"`). Choosing a period clears `hovered`, updates internal state only when `period` is uncontrolled, and calls `onPeriodChange`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `dimmed bars = fillOpacity 0.45, 200ms ease-out`
  Low enough that the hovered bar clearly leads, high enough that the rest still read as data for comparison.
- `bar shape = radius 6 on all corners, maxBarSize 28, barCategoryGap 22%`
  Fully rounded pills match the preview; the size cap keeps bars slim on wide cards so the line stays readable over them.
- `axis widths = left 44px, right 40px`
  Left fits a compact label such as "10.5K" and right fits "6%" at 12px without clipping.
- `line dots = r 3 with a 1.5px background-secondary stroke; active PulseDot r 4.5 with ping`
  Small resting dots show where each monthly rate is measured; the bigger pulsing dot only appears on the hovered month.
- `plot height = 240px`
  The card grows with its header and tiles; a fixed plot box gives `ResponsiveContainer` a definite height.

## API

```ts
function ComboChartCard(props?: ComboChartCardProps): JSX.Element
type ComboChartCardProps = { bars?: ComboMeasure; line?: ComboMeasure; periods?: ComboPeriod[]; period?: string; defaultPeriod?: string; onPeriodChange?: (id: string) => void; periodControl?: "segmented" | "select"; className?: string }
type ComboMeasure = { label: string; tone: ChartTone }
type ComboPoint = { label: string; bar: number; line: number }
type ComboPeriod = { id: string; label: string; data: ComboPoint[]; previousTotal?: number }
```

- `bars: ComboMeasure` — default `{ label: "Sessions", tone: 2 }`
  Name and colour of the bar measure on the left axis.
- `line: ComboMeasure` — default `{ label: "Conversion", tone: 6 }`
  Name and colour of the line measure, in percent, on the right axis.
- `periods: ComboPeriod[]` — default `COMBO_PERIODS`
  Data sets the pill switches between; `previousTotal` feeds the chip.
- `period: string`
  Controlled period id.
- `defaultPeriod: string` — default `first period id`
  Initial period when uncontrolled.
- `onPeriodChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called with the chosen period id.
- `periodControl: "segmented" | "select"` — default `"select"`
  Calendar pill with a listbox, or a segmented switch.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function ComboChartCard({
  bars = { label: "Sessions", tone: 2 },
  line = { label: "Conversion", tone: 6 },
  periods = COMBO_PERIODS,
  period,
  defaultPeriod,
  onPeriodChange,
  periodControl = "select",
  className,
}: ComboChartCardProps = {}) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const [innerPeriod, setInnerPeriod] = useState(defaultPeriod ?? periods[0]?.id ?? "");
  const periodId = period ?? innerPeriod;
  const active = periods.find((p) => p.id === periodId) ?? periods[0];
  const data = active?.data ?? [];
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState<number | null>(null);

  const point = hovered !== null ? data[hovered] : undefined;
  const total = data.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.bar, 0);
  // Session-weighted, so a quiet month does not move the yearly rate as much as a busy one.
  const average = total > 0 ? data.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.bar * p.line, 0) / total : 0;
  const rate = point ? point.line : average;
  const headline = point ? point.bar : total;
  const delta = point
    ? hovered !== null && hovered > 0
      ? describeDelta(point.bar, data[hovered - 1]?.bar)
      : null
    : describeDelta(total, active?.previousTotal);

  const selectPeriod = (id: string) => {
    setHovered(null);
    if (period === undefined) setInnerPeriod(id);
    onPeriodChange?.(id);
  };

  const barFill = (i: number) => (i === hovered ? toneActiveColor(bars.tone) : toneColor(bars.tone));

  return (
    <section aria-label={`${bars.label} and ${line.label} chart`} className={cx(CHART_CARD_FRAME, "gap-3", className)}>
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 px-2 pt-2 @md:flex-row @md:items-start @md:justify-between">
        <ChartHeadline
          label={`${bars.label}${point ? ` · ${point.label}` : ""} · ${line.label} ${pct(rate)}`}
          value={headline}
          delta={delta}
          swapKey={`${periodId}-${hovered ?? "total"}`}
          reducedMotion={reduced}
        />
        <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 @md:items-end">
          {periods.length > 1 ? (
            <ChartPeriodControl
              options={periods}
              value={periodId}
              onChange={selectPeriod}
              variant={periodControl}
              label={`${bars.label} period`}
              className="self-start @md:self-end"
            />
          ) : null}
          <ChartLegend
            items={[
              { key: "bar", label: bars.label, tone: bars.tone },
              { key: "line", label: line.label, tone: line.tone },
            ]}
            className="@md:pe-1"
          />
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className="h-[240px] w-full">
        <ResponsiveContainer width="100%" height="100%" initialDimension={{ width: 520, height: 240 }}>
          <ComposedChart
            data={data}
            barCategoryGap="22%"
            margin={{ top: 8, right: 0, bottom: 0, left: 0 }}
            onMouseMove={(state) => {
              const next = Number(state?.activeTooltipIndex);
              if (state?.isTooltipActive && Number.isFinite(next)) setHovered(next);
            }}
            onMouseLeave={() => setHovered(null)}
          >
            <CartesianGrid vertical={false} stroke={GRID_STROKE} strokeDasharray="4 4" />
            <YAxis
              yAxisId="bars"
              width={44}
              domain={[0, "auto"]}
              tickCount={4}
              tickFormatter={(v: number) => formatCompact(v)}
              tickLine={false}
              axisLine={false}
              tick={AXIS_TICK}
            />
            <YAxis
              yAxisId="line"
              orientation="right"
              width={40}
              domain={[0, (max: number) => Math.max(3, Math.ceil((max * 1.2) / 3) * 3)]}
              tickCount={4}
              tickFormatter={(v: number) => `${Math.round(v)}%`}
              tickLine={false}
              axisLine={false}
              tick={AXIS_TICK}
            />
            <XAxis
              dataKey="label"
              tickLine={false}
              axisLine={false}
              tickMargin={10}
              interval="preserveStartEnd"
              minTickGap={8}
              tick={AXIS_TICK}
            />
            <Tooltip
              cursor={false}
              offset={16}
              isAnimationActive={!reduced}
              animationDuration={160}
              wrapperStyle={{ outline: "none", zIndex: 10 }}
              content={({ active: isActive, activeIndex }) => {
                const at = data[activeIndex == null ? -1 : Number(activeIndex)];
                if (!isActive || !at) return null;
                return (
                  <ChartTooltipCard
                    title={at.label}
                    rows={[
                      { key: "bar", label: bars.label, tone: bars.tone, value: formatNumber(at.bar) },
                      { key: "line", label: line.label, tone: line.tone, value: pct(at.line) },
                    ]}
                  />
                );
              }}
            />
            <Bar
              yAxisId="bars"
              dataKey="bar"
              name={bars.label}
              radius={[6, 6, 6, 6]}
              maxBarSize={28}
              isAnimationActive={!reduced}
              animationDuration={450}
            >
              {data.map((p, i) => (
                <Cell
                  key={p.label}
                  fill={barFill(i)}
                  fillOpacity={hovered !== null && i !== hovered ? 0.45 : 1}
                  className="transition-[fill-opacity] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none"
                />
              ))}
            </Bar>
            <Line
              yAxisId="line"
              type="monotone"
              dataKey="line"
              name={line.label}
              stroke={toneActiveColor(line.tone)}
              strokeWidth={2.5}
              dot={{ r: 3, fill: toneActiveColor(line.tone), stroke: "var(--color-background-secondary-default)", strokeWidth: 1.5 }}
              activeDot={<PulseDot color={toneActiveColor(line.tone)} pulse={!reduced} />}
              isAnimationActive={!reduced}
              animationDuration={450}
            />
          </ComposedChart>
        </ResponsiveContainer>
      </div>

      <ChartStatTiles
        columns={2}
        tiles={[
          {
            key: "bar",
            tone: bars.tone,
            label: point ? `${bars.label} · ${point.label}` : `${bars.label} · total`,
            value: formatNumber(headline),
          },
          {
            key: "line",
            tone: line.tone,
            label: point ? `${line.label} · ${point.label}` : `${line.label} · average`,
            value: pct(rate),
          },
        ]}
      />
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `useCountUp` cancels its animation frame on target change and unmount, `useReducedMotion` unsubscribes its media-query listener, `ResponsiveContainer` disconnects its resize observer, and the kit `Select` tears down its popover when closed. The card adds no listeners or timers of its own.

**Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `useReducedMotion` turns off `isAnimationActive` on the Bar, Line and Tooltip, the headline shows its value without counting, the number fade and the bar opacity transition are disabled with `motion-reduce:` variants, and the active dot drops its ping.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Forgetting `yAxisId` on one of the series. Recharts then plots it against the wrong axis, and a 4% rate sits flat at the bottom of an axis that runs to 9,000.
- Averaging the monthly rates directly. A plain mean gives 3.65% here; weighting by sessions gives 3.68% (shown as 3.7%), which is the rate actually observed across the year.
- Leaving a tooltip cursor on as well as the bar spotlight. Two hover markers on the same month compete; the cursor is turned off.
- Reading `activeIndex` with `Number()` directly. Recharts passes `null` when inactive and `Number(null)` is 0, which would pin the tooltip to January.

## Notes

- `COMBO_PERIODS` and the `ComboPoint`, `ComboPeriod` and `ComboMeasure` types are exported. This year totals 83,200 sessions against 76,050 ("+9.4%") at 3.7% conversion; last year totals 76,050 against 70,300 ("+8.2%") at 3.3%.
- Frame, headline, period pill, legend, tooltip card, tiles and pulse dot come from `line-chart-card-parts.tsx`.

## Definition of done

The card shows "Sessions · Conversion 3.7%", "83,200" with a lime "+9.4%" chip, a "This year" pill, a legend, lime rounded bars on a 0 to 9K left axis and a blue dotted line on a 0% to 6% right axis, and tiles "Sessions · total 83,200" and "Conversion · average 3.7%". Hovering a month darkens its bar, fades the rest, pulses a dot on the line and shows a tooltip with both values. Picking "Last year" from the pill shows "76,050" and "+8.2%".

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Combobox

React Aria's `ComboBox` dressed in the kit's existing parts. The field is Input's `InputBase`, so hover, focus, invalid and disabled states match every other text field, and the menu is Select's surface, so the motion and row styling match every other list. Two details are its own: the popover anchors to the whole field and copies its measured width, and the list scrolls under a progressive top blur that ramps in over the first 24px of scroll.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Type to filter a list: Input's own field with a chevron toggle, and a field-width menu with sections, a check and a scroll fade.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. React Aria would anchor the popover to the bare `<input>`. The component instead passes `groupRef={fieldRef}` into `InputBase` and `triggerRef={fieldRef}` to the `AriaPopover`, so the menu opens under the full field, icon and chevron included.
2. A `ResizeObserver` on that field writes `field.offsetWidth` into state, and the popover gets `style={{ width: fieldWidth }}`. The menu therefore stays exactly as wide as the field through container resizes and font loading.
3. The toggle is an `AriaButton` in `InputBase`'s `trailingAddon`. React Aria finds it by context and wires it as the open button. Its `ChevronDownSmall` turns `rotate-180` while open over 200ms.
4. `useScrollFade()` turns the listbox's `scrollTop` into a 0–1 `progress` over its distance, and `<ScrollFade progress>` overlays a masked backdrop blur plus a wash at the top of the list. `onOpenChange` calls `fade.reset()` on each open, because every opening starts the list at the top.
5. `allowsEmptyCollection` keeps the popover open when the filter matches nothing, and the listbox's `renderEmptyState` shows `emptyMessage` ("No results" by default) instead of closing on the user mid-word.
6. `ComboBoxItem` uses the shared `MENU_ITEM` row and only adds `MENU_ITEM_ACTIVE` for the focused row. Selection shows as a 16px `RiCheckLine` in the accent colour at the end of the row. `ComboBoxSection` adds a muted `Header` and 8px of top padding between groups.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `popover offset = 4px`
  Matches Select, so a combobox and a select in the same form open their menus at the same distance.
- `list height = max-h-[240px], overscroll-contain`
  About six rows before the list scrolls. `overscroll-contain` stops a wheel at the end of the list from scrolling the page behind it.
- `scroll-fade distance = 24px (SCROLL_FADE_DISTANCE)`
  The fade reaches full strength after one row of scrolling. A longer ramp leaves the first rows sharp under the edge, and a shorter one makes the blur pop in.
- `emptyMessage = "No results"`
  Shown in tertiary text instead of closing the list, so a typo leaves the popover in place and the user can correct it.

## API

```ts
function ComboBox<T extends object>(props: Omit<AriaComboBoxProps<T>, "children" | "className"> & { label?: ReactNode; hint?: ReactNode; placeholder?: string; leadingIcon?: IconComponent; size?: InputSize; emptyMessage?: ReactNode; className?: string; popoverClassName?: string; children: ReactNode | ((item: T) => ReactNode); ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element; function ComboBoxItem(props: Omit<AriaListBoxItemProps, "children"> & { children?: ReactNode }): JSX.Element; function ComboBoxSection<T extends object>(props: Omit<AriaListBoxSectionProps<T>, "className" | "children"> & { title?: ReactNode; className?: string; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
```

- `label: ReactNode`
  Field label, wired as the accessible name. Without it, pass `aria-label`.
- `placeholder: string`
  Input placeholder.
- `leadingIcon: ComponentType<{ className?: string }>`
  Icon at the start of the field, for example `RiSearchLine`.
- `hint: ReactNode`
  Help text under the field. Shown in the error colour while the field is invalid.
- `size: "medium" | "small"` — default `"medium"`
  Field height, 36px or 32px, as Input.
- `emptyMessage: ReactNode` — default `"No results"`
  Shown in the list when nothing matches.
- `defaultItems / items: Iterable<T>`
  Data for a function child. `defaultItems` lets React Aria filter; `items` means you filter.
- `value / defaultValue / onChange: Key | null`
  React Aria's selected key, controlled or uncontrolled.
- `inputValue / onInputChange / allowsCustomValue: string / boolean`
  Control the typed text, or keep text that matches no row.
- `popoverClassName: string`
  Classes on the list popover.
- `children: ReactNode | ((item: T) => ReactNode)`
  `ComboBoxItem` rows, optionally grouped in `ComboBoxSection`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function ComboBox<T extends object>({
  label,
  hint,
  placeholder,
  leadingIcon,
  size,
  emptyMessage = "No results",
  className,
  popoverClassName,
  children,
  ref,
  ...props
}: ComboBoxProps<T>) {
  const direction = useDirection();
  const fieldRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const fade = useScrollFade();
  const [fieldWidth, setFieldWidth] = useState<number>();

  useEffect(() => {
    const field = fieldRef.current;
    if (!field) return;
    const observer = new ResizeObserver(() => setFieldWidth(field.offsetWidth));
    observer.observe(field);
    return () => observer.disconnect();
  }, []);

  return (
    <AriaComboBox
      ref={ref}
      allowsEmptyCollection
      {...props}
      className={cx("group flex flex-col gap-1", className)}
      onOpenChange={(isOpen, trigger) => {
        // Each opening starts the list at the top, so the fade starts hidden.
        if (isOpen) fade.reset();
        props.onOpenChange?.(isOpen, trigger);
      }}
    >
      {({ isOpen, isRequired, isInvalid }) => (
        <>
          {label ? <Label isRequired={isRequired}>{label}</Label> : null}
          <InputBase
            groupRef={fieldRef}
            size={size}
            placeholder={placeholder}
            leadingIcon={leadingIcon}
            trailingAddon={
              <AriaButton
                className={({ isFocusVisible }) =>
                  cx(
                    "-m-1 flex shrink-0 cursor-pointer items-center justify-center rounded-md p-1 text-text-secondary outline-none",
                    isFocusVisible && "ring-2 ring-border-focus-ring",
                  )
                }
              >
                <ChevronDownSmall
                  className={cx("size-4 transition-transform duration-200 ease", isOpen && "rotate-180")}
                />
              </AriaButton>
            }
          />
          {hint ? <HintText isInvalid={isInvalid}>{hint}</HintText> : null}
          <AriaPopover
            triggerRef={fieldRef}
            dir={direction}
            offset={4}
            style={{ width: fieldWidth }}
            className={cx(MENU_POPOVER_SURFACE, "flex flex-col overflow-hidden p-2", popoverClassName)}
          >
            <div className="relative flex min-h-0 flex-col">
              <AriaListBox
                onScroll={fade.onScroll}
                renderEmptyState={() => (
                  <div className="px-2 py-2 text-body-medium text-text-tertiary">{emptyMessage}</div>
                )}
                className={cx(MENU_ITEMS_CONTAINER, "max-h-[240px] min-h-0 overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain")}
              >
                {children}
              </AriaListBox>
              <ScrollFade progress={fade.progress} />
            </div>
          </AriaPopover>
        </>
      )}
    </AriaComboBox>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The `ResizeObserver` on the field is disconnected in the effect's cleanup on unmount. React Aria removes the popover portal on close.

**Reduced motion.** The menu fade, scale and blur and the 200ms chevron rotation are CSS transitions from the shared menu recipe. None of them moves content across the screen, so they stay under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The scroll fade follows scroll position directly and has no animation of its own.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Giving rows rich children with no `textValue`. Filtering and the input text after selection both use `textValue`, so an avatar row without it never matches anything typed.
- Leaving out both `label` and `aria-label`. React Aria logs an accessibility warning and the input has no accessible name.
- Expecting `className` to style the input. It goes on the root column. Width belongs there, and field styling comes from `InputBase` and `size`.
- Passing data through `items` and expecting the list to filter as the user types. With `items` the consumer owns filtering. Use `defaultItems` to let React Aria filter by `textValue`.

## Notes

- With a function child, pass the data through `defaultItems` (uncontrolled filtering) or `items` (you filter). With static `ComboBoxItem` children, React Aria filters by `textValue` itself.
- `menuTrigger="focus"` opens the list on focus, which suits short lists such as timezones. The default `"input"` waits for typing.

## Definition of done

Typing "ma" into Assignee narrows the list to Maya Chen and Mateo Ruiz, and the menu is exactly as wide as the field, icon to chevron. Typing "zz" keeps the menu open with "No one by that name". Choosing a row closes the menu, fills the input with the name and shows a check on that row the next time the menu opens. In Timezone the list opens on focus with three headed sections, and scrolling it blurs the rows that pass under the top edge. Escape closes either menu, and arrow keys move the highlight.

and where, so I can check them.
