# Build: Command Palette

A searchable list of actions and destinations opened with ⌘K / Ctrl+K: jump to a page, run a command, find a record. It is React Aria's Autocomplete and Menu inside a modal dialog, so focus stays in the search field while the arrow keys move a highlight through the list, Enter runs the highlighted row, and focus goes back to where it was on close. The panel sits 12vh from the top over a 20% black scrim and fades in while rising 10px and sharpening from a 4px blur over 200ms.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

⌘K palette of searchable commands with sections, icons and shortcuts, built-in or custom filtering, on React Aria Autocomplete and Menu.

- Category: overlay
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `CommandPalette` keeps open state and the query, each controllable (`isOpen` / `onOpenChange`, `inputValue` / `onInputChange`). Its `setOpen` notifies the parent and, on every opening, empties the query (also through `onInputChange("")`) and calls `fade.reset()`, so each opening starts with a blank field and the list at its top.
2. The shortcut is a `keydown` listener on `window` that fires on `metaKey || ctrlKey` plus the `shortcut` letter (default "k", case-insensitive), calls `preventDefault` and toggles the palette. The effect has no dependency array, so it re-subscribes every render and always reads the current `isOpen`; `shortcut={false}` skips it.
3. The overlay is an `AriaModalOverlay` (`isDismissable`, `dir` from `useDirection()`) laid out as `fixed inset-x-0 top-0 z-100 h-(--visual-viewport-height) items-start justify-center px-4 pt-[12vh]`, so the panel stays above a phone's keyboard. A sibling `aria-hidden` div is the `bg-black/20` scrim, fading over 150ms via `group-data-[entering]/palette` and `group-data-[exiting]/palette`.
4. `AriaModal` is `max-h-[min(560px,76vh)] w-full max-w-[560px]` with `transition-[opacity,translate,scale,filter] duration-200 ease-out`: it enters from `opacity-0` and, under `motion-safe:`, `translate-y-2.5 scale-[0.98] blur-[4px]`, and exits to `translate-y-2 scale-[0.98] blur-[3px]`. Inside, an `AriaDialog` (`rounded-3xl`, button border, `shadow-sidebar`, `overflow-clip`) labelled by `aria-label` holds the search row, the list and the footer.
5. `AriaAutocomplete` wires an `autoFocus` `AriaSearchField` (search icon plus a bare `AriaInput`, native cancel button hidden) to an `AriaMenu`. Its filter is `filter ?? contains`, where `contains` comes from `useFilter({ sensitivity: "base" })` (ignores case and accents); `filter={null}` passes no filter, so the children show as given. The menu is the `overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain` scroller with a `ScrollFade` over its top, `renderEmptyState` shows `emptyState`, and `onAction` closes the palette first and then calls the consumer's `onAction(key)`.
6. `CommandPaletteItem` is an `AriaMenuItem` whose `textValue` falls back to string children; it is a `rounded-xl px-3 py-2.5` row that takes `bg-background-secondary-default` while focused (100ms colour transition), with a 16px icon, the label, an optional muted `description` and an optional `Kbd` shortcut. `CommandPaletteSection` is an `AriaMenuSection` with an `AriaHeader` title (`text-body-2-medium text-text-tertiary`) and `pt-2` on every section after the first. The default footer reads "Navigate with ↑ ↓" and "Select ↵"; `footer={false}` hides it.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `panel position = pt-[12vh], max-w-[560px], max-h-[min(560px,76vh)]`
  High enough that the results list has room to grow downward, but not pinned to the top edge; the height cap keeps the footer on screen on short viewports.
- `enter motion = 200ms ease-out, opacity 0, translate-y 10px, scale 0.98, blur 4px`
  The docs-site search's motion: a short lift and sharpen reads as the panel arriving, without travelling far enough to delay typing.
- `exit motion = translate-y 8px, scale 0.98, blur 3px`
  Slightly smaller than the entrance so closing feels quicker than opening.
- `scrim = bg-black/20, 150ms fade`
  Dims the page enough to focus the palette while keeping the page legible behind it.
- `shortcut = "k" with ⌘ or Ctrl`
  The common convention for command palettes; `metaKey || ctrlKey` covers macOS and Windows/Linux with one listener.

## API

```ts
function CommandPalette(props: { isOpen?: boolean; defaultOpen?: boolean; onOpenChange?: (isOpen: boolean) => void; shortcut?: string | false; "aria-label"?: string; placeholder?: string; inputValue?: string; onInputChange?: (value: string) => void; filter?: ((textValue: string, inputValue: string) => boolean) | null; onAction?: (key: Key) => void; emptyState?: ReactNode; footer?: ReactNode | false; className?: string; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
function CommandPaletteItem(props: Omit<AriaMenuItemProps, "children" | "className"> & { icon?: IconComponent; description?: ReactNode; shortcut?: string; className?: string; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
function CommandPaletteSection(props: { title?: ReactNode; className?: string; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
```

- `isOpen / onOpenChange: boolean / (isOpen: boolean) => void`
  Controlled open state; `defaultOpen` for uncontrolled.
- `shortcut: string | false` — default `"k"`
  Letter that toggles the palette with ⌘ / Ctrl; `false` turns it off.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Command palette"`
  Accessible name of the dialog, field and menu.
- `placeholder: string` — default `"Type a command or search…"`
  Search field placeholder.
- `inputValue / onInputChange: string / (value: string) => void`
  Controlled query, e.g. for remote search.
- `filter: ((textValue, inputValue) => boolean) | null` — default `locale-aware contains`
  Row matcher; `null` shows the children unfiltered.
- `onAction: (key: Key) => void`
  Runs with the chosen item's id after the palette closes.
- `emptyState: ReactNode` — default `"No results"`
  Shown when nothing matches.
- `footer: ReactNode | false` — default `navigate / select hints`
  The hint row under the list; `false` hides it.
- `CommandPaletteItem.icon / description / shortcut: IconComponent / ReactNode / string`
  Leading icon, trailing muted text and a keyboard hint for the row.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function CommandPalette({
  isOpen: controlledOpen,
  defaultOpen = false,
  onOpenChange,
  shortcut = "k",
  "aria-label": ariaLabel = "Command palette",
  placeholder = "Type a command or search…",
  inputValue: controlledInput,
  onInputChange,
  filter,
  onAction,
  emptyState = "No results",
  footer,
  className,
  children,
}: CommandPaletteProps) {
  const direction = useDirection();
  const localize = useTemplateCopy();
  const label = localize(ariaLabel);
  const { contains } = useFilter({ sensitivity: "base" });
  const fade = useScrollFade();
  const [uncontrolledOpen, setUncontrolledOpen] = useState(defaultOpen);
  const [uncontrolledInput, setUncontrolledInput] = useState("");
  const isOpen = controlledOpen ?? uncontrolledOpen;
  const inputValue = controlledInput ?? uncontrolledInput;

  const setOpen = (next: boolean) => {
    setUncontrolledOpen(next);
    onOpenChange?.(next);
    if (next) {
      // Every opening starts fresh: an empty query and the list at its top.
      setUncontrolledInput("");
      onInputChange?.("");
      fade.reset();
    }
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    if (shortcut === false) return;
    const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (!(event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) || event.key.toLowerCase() !== shortcut.toLowerCase()) return;
      event.preventDefault();
      setOpen(!isOpen);
    };
    window.addEventListener("keydown", onKeyDown);
    return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKeyDown);
  });

  return (
    <AriaModalOverlay
      isOpen={isOpen}
      onOpenChange={setOpen}
      isDismissable
      dir={direction}
      className="group/palette fixed inset-x-0 top-0 z-100 flex h-(--visual-viewport-height) items-start justify-center px-4 pt-[12vh]"
    >
      <div
        aria-hidden
        className="absolute inset-0 bg-black/20 transition-opacity duration-150 ease-out group-data-[entering]/palette:opacity-0 group-data-[exiting]/palette:opacity-0"
      />
      <AriaModal
        className={cx(
          "relative flex max-h-[min(560px,76vh)] w-full max-w-[560px] flex-col outline-none",
          "transition-[opacity,translate,scale,filter] duration-200 ease-out",
          "data-[entering]:opacity-0 data-[exiting]:opacity-0",
          "motion-safe:data-[entering]:translate-y-2.5 motion-safe:data-[entering]:scale-[0.98] motion-safe:data-[entering]:blur-[4px]",
          "motion-safe:data-[exiting]:translate-y-2 motion-safe:data-[exiting]:scale-[0.98] motion-safe:data-[exiting]:blur-[3px]",
        )}
      >
        <AriaDialog
          aria-label={label}
          className={cx(
            "flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col overflow-clip rounded-3xl border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default shadow-sidebar outline-none",
            className,
          )}
        >
          <AriaAutocomplete
            inputValue={inputValue}
            onInputChange={(value) => {
              setUncontrolledInput(value);
              onInputChange?.(value);
            }}
            filter={filter === null ? undefined : filter ?? contains}
          >
            <AriaSearchField aria-label={label} autoFocus className="flex shrink-0 items-center gap-2 border-b border-separator-border p-3">
              <RiSearchLine className="size-5 shrink-0 text-foreground-icon-secondary" aria-hidden />
              <AriaInput
                placeholder={localize(placeholder)}
                className="min-w-0 flex-1 bg-transparent text-body-medium text-text-primary outline-none placeholder:text-text-tertiary [&::-webkit-search-cancel-button]:hidden"
              />
            </AriaSearchField>
            <div className="relative flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col">
              <AriaMenu
                aria-label={label}
                onScroll={fade.onScroll}
                onAction={(key) => {
                  setOpen(false);
                  onAction?.(key);
                }}
                renderEmptyState={() => (
                  <div className="flex min-h-32 flex-col items-center justify-center gap-1 px-4 text-center text-body-medium text-text-tertiary">
                    {localize(emptyState)}
                  </div>
                )}
                className="flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-0.5 overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain p-2 outline-none [scrollbar-width:thin]"
              >
                {children}
              </AriaMenu>
              <ScrollFade progress={fade.progress} />
            </div>
          </AriaAutocomplete>
          {footer === false ? null : (
            <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center justify-between border-t border-separator-border px-3 py-2 text-body-regular text-text-tertiary">
              {localize(
                footer ?? (
                  <>
                    <span>Navigate with ↑ ↓</span>
                    <span className="flex items-center gap-1.5">
                      Select
                      <Kbd aria-label="Enter">
                        <RiCornerDownLeftLine className="size-3" aria-hidden />
                      </Kbd>
                    </span>
                  </>
                ),
              )}
            </div>
          )}
        </AriaDialog>
      </AriaModal>
    </AriaModalOverlay>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The `window` keydown listener is removed by its effect cleanup on every re-render and on unmount. React Aria restores focus to the previously focused element when the modal closes and unmounts it after the exit transition.

**Reduced motion.** The lift, scale and blur are behind `motion-safe:`, so under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the panel only fades over 200ms and the scrim over 150ms.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not move DOM focus into the list. Autocomplete keeps focus in the field and moves a virtual highlight, so typing keeps working while arrowing through results.
- Do not give the shortcut effect an empty dependency array. The listener would capture the first `isOpen` and ⌘K could open the palette but never close it.
- Do not pass non-string children without `textValue`. The filter matches on `textValue`, which only falls back to children when they are a plain string.
- Do not pass `filter={null}` and forget to filter the children yourself. It turns off matching entirely, which is meant for custom ranking.

## Notes

- The palette's own copy (label, placeholder, empty state, footer hints) runs through `useTemplateCopy()`, so a TemplateCopyProvider translates it.
- Escape follows React Aria's search field: with text in the field it clears the query first, and a second Escape closes the palette.
- The overlay is z-100, the same layer as Modal and Drawer.

## Definition of done

Pressing the search bar, or ⌘K / Ctrl+K anywhere, dims the page and brings the palette in 12vh from the top with the field focused. Typing "set" leaves only Settings; arrow keys move the grey highlight; Enter closes the palette and the page reads "Ran Settings". With a query typed, Escape clears it, a second Escape closes the palette and focus returns to the search bar. Clicking the scrim also closes it.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Composer Attachments

The strip of file tiles that sits above a chat prompt. Each 56px tile shows a coloured icon for the file type, the name and the size, with a dismiss in the corner. Give a tile a `progress` value and an accent ring draws clockwise around its rounded edge from top centre while a 9px percentage counts in the corner; when it reaches 100 the percentage blurs out and the dismiss blurs in on the same spot. `ComposerAttachButton` opens the real file picker and hands back `File` objects; only names and sizes are read.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

56px attachment tiles for a chat composer: type icon, name, size and remove, with a ring that traces the tile edge while uploading.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. `kindOf(name, mime)` maps the extension through a lookup table (png → image, xlsx → spreadsheet, tsx → code, and so on), then falls back to the MIME family (`image/`, `video/`, `audio/`), then to "file". Each kind has one Remix icon and one status text token, so a PDF is always rose and a spreadsheet always lime in both themes.
2. `formatBytes` divides by 1024 until the value is under 1024 and prints one decimal below 10 and a whole number above: 812 B, 4.2 KB, 37 MB.
3. The upload ring is one SVG `<path>` laid over the tile at `-inset-px`, so the 2px stroke sits on the 1px border. The path is the tile outline itself: a 54px rect with an 11px radius, starting at (28, 1) top centre and running clockwise. `pathLength={100}` normalises its length, so `strokeDashoffset = 100 - progress` draws exactly that percentage of the edge, with a 200ms transition between ticks.
4. The top-right corner holds two layers: the percentage and the remove button. While `progress < 100` the percentage is visible and the button is at opacity 0 with a 2px blur; landing swaps the two classes, so one blurs out as the other blurs in. Hovering or focusing the tile (`group-hover`, `group-focus-within`) swaps them early, which turns the button into "Cancel <name>" for a file still uploading.
5. `ComposerAttachButton` renders a normal `<button>` that calls `.click()` on a hidden `<input type="file" multiple>`. On change it copies `files` into an array, then clears `value`, so picking the same file twice still fires `change`. `attachmentsFromFiles` turns the `File` list into `{ id, name, size, kind, progress }` without reading file contents.
6. The strip is a horizontally scrolling `<ul>`. New tiles pop in from 50% scale with the kit `cell-pop` keyframes over 240ms, behind `motion-safe:`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `tile = 56px square, 12px radius, 1px composer-panel-tile-border`
  Large enough for an 18px icon over two 11px text lines with 6px padding, small enough that five tiles fit above a 360px-wide prompt. The border token is neutral-200 in light and 14% white in dark, so tiles separate from the composer surface in both themes.
- `RING_PATH = M28 1H44A11 11 0 0 1 55 12 … Z (54px rect, r 11)`
  Centring a 2px stroke 1px inside the 56px box puts it exactly over the border. The radius drops from 12 to 11 because the stroke centre is 1px in from the outer curve. Starting at x=28 makes the ring begin at top centre, not at a corner.
- `pathLength = 100`
  The real path length of a rounded rect is awkward to compute. Normalising it to 100 lets progress go straight into `strokeDashoffset` with no measuring and no `getTotalLength()` call.
- `corner swap = 200ms opacity + blur(2px)`
  Blur alongside opacity makes the percentage and the dismiss read as one element changing, not two elements fighting for the corner.

## API

```ts
function ComposerAttachments(props: { attachments: ComposerAttachment[]; onRemove?: (id: string) => void; className?: string }): JSX.Element | null
function ComposerAttachmentTile(props: { attachment: ComposerAttachment; onRemove?: (id: string) => void; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function ComposerAttachButton(props: ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> & { onFiles: (files: File[]) => void; accept?: string; multiple?: boolean; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
function kindOf(name: string, mime?: string): AttachmentKind
function formatBytes(bytes: number): string
function attachmentsFromFiles(files: File[], idPrefix: string, progress?: number): ComposerAttachment[]
interface ComposerAttachment { id: string; name: string; size: number; kind?: AttachmentKind; progress?: number }
```

- `attachments: ComposerAttachment[]`
  Tiles in order. An empty array renders nothing.
- `attachment.progress: number`
  0-100 draws the ring and the corner percentage. Omit it, or pass 100, for a landed file.
- `attachment.kind: AttachmentKind`
  Icon and colour. Derived from the name with `kindOf` when omitted.
- `onRemove: (id: string) => void`
  Shows the corner dismiss. Called with the attachment id for remove and for cancel.
- `onFiles: (files: File[]) => void`
  `ComposerAttachButton`: receives the picked files. Never called with an empty array.
- `accept: string`
  `ComposerAttachButton`: forwarded to the file input, e.g. "image/*,.pdf".
- `multiple: boolean` — default `true`
  `ComposerAttachButton`: allow picking several files at once.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the strip, tile or button.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/*
 * The ring traces the tile's own rounded edge, starting at top centre and
 * running clockwise. Tile is 56px with a 12px radius; the stroke is centred
 * 1px in, so the path is a 54px rect with an 11px radius. pathLength=100 turns
 * progress straight into a dash offset.
 */
const RING_PATH =
  "M28 1H44A11 11 0 0 1 55 12V44A11 11 0 0 1 44 55H12A11 11 0 0 1 1 44V12A11 11 0 0 1 12 1Z";

function UploadRing({ progress }: { progress: number }) {
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 56 56" aria-hidden className="pointer-events-none absolute -inset-px size-14 overflow-visible">
      <path
        d={RING_PATH}
        pathLength={100}
        fill="none"
        stroke="currentColor"
        strokeWidth={2}
        strokeLinecap="round"
        strokeDasharray="100 100"
        strokeDashoffset={100 - progress}
        className="text-accent-500 transition-[stroke-dashoffset] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none"
      />
    </svg>
  );
}

export interface ComposerAttachmentTileProps {
  attachment: ComposerAttachment;
  /** Removes a landed file, or cancels one still uploading. */
  onRemove?: (id: string) => void;
  className?: string;
}

export function ComposerAttachmentTile({ attachment, onRemove, className }: ComposerAttachmentTileProps) {
  const { id, name, size, progress } = attachment;
  const kind = attachment.kind ?? kindOf(name);
  const { icon: Icon, tone, label } = KIND_STYLE[kind];
  const pct = progress === undefined ? 100 : Math.max(0, Math.min(100, Math.round(progress)));
  const uploading = pct < 100;
  // The corner holds the percentage while uploading and the dismiss once landed.
  // Hover or keyboard focus swaps them early, so an upload can be cancelled.
  const fade = "transition-[opacity,filter] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none";

  return (
    <div
      title={`${name}, ${formatBytes(size)}`}
      data-uploading={uploading || undefined}
      className={cx(
        "group relative flex size-14 shrink-0 flex-col justify-between rounded-xl border border-composer-panel-tile-border bg-background-primary-default p-1.5",
        className,
      )}
    >
      <Icon className={cx("size-[18px] shrink-0", tone)} aria-hidden />
      <span className="sr-only">{label}:</span>
      <span className="flex min-w-0 flex-col">
        <span className="truncate text-[9px]/[11px] font-medium text-text-primary">{name}</span>
        <span className="truncate text-[9px]/[11px] text-text-tertiary tabular-nums">
          {formatBytes(size)}
          {uploading && <span className="sr-only">, uploading {pct}%</span>}
        </span>
      </span>

      {uploading && <UploadRing progress={pct} />}

      <span
        aria-hidden
        className={cx(
          "pointer-events-none absolute end-1 top-1 text-[9px]/[11px] font-semibold text-accent-500 tabular-nums",
          fade,
          uploading
            ? "opacity-100 blur-none group-focus-within:opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-0"
            : "opacity-0 blur-[2px]",
        )}
      >
        {pct}%
      </span>

      {onRemove && (
        <button
          type="button"
          aria-label={uploading ? `Cancel ${name}` : `Remove ${name}`}
          onClick={() => onRemove(id)}
          className={cx(
            "absolute end-1 top-1 grid size-[18px] place-items-center rounded-full bg-background-tertiary-default text-foreground-icon-secondary outline-none hover:bg-background-tertiary-hover hover:text-foreground-icon-primary focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
            fade,
            uploading
              ? "opacity-0 blur-[2px] group-focus-within:opacity-100 group-focus-within:blur-none group-hover:opacity-100 group-hover:blur-none"
              : "opacity-100 blur-none",
          )}
        >
          <RiCloseLine className="size-3" aria-hidden />
        </button>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The component holds no timers or listeners; the file input is part of the tree. The demo's upload interval is keyed to the active file id and cleared when that file lands, is removed, or the demo unmounts.

**Reduced motion.** The ring's dash transition, the corner blur swap and the hover colours all carry `motion-reduce:transition-none`, and the pop-in animation is behind `motion-safe:`, so tiles appear in place and states switch instantly. The demo also skips the simulated upload and lands files at once.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Forgetting to clear the input `value` after reading it. Without that, picking the same file a second time fires no `change` event and the click looks broken.
- Hiding the dismiss completely while uploading. A visitor who attached the wrong file must be able to cancel, so hover and keyboard focus reveal it early.
- Using a `<circle>` or a CSS conic gradient for the ring. The tile is a rounded square, and a ring that does not follow its edge reads as a separate spinner.
- Reading file contents or creating object URLs just to show a name. The tile needs `name`, `size` and `type`, which are on the `File` object already. Object URLs also need revoking.
- Generating tile ids from the file name alone. The same file picked twice would collide. Prefix ids with a per-pick counter, as `attachmentsFromFiles(files, prefix)` expects.

## Notes

- The component never uploads. A real uploader updates `progress` on each attachment; the demo simulates that with a 40ms interval that moves one queued file at a time, so tiles land in order.
- Image files show the image icon, not a thumbnail. Pass your own tile for thumbnails if you create object URLs.

## Definition of done

Three tiles show a coloured type icon, a truncated name and a size. "Add sample files" queues three more that upload one after another: an accent ring draws clockwise from top centre and the corner counts up, then the percentage blurs into a dismiss. Hovering an uploading tile shows "Cancel". The + button opens the browser file picker and picked files appear as tiles with their real names and sizes. Clicking a dismiss removes that tile.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Composer Footer

The row under a composer prompt. On the left are a paperclip that opens the file picker, icon toggles for tools such as web search, and a slot for a model picker. A keyboard hint fills the middle, and on the right one round button sends, then turns into stop while a reply is generating, with an accent arc spinning around it. The footer owns no text field; the host passes `canSend`, `generating` and the two callbacks.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Bottom bar of a chat composer: attach, tool toggles, a model slot and a key hint, with a send button that becomes stop while replying.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `SendStopButton` is a single React Aria `Button`. While `generating` it is labelled "Stop generating" and calls `onStop`; otherwise it is labelled "Send", calls `onSend`, and is disabled until `canSend` is true. Keeping one element means focus and the pointer stay put when the job flips.
2. The arrow and the stop square share one grid cell (`[grid-area:1/1]`). The one not in use goes to `scale-50 opacity-0 blur-[2px]` and the other to full size, over a 200ms transition, so the icons cross-fade instead of jumping.
3. An SVG circle sits 4px outside the button. Its arc is `strokeDasharray="28 100"` on `pathLength={100}`, and while generating the SVG fades in and gets `motion-safe:animate-spin`. A visually hidden `role="status"` span says "Generating a reply" for screen readers.
4. Tools are React Aria `ToggleButton`s, so each one exposes `aria-pressed`. The set of active ids is controlled through `activeTools` / `onToolsChange`, or kept in local state seeded from `defaultActiveTools`. Pressed tools take the `status-blue` background and text tokens.
5. The paperclip is a React Aria `Button` that clicks a hidden `<input type="file" multiple>`. Picked files go to `onAttach` as `File[]`, and the input is cleared so the same file can be picked again. Nothing is read or uploaded.
6. The root is a container (`@container`). The hint paragraph carries `@max-[34rem]:hidden`, so in a narrow composer it disappears before the buttons have to shrink. The model slot is `min-w-0 shrink`, so a long model name truncates instead of pushing send off the edge.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `send button = 36px, arc ring 44px`
  The ring sits 4px outside the button, which leaves a visible gap. The arc covers 28% of the circle, enough to read as spinning without looking like a progress bar.
- `hint breakpoint = container width 34rem`
  Below this, the hint would truncate into fragments like "Enter to se…". Hiding it entirely keeps the controls intact at phone widths.
- `tooltip delay = 300ms`
  The kit tooltip defaults to no delay. In a row of five icon buttons, that makes tooltips flash while the pointer is moving across to send.

## API

```ts
function ComposerFooter(props: { onAttach?: (files: File[]) => void; accept?: string; tools?: ComposerTool[]; activeTools?: string[]; defaultActiveTools?: string[]; onToolsChange?: (ids: string[]) => void; model?: ReactNode; hint?: ReactNode; canSend?: boolean; generating?: boolean; onSend?: () => void; onStop?: () => void; className?: string }): JSX.Element
interface ComposerTool { id: string; label: string; icon: RemixiconComponentType }
```

- `onAttach: (files: File[]) => void`
  Shows the paperclip and receives picked files.
- `accept: string`
  Forwarded to the file input.
- `tools: ComposerTool[]` — default `COMPOSER_TOOLS`
  Icon toggles after the paperclip. Pass `[]` to hide them.
- `activeTools: string[]`
  Controlled ids of switched-on tools.
- `defaultActiveTools: string[]` — default `[]`
  Starting ids when uncontrolled.
- `onToolsChange: (ids: string[]) => void`
  Called with the new set after a toggle.
- `model: ReactNode`
  Slot after a divider, usually a ghost `ModelSelect`.
- `hint: ReactNode`
  Overrides the default hint ("Enter to send…" or "Writing a reply…").
- `canSend: boolean` — default `false`
  Enables send when not generating.
- `generating: boolean` — default `false`
  Turns send into stop and spins the ring.
- `onSend: () => void`
  Called when send is pressed.
- `onStop: () => void`
  Called when stop is pressed. Without it the stop button is disabled.
- `className: string`
  Classes for the footer row.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
function SendStopButton({
  generating,
  canSend,
  onSend,
  onStop,
}: Pick<ComposerFooterProps, "generating" | "canSend" | "onSend" | "onStop">) {
  // One button, two jobs. While generating it is always pressable and stops;
  // otherwise it sends and is disabled until there is something to send.
  const isDisabled = generating ? !onStop : !canSend;
  const swap = "[grid-area:1/1] transition-[opacity,scale,filter] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none";
  const shown = "scale-100 opacity-100 blur-none";
  const hidden = "scale-50 opacity-0 blur-[2px]";

  return (
    <span className="relative grid shrink-0 place-items-center">
      <svg
        aria-hidden
        viewBox="0 0 44 44"
        className={cx(
          "pointer-events-none absolute -inset-1 size-11 text-accent-500 transition-opacity duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
          generating ? "opacity-100 motion-safe:animate-spin" : "opacity-0",
        )}
      >
        <circle cx="22" cy="22" r="20.5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2" strokeLinecap="round" pathLength={100} strokeDasharray="28 100" />
      </svg>
      <AriaButton
        aria-label={generating ? "Stop generating" : "Send"}
        isDisabled={isDisabled}
        onPress={() => (generating ? onStop?.() : onSend?.())}
        className={cx(
          "grid size-9 cursor-pointer place-items-center rounded-full bg-button-primary text-text-white shadow-xs outline-none",
          "transition-[scale] duration-150 ease-out data-[pressed]:scale-95 motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:data-[pressed]:scale-100",
          "data-[focus-visible]:ring-2 data-[focus-visible]:ring-border-focus-ring data-[focus-visible]:ring-offset-2",
          "disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:text-button-primary-disabled-foreground",
        )}
      >
        <RiArrowUpLine aria-hidden className={cx("size-[18px]", swap, generating ? hidden : shown)} />
        <RiStopFill aria-hidden className={cx("size-3.5", swap, generating ? shown : hidden)} />
      </AriaButton>
    </span>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The footer has no timers or listeners of its own; React Aria owns the press, toggle and tooltip handlers. The demo clears its streaming interval on completion, on stop and on unmount.

**Reduced motion.** The ring keeps its arc but does not spin (`motion-safe:animate-spin`). The icon cross-fade, the ring fade and the press scale use `motion-reduce:transition-none` and `motion-reduce:data-[pressed]:scale-100`, so states switch instantly. Tooltips follow the kit's own reduced-motion rule.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Rendering separate send and stop buttons. Swapping them unmounts the focused button, so keyboard focus drops to the page body mid-reply.
- Disabling the button while generating. Stop must stay pressable, so the disabled check only applies when not generating.
- Expecting the footer to send on Enter. It has no text field. The default hint describes the usual wiring, which the host does in its textarea's `onKeyDown`; pass `hint` if your keys differ.

## Notes

- The demo streams a canned reply one word every 55ms from an interval that is cleared on completion, on stop and on unmount. Escape in the prompt also stops it.
- The model slot accepts any node. The demo passes a ghost `ModelSelect`, and attachments render above the prompt with `ComposerAttachments`. Below a 26rem container the demo hides the model name (`@max-[26rem]:[&_[data-model-name]]:sr-only`) so only the monogram shows, and the footer tightens its gap from 4px to 2px.
- The tool list is sample data: Search the web, Run code and Think longer. Pass `tools` with your own `{ id, label, icon }` entries.

## Definition of done

Send stays disabled until text is typed. Sending clears the prompt, the button turns into a stop square inside a spinning accent arc, and the reply streams in. Pressing stop, or Escape in the prompt, ends it and marks it Stopped. Letting it finish turns the button back into send. Tool toggles report pressed state, the paperclip opens the file picker, and the hint is hidden in narrow composers.

# Build: Composer Loader

A wrapper that lights up a chat composer while a reply is on its way. It paints the pill surface itself, then runs a band of light around the rim above it: a crisp line, a tight glow and a wide bloom, all dash segments on one SVG rounded-rect stroke. The outer half of each stroke is clipped by the pill, so the glow only bleeds inward. Flipping `active` fades the whole effect in or out over 450ms.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Wraps a chat composer while the agent works: an iridescent band orbits the pill rim with a soft bloom, fading in and out.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. A `ResizeObserver` on the clipping layer keeps `box` (default 640×52) in sync with the rendered size, and the SVG uses that as its `viewBox` with `preserveAspectRatio="none"`, so stroke widths and blur radii stay in real pixels.
2. Each layer is a `<rect>` with `rx = radius ?? h / 2` and `pathLength={100}`, so the dash is measured in percent of the perimeter and travels at constant speed around the end caps. `strokeDasharray` is `len (100 − len)` with `band = arc / 360 × 100`, and the theme's `bui-composer-loader-dash` keyframes move `stroke-dashoffset` from 0 to −100 once per `speed` seconds.
3. Three layers share one horizontal `linearGradient` (c0, c1, the RGB average of c1 and c2, c2, c3): a wide bloom (`bloom × 2` wide, 14px blur, 0.9 × band long), a tight glow (`line × 3.2`, 6px blur, 0.95 × band) and the crisp line (`line`, 0.5px blur, full band).
4. The softer layers are shorter, and their heads are pulled back behind the tip. The perimeter (`2(w + h) − 8r + 2πr`) converts pixels to path units, and each layer's phase becomes its `animation-delay` (at typical sizes a negative one, a head start) to line the heads up: the glow 10px behind the line, the bloom `bloom + 16`px behind.
5. Blurs are SVG `feGaussianBlur` filters (regions widened to 200%) rather than CSS `filter`, because WebKit ignores CSS filters on individual SVG elements.
6. With `taper > 0`, each layer is drawn as 14 centred copies, each shorter by `taper / 14` and at 1/14 of the opacity, so the two ends ramp up in steps that the blur (raised to `max(0.5, line × 0.8)` on the crisp line) melts together.
7. `active` toggles the clipping layer's opacity between 1 and 0 with a 450ms ease transition. Children render in a `relative` layer above the light.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `DEFAULT_COLORS = #5eead4, #46baec, #e633a4, #00faa7`
  Teal, sky, magenta and mint spread left to right; the middle stop averages sky and magenta, so the band never washes out to white.
- `speed / arc = 4.5s per lap / 120°`
  A third of the rim lit at once, moving slowly enough to read as ambient rather than as a progress bar.
- `line / bloom / bloomStrength / intensity = 2.5px / 16px / 0.3 / 0.7`
  A thin bright edge with a soft inward wash, held under full opacity so it sits on the surface instead of glaring.
- `blur radii = 14, 6, 0.5 (stdDeviation)`
  One per layer: the wide bloom, the tight glow and a hint of softness on the crisp line.
- `head pull-back = glow 10px, bloom `bloom + 16`px`
  The sharp line leads and the soft light trails it, like a highlight sliding along glass.
- `TAPER_STEPS = 14`
  Enough copies that the stepped ramp at each end blurs into a gradient.
- `fade = opacity 450ms ease`
  Toggling on send and reply reads as the composer lighting up rather than snapping.

## API

```ts
function ComposerLoader(props: { children: ReactNode; active?: boolean; colors?: [string, string, string, string]; speed?: number; intensity?: number; bloom?: number; bloomStrength?: number; arc?: number; reverse?: boolean; radius?: number; line?: number; bloomOnly?: boolean; surface?: boolean; taper?: number; blend?: CSSProperties["mixBlendMode"]; offset?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  The composer. Rendered above the light, so keep it transparent while active.
- `active: boolean` — default `true`
  Show the light; fades in and out over 450ms.
- `colors: [string, string, string, string]` — default `teal, sky, magenta, mint`
  Four `#rrggbb` colours spread across the pill from left to right.
- `speed: number` — default `4.5`
  Seconds per full lap.
- `arc: number` — default `120`
  Length of the band, in degrees of 360.
- `intensity: number` — default `0.7`
  Overall opacity of the light.
- `line: number` — default `2.5`
  Width of the crisp line in px; the tight glow is 3.2 times this.
- `bloom / bloomStrength: number` — default `16 / 0.3`
  How far the bloom bleeds inward in px, and its opacity.
- `bloomOnly: boolean` — default `false`
  Draw only the wide bloom, as a soft wash.
- `taper: number` — default `0`
  Fraction of the band that ramps at each end, 0 to 1.
- `reverse: boolean` — default `false`
  Travel counter-clockwise.
- `radius: number`
  Corner radius in px; omit for a full pill.
- `surface: boolean` — default `true`
  Paint the pill surface (primary background, xs shadow) behind the light.
- `blend: CSSProperties["mixBlendMode"]`
  How the light composites over what is beneath it.
- `offset: number` — default `0`
  Moves the band forward by a fraction of the perimeter.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const band = (arc / 360) * 100;
const rx = radius ?? box.h / 2;
const cornerRadius = radius ?? 9999;
const direction = reverse ? "reverse" : "normal";

// Path units per px, for pulling each soft layer's head behind the tip.
// Rounded-rect perimeter: straight runs plus the four corner arcs (for the
// default pill, rx = h/2 and this reduces to 2(w−h) + πh).
const cornerR = Math.min(rx, box.w / 2, box.h / 2);
const perimeter = Math.max(1, 2 * (box.w + box.h) - 8 * cornerR + 2 * Math.PI * cornerR);
const pxUnits = (px: number) => (px * 100) / perimeter;
// A layer's delay is its phase: the larger the phase, the further BACK
// along the lap the band sits (a negative delay is a head start). So
// moving a band forward, `offset` included, means subtracting.
const dashPhase = (len: number, backPx: number) =>
  (reverse ? pxUnits(backPx) : len - band + pxUnits(backPx)) - offset * 100;

// Tapering stacks each layer as shorter, centred copies: the ramp at each
// end is a staircase with one step per copy, so it takes many copies and
// a little blur on the crisp line for the steps to melt into a gradient.
const TAPER_STEPS = 14;
const CRISP_BLUR = taper > 0 ? Math.max(0.5, line * 0.8) : 0.5;
const stroke = (width: number, blur: number, opacity: number, dashLen: number, backPx: number) => {
  const copies = taper > 0 ? TAPER_STEPS : 1;
  return Array.from({ length: copies }, (_, index) => {
    // Copy 0 is the full band; each next one is shorter and moved forward
    // by half the difference, so all of them share one midpoint and the
    // ends thin out step by step.
    const len = dashLen * (1 - (taper * index) / copies);
    const phase = dashPhase(dashLen, backPx) - (dashLen - len) / 2;
    return (
      <rect
        key={index}
        x={0}
        y={0}
        width={box.w}
        height={box.h}
        rx={rx}
        pathLength={100}
        fill="none"
        stroke={`url(#${gradientId})`}
        strokeWidth={width}
        strokeLinecap="round"
        strokeDasharray={`${len} ${100 - len}`}
        className="bui-composer-loader-rect"
        // SVG-native blur, not CSS filter: WebKit (iOS Safari and every iPhone
        // browser) ignores CSS filters on individual SVG elements, which
        // rendered the whole light razor-sharp on phones.
        filter={blur > 0 ? `url(#${gradientId}-b${String(blur).replace(".", "_")})` : undefined}
        style={{
          opacity: opacity / copies,
          animation: `bui-composer-loader-dash ${speed}s linear ${(phase * speed) / 100}s infinite ${direction}`,
        }}
      />
    );
  });
};
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The `ResizeObserver` is disconnected on unmount. The band is a CSS animation and stops with the element. Nothing else is scheduled.

**Reduced motion.** The theme sets `animation: none !important` on every `.bui-composer-loader-rect` under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, which overrides the inline animation. The band then rests as a static glow at the start of the rect path, the top edge, near the top-left corner. The 450ms opacity fade on `active` still runs, since it is a state change rather than a loop.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- The wrapped composer must not paint its own background while `active`. Its children render above the light, so an opaque form covers the band completely. Switch it to `bg-transparent` while busy and let `surface` paint the pill.
- `colors` must be four `#rrggbb` strings. The middle gradient stop is computed by parsing hex pairs, so CSS variables, `rgb()` or short hex give an invalid stop colour.
- Pass `radius` when the composer is not a full pill. Without it the stroke uses `h / 2` and the clipping layer uses 9999px, which only match a pill shape.
- Each layer is wrapped in an SVG blur and animates constantly, so the light costs a repaint every frame while it is visible. Set `active={false}` when nothing is pending, rather than leaving it on at low intensity.
- The first paint uses a 640×52 box until the `ResizeObserver` reports, so a very different size may show a slightly mis-scaled band for one frame.

## Notes

- `offset` moves the band forward by a fraction of the lap, so two loaders on one pill can line up: a short beam with `offset` equal to the difference of the two arcs leads a wider glow tip to tip.
- `blend` sets `mix-blend-mode` on the light layer, for example `screen` to read as light on a dark surface.
- BoardUI's free `agent-composer` uses this exactly: `active={busy}` around a 52px form that turns transparent while the agent is busy.

## Definition of done

With `active` on, a band covering about a third of the rim circles the composer pill once every 4.5s, turning smoothly around both rounded ends. The sharp gradient line leads, with a softer glow and a wide wash trailing slightly behind it, and the glow appears only inside the pill. Setting `active` to false fades it out over about 450ms; setting it back fades it in. Resizing the composer keeps the line at the same thickness and the same lap time. Under reduced motion the band holds still.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Composer Panel

The taller composer for agent surfaces. A radius-24 card holds the prompt on top and the controls underneath: a round + that opens the file picker, a permission picker (Auto, Manual, Plan mode, Bypass all), a model menu, an optional mic and send. A 34px grey status tab can hang off the top edge with the branch, the project folder and a 16px context ring. Send is live only when there is text; Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks the line.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Two-row agent composer: a growing prompt over a toolbar with add, permission mode, model and send, plus a status tab with a context ring.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The prompt is a one-row `<textarea>`. A layout effect on every draft change sets `height: auto`, reads `scrollHeight`, and writes back `min(scrollHeight, 10 lines × 20px + 20px padding)`. Resetting to auto first lets the field shrink when lines are deleted; past ten lines it stops growing and scrolls.
2. `onKeyDown` sends on Enter unless Shift is held or `nativeEvent.isComposing` is true, so an IME confirming a word never sends half a message. Shift+Enter falls through to the textarea's own newline. The form's submit handler calls the same `send()`.
3. `send()` returns early unless the trimmed draft is non-empty and `disabled` is false. It calls `onSubmit({ text, attachments, model, permission })`, clears the draft and the attachment strip, and puts focus back in the field. The send button is `disabled` by the same check, and the kit `bg-button-primary` utility paints its own grey disabled gradient.
4. The + is a `ComposerAttachButton` from Composer Attachments: a button that clicks a hidden `<input type="file" multiple>`. Picked files become tiles through `attachmentsFromFiles`, each batch prefixed by a counter so the same file picked twice gets a new id. Tiles render in a `ComposerAttachments` strip above the prompt, and their dismiss removes them.
5. The permission and model pickers are kit `Dropdown`s with controlled `isOpen`, opening upward (`top start` and `top end`). Each row is a `DropdownItem` with a label, a one-line description and a check on the current choice; choosing a row sets state and closes the menu. The permission trigger shows its surface only on hover, press or while open, so at rest it reads as a label.
6. `ComposerStatusTab` is a separate element passed through the `status` slot, inset 28px (`mx-7`) with top corners rounded. Its ring is two SVG circles rotated -90°; the arc uses `pathLength={100}` and `strokeDasharray="<pct> 100"`, so the percentage maps straight onto the dash. It is exposed as `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `MAX_LINES = 10`
  Long enough for a pasted paragraph or a short stack trace without the toolbar leaving the screen; beyond that the field scrolls.
- `LINE_HEIGHT / FIELD_PADDING_Y = 20px / 20px`
  text-body-regular is 14/20, and the textarea carries pt-3.5 + pb-1.5. `scrollHeight` includes padding, so the cap must add it or the tenth line is clipped.
- `status tab = 34px high, 28px inset, composer-panel-tab-background`
  Inset more than the card's 24px radius, so the tab meets the flat part of the top edge and never the curve. The token is neutral-200 in light and half-opacity neutral-700 in dark, so it separates from the card in both themes.
- `card radius = 24px (rounded-3xl)`
  Close to concentric with the round 36px controls in the 8px-padded toolbar (18 + 8 = 26px), so the + and send sit evenly inside the curve. A smaller radius leaves a visible gap at the corners.

## API

```ts

```

- `placeholder: string` — default `"Hi, what do you need today?"`
  Prompt placeholder.
- `status: ReactNode`
  Slot above the card, usually a `ComposerStatusTab`. Omit for the bare card.
- `models: ComposerModel[]` — default `COMPOSER_MODELS`
  Rows of the model menu: `{ id, name, description? }`.
- `defaultModel: string`
  Model id to start on. Defaults to the first model.
- `defaultPermission: ComposerPermission` — default `"auto"`
  Starting permission mode.

  Receives the trimmed text, attachments, model and permission. The panel clears itself after.
- `disabled: boolean` — default `false`
  Greys out send while a turn is in flight. Typing stays possible.
- `onVoice: () => void`
  Shows the mic button and is called when it is pressed.
- `voiceActive: boolean` — default `false`
  Pressed state of the mic button.
- `accept: string`
  Forwarded to the file input, e.g. "image/*,.pdf".
- `inputRef: RefObject<HTMLTextAreaElement | null>`
  Reaches the prompt field, e.g. to focus it.
- `context: number`
  `ComposerStatusTab`: context window used, 0-100, drawn as a 16px ring and a percentage.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Grow with the content a line at a time, then cap and scroll. Resetting to
// "auto" first lets the field shrink again when lines are deleted.
useLayoutEffect(() => {
  const el = fieldRef.current;
  if (!el) return;
  el.style.height = "auto";
  el.style.height = `${Math.min(el.scrollHeight, MAX_LINES * LINE_HEIGHT + FIELD_PADDING_Y)}px`;
}, [draft, fieldRef]);

const send = () => {
  if (!canSend || !model) return;
  onSubmit?.({ text: draft.trim(), attachments, model, permission });
  setDraft("");
  setAttachments([]);
  fieldRef.current?.focus();
};

// Enter sends; Shift+Enter falls through to the textarea's own newline.
// isComposing keeps an IME's confirming Enter from sending half a word.
const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement>) => {
  if (e.key !== "Enter" || e.shiftKey || e.nativeEvent.isComposing) return;
  e.preventDefault();
  send();
};
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is

`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Measuring `scrollHeight` without first setting `height: auto`. The field can then grow but never shrink back after text is deleted.
- Sending on every Enter. During IME composition (Japanese, Chinese, Korean) Enter confirms the candidate; check `isComposing` or the half-typed word is sent.
- Leaving the dropdowns uncontrolled. Kit `DropdownItem` is a plain button and does not close its popover; the panel closes each menu in `onSelect`.
- Painting a background over the disabled send button. `bg-button-primary` already has a disabled gradient; overriding it breaks dark mode. Only the icon colour changes.

## Notes

- Attachments live inside the panel and are handed to `onSubmit`, then cleared. Nothing is uploaded; only names and sizes are read from the picked files.
- The mic button appears only when `onVoice` is passed. The panel does no speech recognition; `voiceActive` only sets its pressed look.

# Build: Compound Group Hover Card

A content card that answers a hover with a short sequence rather than a single state flip: it lifts, its icon tilts and overshoots its scale, a corner blob brightens, and the affordance arrow slides in — each on its own duration and delay. The trigger is `:hover, :has(:focus-visible)`, so a keyboard user tabbing to the link inside gets exactly the same four changes.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

One hover drives four changes on three elements, each with its own duration and curve. Keyboard gets all four.

- Category: primitive
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The card owns `translate` and `border-color` on a 260ms `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`. It is the fastest change in the set because it is the one that acknowledges the pointer — anything slower and the card feels like it is deciding whether to respond.
2. The icon animates `rotate` over 320ms on the same ease and `scale` over 420ms on `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`, both delayed 40ms. Two curves on one element is only possible because `rotate` and `scale` are independent properties; packed into `transform` they would share a single duration and a single easing, and the overshoot would drag the rotation with it.
3. The corner blob is a radial gradient that is blurred once at paint time (`filter: blur(2rem)`) and thereafter only changes `opacity` 0.12 to 0.4 over 500ms and `scale` 1 to 1.15 over 700ms. It is the slowest element in the group, which is what makes it read as lighting rather than as a moving object.
4. `z-index: -1` on the blob places it above the card background and below the card content with no extra wrapper, and `isolation: isolate` on the card stops that negative index from escaping into the page stacking context and sliding behind an ancestor background.
5. The arrow translates 4px and goes from 0.4 to 1 opacity after an 80ms delay — last in the sequence, so the eye arrives at the call to action after the card has already committed to the hover.
6. The whole card is clickable through a stretched pseudo-element on the anchor (`::after { position: absolute; inset: 0 }`), so there is exactly one focusable, screen-reader-announced target. The card responds to that anchor's focus through `:has(:focus-visible)`, which is what gives keyboard parity without a single line of JavaScript.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `lift = -6px`
  Card travel on hover. Under 3px it is not distinguishable from a rendering shift; over about 10px the card visibly overlaps its neighbour in a tight grid and the shadow it does not have becomes conspicuous.
- `durations = 260 / 320 / 420 / 500 / 700 ms`
  Ascending by element weight: card, icon rotation, icon scale, blob opacity, blob scale. Equal durations collapse the sequence into a single snap; the spread is the entire effect. The 260ms floor is roughly the shortest a positional change can be and still be perceived as movement rather than a jump.
- `delays = 40ms icon, 80ms arrow`
  Small enough to feel like consequence rather than queueing. Past about 120ms the arrow reads as a second, separate event and a fast pointer pass leaves it half-animated.
- `icon scale = 1.1 with cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`
  The 1.56 control point overshoots to roughly 1.13 before settling. Overshoot on a small element reads as physical; on the card itself it would read as a bug, which is why only the icon gets it.
- `blob opacity range = 0.12 to 0.40`
  It must be visible at rest — a blob that appears only on hover reads as a new object arriving, not as a light coming up. 0.12 is enough to establish it; past about 0.5 the accent starts tinting the body copy.
- `icon rotation = -6deg`
  Anticlockwise, because the arrow moves right and the two would otherwise both push the same direction and read as a shear. Past about 10deg a glyph-based icon starts to look misaligned rather than tilted.

## API

```ts
function CompoundGroupHover(props: { title: string; description: string; eyebrow?: string; icon?: ReactNode; href?: string; accent?: string; action?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `title: string`
  Card heading, rendered as an `h3`.
- `description: string`
  Body copy under the heading.
- `eyebrow: string`
  Small uppercase label above the title.
- `icon: ReactNode`
  Rendered inside the tilting badge. An inline SVG or a single character.
- `href: string`
  Renders the affordance link and stretches it over the whole card.
- `accent: string` — default `'var(--color-accent, currentColor)'`
  Drives the blob, the icon border and the link colour.
- `action: string` — default `'Read more'`
  Text of the affordance link.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card via `cn`. Use it for sizing inside a grid.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const HOVER_CARD_CSS = `
.kx-hcard {
  --kx-hcard-ease: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1);
  --kx-hcard-overshoot: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);

  position: relative;
  isolation: isolate;
  overflow: hidden;
  display: flex;

/* Icon: two properties, two curves. The rotation settles cleanly; the scale
   overshoots slightly and comes back, which is what reads as "picked up". */

  align-items: center;

  description,

        {HOVER_CARD_CSS}
      </style>
      <article className={cn('kx-hcard p-6', className)} style={style}>
        <span className="kx-hcard-blob" aria-hidden="true" />

          <span className="kx-hcard-icon" aria-hidden="true">
            {icon}
          </span>
        ) : null}

        {eyebrow ? <span className="meta">{eyebrow}</span> : null}

        <h3 className="text-base tracking-tight text-fg">{title}</h3>
        <p className="text-[13px] leading-relaxed text-muted">{description}</p>

        {href ? (
          <a href={href} className="kx-hcard-link mt-auto pt-2 text-xs tracking-tight">
            {action}
            <span className="kx-hcard-arrow ml-1.5" aria-hidden="true">
              &rarr;
            </span>
          </a>
        ) : null}
      </article>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. No listeners, no timers, no animation frames; the hover state lives entirely in the cascade. React removes the hoisted `<style>` when the last card unmounts.

**Reduced motion.** A `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block cancels the three positional changes — the card no longer lifts, the icon no longer tilts or scales, the arrow no longer slides — while keeping every non-positional one. The border still brightens, the blob still comes up from 0.12 to 0.4 opacity, and the arrow still reaches full opacity, so hover and keyboard focus remain visibly acknowledged.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Packing the icon lift into `transform: rotate(-6deg) scale(1.1)`. It works, but both halves are now one property with one duration — the moment you want the scale to overshoot and the rotation not to, you have to split them, and splitting `transform` mid-project means rewriting every rule that touches it.
- Transitioning `filter: blur()` on the blob instead of `opacity`. Every frame re-runs a 2rem blur over a 14rem box; on a grid of six cards a single pointer sweep drops the page into the teens.
- Making the card itself a `<div role="link" tabindex="0">` to get a focus state. It is not announced as a link, it does not middle-click, it does not open in a new tab, and it needs a keydown handler. The stretched `::after` on a real anchor gives all of that for one pseudo-element.
- Using `:focus-within` instead of `:has(:focus-visible)`. `:focus-within` fires on mouse clicks too, so the card sticks in its hover state after every click and only releases when something else is focused.
- Omitting `isolation: isolate` on the card. The blob's `z-index: -1` then resolves against whichever ancestor last created a stacking context and the blob disappears behind a section background — intermittently, depending on what else is on the page.
- Leaving all four changes in place under reduced motion. Lift, tilt and slide are motion; the border, the blob and the arrow opacity are not. Disabling the whole hover state is over-correction and leaves the card with no feedback at all.
- Forgetting `overflow: hidden` on the card. The blob is positioned 4rem outside the card on two sides and paints over the neighbouring card in a grid.

## Notes

- `:has()` needs Safari 15.4+, Chrome 105+ and Firefox 121+. Where it is unsupported the pointer hover still works exactly as written and the keyboard path degrades to the browser's own focus ring on the link.
- Independent `translate` / `rotate` / `scale` need Chrome 104+, Safari 14.1+, Firefox 72+. In older engines the properties are dropped and the card still changes colour and opacity on hover.
- The accent is one custom property, `--kx-hcard-accent`, read by the blob, the icon and the link. A grid of these differs only by that value.

## Definition of done

Hover the card and four things change on four different timings — you can see the arrow arrive after the card has already lifted. Tab to the link with the keyboard and the identical four changes happen. Click the card anywhere, including on the description text, and the link activates. Turn reduced motion on: nothing moves, but the border, blob and arrow still respond.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Conic @property Border

A rounded box wearing an animated conic-gradient border. Two bright stops travel around the ring in opposite quadrants, so the ring reads as rotating rather than blinking. The whole thing is one element and one keyframe — the only moving part is a registered custom property holding an angle, which the browser interpolates for you.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A gradient ring that rotates around a rounded box. Two highlights chase each other; no JavaScript runs.

- Category: primitive
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. `@property --kx-conic-angle { syntax: "<angle>"; inherits: false; initial-value: 0deg }` registers the custom property so the browser knows its value is an angle. An unregistered custom property is an untyped token stream: a keyframe from `0deg` to `360deg` has no interpolation rule and the value flips at the 50% mark instead of sweeping.
2. A single keyframe block, `@keyframes kx-conic-spin { to { --kx-conic-angle: 360deg } }`, drives that property from its `initial-value` to a full turn over `--kx-conic-duration` with `linear` timing. Linear is required: any ease makes the highlights visibly hesitate once per revolution.
3. The element carries two backgrounds. `linear-gradient(fill, fill) padding-box` paints the interior flat; `conic-gradient(from var(--kx-conic-angle), …) border-box` paints under the border. With `border: 1.5px solid transparent`, the conic layer survives the clip only in the ring, which is how the gradient follows `border-radius` — `border-image` cannot round corners.
4. The gradient has six stops with the glow colour at 55deg and 305deg and the rest colour everywhere else. Two highlights roughly opposite each other read as rotation; a single highlight reads as a light blinking on and off once per cycle.
5. `inherits: false` on the registration stops descendants from picking up the animating value. With inheritance on, every element in the subtree re-resolves its computed style on every frame of the animation, which turns a one-element repaint into a whole-subtree style recalculation.
6. Every colour is read through `var(--name, fallback)`, so the component renders correctly with no props and can be re-themed by setting `--conic-glow` or `--conic-fill` on any ancestor.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `glow stop positions = 55deg and 305deg`
  Two highlights, not one, and not diametrically opposite. 250 degrees apart means one is entering the top edge as the other leaves the bottom, so there is always motion somewhere on the ring. At 180 degrees apart the pair reads as a symmetric pulse; with one stop it reads as a blinking dot.
- `durationMs = 4000`
  One revolution. Below ~2500 ms the ring reads as a loading spinner and demands attention; above ~7000 ms the highlight barely appears to move and the border looks like a static gradient someone got wrong.
- `thickness = 1.5px`
  Sub-pixel on a 1x display, which is what keeps it a hairline rather than a stripe. At 1px the highlight is too thin to read colour; at 3px or more the conic banding between stops becomes visible as facets.
- `rest colour alpha = currentColor at 10%`
  The dim majority of the ring. At 0% the border disappears between highlights and the box appears to lose its outline; above ~20% the contrast against the glow collapses and the rotation stops reading.
- `reduced-motion parked angle = 132deg`
  Puts one highlight past the top-left shoulder rather than exactly on an edge or a corner. At the `initial-value` of 0deg the highlight sits dead centre on the right edge, which looks like a rendering artefact rather than a decision.

## API

```ts
function ConicBorder(props: { children: ReactNode; durationMs?: number; thickness?: string; radius?: string; glow?: string; rest?: string; fill?: string; paused?: boolean; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Content rendered inside the ring. The element is `inline-flex`, centred.
- `durationMs: number` — default `4000`
  Milliseconds for one full revolution.
- `thickness: string` — default `'1.5px'`
  Ring thickness. Becomes the transparent border width.
- `radius: string` — default `'9999px'`
  Corner radius. The gradient follows it, unlike `border-image`.
- `glow: string`
  Colour of the two travelling highlights. Defaults to `currentColor`.
- `rest: string`
  Colour of the dim ring between highlights. Defaults to `currentColor` at 10%.
- `fill: string`
  Interior fill. Must be opaque or the gradient shows through the middle.
- `paused: boolean` — default `false`
  Sets `animation-play-state: paused`, freezing the ring at its current angle.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the ring element via `cn`. Use it for padding and typography.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/* Injected once per document. React 19 hoists `<style href precedence>` into
   <head> and de-duplicates by `href`, so a hundred rings ship one rule set —
   and `@property` registration is global anyway, so re-declaring it per
   instance would be pure waste. */
const CONIC_BORDER_CSS = `
@property --kx-conic-angle {
  syntax: "<angle>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0deg;
}

@keyframes kx-conic-spin {
  to { --kx-conic-angle: 360deg; }
}

.kx-conic {
  position: relative;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  isolation: isolate;

  border: var(--kx-conic-width, 1.5px) solid transparent;
  border-radius: var(--kx-conic-radius, 9999px);

  /* padding-box layer paints the interior, border-box layer paints under the
     ring. Order matters: the first background listed is the topmost. */
  background:
    linear-gradient(var(--kx-conic-fill), var(--kx-conic-fill)) padding-box,
    conic-gradient(
      from var(--kx-conic-angle),
      var(--kx-conic-rest)   0deg,
      var(--kx-conic-glow)  55deg,
      var(--kx-conic-rest) 130deg,
      var(--kx-conic-rest) 230deg,
      var(--kx-conic-glow) 305deg,
      var(--kx-conic-rest) 360deg
    ) border-box;

  animation: kx-conic-spin var(--kx-conic-duration, 4s) linear infinite;
}

.kx-conic[data-paused='true'] {
  animation-play-state: paused;
}

/* No motion: keep the ring, stop the revolution, and park a highlight
   off-axis so the border still reads as decorated rather than broken. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .kx-conic {
    animation: none;
    --kx-conic-angle: 132deg;
  }
}
`;

export function ConicBorder({
  children,
  durationMs = 4000,
  thickness = '1.5px',
  radius = '9999px',
  glow,
  rest,
  fill,
  paused = false,
  className,
}: ConicBorderProps) {
  /* Every colour resolves through a `var(..., fallback)` chain, so the
     component works with zero configuration and is themeable by setting one
     property on any ancestor. `Canvas` is the system background keyword — a
     last resort that is at least the right polarity in both colour schemes. */
  const style: StyleWithVars = {
    '--kx-conic-duration': `${durationMs}ms`,
    '--kx-conic-width': thickness,
    '--kx-conic-radius': radius,
    '--kx-conic-glow': glow ?? 'var(--conic-glow, currentColor)',
    '--kx-conic-rest':
      rest ?? 'var(--conic-rest, color-mix(in oklab, currentColor 10%, transparent))',
    '--kx-conic-fill': fill ?? 'var(--conic-fill, var(--color-bg, Canvas))',
  };

  return (
    <>
      <style href="kinetic-conic-property-border" precedence="medium">
        {CONIC_BORDER_CSS}
      </style>
      <div
        className={cn('kx-conic', className)}
        style={style}
        data-paused={paused ? 'true' : undefined}
      >
        {children}
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. There is no listener, no timer and no animation frame; unmounting the element removes the only thing that was running. The hoisted `<style>` is reference-counted by React and removed when the last instance unmounts.

**Reduced motion.** A `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block sets `animation: none` and pins `--kx-conic-angle` to 132deg. The gradient border stays — same colours, same thickness — it simply does not revolve. Nothing is removed from the layout and no size changes.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Animating the custom property without registering it with `@property`. The animation runs — `getComputedStyle` even reports it — but the gradient snaps from its start angle to its end angle at the halfway point, because an unregistered custom property interpolates as a discrete token stream. This is the single most common way this effect is reported "broken".
- Writing `border: 1.5px solid` with no colour, or omitting the border entirely. With no border there is no border-box area outside the padding box, the conic layer is fully covered by the fill layer, and the ring is invisible. The border must exist and must be transparent.
- Putting the fill layer second in the `background` list. Backgrounds paint first-listed on top; with the order reversed the flat fill is painted underneath and the conic gradient covers the entire box, not just the ring.
- Leaving `inherits` at its default of `true`. Descendants then inherit an animating value, so the browser recomputes styles for the whole subtree every frame. On a card with 40 children this shows up as a steady 3-5 ms of style recalculation per frame in a performance profile.
- Assuming the animation is compositor-driven and reaching for `will-change: transform`. It is not: animating a registered property repaints the element background on the main thread every frame. That is cheap on a button and expensive on a full-width hero — scale the element, not the hint.
- Using a semi-transparent interior fill. The conic layer extends under the whole border box, so anything less than opaque lets the gradient bleed through the middle of the card.

## Notes

- `@property` needs Safari 16.4+, Chrome 85+, Firefox 128+. Where it is unsupported the `@property` rule is dropped, the keyframe cannot animate the custom property, and `from var(--kx-conic-angle)` falls back to the guaranteed-invalid initial value — the conic gradient still paints from 0deg. The degradation is a static two-highlight ring, which is an acceptable border on its own.
- The CSS ships inside the component as a `<style href precedence>` element. React 19 hoists it into `<head>` and de-duplicates by `href`, so any number of instances contribute one rule set and one `@property` registration.
- The class name is prefixed `kx-` rather than scoped per instance on purpose: `@property` registration is document-global, so per-instance scoping would buy nothing and cost a style element per mount.

## Definition of done

Two bright arcs travel continuously around the border and pass the corners without pausing or jumping — in particular, nothing snaps at the halfway point of the cycle. The interior stays fully opaque. Set `paused` and the arcs freeze where they are. Enable reduced motion at the OS level and the ring is still coloured but completely still.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
