# Build: One Reveal Engine, Two Axes

Lines rise out of a clipping box and fade up as their group enters. The interesting part is that the same builder serves a vertical page section and a panel riding a pinned horizontal strip — handed the strip's tween as `containerAnimation`, ScrollTrigger measures against that timeline's progress instead of scroll position. One set of numbers, two directions, nothing to keep in sync by hand.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

The same staggered line reveal fires for vertical sections and for panels on a horizontal track.

- Category: scroll
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. The subtree is scanned for `[data-reveal-group]` elements; each becomes one ScrollTrigger. A subtree with no groups reveals as a single group rooted on the component itself.
2. Inside a group, every `[data-reveal]` element is a target of one `gsap.fromTo` running `{ yPercent: 110, opacity: 0.15 }` to `{ yPercent: 0, opacity: 1 }` on `power3.out` with a 0.12 s stagger — so the group is one tween, not one tween per line, and the stagger is real rather than simulated with delays.
3. When a `containerAnimation` is supplied it is spread into the trigger vars and the position keywords flip from `top 88% / top 45%` to `left 85% / left 45%`, because a trigger attached to a container animation measures along that container's axis.
4. The `containerAnimation` prop is tri-state: `undefined` means vertical flow, an animation means horizontal, and `null` means "a sibling owns the timeline and has not built it yet" — in which case nothing is built at all this commit.
5. `scrub: 0.4` ties the reveal to scroll position with a short catch-up, so reversing direction reverses the reveal instead of replaying it.
6. Everything is created inside a `gsap.context` scoped to the root, so `ctx.revert()` kills the triggers and restores the inline `transform` and `opacity` the tween wrote.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `lift = 110`
  Start offset as a percentage of the element's own height. 100 puts the line exactly at the bottom edge of its clipping box; 110 adds a sliver of overshoot so descenders are hidden through the whole travel rather than peeking under the mask on the first frame.
- `START_OPACITY = 0.15`
  Not 0. A line that fades from fully transparent reads as two separate events — a fade and a move. Starting at 0.15 makes the movement the thing you notice and the fade a supporting detail.
- `stagger = 0.12`
  Seconds between lines within a group. Below ~0.06 the lines read as one block; above ~0.2 the last line arrives after the eye has already moved on, which reads as lag rather than rhythm.
- `scrub = 0.4`
  Short catch-up so the reveal follows the scrollbar but survives a wheel step. At 0 the tween inherits every input spike; above ~1 the lines are still arriving after the section has left.
- `start / end (horizontal) = 'left 85%' / 'left 45%'`
  With `containerAnimation` the trigger is measured along the container's axis. Vertical keywords resolve to a position the element never occupies on that axis, so the tween simply never runs.

## API

```ts
function AxisReveals(props: { children: ReactNode; scroller?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; containerAnimation?: gsap.core.Animation | null; scrub?: number; lift?: number; stagger?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Markup containing `[data-reveal-group]` scopes and `[data-reveal]` targets.
- `scroller: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>`
  Scroll container the triggers read. Omit for the document.
- `containerAnimation: gsap.core.Animation | null`
  Omit for vertical flow, pass a horizontal tween to measure against it, pass `null` to hold off until that tween exists.
- `scrub: number` — default `0.4`
  Seconds of catch-up on the reveal.
- `lift: number` — default `110`
  Start offset as a percentage of the element height.
- `stagger: number` — default `0.12`
  Seconds between elements inside a group.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the wrapper. Use `contents` when the wrapper must not affect layout.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function AxisReveals({
  children,
  scroller,
  containerAnimation,
  scrub = 0.4,
  lift = 110,
  stagger = 0.12,
  className,
}: AxisRevealsProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  useEffect(() => {
    const rootEl = root.current;
    if (!rootEl || reduced) return;
    // Explicit "not ready": a sibling owns the timeline and has not built it.
    if (containerAnimation === null) return;

    const scrollerEl = scroller?.current ?? undefined;
    const horizontal = containerAnimation !== undefined;

    const ctx = gsap.context(() => {
      const groups = Array.from(rootEl.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-reveal-group]'));
      // A subtree with no explicit groups reveals as one group.
      const scopes = groups.length > 0 ? groups : [rootEl];

      for (const group of scopes) {
        const targets = Array.from(group.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-reveal]'));
        if (targets.length === 0) continue;

        gsap.fromTo(
          targets,
          { yPercent: lift, opacity: START_OPACITY },
          {
            yPercent: 0,
            opacity: 1,
            ease: 'power3.out',
            duration: 1,
            stagger,
            scrollTrigger: {
              trigger: group,
              scroller: scrollerEl,
              // The line everyone gets wrong. With `containerAnimation` the
              // trigger measures along the container's axis, so the position
              // keywords must be horizontal. "top 85%" against a horizontal
              // container resolves to a position the element never occupies,
              // and the reveal silently never fires.
              start: horizontal ? 'left 85%' : 'top 88%',
              end: horizontal ? 'left 45%' : 'top 45%',
              scrub,
              // Spreading rather than passing `undefined`: ScrollTrigger
              // branches on the key's presence, not on its value.
              ...(containerAnimation ? { containerAnimation } : {}),
            },
          },
        );
      }
    }, rootEl);

    return () => ctx.revert();
  }, [scroller, containerAnimation, scrub, lift, stagger, reduced]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `ctx.revert()` on unmount and on every dependency change: it kills each group's tween and ScrollTrigger and restores the inline `transform` and `opacity` GSAP wrote, so a re-mount measures clean markup rather than the last run's end state.

**Reduced motion.** No triggers are created and no `fromTo` runs, so every line renders at its final position and full opacity on first paint. The clipping boxes stay in the markup and do nothing, so the layout is byte-for-byte the finished state.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Keeping vertical keywords when passing `containerAnimation`. `start: "top 85%"` produces no error, no warning and no animation — the panels simply arrive already revealed, and the bug survives review because nothing is broken, only absent.
- Passing `containerAnimation: undefined` explicitly. ScrollTrigger branches on whether the key exists, so an `undefined` value is not the same as an absent key; the code spreads the object conditionally for exactly this reason.
- Treating a not-yet-built timeline as the vertical case. The strip's tween is created in a sibling effect and arrives one render later, so a naive `containerAnimation ?? undefined` builds a full set of vertical triggers on horizontal content and tears them down on the next commit — visible as a flash of pre-revealed panels.
- Writing a second reveal system for the horizontal section. Two systems mean two staggers, two easings and two sets of position keywords, and they diverge the first time someone tunes one of them.
- Building one tween per line instead of one tween per group. Stagger stops being a property of the group and becomes a pile of hand-computed delays, which no longer reverse correctly when the user scrolls back up.

## Notes

- Combine with `pinned-horizontal-track`: pass its `onTrack` payload's `animation` straight into `containerAnimation`.
- ScrollTrigger forbids `pin` on a trigger that has a `containerAnimation`. Pin the strip's section, never the panels riding it.

## Definition of done

Scroll the vertical section: the three lines rise out of their masks in sequence and reverse cleanly when you scroll back up. Keep scrolling into the pinned strip: each panel's lines rise with the same rhythm as it crosses the container, not as it crosses the viewport. With reduced motion on, every line is already in place.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Context Menu

The actions for whatever is under the pointer: a file, a row, a message, a spot on a canvas. It opens on right-click, on a 500ms touch long-press, and on Shift+F10 or the Menu key while the target has focus, with the menu's corner at the pointer. React Aria's Menu in a non-modal popover supplies arrows, typeahead, submenus, Escape and focus return; the component adds the pointer anchor and, like the browser's own menu, closes on any press or scroll outside it. The compact panel (14px radius, 32px rows, 20px icons) grows from the pointer with the menu family's 150ms fade, scale and blur.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Right-click, long-press and Shift+F10 menu anchored to the pointer, with icons, shortcuts, submenus and checkable rows.

- Category: overlay
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `ContextMenuTrigger` wraps its children in a `display: contents` div (so it adds no box) with `[-webkit-touch-callout:none]`, and listens for `contextmenu`, `keydown`, `pointerdown`, `pointermove`, `pointerup` and `pointercancel`. Children can be a function of `{ isOpen }` so the target can highlight while its menu is open.
2. Opening records the point and portals a 1px `pointer-events-none fixed` anchor div to `document.body` at `left: x, top: y`; `ContextMenu` positions an `AriaPopover` against it with `triggerRef={anchorRef}`, `placement="bottom start"`, `offset={2}` and `dir` from `useDirection()`, so the panel's corner sits at the pointer towards the reading direction and flips or shifts to stay on screen. `openCount` is bumped on every opening and used as the popover's `key`, so each menu mounts fresh at its own point.
3. Right-click calls `preventDefault` and opens at `clientX/clientY` with the menu itself focused (`autoFocus` true, as the browser does). Keyboard openings (Shift+F10, the `ContextMenu` key, or a `contextmenu` event at 0,0) use `openFrom(element)`: just inside the focused element's start edge, `min(24, width/2)` in and `min(height, 40)` down, with `autoFocus="first"` so the first item is focused. A touch `pointerdown` starts a 500ms timer that is cancelled if the finger drifts more than 10px or lifts.
4. The popover is `isNonModal`, so React Aria leaves it open on outside presses. While open, capture-phase `pointerdown` and `scroll` listeners on `document` close it unless the event target sits inside an element whose `data-context-menu` equals this trigger's `useId()` (the root panel and every submenu carry it). `contextmenu` events bubbling back through the portal are `preventDefault`ed so the browser menu never stacks on top; nested triggers: the innermost handles the event first and the outer sees `defaultPrevented`.
5. Panels share `PANEL`: `z-110 min-w-52 max-w-[calc(100vw-32px)] rounded-[14px] border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default shadow-dropdown`, `origin-(--trigger-anchor-point)`, `transition-[opacity,scale,filter] duration-150 ease-out`, `opacity-0` on `data-[entering]` / `data-[exiting]` and, under `motion-safe:`, `scale-95 blur-[2px]`. `MenuList` is an `AriaMenu` scroller (`gap-1 p-1 overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain`) with a `ScrollFade`.
6. `ContextMenuItem` is an `AriaMenuItem` using `MENU_ITEM` plus `px-2 py-1.5 text-body-medium`, highlighted with `MENU_ITEM_ACTIVE` while focused or while its submenu is open; it renders a 20px icon, the label, a check when selected, a `<kbd>` shortcut and a chevron (mirrored in RTL) when it has a submenu. `ContextMenuSubmenu` is an `AriaSubmenuTrigger` whose popover uses `offset={9}` and `crossOffset={-5}` and forwards the root's `onAction` and `close` through `RootMenuContext`, so submenu item ids reach the root handler.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `LONG_PRESS_MS = 500`
  How long a touch must rest before the menu opens: long enough not to fire on a tap or the start of a scroll, about what native long-press menus use.
- `LONG_PRESS_SLOP = 10 (px)`
  A resting finger still drifts a few pixels; more than 10px means the reader is scrolling or dragging, so the press is cancelled.
- `keyboard anchor = min(24, width/2) in from the start edge, min(height, 40) down`
  A keyboard opening has no pointer; this places the menu just inside the focused element so it visibly belongs to it, even on a small target.
- `submenu offset = offset 9, crossOffset -5`
  9px clears the parent's 4px padding and 1px border for a 4px gap; -5px lines the submenu's first row up with the row that opened it.
- `panel = rounded-[14px], p-1, min-w-52 (208px), 150ms scale 0.95 / blur 2px`
  The compact look of Multi-agent Chat's chat menu it was promoted from, with the shared menu motion so all anchored menus open alike.

## API

```ts
function ContextMenuTrigger(props: { children: ReactNode | ((state: { isOpen: boolean }) => ReactNode); isDisabled?: boolean; onOpenChange?: (isOpen: boolean) => void; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function ContextMenu<T extends object>(props: Omit<AriaMenuProps<T>, "className" | "autoFocus" | "onClose"> & { "aria-label"?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function ContextMenuItem(props: Omit<AriaMenuItemProps, "children" | "className"> & { icon?: IconComponent; shortcut?: string; variant?: "default" | "danger"; className?: string; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
function ContextMenuSubmenu(props: { label: ReactNode; icon?: IconComponent; textValue?: string; isDisabled?: boolean; className?: string; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
function ContextMenuSection(props: Omit<AriaMenuSectionProps<object>, "children" | "className"> & { title?: ReactNode; className?: string; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
function ContextMenuSeparator(props: { className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `ContextMenuTrigger.children: ReactNode | ((state: { isOpen: boolean }) => ReactNode)`
  The target, then its ContextMenu. The function form lets the target highlight while open.
- `ContextMenuTrigger.isDisabled: boolean` — default `false`
  Leave the browser's own menu in place.
- `ContextMenuTrigger.onOpenChange: (isOpen: boolean) => void`
  Called when the menu opens or closes.
- `ContextMenu.aria-label: string` — default `"Actions"`
  Names the menu for screen readers.
- `ContextMenu.onAction: (key: Key) => void`
  Runs with the chosen item's id, including items inside submenus.
- `ContextMenuItem.icon: IconComponent`
  Remix Icon component drawn at 20px before the label.
- `ContextMenuItem.shortcut: string`
  Keyboard hint at the end of the row, e.g. "⌘C".
- `ContextMenuItem.variant: "default" | "danger"` — default `"default"`
  Danger tints the row and its icon with the destructive text colour.
- `ContextMenuSection.selectionMode: "single" | "multiple"`
  Makes the section's rows checkable.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function ContextMenuTrigger({ children, isDisabled = false, onOpenChange, className }: ContextMenuTriggerProps) {
  const id = useId();
  const direction = useDirection();
  const anchorRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const openRef = useRef(false);
  const press = useRef<{ x: number; y: number; timer: number } | null>(null);
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
  const [point, setPoint] = useState<{ x: number; y: number } | null>(null);
  const [openCount, setOpenCount] = useState(0);
  const [autoFocus, setAutoFocus] = useState<"first" | true>(true);

  const setOpen = useCallback(
    (next: boolean) => {
      if (openRef.current === next) return;
      openRef.current = next;
      setIsOpen(next);
      onOpenChange?.(next);
    },
    [onOpenChange],
  );
  const close = useCallback(() => setOpen(false), [setOpen]);

  // A pointer opening focuses the menu itself, as the browser's menu does;
  // a keyboard opening lands on the first item.
  const openAt = (x: number, y: number, focus: "first" | true) => {
    setPoint({ x, y });
    setAutoFocus(focus);
    setOpenCount((count) => count + 1);
    setOpen(true);
  };

  /** Keyboard openings have no pointer: open just inside the focused element's start edge. */
  const openFrom = (element: Element) => {
    const rect = element.getBoundingClientRect();
    const inset = Math.min(24, rect.width / 2);
    openAt(direction === "rtl" ? rect.right - inset : rect.left + inset, rect.top + Math.min(rect.height, 40), "first");
  };

  const cancelPress = () => {
    if (!press.current) return;
    window.clearTimeout(press.current.timer);
    press.current = null;
  };

  useEffect(() => () => {
    if (press.current) window.clearTimeout(press.current.timer);
  }, []);

  // React Aria leaves non-modal popovers open on outside presses, and the
  // anchor is fixed, so close on a press or a scroll outside this menu tree.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isOpen) return;
    const onOutside = (event: Event) => {
      if (menuOf(event.target) !== id) close();
    };
    document.addEventListener("pointerdown", onOutside, true);
    document.addEventListener("scroll", onOutside, true);
    return () => {
      document.removeEventListener("pointerdown", onOutside, true);
      document.removeEventListener("scroll", onOutside, true);
    };
  }, [isOpen, id, close]);

  const onContextMenu = (event: MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    // Events from the open menu bubble here through its portal; never show
    // the browser's menu on top of it.
    if (menuOf(event.target) === id) {
      event.preventDefault();
      return;
    }
    if (isDisabled || event.defaultPrevented || !event.currentTarget.contains(event.target as Node)) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    if (openRef.current) return;
    // Some keyboard-made events carry no position.
    if (event.clientX === 0 && event.clientY === 0) openFrom(event.target as Element);
    else openAt(event.clientX, event.clientY, true);
  };

  const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (isDisabled || event.defaultPrevented || !event.currentTarget.contains(event.target as Node)) return;
    if (event.key !== "ContextMenu" && !(event.shiftKey && event.key === "F10")) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    openFrom(event.target as Element);
  };

  const onPointerDown = (event: ReactPointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (event.pointerType !== "touch" || isDisabled || !event.currentTarget.contains(event.target as Node)) return;
    cancelPress();
    const { clientX: x, clientY: y } = event;
    press.current = {
      x,
      y,
      timer: window.setTimeout(() => {
        press.current = null;
        if (!openRef.current) openAt(x, y, true);
      }, LONG_PRESS_MS),
    };
  };

  const onPointerMove = (event: ReactPointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (press.current && Math.hypot(event.clientX - press.current.x, event.clientY - press.current.y) > LONG_PRESS_SLOP) {
      cancelPress();
    }
  };

  const content = typeof children === "function" ? children({ isOpen }) : children;

  return (
    <TriggerContext.Provider value={{ id, isOpen, openCount, anchorRef, autoFocus, close }}>
      <div
        className={cx("contents [-webkit-touch-callout:none]", className)}
        data-open={isOpen || undefined}
        onContextMenu={onContextMenu}
        onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
        onPointerDown={onPointerDown}
        onPointerMove={onPointerMove}
        onPointerUp={cancelPress}
        onPointerCancel={cancelPress}
      >
        {content}
      </div>
      {point
        ? createPortal(
            <div
              ref={anchorRef}
              aria-hidden
              className="pointer-events-none fixed size-px"
              style={{ left: point.x, top: point.y }}
            />,
            document.body,
          )
        : null}
    </TriggerContext.Provider>
  );
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------- menu */

/** A menu's scrolling list, with the shared progressive top blur. */
function MenuList<T extends object>({ children, ...props }: Omit<AriaMenuProps<T>, "className">) {
  const fade = useScrollFade();
  return (
    <div className="relative flex min-h-0 flex-col">
      <AriaMenu
        {...props}
        onScroll={fade.onScroll}
        className="flex min-h-0 flex-col gap-1 overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain p-1 outline-none [scrollbar-width:thin]"
      >
        {children}
      </AriaMenu>
      <ScrollFade progress={fade.progress} />
    </div>
  );
}

export interface ContextMenuProps<T extends object> extends Omit<AriaMenuProps<T>, "className" | "autoFocus" | "onClose"> {
  /** Names the menu for screen readers. Default "Actions". */
  "aria-label"?: string;
  /** Classes on the panel, e.g. a width. */
  className?: string;
}

export function ContextMenu<T extends object>({
  "aria-label": ariaLabel = "Actions",
  onAction,
  className,
  ...props
}: ContextMenuProps<T>) {
  const trigger = useContext(TriggerContext);
  const direction = useDirection();
  const localize = useTemplateCopy();
  if (!trigger) throw new Error("ContextMenu must be inside a ContextMenuTrigger.");
  const { id, isOpen, openCount, anchorRef, autoFocus, close } = trigger;

  return (
    <RootMenuContext.Provider
      value={{ id, onAction: onAction as ((key: Key, value: object) => void) | undefined, close }}
    >
      <AriaPopover
        key={openCount}
        triggerRef={anchorRef}
        isOpen={isOpen}
        onOpenChange={(open) => {
          if (!open) close();
        }}
        isNonModal
        placement="bottom start"
        offset={2}
        dir={direction}
        data-context-menu={id}
        className={cx(PANEL, className)}
      >
        <MenuList {...props} aria-label={localize(ariaLabel)} autoFocus={autoFocus} onAction={onAction} onClose={close} />
      </AriaPopover>
    </RootMenuContext.Provider>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The document `pointerdown` and `scroll` capture listeners exist only while the menu is open and are removed by their effect cleanup. An unmount effect clears any pending long-press timer. The portalled anchor div unmounts with the trigger.

**Reduced motion.** The panel's scale and blur are behind `motion-safe:`, so under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the menu and its submenus only fade in and out over 150ms.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not anchor the popover to the target element. The menu belongs at the pointer; a 1px fixed anchor portalled to the body at the click point is what React Aria positions against.
- Do not reuse one popover instance across openings. Without the `key={openCount}` remount, a second right-click elsewhere animates from the old position.
- Do not rely on React Aria to close a non-modal popover on outside presses; it does not. Close on capture-phase `pointerdown` and `scroll` outside elements tagged with this menu's `data-context-menu` id, or submenus will count as "outside".
- Do not let `contextmenu` from inside the open menu reach the browser. Events from the portal bubble through React to the trigger, so they must be `preventDefault`ed or the native menu appears on top.
- Do not depend on the browser's `contextmenu` event for touch. Not every mobile browser fires it on a long-press, so the trigger runs its own 500ms timer on touch `pointerdown` and opens at the press point.

## Notes

- `isDisabled` on the trigger leaves the browser's own menu in place.
- A `ContextMenuSection` with `selectionMode` makes its rows checkable; selected rows show a check in the accent colour.
- The default `aria-label` is "Actions", passed through `useTemplateCopy()` so localized templates can translate it.

## Definition of done

Right-clicking anywhere on the file card opens the menu with its top-left corner at the pointer (no browser menu), the card highlights, and pressing outside or scrolling closes it. Hovering "Move to" opens a submenu aligned with that row; choosing "Archive" closes everything and the status reads "Moved to Archive". Tabbing to the card and pressing Shift+F10 opens the menu just inside the card with the first item focused; arrows, typeahead and Escape work. On touch, holding still for half a second opens it, while dragging cancels.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Context Usage Ring

A compact pill for a chat header or status bar that shows how much of the model's context window is in use. A 16px ring fills clockwise next to the percentage, and the pill moves from neutral to orange to rose as the window fills. Hovering or focusing it opens the kit tooltip with used and total tokens, a stacked bar, a per-source list and a "Free" row.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Small ring and percentage for how full a chat context window is. Turns orange, then rose, near the limit; a tooltip breaks the tokens down.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `ratio = clamp(used / limit, 0, 1)` and `pct = round(ratio * 100)`. `contextLevel(ratio, warnAt, dangerAt)` returns `"normal"`, `"warning"` (from 0.75) or `"danger"` (from 0.9), and the level picks the pill and arc classes from `LEVEL_STYLE`.
2. The ring is two SVG circles with `pathLength={100}`, rotated -90deg so it starts at 12 o'clock. The track uses the quaternary icon colour. The arc is `strokeDasharray="{pct} 100"`, so the dash length is the percentage with no circumference maths. It is hidden at 0% because a round cap on a zero-length dash still draws a dot.
3. Arc length and colour animate together with `transition-[stroke-dasharray,color] duration-300 ease-out`, and the pill background and text animate with `transition-colors`. A new token count slides the arc forward and crossing a threshold fades the colour.
4. The pill is a React Aria `Button` wrapped in the kit `TooltipTrigger`, so the tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus. The button's accessible name is "Context window N% used", and it carries `data-level` for styling and tests.
5. Inside the tooltip, each `breakdown` slice gets a width of `tokens / limit` in a flex bar on the track colour, so the empty tail of the bar is the free space. The list repeats the slices with a dot in the same tone and ends with a "Free" row of `limit - used`. Above the warning threshold a one-line note explains what happens next.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `warnAt / dangerAt = 0.75 / 0.9`
  Orange at three quarters leaves room for a couple of large file reads before the window is full. Rose at 90% is roughly the point where a long reply or one more file forces older turns out.
- `ring size = 16px, stroke 2px (2.5px above 16px)`
  Matches the 16px icons in a status bar. Thicker strokes at that size close up the centre, and thinner ones vanish at 0-10%.
- `tooltip width = 248px, capped at 100vw - 32px`
  Wide enough for a label, a token count and the warning note on two lines. The cap keeps it inside a 360px screen.

## API

```ts
function ContextUsageRing(props: { used: number; limit: number; breakdown?: ContextSlice[]; warnAt?: number; dangerAt?: number; hideLabel?: boolean; size?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
interface ContextSlice { label: string; tokens: number; tone?: "accent" | "blue" | "purple" | "orange" | "cyan" | "lime" | "rose" | "yellow" }
function contextLevel(ratio: number, warnAt?: number, dangerAt?: number): "normal" | "warning" | "danger"
function formatTokens(n: number): string
```

- `used: number`
  Tokens currently in the window.
- `limit: number`
  Window size in tokens.
- `breakdown: ContextSlice[]`
  What the used tokens are made of. Shown as a stacked bar and a list in the tooltip; zero slices are skipped.
- `warnAt: number` — default `0.75`
  Share of the window where the pill turns orange.
- `dangerAt: number` — default `0.9`
  Share of the window where the pill turns rose.
- `hideLabel: boolean` — default `false`
  Shows the ring alone. The accessible name still includes the percentage.
- `size: number` — default `16`
  Ring diameter in px.
- `className: string`
  Classes for the pill button.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
function Ring({ pct, size, arcClass }: { pct: number; size: number; arcClass: string }) {
  const stroke = size <= 16 ? 2 : 2.5;
  const r = (size - stroke) / 2;
  return (
    <svg aria-hidden width={size} height={size} viewBox={`0 0 ${size} ${size}`} className="shrink-0 -rotate-90">
      <circle cx={size / 2} cy={size / 2} r={r} fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth={stroke} className="text-foreground-icon-quaternary" />
      <circle
        cx={size / 2}
        cy={size / 2}
        r={r}
        fill="none"
        stroke="currentColor"
        strokeWidth={stroke}
        strokeLinecap="round"
        pathLength={100}
        // A round cap pokes past a zero-length dash, so an empty window draws nothing.
        strokeDasharray={pct > 0 ? `${pct} 100` : "0 100"}
        opacity={pct > 0 ? 1 : 0}
        className={cx(
          "transition-[stroke-dasharray,color] duration-300 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
          arcClass,
        )}
      />
    </svg>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers, listeners or observers. React Aria owns the hover, focus and tooltip state.

**Reduced motion.** The arc, its colour and the pill colours use `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so they jump straight to the new value. The tooltip follows the kit's own reduced-motion rule.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using `strokeDashoffset` with a computed circumference. `pathLength={100}` lets the dash array be the percentage directly and keeps working at any `size`.
- Drawing the arc at 0% with a round cap. A zero-length dash still renders as a dot, so the arc is hidden until there is at least 1%.
- Putting the tooltip on a plain `<div>`. The kit tooltip needs a focusable React Aria trigger, otherwise keyboard users never see the breakdown.

## Notes

- Slices without a `tone` take accent, purple, cyan, lime and yellow in turn. Orange and rose are left for the warning levels so a slice is never mistaken for the alert colour.
- `formatTokens` prints 812, 4.2k, 114k and 1.2M, and is exported for labels next to the ring.
- The demo is a session header with branch, project and the ring. Its buttons add tokens for a file, a tool run or a message, Compact keeps 20% of messages and drops tool output, and three cards show normal, warning and danger examples with `hideLabel`.

## Definition of done

At 35% the pill is neutral with a third of the ring filled. Adding tokens grows the arc; at 75% the pill turns orange and at 90% rose, each with a note in the tooltip. Hover or Tab onto the pill to see used/limit, a stacked bar, one row per source and a Free row. Compacting brings it back to neutral.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Context Window Card

A small usage tile that shows how much of a model's context window is taken and by what. Each category (messages, tools, memory, system prompt) is a coloured segment on a 4px track, and whatever is left of the track is the free space. A chevron next to the totals opens a legend with each category's tokens and share, and hovering a row or a segment dims the rest so the pair reads together.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

An agent's context window as one thin segmented bar by category, with a disclosable legend of token counts and shares.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Sum the segment tokens, clamped to `capacity`, as `used`; `free = capacity − used`; the header prints `formatTokens(used) / formatTokens(capacity) (pct%)` with the percentage in the semibold primary style.
2. Compute each segment's width as its share of the WHOLE window (`tokens / capacity × 100%`), walking a `remaining` budget so an over-full list never paints past the track. Draw them left to right in a `flex h-1 gap-px overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-chart-track` row, so the empty track on the right is the free space with no element of its own.
3. Give the bar `role="meter"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax=capacity`, `aria-valuenow=used` and an `aria-valuetext` like "820k of 1M tokens used (82%)". The segments themselves are decorative.
4. The header totals are a `<button aria-expanded aria-controls>` that toggles the legend (controlled `expanded` or uncontrolled `defaultExpanded`). The legend collapses with a `grid-rows-[0fr] → [1fr]` transition plus opacity, and is `inert` while closed so its rows leave the tab and reading order.
5. One `active` id is shared by the segments and the legend rows: `pointerenter` sets it, `pointerleave` clears it, and every other segment drops to 35% opacity (rows to 60%) while the active row gets the hover surface.
6. Segment widths transition over 500ms ease-out, so adding or compacting tokens visibly grows or shrinks the bar. `children` render below an `<hr>` divider, which is how plan limits share the same tile.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `bar height = h-1 (4px) with gap-px between segments`
  Matches the hairline bar on BoardUI's Agent limits tile. The 1px gap is what keeps seven adjacent colours readable as separate categories without outlines.
- `width transition = 500ms ease-out`
  Long enough to read a compaction as the bar draining, short enough that a fast run of turns does not lag behind the totals in the header.
- `dim opacity = segments 35%, legend rows 60%`
  The thin bar needs a stronger drop than the text rows for the highlighted segment to pop; rows keep 60% so their numbers stay legible.
- `compact format = ≥1M → one decimal M (trailing .0 dropped), ≥1k → rounded k`
  Gives "820k / 1M" exactly as on the tile; decimals in k would make the header jitter on every turn.

## API

```ts
function ContextWindowCard(props: { segments: ContextSegment[]; capacity: number; label?: ReactNode; freeLabel?: string; expanded?: boolean; defaultExpanded?: boolean; onExpandedChange?: (expanded: boolean) => void; formatTokens?: (tokens: number) => string; children?: ReactNode; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type ContextSegment = { id: string; label: string; tokens: number; color?: "blue" | "purple" | "pink" | "yellow" | "green" | "sky" | "teal" | "indigo" | "lime" }
function formatTokensCompact(tokens: number): string
```

- `segments: ContextSegment[]`
  Category usage drawn left to right: id, label, tokens and a palette colour.
- `capacity: number`
  Window size in tokens. Segment widths are shares of this, the rest is free track.
- `label: ReactNode` — default `"Context window"`
  Header label; also the meter's accessible name when it is a string.
- `freeLabel: string` — default `"Free space"`
  Legend label for the unused remainder.
- `expanded: boolean`
  Controlled legend state.
- `defaultExpanded: boolean` — default `false`
  Uncontrolled legend state on mount.
- `onExpandedChange: (expanded: boolean) => void`
  Called when the header toggle is pressed.
- `formatTokens: (tokens: number) => string` — default `formatTokensCompact`
  Formats every count in the header and legend.
- `children: ReactNode`
  Rows rendered under a divider in the same tile (plan limits, actions).
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card surface.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function ContextWindowCard({
  segments,
  capacity,
  label = "Context window",
  freeLabel = "Free space",
  expanded,
  defaultExpanded = false,
  onExpandedChange,
  formatTokens = formatTokensCompact,
  children,
  className,
}: ContextWindowCardProps) {
  const legendId = useId();
  const [uncontrolledOpen, setUncontrolledOpen] = useState(defaultExpanded);
  const open = expanded ?? uncontrolledOpen;
  const [active, setActive] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const setOpen = (next: boolean) => {
    setUncontrolledOpen(next);
    onExpandedChange?.(next);
  };

  // Clamp so an over-full window never paints past the track.
  const used = Math.min(
    capacity,
    segments.reduce((sum, s) => sum + Math.max(0, s.tokens), 0),
  );
  const free = Math.max(0, capacity - used);
  const usedPct = Math.round(percentOf(used, capacity));

  // Each segment's width is its share of the WHOLE window, so the empty
  // track to the right is the free space with no extra element.
  let remaining = capacity;
  const widths = segments.map((s) => {
    const tokens = Math.min(Math.max(0, s.tokens), remaining);
    remaining -= tokens;
    return percentOf(tokens, capacity);
  });

  return (
    <section
      className={cx(
        "flex w-full min-w-0 flex-col gap-3 rounded-[14px] bg-background-secondary-default p-3.5",
        className,
      )}
    >
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-3">
        <h3 className="text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary">{label}</h3>
        <button
          type="button"
          aria-expanded={open}
          aria-controls={legendId}
          onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}
          className="-me-1 inline-flex cursor-pointer items-center gap-1 rounded-md px-1 py-0.5 text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary tabular-nums outline-none transition-colors duration-150 ease-out hover:bg-background-secondary-hover hover:text-text-primary focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring"
        >
          <span>
            {formatTokens(used)} / {formatTokens(capacity)}{" "}
            <span className="text-caption-1-semibold text-text-primary">({usedPct}%)</span>
          </span>
          <span className="sr-only">{open ? "Hide breakdown" : "Show breakdown"}</span>
          <ChevronDownSmall
            aria-hidden
            className={cx(
              "size-3.5 shrink-0 transition-transform duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
              open && "rotate-180",
            )}
          />
        </button>
      </div>

      <div
        role="meter"
        aria-label={typeof label === "string" ? label : "Context window"}
        aria-valuemin={0}
        aria-valuemax={capacity}
        aria-valuenow={used}
        aria-valuetext={`${formatTokens(used)} of ${formatTokens(capacity)} tokens used (${usedPct}%)`}
        className="flex h-1 w-full gap-px overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-chart-track"
      >
        {segments.map((s, i) => (
          <span
            key={s.id}
            onPointerEnter={() => setActive(s.id)}
            onPointerLeave={() => setActive(null)}
            className={cx(
              "h-full shrink-0 first:rounded-s-full",
              "transition-[width,opacity] duration-500 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
              swatch[s.color ?? DEFAULT_SEGMENT_COLOR],
              active !== null && active !== s.id && "opacity-35",
            )}
            style={{ width: `${widths[i] ?? 0}%` }}
          />
        ))}
      </div>

      <div
        id={legendId}
        className={cx(
          "grid transition-[grid-template-rows,opacity,margin] duration-300 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
          // Closed, the -mt-3 cancels the flex gap so the empty row adds no space.
          open ? "grid-rows-[1fr] opacity-100" : "-mt-3 grid-rows-[0fr] opacity-0",
        )}
        inert={!open}
      >
        <ul className="min-h-0 overflow-hidden">
          {segments.map((s, i) => (
            <li
              key={s.id}
              onPointerEnter={() => setActive(s.id)}
              onPointerLeave={() => setActive(null)}
              className={cx(
                "flex items-center gap-2 rounded-md px-1 py-1 text-caption-1-medium transition-[background-color,opacity] duration-150 ease-out",
                active === s.id && "bg-background-secondary-hover",
                active !== null && active !== s.id && "opacity-60",
              )}
            >
              <span aria-hidden className={cx("size-2 shrink-0 rounded-[3px]", swatch[s.color ?? DEFAULT_SEGMENT_COLOR])} />
              <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-text-primary">{s.label}</span>
              <span className="shrink-0 text-text-secondary tabular-nums">{formatTokens(s.tokens)}</span>
              <span className="w-10 shrink-0 text-end text-text-tertiary tabular-nums">
                {(widths[i] ?? 0).toFixed(1)}%
              </span>
            </li>
          ))}
          <li className="flex items-center gap-2 px-1 py-1 text-caption-1-medium">
            <span aria-hidden className="size-2 shrink-0 rounded-[3px] bg-chart-track ring-1 ring-border-button-default ring-inset" />
            <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-text-secondary">{freeLabel}</span>
            <span className="shrink-0 text-text-secondary tabular-nums">{formatTokens(free)}</span>
            <span className="w-10 shrink-0 text-end text-text-tertiary tabular-nums">
              {percentOf(free, capacity).toFixed(1)}%
            </span>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </div>

      {children != null && children !== false ? (
        <>
          <hr className="border-border-table" />
          {children}
        </>
      ) : null}
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up: two pieces of React state, pointer handlers on rendered elements, and CSS transitions that end on their own.

**Reduced motion.** Segment width, legend open/close and chevron rotation transitions carry `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so the bar and legend jump straight to their new state. Hover dimming still applies because it carries meaning, not motion.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Sizing segments as a share of `used` instead of `capacity`. The bar then always looks full and the free space disappears.
- Rendering a separate "free" segment. The track already is the free space, and an extra element breaks the 1px gap rhythm at the end.
- Hiding the collapsed legend with `height: 0` alone. Its rows stay focusable and announced; `inert` on the wrapper is what removes them.
- Animating `flex-grow` instead of `width`. Grow values are relative to each other, so one segment changing reflows all the others in the same frame.

## Notes

- `formatTokensCompact` is exported so surrounding UI (a composer badge, a toast) can print counts the same way.
- Colours come from the kit chart palette (`bg-chart-1…9`) plus `bg-accent-500` for the leading blue, so both themes are handled by the token sheet.

## Definition of done

The header reads "820k / 1M (82%)" for the demo data and the bar fills 82% of its track in seven colours with 1px gaps. Pressing the header toggle flips aria-expanded and shows or hides the legend; when hidden, Tab skips its rows. Hovering "System tools" in the legend dims every other segment. "Add a turn" grows the blue segment and the totals; "Compact" shrinks it back with an eased width change.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Contributions Card

A grey dashboard card with a yearly total, a change chip and four stat tiles above a contributions calendar: one rounded cell per day, seven weekday rows by up to 53 week columns, coloured in five intensity steps of an accent family. Weekly, Monthly and Yearly tabs regroup the same counts into days, weeks of each month or whole months across years, at the same grid height. Hovering a cell or moving to it with the arrow keys rings it and shows a tooltip with the count and the date. Everything is a CSS grid of spans, with no chart library and no Date objects.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A GitHub-style contributions card: a week by weekday calendar in five intensity steps, stat tiles, month labels and nine accent palettes.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Counts are plain arrays, one number per day of the year. Calendar positions come from integer arithmetic: Sakamoto's formula gives the weekday of Jan 1, a month-length table gives each day its month and date, and a day at index i sits in row `(offset + i) % 7` and column `floor((offset + i) / 7)`. Without `Date` there is no time zone, so the server and the client always agree.
2. The view picks a matrix of cells. Weekly is 7 rows by `ceil((offset + days) / 7)` weeks, with `null` placeholders before Jan 1 and after Dec 31. Monthly sums days 1–7, 8–14, 15–21, 22–28 and 29–31 of each month into 5 rows by 12 columns. Yearly sums each month into one row per year.
3. A cell's tier is 0 for no activity, else `ceil((count / peak) ** 0.7 * 5)` clamped to 1–5, where peak is the busiest cell in the current view. The 0.7 power lifts the many quiet days off tier 1 so a single spike does not wash the year out. The cell carries it as `data-tier`, and the theme's `.contributions-grid[data-accent]` rules map tiers 0–5 to the neutral chart colour and the 200, 400, 500, 600 and 700 shades of the accent (950 to 500 in dark mode). Swapping `accent` recolours the whole grid with one attribute.
4. A ResizeObserver measures the grid. The weekly view keeps the most recent weeks that fit at 8px per cell plus a 3px gap, so a phone shows about half a year and a 640px grid shows all 53 weeks. Rows are as tall as the weekly cells are wide, clamped to 8–14px, and every view shares that seven-row height so switching tabs never resizes the card.
5. Month labels sit in an extra grid row with `grid-column-start` set to the week the month begins in. In the weekly view a label is dropped when the next month starts less than 3 columns later.
6. Cells pop in with `.animate-cell-pop`, delayed by `min(k * 9 + r * 12, 520)` ms so the sweep runs left to right. The grid is keyed by the view, so each tab switch replays it.
7. The grid is one tab stop (`role="group"`). Arrow keys move the active cell and skip placeholders, Home and End jump to the first and last day, and Escape, blur or leaving with the pointer clears it. The active cell gets a 2px outline and `z-10`, and holds a tooltip with the count and a label such as "Wed, Jan 1, 2025". A polite live line under the grid repeats it for screen readers.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `MIN_CELL / GAP = 8px / 3px`
  The smallest cell that still reads as a square with a visible gap. At this pitch a typical 640px card fits all 53 weeks.
- `tiers = 0 + 5 steps, ceil((count / peak)^0.7 × 5)`
  Empty days stay neutral grey, and any activity at all lands in at least tier 1, so a single contribution is never invisible.
- `ROW_HEIGHT = 8–14px`
  Weekly rows track the cell width so cells stay square; the clamp stops a wide card from growing a tall calendar.
- `label spacing = ≥ 3 weeks`
  A month that starts within two columns of the next would print its label on top of the neighbour, as happens when a year starts on a Saturday.

## API

```ts

type ContributionAccent = "emerald" | "green" | "teal" | "cyan" | "blue" | "indigo" | "violet" | "rose" | "amber"
type ContributionView = "weekly" | "monthly" | "yearly"

```

  Header label.
- `years: ContributionYear[]` — default `CONTRIBUTION_YEARS`
  Daily counts per year, oldest first. The last year is the one on show; the Yearly view lists them all.
- `accent: ContributionAccent` — default `"violet"`
  Accent family for tiers 1–5.
- `change: number` — default `change against the previous year`
  Percent for the chip.
- `stats: ContributionStat[] | false` — default `derived tiles`
  Tiles under the header, or false to hide them.

  Controlled granularity.

  Uncontrolled starting granularity.

  Called when a tab is picked.
- `unit: [string, string]` — default `["contribution", "contributions"]`
  Singular and plural noun for the tooltip.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

```tsx
const summary = useMemo(() => {
  const total = current.counts.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  const previous = years[years.length - 2];
  const prevTotal = previous ? previous.counts.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) : 0;
  let best = 0;
  let bestAt = 0;
  let streak = 0;
  let longest = 0;
  current.counts.forEach((n, i) => {
    if (n > best) [best, bestAt] = [n, i];
    streak = n > 0 ? streak + 1 : 0;
    longest = Math.max(longest, streak);
  });
  const { m, d } = monthDay(current.year, bestAt);
  const derived: ContributionStat[] = [
    { label: "Active days", value: String(current.counts.filter((n) => n > 0).length) },
    { label: `Best day · ${MONTHS[m]} ${d}`, value: String(best) },
    { label: "Longest streak", value: `${longest} days` },
    { label: "Daily average", value: numberFormat.format(total / Math.max(1, current.counts.length)) },
  ];
  return { total, change: prevTotal > 0 ? Math.round(((total - prevTotal) / prevTotal) * 1000) / 10 : undefined, derived };
}, [current, years]);

const matrix = useMemo(
  () => (view === "weekly" ? weeklyMatrix(current) : view === "monthly" ? monthlyMatrix(current) : yearlyMatrix(years)),
  [view, current, years],
);

// Weekly view keeps the most recent weeks that fit at MIN_CELL; the other views always fit.
const allCols = matrix.rows[0]?.length ?? 0;
const weeks = Math.ceil((weekday(current.year, 1, 1) + (isLeap(current.year) ? 366 : 365)) / 7);
const weekCols = width > 0 ? Math.max(1, Math.min(weeks, Math.floor((width + GAP) / (MIN_CELL + GAP)))) : weeks;
const cols = view === "weekly" ? weekCols : allCols;
const first = allCols - cols;
// Every view shares the height of seven square weekly rows, so switching never resizes the card.
const weekCell = width > 0 ? (width - (weekCols - 1) * GAP) / weekCols : 11;
const weekRow = Math.max(ROW_HEIGHT[0], Math.min(ROW_HEIGHT[1], weekCell));
const gridHeight = 7 * weekRow + 6 * GAP;
const rowHeight = (gridHeight - (matrix.rows.length - 1) * GAP) / matrix.rows.length;

const peak = Math.max(1, ...matrix.rows.flat().map((cell) => cell?.count ?? 0));
const tierOf = (count: number) => (count <= 0 ? 0 : Math.min(5, Math.max(1, Math.ceil((count / peak) ** 0.7 * 5))));
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `useResizeObserver` disconnects its observer on unmount. Everything else is CSS and React event props, so nothing else needs tearing down.

**Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the cells appear at once (`motion-reduce:animate-none` on `.animate-cell-pop`, which the theme also disables), and the tab colour change is instant.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Building the calendar with `new Date(year, month, day)`. Local time zones and DST shift days across the server and the client and cause hydration mismatches; integer weekday arithmetic is exact everywhere.
- Scaling tiers by the year's peak in every view. A month total is about thirty times a day, so each view needs its own peak or the Monthly view goes solid dark.
- Leaving the hovered cell at the default stacking order. The pop animation gives every cell its own stacking context, so later cells paint over the tooltip unless the active cell gets `z-10`.

## Notes

- `CONTRIBUTION_YEARS` (2023–2025, seeded with `createRng`) and the `ContributionYear`, `ContributionAccent`, `ContributionView` and `ContributionStat` types are exported.
- Pass `stats` to replace the derived tiles (Active days, Best day, Longest streak, Daily average), or `stats={false}` to hide them.
- The accent families come from the theme: emerald, green, teal, cyan, blue, indigo, violet, rose and amber.

# Build: Converging Flow Steps

A process diagram that assembles itself as you scroll. The two outer cards converge toward the middle from opposite ends while the connectors between them pop in at 35% through the timeline — after the cards are already moving. That ordering is the entire effect: connectors that arrive first read as "boxes with arrows", connectors that arrive during the movement read as "these things connect".

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A process diagram that closes from both ends while the connectors pop in a third of the way through.

- Category: scroll
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. One `gsap.timeline` on a `scrollTrigger` with `start: "top 92%"`, `end: "center 52%"` and `scrub: 1.2` — deliberately the slowest scrub in the set, because a diagram should settle rather than track the wheel.
2. The first and last cards get `fromTo` tweens at position 0 with `±14` on the layout axis, so they close toward the centre from opposite ends. Cards in between have nowhere to converge from and only fade; giving them a direction too makes the row look shuffled rather than closing.
3. The connectors get `fromTo({ autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.6 }, { autoAlpha: 1, scale: 1, stagger: 0.2 })` placed at absolute timeline position `0.35`. The card tweens run 0 → 1, so 0.35 is a third of the way into their travel.
4. The convergence axis is chosen from the measured container width, not the viewport: under `stackBelow` px the row becomes a column and the tweens switch from `xPercent` to `yPercent`. A stacked column with horizontal convergence has cards sliding past each other sideways.
5. The single-step case is handled explicitly — `first === last` would otherwise mean two `fromTo` tweens fighting over one element, one pulling it from -14 and one from +14.
6. `ease: "none"` throughout. Under a scrub the ease applies to timeline time, so easing here desynchronises the two converging cards from each other.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `scrub = 1.2`
  Over a second of catch-up — very slow. Right for a diagram, which you want to see settle; wrong for a hero, which would feel unresponsive. Below ~0.6 the diagram snaps together as fast as you scroll and the assembly reads as a jump.
- `connectorAt = 0.35`
  Absolute timeline position, in seconds, where the connectors start. The cards run 0 → 1, so this is a third of the way into their travel. At 0 the arrows are present before there is anything to connect; past ~0.6 they arrive after everything has stopped and read as an afterthought.
- `converge = 14`
  Percent of the card's own size. Small on purpose: this is a settling gesture, not an entrance. Past ~25% the outer cards start visibly outside the tinted wrapper and the diagram looks broken at the start of the scrub.
- `CONNECTOR_SCALE = 0.6`
  Starting scale for the pop. Below ~0.4 the arrow is a dot for the first half of its tween; above ~0.8 there is no pop left to see.
- `connectorStagger = 0.2`
  Seconds between connectors. Long enough that a three-step flow reads left to right rather than all at once, which is what tells the reader the diagram has a direction.
- `stackBelow = 420`
  Container width in px below which three cards in a row are too narrow to hold a title and a line of body. Measured from the element, not the window, because this component is usually inside a column that is narrow while the window is wide.

## API

```ts
function ConvergingFlowSteps(props: { steps: { title: string; body?: string; kicker?: string }[]; converge?: number; scrub?: number; connectorAt?: number; connectorStagger?: number; stackBelow?: number; start?: string; end?: string; scrollerRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `steps: { title: string; body?: string; kicker?: string }[]`
  Ordered steps. Connectors are inserted between consecutive pairs.
- `converge: number` — default `14`
  Outer-card travel as a percentage of its own size, along the layout axis.
- `scrub: number` — default `1.2`
  Seconds of catch-up behind the scroll position.
- `connectorAt: number` — default `0.35`
  Timeline position, in seconds, at which the connectors begin.
- `connectorStagger: number` — default `0.2`
  Seconds between connectors.
- `stackBelow: number` — default `420`
  Container width in px below which the row becomes a column and the axis flips.
- `start: string` — default `'top 92%'`
  ScrollTrigger start.
- `end: string` — default `'center 52%'`
  ScrollTrigger end.
- `scrollerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>`
  The scroll container that owns the scroll position. Omit for the document.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the wrapper via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const CONNECTOR_SCALE = 0.6;

export function ConvergingFlowSteps({
  steps,
  converge = 14,
  scrub = 1.2,
  connectorAt = 0.35,
  connectorStagger = 0.2,
  stackBelow = 420,
  start = 'top 92%',
  end = 'center 52%',
  scrollerRef,
  className,
}: ConvergingFlowStepsProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const { width } = useResizeObserver(root);

  // The convergence axis has to follow the layout axis, or a stacked column
  // gets cards sliding in sideways past each other. Measured from the element
  // rather than the viewport: this component is often inside a panel that is
  // narrow while the window is wide.
  const stacked = width > 0 && width < stackBelow;

  useGsap(
    gsap,
    () => {
      const container = root.current;
      if (!container || reduced) return;

      const cards = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-flow-card]'));
      const connectors = Array.from(
        container.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-flow-connector]'),
      );
      const first = cards[0];
      const last = cards[cards.length - 1];
      if (!first || !last) return;

      const axis = stacked ? 'yPercent' : 'xPercent';
      const tl = gsap.timeline({
        scrollTrigger: {
          trigger: container,
          scroller: scrollerRef?.current ?? undefined,
          start,
          end,
          scrub,
          invalidateOnRefresh: true,
        },
      });

      // Outer cards travel toward the centre from opposite ends. When there is
      // only one card, `first === last` and the two tweens would fight over
      // the same target, so it takes the middle treatment instead.
      if (first === last) {
        tl.fromTo(first, { autoAlpha: 0 }, { autoAlpha: 1, ease: 'none', duration: 1 }, 0);
      } else {
        tl.fromTo(
          first,
          { autoAlpha: 0, [axis]: -converge },
          { autoAlpha: 1, [axis]: 0, ease: 'none', duration: 1 },
          0,
        );
        tl.fromTo(
          last,
          { autoAlpha: 0, [axis]: converge },
          { autoAlpha: 1, [axis]: 0, ease: 'none', duration: 1 },
          0,
        );
      }

      // Everything between the ends has nowhere to converge from, so it only
      // fades. Giving it a direction too would make the row look like it was
      // being shuffled rather than closing.
      const middle = cards.slice(1, -1);
      if (middle.length > 0) {
        tl.fromTo(middle, { autoAlpha: 0 }, { autoAlpha: 1, ease: 'none', duration: 1 }, 0);
      }

      if (connectors.length > 0) {
        tl.fromTo(
          connectors,
          { autoAlpha: 0, scale: CONNECTOR_SCALE },
          {
            autoAlpha: 1,
            scale: 1,
            ease: 'none',
            duration: 1 - connectorAt,
            stagger: connectorStagger,
          },
          // Absolute timeline position in seconds. The cards occupy 0 -> 1, so
          // 0.35 puts the first connector a third of the way into their
          // travel: they are already moving when the link appears.
          connectorAt,
        );
      }
    },
    root,
    [converge, scrub, connectorAt, connectorStagger, start, end, stacked, reduced, steps.length],
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `useGsap` reverts the `gsap.context` on unmount and whenever the layout axis or any timing prop changes. That kills the ScrollTrigger and strips the inline transform and opacity from every card and connector, which matters here because the axis flip rebuilds the whole timeline on resize and a stale trigger would keep writing `xPercent` to elements now laid out in a column.

**Reduced motion.** No timeline is built, so the diagram renders assembled: cards at their layout positions, connectors at full opacity and scale. The layout still responds to container width, because that is layout rather than motion.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Animating the connectors at position 0 alongside the cards. Everything arriving together reads as a set of boxes that happen to have arrows between them; the whole point is that the link appears while the boxes are still closing.
- Giving the middle cards a convergence direction too. With every card sliding, the row reads as being reshuffled rather than closing, and the two outer cards stop being the subject.
- Not handling the one-step case. `cards[0]` and `cards[cards.length - 1]` are the same element, so it receives two `fromTo` tweens with opposite start values and ends up wherever the second one decided.
- Choosing the layout axis from `window.innerWidth`. The component is usually inside a content column; a wide window with a narrow column stacks the cards visually while the tweens still converge horizontally, so they cross each other on the way in.
- Using `opacity` rather than `autoAlpha` on the connectors. An invisible SVG still takes hit-testing area between two cards, which quietly swallows clicks aimed at the card edges.
- Assuming `stagger` inside a scrubbed timeline behaves like duration. Each connector's start is offset in timeline seconds, so a large stagger pushes the timeline total past the card tweens and the cards finish before the scroll range ends — which is intended here, but is a surprise if you assumed the total was 1.

## Notes

- The wrapper tint is derived from the accent token rather than a second hard-coded colour, so re-theming the accent moves the panel with it.
- Connectors are inline SVG paths, so they inherit `currentColor` and need no asset.

## Definition of done

Scroll the diagram into view: the leftmost and rightmost cards slide toward the middle, and only once they are moving do the arrows between them scale up one after the other. Stop scrolling mid-way and the diagram keeps settling for more than a second. Narrow the container below 420px and the same sequence plays vertically with the arrows rotated. With reduced motion on, the diagram is complete before it scrolls into view.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Converging Headline Words

A stacked headline assembles out of the margins as you approach it. Odd lines enter from the right, even lines from the left, and both land on zero at the same scrub position, so they cross the frame in opposite directions and lock into a sentence. Because the tween is scrubbed, scrolling back up disassembles it — the headline is a function of scroll position, not a playback that has happened or not happened.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Headline words slide in from opposite margins and lock into a sentence, pinned to scroll position.

- Category: text
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. Each word is a block-level span with `data-word`. A single `gsap.timeline` with a `scrollTrigger` holds one `fromTo` per word, all inserted at position `0`, so every word shares the timeline's full length and therefore the full scroll range.
2. The travel is `xPercent`, not `x`: percent of *the element's own width*, so a short word and a long word both start entirely outside the frame and neither needs a hand-tuned pixel value.
3. Direction alternates on index parity — `i % 2 === 0 ? -travel : travel` — and the text alignment alternates with it, so each word enters from the side it is aligned to and travels the shortest distance to its resting place.
4. `ease: "none"` on every tween. Under `scrub` the scroll position *is* the easing curve; layering `power2.out` on top means the words accelerate away from the scrollbar and then wait for it, which is precisely the sensation people describe as the scroll feeling sticky.
5. `fromTo`, not `to`. A bare `to` reads its start value from the DOM, and the DOM already says `xPercent: 0` because the rendered markup is the assembled headline — that is what the no-JS and reduced-motion renders show.
6. `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger)` is called inside the effect rather than at module scope, because `registerPlugin` touches `window` and this module is still evaluated during server rendering.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `TRAVEL = 120`
  Percent of each word's own width. At exactly 100 the word starts flush against the frame edge and is already peeking in on the first pixel of scroll; the extra 20% buys a moment of empty margin before it arrives.
- `SCRUB = 1`
  One second of catch-up between the scrollbar and the words. `scrub: true` welds them exactly, which on a trackpad exposes every jitter in the input; past ~1.5s the headline is still assembling well after the reader has stopped scrolling.
- `START = 'top bottom'`
  The scrub begins the instant the headline's top edge enters the viewport. Starting later means the words are still outside the frame when the headline is already half on screen, which reads as missing content rather than as an entrance.
- `END = 'top 25%'`
  Assembly completes when the headline top reaches the upper quarter of the viewport. Ending at centre leaves the headline unresolved while it is the dominant thing on screen; ending earlier compresses the whole effect into the bottom sliver of the viewport.

## API

```ts
function ConvergingScrubWords(props: { words: string[]; travel?: number; scrub?: number; start?: string; end?: string; scroller?: Element | null; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `words: string[]`
  One per line. Even indices enter from the left, odd from the right.
- `travel: number` — default `120`
  Percent of each word's own width that it starts offset by.
- `scrub: number` — default `1`
  Seconds of catch-up between the scrollbar and the words.
- `start: string` — default `'top bottom'`
  ScrollTrigger `start`.
- `end: string` — default `'top 25%'`
  ScrollTrigger `end`.
- `scroller: Element | null` — default `null`
  Scroll container, when the headline is not in the document scroller.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the wrapper via `cn` — type size and tracking go here.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const TRAVEL = 120;
const SCRUB = 1;
const START = 'top bottom';
const END = 'top 25%';

export function ConvergingScrubWords({
  words,
  travel = TRAVEL,
  scrub = SCRUB,
  start = START,
  end = END,
  scroller = null,
  className,
}: ConvergingScrubWordsProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  /* The words by content, not by array identity. A caller writes
     `words={['Between', 'Signals']}` inline, which is a new array on every
     parent render — and this component's parent re-renders often, because the
     preview host's `useInView` sets state on every IntersectionObserver entry
     and there are five thresholds. With the array itself in the dep list below,
     a single scroll past the card tore the timeline and its ScrollTrigger down
     and rebuilt them up to five times, each rebuild forcing a layout-reading
     `refresh()` and visibly resetting the scrub mid-gesture. The effect never
     reads `words` anyway — it works off the rendered `[data-word]` nodes — so
     content is the only thing that should re-run it. */
  // Joined on an escaped NUL rather than a space: ['a b'] and ['a', 'b']
  // render a different number of nodes and must not share a key.
  const wordsKey = words.join('\u0000');

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = root.current;
    // Reduced motion: the JSX below already renders the assembled headline at
    // its final position, so declining to attach the trigger is the whole
    // implementation. Nothing is hidden and nothing is left off-screen.
    if (!el || reduced) return;

    // Registered here rather than at module scope: registerPlugin touches
    // window, and this file is still evaluated during server rendering.
    gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger);

    const wordEls = Array.from(el.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-word]'));
    if (wordEls.length === 0) return;

    const ctx = gsap.context(() => {
      const tl = gsap.timeline({
        scrollTrigger: {
          trigger: el,
          scroller: scroller ?? undefined,
          start,
          end,
          scrub,
        },
      });

      wordEls.forEach((w, i) => {
        // fromTo, not to. A bare `to` would read the start value off the DOM,
        // and the DOM already says 0 because the inline style below is the
        // final position for the no-JS and reduced-motion renders.
        tl.fromTo(
          w,
          { xPercent: i % 2 === 0 ? -travel : travel },
          { xPercent: 0, ease: 'none' },
          0,
        );
      });
    }, el);

    return () => ctx.revert();
    // `wordsKey` stands in for `words`, which the effect never reads.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [wordsKey, travel, scrub, start, end, scroller, reduced]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `ctx.revert()` on the `gsap.context` scoped to the root. That kills the timeline, disposes the ScrollTrigger instance (so it stops measuring a detached element and stops contributing to `ScrollTrigger.refresh()`), and strips the inline transforms GSAP wrote.

**Reduced motion.** No ScrollTrigger is attached and no tween is created. The markup React renders is already the assembled headline at `xPercent: 0`, so the finished sentence is on screen from first paint — nothing is off-screen waiting for a scroll that will not drive it.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using an ease other than `none` under `scrub`. The words lead or lag the scrollbar and the page feels like it is fighting the input — the single most common complaint about scrubbed animation.
- Using `to` instead of `fromTo`. GSAP samples the current DOM value as the start, which is the resting position, so nothing moves — or worse, it moves only after a resize invalidates the cached start.
- Animating `x` in pixels. A word that is 400px wide and one that is 120px wide need different offsets to clear the frame; `xPercent` is self-scaling and survives a font-size change.
- Setting `overflow: hidden` on the container. It stops the horizontal scrollbar, but CSS forces `overflow-y` to `auto` when one axis is `hidden`, which silently breaks any sticky ancestor and clips descenders. `overflow-x: clip` does the same job without that side effect.
- Omitting the `scroller` option when the headline lives inside a scrolling panel rather than the document. ScrollTrigger measures against the window, so the trigger fires at the wrong time or never.
- Registering ScrollTrigger at module scope. `registerPlugin` reaches for `window` and throws during server rendering.
- Cleaning up with `kill()` on the timeline only. The ScrollTrigger instance survives and keeps measuring a detached element; `ctx.revert()` disposes both and strips the inline transforms.

## Notes

- No text-splitting library: the words arrive as an array prop and are rendered as spans by React. A splitter would add a dependency and a DOM-mutation lifecycle for something the caller already has as data.
- If you feed this component text you split elsewhere, gate the split on `document.fonts.ready` — measuring before the webfont lands gives fallback-font line breaks that never re-flow. See `font-safe-text-split`.
- The `scroller` prop exists so the component can be demoed and used inside an `overflow-y-auto` panel rather than only in the document scroller.

## Definition of done

Scroll down slowly: the words travel inward from alternating sides and are exactly aligned when the headline top reaches the upper quarter of the viewport. Scroll back up and they separate again, tracking the scrollbar. No horizontal scrollbar appears on the document at any point. With reduced motion enabled the assembled headline is present on first paint and does not move.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
