# Build: Cylinder Gallery Drum

A flat PlaneGeometry per item, all sharing one compiled program, each bent around a common cylinder by its own uniform. The camera never moves and the CPU never touches a vertex: scrolling changes one float, `position`, and every plane recomputes its angle, its height and its focus weight from that single scalar. Because the ring offset is the shortest signed distance on a circular index, the list is genuinely endless in both directions with no clones and no rebuilding.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Nineteen planes wrapped around a drum in the vertex shader, spun by wheel or scroll, focus falling off from centre.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1, gsap@^3.15.0, lenis@^1.3.11

## How it works

1. The vertex shader treats a vertex's own x as an arc offset: `angle = uSpiralAngle + position.x`, then `pos.x = uRadius * sin(angle)` and `pos.z = uRadius * cos(angle)`, so one world unit of plane width wraps exactly one radian of drum. `pos.y = sin(position.y)` pulls the top and bottom edges in, which turns a rolled sheet into a barrel.
2. Per frame and per plane, `wrappedOffset(i, position, count)` returns the shortest signed distance from that plane to the focused index — the value that makes index 0 sit one step before index 18 rather than eighteen steps after it. That offset drives `uSpiralAngle = (offset / count) * 2π * turns`, the vertical stack `y = -offset * spacing`, and the focus term.
3. Focus is `gaussian(offset)` = `exp(-offset²)`: 1.0 at the centre, 0.368 one step out, 0.018 two, 0.0001 three. The fragment shader mixes toward luminance and dims by that weight, so attention falls off continuously instead of one plane being flagged "selected".
4. A single `uIntro` scalar lerps between two complete layouts inside the shader — `mix(rowPos, ringPos, uIntro)` — where `rowPos` is a flat facing row and `ringPos` is the drum. Every intermediate value is a valid frame, and the CPU lerps the mesh x/y positions with the same scalar so the two layouts stay consistent.
5. Signed scroll velocity feeds `uDeform`, which adds `sin(position.y * 3.0 + 100.0) * uDeform * 0.07` to z and `sin(position.x * 3.0) * uDeform * 0.04` to y. It samples `position` — the original flat coordinates — not the already-bent `pos`, so the ripple is locked to the picture and reads as the image flexing rather than the drum wobbling.
6. Pointer proximity is measured inside the vertex shader by projecting each vertex once as a probe (`ndc = probe.xy / probe.w`), taking `exp(-mouseDist² * 5.0)`, lifting z by half of it and passing it to the fragment shader, which pushes the centred UV outward by the same weight so the bump also magnifies — a lens, not a bump.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `PLANE_WIDTH / PLANE_HEIGHT = 1 / 1.95`
  Width 1 because the bend uses the vertex's raw x as radians — at width 1 each plane spans exactly 1 rad of the drum, which is the whole reason no trigonometry is needed on the CPU. Height must stay under 2π/3 or `sin(position.y)` leaves its monotonic range and the barrel folds its own edges back through the surface.
- `CAMERA_FOV / CAMERA_Z = 45 / 5`
  The camera never animates, so these only set how much drum is in shot. Below ~35° the ring flattens into a row and the depth cue vanishes; above ~60° the near plane balloons and the barrel curve reads as a keystone error.
- `OVERSCAN = 1.12`
  The cover-fit UV is divided by this, zooming the crop in 12%. At exactly 1.0 the wave and the bulge push vertices past the sampled region and the texture's own clamped border smears along the edge. Beyond ~1.25 the crop eats the subject.
- `segments = 64`
  The bend is evaluated per vertex, so subdivision *is* the curve. Below ~24 the drum visibly becomes a folded card and the mouse bulge turns into a triangular tent; past ~128 you are paying vertex cost for a curve the pixel grid cannot resolve.
- `POSITION_SMOOTHING = 0.0006`
  Fraction of remaining distance left after one second. Larger (slower) and the drum lags visibly behind the wheel; much smaller and the velocity spike that drives `uDeform` never has time to build, so the wave disappears.
- `SNAP_DELAY_MS = 170`
  Idle time before the drum eases to a whole index. Under ~120 ms it fires between the discrete events of a single trackpad flick and fights the gesture; over ~250 ms the gallery feels like it forgot to settle.
- `MAX_DEFORM / DEFORM_PER_INDEX = 1.5 / 0.42`
  Deform is clamped to ±1.5 because the shader multiplies it by 0.07 world units — past that the planes intersect each other and the far side of the drum pokes through the near side. 0.42 sets how many index-steps per second count as full deflection.
- `RADIUS_VELOCITY_GAIN = 0.5`
  The drum widens up to 50% at full speed, which is what sells inertia. Above ~0.8 the nearest plane crosses the camera's near plane during a fast flick and clips away.
- `gaussian falloff = 1 (exp(-offset²))`
  A falloff of 1 keeps the immediate neighbours legible at 0.37 while the third plane out is effectively gone. Raising it dims the neighbours to black and the ring loses its context; lowering it flattens every plane to the same weight.
- `renderOrder scale = -worldZ * 1000`
  Reconstructed drum depth, scaled up so it survives rounding to an integer sort key. At a smaller scale adjacent planes collapse into the same bucket and flicker between frames.

## API

```ts
function CylinderGallery(props: { items: CylinderGalleryItem[]; drive?: "pointer" | "page"; radius?: number; turns?: number; spacing?: number; segments?: number; pixelsPerIndex?: number; opacity?: number; paint?: (ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, item: CylinderGalleryItem, index: number, size: { width: number; height: number }) => void; onSelect?: (item: CylinderGalleryItem, index: number) => void; onFocusChange?: (item: CylinderGalleryItem, index: number) => void; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `items: CylinderGalleryItem[]`
  `{ id, title, meta?, hue? }` per plane. One mesh and one generated texture each.
- `drive: "pointer" | "page"` — default `"pointer"`
  Wheel and drag inside the component, or document scroll via a shared infinite Lenis.
- `radius: number` — default `2`
  Drum radius in world units, before the velocity widening.
- `turns: number` — default `3`
  Full revolutions the ring spans across the whole list.
- `spacing: number` — default `0.8`
  World units of vertical travel per index step.
- `segments: number` — default `64`
  Plane subdivisions per axis. This is the resolution of the bend.
- `pixelsPerIndex: number` — default `240`
  Document scroll pixels per index step, in `page` mode only.
- `opacity: number` — default `1`
  Global alpha multiplier applied before the focus falloff.
- `paint: (ctx, item, index, size) => void`
  Override the generated plate. Receives a 2D context for a 512x1024 canvas.
- `onSelect: (item, index) => void`
  Tap on the drum. A drag never counts as a tap.
- `onFocusChange: (item, index) => void`
  Fires when a different index takes the centre.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the wrapper via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function CylinderGallery({
  items,
  drive = 'pointer',
  radius = 2,
  turns = 3,
  spacing = 0.8,
  segments = 64,
  pixelsPerIndex = 240,
  opacity = 1,
  paint,
  onSelect,
  onFocusChange,
  className,
}: CylinderGalleryProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const { inView } = useInView(host, { threshold: 0 });
  const visible = useVisibility();
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const pointer = useSmoothPointer({ target: host, smoothing: 0.0015 });

  // `hasWebGL` touches `document`, so it cannot run during render without
  // disagreeing with the server. Start optimistic and correct after mount:
  // both renders then agree and nothing hydrates twice.
  const [supported, setSupported] = useState(true);
  useEffect(() => setSupported(hasWebGL()), []);

  const [focused, setFocused] = useState(0);

  const position = useRef(0);
  const target = useRef(0);
  const velocity = useRef(0);
  const intro = useRef(0);
  const strength = useRef(0);
  const hovered = useRef(false);
  const focusedRef = useRef(0);
  const snapTimer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
  const snapTween = useRef<Tween | null>(null);

  // Everything the frame loop reads but must not resubscribe on. Written on
  // every render, read once per frame; the loop itself never re-creates.
  const live = useRef({ radius, turns, spacing, opacity, drive, pixelsPerIndex, items, onSelect, onFocusChange });
  live.current = { radius, turns, spacing, opacity, drive, pixelsPerIndex, items, onSelect, onFocusChange };

  // Rebuilding the scene is expensive, so it is keyed on what actually changes
  // the meshes — identity, label and hue — not on the array's reference, which
  // is new on every render for any caller who writes the list inline.
  const itemsKey = items.map((item) => `${item.id}:${item.title}:${item.hue ?? ''}`).join('|');

  const lenis = useLenis({ infinite: true, enabled: drive === 'page' });

  const killSnap = useCallback(() => {
    if (snapTimer.current !== null) {
      clearTimeout(snapTimer.current);
      snapTimer.current = null;
    }
    snapTween.current?.kill();
    snapTween.current = null;
  }, []);

  const scheduleSnap = useCallback(() => {
    if (snapTimer.current !== null) clearTimeout(snapTimer.current);
    snapTimer.current = setTimeout(() => {
      snapTimer.current = null;
      // Snap the TARGET, not the position: the frame loop keeps damping
      // toward it, so the settle stays one continuous motion instead of a
      // second animation fighting the first.
      snapTween.current = gsap.to(target, {
        current: Math.round(target.current),
        duration: SNAP_DURATION,
        ease: 'power3.out',
      });
    }, SNAP_DELAY_MS);
  }, []);

  /* ---- scene construction ------------------------------------------------ */

  const ready = width > 1 && height > 1 && supported;

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready || items.length === 0) return;

    let renderer: THREE.WebGLRenderer;
    try {
      renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true, alpha: true });
    } catch {
      // A context can still be refused between the probe and the construction —
      // the tab may have hit the browser's live-context ceiling in between. three
      // throws rather than returning null, and an uncaught throw here takes the
      // page with it.
      setSupported(false);
      return;
    }
    // Capped, not raw. A 3x phone with an uncapped ratio pays 9x the fill rate
    // for a difference nobody can see.
    renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio());
    renderer.setSize(el.clientWidth, el.clientHeight, false);
    renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 0);
    renderer.domElement.style.display = 'block';
    renderer.domElement.style.width = '100%';
    renderer.domElement.style.height = '100%';
    el.appendChild(renderer.domElement);

    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(
      CAMERA_FOV,
      el.clientWidth / Math.max(el.clientHeight, 1),
      0.1,
      100,
    );
    camera.position.z = CAMERA_Z;

    // One geometry for every plane. The bend is per-vertex, so the mesh has to
    // be dense enough that the curve reads as a curve: below ~24 segments the
    // drum visibly becomes a folded card.
    const geometry = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(PLANE_WIDTH, PLANE_HEIGHT, segments, segments);
    const planeAspect = PLANE_WIDTH / PLANE_HEIGHT;
    const paintItem = paint ?? paintPlate;
    const maxAnisotropy = Math.min(4, renderer.capabilities.getMaxAnisotropy());

    const planes: Plane[] = items.map((item, index) => {
      const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
      canvas.width = TEXTURE_WIDTH;
      canvas.height = TEXTURE_HEIGHT;
      const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
      if (ctx) paintItem(ctx, item, index, { width: TEXTURE_WIDTH, height: TEXTURE_HEIGHT });

      const texture = new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas);
      // sRGB in, sRGB out. Skip this and the plates render noticeably darker
      // than the CSS colours sitting next to them.
      texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
      texture.anisotropy = maxAnisotropy;
      texture.needsUpdate = true;

      const uniforms: PlaneUniforms = {
        uTexture: { value: texture },
        uTextureAspect: { value: TEXTURE_WIDTH / TEXTURE_HEIGHT },
        uPlaneAspect: { value: planeAspect },
        uOverscan: { value: OVERSCAN },
        uSpiralAngle: { value: 0 },
        uRadius: { value: radius },
        uIntro: { value: 0 },
        uFocus: { value: 1 },
        uOpacity: { value: opacity },
        uDeform: { value: 0 },
        uMouseNdc: { value: new THREE.Vector2(0, 0) },
        uMouseStrength: { value: 0 },
      };

      // A material per mesh, because every plane needs its own spiralAngle,
      // radius and focus. three keys its program cache on the shader source,
      // so all of these share one compiled program regardless.
      const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
        vertexShader: cylinderGalleryVertexShader,
        fragmentShader: cylinderGalleryFragmentShader,
        uniforms,
        transparent: true,
        side: THREE.DoubleSide,
        // Painted strictly back to front via renderOrder below, so neither
        // depth write nor depth test has anything to contribute — and both
        // would be wrong anyway, since the depth they compare is the depth of
        // a mesh the CPU thinks is still flat at the origin.
        depthWrite: false,
        depthTest: false,
      });

      const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
      // The CPU-side geometry is a flat plane at mesh.position; the shape you
      // can actually see is somewhere else entirely. Frustum culling compares
      // against that stale bounding sphere and blanks planes that are plainly
      // on screen.
      mesh.frustumCulled = false;
      scene.add(mesh);
      return { mesh, uniforms, texture };
    });

    stage.current = { renderer, scene, camera, geometry, planes };
    renderer.render(scene, camera);

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      for (const plane of planes) {
        scene.remove(plane.mesh);
        // disposeObject walks a material's own properties looking for
        // textures. These live inside `uniforms`, two levels down, so it will
        // never find them — they have to be released by hand.
        plane.texture.dispose();
      }
      disposeObject(scene);
      geometry.dispose();
      // dispose() frees GPU objects and leaves the context alive. Only
      // forceContextLoss, which disposeRenderer calls, hands it back.
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      renderer.domElement.remove();
    };
    // `items` is read through the key; `radius`/`opacity` only seed uniforms
    // the frame loop overwrites immediately.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [ready, itemsKey, segments, paint]);

  /* ---- size ------------------------------------------------------------- */

  useEffect(() => {
    const current = stage.current;
    if (!current || width < 1 || height < 1) return;
    current.renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio());
    // `false` — the canvas is sized by CSS at 100%/100%; letting three write
    // inline pixel dimensions makes it fight the flex parent on every resize.
    current.renderer.setSize(width, height, false);
    current.camera.aspect = width / height;
    current.camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
  }, [width, height]);

  /* ---- intro morph ------------------------------------------------------- */

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!ready) return;
    if (reduced) {
      intro.current = 1;
      return;
    }
    intro.current = 0;
    const tween = gsap.to(intro, {
      current: 1,
      duration: INTRO_DURATION,
      delay: INTRO_DELAY,
      ease: 'power3.inOut',
    });
    return () => {
      tween.kill();
    };
  }, [ready, reduced]);

  /* ---- input ------------------------------------------------------------- */

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || drive !== 'pointer') return;

    const onWheel = (event: WheelEvent) => {
      // Non-passive on purpose: without preventDefault the drum spins AND the
      // page scrolls under it, which reads as two competing gestures.
      event.preventDefault();
      killSnap();
      target.current += event.deltaY * WHEEL_INDEX_PER_PIXEL;
      scheduleSnap();
    };

    el.addEventListener('wheel', onWheel, { passive: false });
    return () => el.removeEventListener('wheel', onWheel);
  }, [drive, killSnap, scheduleSnap]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el) return;
    const enter = () => {
      hovered.current = true;
    };
    const leave = () => {
      hovered.current = false;
    };
    el.addEventListener('pointerenter', enter);
    el.addEventListener('pointerleave', leave);
    return () => {
      el.removeEventListener('pointerenter', enter);
      el.removeEventListener('pointerleave', leave);
    };
  }, []);

  useDrag(host, {
    enabled: drive === 'pointer',
    onDragStart: killSnap,
    onDrag: (state) => {
      target.current -= state.deltaY * DRAG_INDEX_PER_PIXEL;
    },
    onDragEnd: (_state, moved) => {
      if (!moved) {
        const { items: list, onSelect: select } = live.current;
        const index = wrapIndex(Math.round(position.current), list.length);
        const item = list[index];
        if (item) select?.(item, index);
      }
      scheduleSnap();
    },
  });

  useEffect(() => killSnap, [killSnap]);

  /* ---- the frame --------------------------------------------------------- */

  useRaf(
    (dt) => {
      const current = stage.current;
      if (!current) return;
      const {
        radius: baseRadius,
        turns: baseTurns,
        spacing: baseSpacing,
        opacity: alpha,
        drive: mode,
        pixelsPerIndex: perIndex,
        items: list,
        onFocusChange: notify,
      } = live.current;

      const count = current.planes.length;
      if (count === 0) return;

      if (mode === 'page') {
        const instance = lenis.current;
        if (instance) target.current = instance.scroll / Math.max(perIndex, 1);
      }

      const previous = position.current;
      position.current = damp(position.current, target.current, POSITION_SMOOTHING, dt);

      // Index steps per second, smoothed by the same damp that produced the
      // position, so the wave can never lead the geometry it is bending.
      const instant = dt > 0 ? (position.current - previous) / dt : 0;
      velocity.current = damp(velocity.current, instant, 0.002, dt);
      const normalized = clamp(velocity.current / VELOCITY_REFERENCE, -1, 1);

      strength.current = damp(
        strength.current,
        hovered.current && !reduced ? 1 : 0,
        STRENGTH_SMOOTHING,
        dt,
      );

      const s = intro.current;
      const speed = Math.abs(normalized);
      const liveRadius = baseRadius * (1 + RADIUS_VELOCITY_GAIN * speed);
      const liveSpacing = baseSpacing * (1 + SPACING_VELOCITY_GAIN * speed);
      const angularScale = 1 + ANGULAR_VELOCITY_GAIN * speed;
      const deform = reduced
        ? 0
        : clamp(velocity.current * DEFORM_PER_INDEX, -MAX_DEFORM, MAX_DEFORM);

      // The flat-row layout spans the frustum's visible WIDTH at z = 0. Sizing
      // it from window.innerWidth, or from the visible height, leaves the row
      // short on wide viewports and clipped on narrow ones.
      const visibleWidth =
        2 * Math.tan((CAMERA_FOV * Math.PI) / 360) * CAMERA_Z * current.camera.aspect * 0.86;
      const step = visibleWidth / Math.max(count - 1, 1);
      const rowWidth = (count - 1) * step;

      const mx = pointer.current.active ? pointer.current.ndcX : 0;
      const my = pointer.current.active ? pointer.current.ndcY : 0;

      for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const plane = current.planes[i];
        if (!plane) continue;

        // The one call that makes a finite array behave like an infinite ring:
        // item 0 is one step BEFORE item 18, not eighteen steps after it.
        const offset = wrappedOffset(i, position.current, count);
        const angle = (offset / count) * Math.PI * 2 * baseTurns * angularScale;
        const y = -offset * liveSpacing;

        plane.mesh.position.x = (i * step - rowWidth / 2) * (1 - s);
        plane.mesh.position.y = y * s;
        plane.mesh.scale.setScalar(lerp(0.62, 1, s));

        const u = plane.uniforms;
        u.uSpiralAngle.value = angle;
        u.uRadius.value = liveRadius;
        u.uIntro.value = s;
        u.uDeform.value = deform;
        u.uOpacity.value = alpha;
        u.uMouseStrength.value = strength.current;
        u.uMouseNdc.value.set(mx, my);
        // exp(-d²): 1.000 at the centre, 0.368 one step out, 0.018 two, 0.0001
        // three. Continuous, branchless, and the reason the drum reads as
        // analogue rather than as a list with a selected row.
        u.uFocus.value = lerp(1, gaussian(offset), s);

        // Transparent meshes are sorted by three using the CPU position, which
        // for this drum is (0, y, 0) for every plane. Reconstructing the depth
        // the shader will actually produce and painting back to front is the
        // only way the far side of the ring stays behind the near side.
        const worldZ = liveRadius * Math.cos(angle) * s;
        plane.mesh.renderOrder = Math.round(-worldZ * 1000);
      }

      const nextFocus = wrapIndex(Math.round(position.current), count);
      if (nextFocus !== focusedRef.current) {
        focusedRef.current = nextFocus;
        setFocused(nextFocus);
        const item = list[nextFocus];
        if (item) notify?.(item, nextFocus);
      }

      current.renderer.render(current.scene, current.camera);
    },
    ready && inView && visible,
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes the wheel and pointerenter/pointerleave listeners, kills the intro tween and any pending snap timeout plus its tween, removes every mesh from the scene, disposes each `CanvasTexture` by hand (they sit inside `material.uniforms`, where `disposeObject` cannot reach), runs `disposeObject` for the geometries and materials, disposes the shared geometry, then `disposeRenderer` — `setAnimationLoop(null)`, `dispose()`, `forceContextLoss()` — and removes the canvas from the DOM. The frame loop reads a stage ref that is nulled first, so a queued frame after teardown is a no-op rather than a null context throw.

**Reduced motion.** The intro morph is skipped — `uIntro` is set to 1 on mount, so the drum is simply already assembled. The velocity wave is pinned to 0 and the pointer bulge never engages, so the surface stays flat. Navigation still works and still eases: wheel, drag and the snap-to-index tween are unchanged, because the user asked for less motion, not for a gallery that cannot move.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Scaling `uRadius` from 0 to animate the intro. At radius 0 every vertex of every plane lands on the origin, so the "flat" state is nineteen invisible slivers stacked in one spot. Lerp between two position vectors — `mix(rowPos, ringPos, uIntro)` — and the flat state is a real layout you can hold.
- Leaving `frustumCulled` at its default. The CPU-side geometry is still a flat plane sitting at `mesh.position`; the visible shape is somewhere else entirely. three culls against that stale bounding sphere and planes that are plainly on screen blink out at the edges.
- Trusting three's transparency sort. It orders transparent meshes by their object position, which for this drum is `(0, y, 0)` for every single plane, so the far side of the ring paints over the near side at random. Reconstruct the depth the shader will produce (`radius * cos(angle) * intro`) and set `renderOrder` from it each frame.
- Expecting `disposeObject` to free the plate textures. It scans a material's own properties for anything with `isTexture`; these textures live two levels down inside `material.uniforms`, so it never sees them and nineteen 512x1024 canvases stay resident on the GPU after unmount. They are disposed explicitly from a tracked list.
- Calling `renderer.dispose()` and stopping there. That releases GPU objects but keeps the WebGL context alive; Chromium caps a renderer process at roughly 16 and silently kills the oldest, so a docs page that mounts several of these blanks the ones above it. `disposeRenderer` calls `forceContextLoss`.
- Attaching the wheel listener passively. Without `preventDefault` the drum spins and the host page scrolls at the same time, which reads as two gestures fighting; the listener is registered with `{ passive: false }`.
- Sampling the deformation wave from the already-bent `pos` instead of the original `position`. The ripple then travels with the drum rotation rather than staying pinned to the image, and the effect looks like a rendering fault instead of the picture flexing.
- Sizing the flat-row layout from `window.innerWidth`. The row has to span the frustum's visible width at z = 0, which is `2 * tan(fov/2) * cameraZ * aspect` — the container width in pixels has no fixed relationship to that, so the row overshoots on wide viewports and clips on narrow ones.
- Omitting `#include <colorspace_fragment>` from a `ShaderMaterial`. three only injects output conversion into its own materials, so raw linear values ship into an sRGB framebuffer and the plates render visibly washed out next to the CSS around them.
- Rebuilding the scene when the `items` array identity changes. Any caller who writes the list inline hands over a new array every render, which would tear down nineteen textures and a GL context on every keystroke. The setup effect keys on a string built from id, title and hue.

## Notes

- Textures are drawn at mount to a 512x1024 canvas per item — a hue ramp, hairline bands and a numeral. The bands are not decoration: a smooth gradient hides every deformation the shader applies, so the plate needs structure for the wave and the bulge to bend.
- All nineteen materials are separate `ShaderMaterial` instances because each needs its own uniforms, but three keys its program cache on the shader source, so they share a single compiled program.
- `drive: "page"` opts into a shared refcounted Lenis with `infinite: true`, which is the technique in its original form — the gallery *is* the page. The default `drive: "pointer"` keeps every gesture inside the component's own box.

## Definition of done

On mount the planes start as a flat row facing you and curl into a drum over about 1.6 s. Wheel or drag spins it endlessly in both directions with no seam and no jump at the ends; stop moving and it eases to centre one plane. The centred plane is full colour and the neighbours fade toward grey within two steps. Flick hard and the images ripple, the drum widens, and the ripple runs opposite ways depending on direction. Move the pointer over a plane and a soft lens follows it, magnifying rather than just denting. Unmount from React DevTools and the canvas leaves the DOM with no context-lost warning; mount and unmount twenty times and no context is dropped. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the drum is already assembled on the first frame and neither the ripple nor the lens ever appears.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Dashboard Page Header

The strip that opens every dashboard page: a small breadcrumb whose team and person crumbs carry a 16px initials circle, a 20px title, and a toolbar on the right. The toolbar has three fixed slots in order (date range, notification bell, actions), so pages line up the same way, and it wraps under the title on narrow screens. A companion PeriodStepper gives the "< Jun 29 - Jul 5 >" control that walks the window by its own length.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Dashboard page header: breadcrumb with initials crumbs, title, week stepper, unread bell and trailing action buttons.

- Category: navigation
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @internationalized/date@^3.12.4, react-aria@^3.53.1, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Breadcrumbs are plain data ({ label, href, onPress, initials, tone, icon }); each maps to the kit BreadcrumbItem, and the last one is rendered with current (aria-current="page", no link or click handler).
2. A crumb with initials renders an aria-hidden 16px rounded-full span tinted with status-blue / status-lime / status-purple tokens or the tertiary background for neutral; otherwise its icon goes through BreadcrumbItem's icon prop.
3. The title row is flex-wrap justify-between: the heading (h1 by default, headingLevel 1-3) truncates, and the toolbar is its own flex-wrap gap-2 group so it drops onto a second line instead of squeezing the title.
4. The bell slot is the notifications prop when given, else a built-in PageHeaderBell whenever notificationCount is defined: an IconButton whose aria-label carries the unread count, plus an aria-hidden red badge that scales from 50% and fades out at zero.
5. PeriodStepper shifts the range by an explicit step when given; otherwise a whole-calendar-month range moves by its month count (the end rebuilt with endOfMonth from the new start), and any other range moves by its own length in days.
6. The stepper label comes from useDateFormatter({ day: numeric, month: short, timeZone: UTC }).formatRange, shown in an aria-live <output> so each step is announced; previous/next disable when the shifted range would cross minValue / maxValue.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `crumb initials = 16px circle, 9px semibold`
  Sits on the 12px breadcrumb line at the same size as the kit's 16px crumb icons.
- `badge position = top-1 start-[18px], h-3.5 min-w-3.5`
  Puts the count over the bell glyph's top-right shoulder inside the 36px IconButton without covering the bell.
- `badge max = 9`
  A 14px badge holds two characters; larger counts read as 9+.
- `stepper height = h-9 (medium) / h-8 (small)`
  Matches the 36px Button and IconButton beside it so the toolbar shares one baseline.
- `badge transition = 200ms ease-out on scale and opacity`
  Quick enough to confirm "marked read" without delaying the next click; removed under motion-reduce.

## API

```ts
export function DashboardPageHeader({ title, description, breadcrumbs, breadcrumbLabel, dateRange, notificationCount, onNotificationsPress, notificationsLabel, notifications, actions, headingLevel, className, ...props }: DashboardPageHeaderProps): JSX.Element
export function PageHeaderBell({ count, max, label, onPress, className }: PageHeaderBellProps): JSX.Element
export function PeriodStepper({ value, defaultValue, onChange, step, minValue, maxValue, formatOptions, size, 'aria-label', previousLabel, nextLabel, className }: PeriodStepperProps): JSX.Element
export function shiftPeriod(range: PeriodRange, direction: 1 | -1, step?: DateDuration): PeriodRange
export function usePeriodLabel(range: PeriodRange, formatOptions?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions): string
```

- `title: ReactNode`
  Page title, rendered as a truncating 20px heading.
- `description: ReactNode`
  Optional secondary line under the title.
- `breadcrumbs: readonly PageHeaderCrumb[]` — default `[]`
  Ancestors first; the last crumb is the current page. Each crumb: label, href, onPress, initials, tone, icon.
- `breadcrumbLabel: string` — default `'Breadcrumb'`
  Accessible name of the breadcrumb nav.
- `dateRange: ReactNode`
  First toolbar slot, typically a PeriodStepper.
- `notificationCount: number`
  Unread count for the built-in bell; leaving it undefined (and notifications unset) hides the bell.
- `onNotificationsPress: () => void`
  Called when the built-in bell is clicked.
- `notificationsLabel: string` — default `'Notifications'`
  Base accessible label of the bell; ", N unread" is appended when the count is above zero.
- `notifications: ReactNode`
  Replaces the built-in bell in the second toolbar slot.
- `actions: ReactNode`
  Trailing buttons; put the primary action last.
- `headingLevel: 1 | 2 | 3` — default `1`
  Heading element used for the title.
- `PeriodStepper.value / defaultValue: PeriodRange`
  Controlled or initial { start, end } CalendarDate range.
- `PeriodStepper.onChange: (range: PeriodRange) => void`
  Called with the shifted range after each previous / next press.
- `PeriodStepper.step: DateDuration`
  Fixed shift per press; defaults to the range length, or its month count for whole months.
- `PeriodStepper.minValue / maxValue: CalendarDate`
  Bounds; the matching button disables once a step would cross them.
- `PeriodStepper.size: 'medium' | 'small'` — default `'medium'`
  36px or 32px tall.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function DashboardPageHeader({
  title,
  description,
  breadcrumbs = [],
  breadcrumbLabel = 'Breadcrumb',
  dateRange,
  notificationCount,
  onNotificationsPress,
  notificationsLabel,
  notifications,
  actions,
  headingLevel = 1,
  className,
  ...props
}: DashboardPageHeaderProps) {
  const Heading = (['h1', 'h2', 'h3'] as const)[headingLevel - 1] ?? 'h1';
  const bell =
    notifications ??
    (notificationCount !== undefined ? (
      <PageHeaderBell count={notificationCount} label={notificationsLabel} onPress={onNotificationsPress} />
    ) : null);
  const hasToolbar = Boolean(dateRange || bell || actions);
  const lastIndex = breadcrumbs.length - 1;

  return (
    <header {...props} className={cx('flex w-full min-w-0 flex-col gap-4', className)}>
      {breadcrumbs.length > 0 ? (
        <Breadcrumb aria-label={breadcrumbLabel} className="-mx-1">
          {breadcrumbs.map((crumb, index) => (
            <BreadcrumbItem
              key={`${index}-${crumb.label}`}
              icon={crumb.initials ? undefined : crumb.icon}
              href={index === lastIndex ? undefined : crumb.href}
              onClick={index === lastIndex ? undefined : crumb.onPress}
              current={index === lastIndex}
            >
              {crumb.initials ? <CrumbInitials initials={crumb.initials} tone={crumb.tone} /> : null}
              {crumb.label}
            </BreadcrumbItem>
          ))}
        </Breadcrumb>
      ) : null}

      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-x-6 gap-y-3">
        <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-0.5">
          <Heading className="truncate text-title-2-medium text-text-primary">{title}</Heading>
          {description ? <p className="text-body-regular text-text-secondary">{description}</p> : null}
        </div>
        {hasToolbar ? (
          <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
            {dateRange}
            {bell}
            {actions}
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </div>
    </header>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to release: no timers, listeners or observers; all state is React state.

**Reduced motion.** The badge appears and disappears without its scale/opacity transition, and the stepper and crumb hover colours change instantly (motion-reduce:transition-none). Nothing else moves.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not shift a whole-month range by adding months to its end: Jan 31 + 1 month clamps to Feb 28 and stays clamped (Mar 28). Rebuild the end from the new start.
- Do not format CalendarDate ranges in the local time zone: toDate(local) plus a local formatter can render the previous day for users west of UTC. Format with timeZone UTC from toDate("UTC").
- Do not put the unread count only in the badge: it is aria-hidden, so the IconButton's aria-label must carry it.
- Do not give the last crumb a link; it is the current page and gets aria-current="page".

## Notes

- Pass notifications={<YourBellPopover />} to replace the built-in bell, e.g. with a bell that opens a notification list.
- PeriodStepper is controlled (value + onChange) or uncontrolled (defaultValue); it throws when given neither.
- Without dateRange, the bell and actions the toolbar is not rendered, leaving a plain breadcrumb and title.

## Definition of done

Pressing "Next week" changes the stepper label from Jun 29 - Jul 5 to Jul 6 - 12, and pressing the bell hides its badge and drops the count from its accessible name.

# Build: Data Grid

A spreadsheet-style grid for thousands of rows: only the rows in view are mounted, a frozen first column and a row-number gutter stay put while the body scrolls, and a keyboard-driven cell cursor selects ranges, edits cells and pastes blocks from a spreadsheet. Every edit, paste and row delete goes back through `onDataChange` as a new array and lands on a 100-step undo stack. Around the body sit a toolbar (search, filters, column visibility, density, export) that swaps to a bulk-action bar when rows are checked, a summary row and a status bar with the selection address, count, sum and average.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A virtualized spreadsheet with range selection, validated in-cell edits, block paste, undo and redo, filters, summaries and CSV export.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, motion@^12.43.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Virtualization: the body is a fixed-height scroller (`height`, default 396) holding one spacer `rows.length * rowHeight` tall. Only rows from `floor(scrollTop / rowHeight) - 4` to `ceil((scrollTop + height) / rowHeight) + 4` render, each absolutely positioned at `top: r * rowHeight`. Rows are 44px, or 36px in Compact density, and every row shares one CSS grid template: a 48px gutter plus each column's width.
2. The header and summary rows sit outside the scroller with `overflow: hidden`; the body's `onScroll` copies its `scrollLeft` into both so the columns stay aligned. A `ResizeObserver` measures the body, and the first column is frozen (`sticky` at `inset-inline-start: 48px`) only while the body is at least gutter + first column + 96px wide, so on a phone it scrolls away instead of covering everything.
3. Range selection stores an anchor and a focus as `{ rowId, columnKey }`, not indices. `bounds` maps them through the current row and column index maps, so sorting, filtering or hiding columns keeps the selection on the same cells, and if an end cell drops out no range is drawn. Click selects, Shift+click and mouse drag (`pointerenter` with the button held) extend, Ctrl/Cmd+A selects everything, and `selectCell` scrolls the cursor into view on both axes, accounting for the frozen column and RTL.
4. The grid is one focusable `role="grid"` element with `aria-activedescendant` pointing at the focused cell id (only while that row is mounted). Arrows move (mirrored in RTL), Page Up/Down jump by a viewport of rows, Home/End go to the row ends (with Ctrl/Cmd, to the first or last row), Enter or F2 opens the editor, Escape clears the range, Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes and Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z or Ctrl/Cmd+Y redoes. The cursor outline is a `motion.span` with a shared `layoutId`, so it springs from cell to cell.
5. Editing: double-click, Enter or F2 swaps the cell for an input (select columns show their select whenever the cell is active). On commit the text goes through `parseGridValue` (numbers, min, max, allowed options) and the column's `validate`; a failure keeps the editor open and shows "Header: message" in a `role="alert"` bar. Enter commits and moves down, Shift+Enter up, Tab and Shift+Tab to the next or previous cell in reading order, and Escape cancels.
6. Clipboard and history: `onCopy` writes the range as TSV; `onPaste` parses TSV (quotes, CRLF), validates every cell first and cancels the whole paste on the first bad value, so a paste is all or nothing and one undo step. `commitEdits` applies `{ rowId, key, before, after }` edits with `applyGridEdits` and pushes them onto the undo stack (last 100 kept); deleting checked rows records each row with its index so undo splices them back. Before undoing, the grid checks the current data still holds the values it expects and clears the history instead if something outside changed them.
7. Toolbar and footer: the default toolbar shows the row count, Undo, Redo, Filter (a column switcher, a value search and one exact-match value per column), Columns, Row density, Export and Search. Checking rows cross-fades it (180ms, `AnimatePresence`, the leaving one `inert`) to a bar with Delete, Copy and Export for the checked rows. Summary cells show Sum, Avg or Count over the filtered rows; the status bar shows the range address ("B3:D7"), the count of filled cells and, for numbers, their sum and average.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `row height = 44px Comfortable, 36px Compact`
  Fixed row heights are what make virtualization pure arithmetic: the scroll offset alone tells the grid which rows to mount and where.
- `OVERSCAN = 4 rows above and below the viewport`
  A small buffer so a fast wheel flick does not show blank rows before React renders the next window.
- `GUTTER = 48px row-number and checkbox column`
  Holds the row number and the row checkbox, which fades in over the number on hover or focus and stays visible once checked.
- `column width = default 160px, resizable 96 to 480px, 16px per arrow key`
  The clamp keeps a column from vanishing or eating the viewport; double-clicking the resize handle restores the column's own width.
- `cursor spring = stiffness 480, damping 38, mass 0.7`
  Stiff and well damped, so the outline arrives under key repeat without overshooting into the next cell.
- `undo depth = 100 transactions`
  Bounds memory for long sessions; each paste or bulk delete is one transaction however many cells it touched.

## API

```ts
function DataGrid<T extends object>(props: DataGridProps<T>): JSX.Element
```

- `aria-label: string`
  Names the grid; also labels the search field.
- `data: readonly T[]`
  The rows. Treat as immutable; changes come back through `onDataChange`.
- `columns: readonly DataGridColumn<T>[]`
  Key, header, width, type (text, number or select), options, min, max, align, editable, filterable, summary (sum, average or count), format, formatSummary and validate.
- `getRowId: (row: T) => string`
  Stable id per row; selection, edits and undo are keyed by it.
- `onDataChange: (data: T[]) => void`
  Receives the next array after an edit, paste, delete, undo or redo. Omit for read-only.
- `height: number` — default `396`
  Height of the scrolling body in pixels.
- `exportFileName: string` — default `"data-grid.csv"`
  File name for CSV export.
- `emptyState: ReactNode` — default `"No matching rows. Try another search or clear your filters."`
  Shown when search or filters leave no rows.
- `className: string`
  Classes for the outer frame.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const rows = useMemo(() => {
  const search = query.trim().toLocaleLowerCase();
  const filtered = data.filter((row) =>
    (!search || columns.some((column) => String(row[column.key] ?? "").toLocaleLowerCase().includes(search))) &&
    columns.every((column) => filters[column.key] === undefined || String(row[column.key] ?? "") === filters[column.key]),
  );
  if (!sort) return filtered;
  const key = sort.key as keyof T;
  return filtered.sort((a, b) => {
    const left = a[key], right = b[key];
    const result = typeof left === "number" && typeof right === "number" ? left - right : String(left ?? "").localeCompare(String(right ?? ""), undefined, { numeric: true });
    return sort.descending ? -result : result;
  });
}, [data, columns, filters, query, sort]);
const rowIndices = useMemo(() => new Map(rows.map((row, index) => [getRowId(row), index])), [rows, getRowId]);
const columnIndices = useMemo(() => new Map(visibleColumns.map((column, index) => [column.key as string, index])), [visibleColumns]);
const bounds: Bounds | null = useMemo(() => {
  if (!range) return null;
  const a = rowIndices.get(range.anchor.rowId), b = rowIndices.get(range.focus.rowId);
  const c = columnIndices.get(range.anchor.columnKey), d = columnIndices.get(range.focus.columnKey);
  return a === undefined || b === undefined || c === undefined || d === undefined ? null : {
    top: Math.min(a, b), bottom: Math.max(a, b), start: Math.min(c, d), end: Math.max(c, d),
  };
}, [range, rowIndices, columnIndices]);
const columnWidths = visibleColumns.map((column) => widths[column.key] ?? column.width ?? 160);
const freezeFirstColumn = viewportWidth === 0 || viewportWidth >= GUTTER + (columnWidths[0] ?? 0) + 96;
const totalWidth = GUTTER + columnWidths.reduce((sum, width) => sum + width, 0);
const rowStyle: CSSProperties = { gridTemplateColumns: `${GUTTER}px ${columnWidths.map((width) => `${width}px`).join(" ")}`, width: totalWidth, minWidth: "100%" };
const firstRow = Math.max(0, Math.floor(scrollTop / rowHeight) - OVERSCAN);
const lastRow = Math.min(rows.length, Math.ceil((scrollTop + height) / rowHeight) + OVERSCAN);
const filterCount = Object.keys(filters).length;
const visibleSelected = rows.reduce((count, row) => count + Number(selectedRows.has(getRowId(row))), 0);
const filterColumns = columns.filter((column) => column.filterable || column.type === "select");
const filterOptions = useMemo(() => Object.fromEntries(columns.filter((column) => column.filterable || column.type === "select").map((column) => [column.key, column.options ?? Array.from(new Set(data.map((row) => String(row[column.key] ?? "")))).sort()])), [columns, data]);
const summaries = useMemo(() => Object.fromEntries(visibleColumns.map((column) => {
  if (!column.summary) return [column.key, null];
  const values = rows.map((row) => row[column.key]).filter((value): value is T[Extract<keyof T, string>] & number => typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value));
  const sum = values.reduce((total, value) => total + value, 0);
  return [column.key, column.summary === "count" ? rows.length : column.summary === "average" ? (values.length ? sum / values.length : null) : sum];
})), [rows, visibleColumns]);
const selectionStats = useMemo(() => {
  if (!bounds) return { count: 0, sum: null as number | null, average: null as number | null };
  let count = 0, sum = 0, numbers = 0;
  for (let r = bounds.top; r <= bounds.bottom; r++) for (let c = bounds.start; c <= bounds.end; c++) {
    const value = rows[r]![visibleColumns[c]!.key];
    if (value !== null && value !== undefined && value !== "") count++;
    if (typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value)) { sum += value; numbers++; }
  }
  return { count, sum: numbers ? sum : null, average: numbers ? sum / numbers : null };
}, [bounds, rows, visibleColumns]);
const focusRow = range ? rowIndices.get(range.focus.rowId) : undefined;
const focusColumn = range ? columnIndices.get(range.focus.columnKey) : undefined;
useEffect(() => {
  if (!freezeFirstColumn && focusColumn === 0 && bodyRef.current) bodyRef.current.scrollLeft = 0;
}, [freezeFirstColumn, focusColumn]);
const cellId = (r: number, c: number) => `${id}-cell-${r}-${c}`;
const activeId = focusRow !== undefined && focusColumn !== undefined && focusRow >= firstRow && focusRow < lastRow ? cellId(focusRow, focusColumn) : undefined;
const selectionAddress = bounds ? `${columnLetter(bounds.start)}${bounds.top + 1}${bounds.top !== bounds.bottom || bounds.start !== bounds.end ? `:${columnLetter(bounds.end)}${bounds.bottom + 1}` : ""}` : "—";

function resetScroll() {
  if (bodyRef.current) bodyRef.current.scrollTop = 0;
  setScrollTop(0);
  setEditing(null);
  setErrorMessage("");
}

function selectCell(r: number, c: number, extend = false) {
  if (!rows.length || !visibleColumns.length) return;
  r = Math.max(0, Math.min(rows.length - 1, r));
  c = Math.max(0, Math.min(visibleColumns.length - 1, c));
  const cell = { rowId: getRowId(rows[r]!), columnKey: visibleColumns[c]!.key };
  setRange((previous) => ({ anchor: extend && previous && bounds ? previous.anchor : cell, focus: cell }));
  setErrorMessage("");
  gridRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true });
  const body = bodyRef.current;
  if (body) {
    const top = r * rowHeight;
    if (top < body.scrollTop) body.scrollTop = top;
    else if (top + rowHeight > body.scrollTop + body.clientHeight) body.scrollTop = top + rowHeight - body.clientHeight;
    if (c > 0 || !freezeFirstColumn) {
      const start = GUTTER + columnWidths.slice(0, c).reduce((sum, width) => sum + width, 0);
      const offset = Math.abs(body.scrollLeft);
      const frozenWidth = GUTTER + (freezeFirstColumn ? (columnWidths[0] ?? 0) : 0);
      if (start < offset + frozenWidth) body.scrollLeft = (direction === "rtl" ? -1 : 1) * Math.max(0, start - frozenWidth);
      else if (start + columnWidths[c]! > offset + body.clientWidth) body.scrollLeft = (direction === "rtl" ? -1 : 1) * (start + columnWidths[c]! - body.clientWidth);
    }
  }
}

function commitEdits(edits: GridEdit<T>[]) {
  if (!onDataChange || !edits.length) return;
  onDataChange(applyGridEdits(data, getRowId, edits));
  setHistory((previous) => ({ undo: [...previous.undo.slice(-99), { type: "edit", edits }], redo: [] }));
  setMessage(`${integerFormat.format(edits.length)} ${edits.length === 1 ? "cell updated" : "cells updated"}.`);
  setErrorMessage("");
}

function travelHistory(undo: boolean) {
  const source = undo ? history.undo : history.redo;
  const transaction = source.at(-1);
  if (!transaction || !onDataChange) return;
  // External updates must not be overwritten by an old local history entry.
  const current = new Map(data.map((row) => [getRowId(row), row]));
  const stale = transaction.type === "edit"
    ? transaction.edits.some((edit) => !current.has(edit.rowId) || !Object.is(current.get(edit.rowId)![edit.key], undo ? edit.after : edit.before))
    : transaction.rows.some(({ row }) => undo ? current.has(getRowId(row)) : current.get(getRowId(row)) !== row);
  if (stale) {
    setHistory({ undo: [], redo: [] });
    setMessage("The data changed outside this grid. Change history has been cleared.");
    return;
  }
  if (transaction.type === "edit") onDataChange(applyGridEdits(data, getRowId, transaction.edits, undo));
  else if (undo) {
    const next = [...data];
    for (const { row, index } of transaction.rows) next.splice(Math.min(index, next.length), 0, row);
    onDataChange(next);
  } else {
    const removed = new Set(transaction.rows.map(({ row }) => getRowId(row)));
    onDataChange(data.filter((row) => !removed.has(getRowId(row))));
  }
  setHistory((previous) => undo ? { undo: previous.undo.slice(0, -1), redo: [...previous.redo, transaction] } : { undo: [...previous.undo, transaction], redo: previous.redo.slice(0, -1) });
  setEditing(null);
  setMessage(undo ? "Change undone." : "Change redone.");
  setErrorMessage("");
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The `ResizeObserver` on the body disconnects on unmount. Column-resize listeners live on the handle and are removed on `lostpointercapture`. The CSV export's object URL is revoked one second after the download starts.

**Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion` (via motion's `useReducedMotion`) the toolbar cross-fade and the cursor spring get zero duration, so the bars swap and the outline jumps instantly. The 150ms cell background fade is dropped with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not track the selection by row index. The range stores row ids and column keys, which is why a sort or filter keeps it on the same cells; index-based ranges jump to different data.
- Do not mutate `data` in place. The filtered rows, index maps, filter options and summaries are memoized on the `data` reference, so an in-place change leaves them stale; replace the array, as the one `onDataChange` hands back does.
- Do not create `columns` or `getRowId` inline on every render. They are memo dependencies, so each new identity rebuilds the filtered and sorted rows and the index maps.
- Do not swap the grid's number formatting back to `toLocaleString()`. Footer summaries without `formatSummary`, the selection Count/Sum/Avg and the row counts all go through module-level `Intl.NumberFormat("en-US")` formatters, so a de-DE browser shows the same "100,716" as the server render instead of "100.716". To show another locale, pass `formatSummary` with your own formatter.

## Notes

- Omit `onDataChange` for a read-only grid: editing, paste, undo, redo and row delete are disabled and the grid reports `aria-readonly`.
- Search matches any column's text, case-insensitively; filters match exact values. Filter options come from `options` or from the distinct values in `data`.
- Export writes the visible columns of the checked rows (or of every filtered row when none are checked) as UTF-8 CSV with a BOM. `serializeGridRows` prefixes cells that start with =, +, - or @ with an apostrophe so spreadsheets do not run them as formulas.
- Copy selected rows uses `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, so it needs a secure context and clipboard permission; a refusal shows an error instead of failing silently.
- Composes kit items: Button, CloseButton, Checkbox, Dropdown, Input, Select, SegmentedControl and Tooltip.

## Definition of done

The grid shows its row count, a header with a frozen first column and a body that scrolls smoothly with only a window of rows in the DOM. Arrow keys move the outlined cursor, Shift+arrows extend a range and the status bar shows its address, count, sum and average. Double-clicking a number cell and entering text shows "Seats: Enter a valid number." and keeps the editor open; a valid value updates the cell and the column summary, and Ctrl/Cmd+Z restores it. Pasting a 2x2 block from a spreadsheet fills four cells as one undo step. Checking rows swaps the toolbar to the bulk bar; Delete removes them and Undo brings them back in place. Filter by a value, hide a column, switch to Compact and export a CSV.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Data Table

The dashboard customers table from BoardUI: a toolbar with a result count, price, product and region selects and a search field, then a sortable, selectable, paginated table of 48 seeded customers with avatar initials, a purchase-status select, a status chip, a date, a price and row actions. A @tanstack/react-table instance owns the sort, selection and page state, and the kit's React Aria `Table` only renders what TanStack hands it. A Normal / Compact switch under the table changes the density of every cell at once.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A customers table where TanStack owns sorting, selection and pages, filters narrow the rows, and React Aria renders the grid.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, @tanstack/react-table@^8.21.3, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Rows come from a module-level array: 48 customers drawn from a seeded PRNG (seed 42), so server and client generate the same list. The first eight use fixed names; the rest combine random first and last names. Each row carries a purchase state, one of four statuses, a product, a region, a price from $20 to $3,999 and a 2026 date, plus `updatedTs` for sorting.
2. Filtering happens before TanStack sees the data: a `useMemo` keeps the customers that match the price bucket, product, region and a case-insensitive name search. Every filter `onSelectionChange` and every keystroke in search calls `table.setPageIndex(0)`, so narrowing the list never strands you on a page that no longer exists.
3. `useReactTable` gets the filtered data, column defs, `getRowId: row => row.id` and controlled `sorting`, `rowSelection` and `pagination` state, with the core, sorted and pagination row models. Name, Last updated (sorted on `updatedTs`) and Price are sortable; Purchase, Status and Actions set `enableSorting: false`. Two rows start selected.
4. The kit `Table` is React Aria's with `selectionMode="none"`, so React Aria never keeps a second selection. Selection is TanStack's: each name cell holds a `Checkbox` with `slot={null}` wired to `row.toggleSelected`, the header holds a select-all-on-this-page checkbox that shows indeterminate for a partial page, and selected rows get the secondary background through an inline style.
5. Sortable headers are plain buttons calling `column.getToggleSortingHandler()`; the `SortChevron` turns 180 degrees for ascending over 150ms and darkens when active. Rows render `flexRender` cells into fixed-width columns inside a `min-w-[1000px]` table whose container scrolls horizontally on narrow screens. An empty filter result shows "No customers match your filters."
6. Row actions are Delete and Edit `IconButton`s wrapped in `Focusable` so a React Aria `TooltipTrigger` can attach (200ms delay), and a More trigger styled like an IconButton that opens a four-item dropdown. The pagination footer appears only when there is more than one page. The density switch sets the table `size` to `md` or `sm`, which also swaps avatar, select and chip sizes, and the `.bui-table` styles animate cell padding and font size over 200ms.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `page size = 8 rows (prop `pageSize`)`
  Eight Normal-density rows plus the toolbar and footer fit a laptop viewport; BoardUI's landing collage passes 5 to match the Figma crop.
- `seeded data = mulberry32-style PRNG, seed 42, 48 rows`
  Enough rows for six pages and meaningful filtering, and deterministic so server-rendered markup matches the client.
- `column widths = name 240, purchase 172, status 168, updated 160, price 140, actions 132 (px); table min-w-[1000px]`
  Fixed widths stop columns from jumping when sorting or paging changes the longest value; the minimum width keeps the action buttons from wrapping and lets the container scroll instead.
- `cell density = Normal px-3 py-2.5 body; Compact px-2.5 py-1.5 body-2; 200ms transition`
  The density switch animates padding and font size together, so the rows compress smoothly instead of snapping.
- `tooltip delay = 200ms`
  Long enough that sweeping across a row of icon buttons does not flash tooltips, short enough to label an icon on purpose.

## API

```ts
function DataTableExample(props?: { showSizeToggle?: boolean; pageSize?: number }): JSX.Element
```

- `pageSize: number` — default `8`
  Rows per page.
- `showSizeToggle: boolean` — default `true`
  Shows the Normal / Compact density switch below the table.

## Reference implementation of the core

the component as fixed.

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers or global listeners of its own. The TanStack instance lives in component state, and React Aria tears down tooltip, select and dropdown overlays when they close or unmount.

**Reduced motion.** The block does not branch on `prefers-reduced-motion`. Its motion is the 150ms sort-chevron turn, 150ms row and button colour fades, the 200ms density change and the kit popovers' short entrances; none of it carries information the static state lacks.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not let React Aria and TanStack both own selection. The table uses `selectionMode="none"` and the checkboxes use `slot={null}`; otherwise React Aria claims the checkboxes for its own selection model and the two states drift apart.
- Do not drop `getRowId`. With TanStack's default index ids, selection belongs to positions, so filtering or sorting moves the checkmarks onto different customers.
- Do not change filters without resetting `pageIndex`. Filtering to fewer rows while on page 5 leaves the table showing an empty page.
- Do not put the real `IconButton` inside `DropdownTrigger`. Both render buttons, so the More trigger restyles the trigger itself to avoid nesting a button in a button.
- Do not generate the sample data with `Math.random()` at render time. The seeded PRNG at module level is what keeps hydration stable.

## Notes

- The purchase select in each row is uncontrolled (`defaultSelectedKey`) and does not write back to the data, so a change resets when the row remounts, for example after paging. Lift it into state if it must persist.
- `formatPrice` prints prices of 1,000 or more with a dot separator ("$1.250"), as in the Figma frame; swap in `Intl.NumberFormat` for your locale.
- All strings go through `useTemplateCopy`, so a `TemplateCopyProvider` can translate the toolbar, headers and empty state.
- Composes kit items: Table, Select, Checkbox, Avatar, Chip, StatusDot, IconButton, Tooltip, Dropdown, InputBase, Pagination and SegmentedControl.

# Build: Dataset-Driven Parallax

Depth is declared in the markup: any descendant carrying `data-parallax="0.3"` drifts at that rate. One effect walks the container, parses the attribute and builds a scrubbed tween per layer, so adding a new plane to a hero is an attribute rather than a code change. Travel is expressed as a percentage of the element's own height, which keeps the effect proportional at every breakpoint.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Layers drift at a rate written on the element itself, over the widest possible scroll window.

- Category: scroll
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. The container is walked once for `[data-parallax]` descendants. The depth is read with a double fallback — `parseFloat(el.getAttribute(attr) ?? "") || fallback` — so a missing value, an empty value and a non-numeric value all land on the same default.
2. Each layer gets `gsap.to(layer, { yPercent: -(100 * depth), ease: "none" })`. `yPercent` is a percentage of the element's own height, so a 2000px hero and a 400px mobile hero travel proportionally with no media query.
3. `ease: "none"` is required, not stylistic. Any easing on a scrubbed tween means the layer accelerates and decelerates independently of the wheel, so two layers at different depths drift out of sync mid-scroll and snap back at the ends.
4. The trigger window is `start: "top bottom"` to `end: "bottom top"` — the full travel range, from the instant the element enters the scroller to the instant it leaves. That is the widest window available, which spreads the same travel across the most scroll distance.
5. `invalidateOnRefresh: true` makes ScrollTrigger recompute start and end on resize; percentage-based travel is derived from element height and a stale measurement leaves every layer offset.
6. Under reduced motion the effect returns before creating anything, so the layers render at their authored positions.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `DEFAULT_DEPTH = 0.15`
  Fallback drift: 15% of the element's height across the whole window. Below ~0.05 the layer looks static next to its neighbours; above ~0.4 it visibly separates from the content it belongs to and reads as a rendering fault.
- `start / end = 'top bottom' / 'bottom top'`
  The maximum-length window. Narrowing it (say `top 80%` to `bottom 20%`) forces the same travel through less scroll, which is the difference between drift and the page appearing to come apart.
- `yPercent multiplier = -100`
  Negative so layers move against the scroll — the direction that reads as distance. A positive multiplier moves them with the scroll, which reads as the layer being dragged.
- `scrub = true`
  Locked to scroll position with no lag. Parallax is a spatial relationship: a numeric scrub adds lag, and lagging layers cross each other during a fast flick.

## API

```ts
function DatasetParallax(props: { children: ReactNode; attribute?: string; fallback?: number; scrub?: boolean | number; scrollerRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Section content. Any descendant with the depth attribute becomes a layer.
- `attribute: string` — default `'data-parallax'`
  Attribute carrying the depth. Its value is parsed as a float.
- `fallback: number` — default `0.15`
  Depth used when the attribute is missing, empty or not a number.
- `scrub: boolean | number` — default `true`
  ScrollTrigger scrub. A number adds that many seconds of lag.
- `scrollerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>`
  The scroll container that owns the scroll position. Omit for the document.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the container via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const DEFAULT_DEPTH = 0.15;

export function DatasetParallax({
  children,
  attribute = 'data-parallax',
  fallback = DEFAULT_DEPTH,
  scrub = true,
  scrollerRef,
  className,
}: DatasetParallaxProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  useGsap(
    gsap,
    () => {
      const el = root.current;
      if (!el || reduced) return;

      const scroller = scrollerRef?.current ?? undefined;

      for (const layer of Array.from(el.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(`[${attribute}]`))) {
        // `?? ''` handles a bare `data-parallax` with no value, and the finite
        // check handles `parseFloat` returning NaN on anything non-numeric. A
        // NaN reaching `yPercent` does not throw — it silently pins the layer
        // at its untransformed position, which looks like the effect simply
        // not working on that one element.
        //
        // Tested with `Number.isFinite`, not `||`. `data-parallax="0"` is the
        // documented way to hold a layer still against the scroll, and zero is
        // falsy: `|| fallback` read that as "no value given" and moved the one
        // layer the author had explicitly asked not to move.
        const raw = layer.getAttribute(attribute) ?? '';
        const parsed = parseFloat(raw);
        const depth = Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : fallback;

        gsap.to(layer, {
          yPercent: -(100 * depth),
          ease: 'none',
          scrollTrigger: {
            trigger: layer,
            scroller,
            // The widest possible window: begins the instant the layer's top
            // touches the bottom of the scroller and ends when its bottom
            // leaves the top. Any narrower range concentrates the same travel
            // into less scroll, which is what makes cheap parallax feel like
            // the page is sliding apart.
            start: 'top bottom',
            end: 'bottom top',
            scrub,
            // Percent-based travel is recomputed from element height; without
            // this a resize leaves every layer measured against the old one.
            invalidateOnRefresh: true,
          },
        });
      }
    },
    root,
    [attribute, fallback, scrub, reduced],
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `useGsap` wraps the whole walk in a `gsap.context`; `ctx.revert()` on unmount kills every tween and its ScrollTrigger and strips the inline `transform` GSAP wrote. Without the revert the triggers survive the unmount and keep scrubbing detached nodes on the next page.

**Reduced motion.** The effect returns before creating any tween, so every layer stays exactly where the stylesheet put it. The layout is authored to be correct at rest, so nothing is missing — the planes simply do not separate.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using `y` in pixels instead of `yPercent`. It looks correct at the breakpoint you tuned and wrong at every other one — on a short viewport a fixed 300px offset can push the layer entirely out of its own container.
- A single `|| 0.15` fallback. `el.dataset.parallax || "0.15"` covers the missing attribute, but `parseFloat("fast")` returns `NaN` and `NaN` reaching `yPercent` does not throw — the layer just silently stops moving, which is a bug you find by eye weeks later.
- Adding an ease to a scrubbed tween. The layer then accelerates on its own schedule rather than the wheel's, so layers at different depths drift out of relative order and snap at each end of the range.
- Omitting `invalidateOnRefresh`. Rotating a phone or opening a sidebar changes element height; the tween keeps using the height measured on mount and every layer sits at the wrong offset until reload.
- Leaving the scroller as the document when the content lives in an `overflow-y-auto` container. Every start and end is then measured against the window, so nothing moves at the right time — or at all.
- Building one giant timeline for all layers. Independent triggers per layer are correct here: a layer must respond to its own position in the scroller, not to a shared progress value.

## Notes

- The attribute name is configurable so the component can coexist with an existing convention rather than forcing `data-parallax` onto a codebase that already has one.
- Depths above 1 are legal and useful for a single foreground element that should outrun everything, but two such layers next to each other stop reading as depth.

## Definition of done

Scroll the section: layers with a larger `data-parallax` value visibly outrun the ones with smaller values, and every layer is back in its authored position when it leaves the scroller. Change an attribute value in devtools and reload — the rate changes with no code edit. Resize the window mid-scroll and the layers stay aligned with their content.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
