# Build: Date Calendar

A month laid out on the page instead of in a popover: `DateCalendar` picks one day, `DateRangeCalendar` picks a span across one or two months. Both are thin wrappers that hand React Aria's `Calendar` and `RangeCalendar` the Date Picker's shared `MonthPanel`, so the card, the 32px day cells and the accent range band are identical to the popover pickers. Selection fades in on opacity rather than popping.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

An inline month calendar for one date or a range, with a continuous range band, a today dot and struck-through unavailable days.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1, @internationalized/date@^3.12.4

## How it works

1. `DateCalendar` renders `<Calendar>` from react-aria-components with one `MonthPanel offset={0} showPrev showNext}`. `DateRangeCalendar` renders `<RangeCalendar visibleDuration={{ months: visibleMonths }}>` and either one panel with both chevrons or two panels in a `flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-2` row, the first carrying only the previous chevron and the second (`offset={1}`) only the next, so the pair pages as one unit and stacks when the row is narrow.
2. `MonthPanel` reads `RangeCalendarStateContext` and `CalendarStateContext`; exactly one is non-null, which tells it whether it sits in a range or a single calendar. The title is `visibleRange.start.add({ months: offset })` formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { month: "long", year: "numeric" })`. The prev/next buttons are RAC `Button`s with `slot="previous"` / `slot="next"`, so the calendar wires their paging itself.
3. The grid is a `CalendarGrid` table with `border-separate border-spacing-3` (12px), pulled out by `-m-3` so the outer spacing does not pad the card. At `max-[380px]` the column spacing drops to 8px (`border-spacing-x-2`, `-mx-2`), so the card is 302px and fits a 360px phone. Weekday headers are cut to two letters when the locale's short weekday is Latin script, and fall back to the `narrow` style otherwise.
4. Each `DayCell` always renders two absolutely positioned layers: a range band (`bg-date-range-background`) and an edge pill (`bg-date-range-edge-background`). Selection only flips their `opacity` between 0 and 1 with `transition-[opacity,border-radius] duration-100`, so dragging a range across ~40 cells is a CSS transition, not mounts and unmounts.
5. The band bridges the 12px gaps: a selected middle cell extends 6px (`-start-1.5` / `-end-1.5`) toward each selected neighbour, the start and end cells begin at `start-1/2` / `end-1/2` so the band runs under half the pill, and the first and last column of a week never extend and get `rounded-s-lg` / `rounded-e-lg` instead.
6. A plain `Calendar` never sets `isSelectionStart` / `isSelectionEnd`, so the cell computes `isSingleDay` and `isEdge` from `isSelected` when not in a range; otherwise the one picked day would render as a mid-range band. Days outside the month render as an empty `size-8` box, unavailable days (`isDateUnavailable`) get `line-through text-text-tertiary`, and `showToday` adds a 4px dot at `bottom-1`, accent on a plain day and `bg-text-primary` on a selected one.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `panel = w-[326px], p-[15px], rounded-2xl, shadow-xs; w-[302px] at max-[380px]`
  Seven 32px cells with six 12px gaps is 296px; 15px of padding on each side gives the 326px card from Figma. The bare variant is exactly that 296px. A 360px phone leaves about 312px, so up to 380px the column gap is 8px: 272px of grid, a 302px card.
- `day cell / gap = 32px (size-8) / border-spacing 12px (8px × 12px at max-[380px])`
  The Figma grid. The gap is real table spacing, which is why the range band needs the 6px bridge to read as one continuous strip.
- `band bridge = 6px (-start-1.5 / -end-1.5); 4px at max-[380px]`
  Half of the 12px gap from each side meets in the middle. More would overlap the neighbouring band and double the colour where the two layers cross.
- `selection fade = 100ms ease-out on opacity and border-radius`
  Fast enough that a range follows the pointer, slow enough that the band visibly grows rather than flickering. Radius rides the same transition so a deselected edge eases square in sync with the fade.
- `today dot = size-1 (4px) at bottom-1`
  Sits under the numeral inside the 32px cell without touching it, and stays visible on top of the selected pill by switching to `bg-text-primary`.

## API

```ts
function DateCalendar<T extends DateValue>(props: Omit<CalendarProps<T>, "className" | "children" | "visibleDuration"> & { showToday?: boolean; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function DateRangeCalendar<T extends DateValue>(props: Omit<RangeCalendarProps<T>, "className" | "children" | "visibleDuration"> & { visibleMonths?: 1 | 2; showToday?: boolean; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `value / defaultValue: T | null (DateCalendar) · RangeValue<T> | null (DateRangeCalendar)`
  Controlled or initial selection as `@internationalized/date` values.
- `onChange: (value) => void`
  Fires with the picked date, or with `{ start, end }` once a range is complete.
- `visibleMonths: 1 | 2` — default `2`
  DateRangeCalendar only. Two months side by side that wrap to a stack when narrow, or one.
- `showToday: boolean` — default `true`
  Draws a 4px dot under today's date.
- `isDateUnavailable: (date: DateValue) => boolean`
  Days that can be focused but not picked; rendered struck through.
- `minValue / maxValue: DateValue`
  Bounds; days outside are disabled and faded.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the `inline-flex` root.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function DateCalendar<T extends DateValue>({ showToday = true, className, ...props }: DateCalendarProps<T>) {
  return (
    <AriaCalendar {...props} className={cx("inline-flex outline-none", className)}>
      <MonthPanel offset={0} showPrev showNext showToday={showToday} />
    </AriaCalendar>
  );
}

export interface DateRangeCalendarProps<T extends DateValue>
  extends Omit<AriaRangeCalendarProps<T>, "className" | "children" | "visibleDuration"> {
  /** One month, or two side by side (default). They stack when the space is narrow. */
  visibleMonths?: 1 | 2;
  /** Mark today with a dot. Default true. */
  showToday?: boolean;
  className?: string;
}

export function DateRangeCalendar<T extends DateValue>({
  visibleMonths = 2,
  showToday = true,
  className,
  ...props
}: DateRangeCalendarProps<T>) {
  return (
    <AriaRangeCalendar
      {...props}
      visibleDuration={{ months: visibleMonths }}
      className={cx("inline-flex outline-none", className)}
    >
      <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-2">
        {visibleMonths === 2 ? (
          <>
            <MonthPanel offset={0} showPrev showToday={showToday} />
            <MonthPanel offset={1} showNext showToday={showToday} />
          </>
        ) : (
          <MonthPanel offset={0} showPrev showNext showToday={showToday} />
        )}
      </div>
    </AriaRangeCalendar>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to release. The calendar holds React Aria state only; there are no timers, observers or global listeners.

**Reduced motion.** The only motion is the 100ms opacity and radius fade on selection plus 150ms colour on the chevrons. Neither moves anything, so nothing changes under `prefers-reduced-motion`; months swap instantly with no slide.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not mount the range band and edge pill only when selected. They exist on every cell and change `opacity`; conditional rendering removes the fade and makes range drags janky.
- Do not derive the single-day pill from `isSelectionStart && isSelectionEnd` in a plain `Calendar`. Those flags are range-only and stay false, so the picked day falls through to the mid-range band. Branch on whether a `RangeCalendarStateContext` exists.
- Do not replace `border-spacing` with `gap` utilities. `CalendarGrid` is a `<table>`; only `border-separate` plus `border-spacing` spaces its cells.
- Do not render the calendar without a `value` or `defaultValue` in server-rendered pages. React Aria then focuses today, and today can differ between server and client.
- Do not omit `aria-label` (or a visible label wired with `aria-labelledby`). The grid is a labelled region, and React Aria warns without one.

## Notes

- Values are `@internationalized/date` objects (`parseDate("2026-03-18")` gives a `CalendarDate`). `minValue` and `maxValue` fade the days outside them; `isDateUnavailable` keeps a day focusable but unpickable and strikes it through.
- The same `MonthPanel` and `DayCell` power `DatePicker` and `DateRangePicker`, so a fix to the cell lands in all four components.

## Definition of done

A month card renders with two-letter weekday headers and 32px days spaced 12px apart. Clicking a day in `DateCalendar` fades in a rounded accent pill and fires `onChange`. In `DateRangeCalendar`, clicking a start and then an end day draws one continuous band between two pills that breaks with rounded ends at week boundaries. Arrow keys move focus by day and Page Up/Down by month; the chevrons page the month. Days passed to `isDateUnavailable` are struck through and cannot be picked.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Date Picker

A single-date picker: a calendar-icon trigger shows the committed date, and clicking it opens a popover holding one month, a typed date chip and Cancel / Apply buttons. Picking a day only changes a draft; `onChange` fires on Apply. The popover scales in from 95% with a 2px blur, and the date chip drops in with a slight overshoot the first time a day is chosen.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A trigger button that opens one month in a popover, with an editable DD/MM/YYYY chip and Cancel / Apply so nothing commits early.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1, @internationalized/date@^3.12.4, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, motion@^12.43.0

## How it works

1. The trigger is a plain `<button>` styled with the shared `triggerButtonClassName` (white surface, `rounded-2lg`, `shadow-xs`, 150ms colour transition). Its label is the committed value through `Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { month: "short", day: "numeric", year: "numeric" })`, or "Select date" when empty, next to a 20px `RiCalendarLine`.
2. The surface is a standalone React Aria `Popover` with `triggerRef`, `isOpen`, `offset={4}`, `placement="bottom end"` and `isNonModal`, wrapping a `Dialog`. Non-modal avoids the scroll lock and focus trap, but it also turns off outside-click dismissal, so `useDismissOnOutsidePress` closes it on any `pointerdown` outside both the trigger and the popover.
3. Value is split in two. `committedValue` is the controlled `value` or internal state from `defaultValue`. `pendingValue` is what the `Calendar` edits. Apply calls `commit(pendingValue)`, which sets internal state when uncontrolled, fires `onChange` and closes; Cancel resets the draft to the committed value and closes.
4. An effect keyed on `isOpen` resets the draft to the committed value and increments `openKey` on every open, and `Calendar` is keyed on `openKey`. React Aria's Calendar keeps its own visible month while mounted (the Popover stays mounted through its exit animation), so without the remount a value changed from outside would reopen on the old month.
5. Inside the Calendar sits the shared `MonthPanel` (326px card, 32px cells, 12px spacing). The footer's `AnimatePresence` mounts a `motion.div` with the editable `DateChipInput` once a draft exists: `initial { opacity: 0, y: -12 }` to `{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }` over 0.25s with the overshoot curve `[0.34, 1.2, 0.64, 1]`. The chip keeps its own text while typing and commits on blur or Enter; text that does not parse as `DD/MM/YYYY` reverts.
6. Passing `triggerRef` switches to external mode: DatePicker hides its own button, anchors the popover to the given element and takes `isOpen` / `onOpenChange` from the caller.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `popover offset / placement = 4px, bottom end`
  Four pixels clears the trigger's shadow without looking detached. `end` right-aligns the 342px popover to the trigger, so a trigger at the right of a toolbar or card header opens inward.
- `popover enter / exit = 150ms ease-out, opacity 0, scale-95, blur-[2px], origin-top`
  From the shared `popoverClassName`. The scale grows down from the trigger edge; the blur hides the text snapping in on the first frame.
- `date chip entrance = y -12 → 0, 0.25s, ease [0.34, 1.2, 0.64, 1]`
  The control point above 1 overshoots slightly, so the chip settles rather than sliding to a dead stop. Twelve pixels reads as dropping out of the calendar above it.
- `z-index = z-110`
  Above the kit's modal layer (z-100), so a date picker inside a dialog opens over it.
- `chip width = w-[104px]`
  Fits "DD/MM/YYYY" at the body-medium size with 8px padding, so the field does not resize as digits are typed.

## API

```ts
function DatePicker(props: { value?: CalendarDate | null; defaultValue?: CalendarDate | null; onChange?: (value: CalendarDate | null) => void; isDisabled?: boolean; className?: string; "aria-label"?: string; triggerRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; isOpen?: boolean; onOpenChange?: (isOpen: boolean) => void }): JSX.Element
```

- `value: CalendarDate | null`
  Controlled committed date. Leave undefined for uncontrolled use.
- `defaultValue: CalendarDate | null` — default `null`
  Initial committed date when uncontrolled.
- `onChange: (value: CalendarDate | null) => void`
  Fires on Apply with the drafted date, never while browsing the month.
- `isDisabled: boolean`
  Disables the built-in trigger button.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Date"`
  Labels the dialog and the calendar grid.
- `triggerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>`
  Anchor the popover to your own element; DatePicker's button is then not rendered.
- `isOpen / onOpenChange: boolean / (isOpen: boolean) => void`
  Open state, used only together with `triggerRef`.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the trigger button.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function DatePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onChange,
  isDisabled,
  className,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel = "Date",
  triggerRef: externalTriggerRef,
  isOpen: controlledIsOpen,
  onOpenChange: controlledOnOpenChange,
}: DatePickerProps) {
  const localize = useTemplateCopy();
  const { locale } = useLocale();
  const ownTriggerRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const triggerRef = externalTriggerRef ?? ownTriggerRef;
  const isExternal = externalTriggerRef !== undefined;
  const popoverRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);

  const [internalOpen, setInternalOpen] = useState(false);
  const isOpen = isExternal ? (controlledIsOpen ?? false) : internalOpen;
  const setIsOpen = isExternal ? (controlledOnOpenChange ?? (() => {})) : setInternalOpen;

  const isControlled = value !== undefined;
  const [internalValue, setInternalValue] = useState<CalendarDate | null>(defaultValue);
  const committedValue = isControlled ? (value ?? null) : internalValue;

  const [pendingValue, setPendingValue] = useState<CalendarDate | null>(committedValue);
  // React Aria's `Calendar` keeps its own internal `visibleRange` state for
  // as long as it stays mounted (Popover keeps its content mounted between
  // opens for the exit animation), so it never re-derives the visible month
  // from a later `value` change on its own. Bumping this on every open and
  // keying `Calendar` on it forces a fresh mount showing the right month —
  // needed for the external-trigger case, where `value` can jump (e.g. the
  // calendar template's month switcher) between one open and the next.
  const [openKey, setOpenKey] = useState(0);

  // Re-sync the calendar's displayed month/selection to the current
  // committed value every time the popover opens — not just when DatePicker's
  // own trigger toggles it, but also when `isOpen` is flipped true by an
  // external trigger (`triggerRef`), which never runs `openChange` below.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (isOpen) {
      setPendingValue(committedValue);
      setOpenKey((k) => k + 1);
    }
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps -- resync on the open transition only, not every committedValue change
  }, [isOpen]);

  const commit = (next: CalendarDate | null) => {
    if (!isControlled) setInternalValue(next);
    onChange?.(next);
    setIsOpen(false);
  };

  const openChange = (open: boolean) => {
    setIsOpen(open);
  };

  useDismissOnOutsidePress(isOpen, () => setIsOpen(false), [triggerRef, popoverRef]);

  return localize((
    <>
      {!isExternal && (
        <button
          ref={ownTriggerRef}
          type="button"
          disabled={isDisabled}
          onClick={() => openChange(!isOpen)}
          className={cx(triggerButtonClassName, className)}
        >
          <RiCalendarLine className="size-5 shrink-0 text-foreground-icon-primary" aria-hidden />
          <span className="flex items-center justify-center whitespace-nowrap px-1 text-body-medium text-text-primary">
            {committedValue ? formatTriggerDate(committedValue, locale) : "Select date"}
          </span>
        </button>
      )}
      <Popover
        ref={popoverRef}
        triggerRef={triggerRef}
        isOpen={isOpen}
        onOpenChange={openChange}
        offset={4}
        placement="bottom end"
        isNonModal
        className={popoverClassName}
      >
        <Dialog aria-label={ariaLabel} className="outline-none">
          <Calendar key={openKey} aria-label={ariaLabel} value={pendingValue} onChange={setPendingValue}>
            <div className="flex flex-col pt-2 pe-2 pb-3 ps-2">
              <MonthPanel offset={0} showPrev showNext />
              <div className="flex items-center justify-between pt-3 pe-4 ps-4">
                <div>
                  <AnimatePresence>
                    {pendingValue && (
                      <motion.div
                        key="date-summary"
                        initial={{ opacity: 0, y: -12 }}
                        animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
                        exit={{ opacity: 0, y: -12 }}
                        transition={{ duration: 0.25, ease: [0.34, 1.2, 0.64, 1] }}
                      >
                        <DateChipInput date={pendingValue} label="Date" onCommit={setPendingValue} />
                      </motion.div>
                    )}
                  </AnimatePresence>
                </div>
                <div className="flex items-center gap-2.5">
                  <Button
                    variant="secondary"
                    onClick={() => {
                      setPendingValue(committedValue);
                      setIsOpen(false);
                    }}
                  >
                    Cancel
                  </Button>
                  <Button onClick={() => commit(pendingValue)} disabled={!pendingValue}>
                    Apply
                  </Button>
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
          </Calendar>
        </Dialog>
      </Popover>
    </>
  ));
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The outside-press hook removes its document `pointerdown` listener when the popover closes or the component unmounts. Motion's `AnimatePresence` finishes or cancels the chip animation on unmount. No timers.

**Reduced motion.** The component does not branch on `prefers-reduced-motion`: the popover's 150ms fade, scale and blur and the chip's 12px drop still play. Both are short. Wrap the app in Motion's `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">` to drop the chip's transform; the day-cell selection only fades opacity.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not fire `onChange` from the Calendar's own `onChange`. The calendar edits a draft; only Apply commits, and Cancel must leave the committed value untouched.
- Do not remove the `openKey` remount. The popover content stays mounted between opens, so the Calendar keeps showing the month it last displayed even after `value` moved to another month.
- Do not set `isNonModal` without restoring outside dismissal. React Aria couples the two, and the popover would then only close through Cancel, Apply or Escape.
- Do not pass a JS `Date`. `value`, `defaultValue` and `onChange` use `CalendarDate` from `@internationalized/date` (`parseDate("2026-03-18")`).
- Do not render it with an initial `isOpen` on a server-rendered page. Open it from the trigger.

## Notes

- Strings are run through `useTemplateCopy`, so a `TemplateCopyProvider` higher up can translate "Select date", "Cancel" and "Apply" without forking the component.
- The month grid, day cell, chip input and popover chrome come from the shared date-picker module, the same code that renders `DateRangePicker` and `DateCalendar`.

## Definition of done

The trigger shows the current date (e.g. "Mar 18, 2026"). Clicking it opens a month card below, right-aligned, fading and scaling in. Clicking a day moves the pill and drops a DD/MM/YYYY chip into the footer, but the trigger label does not change. Typing a valid date in the chip and pressing Enter moves the selection; invalid text reverts on blur. Apply updates the trigger and fires `onChange` once; Cancel or a click outside closes it with the old date intact. Reopening shows the month of the committed date.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Date Range Picker

A dashboard-style range picker. The trigger shows the committed span ("Mar 2, 2026 - Mar 15, 2026"); the popover pairs a column of presets (Today through All time) with two side-by-side months whose selection reads as one continuous band. The footer drops in editable start and end chips and a "14 days selected" pill, and nothing is committed until Apply.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Two adjacent months in a popover with a quick-select sidebar, typed start and end chips, a day count and Cancel / Apply.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1, @internationalized/date@^3.12.4, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, motion@^12.43.0

## How it works

1. A controlled React Aria `DialogTrigger` wraps an `AriaButton` trigger and a `Popover` (`offset={4}`, `placement="bottom end"`, `isNonModal`). Its `onOpenChange` first asks `useTriggerToggle` whether to allow the change, then on open resets the draft to the committed range. `useDismissOnOutsidePress` restores the outside-click close that `isNonModal` turns off.
2. State is two ranges: `committedValue` (controlled `value`, or internal state seeded from `defaultValue`) and `pendingValue`, which the `RangeCalendar`, the presets and the chips all edit. Apply calls `commit(pendingValue)` (internal state when uncontrolled, then `onChange`) and the Dialog render prop's `close()`; Cancel resets the draft and closes.
3. `RangeCalendar` gets `visibleDuration={{ months: 2 }}` and renders two shared `MonthPanel`s in a `flex gap-2` row: `offset={0}` with only the previous chevron, `offset={1}` with only the next one. The inner chevron slots render as invisible 16px spacers, because two adjacent months share one navigation state.
4. The 118px `QuickSelect` column lists eight presets built in a `useMemo` from `today(getLocalTimeZone())`: Today, Yesterday, Last week (the 7 days before today), This month, Last month, This year, Last year and All time (10 years back). A preset whose start and end match the draft with `isSameDay` gets `bg-background-tertiary-default`.
5. The footer's `AnimatePresence` mounts the summary once a draft exists, sliding from `y: -12` over 0.25s on `[0.34, 1.2, 0.64, 1]`. Two `DateChipInput`s edit start and end as DD/MM/YYYY; a typed start after the end moves the end to it, and a typed end before the start moves the start. The pill counts days inclusively: `Math.round((end - start) / 86_400_000) + 1` using local-time `Date`s.
6. Day cells come from the shared `DayCell`: a band layer and an edge-pill layer that only change opacity (100ms), with the band reaching 6px into the 12px cell gaps so a range across both months reads as one strip broken only at week edges.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `ms per day + round = 86_400_000, Math.round(...) + 1`
  Local-time dates across a DST change are 23 or 25 hours apart; rounding absorbs that. The +1 makes the count inclusive, so a one-day range says "1 day selected", not 0.
- `quick-select width = w-[118px], gap-1.5`
  Fits the longest preset label ("Last month") at body-medium with 8px padding, so the months beside it never shift as the active preset changes.
- `popover offset / placement = 4px, bottom end`
  The popover is wider than most triggers (sidebar plus two 326px months), so aligning its end edge to the trigger keeps it opening inward from a right-hand toolbar slot.
- `summary entrance = y -12 → 0, 0.25s, ease [0.34, 1.2, 0.64, 1]`
  A small overshoot so the chips settle in under the months. The same values as the single Date Picker, so the two read as one family.
- `All time preset = today minus 10 years`
  A bounded stand-in for "everything". An unbounded start would leave the calendar no month to show.

## API

```ts
interface DateRangeValue { start: CalendarDate; end: CalendarDate }
function DateRangePicker(props: { value?: DateRangeValue | null; defaultValue?: DateRangeValue | null; onChange?: (value: DateRangeValue | null) => void; isDisabled?: boolean; className?: string; popoverClassName?: string; "aria-label"?: string; placeholder?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `value: DateRangeValue | null`
  Controlled committed range of `CalendarDate`s.
- `defaultValue: DateRangeValue | null` — default `null`
  Initial range when uncontrolled.
- `onChange: (value: DateRangeValue | null) => void`
  Fires once on Apply.
- `isDisabled: boolean`
  Disables the trigger.
- `placeholder: string` — default `"Select date range"`
  Trigger text when no range is committed.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Date range"`
  Labels the dialog and the range calendar.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the trigger button.
- `popoverClassName: string`
  Extra classes for the portalled popover surface.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function DateRangePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onChange,
  isDisabled,
  className,
  popoverClassName: calendarClassName,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel = "Date range",
  placeholder = "Select date range",
}: DateRangePickerProps) {
  const localize = useTemplateCopy();
  const { locale } = useLocale();
  const isControlled = value !== undefined;
  const [internalValue, setInternalValue] = useState<DateRangeValue | null>(defaultValue);
  const committedValue = isControlled ? (value ?? null) : internalValue;

  const [pendingValue, setPendingValue] = useState<DateRangeValue | null>(committedValue);

  const commit = (next: DateRangeValue | null) => {
    if (!isControlled) setInternalValue(next);
    onChange?.(next);
  };

  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const popoverRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
  useDismissOnOutsidePress(isOpen, () => setIsOpen(false), [triggerRef, popoverRef]);
  // Pressing the trigger while open closes the popover instead of reopening
  const allowOpenChange = useTriggerToggle(isOpen, triggerRef);

  return localize((
    <DialogTrigger
      isOpen={isOpen}
      onOpenChange={(open) => {
        if (!allowOpenChange(open)) return;
        if (open) setPendingValue(committedValue);
        setIsOpen(open);
      }}
    >
      <AriaButton ref={triggerRef} isDisabled={isDisabled} className={cx(triggerButtonClassName, className)}>
        <RiCalendarLine className="size-5 shrink-0 text-foreground-icon-primary" aria-hidden />
        <span className="flex items-center justify-center whitespace-nowrap px-1 text-body-medium text-text-primary">
          {committedValue ? `${formatTriggerDate(committedValue.start, locale)} - ${formatTriggerDate(committedValue.end, locale)}` : placeholder}
        </span>
      </AriaButton>
      <Popover ref={popoverRef} offset={4} placement="bottom end" isNonModal className={cx(popoverClassName, calendarClassName)}>
        <Dialog aria-label={ariaLabel} className="outline-none">
          {({ close }) => (
            <RangeCalendar
              aria-label={ariaLabel}
              visibleDuration={{ months: 2 }}
              value={pendingValue}
              onChange={setPendingValue}
            >
              <div className="flex gap-3">
                <div className="pt-4 ps-4">
                  <QuickSelect
                    value={pendingValue}
                    onSelect={(range) => setPendingValue(range)}
                  />
                </div>
                <div className="flex flex-col pt-2 pe-2 pb-3">
                  <div className="flex gap-2">
                    <MonthPanel offset={0} showPrev />
                    <MonthPanel offset={1} showNext />
                  </div>
                  <Footer
                    value={pendingValue}
                    onChange={setPendingValue}
                    onCancel={() => {
                      setPendingValue(committedValue);
                      close();
                    }}
                    onApply={() => {
                      commit(pendingValue);
                      close();
                    }}
                  />
                </div>
              </div>
            </RangeCalendar>
          )}
        </Dialog>
      </Popover>
    </DialogTrigger>
  ));
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The outside-press and trigger-toggle hooks add document `pointerdown` listeners only while open and remove them on close and unmount. `AnimatePresence` handles the footer's exit. No timers.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing branches on `prefers-reduced-motion`. The popover's 150ms fade, scale and 2px blur and the footer's 12px drop still play; day selection only fades opacity. Wrap the app in Motion's `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">` to drop the footer's transform.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not remove `useTriggerToggle`. With `isNonModal`, pressing the trigger while open makes React Aria fire `onOpenChange(false)` and then `onOpenChange(true)` in the same press, so the popover would never close from its trigger.
- Do not wire the two inner chevrons. The months are always adjacent, so there is one paging state; four buttons would give two that do the same thing as the outer pair.
- Do not count days as `end.day - start.day` or with a floor. That breaks across months and across DST changes; subtract real dates, round, and add one.
- Do not hoist the presets to module scope. They are built from `today()` when the popover renders, so a module-level list would freeze "today" at import time and differ between server and client.
- Do not commit on every calendar click. The draft only becomes the value on Apply, and Cancel must restore the trigger's range.

## Notes

- `popoverClassName` adds classes to the portalled surface (for a locale-specific font, for example), since the popover renders outside the trigger's tree.
- Strings run through `useTemplateCopy`, so preset labels, "days selected", Cancel and Apply can be translated by a `TemplateCopyProvider`.
- The popover is wide (sidebar plus two months, about 810px). On a phone-width viewport the popover is capped at `calc(100vw - 2rem)` and scrolls sideways inside, so Apply stays reachable; for narrow layouts, `DateRangeCalendar` with `visibleMonths={1}` fits without scrolling.

## Definition of done

The trigger reads "Mar 2, 2026 - Mar 15, 2026" for that committed range. Clicking it opens a popover with eight presets on the left and two consecutive months; clicking a start and then an end day draws a single band (crossing into the second month if needed) and the footer shows both dates as DD/MM/YYYY chips and "N days selected" counted inclusively. Clicking "This month" selects today's month and highlights the preset. Pressing the trigger again closes the popover. Apply updates the trigger and fires `onChange` once; Cancel or an outside click leaves it unchanged.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Date Range Stepper

The small period switcher from BoardUI's dashboard card headers: a 32px white pill with a left chevron, a centred "Jun 29 – Jul 5" (or "July") label and a right chevron. It steps whole weeks or months of `CalendarDate`s from @internationalized/date, controlled or uncontrolled, and greys out an arrow once the next step would leave `minValue` / `maxValue`. The pure helpers that compute and format a period are exported for the card that shows the data.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A bordered pill with prev/next chevrons that steps a week or month period, with min/max bounds and a label that slides in.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @internationalized/date@^3.12.4, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The current period is derived on every render from an anchor date (`value`, or internal state seeded from `defaultValue`): `getStepperRange` returns `startOfWeek`/`endOfWeek` (with `weekStartsOn`, Monday by default) or `startOfMonth`/`endOfMonth`. `shiftStepperRange` moves the period start by `{ weeks: ±1 }` or `{ months: ±1 }` and re-derives the range, giving the previous and next periods.
2. Bounds: Previous is allowed while `prev.end >= minValue`, Next while `next.start <= maxValue` (`CalendarDate.compare`). A blocked arrow keeps focus and gets `aria-disabled` (styled with `aria-disabled:` variants) instead of `disabled`, so stepping to the edge never drops keyboard focus to the body; the click handler ignores it.
3. A step updates internal state only when uncontrolled and always calls `onChange(start, range)`. The group handles ArrowLeft/PageUp and ArrowRight/PageDown as steps and Home as a jump back to the first period shown.
4. The label is formatted with `DateFormatter` (en-US by default) on `date.toDate("UTC")` with `timeZone: "UTC"`: week as two "MMM d" parts joined with a plain " – ", month as the long month name. With `yearDisplay="auto"` the year is added only when the period leaves the year of the first period shown. A visually hidden `aria-live="polite"` span announces the full range with year; the visible label is aria-hidden.
5. The slide direction is derived during render by comparing the new period start (ISO string) with the last one shown, so it also follows a controlled value. The label span is keyed by unit and start, so it remounts; Tailwind `starting:translate-x-2 starting:opacity-0` (or `-translate-x-2` going back) with a 200ms opacity/translate transition slides the new label in from the side it came from. The first render has direction 0 and no starting style, so nothing animates on load.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `pill height = 32px (h-8) with 28px (size-7) arrow buttons`
  Matches the header row of the medical and dashboard cards; the arrows fit inside the 1px border.
- `label min width = 6.75rem week, 5.5rem month`
  Keeps the pill from jumping between "Jun 29 – Jul 5" and "Jul 6 – Jul 12", and gives "July" the roomy centred look of the reference.
- `slide = 8px (translate-x-2), 200ms ease-out`
  Enough to show the direction of the step without the label leaving its overflow-hidden slot.
- `weekStartsOn = "mon"`
  The reference periods run Monday 29 Jun to Sunday 5 Jul.

## API

```ts
export function DateRangeStepper({ value, defaultValue, onChange, unit = "week", minValue, maxValue, weekStartsOn = "mon", locale = "en-US", yearDisplay = "auto", formatLabel, label = "Date range", isDisabled = false, className }: DateRangeStepperProps): JSX.Element
```

- `value: CalendarDate`
  Controlled: any day inside the shown period.
- `defaultValue: CalendarDate`
  Uncontrolled: any day inside the first period (one of value/defaultValue is required).
- `onChange: (start: CalendarDate, range: DateRangeStepperRange) => void`
  Called with the first day of the new period and the whole period.
- `unit: "week" | "month"` — default `"week"`
  Length of one step.
- `minValue: CalendarDate`
  Earliest day a period may reach.
- `maxValue: CalendarDate`
  Latest day a period may reach.
- `weekStartsOn: DayOfWeek` — default `"mon"`
  First day of a week period.
- `locale: string` — default `"en-US"`
  Locale of the label and announcement.
- `yearDisplay: "auto" | "always" | "never"` — default `"auto"`
  Auto adds the year once the period leaves the first period's year.
- `formatLabel: (range: DateRangeStepperRange, unit: DateRangeStepperUnit) => string`
  Replaces the visible label.
- `label: string` — default `"Date range"`
  Accessible name of the group.
- `isDisabled: boolean` — default `false`
  Blocks both arrows and dims the pill.
- `className: string`
  Classes on the pill.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function DateRangeStepper(props: DateRangeStepperProps) {
  const {
    value,
    defaultValue,
    onChange,
    unit = "week",
    minValue,
    maxValue,
    weekStartsOn = "mon",
    locale = "en-US",
    yearDisplay = "auto",
    formatLabel,
    label = "Date range",
    isDisabled = false,
    className,
  } = props;

  // The union type guarantees one of the two is set.
  const seed = (value ?? defaultValue) as CalendarDate;
  const [internal, setInternal] = useState<CalendarDate>(seed);
  // The first period shown: Home returns to it and "auto" years compare to it.
  const [home] = useState<CalendarDate>(seed);

  const anchor = value ?? internal;
  const range = getStepperRange(anchor, unit, locale, weekStartsOn);
  const prev = shiftStepperRange(anchor, unit, -1, locale, weekStartsOn);
  const next = shiftStepperRange(anchor, unit, 1, locale, weekStartsOn);
  const canPrev = !isDisabled && (!minValue || prev.end.compare(minValue) >= 0);
  const canNext = !isDisabled && (!maxValue || next.start.compare(maxValue) <= 0);

  // Slide direction is derived from the change of period start, so it also
  // follows a controlled value set from outside. ISO date strings sort in
  // date order, so a string compare is enough.
  const startKey = range.start.toString();
  const [shownKey, setShownKey] = useState(startKey);
  const [direction, setDirection] = useState<-1 | 0 | 1>(0);
  if (shownKey !== startKey) {
    setShownKey(startKey);
    setDirection(startKey > shownKey ? 1 : -1);
  }

  const go = (target: DateRangeStepperRange) => {
    if (!isControlled(value)) setInternal(target.start);
    onChange?.(target.start, target);
  };
  const step = (offset: -1 | 1) => {
    if (offset < 0 ? !canPrev : !canNext) return;
    go(offset < 0 ? prev : next);
  };

  const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (event.key === "ArrowLeft" || event.key === "PageUp") step(-1);
    else if (event.key === "ArrowRight" || event.key === "PageDown") step(1);
    else if (event.key === "Home" && !isDisabled) {
      const target = getStepperRange(home, unit, locale, weekStartsOn);
      if (target.start.compare(range.start) !== 0) go(target);
    } else return;
    event.preventDefault();
  };

  const showYear =
    yearDisplay === "always" ||
    (yearDisplay === "auto" && (range.start.year !== home.year || range.end.year !== home.year));
  const text = formatLabel ? formatLabel(range, unit) : formatStepperRange(range, unit, locale, showYear);
  const noun = unit === "month" ? "month" : "week";

  return (
    <div
      role="group"
      aria-label={label}
      aria-disabled={isDisabled || undefined}
      onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
      data-unit={unit}
      className={cx(
        "inline-flex h-8 shrink-0 items-center rounded-lg border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default px-0.5 shadow-2xs",
        isDisabled && "opacity-60",
        className,
      )}
    >
      <button
        type="button"
        className={arrowClass}
        aria-label={`Previous ${noun}`}
        aria-disabled={!canPrev || undefined}
        onClick={() => step(-1)}
      >
        <RiArrowLeftSLine className="size-4" aria-hidden />
      </button>
      <span
        aria-hidden
        className={cx(
          "flex justify-center overflow-hidden px-1",
          unit === "month" ? "min-w-[5.5rem]" : "min-w-[6.75rem]",
        )}
      >
        <span
          key={`${unit}:${startKey}`}
          data-stepper-label=""
          className={cx(
            "inline-block text-body-medium whitespace-nowrap text-text-primary tabular-nums",
            "transition-[opacity,translate] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
            direction === 1 && "starting:translate-x-2 starting:opacity-0",
            direction === -1 && "starting:-translate-x-2 starting:opacity-0",
          )}
        >
          {text}
        </span>
      </span>
      <span className="sr-only" aria-live="polite">
        {announceRange(range, unit, locale)}
      </span>
      <button
        type="button"
        className={arrowClass}
        aria-label={`Next ${noun}`}
        aria-disabled={!canNext || undefined}
        onClick={() => step(1)}
      >
        <RiArrowRightSLine className="size-4" aria-hidden />
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers, listeners or observers: the slide is a CSS @starting-style transition on a remounted span.

**Reduced motion.** The label slide uses motion-reduce:transition-none, so the new label appears in place without sliding or fading.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not use `Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatRange` for the label: its spacing around the dash differs between ICU builds (Node vs browser) and causes a hydration mismatch. Format start and end separately and join them.
- Do not format a `CalendarDate` in the viewer's timezone: convert with `toDate("UTC")` and format with `timeZone: "UTC"`, or the label can show the previous day west of UTC.
- Do not set `disabled` on an arrow that reached a bound while it has focus: the focus falls to the body. Use `aria-disabled` and ignore the click.
- Do not default the value to today during render: server and browser can disagree on the date. The props type requires `value` or `defaultValue`.

## Notes

- Exports `getStepperRange`, `shiftStepperRange` and `formatStepperRange` so a card can compute the same period for its data.
- Chevrons are Remix `RiArrowLeftSLine` / `RiArrowRightSLine` at 16px.
- The demo pairs a week stepper bounded to Jun 1 – Jul 12, 2026 over a seeded steps bar chart with a month stepper over an activity calendar.

## Definition of done

Starting at Jun 29 2026 the week pill reads "Jun 29 – Jul 5"; Next shows "Jul 6 – Jul 12" and calls onChange with 2026-07-06; with maxValue Jul 12 the Next arrow then has aria-disabled="true" and clicking it changes nothing. A month pill at July reads "July", and stepping back past January reads "December 2025".

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Delayed-Unmount Loader

An inverted full-cover loading panel that fades out on a plain CSS transition. The mechanism is the timing of its own removal: when `loading` goes false the element sets `data-exit` and starts a 600ms fade, and a matching 600ms timeout is what finally unmounts it. Nothing is animated in JavaScript — one boolean, one timeout, one transition.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A loading overlay that stays mounted 600ms past the signal so its fade can actually play before it leaves.

- Category: transition
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Internal `mounted` state starts true so the overlay is present in the very first paint, before any effect has run. Deriving visibility from the `loading` prop alone is what makes the exit impossible to animate.
2. When `loading` flips false, `data-exit="true"` lands on the element and the CSS rule `.k-dul[data-exit="true"] { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none }` takes over the transition declared on `.k-dul`.
3. In the same effect a `setTimeout(() => setMounted(false), exitMs)` is armed. The timeout and the transition read the same `exitMs`, passed to CSS as the custom property `--k-dul-exit`, so they cannot drift apart.
4. If `loading` goes true again — a second route, a refetch — the effect clears the pending timeout and re-arms the overlay. Because the exit is a CSS transition rather than a keyframe, an interruption mid-fade reverses from wherever the opacity had got to instead of jumping to 1.
5. The panel is drawn with the foreground colour as its background and the background colour as its text, so the reveal reads as a tonal inversion rather than a curtain, and a single pulsing dot between two brackets is the only moving part.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `exitMs = 600`
  Drives both the CSS transition and the unmount timeout. Under ~350ms a full-bleed tonal flip reads as a flicker; over ~800ms the page is legible behind a veil that is still technically covering it. Whatever value you pick, the timeout must be >= the transition or the node disappears mid-fade.
- `pulse period = 1s`
  One cycle per second is close to a resting heart rate and reads as "alive, waiting". Faster reads as urgency and makes a slow load feel worse than it is.
- `pulse scale range = 0.86 -> 1`
  Small enough that the dot never appears to change its typographic size between the brackets; a larger range makes the bracket pair look mis-set.

## API

```ts
function DelayedUnmountLoader(props: { loading: boolean; exitMs?: number; label?: string; hint?: string; position?: 'fixed' | 'absolute'; className?: string }): JSX.Element | null
```

- `loading: boolean`
  While true the overlay is opaque. False starts the reveal.
- `exitMs: number` — default `600`
  Fade length and unmount delay. One number drives both.
- `label: string` — default `'Loading experience'`
  Left-hand text.
- `hint: string` — default `'it won’t be long'`
  Right-hand text.
- `position: 'fixed' | 'absolute'` — default `'fixed'`
  Viewport cover, or cover of the nearest positioned ancestor.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the overlay.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function DelayedUnmountLoader({
  loading,
  exitMs = 600,
  label = 'Loading experience',
  hint = 'it won’t be long',
  position = 'fixed',
  className,
}: DelayedUnmountLoaderProps) {
  // Starts true so the overlay is in the very first paint. Deriving it from
  // `loading` alone is what makes the exit un-animatable.
  const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(true);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (loading) {
      // A second load (route change, refetch) re-arms the overlay.
      setMounted(true);
      return;
    }
    const t = setTimeout(() => setMounted(false), exitMs);
    return () => clearTimeout(t);
  }, [loading, exitMs]);

  if (!mounted && !loading) return null;

  return (
    <div
      // `data-exit` is the only thing that changes on the element. The
      // transition is declarative, so an interrupted reveal (loading goes
      // true again mid-fade) reverses from wherever it got to instead of
      // jumping.
      data-exit={!loading}
      aria-hidden={!loading}
      className={cn(
        'k-dul z-50 flex items-center justify-center',
        // Inverted: the loader is the page's negative, so the reveal reads as
        // a tonal flip rather than a curtain being pulled aside.
        'bg-fg text-bg',
        position === 'fixed' ? 'fixed inset-0' : 'absolute inset-0',
        className,
      )}
      style={{ ['--k-dul-exit' as string]: `${exitMs}ms` }}
    >
      <style>{CSS}</style>
      <div className="flex w-full items-center justify-between gap-2 px-4">
        <p className="w-1/3 font-mono text-[0.6875rem] uppercase leading-none tracking-[0.08em]">
          {label}
        </p>
        <p className="flex w-1/3 justify-center font-mono text-2xl leading-none tracking-[0.1em]">
          <span aria-hidden>[</span>
          <span className="k-dul-dot inline-block px-[0.15em]" aria-hidden>
            &middot;
          </span>
          <span aria-hidden>]</span>
        </p>
        <p className="w-1/3 text-right font-mono text-[0.6875rem] uppercase leading-none tracking-[0.08em]">
          {hint}
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The single timeout is cleared in the effect's cleanup, so a route change or an unmount during the fade cannot call `setMounted` on a component React has already released.

**Reduced motion.** The dot stops pulsing and sits at a fixed opacity, and the fade collapses to 1ms so the overlay simply disappears. The unmount delay is unchanged, and the exiting overlay is `pointer-events: none` throughout, so nothing is blocked while it waits.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Rendering `{loading && <Loader />}`. React removes the node on the same commit that flips the flag, so the transition has no element to run on and the loader disappears on a cut. The component owns its own removal.
- Using a keyframe animation with `forwards` for the exit. Interrupt it by starting a second load and it snaps to the start; a transition on a class/attribute is interruptible in both directions for free.
- Letting the timeout and the transition duration live in different files. They drift, and either the loader is cut off mid-fade or a fully transparent overlay sits on top of the page eating clicks. One `exitMs` feeds both, and the CSS reads it from a custom property.
- Forgetting `pointer-events: none` in the exit state. For the whole fade the page is visible but not clickable, which reads as the site having frozen just as it finished loading.
- Not clearing the timeout when `loading` goes true again. The stale timer unmounts the re-armed overlay mid-load and the page flashes through underneath.
- Leaving the pulse running under `prefers-reduced-motion`. An indefinitely looping animation is exactly what that preference exists to stop; the media query drops it to a static dot.

## Notes

- App Router wiring: render this in `app/layout.tsx` above `{children}` and drive `loading` from your own readiness state — `document.fonts.ready`, a data promise, or a route-change flag from `usePathname()`. For a first-load preloader that must never hang, use `safe-preloader` instead: this component trusts whoever owns the boolean.
- `position="absolute"` covers the nearest positioned ancestor instead of the viewport, which is what makes it embeddable in a card or a preview frame.
- The delayed-unmount pattern generalises: any exit animation on a conditionally rendered node needs the node to outlive the condition by at least the animation duration.

## Definition of done

Load the page and the inverted panel is in the first paint with its dot pulsing. When loading ends the panel fades over 600ms and the node is gone from the DOM immediately afterwards — not before. Trigger a second load mid-fade and the panel returns from its current opacity rather than snapping to full.

# Build: Depth Fade And Travelling Pulse

A lattice of dots bent around a shallow arc and lit by a pulse that travels across it. Depth is faked entirely from model-space z, which drives alpha and point size at the same time, so the arc reads as curved with no depth buffer and no perspective camera. The pulse is a cosine whose phase varies per column, and its crest also pushes dots toward the viewer, so the two techniques compound: the wave arrives as a moving band of brighter, larger dots.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A dot lattice on an arc: z drives alpha and point size together, and a per-column phase sweeps the pulse across the field.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1

## How it works

1. Columns are placed by angle across `arcSpan`, then z is renormalised so the centre column lands at exactly `+arcDepth` and both edges at `-arcDepth`, independent of the span. Without that renormalisation the usable z range shrinks with the span and the depth cue silently weakens whenever the arc is flattened.
2. The depth cue is `depthT = clamp((z + 0.55) / 1.1, 0, 1)`, which drives alpha from 0.25 to 1.0 *and* point size from 0.65 to 1.0. Both together are the point: alpha alone reads as a grey copy of the near dots, size alone reads as a resolution change, and only the pair reads as distance.
3. The pulse is `raw = 0.65 + 0.35 * cos(2π * (uElapsed / pulseCycle - phase))`, with `phase = columnT * waveTurns + rowT * 0.12` baked into an attribute. Subtracting the phase inside the cosine is what makes the crest move *along* the lattice rather than the whole field breathing in unison.
4. The crest, renormalised to 0..1, is added to z as `p.z += crest * uWaveDepth`, so the wave feeds the depth cue. A dot at the crest is pushed nearer, and the depth fade then brightens and enlarges it — one displacement drives three visible changes.
5. The pulse ramps in over the first second (`clamp(uElapsed / 1.0, 0, 1)`), so the first frame does not land on an arbitrary point of the cosine and flash. Yaw is `sin(elapsed * yawSpeed * 2π) * yawAmplitude` degrees, applied in the shader after the wave so the lattice rocks through its own depth range.
6. `gl_PointSize` is clamped to a 2px floor and alpha is compensated by `unclamped² / clamped²`, so the field keeps the same apparent density at DPR 1 and DPR 2 instead of getting heavier on retina.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `PULSE_BASE / PULSE_SWING = 0.65 / 0.35`
  The pulse rides between 0.30 and 1.00 of nominal size and alpha. A trough at 0 would make dots vanish entirely and the lattice would look like it is dropping frames rather than breathing.
- `DEFAULT_CYCLE / pulseCycle = 3.0 seconds`
  Under ~2s the crest outruns the eye following it across the lattice; over ~5s it stops reading as a wave and becomes an idle shimmer.
- `INTRO_SECONDS = 1.0`
  Ramps the pulse amplitude from 0. Without it the first rendered frame samples the cosine at an arbitrary phase and the whole field flashes on mount.
- `DEPTH_HALF_RANGE = 0.55`
  The arc spans ±0.34 and the wave adds up to +0.18, so normalising over ±0.55 leaves headroom at both ends — no dot sits at exactly 0 or 1 and the falloff never visibly clips.
- `DEPTH_MIN_SIZE / DEPTH_MAX_SIZE = 0.65 / 1.0`
  Far dots at 65% of near ones. Paired with the 0.25→1.0 alpha ramp; either cue on its own is ambiguous, and this ratio is the smallest that still reads as depth at preview-card sizes.
- `waveTurns = 1.4`
  Wavelengths visible across the lattice at any instant. At 1 the crest and trough sit at opposite edges and it reads as a tilt; past ~2.5 the bands are too narrow to track and the field just shimmers.
- `ROW_PHASE_LEAN = 0.12`
  Small row contribution to the phase, so the crest leans instead of arriving as a perfectly vertical bar. Bigger than ~0.3 and the wave starts reading as diagonal stripes.
- `yawAmplitude / yawSpeed = 16 degrees / 0.25 Hz`
  The lattice rocks rather than spins. A full rotation would carry columns through the arc's entire depth range and destroy the near/far reading the crest depends on.
- `crest tint threshold = smoothstep(0.65, 1.0, crest)`
  Only the top third of the crest picks up `crestColor`. Tinting the whole cosine spreads the accent across the field and the wave stops having a location.

## API

```ts
function DepthPulseTravellingWave(props: { columns?: number; rows?: number; arcSpan?: number; arcDepth?: number; fieldHeight?: number; pulseCycle?: number; waveTurns?: number; waveDepth?: number; yawAmplitude?: number; yawSpeed?: number; dotScale?: number; viewScale?: number; opacity?: number; color?: string; crestColor?: string; seed?: number | string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `columns: number` — default `110`
  Columns across the arc.
- `rows: number` — default `44`
  Rows down each column.
- `arcSpan: number` — default `110`
  Arc the lattice is bent around, in degrees.
- `arcDepth: number` — default `0.34`
  Half-depth of the arc in model units — how far the edges recede.
- `fieldHeight: number` — default `1.1`
  Lattice height in model units.
- `pulseCycle: number` — default `3`
  Seconds per pulse.
- `waveTurns: number` — default `1.4`
  Wavelengths visible across the lattice at any instant.
- `waveDepth: number` — default `0.18`
  How far a crest pushes a dot toward the viewer, in model units.
- `yawAmplitude: number` — default `16`
  Peak yaw of the whole lattice, in degrees.
- `yawSpeed: number` — default `0.25`
  Yaw oscillations per second.
- `dotScale: number` — default `1`
  Dot radius multiplier in CSS pixels.
- `viewScale: number` — default `0.46`
  Model-to-pixel scale as a fraction of the container short side.
- `opacity: number` — default `1`
  Multiplier applied to every dot.
- `color: string` — default `'#6f757e'`
  Base dot colour.

  Colour mixed in at the top of the crest.

  Seeds the sub-cell jitter for a stable, hydration-safe lattice.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the host element via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function DepthPulseTravellingWave({
  columns = 110,
  rows = 44,
  arcSpan = 110,
  arcDepth = 0.34,
  fieldHeight = 1.1,
  pulseCycle = 3,
  waveTurns = 1.4,
  waveDepth = 0.18,
  yawAmplitude = 16,
  yawSpeed = 0.25,
  dotScale = 1,
  viewScale = 0.46,
  opacity = 1,
  color = '#6f757e',
  crestColor = '#ffffff',
  seed = 'depth-pulse-travelling-wave',
  className,
}: DepthPulseTravellingWaveProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);
  const [unsupported, setUnsupported] = useState(false);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const size = useRef({ width, height });
  size.current = { width, height };

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const ready = width > 0 && height > 0;

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready) return;

    if (!hasWebGL()) {
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }

    let renderer: THREE.WebGLRenderer;
    try {
      renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: false, alpha: true });
    } catch {
      // A context can still be refused between the probe and the construction —
      // the tab may have hit the browser's live-context ceiling in between. three
      // throws rather than returning null, and an uncaught throw here takes the
      // page with it.
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }
    renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio());
    renderer.setClearAlpha(0);

    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const camera = new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0.1, 10);
    camera.position.z = 1;

    const rng = createRng(seed);

    const total = columns * rows;
    const positions = new Float32Array(total * 3);
    const wave = new Float32Array(total * 2);

    /* ------------------------------------------------------------------
       The arc. Columns are placed by angle, then z is renormalised so the
       centre column sits at +arcDepth and the two edges at -arcDepth
       exactly. Without the renormalisation the usable z range depends on
       arcSpan, and the depth fade would get weaker every time the arc was
       flattened — the cue would silently stop working at shallow spans.
       ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
    const halfSpan = (arcSpan * Math.PI) / 360;
    const cosEdge = Math.cos(halfSpan);
    // Guard the degenerate case: a 0 degree span has no depth to normalise.
    const depthSpan = Math.max(1e-4, 1 - cosEdge);

    let cursor = 0;
    for (let c = 0; c < columns; c += 1) {
      const colT = columns === 1 ? 0.5 : c / (columns - 1);
      const angle = (colT - 0.5) * 2 * halfSpan;
      const x = Math.sin(angle);
      const z = ((Math.cos(angle) - cosEdge) / depthSpan) * 2 * arcDepth - arcDepth;

      for (let r = 0; r < rows; r += 1) {
        const rowT = rows === 1 ? 0.5 : r / (rows - 1);
        // Sub-cell jitter, seeded. A perfect lattice moirés against the pixel
        // grid and shows banding as the field yaws.
        const jx = (rng() - 0.5) * (1 / columns) * 0.9;
        const jy = (rng() - 0.5) * (1 / rows) * 0.9;

        positions[cursor * 3] = x + jx;
        positions[cursor * 3 + 1] = (rowT - 0.5 + jy) * fieldHeight;
        positions[cursor * 3 + 2] = z;

        // Phase is what makes it travel. Constant phase across the lattice
        // would give a field that breathes in unison.
        wave[cursor * 2] = colT * waveTurns + rowT * ROW_PHASE_LEAN;
        wave[cursor * 2 + 1] = rng() - 0.5;
        cursor += 1;
      }
    }

    const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
    geometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(positions, 3));
    geometry.setAttribute('aWave', new THREE.BufferAttribute(wave, 2));

    const uniforms: Uniforms = {
      uElapsed: { value: 0 },
      uViewScale: { value: 1 },
      uPixelRatio: { value: renderer.getPixelRatio() },
      uDotScale: { value: dotScale },
      uOpacity: { value: opacity },
      uPulseCycle: { value: pulseCycle },
      uWaveDepth: { value: waveDepth },
      uYaw: { value: 0 },
      uColor: { value: new THREE.Color(color) },
      uCrestColor: { value: new THREE.Color(crestColor) },
    };

    const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader: DEPTH_PULSE_WAVE_VERT,
      fragmentShader: DEPTH_PULSE_WAVE_FRAG,
      uniforms,
      transparent: true,
      // Every dot is projected at z = 0; the depth cue is alpha and size, not
      // the depth buffer. Leaving these on would let near dots reject far ones
      // that were rasterised first and punch holes through the lattice.
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
    });

    const points = new THREE.Points(geometry, material);
    // Positions are unit-scale around the origin and the real placement happens
    // in the shader, so three's bounding sphere does not describe what is on
    // screen and culling against it would blank the field at some sizes.
    points.frustumCulled = false;
    scene.add(points);

    el.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
    renderer.domElement.style.display = 'block';
    renderer.domElement.style.width = '100%';
    renderer.domElement.style.height = '100%';

    const resize = (w: number, h: number) => {
      renderer.setSize(w, h, false);
      camera.left = -w / 2;
      camera.right = w / 2;
      camera.top = h / 2;
      camera.bottom = -h / 2;
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
      uniforms.uViewScale.value = Math.min(w, h) * viewScale;
      uniforms.uPixelRatio.value = renderer.getPixelRatio();
    };

    const draw = (elapsed: number) => {
      uniforms.uElapsed.value = elapsed;
      // Yaw oscillates rather than spins. A full rotation would carry columns
      // through the arc's own depth range and the travelling crest would stop
      // being readable as a wave.
      uniforms.uYaw.value = Math.sin(elapsed * yawSpeed * Math.PI * 2) * yawAmplitude;
      renderer.render(scene, camera);
    };

    resize(size.current.width, size.current.height);
    stage.current = { resize, draw };
    draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      disposeObject(scene);
      material.dispose();
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      renderer.domElement.remove();
    };
  }, [
    ready,
    columns,
    rows,
    arcSpan,
    arcDepth,
    fieldHeight,
    pulseCycle,
    waveTurns,
    waveDepth,
    yawAmplitude,
    yawSpeed,
    dotScale,
    viewScale,
    opacity,
    color,
    crestColor,
    seed,
  ]);

  useEffect(() => {
    stage.current?.resize(width, height);
    if (reduced) stage.current?.draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);
  }, [width, height, reduced]);

  useRaf((_dt, elapsed) => stage.current?.draw(elapsed), ready && !reduced && !unsupported);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nulls the stage ref so a queued frame cannot touch a dead renderer, disposes the geometry through `disposeObject(scene)`, disposes the material, calls `disposeRenderer` for `dispose` + `forceContextLoss` + a zeroed backing store, and removes the canvas. `useRaf` unsubscribes on unmount, so a StrictMode double-invoke leaves no orphaned context.

**Reduced motion.** No frame loop is opened. A single frame is drawn at `uElapsed = 1.9` — past the one-second amplitude ramp, and a third of the way through the default cycle, so the crest sits inside the lattice rather than off its edge. Both the depth falloff and the wave band are visible in that still; neither advances.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Giving every dot the same phase. The field then pulses in unison, which reads as a loading state rather than as something moving through the lattice — the per-column phase offset *is* the effect.
- Fading alpha with depth but leaving point size constant. The far edge of the arc becomes a grey copy of the near edge instead of receding, because size is the cue the eye actually uses for distance at these scales.
- Leaving `depthTest` on. Every dot is projected at z = 0, so whichever dot rasterises first wins the pixel and the lattice develops holes wherever it folds back on itself.
- Starting the pulse at full amplitude. The first frame samples the cosine at whatever phase `elapsed` happens to be, and the field flashes on mount — hence the one-second amplitude ramp.
- Placing columns by angle without renormalising z. The depth range then scales with `cos(arcSpan/2)`, so flattening the arc quietly kills the depth fade and the component looks broken at shallow spans while working at wide ones.
- A perfectly regular lattice. It moirés against the pixel grid and shows banding as the field yaws; the seeded sub-cell jitter costs nothing and removes it.
- Rebuilding the buffer on resize. Model space is size-independent — only `uViewScale` and `uPixelRatio` change, so a container reflow costs two uniform writes rather than a dropped GL context.

## Notes

- Dot count is `columns * rows`, 4840 at the defaults, in one draw call with one attribute beyond position.
- The wave is purely a function of `uElapsed` and a baked per-dot phase, so there is no simulation state and no drift — pausing and resuming lands exactly where the clock says it should.

## Definition of done

A curved lattice of dots is visibly dimmer and smaller toward its left and right edges than at its centre. A band of brighter, larger dots sweeps repeatedly across the field, roughly once every three seconds, rather than the whole field brightening at once. The lattice rocks gently side to side. Nothing flashes on mount. Resize the container and the field rescales without a flicker or a dropped context. With reduced motion it holds a single frame showing both the depth falloff and the crest.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
