# Build: Device Preview Frame

A rounded app-window frame (three chrome dots, a lock-and-address pill, a refresh glyph) around a screen that shows real content laid out at a device width: 1280px for desktop, 768 for tablet, 375 for mobile, scaled down to fit the space. A segmented Desktop / Tablet / Mobile toggle above it narrows or widens the frame, and the content reflows continuously while it does, like dragging a window edge. Because the screen is a size container named `frame`, children respond with `@…/frame:` container queries.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Browser-window frame that lays any content out at a device width and scales it in; a Desktop/Tablet/Mobile toggle resizes it live.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. One virtual width `p` drives the whole fit. With `available` the measured row width, the scale is `s = min(1, (available − 16) / p)`; the frame is set to `p · s + 16` px wide (16 = frame border, padding and screen border), the content box to `p` px wide and `height / s` px tall, with `scale: s` from its top-left corner. Content therefore always fills the screen exactly, and a narrow device is shown at up to 1:1 instead of shrinking with the desktop.
2. Device switch: a rAF loop tweens `p` from the old device width to the new one over 560ms with `easeOutQuart` and writes the four styles straight to the DOM each frame, with no React re-render. Frame width and content width derive from the same number, so they cannot drift apart mid-animation the way two independent CSS transitions would when the scale also changes.
3. `available` comes from a ResizeObserver content box on the row that holds the frame: layout pixels, unaffected by transforms, so the fit is correct inside CSS-scaled previews. Resizing the page re-applies the fit at the current `p` (mid-tween included).
4. Toggle: the kit `SegmentedControl` (react-aria ToggleButtonGroup with a sliding thumb). It works controlled (`device` plus `onDeviceChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultDevice`). The root carries `data-device` for styling and tests.
5. The screen scrolls vertically inside the frame (`overflow-y-auto`, `overscroll-contain`), so tall pages can be explored without scrolling the host page.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `device widths = 1280 / 768 / 375 px`
  Common laptop, portrait tablet and phone CSS widths; each hits a different container-query step in typical layouts.
- `tween = 560ms easeOutQuart`
  Most of the reflow happens in the first third, so the result is readable quickly while the frame settles softly.
- `chrome = 16px horizontal`
  Border + 6px padding + screen border; subtracted before computing the scale so content never overflows the screen.
- `max scale = 1`
  Content is never enlarged; a phone width in a wide container is shown at true size.

## API

```ts
function DevicePreviewFrame(props: { children: ReactNode; device?: "desktop" | "tablet" | "mobile"; defaultDevice?: PreviewDevice; onDeviceChange?: (device: PreviewDevice) => void; widths?: Partial<Record<PreviewDevice, number>>; height?: number; url?: string; showToggle?: boolean; toolbar?: ReactNode; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Content laid out at the device width; may use `@…/frame:` container queries.
- `device: "desktop" | "tablet" | "mobile"`
  Controlled device.
- `defaultDevice: PreviewDevice` — default `"desktop"`
  Initial device when uncontrolled.
- `onDeviceChange: (device) => void`
  Called when the toggle changes.
- `widths: Partial<Record<PreviewDevice, number>>`
  Override device CSS widths.
- `height: number` — default `420`
  Visible screen height in px, constant across devices.
- `url: string` — default `"app.example.com"`
  Text in the address pill.
- `showToggle: boolean` — default `true`
  Show the device toggle.
- `toolbar: ReactNode`
  Extra controls beside the toggle.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * One number drives everything: `p`, the virtual width the content is laid out
 * at. For a given p the screen scale is s = min(1, (available - chrome) / p),
 * the frame is p * s + chrome wide and the content box is p wide, scaled by s,
 * and height / s tall so it always fills the screen. Switching device tweens p
 * from the old width to the new one in a rAF loop that writes those styles
 * straight to the DOM, so the page inside reflows continuously like a window
 * being resized and frame and content can never drift apart mid-animation.
 * `available` comes from a ResizeObserver content box: layout pixels, which
 * stay correct inside CSS-scaled previews where rects would not.
 */
function useDeviceFit(targetWidth: number, height: number, reduced: boolean) {
  const measureRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const frameRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const contentRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const fit = useRef({ p: targetWidth, available: 0, raf: 0, height });
  fit.current.height = height;

  const apply = () => {
    const { p, available, height: h } = fit.current;
    const frame = frameRef.current;
    const content = contentRef.current;
    if (!frame || !content || available <= CHROME_X) return;
    const s = Math.min(1, (available - CHROME_X) / p);
    frame.style.width = `${p * s + CHROME_X}px`;
    content.style.width = `${p}px`;
    content.style.height = `${h / s}px`;
    content.style.scale = String(s);
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = measureRef.current;
    if (!el) return;
    const ro = new ResizeObserver(([entry]) => {
      const box = entry?.contentBoxSize?.[0];
      fit.current.available = box ? box.inlineSize : el.clientWidth;
      apply();
    });
    ro.observe(el);
    return () => ro.disconnect();
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    const state = fit.current;
    cancelAnimationFrame(state.raf);
    const from = state.p;
    if (reduced || from === targetWidth || state.available === 0) {
      state.p = targetWidth;
      apply();
      return;
    }
    const start = performance.now();
    const step = (now: number) => {
      const t = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (now - start) / DURATION));
      state.p = from + (targetWidth - from) * easeOutQuart(t);
      apply();
      if (t < 1) state.raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
    };
    state.raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
    return () => cancelAnimationFrame(state.raf);
  }, [targetWidth, reduced, height]);

  return { measureRef, frameRef, contentRef };
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The ResizeObserver disconnects on unmount, and any running animation frame is cancelled when the device changes again or the frame unmounts.

**Reduced motion.** The device switch applies the new width at once (no tween); the kit SegmentedControl drops its thumb slide under the same preference.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Animating the frame width and the content scale as two CSS transitions. When both the virtual width and the scale change, their product is not linear in time and the content overflows or leaves a gap mid-animation. Derive both from one tweened width.
- Fitting with `getBoundingClientRect`: inside a scaled parent it returns scaled sizes and the computed scale compounds. Measure layout boxes.
- Using `md:`/`lg:` media queries inside the previewed content. They follow the real window, not the frame; use `@…/frame:` container queries.
- Using `transform: scale()` on the content while it also has its own transforms; the standalone `scale` property composes cleanly.

## Notes

- The demo previews a small dashboard: sidebar and two-column body at desktop, sidebar gone at tablet, single column at mobile.
- Pass `showToggle={false}` with a controlled `device` to drive it from elsewhere, e.g. the tabs of a template showcase.
- `DEVICE_WIDTHS` is exported, and `widths` overrides any of them.

## Definition of done

At 1280px the frame fills the row and shows the dashboard with a sidebar and a two-column body. Choosing Tablet narrows the frame over about half a second while the content reflows: the sidebar disappears and the body stacks. Mobile narrows it further to a single column at true 375px width. Desktop restores it. At 360px the frame still fits, just smaller. Light and dark both read.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Dither Trail Image Reveal

The image rests dimmed and near-monochrome; dragging across it restores it through a trail of 5px blocks, each block either lit or not according to an 8x8 Bayer threshold. Twenty-four pointer samples live about a second and ride in two flat uniform arrays, so the whole trail is one fullscreen quad with no geometry and no render targets. Samples are spawned on distance travelled by a damped follower rather than per event, and each carries the velocity it was born with, so the reveal smears the way the hand moved.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A dimmed image restored through a trail of Bayer-thresholded blocks that smear in the direction the pointer moved.

- Category: cursor
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1

## How it works

1. The trail is state, not geometry. Twenty-four samples sit in a ring buffer as `vec4(u, v, life, speed)` plus a parallel `vec2` of velocity, uploaded as two flat uniform arrays every frame. The fragment shader loops all twenty-four and takes `max()` of their contributions, so a full trail costs one quad and twenty-four `length()` calls per fragment — no instanced sprites, no ping-pong feedback buffer, nothing to resize.
2. A sample is released when the FOLLOWER has travelled `spawnDistance`, or after `spawnInterval` with no movement. Spawning per pointer event instead clumps on a slow drag — events fire on sub-pixel movement — and leaves gaps on a flick, because the ring is short and a fast sweep can consume all of it between two frames. The time floor is what keeps a stationary hover from decaying to nothing under the cursor.
3. The Bayer threshold is sampled at the CENTRE of the 5px block the fragment sits in, not at the fragment itself. Per-fragment sampling lets the disc edge cut through a block, which puts a soft antialiased boundary on an effect whose entire argument is that it has none. Per-block, a block is wholly lit or wholly absent and the reveal has a dither vocabulary.
4. The 8x8 matrix is built recursively — `bayer4(a) = bayer2(a * 0.5) * 0.25 + bayer2(a)`, and again for 8 — because GLSL ES 1.00 has no integer bitwise operators and the usual derivation is bit-twiddled. Three multiplies and a `fract` produce the same 64-value ordering with no lookup texture and no GLSL3 upgrade.
5. Each sample contributes its stored velocity to a flow vector, weighted by how much it contributed to the mask, and the sum is clamped. The image is then sampled at `uv - flow`, with the flow SNAPPED to the same 5px grid as the dither: a smooth sub-pixel offset is a directional blur laid on top of the picture, while a snapped one moves whole blocks and belongs to the same rendering as the dots.
6. Colour is quantised twice at two different frequencies — the reveal mask against a per-block threshold, the tone against a per-pixel one — so the shape of the trail and the banding of the image do not moire against each other.
7. `object-fit: cover` is reproduced in uv space from the intrinsic aspect of the decoded texture, so the shader crops exactly the way the equivalent CSS would and a resize is two uniform writes rather than a re-layout.
8. The pointer state updates every frame while the DRAW is throttled to 30fps. The trail geometry is smooth because the samples are, and 30fps is invisible through 5px blocks; halving the draw rate halves the fill, which is the only real cost here.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `TRAIL_POINTS = 24`
  Ring length, and a compile-time `#define` because GLSL ES 1.00 needs a constant loop bound. At the default spacing this is roughly a second of trail. Past ~48 the shader is doing more work than the image is worth, and the far end of the trail is below the first dither level anyway.
- `MAX_BUFFER_WIDTH = 1100`
  Absolute cap on drawing-buffer width in device pixels, applied on top of the dpr cap. The output is 5px blocks quantised to four levels, so a wider buffer resolves nothing: a 2560px hero at dpr 2 would shade 26 million fragments per draw for a picture with no detail above the block size.
- `fps = 30`
  Draw ceiling. This is an overlay, not the subject, and the block size hides the difference between 30 and 120. The accumulator subtracts the budget rather than zeroing, so the long-run rate is exact instead of quietly losing the remainder each frame.
- `smoothing = 0.0002`
  Fraction of the pointer gap still remaining after one second — an ~80ms half-life. Tighter than a glow needs, because the trail has a visible head: lag past ~150ms and the reveal is drawing where the pointer was, which reads as dropped frames.
- `spawnDistance / spawnInterval = 0.012 / 0.042`
  Roughly 1.2% of the container per sample, or one every 42ms if the pointer is still. Below ~0.006 a slow drag exhausts the ring in a few centimetres; above ~0.03 a fast sweep is visibly a string of beads.
- `trail radius = 0.055 -> 0.115`
  A sample GROWS as it ages, so the trail widens and softens behind the head instead of fading as a constant-width stripe. Equal radii read as a paint stroke; the taper is what makes it a wake.
- `FLOW_MAX / FLOW_CLAMP = 0.04 / 0.055`
  Per-sample and total displacement ceilings in uv units. Uncapped, a flick tears the image into unrecognisable stripes; the total clamp also stops overlapping samples from summing into a displacement several times either individual one.
- `levels = 4`
  Quantisation steps per channel inside the reveal. Two is a duotone stencil that loses the photograph; past ~8 the dither is too fine to read as one and the effect looks like a slightly noisy image.
- `Bayer epsilon = 0.001`
  The matrix contains a zero cell, so `step(threshold, soft)` lights that cell in every block on the canvas — a permanent sparse grid of stray pixels everywhere the trail has never been. Biasing the threshold is what keeps the untouched area untouched.

## API

```ts
function DitherTrailImageReveal(props: { src: string; alt?: string; levels?: number; blockSize?: number; trailLife?: number; spawnDistance?: number; spawnInterval?: number; flowGain?: number; smoothing?: number; restBrightness?: number; restSaturation?: number; fps?: number; maxDpr?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `src: string`
  Required. Image URL — http(s), blob: or data:. Never a bundled asset.
- `alt: string` — default `''`
  Accessible name for the panel. Empty marks it decorative.
- `levels: number` — default `4`
  Quantisation steps per channel inside the reveal.
- `blockSize: number` — default `5`
  Dither block size in CSS pixels.
- `trailLife: number` — default `1.05`
  Life of one trail sample in seconds.
- `spawnDistance: number` — default `0.012`
  Follower travel in uv units that releases the next sample.
- `spawnInterval: number` — default `0.042`
  Seconds after which a sample is released even with no movement.
- `flowGain: number` — default `0.03`
  uv offset stored per uv/second of pointer velocity.
- `smoothing: number` — default `0.0002`
  Fraction of the pointer gap still remaining after one second.
- `restBrightness: number` — default `0.5`
  Brightness of the untouched image, 0 to 1.
- `restSaturation: number` — default `0.16`
  Saturation of the untouched image, 0 to 1.
- `fps: number` — default `30`
  Draw rate ceiling. Pointer state still updates every frame.
- `maxDpr: number` — default `1.5`
  Device pixel ratio cap, before the 1100px absolute buffer cap.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root container via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Samples in the ring. Must match TRAIL_POINTS in the fragment shader. */
const TRAIL_POINTS = 24;
/**
 * Hard cap on drawing-buffer width in device pixels. An overlay of 5px blocks
 * carries no detail a wider buffer could resolve, and fill is the whole cost:
 * a 2560px hero at dpr 2 would shade 26 million fragments per draw for a
 * picture that is quantised to four levels.
 */
const MAX_BUFFER_WIDTH = 1100;
/** uv units per second at which the speed term saturates. */
const SPEED_FULL_SCALE = 1.6;
/** Fraction of the velocity gap left after a second. Fast: speed must track. */
const VELOCITY_SMOOTHING = 0.001;
/** Ceiling on a single sample's stored flow, in uv units. */
const FLOW_MAX = 0.04;
/** Ceiling on the SUM of all samples' flow, applied in the shader. */
const FLOW_CLAMP = 0.055;

/** The reduced-motion still: a frozen swipe with a plausible velocity. */
const STILL_POINTS = 9;
const STILL_FLOW: readonly [number, number] = [0.02, 0.008];

interface RevealUniforms {
  /** three types `uniforms` as an open record; the index signature matches it. */
  [name: string]: THREE.IUniform;
  uResolution: THREE.IUniform<THREE.Vector2>;
  uImage: THREE.IUniform<THREE.Texture | null>;
  uHasImage: THREE.IUniform<number>;
  uUvScale: THREE.IUniform<THREE.Vector2>;
  uUvOffset: THREE.IUniform<THREE.Vector2>;
  /** Flat vec4 array: three's uniform setters take a typed array unchanged. */
  uTrail: THREE.IUniform<Float32Array>;
  uFlow: THREE.IUniform<Float32Array>;
  uBlock: THREE.IUniform<number>;
  uLevels: THREE.IUniform<number>;
  uFlowClamp: THREE.IUniform<number>;
  uRestBrightness: THREE.IUniform<number>;
  uRestSaturation: THREE.IUniform<number>;
}

interface Stage {
  renderer: THREE.WebGLRenderer;
  scene: THREE.Scene;
  camera: THREE.OrthographicCamera;
  geometry: THREE.PlaneGeometry;
  material: THREE.ShaderMaterial;
  uniforms: RevealUniforms;
  placeholder: THREE.DataTexture;
  render: () => void;
}

interface TrailSample {
  x: number;
  y: number;
  /** Elapsed seconds at spawn. Negative means the slot has never been used. */
  born: number;
  flowX: number;
  flowY: number;
  speed: number;
}

/**
 * A 1x1 opaque texture, bound before anything has loaded. Sampling an unbound
 * sampler2D is undefined behaviour: some drivers return black, some warn on
 * every draw, and one of them will be the reviewer's.
 */
function createPlaceholder(): THREE.DataTexture {
  const texture = new THREE.DataTexture(new Uint8Array([16, 17, 21, 255]), 1, 1);
  texture.needsUpdate = true;
  return texture;
}

export function DitherTrailImageReveal({
  src,
  alt = '',
  levels = 4,
  blockSize = 5,
  trailLife = 1.05,
  spawnDistance = 0.012,
  spawnInterval = 0.042,
  flowGain = 0.03,
  smoothing = 0.0002,
  restBrightness = 0.5,
  restSaturation = 0.16,
  fps = 30,
  maxDpr = 1.5,
  className,
}: DitherTrailImageRevealProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const mount = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const { inView } = useInView(host, { rootMargin: '10%' });
  const visible = useVisibility();
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  /* A trail needs a pointer that exists while no button is held. On touch
     `pointermove` only fires mid-drag, so the reveal would appear under the
     finger that is covering it and then be stranded on lift. */
  const finePointer = useMediaQuery('(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)');

  const [supported, setSupported] = useState(true);
  useEffect(() => setSupported(hasWebGL()), []);
  const [failed, setFailed] = useState(false);

  /** The decoded image, kept across renderer rebuilds so a resize never refetches. */
  const image = useRef<THREE.Texture | null>(null);
  /** Intrinsic aspect of that image; 0 until one has decoded. */
  const imageAspect = useRef(0);

  const target = useRef<{ x: number; y: number } | null>(null);
  const inside = useRef(false);
  const follow = useRef({ x: 0.5, y: 0.5 });
  const velocity = useRef({ x: 0, y: 0 });
  const lastSpawn = useRef({ x: 0.5, y: 0.5, at: -1 });
  const writeIndex = useRef(0);
  const budget = useRef(0);

  const trail = useRef<TrailSample[]>(
    Array.from({ length: TRAIL_POINTS }, () => ({
      x: 0,
      y: 0,
      born: -1,
      flowX: 0,
      flowY: 0,
      speed: 0,
    })),
  );

  const live = useRef({
    levels,
    blockSize,
    trailLife,
    spawnDistance,
    spawnInterval,
    flowGain,
    smoothing,
    restBrightness,
    restSaturation,
    fps,
  });
  live.current = {
    levels,
    blockSize,
    trailLife,
    spawnDistance,
    spawnInterval,
    flowGain,
    smoothing,
    restBrightness,
    restSaturation,
    fps,
  };

  const ready = supported && width > 1 && height > 1;

  /* The measured size, readable from an async callback. The image loader below
     runs on `[src, ready]`, so its success handler closes over whichever size
     was current when the fetch STARTED — and a decode routinely lands a few
     hundred milliseconds later, after the observer has reported the real box.
     Fitting against the stale numbers left the picture visibly mis-cropped
     until something else happened to resize the element. */
  const size = useRef({ width, height });
  size.current = { width, height };

  /** object-fit: cover, replicated in uv space so the shader matches the CSS. */
  const applyCover = (w: number, h: number) => {
    const s = stage.current;
    if (!s || w < 1 || h < 1) return;
    const ia = imageAspect.current;
    if (ia <= 0) {
      s.uniforms.uUvScale.value.set(1, 1);
      s.uniforms.uUvOffset.value.set(0, 0);
      return;
    }
    const canvasAspect = w / h;
    if (ia > canvasAspect) {
      // Image is wider than the box: crop the sides.
      const scale = canvasAspect / ia;
      s.uniforms.uUvScale.value.set(scale, 1);
      s.uniforms.uUvOffset.value.set((1 - scale) * 0.5, 0);
    } else {
      const scale = ia / canvasAspect;
      s.uniforms.uUvScale.value.set(1, scale);
      s.uniforms.uUvOffset.value.set(0, (1 - scale) * 0.5);
    }
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const slot = mount.current;
    if (!slot || !ready) return;

    /* The canvas is created here rather than owned by React. `reactStrictMode`
       double-invokes this effect; the first cleanup calls `forceContextLoss()`,
       and `getContext` on that same element afterwards returns the DEAD context
       instead of a fresh one — blank in development, fine in production, which
       is the worst way for a bug to behave. */
    let renderer: THREE.WebGLRenderer;
    try {
      renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({
        antialias: false,
        alpha: false,
        powerPreference: 'low-power',
      });
    } catch {
      // A context can still be refused between the probe and the construction —
      // the tab may have hit the browser's live-context ceiling in between. three
      // throws rather than returning null, and an uncaught throw here takes the
      // page with it.
      setSupported(false);
      return;
    }
    // Two caps, and the lower wins: a ratio cap for sane machines and an
    // absolute width cap so a 4K hero cannot ask for a 7680px buffer.
    const ratio = Math.min(pixelRatio(maxDpr), MAX_BUFFER_WIDTH / Math.max(width, 1));
    renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.max(ratio, 0.5));
    renderer.setSize(width, height, false);
    const canvas = renderer.domElement;
    canvas.style.display = 'block';
    canvas.style.width = '100%';
    canvas.style.height = '100%';
    slot.appendChild(canvas);

    const placeholder = createPlaceholder();

    const uniforms: RevealUniforms = {
      uResolution: { value: new THREE.Vector2(width, height) },
      uImage: { value: image.current ?? placeholder },
      uHasImage: { value: image.current ? 1 : 0 },
      uUvScale: { value: new THREE.Vector2(1, 1) },
      uUvOffset: { value: new THREE.Vector2(0, 0) },
      uTrail: { value: new Float32Array(TRAIL_POINTS * 4) },
      uFlow: { value: new Float32Array(TRAIL_POINTS * 2) },
      uBlock: { value: blockSize },
      uLevels: { value: levels },
      uFlowClamp: { value: FLOW_CLAMP },
      uRestBrightness: { value: restBrightness },
      uRestSaturation: { value: restSaturation },
    };

    const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader: ditherTrailImageRevealVertexShader,
      fragmentShader: ditherTrailImageRevealFragmentShader,
      uniforms,
    });

    const geometry = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(2, 2);
    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material));
    const camera = new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0, 1);
    const render = () => renderer.render(scene, camera);

    /* Listeners on the CANVAS, not the window: a document-level handler
       outlives the renderer it drives, and the rect it measures is not the rect
       being drawn into. Passive, because nothing calls preventDefault here and
       a non-passive move handler stalls the compositor on every event. */
    const onMove = (event: PointerEvent) => {
      const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;
      target.current = {
        x: (event.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width,
        // Flipped: uv y is up, client y is down.
        y: 1 - (event.clientY - rect.top) / rect.height,
      };
      if (!inside.current) {
        // Entering: teleport the follower rather than damping to it, or the
        // trail draws a stripe from wherever the pointer was last seen.
        follow.current.x = target.current.x;
        follow.current.y = target.current.y;
        lastSpawn.current.x = target.current.x;
        lastSpawn.current.y = target.current.y;
        velocity.current.x = 0;
        velocity.current.y = 0;
      }
      inside.current = true;
    };
    const onLeave = () => {
      inside.current = false;
      // Samples already in the ring keep ageing out on their own, so the trail
      // finishes its life instead of vanishing the instant the pointer leaves.
    };

    canvas.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove, { passive: true });
    canvas.addEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave, { passive: true });
    canvas.addEventListener('pointercancel', onLeave, { passive: true });

    stage.current = {
      renderer,
      scene,
      camera,
      geometry,
      material,
      uniforms,
      placeholder,
      render,
    };
    applyCover(width, height);
    render();

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      canvas.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
      canvas.removeEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);
      canvas.removeEventListener('pointercancel', onLeave);
      // `dispose()` frees GPU objects but leaves the context alive until GC
      // decides otherwise. `disposeRenderer` is the one that force-loses it,
      // and the per-process budget is about sixteen contexts.
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      geometry.dispose();
      material.dispose();
      placeholder.dispose();
      canvas.remove();
    };
    // Everything else is pushed through `live` or the uniforms from the loop.
    // Rebuilding on a prop change would churn WebGL contexts.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [ready, maxDpr]);

  /* Loading is its own effect and its own lifetime. It never throws: a 404
     leaves `uHasImage` at 0 and the shader keeps drawing its stand-in. */
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!ready || !src) return;
    let cancelled = false;
    setFailed(false);

    const loader = new THREE.TextureLoader();
    loader.load(
      src,
      (texture) => {
        if (cancelled) {
          // The component unmounted, or `src` changed, mid-decode. Without this
          // the texture is uploaded to a dead context and then leaked.
          texture.dispose();
          return;
        }
        texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
        // No mipmaps: the quad is screen-filling, the image is never minified
        // past 1:1, and mipmapping a non-power-of-two texture silently fails.
        texture.generateMipmaps = false;
        texture.minFilter = THREE.LinearFilter;
        texture.magFilter = THREE.LinearFilter;
        texture.wrapS = THREE.ClampToEdgeWrapping;
        texture.wrapT = THREE.ClampToEdgeWrapping;

        image.current?.dispose();
        image.current = texture;

        const source = texture.image as { width?: number; height?: number } | null;
        const w = source?.width ?? 0;
        const h = source?.height ?? 0;
        imageAspect.current = w > 0 && h > 0 ? w / h : 0;

        const s = stage.current;
        if (!s) return;
        s.uniforms.uImage.value = texture;
        s.uniforms.uHasImage.value = 1;
        // From the ref, not the closure: see the note on `size` above.
        applyCover(size.current.width, size.current.height);
        s.render();
      },
      undefined,
      () => {
        if (cancelled) return;
        // A missing image is a content problem, not a crash. The stand-in field
        // keeps the panel legible and the trail keeps working on top of it.
        setFailed(true);
        imageAspect.current = 0;
        const s = stage.current;
        if (!s) return;
        s.uniforms.uHasImage.value = 0;
        s.render();
      },
    );

    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
    };
    // `width`/`height` are read for the cover fit but must not retrigger a
    // fetch; the resize effect re-applies the fit on its own.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [src, ready]);

  // The decoded texture outlives the renderer, so it is released on unmount
  // rather than in the loader effect, which reruns whenever `src` changes.
  useEffect(() => {
    return () => {
      image.current?.dispose();
      image.current = null;
    };
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    const s = stage.current;
    if (!s || width < 1 || height < 1) return;
    const ratio = Math.min(pixelRatio(maxDpr), MAX_BUFFER_WIDTH / width);
    s.renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.max(ratio, 0.5));
    s.renderer.setSize(width, height, false);
    s.uniforms.uResolution.value.set(width, height);
    applyCover(width, height);
    // Redraw once, or a resize while the loop is paused leaves the previous
    // framebuffer stretched across the new size.
    s.render();
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [width, height, maxDpr]);

  const writeTrailUniforms = (elapsed: number, life: number) => {
    const s = stage.current;
    if (!s) return;
    const points = s.uniforms.uTrail.value;
    const flows = s.uniforms.uFlow.value;
    let i = 0;
    for (const sample of trail.current) {
      const age = sample.born < 0 ? Infinity : elapsed - sample.born;
      const remaining = clamp(1 - age / life, 0, 1);
      points[i * 4] = sample.x;
      points[i * 4 + 1] = sample.y;
      points[i * 4 + 2] = remaining;
      points[i * 4 + 3] = sample.speed;
      flows[i * 2] = sample.flowX;
      flows[i * 2 + 1] = sample.flowY;
      i += 1;
    }
  };

  useRaf(
    (dt, elapsed) => {
      const s = stage.current;
      if (!s) return;
      const cfg = live.current;

      const previousX = follow.current.x;
      const previousY = follow.current.y;

      const aim = target.current;
      if (aim) {
        follow.current.x = damp(follow.current.x, aim.x, cfg.smoothing, dt);
        follow.current.y = damp(follow.current.y, aim.y, cfg.smoothing, dt);
      }

      // Velocity of the FOLLOWER, in uv units per second. Dividing by dt is
      // what makes it a velocity rather than a per-frame delta that measures
      // twice as large at 60Hz as at 120Hz for the same hand movement.
      const step = Math.max(dt, 0.0001);
      velocity.current.x = damp(
        velocity.current.x,
        (follow.current.x - previousX) / step,
        VELOCITY_SMOOTHING,
        dt,
      );
      velocity.current.y = damp(
        velocity.current.y,
        (follow.current.y - previousY) / step,
        VELOCITY_SMOOTHING,
        dt,
      );

      /* Spawn on DISTANCE travelled, or on a time floor. Distance alone gives
         an evenly spaced trail but lets the reveal decay to nothing under a
         pointer that has stopped; the time floor keeps a stationary hover
         alive. Spawning per event instead would clump on a slow drag and smear
         on a flick, because events fire on sub-pixel movement. */
      if (inside.current && aim) {
        const moved = Math.hypot(
          follow.current.x - lastSpawn.current.x,
          follow.current.y - lastSpawn.current.y,
        );
        const waited = elapsed - lastSpawn.current.at;
        if (moved >= cfg.spawnDistance || waited >= cfg.spawnInterval) {
          const slot = trail.current[writeIndex.current % TRAIL_POINTS];
          if (slot) {
            writeIndex.current = (writeIndex.current + 1) % TRAIL_POINTS;
            slot.x = follow.current.x;
            slot.y = follow.current.y;
            slot.born = elapsed;
            slot.flowX = clamp(velocity.current.x * cfg.flowGain, -FLOW_MAX, FLOW_MAX);
            slot.flowY = clamp(velocity.current.y * cfg.flowGain, -FLOW_MAX, FLOW_MAX);
            slot.speed = clamp(
              Math.hypot(velocity.current.x, velocity.current.y) / SPEED_FULL_SCALE,
              0,
              1,
            );
          }
          lastSpawn.current.x = follow.current.x;
          lastSpawn.current.y = follow.current.y;
          lastSpawn.current.at = elapsed;
        }
      }

      const life = Math.max(cfg.trailLife, 0.05);
      writeTrailUniforms(elapsed, life);

      const u = s.uniforms;
      u.uBlock.value = Math.max(cfg.blockSize, 1);
      u.uLevels.value = Math.max(cfg.levels, 2);
      u.uRestBrightness.value = cfg.restBrightness;
      u.uRestSaturation.value = cfg.restSaturation;

      /* Draw-rate throttle. The state above updates every frame — a trail
         sampled at 30Hz has visible corners — but the DRAW is the expensive
         half and 30fps is indistinguishable through 5px blocks. Subtracting
         the budget rather than zeroing the accumulator keeps the long-run rate
         exact instead of quietly losing the remainder every frame. */
      const frameBudget = 1 / clamp(cfg.fps, 10, 120);
      budget.current += dt;
      if (budget.current < frameBudget) return;
      budget.current = Math.min(budget.current - frameBudget, frameBudget);

      s.render();
    },
    ready && inView && visible && !reduced && finePointer,
  );

  /* Reduced motion, and coarse pointers, get a composed still: a short frozen
     swipe baked into the ring so the panel shows what the effect produces. The
     listeners stay attached and their target is never consumed. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const s = stage.current;
    if (!s || !ready) return;
    if (!reduced && finePointer) return;

    const [flowX = 0.02, flowY = 0.008] = STILL_FLOW;
    let i = 0;
    for (const sample of trail.current) {
      const t = i / (STILL_POINTS - 1);
      const inSwipe = i < STILL_POINTS;
      sample.x = 0.3 + t * 0.42;
      sample.y = 0.4 + Math.sin(t * 2.2) * 0.12;
      sample.flowX = flowX;
      sample.flowY = flowY;
      sample.speed = inSwipe ? 0.45 : 0;
      // `born` is unused by the still: lives are written straight below.
      sample.born = -1;
      i += 1;
    }

    const points = s.uniforms.uTrail.value;
    const flows = s.uniforms.uFlow.value;
    let j = 0;
    for (const sample of trail.current) {
      const remaining = j < STILL_POINTS ? 1 - j / STILL_POINTS : 0;
      points[j * 4] = sample.x;
      points[j * 4 + 1] = sample.y;
      points[j * 4 + 2] = remaining;
      points[j * 4 + 3] = sample.speed;
      flows[j * 2] = sample.flowX;
      flows[j * 2 + 1] = sample.flowY;
      j += 1;
    }
    s.render();
  }, [reduced, finePointer, ready, width, height]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes the three pointer listeners from the canvas, nulls the stage ref so an in-flight frame cannot touch a dead renderer, then `disposeRenderer(renderer)` — which force-loses the context, not just `dispose()`, since Chromium keeps roughly sixteen per process and drops the oldest — followed by the geometry, the material and the 1x1 placeholder texture, and finally removes the canvas from the DOM. The decoded image texture is disposed in a separate unmount effect, and an in-flight decode is cancelled by a flag so its callback disposes the result instead of binding it.

**Reduced motion.** The loop never starts. A short frozen swipe — nine samples with descending life and a plausible velocity — is baked into the ring and one frame is drawn, so the panel shows what the effect produces rather than a flat dimmed image. Coarse pointers get the same still, for the same reason. The listeners stay attached but their target is never consumed, so moving the pointer changes nothing.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Pushing pointer events straight into the trail. Event positions are not a path: they arrive at whatever rate the device chooses, cluster on slow movement and stop dead when the hand pauses. The handler records a target only; the loop damps a follower toward it and samples the follower.
- Damping with a per-frame constant (`x += (t - x) * 0.1`) instead of `damp(..., dt)`. The trail is visibly tighter at 120Hz than at 60Hz, so the feel is tuned to whichever machine it was authored on.
- Measuring velocity as a per-frame delta rather than dividing by `dt`. The same hand movement then reads as half the speed at 120Hz, and the smear strength — and with it the whole character of the effect — depends on the display.
- Sampling the Bayer threshold per fragment instead of per block. The reveal edge becomes smooth, which is precisely the thing a dither is supposed to replace, and the block grid stops being legible.
- Comparing against the Bayer matrix without an epsilon. Its zero cell passes `step()` everywhere, so one pixel in every 5x5 block is lit across the entire canvas, including areas the pointer has never visited.
- Dividing the 8x8 matrix by 63 instead of 64. A threshold of exactly 1.0 means the brightest level can never be selected, and the whitest part of the image clips one step down.
- Assuming `src` is decoded. A `TextureLoader` result arrives asynchronously and may never arrive at all. Leaving the sampler unbound until then is undefined behaviour — black on some drivers, a console warning per draw on others. A 1x1 placeholder is bound from the first frame and a `uHasImage` float selects a procedural stand-in.
- Letting a 404 throw or blank the panel. A component that cannot survive a missing image cannot be dropped into a CMS-backed page. The error callback leaves `uHasImage` at 0 and the trail keeps working over the stand-in field.
- Not cancelling an in-flight decode. If `src` changes or the component unmounts mid-load, the callback fires against a dead renderer and the texture is uploaded and then leaked. A `cancelled` flag disposes it instead.
- Rendering at full device pixel ratio. Fill is the entire cost of a fullscreen quad and it scales with the square of the ratio, for an image whose smallest feature is deliberately five pixels wide.
- Owning the canvas in React while calling `forceContextLoss()` on cleanup. Under `reactStrictMode` the effect runs twice and the second `getContext` on that same element returns the DEAD context: blank in development, fine in production, which is the worst way for a bug to behave.
- Shipping the demo image as a committed asset. The image is a prop; the demo paints its own canvas and passes a data URL, so the registry carries no binary.

## Notes

- `src` is required and is never bundled. Anything a browser can fetch works: an http(s) URL, a `blob:` from an upload, or a `data:` URL.
- Coarse pointers get the composed still rather than the live effect. `pointermove` only fires mid-drag on touch, so the reveal would appear under the finger covering it and then be stranded on lift.
- Without WebGL the component renders the image plainly with `object-fit: cover`. The picture is the content; the dither is decoration on top of it.
- The decoded texture is held across renderer rebuilds, so a resize or a dpr change re-uploads it rather than refetching. It is disposed in its own unmount effect, separate from the loader effect that reruns on every `src` change.
- Leaving the panel does not clear the trail. Samples keep ageing out on their own, so the reveal finishes its life instead of vanishing on `pointerleave`.
- The root carries `role="img"` and the `alt` text; an empty `alt` marks the whole panel decorative with `aria-hidden` instead.

## Definition of done

At rest the image is visible but dimmed and nearly grey. Drag across it and full colour appears in a trail of hard-edged square blocks that widens and fades behind the pointer, with the blocks smeared along the direction of travel — more on a flick, less on a slow drag. The untouched area contains no stray lit pixels anywhere. Stop moving and the reveal stays alive under the cursor instead of dying. Leave the panel and the trail finishes ageing out where it stands. The follow lag is identical on a 60Hz and a 120Hz display. Point at a `src` that 404s: the panel shows a banded stand-in field, the trail still works, and the console carries no exception. Resize wide and the image stays cover-cropped with no stretching, and the trail discs stay round.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Divider

One primitive for every horizontal break in the kit. With no children it is a bare `role="separator"` rule; with children (a label such as "or", a date heading, a small button) it becomes a flex row whose lines grow around the content. Three variants change the treatment: a single hairline, a pair of framing hairlines, or a soft filled strip on the secondary surface.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Horizontal divider in single-hairline, double-line and filled-strip treatments, with optional start, centre or end content.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Decide the branch with `hasContent = children !== undefined && children !== null`, so `0` or an empty string still count as content and only a missing child yields a bare rule.
2. Empty branch: render one `<div role="separator" aria-orientation="horizontal">` with `w-full` plus the variant's empty class: `h-px bg-separator-border` (single), `h-2 border-y border-separator-border` (double) or `h-2 rounded-full bg-background-secondary-default` (fill).
3. Content branch: render a `<div>` with `w-full`, the variant's row class and the `align` justify class. Single is `flex items-center gap-3`; double is `flex items-center border-y border-separator-border py-2.5`; fill is `flex items-center rounded-2lg bg-background-secondary-default px-4 py-2.5`.
4. Only the single variant draws inline lines. Compute `showLeadingLine = variant === "single" && align !== "start"` and `showTrailingLine = variant === "single" && align !== "end"`, and render each as `<span aria-hidden className="h-px min-w-0 flex-1 bg-separator-border">`, so the content sits at the start, centre or end and the remaining line stays flexible.
5. Wrap the children in `<div className="shrink-0 text-body-medium text-text-secondary">` merged with `contentClassName`, so a label never shrinks and inherits the kit's secondary body style. The root gets `data-variant` and `data-align` for styling hooks.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `gap / line = gap-3 (12px), h-px flex-1`
  12px of air on both sides of the label keeps "or" from touching the rule. `min-w-0` on the lines lets them shrink to nothing in a narrow column rather than pushing the label out.
- `double / fill padding = py-2.5 (10px); fill adds px-4 and rounded-2lg (10px)`
  A 20px body line plus 10px top and bottom gives a 40px band, the height of a list section heading in the dashboards.
- `empty heights = single 1px, double / fill 8px (h-2)`
  The double rule needs height between its two borders to read as two lines; the fill strip at 8px reads as a soft spacer band.
- `separator colour = light neutral-200, dark neutral-800`
  `--color-separator-border` is the kit's quietest line colour, so dividers never compete with card borders.

## API

```ts
type DividerVariant = "single" | "double" | "fill"
type DividerAlign = "start" | "center" | "end"
interface DividerProps extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "children"> { variant?: DividerVariant; align?: DividerAlign; children?: ReactNode; contentClassName?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }
function Divider(props: DividerProps): JSX.Element
```

- `variant: "single" | "double" | "fill"` — default `"single"`
  One hairline, two framing hairlines, or a filled secondary-surface strip.
- `align: "start" | "center" | "end"` — default `"center"`
  Where the content sits. On the single variant it also removes the line on that side.
- `children: ReactNode`
  Optional label or control. Without it the divider is a bare `role="separator"` rule.
- `contentClassName: string`
  Extra classes for the content wrapper.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root through `tailwind-merge`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const styles = sortCx({
  root: "w-full",
  line: "h-px min-w-0 flex-1 bg-separator-border",
  content: "shrink-0 text-body-medium text-text-secondary",
  align: {
    start: "justify-start",
    center: "justify-center",
    end: "justify-end",
  },
  withContent: {
    single: "flex items-center gap-3",
    double: "flex items-center border-y border-separator-border py-2.5",
    fill: "flex items-center rounded-2lg bg-background-secondary-default px-4 py-2.5",
  },
  empty: {
    single: "h-px bg-separator-border",
    double: "h-2 border-y border-separator-border",
    fill: "h-2 rounded-full bg-background-secondary-default",
  },
});

/**
 * Horizontal content divider with three BoardUI surface treatments.
 *
 * `single` places content within one continuous hairline, `double` frames it
 * with a line above and below, and `fill` uses the secondary surface color.
 * Children stay completely composable, so labels, buttons, and small controls
 * can share the same primitive.
 */
export function Divider({
  variant = "single",
  align = "center",
  children,
  contentClassName,
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: DividerProps) {
  const hasContent = children !== undefined && children !== null;

  if (!hasContent) {
    return (
      <div
        ref={ref}
        role="separator"
        aria-orientation="horizontal"
        data-variant={variant}
        className={cx(styles.root, styles.empty[variant], className)}
        {...props}
      />
    );
  }

  const showLeadingLine = variant === "single" && align !== "start";
  const showTrailingLine = variant === "single" && align !== "end";

  return (
    <div
      ref={ref}
      data-variant={variant}
      data-align={align}
      className={cx(
        styles.root,
        styles.withContent[variant],
        styles.align[align],
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      {showLeadingLine ? <span aria-hidden className={styles.line} /> : null}
      <div className={cx(styles.content, contentClassName)}>{children}</div>
      {showTrailingLine ? <span aria-hidden className={styles.line} /> : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component is stateless markup with no listeners, timers or effects.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing animates, so the divider renders identically under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not expect the content form to be announced as a separator. Only the empty form carries `role="separator"`; with children the row is plain layout and its label is read as text.
- Do not put long, wrapping text in a divider. The content wrapper is `shrink-0`, so a long label pushes the lines to zero and can overflow a narrow column.
- Do not pass `children={null}` expecting a labelled divider; `null` and `undefined` both select the bare-rule branch.
- Do not hard-code `bg-neutral-200` on a custom line. Use `bg-separator-border` so the hairline flips to neutral-800 in dark mode.

## Notes

- Children are fully composable: a label, a date, or a compact control such as a "Show more" button all work.
- Defaults are `variant="single"` and `align="center"`.

## Definition of done

`<Divider />` renders a full-width 1px rule with `role="separator"`. `<Divider>or</Divider>` renders "or" centred with a hairline growing on each side and 12px between label and line. `align="start"` removes the leading line so the label sits flush left. The double variant frames its label between a top and bottom border with 10px padding, the fill variant sits on a rounded secondary-surface strip, and all lines switch to the dark separator colour in dark mode.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Docs Callout

The aside a docs page drops between paragraphs: a softly tinted, bordered box with a coloured icon chip, a bold title and body copy that styles inline `code` and links. Info is blue, tip lime, warning yellow and danger rose, all from the kit status tokens so both themes stay legible. A dismissible callout shows a close button and folds its row shut before it unmounts.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Docs callout in four variants (note, tip, warning, danger) with a tinted icon chip, title, rich body and an optional collapsing dismiss.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Each variant maps to one status token pair: the surface is `bg-status-*-background/45` with a `border-status-*-text/20` hairline, and the 24px icon chip uses the full-strength background with the status text colour. The title defaults to the variant label; a custom title keeps the label for screen readers as an `sr-only` "Warning: " prefix.
2. The box is `role="note"` labelled by its title, which is the ARIA role for a parenthetical aside; it is never `alert`, because docs callouts are static content.
3. The body gets descendant styles through arbitrary variants (`[&_code]:`, `[&_a]:`, `[&_p+p]:`), so MDX or plain JSX children pick up code chips, underlined links and paragraph spacing without extra components.
4. Dismiss runs a three-phase state: pressing close calls `onDismiss` immediately (so the caller can move focus), then the wrapper goes to "leaving": `inert`, `grid-rows-[0fr]`, `opacity-0` and `-translate-y-1` over 200ms. A 200ms timeout in an effect flips it to "gone" and the component returns null. With reduced motion it skips straight to "gone".

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `surface tint = status background at 45%, border at 20% of status text`
  Reads as a coloured note in both themes without competing with the page heading.
- `exit = 200ms ease-out, grid rows 1fr to 0fr`
  Short enough to feel like a direct response; collapsing the row lets the content below slide up instead of jumping.
- `icon chip = 24px, rounded-lg, 16px glyph`
  Matches the close button size so the first line aligns on both edges.

## API

```ts
function DocsCallout(props: { variant?: "info" | "tip" | "warning" | "danger"; title?: ReactNode; children?: ReactNode; icon?: IconComponent | null; dismissible?: boolean; onDismiss?: () => void; dismissLabel?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element | null
```

- `variant: "info" | "tip" | "warning" | "danger"` — default `"info"`
  Colour, icon and default title.
- `title: ReactNode` — default `"Note" / "Tip" / "Warning" / "Danger"`
  Heading; a custom one keeps the variant name as an sr-only prefix.
- `children: ReactNode`
  Body copy; inline `code`, links and paragraphs are styled.
- `icon: IconComponent | null`
  Replaces the variant icon; `null` hides the chip.
- `dismissible: boolean` — default `false`
  Shows a close button that collapses and unmounts the callout.
- `onDismiss: () => void`
  Called on press, before the exit animation; move focus here.
- `dismissLabel: string` — default `"Dismiss <variant>"`
  Accessible name of the close button.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the outer wrapper.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Dismiss: "shown" -> "leaving" (row collapses 1fr -> 0fr while fading, content inert)
// -> "gone" (unmounted). Reduced motion skips straight to "gone". onDismiss runs on
// press so the caller can move focus before the close button disappears.
const [phase, setPhase] = useState<"shown" | "leaving" | "gone">("shown");

useEffect(() => {
  if (phase !== "leaving") return;
  const t = window.setTimeout(() => setPhase("gone"), LEAVE_MS);
  return () => window.clearTimeout(t);
}, [phase]);

const dismiss = () => {
  if (phase !== "shown") return;
  onDismiss?.();
  setPhase(reduced ? "gone" : "leaving");
};

const leaving = phase === "leaving";
const wrapperClass = cx(
  "grid transition-[grid-template-rows,opacity,translate] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
  leaving ? "-translate-y-1 grid-rows-[0fr] opacity-0" : "grid-rows-[1fr] opacity-100",
  className,
);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The only timer is the 200ms leaving timeout, set in an effect keyed on the phase and cleared in its cleanup, so unmounting mid-exit leaves nothing running.

**Reduced motion.** With `prefers-reduced-motion` the component skips the leaving phase and unmounts at once (`useReducedMotion`), and the wrapper transition carries `motion-reduce:transition-none`.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using `role="alert"` for danger callouts. Screen readers interrupt to announce static docs text on page load; `role="note"` is the right semantics.
- Unmounting on press with no focus plan. The focused close button vanishes and focus falls to `<body>`; use `onDismiss` to move focus to a nearby control.
- Animating `height: auto` with JS measurements. Transitioning `grid-template-rows` from 1fr to 0fr collapses to zero with pure CSS.
- Relying on colour alone for the variant. The title (or the sr-only prefix) names it in words.

## Notes

- The callout keeps its own dismissed state. To bring it back, remount it (change its `key`), as the demo's Restore button does.
- `className` lands on the outer wrapper, so grid placement and margins work; pass `icon={null}` to drop the chip.

## Definition of done

The demo shows Note, Tip, "Captions are for labels" (warning) and Danger callouts in a two-column grid that stacks to one column on phones. Each is a `role="note"` named by its title. Pressing "Dismiss tip" moves focus to Restore, the tip folds away within about 200ms and Restore reads "Restore (1)"; dismissing the warning makes it "Restore (2)". Pressing Restore brings both back and the button returns to "Restore", aria-disabled.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Docs Pager

Two bordered cards that close a documentation page, pointing to the page before and the page after. The previous card sits left with a back arrow, the next card sits right with its text end-aligned, and each shows the page title over a short tertiary description. On hover the card fills and its arrow nudges toward where it leads.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Previous / next cards for the foot of a docs page: arrow and title on top, a one-line summary below, mirrored for RTL.

- Category: navigation
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The nav is a one-column grid that becomes two columns from `sm`. The next card always takes `sm:col-start-2`, so on the first page (no previous) it still sits on the right instead of sliding into the empty left slot.
2. Each card is an `<a rel="prev|next">` when the link has an `href`, otherwise a `<button>` that only calls `onNavigate(direction, link)`, which suits client routers and demos. The direction is read out through a visible label (`showLabels`) or an `sr-only` "Previous:" / "Next:" prefix, so the title and description stay part of the accessible name.
3. The arrow uses `directionalIconClass` (`rtl:rotate-180`) and the hover nudge flips sign under `rtl:`, so in a right-to-left document the previous card points right and moves right. Because Tailwind v4 writes `translate` and `rotate` as separate properties, the nudge and the mirror compose without overriding each other.
4. In button mode the pager re-renders in place. When the clicked card disappears (the first or last page was reached), an effect keyed on the two titles sees focus on `<body>` and moves it to the card that remains, so keyboard users are not dropped to the top of the document.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `card = rounded-xl, 1px border, px-4 py-3.5, shadow-xs`
  Matches the reference pager: a quiet bordered card that reads as part of the page rather than a primary button.
- `arrow nudge = 2px (translate-x-0.5), 200ms ease-out`
  Enough to hint at direction on hover without moving the title text.
- `type = title body-medium primary, description caption-1 tertiary`
  Same hierarchy as the reference: page name first, a muted one-liner under it.

## API

```ts
function DocsPager(props: { prev?: DocsPagerLink | null; next?: DocsPagerLink | null; onNavigate?: (direction: "prev" | "next", link: DocsPagerLink) => void; showLabels?: boolean; prevLabel?: string; nextLabel?: string; "aria-label"?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element | null
type DocsPagerLink = { title: string; description?: ReactNode; href?: string }
```

- `prev / next: DocsPagerLink | null`
  `{ title, description?, href? }` for each neighbour; omit one at the ends of a section.
- `onNavigate: (direction: "prev" | "next", link: DocsPagerLink) => void`
  Called on click; the only effect when the link has no `href`.
- `showLabels: boolean` — default `false`
  Shows "Previous" / "Next" above the titles instead of keeping them screen-reader only.
- `prevLabel / nextLabel: string` — default `"Previous" / "Next"`
  Direction words, visible or `sr-only`.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Previous and next page"`
  Name of the wrapping `<nav>`.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the grid.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// In button mode the pager re-renders in place with new neighbours. When the
// card that was clicked disappears (first or last page reached), focus would
// fall to <body>; hand it to the card that is still there instead.
useEffect(() => {
  const side = pendingFocus.current;
  if (!side) return;
  pendingFocus.current = null;
  const active = document.activeElement;
  if (active && active !== document.body && active.isConnected) return;
  const other: DocsPagerDirection = side === "prev" ? "next" : "prev";
  (refs.current[side] ?? refs.current[other])?.focus();
}, [prev?.title, next?.title]);

const card = (direction: DocsPagerDirection, link: DocsPagerLink) => {
  const isPrev = direction === "prev";
  const Arrow = isPrev ? RiArrowLeftLine : RiArrowRightLine;
  const label = isPrev ? prevLabel : nextLabel;
  const className = cx(
    "group flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-1 rounded-xl border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default px-4 py-3.5 shadow-xs outline-none",
    "transition-[background-color,border-color] duration-150 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
    "hover:border-border-button-hover hover:bg-background-secondary-hover",
    "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-background-primary-default",
    isPrev ? "items-start text-start" : "items-end text-end sm:col-start-2",
  );
  const content = (
    <>
      {showLabels ? (
        <span className="text-caption-1-regular text-text-tertiary">{label}</span>
      ) : (
        <span className="sr-only">{label}: </span>
      )}
      <span className={cx("flex max-w-full items-center gap-1.5 text-body-medium text-text-primary", !isPrev && "flex-row-reverse")}>
        <Arrow
          aria-hidden
          className={cx(
            "size-4 shrink-0 text-foreground-icon-secondary transition-transform duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
            "group-hover:text-foreground-icon-primary",
            isPrev
              ? "group-hover:-translate-x-0.5 rtl:group-hover:translate-x-0.5"
              : "group-hover:translate-x-0.5 rtl:group-hover:-translate-x-0.5",
            directionalIconClass(Arrow),
          )}
        />
        <span className="truncate">{link.title}</span>
      </span>
      {link.description ? (
        <span className="max-w-full truncate text-caption-1-regular text-text-tertiary">{link.description}</span>
      ) : null}
    </>
  );
  const setRef = (node: HTMLElement | null) => {
    refs.current[direction] = node;
  };
  const handle = () => {
    pendingFocus.current = direction;
    onNavigate?.(direction, link);
  };
  return link.href ? (
    <a key={direction} ref={setRef} href={link.href} rel={direction} onClick={handle} className={className}>
      {content}
    </a>
  ) : (
    <button key={direction} ref={setRef} type="button" onClick={handle} className={cx(className, "cursor-pointer")}>
      {content}
    </button>
  );
};
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to release: there are no timers, listeners or observers. The focus hand-off is a one-shot effect that reads `document.activeElement`.

**Reduced motion.** The hover arrow nudge and the card colour transitions carry `motion-reduce:transition-none`; the arrow still shifts 2px but without animating.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Letting the next card fall into the first grid column when there is no previous page. Readers expect "next" on the right; pin it with `col-start-2`.
- Putting `aria-label="Next page"` on the card. It replaces the title and description for screen readers; prefix an `sr-only` label instead.
- Mirroring the arrow with a `rotate-180` class that also sets `transform`, then adding a hover translate on the same property. One wins and the other is lost; keep them on separate properties.
- Re-rendering a pager whose clicked card unmounts without moving focus. Focus falls back to `<body>` and the next Tab starts from the top of the page.

## Notes

- Pass `href` from your router's page list; `rel="prev"` / `rel="next"` also helps crawlers and reader modes.
- The component renders nothing when both links are missing, so it can sit in a layout unconditionally.

## Definition of done

The demo opens on Line Chart Card with "Heatmap Chart" on the left and "Most Active Days" on the right. Clicking Next twice reaches Sankey Flow (6 of 6), the right card disappears and focus moves to the remaining Previous card. Clicking Previous walks back; on Area Chart Card (1 of 6) only the Next card shows and it stays on the right.

# Build: Docs Sidebar Nav

The left rail of a documentation site: a rounded floating panel with a brand slot, a pill filter, and grouped page links drawn on a thin tree rail. Group headers fold their lists with a height transition, the current page sits on a grey fill, and New/Pro pills flag pages. Typing in the filter narrows every group at once, opens all groups and highlights the matched letters.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Floating docs sidebar with collapsible groups, tree rails, New/Pro badges, an active page and a ⌘K filter that highlights matches.

- Category: navigation
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Data is an array of groups, each with items `{ id, label, icon?, badge?, href?, disabled?, keywords? }`. Active page, collapsed group ids and filter text are each controlled-or-uncontrolled through a small `useControllable` helper, so the nav works stand-alone or wired to a router.
2. `filterDocsNav(groups, query)` lower-cases the query; a group whose own label matches is kept whole, otherwise only items whose label or `keywords` contain the query survive, and empty groups drop out. While a query is active every surviving group is forced open and its header renders as a plain label instead of a toggle, so a match can never hide inside a folded group.
3. Each group panel is a CSS grid that transitions `grid-template-rows` between `0fr` and `1fr` (with opacity) over 200ms. The inner list has `min-h-0 overflow-hidden`, so the fold animates to the real content height without measuring. A folded panel gets `inert`, which removes its links from the tab order and from the accessibility tree.
4. Every row is a `<button>` (or an `<a>` when `href` is given) with `aria-current="page"` on the active one. The tree rail is two absolutely positioned spans per row painted after the button: a 8px "corner" with `border-s border-b rounded-es-[6px]` from the row top to its middle, and, for all but the last row, a straight line from the middle to the next row. Because they come after the row they stay visible over the active fill.
5. Keyboard: ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End on the nav move focus across the filter, group headers and rows (anything with `data-docs-nav-focus` that is not inside an `inert` panel or disabled). Escape in the filter clears it. With `hotkey`, a window `keydown` listener focuses and selects the filter on ⌘K / Ctrl+K and is removed on unmount.
6. On mount, if the active row is outside the list viewport, the list scroller's `scrollTop` is adjusted to centre it (rect maths on the scroller, never `scrollIntoView`, so the page itself never jumps). The list fades out over its last 32px with a mask and pads 32px at the bottom so the last row can scroll clear of the fade.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `rail inset = start-[13px], 8px corner, rounded-es-[6px]`
  Puts the rail under the group label's first letter column and leaves room for the 16px icon at 33px, matching the reference spacing where icons start 33px from the list edge and plain labels 32px.
- `row height / gap = h-8 with gap-0.5 (34px pitch)`
  The reference rows sit 34px apart with a 32px tall active fill; the 2px gap keeps neighbouring hover fills from touching.
- `fold duration = 200ms ease-out on grid-template-rows + opacity`
  Long enough to read as a fold, short enough that toggling several groups in a row never queues up visible motion.
- `bottom fade = mask-b-from-[calc(100%-32px)] with pb-8`
  The fade signals more content below; the matching 32px of padding lets the last row scroll fully out of the faded band.
- `panel width = w-[260px], rounded-3xl, shadow-sidebar`
  Same floating panel recipe as the kit dashboard sidebar so the two read as one system.

## API

```ts
function DocsSidebarNav(props: { groups: DocsNavGroup[]; value?: string | null; defaultValue?: string | null; onValueChange?: (id: string, item: DocsNavItem) => void; collapsedGroups?: string[]; defaultCollapsedGroups?: string[]; onCollapsedGroupsChange?: (ids: string[]) => void; query?: string; defaultQuery?: string; onQueryChange?: (query: string) => void; showFilter?: boolean; filterPlaceholder?: string; filterLabel?: string; hotkey?: boolean; hotkeyLabel?: string; header?: ReactNode; footer?: ReactNode; emptyMessage?: (query: string) => ReactNode; "aria-label"?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function filterDocsNav(groups: DocsNavGroup[], query: string): DocsNavGroup[]
```

- `groups: DocsNavGroup[]`
  Sections of `{ id, label, items }`; each item is `{ id, label, icon?, badge?: "new" | "pro", href?, disabled?, keywords? }`.
- `value / defaultValue: string | null` — default `null`
  Id of the active page. Gets the grey fill and `aria-current="page"`.
- `onValueChange: (id: string, item: DocsNavItem) => void`
  Called when a row is activated.
- `collapsedGroups / defaultCollapsedGroups: string[]` — default `[]`
  Ids of folded groups.
- `onCollapsedGroupsChange: (ids: string[]) => void`
  Called with the next folded ids when a header is toggled.
- `query / defaultQuery: string` — default `""`
  Filter text. Non-empty text filters rows, opens all groups and highlights matches.
- `onQueryChange: (query: string) => void`
  Called as the filter changes or is cleared.
- `showFilter: boolean` — default `true`
  Renders the pill filter input.
- `hotkey: boolean` — default `false`
  Focuses the filter on ⌘K / Ctrl+K and shows `hotkeyLabel` in the pill.
- `header / footer: ReactNode`
  Brand row above the filter and a pinned row below the list.
- `emptyMessage: (query: string) => ReactNode` — default `No pages match “…”`
  Shown when the filter leaves nothing.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the panel; set the height here so the list can scroll.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Keeps groups whose label matches whole; otherwise keeps only matching items. Empty groups drop out. */
export function filterDocsNav(groups: DocsNavGroup[], rawQuery: string): DocsNavGroup[] {
  const query = rawQuery.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!query) return groups;
  const out: DocsNavGroup[] = [];
  for (const group of groups) {
    if (group.label.toLowerCase().includes(query)) {
      out.push(group);
      continue;
    }
    const items = group.items.filter(
      (item) =>
        item.label.toLowerCase().includes(query) ||
        (item.keywords ?? []).some((word) => word.toLowerCase().includes(query)),
    );
    if (items.length > 0) out.push({ ...group, items });
  }
  return out;
}

interface GroupSectionProps {
  group: DocsNavGroup;
  open: boolean;
  filtering: boolean;
  query: string;
  activeId: string | null;
  onToggle: (id: string) => void;
  onSelect: (item: DocsNavItem) => void;
}

function GroupSection({ group, open, filtering, query, activeId, onToggle, onSelect }: GroupSectionProps) {
  const panelId = useId();
  const headerClass = "flex h-7 w-full items-center justify-between rounded-lg pr-2.5 pl-2.5 text-caption-1-medium tracking-[0.04em] text-text-tertiary uppercase";

  return (
    <li className="flex flex-col">
      {filtering ? (
        <div className={headerClass}>{group.label}</div>
      ) : (
        <button
          type="button"
          data-docs-nav-focus=""
          aria-expanded={open}
          aria-controls={panelId}
          onClick={() => onToggle(group.id)}
          className={cx(
            headerClass,
            "cursor-pointer outline-none hover:text-text-secondary focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring focus-visible:ring-inset",
          )}
        >
          <span>{group.label}</span>
          <RiArrowDownSLine
            aria-hidden
            className={cx(
              "size-4 transition-transform duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
              !open && "-rotate-90 rtl:rotate-90",
            )}
          />
        </button>
      )}

      {/* 0fr -> 1fr animates to the content's real height without measuring it. */}
      <div
        id={panelId}
        inert={!open}
        className={cx(
          "grid transition-[grid-template-rows,opacity] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
          open ? "grid-rows-[1fr] opacity-100" : "grid-rows-[0fr] opacity-0",
        )}
      >
        <ul className="flex min-h-0 flex-col gap-0.5 overflow-hidden pt-1">
          {group.items.map((item, index) => {
            const last = index === group.items.length - 1;
            const active = item.id === activeId;
            const Icon = item.icon;
            const badge = item.badge ? badgeStyles[item.badge] : null;
            const rowClass = cx(
              "flex h-8 w-full items-center gap-2 rounded-lg pr-2.5 text-start text-body-medium outline-none",
              "transition-colors duration-150 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
              "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring focus-visible:ring-inset",
              Icon ? "ps-[33px]" : "ps-8",
              item.disabled
                ? "cursor-not-allowed text-text-disabled"
                : active
                  ? "bg-background-tertiary-default text-text-primary"
                  : "cursor-pointer text-text-secondary hover:bg-background-secondary-hover hover:text-text-primary",
            );
            const content = (
              <>
                {Icon ? (
                  <Icon
                    aria-hidden
                    className={cx("size-4 shrink-0", active ? "text-foreground-icon-primary" : "text-foreground-icon-secondary")}
                  />
                ) : null}
                <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate">
                  <Highlight text={item.label} query={query} />
                </span>
                {badge ? (
                  <span
                    className={cx(
                      "rounded-[4px] px-1.5 py-px text-caption-2-semibold tracking-[0.02em] uppercase",
                      badge.className,
                    )}
                  >
                    {badge.label}
                  </span>
                ) : null}
              </>
            );

            return (
              <li key={item.id} className="relative">
                {item.href && !item.disabled ? (
                  <a
                    href={item.href}
                    data-docs-nav-focus=""
                    aria-current={active ? "page" : undefined}
                    onClick={() => onSelect(item)}
                    className={rowClass}
                  >
                    {content}
                  </a>
                ) : (
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    data-docs-nav-focus=""
                    disabled={item.disabled}
                    aria-current={active ? "page" : undefined}
                    onClick={() => onSelect(item)}
                    className={rowClass}
                  >
                    {content}
                  </button>
                )}
                {/* Tree rail: drawn after the row so it stays visible over the active fill. */}
                <span
                  aria-hidden
                  className="pointer-events-none absolute start-[13px] top-0 h-1/2 w-2 rounded-es-[6px] border-b border-s border-border-checkbox-default"
                />
                {last ? null : (
                  <span
                    aria-hidden
                    className="pointer-events-none absolute start-[13px] top-1/2 -bottom-0.5 border-s border-border-checkbox-default"
                  />
                )}
              </li>
            );
          })}
        </ul>
      </div>
    </li>
  );
}
```
