# Build: Dual-Canvas Depth Split

Two stacked canvases render the same instanced particle system with opposite `uZSign`, and the page content is a DOM sibling between them. Particles with negative depth pass behind the text and positive ones pass in front. Because size, parallax rate, brightness and softness are one continuous ramp across the depth axis, the plane where the split happens cannot be seen — the effect is that the copy is embedded in the field, and it stays live, selectable text throughout.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

One particle field rendered twice with the depth sign flipped, so the text sits inside the field rather than on top of it.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: ogl@^1.0.11

## How it works

1. `aDepth` is the camera axis, not a distance: -1 is far behind the content plane, +1 is close to the viewer, 0 is the content plane itself. The SIGN chooses which canvas draws a particle; the magnitude drives everything else, which is why the two layers look like one field.
2. Both layers share the same typed arrays, so the two contexts hold identical particles rather than two independent fields. Only the attribute descriptor objects are per-layer, because ogl writes the buffer handle and element count into the object it is given.
3. A particle on the wrong side of the plane is rejected in the VERTEX shader by writing `gl_Position = vec4(2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 1.0)` — outside the frustum on every axis, so all four vertices are clipped before rasterisation and it costs no fragments. The vertex cost doubles across the two layers; the fragment cost, which is the only cost that mattered, does not.
4. Near particles are bigger (`mix(minSize, maxSize, depth01)`), drift further per second (`0.35 + 0.65 * depth01`), are brighter, and have a softer edge — a defocus that stops the front layer reading as dirt on the screen. Four cues from one number.
5. The back canvas is opaque and blends additively (`ONE, ONE`), which is order independent so nothing needs sorting. The front canvas sits over live text and must be transparent, which rules additive out — there is nothing on the GPU to add to — so it blends premultiplied source-over (`ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA`). One fragment shader emits premultiplied colour and serves both.
6. The population is derived from container area — `clamp(round(megapixels * density), 250, maxCount)` — and applied with `setInstancedCount` on both layers. Buffers are allocated once at `maxCount`, so a resize never reallocates.
7. Drift is a pure function of `elapsed` and the per-particle seed, with `fract` wrapping the field vertically and `uFadeBand` fading alpha to zero at both ends so the wrap seam is never visible. No per-particle state, so a still frame is drawable from one number.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `split = 0.38`
  Fraction of the population placed in front of the content. Under a half on purpose: dust in front of body copy is a legibility cost, and at 0.5 the text reads as fogged rather than embedded.
- `FRONT_OPACITY = 0.55`
  Extra alpha scale on the front layer only. Depth already brightens near particles, and the front layer is entirely near particles, so without this the layer that overlaps the text is the brightest thing on screen.
- `DEPTH_FLOOR = 0.05`
  Dead zone around the content plane. A particle at exactly 0 is rejected by both layers — `aDepth * uZSign <= 0.0` is false for neither sign — so it would silently never render.
- `sizeRange = [3, 34]`
  Disc diameter at the far and near ends of the ramp. The span is what sells the depth; at 8-to-14 the field is flat, and above ~40 the near particles are large enough that their own softness becomes the dominant texture of the page.
- `parallax factor = 0.35 + 0.65 * depth01`
  Near particles travel about three times as far per second as far ones. A larger ratio makes the far layer look frozen; a smaller one and the field moves as a single sheet, which removes the only depth cue that survives in a static screenshot.
- `MAX_DPR = 1.5`
  Two layers of soft additive discs is a fill-rate problem and fill scales with the square of the pixel ratio. Dust has no detail a third sample per axis would resolve, so a 3x phone renders at 1.5x and pays a quarter of the fragments.
- `FADE_BAND = 0.14`
  Fraction of the field height the wrap fade occupies at each end. Larger than a single-layer field needs, because the near particles are up to 34px across and their radius alone is a few percent of a short container.
- `size jitter = 0.7 .. 1.3`
  Multiplier on top of the depth ramp. Without it the depth ordering is perfectly readable from size alone, which reads as a diagram of a depth field rather than a depth field.

## API

```ts
function DualCanvasZSplit(props: { children?: ReactNode; density?: number; maxCount?: number; split?: number; sizeRange?: readonly [number, number]; speed?: number; wander?: number; opacity?: number; colorA?: string; colorB?: string; background?: string; seed?: number | string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Content rendered between the two particle layers. Ordinary DOM, fully interactive.
- `density: number` — default `850`
  Particles per megapixel of container area. The count is derived from this, not fixed.
- `maxCount: number` — default `1600`
  Population ceiling, and the size the shared buffers are allocated at.
- `split: number` — default `0.38`
  Fraction of the population placed in front of the content.
- `sizeRange: readonly [number, number]` — default `[3, 34]`
  Disc diameter in CSS pixels at the far and near ends of the depth ramp.
- `speed: number` — default `1`
  Multiplier on the whole drift, including the upward march.
- `wander: number` — default `0.05`
  Sinusoidal wander amplitude in field units, where 1 is the container.
- `opacity: number` — default `0.6`
  Overall alpha multiplier. The front layer takes 0.55 of it.
- `colorA: string` — default `'#8ea6c4'`
  First tint. Any value ogl's `Color` accepts.
- `colorB: string` — default `'#e6d9c4'`
  Second tint; each particle mixes between the two by a seeded amount.
- `background: string` — default `'#06080c'`
  Opaque clear colour of the back canvas. The front canvas is transparent.
- `seed: number | string` — default `'dual-canvas-z-split'`
  Seeds the scatter. Same seed, same field on every reload and on the server.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the host element via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
function createLayer(
  host: HTMLElement,
  data: FieldData,
  opts: {
    zSign: number;
    opaque: boolean;
    background: Color;
    colorA: Color;
    colorB: Color;
    speed: number;
    wander: number;
    opacity: number;
    minSize: number;
    maxSize: number;
  },
): Layer {
  const renderer = new Renderer({
    dpr: pixelRatio(MAX_DPR),
    // The back layer owns its pixels, so it is opaque and can blend
    // additively. The front layer sits over live DOM text and must be
    // transparent, which rules additive out — there is nothing on the GPU to
    // add to. It blends premultiplied source-over instead.
    alpha: !opts.opaque,
    premultipliedAlpha: !opts.opaque,
    // Nothing occludes anything in either layer; the depth ORDER is expressed
    // by which canvas a particle lands on, not by a z-buffer.
    depth: false,
    antialias: false,
    powerPreference: 'low-power',
  });

  const gl = renderer.gl;
  const canvas = gl.canvas;

  if (opts.opaque) gl.clearColor(opts.background.r, opts.background.g, opts.background.b, 1);
  else gl.clearColor(0, 0, 0, 0);

  // Each layer needs its own attribute descriptors — ogl writes the buffer
  // handle and the element count into the object it is handed — but the
  // underlying typed arrays are shared, so the two contexts hold identical
  // particles rather than two independent fields.
  const geometry = new Geometry(gl, {
    index: { data: data.index },
    position: { size: 2, data: data.quad },
    aOrigin: { size: 2, data: data.origins, instanced: 1 },
    aDepth: { size: 1, data: data.depths, instanced: 1 },
    aSeed: { size: 4, data: data.seeds, instanced: 1 },
  });

  const uniforms: Uniforms = {
    uResolution: { value: [1, 1] },
    uPixelRatio: { value: renderer.dpr },
    uElapsed: { value: 0 },
    uZSign: { value: opts.zSign },
    uDrift: { value: opts.speed },
    uRise: { value: RISE },
    uFlowScale: { value: FLOW_SCALE },
    uWander: { value: opts.wander },
    uFadeBand: { value: FADE_BAND },
    uMinSize: { value: opts.minSize },
    uMaxSize: { value: opts.maxSize },
    uColorA: { value: opts.colorA },
    uColorB: { value: opts.colorB },
    uOpacity: { value: opts.opacity },
  };

  const program = new Program(gl, {
    vertex: DUAL_CANVAS_Z_SPLIT_VERT,
    fragment: DUAL_CANVAS_Z_SPLIT_FRAG,
    uniforms,
    transparent: true,
    depthTest: false,
    depthWrite: false,
    // ogl defaults `cullFace` to BACK, and a culled particle is absent with no
    // error anywhere. Nothing here has a back face worth culling.
    cullFace: false,
  });
  if (opts.opaque) program.setBlendFunc(gl.ONE, gl.ONE);
  else program.setBlendFunc(gl.ONE, gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);

  const mesh = new Mesh(gl, { geometry, program });

  host.appendChild(canvas);
  canvas.style.display = 'block';

  return { renderer, geometry, program, mesh, uniforms, canvas };
}

export function DualCanvasZSplit({
  children,
  density = 850,
  maxCount = 1600,
  split = 0.38,
  sizeRange = [3, 34],
  speed = 1,
  wander = 0.05,
  opacity = 0.6,
  colorA = '#8ea6c4',
  colorB = '#e6d9c4',
  background = '#06080c',
  seed = 'dual-canvas-z-split',
  className,
}: DualCanvasZSplitProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const backHost = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const frontHost = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);
  const [unsupported, setUnsupported] = useState(false);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const size = useRef({ width, height });
  size.current = { width, height };

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const visible = useVisibility();
  const { inView } = useInView(host, { rootMargin: '10%' });
  const ready = width > 1 && height > 1;

  const [minSize = 3, maxSize = 34] = sizeRange;

  useEffect(() => {
    const back = backHost.current;
    const front = frontHost.current;
    if (!back || !front || !ready) return;

    if (!hasWebGL()) {
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }

    const total = Math.max(MIN_COUNT, Math.round(maxCount));
    const data: FieldData = {
      quad: new Float32Array([-0.5, -0.5, 0.5, -0.5, 0.5, 0.5, -0.5, 0.5]),
      index: new Uint16Array([0, 1, 2, 0, 2, 3]),
      origins: new Float32Array(total * 2),
      depths: new Float32Array(total),
      seeds: new Float32Array(total * 4),
    };

    const rng = createRng(seed);
    const frontShare = clamp(split, 0, 1);
    const lo = Math.max(1, Math.min(minSize, maxSize));
    const hi = Math.max(lo + 0.5, Math.max(minSize, maxSize));

    for (let i = 0; i < total; i += 1) {
      data.origins[i * 2] = randRange(rng, X_MIN, X_MAX);
      data.origins[i * 2 + 1] = rng();

      // The sign picks the canvas, the magnitude drives size, parallax,
      // brightness and softness. A particle exactly at 0 would be on the
      // content plane and belongs to neither layer, so the range excludes it.
      const inFront = rng() < frontShare;
      data.depths[i] = inFront
        ? randRange(rng, DEPTH_FLOOR, 1)
        : -randRange(rng, DEPTH_FLOOR, 1);

      data.seeds[i * 4] = rng() * Math.PI * 2;
      data.seeds[i * 4 + 1] = rng() * Math.PI * 2;
      data.seeds[i * 4 + 2] = rng();
      // Size jitter on top of the depth ramp. Without it the depth ordering is
      // perfectly legible from size alone, which reads as a diagram.
      data.seeds[i * 4 + 3] = randRange(rng, 0.7, 1.3);
    }

    const colA = new Color(colorA);
    const colB = new Color(colorB);
    const bg = new Color(background);
    const shared = {
      background: bg,
      colorA: colA,
      colorB: colB,
      speed,
      wander,
      minSize: lo,
      maxSize: hi,
    };

    const layers = [
      createLayer(back, data, { ...shared, zSign: -1, opaque: true, opacity }),
      createLayer(front, data, {
        ...shared,
        zSign: 1,
        opaque: false,
        opacity: opacity * FRONT_OPACITY,
      }),
    ];

    const resize = (w: number, h: number) => {
      // Population from area, not a fixed number, so one density reads right in
      // a 320px card and a 2000px hero. The buffers already hold `total`
      // particles in scattered order, so a prefix is still an even field —
      // nothing is reallocated.
      const megapixels = (w * h) / 1_000_000;
      const count = clamp(Math.round(megapixels * density), MIN_COUNT, total);

      for (const layer of layers) {
        layer.renderer.setSize(w, h);
        // `setSize` writes literal px into the canvas's inline style, which
        // beats any class. Re-asserting percentages keeps it fluid.
        layer.canvas.style.width = '100%';
        layer.canvas.style.height = '100%';
        layer.uniforms.uResolution.value = [
          layer.renderer.gl.drawingBufferWidth,
          layer.renderer.gl.drawingBufferHeight,
        ];
        layer.uniforms.uPixelRatio.value = layer.renderer.dpr;
        layer.geometry.setInstancedCount(count);
      }
    };

    const draw = (elapsed: number) => {
      for (const layer of layers) {
        layer.uniforms.uElapsed.value = elapsed;
        layer.renderer.render({ scene: layer.mesh });
      }
    };

    resize(size.current.width, size.current.height);
    stage.current = { layers, resize, draw };
    draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);

    // Two contexts means two ways to be dropped, and a layer nobody hears lose
    // its context is a blank canvas for the rest of the page's life, with no
    // fallback. Either loss retires both layers; `preventDefault` is required
    // or the browser will never offer a restore.
    const onLost = (event: Event): void => {
      event.preventDefault();
      setUnsupported(true);
    };
    for (const layer of layers) layer.canvas.addEventListener('webglcontextlost', onLost);

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      for (const layer of layers) {
        layer.canvas.removeEventListener('webglcontextlost', onLost);
        // ogl has no `dispose()`: `remove()` deletes the VAOs and every buffer,
        // then the program and its shaders, and only `WEBGL_lose_context` gives
        // the context itself back. This component holds two of them.
        layer.geometry.remove();
        layer.program.remove();
        loseContext(layer.renderer.gl);
        layer.canvas.width = 0;
        layer.canvas.height = 0;
        layer.canvas.remove();
      }
    };
  }, [
    ready,
    density,
    maxCount,
    split,
    minSize,
    maxSize,
    speed,
    wander,
    opacity,
    colorA,
    colorB,
    background,
    seed,
  ]);

  // Resize is its own effect: a reflow costs two `setSize` calls and an
  // instanced-count change, never a rebuild of the shared buffers.
  useEffect(() => {
    stage.current?.resize(width, height);
    if (reduced) stage.current?.draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);
  }, [width, height, reduced]);

  useRaf(
    (_dt, elapsed) => stage.current?.draw(elapsed),
    ready && inView && visible && !reduced && !unsupported,
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Per layer: `geometry.remove()` deletes the VAOs and every buffer, `program.remove()` deletes the shaders and the program, `loseContext(gl)` hands the context back through `WEBGL_lose_context` — ogl has no `dispose()` and nothing else releases a context — then the canvas backing store is zeroed and the node removed. Both layers are torn down in the same cleanup, so the component never holds one context after the other has gone.

**Reduced motion.** The rAF subscription is never made and both layers are drawn once at `elapsed` 0. That is a complete frame, not a collapsed one: the scatter, depths, sizes, tints and wrap fade are all per-particle seeds that already vary at t=0, so the still shows the same depth split, in front of and behind the same text, with only the drift absent. Resizing redraws the same still in both layers.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Trying to do this with one canvas. A canvas is a single stacking-context leaf, so DOM content cannot be interleaved with parts of it. Two contexts is not an inefficiency here, it is the requirement — and it is two of the roughly sixteen a Chromium renderer process allows, which is exactly why both are released on unmount.
- Making the front canvas additive. With `alpha: true` the destination is zero, so an additive particle over text is a flat colour patch: the layer stops looking like light and starts looking like a sticker.
- Forgetting `pointer-events: none` on the front layer. It covers the content by construction, so every link and button underneath it stops responding, and nothing about the failure looks graphical.
- Letting a particle sit at depth exactly 0. `aDepth * uZSign <= 0.0` rejects it in BOTH layers, so it is uploaded, transformed and never seen — a silent leak of the population.
- Rejecting with `discard` in the fragment shader instead of parking the vertex. `discard` still rasterises the quad and runs the shader per fragment; a clip-space position outside the frustum throws the primitive away after four vertex invocations.
- Writing `gl_Position = vec4(2.0)` for the rejection. w is then 2, the perspective divide brings it back to exactly 1.0 on every axis, and the vertex survives clipping at the frustum boundary — a row of specks in the corner.
- Giving both layers the same attribute descriptor objects. ogl mutates them with a buffer handle belonging to the first context, and the second layer then renders from a buffer its context has never heard of.
- Assuming `renderer.setSize` leaves the CSS alone. ogl writes literal px into the canvas inline style, which beats any class, so the percentages must be re-asserted after every call in both layers.

## Notes

- The content is a DOM sibling, not a texture. It stays selectable, focusable and available to a screen reader while particles pass on both sides of it — which is the entire reason to accept two contexts instead of drawing the text into the field.
- ogl rather than three: two contexts, two instanced meshes, no lights, no cameras and no scene graph. `renderer.render` is called without a camera, so ogl skips frustum culling and the matrix uniforms — the shader writes clip space itself.
- `depth: false` on both contexts. The depth ORDER is expressed by which canvas a particle lands on, so a z-buffer would be memory plus a clear per frame for no result.
- Sizes are authored in CSS pixels and scaled by the pixel ratio in the shader, so the field is identical across a dpr change and nothing rebuilds when one happens.
- GLSL ES 1.00 with no derivative functions — the anti-aliasing floor is `1.0 / sizePx`, exact for a quad of that pixel size — so the same source compiles under a WebGL1 fallback context.

## Definition of done

Particles visibly pass both behind and in front of the text, and the text is still selectable with the mouse while they do. There is no horizontal line anywhere in the container where the field changes character. Near particles are larger, softer and move further per second than far ones. Links inside the content still respond to hover and click. Resize narrow and wide: discs stay circular and the population changes without a stutter. Two contexts per instance, both released on unmount — mount and unmount six instances and none of the earlier ones go black.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Dual-Direction Scrub Entrance

Two elements arrive on the same scrubbed trigger from different directions — the copy rises 60px, the panel slides in from the side by 55% of its own width. Because both tweens sit at position 0 of one timeline, their progress is identical at every scroll position, so the pair reads as one composed arrival. The 0.6s scrub lets them keep moving briefly after the wheel stops, which is the difference between weighted and welded.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Copy rises while a panel slides in from the side, both on one scrub with 600ms of lag.

- Category: scroll
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. A single `gsap.timeline` is created with `scrollTrigger: { trigger: root, start: "top 82%", end: "top 38%", scrub: 0.6 }`. One trigger drives both elements, so there is exactly one progress value in the system.
2. The primary element gets `fromTo({ autoAlpha: 0, y: 60 }, { autoAlpha: 1, y: 0 })` at position 0. `autoAlpha` rather than `opacity`: it also flips `visibility`, so the invisible element is not a click target on the way in.
3. The secondary gets `fromTo({ autoAlpha: 0, xPercent: ±55 }, { autoAlpha: 1, xPercent: 0 })`, also at position 0. `xPercent` is a share of its own width, so the entrance distance scales with the layout instead of being tuned per breakpoint.
4. Both tweens use `ease: "none"`. Under a scrub the ease is applied to timeline time, so easing here means the two elements travel at different rates through the same scroll range and stop looking like one gesture.
5. The secondary is wrapped in an `overflow-hidden` cell. At `xPercent: 55` it begins more than half its width outside the grid column, which without the clip is a horizontal scrollbar on the whole document.
6. `scrub: 0.6` gives ScrollTrigger 0.6s to catch the timeline up to the scroll position, so the elements decelerate into place after the wheel stops rather than freezing with it.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `scrub = 0.6`
  Seconds of catch-up. `true` (zero lag) welds the animation to the wheel and reads as dragging a slider. Past about 1.5s the section is still arriving long after you have stopped, which reads as lag rather than weight. 0.6 is the point where it feels like mass.
- `start / end = 'top 82%' / 'top 38%'`
  The section begins arriving just as it clears the bottom edge and is fully composed while still in the lower half of the screen. Ending at `top 38%` means the entrance completes before the content reaches the reading position — an animation that is still resolving under the eye is unreadable.
- `rise = 60`
  Pixels of vertical travel for the copy. Enough to register as arriving; small enough that the text is legible for most of the transit, which matters because the user is reading during it.
- `slide = 55`
  Percent of the secondary's own width. Above ~60% it starts entirely outside its column and the first half of the scrub shows an empty cell; below ~30% it reads as a nudge rather than an entrance.

## API

```ts
function DualDirectionScrubEntrance(props: { primary: ReactNode; secondary: ReactNode; from?: "left" | "right"; rise?: number; slide?: number; scrub?: number; start?: string; end?: string; scrollerRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `primary: ReactNode`
  Rises from below. The reading anchor — usually the copy.
- `secondary: ReactNode`
  Slides in horizontally. Usually the card, figure or panel.
- `from: "left" | "right"` — default `'right'`
  Which edge the secondary enters from. Also flips the grid order.
- `rise: number` — default `60`
  Pixels the primary rises through.
- `slide: number` — default `55`
  Secondary travel as a percentage of its own width.
- `scrub: number` — default `0.6`
  Seconds of catch-up behind the scroll position.
- `start: string` — default `'top 82%'`
  ScrollTrigger start.
- `end: string` — default `'top 38%'`
  ScrollTrigger end.
- `scrollerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>`
  The scroll container that owns the scroll position. Omit for the document.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the grid container via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function DualDirectionScrubEntrance({
  primary,
  secondary,
  from = 'right',
  rise = 60,
  slide = 55,
  scrub = 0.6,
  start = 'top 82%',
  end = 'top 38%',
  scrollerRef,
  className,
}: DualDirectionScrubEntranceProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const primaryRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const secondaryRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  useGsap(
    gsap,
    () => {
      const container = root.current;
      const a = primaryRef.current;
      const b = secondaryRef.current;
      if (!container || !a || !b || reduced) return;

      const tl = gsap.timeline({
        scrollTrigger: {
          trigger: container,
          scroller: scrollerRef?.current ?? undefined,
          start,
          end,
          // The number, not `true`. `true` welds the timeline to the wheel and
          // the section stops moving in the same millisecond the wheel does.
          scrub,
          invalidateOnRefresh: true,
        },
      });

      // `fromTo`, deliberately, and not `from`. A `from` tween on a scrubbed
      // trigger renders its start state immediately at build time and then
      // treats the element's *current* values as the destination — so a second
      // tween, a resize, or React re-applying a style mid-scroll silently
      // rewrites where the animation is heading. Stating both ends makes the
      // timeline idempotent.
      tl.fromTo(
        a,
        { autoAlpha: 0, y: rise },
        { autoAlpha: 1, y: 0, ease: 'none', duration: 1 },
        0,
      );

      tl.fromTo(
        b,
        { autoAlpha: 0, xPercent: from === 'right' ? slide : -slide },
        { autoAlpha: 1, xPercent: 0, ease: 'none', duration: 1 },
        // Position 0: both tweens share one progress value. Offsetting them
        // would make the pair read as a queue instead of a single arrival.
        0,
      );
    },
    root,
    [from, rise, slide, scrub, start, end, reduced],
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `useGsap` builds the timeline inside a `gsap.context` and reverts it on unmount or any prop change. The revert kills the ScrollTrigger and restores the inline `transform`, `opacity` and `visibility` the tweens wrote — without it an unmount mid-scrub leaves the panel permanently half-slid and invisible if React reuses the node.

**Reduced motion.** No timeline and no trigger are created, so both elements render in their final layout position at full opacity on first paint. Nothing is hidden waiting for a scroll that the user may never make.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- `gsap.from()` on a scrubbed trigger. It renders the start state immediately at build time and treats whatever the element's values happen to be as the destination — so any later style change silently rewrites the target and the element ends up somewhere other than where the layout says. `fromTo` states both ends and is idempotent under a scrub.
- Two separate ScrollTriggers, one per element. Their start positions are computed from their own bounding boxes, so on a tall screen the copy is already finished before the panel has begun, and the composition falls apart at exactly the viewport heights you did not test.
- Easing a scrubbed tween. The ease is applied to timeline time, so the two elements move at different rates through the same scroll window and the pair stops reading as one gesture. Use `ease: "none"` and let the scrub supply the smoothing.
- No `overflow-hidden` around the sliding element. At `xPercent: 55` it sits outside its column at the start of the scrub, which extends the document width and adds a horizontal scrollbar that appears and disappears as you scroll.
- Using `opacity` instead of `autoAlpha`. The invisible element still receives pointer events, so a link inside a panel that has not arrived yet is clickable and focusable.
- Omitting `invalidateOnRefresh`. `xPercent` and the trigger boundaries are both derived from measurements taken at build time; after a resize the panel travels the wrong distance and starts at the wrong scroll position.

## Notes

- `from="left"` also reverses the grid order, so the panel enters from the side it visually occupies rather than crossing the copy on its way in.
- The `will-change-transform` hints sit on the two moving wrappers rather than on their contents, so the promoted layer is created once and the children are not each given their own.

## Definition of done

Scroll the section up from the bottom: the copy rises and the panel comes in from the right at exactly the same rate, both finishing together before the section reaches the middle of the screen. Stop the wheel mid-entrance and they keep moving for about half a second before settling. Scroll back down and the entrance reverses. No horizontal scrollbar appears at any point. With reduced motion on, the section is composed and static from the start.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Earnings Chart Card

A grey dashboard card with a Weekly / Monthly / Yearly switch and twelve rounded Recharts bars, each standing in a full-height grey track. The newest bar is the bucket still running, so it is drawn in the darker active tone and its value is the "Earned so far" headline, counted up in dollars with a chip comparing it to the bar before. Hovering another bar moves the highlight there, fades in an outline ring around its track, opens a small tooltip and switches the headline and chip to that bar.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

An "Earned so far" card of rounded bars in grey tracks; the current or hovered bar darkens, gets an outline ring and drives the headline.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: recharts@^3.10.1

## How it works

1. The tracks are the `Bar` `background`, given as a render function. Recharts calls it once per category with the full-height column (`x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `index`); it draws a `--color-chart-track` rect with an 8px corner radius and, around it, a second rect 3px larger on every side with no fill and a 1.5px stroke in the tone's `-active` colour.
2. The ring is always mounted. Its `opacity` is 1 only for `index === hovered`, and a 150ms `transition-opacity` fades it in and out, so moving across bars reads as the ring sliding between columns.
3. `onMouseMove` stores `state.activeTooltipIndex` in `hovered` when `isTooltipActive` is true and the index is finite; `onMouseLeave` clears it. The focused bar is `hovered ?? data.length - 1`. Each bar is a `Cell` whose fill is the `-active` colour for the focused bar and the base `chart-N` colour otherwise, with a 200ms `transition-[fill]`.
4. The headline renders the focused bar through `ChartHeadline` with a "$" formatter, so it counts from the old value to the new one in 320ms. Its chip is `describeDelta(focused, previous)`; the first bar has nothing before it, so the chip is hidden. The label reads "Earned so far" at rest and "Earned · W3" while hovering.
5. A period can carry fixed Y ticks. The weekly set uses `[0, 3000, 5000, 10000]` ("$0 $3K $5K $10K") as in the preview; the others leave `ticks` out and get four automatic ticks from `tickCount`. All ticks go through `formatCompact` with the "$" prefix.
6. The `Tooltip` has `cursor={false}` because the ring already marks the column. Its content maps `activeIndex` from `null` to -1 first, then shows the bar's value and its change against the bar before.
7. Choosing a period clears `hovered`, updates internal state only when `period` is uncontrolled, and calls `onPeriodChange`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `bar shape = radius 8, maxBarSize 32, barCategoryGap 30%`
  Slim pill bars inside slightly wider-looking tracks match the preview; the size cap keeps six yearly bars from turning into blocks.
- `hover ring = 3px outside the track, radius 11, 1.5px stroke, 150ms opacity fade`
  The gap separates the ring from the grey track so it reads as an outline, and the chart margin is 3px wider on the top and right so the ring is never clipped.
- `weekly ticks = [0, 3000, 5000, 10000]`
  Uneven on purpose, as in the preview: the $3K and $5K rules help read the many smaller weeks while $10K marks the peaks.
- `plot height = 248px`
  A fixed plot box gives `ResponsiveContainer` a definite height while the card grows with its header.
- `motion = bars 450ms, tooltip 160ms, bar fill 200ms, ring 150ms, count-up 320ms`
  Fast enough to follow a pointer sweeping across twelve bars, and all of it is off under reduced motion.

## API

```ts
function EarningsChartCard(props?: EarningsChartCardProps): JSX.Element
type EarningsChartCardProps = { title?: string; periods?: EarningsPeriod[]; period?: string; defaultPeriod?: string; onPeriodChange?: (id: string) => void; tone?: ChartTone; valuePrefix?: string; periodControl?: "segmented" | "select"; className?: string }
type EarningsPeriod = { id: string; label: string; data: { label: string; value: number }[]; ticks?: number[] }
```

- `title: string` — default `"Earned so far"`
  Header label while nothing is hovered.
- `periods: EarningsPeriod[]` — default `EARNINGS_PERIODS`
  Data sets for the switch, oldest bar first; the last bar is the current one. `ticks` fixes the Y ticks.
- `period: string`
  Controlled period id.
- `defaultPeriod: string` — default `first period id`
  Initial period when uncontrolled.
- `onPeriodChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called with the chosen period id.
- `tone: ChartTone` — default `2`
  Bar hue; the current or hovered bar and the ring use its `-active` step.
- `valuePrefix: string` — default `"$"`
  Prefix for the headline, axis ticks and tooltip.
- `periodControl: "segmented" | "select"` — default `"segmented"`
  Segmented switch, or a calendar pill that opens a listbox.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function EarningsChartCard({
  title = "Earned so far",
  periods = EARNINGS_PERIODS,
  period,
  defaultPeriod,
  onPeriodChange,
  tone = 2,
  valuePrefix = "$",
  periodControl = "segmented",
  className,
}: EarningsChartCardProps = {}) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const [innerPeriod, setInnerPeriod] = useState(defaultPeriod ?? periods[0]?.id ?? "");
  const periodId = period ?? innerPeriod;
  const active = periods.find((p) => p.id === periodId) ?? periods[0];
  const data = active?.data ?? [];
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState<number | null>(null);

  // The highlighted bar is the hovered one, else the newest (the bucket still running).
  const focus = hovered ?? data.length - 1;
  const point = data[focus];
  const before = focus > 0 ? data[focus - 1] : undefined;
  const delta = point && before ? describeDelta(point.value, before.value) : null;
  const money = (value: number) => `${valuePrefix}${formatNumber(value)}`;

  const selectPeriod = (id: string) => {
    setHovered(null);
    if (period === undefined) setInnerPeriod(id);
    onPeriodChange?.(id);
  };

  // Grey full-height track behind each bar, plus an outline ring that fades in on the hovered one.
  const renderTrack = ({ x, y, width, height, index }: TrackShape) => {
    if (x === undefined || y === undefined || width === undefined || height === undefined) return <g />;
    return (
      <g pointerEvents="none">
        <rect x={x} y={y} width={width} height={height} rx={BAR_RADIUS} fill="var(--color-chart-track)" />
        <rect
          x={x - RING_OFFSET}
          y={y - RING_OFFSET}
          width={width + RING_OFFSET * 2}
          height={height + RING_OFFSET * 2}
          rx={BAR_RADIUS + RING_OFFSET}
          fill="none"
          stroke={toneActiveColor(tone)}
          strokeWidth={1.5}
          opacity={index === hovered ? 1 : 0}
          className="transition-opacity duration-150 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none"
        />
      </g>
    );
  };

  return (
    <section aria-label={`${title} chart`} className={cx(CHART_CARD_FRAME, "gap-3", className)}>
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 px-2 pt-2 @md:flex-row @md:items-start @md:justify-between">
        <ChartHeadline
          label={hovered !== null && point ? `Earned · ${point.label}` : title}
          value={point?.value ?? 0}
          format={money}
          delta={delta}
          swapKey={`${periodId}-${hovered ?? "current"}`}
          reducedMotion={reduced}
        />
        {periods.length > 1 ? (
          <ChartPeriodControl
            options={periods}
            value={periodId}
            onChange={selectPeriod}
            variant={periodControl}
            label={`${title} period`}
            className="self-start"
          />
        ) : null}
      </div>

      <div className="h-[248px] w-full pe-2 pb-1">
        <ResponsiveContainer width="100%" height="100%" initialDimension={{ width: 520, height: 248 }}>
          <BarChart
            data={data}
            barCategoryGap="30%"
            margin={{ top: RING_OFFSET + 4, right: RING_OFFSET, bottom: 0, left: 0 }}
            onMouseMove={(state) => {
              const next = Number(state?.activeTooltipIndex);
              if (state?.isTooltipActive && Number.isFinite(next)) setHovered(next);
            }}
            onMouseLeave={() => setHovered(null)}
          >
            <CartesianGrid vertical={false} stroke={GRID_STROKE} strokeDasharray="4 4" />
            <YAxis
              width={48}
              domain={[0, "auto"]}
              ticks={active?.ticks}
              tickCount={4}
              tickFormatter={(v: number) => formatCompact(v, valuePrefix)}
              tickLine={false}
              axisLine={false}
              tick={AXIS_TICK}
            />
            <XAxis
              dataKey="label"
              tickLine={false}
              axisLine={false}
              tickMargin={10}
              interval="preserveStartEnd"
              minTickGap={6}
              tick={AXIS_TICK}
            />
            <Tooltip
              cursor={false}
              offset={16}
              isAnimationActive={!reduced}
              animationDuration={160}
              wrapperStyle={{ outline: "none", zIndex: 10 }}
              content={({ active: isActive, activeIndex }) => {
                const i = activeIndex == null ? -1 : Number(activeIndex);
                const at = data[i];
                if (!isActive || !at) return null;
                const prev = data[i - 1];
                return (
                  <ChartTooltipCard
                    title={at.label}
                    rows={[
                      { key: "earned", label: "Earned", tone, value: money(at.value) },
                      ...(prev
                        ? [{ key: "change", label: `vs ${prev.label}`, value: describeDelta(at.value, prev.value).label }]
                        : []),
                    ]}
                  />
                );
              }}
            />
            <Bar
              dataKey="value"
              name="Earned"
              radius={BAR_RADIUS}
              maxBarSize={32}
              background={renderTrack}
              isAnimationActive={!reduced}
              animationDuration={450}
            >
              {data.map((p, i) => (
                <Cell
                  key={p.label}
                  fill={i === focus ? toneActiveColor(tone) : toneColor(tone)}
                  className="transition-[fill] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none"
                />
              ))}
            </Bar>
          </BarChart>
        </ResponsiveContainer>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `useCountUp` cancels its animation frame on target change and unmount, `useReducedMotion` unsubscribes its media-query listener, and `ResponsiveContainer` disconnects its resize observer. The card adds no listeners or timers of its own.

**Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `useReducedMotion` turns off `isAnimationActive` on the Bar and the Tooltip, the headline shows its value without counting, and the number fade, bar fill transition and ring fade are disabled with `motion-reduce:` variants.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using `Bar background={{ fill }}` for the tracks. The object form cannot vary per bar, so there is nowhere to draw the hover ring; the render function gets `index` and can.
- Leaving the chart margin at 0. The ring sits 3px outside the track, and the track runs to the top of the plot, so the ring's top and the last column's right edge would be cut off.
- Reading `activeIndex` with `Number()` directly. Recharts passes `null` when inactive and `Number(null)` is 0, which would pin the tooltip to the first bar.
- Comparing the first bar with `undefined`. There is no bar before it, so the chip is hidden instead of showing "New".

## Notes

- `EARNINGS_PERIODS` and the `EarningsPoint` and `EarningsPeriod` types are exported. Weekly ends on $7,462 against $6,500 ("+14.8%"), monthly on $32,450 against $29,100 ("+11.5%") and yearly on $362,400 against $318,900 ("+13.6%").
- BoardUI's preview shows month labels under the Weekly tab; here each tab has its own buckets (W1 to W12, Jan to Dec, 2019 to 2024) so the labels match the switch.
- The frame, headline, period switch and tooltip card come from `line-chart-card-parts.tsx`.

## Definition of done

The card shows "Earned so far", "$7,462" and a lime "+14.8%" chip with Weekly selected, Y ticks $0, $3K, $5K and $10K, and twelve rounded lime bars in grey tracks with the last one darker. Hovering a bar darkens it, rings its track, shows a tooltip and switches the headline to "Earned · W<n>" and that value. Choosing Monthly shows "$32,450" and "+11.5%"; Yearly shows "$362,400" and "+13.6%".

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Eased Number Counter

A number tweens from one value to another on `power2.inOut` rather than linearly, so it reads as loading rather than as a progress meter — slow to commit, quick through the middle, easing onto the final figure. The thing being tweened is a plain numeric object; the string on screen is formatted from it on every update and written with `textContent`, so React never re-renders while the count runs. A transparent sizer reserves the width of the wider endpoint, so nothing after the counter moves as digits are added.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A statistic that counts up on an eased curve and settles on its exact final figure without shifting the layout.

- Category: text
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. A local object `{ v: from }` is the tween target. `gsap.to(counter, { v: to, duration, ease })` interpolates the number; the DOM is not the tween target at all.
2. `onUpdate` calls a `write()` closure that does `el.textContent = prefix + format.format(counter.v) + suffix`. Writing `textContent` rather than React children means the tween never touches the reconciler.
3. The `Intl.NumberFormat` is built once in a `useMemo` keyed on `[locale, decimals, grouping]` — three primitives, so the memo actually holds. `minimumFractionDigits === maximumFractionDigits` also performs the rounding, so no `Math.round` or `toFixed` is needed in the tick.
4. `onComplete` assigns `counter.v = to` and writes once more. Tween interpolation lands on values like 99.999999997, and a headline number stopping one unit short of itself is a real bug report.
5. Before the tween starts, `write()` runs once with `v = from`, so the live node is never empty on the first frame and the element does not pop into existence when the tween begins.
6. The width reservation compares `format.format(to).length` against `format.format(from).length` and renders the longer of the two as a `text-transparent` cell stacked under the live node in an `inline-grid`, both at `col-start-1 row-start-1`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `DURATION = 1.6`
  Seconds. Under ~1s the eye cannot track the digits and the effect is just a flicker before the answer; past ~2.5s the reader has finished the sentence around it and is waiting on a number that has stopped being interesting.
- `EASE = 'power2.inOut'`
  The in-out pair is what separates a counter from a progress bar. `none` reads as a machine metering out a value; `power2.out` starts at full speed and looks like it began before you looked. The slow start is the part that reads as "committing".
- `VIEW_THRESHOLD = 0.6`
  60% of the element visible before counting. A stat that starts at 1% visibility has finished before it clears the fold, so the reader arrives at a static number and never sees the effect.
- `decimals = 0`
  Also the rounding rule, via matched `minimumFractionDigits`/`maximumFractionDigits`. Leaving them unmatched lets `Intl` vary the digit count between frames, so the string length oscillates and the number jitters horizontally.

## API

```ts
function EasedNumberCounter(props: { to: number; from?: number; duration?: number; ease?: string; delay?: number; locale?: string; decimals?: number; grouping?: boolean; prefix?: string; suffix?: string; startOnView?: boolean; className?: string; onComplete?: () => void }): JSX.Element
```

- `to: number`
  The value to land on.
- `from: number` — default `0`
  The value to start from.
- `duration: number` — default `1.6`
  Seconds of counting.
- `ease: string` — default `'power2.inOut'`
  Any GSAP ease string. `none` makes it read as a meter.
- `delay: number` — default `0`
  Seconds to wait after the trigger before counting.
- `locale: string`
  BCP 47 tag. Omitted uses the runtime default locale.
- `decimals: number` — default `0`
  Fixed fraction digits. Also the rounding.
- `grouping: boolean` — default `true`
  Thousands separators.
- `prefix: string` — default `''`
  Literal text before the number, e.g. a currency sign.
- `suffix: string` — default `''`
  Literal text after the number, e.g. a percent sign.
- `startOnView: boolean` — default `true`
  Count when scrolled into view rather than on mount.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the outer span via `cn`.
- `onComplete: () => void`
  Fired once the final figure is written.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const DURATION = 1.6;
const EASE = 'power2.inOut';
const VIEW_THRESHOLD = 0.6;

export function EasedNumberCounter({
  to,
  from = 0,
  duration = DURATION,
  ease = EASE,
  delay = 0,
  locale,
  decimals = 0,
  grouping = true,
  prefix = '',
  suffix = '',
  startOnView = true,
  className,
  onComplete,
}: EasedNumberCounterProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);
  const live = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const { inView } = useInView(root, { threshold: VIEW_THRESHOLD, once: true });

  // Held in a ref so an inline arrow from the caller does not restart the
  // count on every parent render.
  const complete = useRef(onComplete);
  complete.current = onComplete;

  // One formatter for the whole tween, keyed only on the primitives that
  // change it. An options *object* prop would be a new reference every render
  // and would rebuild the formatter — and restart the tween — continuously.
  const format = useMemo(
    () =>
      new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {
        minimumFractionDigits: decimals,
        maximumFractionDigits: decimals,
        useGrouping: grouping,
      }),
    [locale, decimals, grouping],
  );

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = live.current;
    if (!el) return;

    const counter = { v: from };
    const write = () => {
      el.textContent = `${prefix}${format.format(counter.v)}${suffix}`;
    };

    // Reduced motion is the final figure, immediately — not a blank slot and
    // not a 0.01s tween that still flickers through every intermediate value.
    if (reduced) {
      counter.v = to;
      write();
      complete.current?.();
      return;
    }

    write();
    if (startOnView && !inView) return;

    const tween = gsap.to(counter, {
      v: to,
      duration,
      ease,
      delay,
      overwrite: true,
      onUpdate: write,
      onComplete: () => {
        // Snap to the exact target. Floating-point tweens land on
        // 99.99999999 often enough that a counter visibly stopping one short
        // of its own headline number is a real bug report.
        counter.v = to;
        write();
        complete.current?.();
      },
    });

    return () => {
      tween.kill();
    };
  }, [
    from,
    to,
    duration,
    ease,
    delay,
    prefix,
    suffix,
    format,
    reduced,
    inView,
    startOnView,
  ]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The effect returns `tween.kill()`. Because the tween target is a local object rather than a DOM node, nothing is left written to the element beyond the final string, and there are no inline styles to clear.

**Reduced motion.** Writes the final formatted figure immediately and fires `onComplete`, with no tween created at all. It is never left blank and never runs a shortened tween that still flickers through intermediate values.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Constructing `new Intl.NumberFormat()` inside `onUpdate`. It costs tens of microseconds and it is being built 60-120 times a second per counter; a page of eight stats spends milliseconds a frame building formatters it throws away.
- Tweening the string, or holding the value in `useState`. A `setState` per frame re-renders the subtree at display refresh rate, and worse, any unrelated parent render snaps the number back to the last committed value mid-count.
- Rendering the live value as React children. React will diff and overwrite whatever the tween wrote, so the count freezes on the first parent re-render.
- Not snapping to the exact target in `onComplete`. Floating-point interpolation lands near, not on, the target — the counter finishes at 99,999 instead of 100,000.
- Letting the box size itself from the current text. Every added digit widens the element and shoves the following copy sideways; the count ends up looking like a layout bug.
- Using `visibility: hidden` for the sizer. That removes it from the accessibility tree as well, and the transparent copy is the only readable text on the element — the live node is `aria-hidden` because it is mid-count garbage.

## Notes

- The `onComplete` callback is held in a ref that is reassigned on every render, so passing an inline arrow from the caller does not restart the count on every parent render.
- A number formatting *options object* prop was deliberately not exposed: an object literal is a new reference every render, which would rebuild the formatter, invalidate the effect, and restart the tween continuously.

## Definition of done

Scroll the stat into view: the number counts from its start value, decelerates, and stops on exactly the stated figure — check the last digit. Nothing to the right of the number moves while it counts. Enable reduced motion, reload, and the final figure is present on first paint. Force a parent re-render mid-count and the number keeps counting rather than snapping backwards.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Event Detail Popover

Wraps any trigger, usually a calendar event chip, in the kit Popover and shows the event behind it: a colour key and title, the long date, the time range, location, a meeting code with a Join button, and the guest list with RSVP labels. Edit and Delete sit as neutral icon buttons in the header. Every action closes the popover before handing the event to the caller, so a delete that removes the chip is safe. `EventDetails` is exported on its own for side panels.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Anchored calendar event card: colour key, date and time, location, meeting code with Join, guest RSVPs, edit and delete.

- Category: overlay
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1, @internationalized/date@^3.12.4, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. `EventDetailPopover` keeps its own open state (or takes `isOpen` / `onOpenChange`) and renders `PopoverTrigger` with the child as trigger and a 340px `Popover` placed "bottom start". React Aria positions and flips it, Escape closes it and focus returns to the chip.
2. The card header is a 12px rounded square in the event colour (the `dot` class from `calendarEventColorStyles`), a React Aria `Heading slot="title"` that names the dialog, and the long date from `formatEventDate`, which formats a fixed UTC noon instant so server and client print the same day.
3. A tinted `dl` lists time ("11:30 – 11:45", or "All day"), location and the meeting code; each label is an icon plus an `sr-only` term. The Join button sits at the end of the meeting row.
4. Guests render as initials avatars with the name and an RSVP label (Organizer, Going, Maybe, Declined, Awaiting); declined names are struck through. Past `maxAttendees` the rest collapse into "+N more", and the header counts guests and how many are going.
5. Join, Edit and Delete are wrapped by `act()`: it sets the popover closed first and then calls the handler, so removing the event in `onDelete` unmounts a closed trigger instead of yanking an open overlay.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `popover width = 340px`
  Fits the longest row (meeting code plus Join) on one line; the kit Popover caps it at 100vw − 32px on phones.
- `placement = "bottom start"`
  Opens under the chip aligned to its start edge, like the template; React Aria flips it when the chip is near the bottom.
- `maxAttendees = 4`
  Keeps the card under ~420px tall so it fits beside a month cell without scrolling.
- `colour key = 12px, radius 4px`
  Matches the chip tint so the card reads as the same event at a glance.

## API

```ts
function formatEventDate(date: { year: number; month: number; day: number }, locale?: string, options?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions): string
function EventDetails(props: { event: CalendarEvent; onJoin?: (e: CalendarEvent) => void; onEdit?: (e: CalendarEvent) => void; onDelete?: (e: CalendarEvent) => void; joinLabel?: string; locale?: string; hourCycle?: 12 | 24; maxAttendees?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function EventDetailPopover(props: EventDetailsProps & { children: ReactNode; isOpen?: boolean; defaultOpen?: boolean; onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void; placement?: Placement; closeOnAction?: boolean }): JSX.Element
```

- `event: CalendarEvent`
  The event to show (title, colour, start/end, location, meetingCode, attendees, description).
- `children: ReactNode`
  The trigger; must forward its ref and spread props.
- `isOpen / defaultOpen / onOpenChange: boolean / boolean / (open) => void` — default `uncontrolled, closed`
  Open state.
- `onJoin: (event) => void`
  Shows the Join button on the meeting row.
- `onEdit: (event) => void`
  Shows the edit icon button.
- `onDelete: (event) => void`
  Shows the delete icon button; always closes first.
- `placement: Placement` — default `"bottom start"`
  Preferred side; flips when needed.
- `closeOnAction: boolean` — default `true`
  Close after Join or Edit.
- `maxAttendees: number` — default `4`
  Guests listed before "+N more".
- `hourCycle: 12 | 24` — default `24`
  Time format.
- `locale: string` — default `"en-US"`
  Locale for dates and times.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function EventDetails({
  event,
  onJoin,
  onEdit,
  onDelete,
  joinLabel = "Join",
  locale = "en-US",
  hourCycle = 24,
  maxAttendees = 4,
  className,
}: EventDetailsProps) {
  const c = calendarEventColorStyles[event.color];
  const dateLabel = formatEventDate(event.start, locale);
  const sameDay =
    event.start.year === event.end.year && event.start.month === event.end.month && event.start.day === event.end.day;
  const timeLabel = event.allDay
    ? "All day"
    : `${formatEventTime(event.start, { locale, hourCycle })} – ${formatEventTime(event.end, { locale, hourCycle })}${
        sameDay ? "" : ` (${formatEventDate(event.end, locale, { month: "short", day: "numeric" })})`
      }`;
  const attendees = event.attendees ?? [];
  const going = attendees.filter((a) => a.status === "accepted" || a.organizer).length;
  const shown = attendees.slice(0, maxAttendees);
  const hidden = attendees.length - shown.length;

  return (
    <div className={cx("flex flex-col gap-3", className)}>
      <div className="flex items-start gap-2.5 ps-1">
        <span aria-hidden className={cx("mt-1.5 size-3 shrink-0 rounded-[4px]", c.dot)} />
        <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-0.5">
          <Heading slot="title" className="text-headline-semibold break-words text-text-primary">
            {event.title}
          </Heading>
          <p className="text-body-2-regular text-text-secondary">{dateLabel}</p>
        </div>
        {onEdit || onDelete ? (
          <div className="-me-1 -mt-1 flex shrink-0 items-center gap-0.5">
            {onEdit ? (
              <Button
                variant="secondary"
                size="small"
                iconOnly
                leadingIcon={RiPencilLine}
                aria-label={`Edit ${event.title}`}
                onClick={() => onEdit(event)}
              />
            ) : null}
            {onDelete ? (
              <Button
                variant="secondary"
                size="small"
                iconOnly
                leadingIcon={RiDeleteBinLine}
                aria-label={`Delete ${event.title}`}
                className="hover:text-text-destructive"
                onClick={() => onDelete(event)}
              />
            ) : null}
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </div>

      <dl className="flex flex-col gap-2.5 rounded-[14px] bg-background-secondary-default p-3">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2.5">
          <dt className="shrink-0">
            <RiTimeLine aria-hidden className="size-4 text-foreground-icon-secondary" />
            <span className="sr-only">Time</span>
          </dt>
          <dd className="min-w-0 text-body-2-medium tabular-nums text-text-primary">{timeLabel}</dd>
        </div>
        {event.location ? (
          <div className="flex items-center gap-2.5">
            <dt className="shrink-0">
              <RiMapPin2Line aria-hidden className="size-4 text-foreground-icon-secondary" />
              <span className="sr-only">Location</span>
            </dt>
            <dd className="min-w-0 truncate text-body-2-regular text-text-primary">{event.location}</dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        {event.meetingCode ? (
          <div className="flex items-center gap-2.5">
            <dt className="shrink-0">
              <RiVideoOnLine aria-hidden className="size-4 text-foreground-icon-secondary" />
              <span className="sr-only">Meeting code</span>
            </dt>
            <dd className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 items-center justify-between gap-2">
              <span className="truncate font-mono text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary">{event.meetingCode}</span>
              {onJoin ? (
                <Button size="xs" onClick={() => onJoin(event)} aria-label={`${joinLabel} ${event.title}`}>
                  {joinLabel}
                </Button>
              ) : null}
            </dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </dl>

      {attendees.length > 0 ? (
        <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 px-1">
          <p className="flex items-center gap-2 text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary">
            <RiGroupLine aria-hidden className="size-4 text-foreground-icon-secondary" />
            {attendees.length} {attendees.length === 1 ? "guest" : "guests"}
            <span aria-hidden className="text-text-tertiary">·</span>
            <span>{going} going</span>
          </p>
          <ul className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
            {shown.map((person, i) => (
              <li key={person.email ?? person.name} className="flex items-center gap-2">
                <Avatar size="sm" initials={person.initials} color={AVATAR_TINTS[i % AVATAR_TINTS.length]} aria-hidden />
                <span
                  className={cx(
                    "min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-body-2-regular text-text-primary",
                    person.status === "declined" && "text-text-tertiary line-through",
                  )}
                >
                  {person.name}
                </span>
                <span className="shrink-0 text-caption-1-regular text-text-tertiary">
                  {person.organizer ? "Organizer" : RSVP_LABEL[person.status ?? "pending"]}
                </span>
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
          {hidden > 0 ? <p className="ps-8 text-caption-1-regular text-text-tertiary">+{hidden} more</p> : null}
        </div>
      ) : null}

      {event.description ? (
        <p className="border-t border-border-table px-1 pt-3 text-body-2-regular text-text-secondary">{event.description}</p>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}

export interface EventDetailPopoverProps extends Omit<EventDetailsProps, "className"> {
  /** The trigger, usually a CalendarEventChip. It must forward its ref and spread props. */
  children: ReactNode;
  isOpen?: boolean;
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (isOpen: boolean) => void;
  /** Default "bottom start"; flips when there is no room. */
  placement?: PopoverProps["placement"];
  /** Close after Join / Edit. Delete always closes. Default true. */
  closeOnAction?: boolean;
  /** Classes on the popover surface (default width 340px). */
  className?: string;
}

export function EventDetailPopover({
  children,
  event,
  isOpen: controlledOpen,
  defaultOpen = false,
  onOpenChange,
  placement = "bottom start",
  closeOnAction = true,
  onJoin,
  onEdit,
  onDelete,
  className,
  ...details
}: EventDetailPopoverProps) {
  const [uncontrolledOpen, setUncontrolledOpen] = useState(defaultOpen);
  const isOpen = controlledOpen ?? uncontrolledOpen;
  const setOpen = (next: boolean) => {
    setUncontrolledOpen(next);
    onOpenChange?.(next);
  };
  // Each action closes the popover first, then hands the event to the
  // caller, so a delete that unmounts the trigger never races the overlay.
  const act = (handler: ((e: CalendarEvent) => void) | undefined, close: boolean) =>
    handler
      ? (e: CalendarEvent) => {
          if (close) setOpen(false);
          handler(e);
        }
      : undefined;

  return (
    <PopoverTrigger isOpen={isOpen} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      {children}
      <Popover placement={placement} className={cx("w-[340px]", className)} dialogClassName="p-2">
        <EventDetails
          event={event}
          onJoin={act(onJoin, closeOnAction)}
          onEdit={act(onEdit, closeOnAction)}
          onDelete={act(onDelete, true)}
          {...details}
        />
      </Popover>
    </PopoverTrigger>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No effects of its own. The kit PopoverTrigger owns the outside-press listener and removes it on close and unmount; date formatters are cached in a module-level map.

**Reduced motion.** The kit Popover fades in 150ms and adds a 0.95 scale and 2px blur only under `motion-safe`, so reduced motion keeps just the fade.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Calling the delete handler before closing the popover. The trigger unmounts while React Aria still tracks the open overlay; close first, then remove.
- Passing a trigger that does not forward its ref. PopoverTrigger wraps the child in React Aria `Pressable`, which needs the DOM node to anchor and to restore focus.
- Formatting the date with `toLocaleDateString` on a local Date. The server and browser zones can disagree about the day; format a UTC instant built from the calendar fields.

## Notes

- Control `isOpen` from the parent when the trigger should show a selected state while open, as the demo does with the chip `selected` prop.
- Pass `closeOnAction={false}` to keep the card open after Join or Edit.

## Definition of done

Clicking the "Stand-up" chip opens a dialog named "Stand-up" under it with "Thursday, August 20", "11:30 – 11:45", "Studio 2, 4th floor", the code "brd-xqtm-wav" with a Join button, and "6 guests · 3 going" with four guests and "+2 more". Escape closes it and focus returns to the chip. Join and Edit close it and report below the card. Delete closes it, removes the chip, lowers the event count and shows Undo, which puts the event back in time order.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
