# Build: Exit Warp Before Navigate

Choosing a destination does not navigate. It plays an exit: the DOM chrome lifts and fades, the ring of cards is shoved thirty slots forward while its vertical spacing explodes and its radius collapses, the planes dissolve in index order, and only after one settle frame does the router move. The ease is expo.in, so almost nothing happens for the first half-second and then everything happens at once.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A ring of cards tears itself apart and rushes past the camera, and only then does the route change.

- Category: transition
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1, gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. Four scalars describe the ring — `position`, `spacing`, `hSpacing`, `radius` — and one `layout()` reads them: `angle = wrappedOffset(i, position, count) * (2*PI/count) * hSpacing`, then `mesh.position.set(sin(angle) * radius, offset * spacing * 0.12, cos(angle) * radius - radius)` and `mesh.rotation.y = angle`. Idle and exit both drive the same function, so no second code path can disagree about where a card belongs.
2. Idle rotation is `position += dt * 0.16` inside `setAnimationLoop`, with `dt` in seconds clamped to 50 ms — a per-frame constant would spin twice as fast on a 120 Hz display.
3. On select, a timeline fades the chrome (`opacity: 0, y: -20, 0.5s, power2.out, stagger 0.05`) and a `tl.call` pinned at an absolute 0.4s starts the warp, so the ring begins moving 0.1s before the text has finished leaving.
4. The warp is one `gsap.to` on the scalar object: `position + 30`, `spacing 0.8 -> 10`, `hSpacing 1 -> 3`, `radius 2.3 -> 0.6`, 1.4s, `expo.in`, with `onUpdate` calling `layout()`. Radius shrinking while spacing explodes is what makes the planes leave in different directions instead of receding as a group.
5. Each material tweens `opacity: 0` over 1s with `delay: 0.03 * i`, so the ring dissolves in index order rather than as a single fade.
6. The tween's `onComplete` sets a 50 ms timeout, and only that timeout calls `onNavigate`. Textures are canvas-drawn gradients with the item label baked in, so the component ships without a single image.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `duration = 1.4`
  Seconds of warp. With expo.in the perceived length is roughly half the real one; below ~1.1s the accelerating half is too brief to register and it reads as a cut, above ~1.8s the destination feels withheld.
- `shove = 30`
  Ring slots travelled during the exit. For a six-item ring that is five full revolutions — enough that individual cards stop being trackable and the ring reads as a blur rather than as a carousel scrubbing.
- `WARP_CUE = 0.4`
  Absolute seconds at which the scene warp starts, against a 0.5s chrome fade. The 0.1s overlap fuses two moves into one gesture; at 0.5 they read as sequential steps, and at 0 the ring pulls the eye off the text before it has gone.
- `FADE_STAGGER = 0.03`
  Seconds between per-card dissolves. 30 ms x 6 cards is 180 ms of sweep — visible as a direction, short enough that the last card still fades inside the warp.
- `SETTLE_MS = 50`
  GSAP fires onComplete on the same frame the tween ends, before that frame is presented. Navigating there shows one frame of the un-warped ring. One extra tick guarantees the final layout has been painted.
- `WARP_SPACING / WARP_RADIUS = 10 / 0.6`
  Vertical gap goes 0.8 -> 10 while radius goes 2.3 -> 0.6. Spreading without shrinking looks like a zoom out; shrinking without spreading looks like a dolly. Both together are the only combination that reads as the ring tearing apart around the camera.
- `IDLE_SPEED = 0.16`
  Ring slots per second at rest. One card takes about six seconds to reach the front — slow enough to read as ambience, fast enough that the ring is never mistaken for a static image.

## API

```ts
function ExitWarpNavigation(props: { items: { id: string; label: string }[]; onNavigate: (id: string) => void; children?: ReactNode; duration?: number; shove?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `items: { id: string; label: string }[]`
  Destinations. One card and one nav button each; the label is drawn into the card texture.
- `onNavigate: (id: string) => void`
  Called after the warp and its settle frame. Do the router push here.
- `children: ReactNode`
  Chrome over the canvas. Descendants marked `data-warp-chrome` fade and lift first.
- `duration: number` — default `1.4`
  Warp length in seconds.
- `shove: number` — default `30`
  Ring slots the drum travels during the warp.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the positioned wrapper.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const el = host.current;
  if (!el) return;

  // Checked in an effect, never during render: `hasWebGL()` needs `document`
  // and returning different markup on the server than on the client is a
  // hydration mismatch, not a graceful degradation.
  if (!hasWebGL() || reduced) {
    setFallback(true);
    return;
  }
  setFallback(false);

  let renderer: THREE.WebGLRenderer;
  try {
    renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true, alpha: true });
  } catch {
    // A context can still be refused between the probe and the construction —
    // the tab may have hit the browser's live-context ceiling in between. three
    // throws rather than returning null, and an uncaught throw here takes the
    // page with it.
    setFallback(true);
    return;
  }
  renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio(2));
  renderer.setClearAlpha(0);
  el.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
  renderer.domElement.style.cssText = 'display:block;width:100%;height:100%';

  const scene = new THREE.Scene();
  const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(45, 1, 0.1, 60);

  const geometry = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(1, CARD_H / CARD_W);
  const meshes: THREE.Mesh<THREE.PlaneGeometry, THREE.MeshBasicMaterial>[] = [];
  const textures: THREE.CanvasTexture[] = [];

  items.forEach((item, i) => {
    const texture = new THREE.CanvasTexture(drawCard(item.label, i, items.length));
    texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
    textures.push(texture);
    const material = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ map: texture, transparent: true });
    const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
    scene.add(mesh);
    meshes.push(mesh);
  });

  const state: Warp = {
    position: 0,
    spacing: REST_SPACING,
    hSpacing: 1,
    radius: REST_RADIUS,
  };

  /* One layout function, driven by four scalars. The idle loop and the exit
     tween both call it; there is no second code path that could disagree
     about where a card belongs. */
  const layout = () => {
    const count = meshes.length;
    const step = count > 0 ? (Math.PI * 2) / count : 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
      const mesh = meshes[i];
      if (!mesh) continue;
      const offset = wrappedOffset(i, state.position, count);
      const angle = offset * step * state.hSpacing;
      mesh.position.set(
        Math.sin(angle) * state.radius,
        offset * state.spacing * Y_PER_SLOT,
        Math.cos(angle) * state.radius - state.radius,
      );
      mesh.rotation.y = angle;
    }
  };

  const resize = () => {
    const w = el.clientWidth;
    const h = el.clientHeight;
    if (w === 0 || h === 0) return;
    renderer.setSize(w, h, false);
    camera.aspect = w / h;
    // Pull the camera back on narrow boxes so the ring never grows wider
    // than the frame; a fixed z crops the front card on a phone.
    camera.position.z = 3.2 * Math.max(1, 1.35 / camera.aspect);
    camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
  };

  const observer = new ResizeObserver(resize);
  observer.observe(el);
  resize();
  layout();

  let last = 0;
  renderer.setAnimationLoop((time) => {
    const dt = last === 0 ? 0 : Math.min((time - last) / 1000, 0.05);
    last = time;
    const b = bundle.current;
    if (b && !b.exiting) {
      // Seconds, not frames: a per-frame increment idles twice as fast on a
      // 120 Hz display as it does on 60 Hz.
      state.position += dt * IDLE_SPEED;
      layout();
    }
    renderer.render(scene, camera);
  });

  bundle.current = { renderer, scene, camera, geometry, meshes, textures, state, exiting: false };

  return () => {
    observer.disconnect();
    // A rebuild — the caller changed the item ids — must not leave the latch
    // set, or every button on the new ring is dead for the life of the page.
    exitTl.current?.kill();
    exitTl.current = null;
    exiting.current = false;
    gsap.killTweensOf(state);
    for (const mesh of meshes) gsap.killTweensOf(mesh.material);
    // disposeRenderer stops the animation loop first: a queued frame that
    // renders into a context we just released throws out of cleanup.
    disposeRenderer(renderer);
    for (const mesh of meshes) mesh.material.dispose();
    for (const texture of textures) texture.dispose();
    geometry.dispose();
    renderer.domElement.remove();
    bundle.current = null;
  };
  // `ids` stands in for `items` so a caller passing a fresh array literal
  // every render does not rebuild the whole scene each time.
  // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
}, [ids, reduced]);

const start = useCallback(
  (id: string) => {
    const b = bundle.current;
    const chromeEl = chrome.current;

    // Re-entrancy guard. Without it a double click starts two warps that
    // tween the same scalars in opposite directions and the ring jitters —
    // and on the no-GL branch below, two crossfades each ending in their own
    // `onNavigate`.
    if (exiting.current) return;
    exiting.current = true;

    const chromeTargets = chromeEl
      ? Array.from(chromeEl.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-warp-chrome]'))
      : [];

    if (!b) {
      // No GL: the static crossfade. Same shape, no warp.
      const target = chromeTargets.length > 0 ? chromeTargets : chromeEl;
      if (target) {
        // On the same ref as the GL path's timeline, so one kill on unmount
        // covers both branches — and this is the branch the build effect
        // returns early from, so it has no cleanup of its own.
        exitTl.current = gsap.timeline().to(target, {
          opacity: 0,
          duration: reduced ? 0.15 : 0.3,
          ease: 'power2.out',
          onComplete: () => navigate.current(id),
        });
      } else {
        navigate.current(id);
      }
      return;
    }

    b.exiting = true;
    const state = b.state;

    const tl = gsap.timeline();
    exitTl.current = tl;
    if (chromeTargets.length > 0) {
      tl.to(chromeTargets, {
        opacity: 0,
        y: -20,
        duration: CHROME_DURATION,
        ease: 'power2.out',
        stagger: CHROME_STAGGER,
      });
    }

    // Absolute position: the warp starts 0.1 s before the chrome finishes
    // leaving, so the two overlap into one gesture instead of reading as
    // "text goes, then something else happens".
    tl.call(
      () => {
        gsap.to(state, {
          position: state.position + shove,
          spacing: WARP_SPACING,
          hSpacing: WARP_HSPACING,
          radius: WARP_RADIUS,
          duration,
          ease: 'expo.in',
          onComplete: () => {
            // One more frame before the route changes. GSAP's onComplete
            // fires on the same frame the tween ends, so navigating here
            // shows a single frame of the un-warped ring.
            const t = setTimeout(() => navigate.current(id), SETTLE_MS);
            timers.current.push(t);
          },
        });
        for (let i = 0; i < b.meshes.length; i += 1) {
          const mesh = b.meshes[i];
          if (!mesh) continue;
          gsap.to(mesh.material, {
            opacity: 0,
            duration: 1,
            ease: 'power2.in',
            delay: FADE_STAGGER * i,
          });
        }
      },
      undefined,
      WARP_CUE,
    );
  },
  [duration, shove, reduced],
);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Disconnects the ResizeObserver, kills the tweens on the scalar object and on every material, clears the pending navigation timeout, calls `disposeRenderer` (which stops the animation loop, disposes, forces context loss and zeroes the canvas), then disposes every material, texture and the shared geometry, and removes the canvas element.

**Reduced motion.** No WebGL context is created. The same cards render as a static CSS-gradient grid, and choosing one fades the chrome over 0.15s before navigating — the transition still covers the swap, it just does not move.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Calling `router.push` in the click handler and animating afterwards. React unmounts the canvas as the route resolves, so the warp plays for two frames and then disappears; the navigation must be the last step, inside the tween's completion.
- No re-entrancy guard. A double click starts two warps tweening the same four scalars from different origins — the ring jitters and the second navigation fires into an already-unmounting tree.
- Navigating in `onComplete` instead of one tick later. The final frame has not been presented, so a single frame of the intact ring flashes just before the route changes.
- Calling `renderer.dispose()` and stopping there. The GL context stays alive; Chromium kills the oldest context once about sixteen exist, so an unrelated canvas elsewhere on the page goes black. `disposeRenderer` also calls `forceContextLoss()` and zeroes the backing store.
- Leaving the exit tweens running through unmount. They keep writing to disposed materials and to a scalar object nobody reads; the material writes throw once the context is gone. Cleanup kills the tweens on the state object and every material before disposing.
- Deciding whether WebGL exists during render. `hasWebGL()` needs `document`, so it returns false on the server and true on the client, and the two renders disagree — the check runs in an effect and flips to the static fallback afterwards.
- Advancing the idle rotation by a per-frame constant. The ring idles at double speed on a 120 Hz laptop, which is exactly the sort of bug that never reproduces on the developer's machine.

## Notes

- App Router wiring: `onNavigate={(id) => router.push(`/work/${id}`)}`. Call `router.prefetch` on hover (see `hover-prefetch-wipe`) so the 1.4s warp is spent downloading the destination rather than waiting after it.
- Reduced motion and no-WebGL share one path: a static grid of the same cards, a 0.3s fade of the chrome, then navigate. No context is ever created in that branch.
- The ring is index-driven, not raycast-driven. Picking is done with real DOM buttons over the canvas, which keeps the nav keyboard-reachable and screen-reader-legible for free.

## Definition of done

The ring idles at the same speed on a 60 Hz and a 120 Hz display. Choosing a destination fades the caption, then the ring barely moves for about half a second before tearing outward and past the camera; the new route appears only once the frame is empty, with no flash of the intact ring. Unmount mid-warp and the console stays clean.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: FAQ Section

A `<section>` that pairs a heading block (eyebrow, title, copy, an optional aside) with the kit `Accordion` in its `contained` variant: white question cards on a grey tray, each with a plus that turns into a close. Below 64rem of container width it stacks and centres like the landing page. From 64rem the heading block becomes a sticky left column and the questions fill the right. The question headers also answer to the arrow, Home and End keys.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Landing FAQ: heading block plus the kit accordion tray, two-column at wide container widths, with arrow-key navigation.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. The root is `@container w-full`, and every responsive switch is a container variant (`@xl:`, `@5xl:`), not a media query. The section therefore lays out by the width it is given: a scaled preview, a docs column or a full page all get the right arrangement.
2. In the `split` layout the inner wrapper is `grid grid-cols-1`, which becomes `@5xl:grid-cols-[minmax(0,5fr)_minmax(0,7fr)]` with a 64px gap inside a 1120px max width. The heading block switches from `items-center text-center` to `@5xl:items-start @5xl:text-start @5xl:sticky @5xl:top-10 @5xl:self-start`, so it stays in view while a long answer list scrolls past. `self-start` is what lets sticky work inside a grid cell. `stacked` keeps the single centred 760px column at every width.
3. Questions map to `AccordionItem`s inside `<Accordion variant="contained" indicator="plus">`. The expansion props (`expandedKeys`, `defaultExpandedKeys`, `onExpandedChange`, `allowsMultipleExpanded`) pass straight through to React Aria's DisclosureGroup, so the section can be controlled or uncontrolled. Each question heading is one level below the section title (`headingLevel + 1`), and the section is `aria-labelledby` the title.
4. Every answer body is wrapped in `[data-faq-answer]`. An `onKeyDown` on the list wrapper collects `button[aria-expanded]` elements that are not disabled and not inside an answer. ArrowDown and ArrowUp move focus with wrap-around, Home and End jump to the ends, and `preventDefault` stops the page from scrolling. Keys pressed inside an answer are ignored, so a nested control keeps its own keyboard behaviour.
5. The title runs from `text-display-4-medium` (32px) up to `@xl:text-display-2-medium` (48px), with letter-spacing tightened to -0.035em at the large size. The description is capped at 440px so it wraps to two balanced lines under the title.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `split breakpoint = @5xl (64rem of container width)`
  Below about 1024px a 5:7 split leaves the question column under 560px, and the longest questions start wrapping to three lines. Above it both columns read comfortably.
- `column ratio = minmax(0,5fr) minmax(0,7fr), gap 64px, max 1120px`
  The heading column only needs to fit a two-line display title and its copy. The extra width goes to the questions. `minmax(0, …)` stops a long unbroken answer from pushing the grid wider than its container.
- `title scale = 32px → 48px at @xl, tracking -0.02em → -0.035em`
  The two-line display title from the landing page needs tight tracking at 48px to read as one block. At 32px the same tracking crowds the letters, so it eases off.
- `answer measure = max-w-[60ch]`
  In the wide right column an unbounded answer runs over 100 characters per line. 60ch keeps answers readable without changing the card width.

## API

```ts
function FaqSection(props: { items: { id: string; question: ReactNode; answer: ReactNode; isDisabled?: boolean }[]; title?: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; eyebrow?: ReactNode; layout?: "split" | "stacked"; variant?: "divided" | "contained" | "separated"; expandedKeys?: Iterable<Key>; defaultExpandedKeys?: Iterable<Key>; onExpandedChange?: (keys: Set<Key>) => void; allowsMultipleExpanded?: boolean; aside?: ReactNode; footer?: ReactNode; headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5; id?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `items: FaqEntry[]`
  Questions in order: `{ id, question, answer, isDisabled? }`. `id` is the key that `expandedKeys` holds.
- `title: ReactNode` — default `"Frequently asked questions"`
  Section title, rendered as `h{headingLevel}` and used as the section's accessible name.
- `description: ReactNode`
  Supporting copy under the title, capped at 440px.
- `eyebrow: ReactNode`
  Small uppercase label above the title.
- `layout: "split" | "stacked"` — default `"split"`
  `split` turns two-column from 64rem of container width; `stacked` stays a centred column.
- `variant: "divided" | "contained" | "separated"` — default `"contained"`
  Accordion look, forwarded to the kit Accordion.
- `expandedKeys: Iterable<Key>`
  Controlled open question ids.
- `defaultExpandedKeys: Iterable<Key>`
  Initially open question ids when uncontrolled.
- `onExpandedChange: (keys: Set<Key>) => void`
  Called with the new set of open ids.
- `allowsMultipleExpanded: boolean` — default `false`
  Allow several answers open at once. When false, opening one closes the other.
- `aside: ReactNode`
  Content under the heading block (left column when split).
- `footer: ReactNode`
  Content under the question list.
- `headingLevel: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5` — default `2`
  Title level. Questions use the next level down.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Question headers of this list only: answers may hold their own disclosure buttons. */
function questionButtons(list: HTMLElement) {
  return Array.from(list.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>("button[aria-expanded]")).filter(
    (button) => !button.disabled && button.closest("[data-faq-answer]") === null,
  );
}

function moveFocus(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) {
  const target = event.target as HTMLElement;
  if (target.closest("[data-faq-answer]")) return;
  const buttons = questionButtons(event.currentTarget);
  const index = buttons.indexOf(target as HTMLButtonElement);
  if (index === -1 || buttons.length === 0) return;

  let next: number;
  switch (event.key) {
    case "ArrowDown":
      next = (index + 1) % buttons.length;
      break;
    case "ArrowUp":
      next = (index - 1 + buttons.length) % buttons.length;
      break;
    case "Home":
      next = 0;
      break;
    case "End":
      next = buttons.length - 1;
      break;
    default:
      return;
  }
  event.preventDefault();
  buttons[next]?.focus();
}

export function FaqSection({
  items,
  title = "Frequently asked questions",
  description,
  eyebrow,
  layout = "split",
  variant = "contained",
  expandedKeys,
  defaultExpandedKeys,
  onExpandedChange,
  allowsMultipleExpanded = false,
  aside,
  footer,
  headingLevel = 2,
  id,
  className,
}: FaqSectionProps) {
  const autoId = useId();
  const titleId = `${id ?? autoId}-title`;
  const TitleTag = TITLE_TAGS[headingLevel];
  const questionLevel = (headingLevel + 1) as 3 | 4 | 5 | 6;

  return (
    <section id={id} aria-labelledby={titleId} className={cx("@container w-full", className)}>
      <div className={styles.grid[layout]}>
        <div className={styles.head[layout]}>
          {eyebrow ? <p className={styles.eyebrow}>{eyebrow}</p> : null}
          <TitleTag id={titleId} className={styles.title}>
            {title}
          </TitleTag>
          {description ? <p className={styles.description}>{description}</p> : null}
          {aside ? <div className="mt-2 w-full max-w-[440px] text-start">{aside}</div> : null}
        </div>

        <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-4">
          <div data-faq-list="" onKeyDown={moveFocus}>
            <Accordion
              variant={variant}
              indicator="plus"
              expandedKeys={expandedKeys}
              defaultExpandedKeys={defaultExpandedKeys}
              onExpandedChange={onExpandedChange}
              allowsMultipleExpanded={allowsMultipleExpanded}
            >
              {items.map((item) => (
                <AccordionItem
                  key={item.id}
                  id={item.id}
                  title={item.question}
                  headingLevel={questionLevel}
                  isDisabled={item.isDisabled}
                >
                  <div data-faq-answer="" className="max-w-[60ch] text-pretty">
                    {item.answer}
                  </div>
                </AccordionItem>
              ))}
            </Accordion>
          </div>
          {footer}
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The section adds one React `onKeyDown` handler and no effects, timers or observers. React Aria owns the disclosure state.

**Reduced motion.** The only motion is the accordion's own: the panel height, the content fade-and-blur and the plus rotation. All of them carry `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so answers open and close instantly. Sticky positioning is not animation and stays.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using viewport breakpoints (`lg:`) for the split. Inside a scaled preview, a dashboard column or a modal the viewport says "wide" while the section is narrow, and the two columns crush the questions. The layout must read the container.
- Dropping `self-start` from the sticky heading. Grid items stretch to the row height by default, so a sticky element as tall as the row has nowhere to stick and scrolls away with the page.
- Finding headers with a broad `button` selector. An answer that holds its own disclosure or button would join the arrow-key cycle. Filter by `aria-expanded` and exclude anything inside `[data-faq-answer]`.
- Keeping the question headings at the same level as the section title. Screen-reader heading lists then show the questions as siblings of the section instead of its children. Use `headingLevel + 1`.

## Notes

- Pass `layout="stacked"` for the exact centred column of the landing page at every width. The `aside` slot sits under the heading in either layout, which suits a contact card or an expand-all control.
- Collapsed answers use React Aria's `hidden="until-found"`, so the browser's find-in-page still searches them and opens the matching row.

## Definition of done

In a container at least 1024px wide the title and copy sit in a left column and the nine questions run down the right column. Below that width everything centres in one column. Clicking a question opens its answer and turns its plus into a close. With `allowsMultipleExpanded` false, opening a second question closes the first. With a header focused, ArrowDown and ArrowUp move focus to the next and previous header (wrapping), Home and End jump to the ends, and Enter toggles the focused one. Expanding all from controlled state shows every answer.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Feature Card Grid

The "what is in the box" section of a component-kit landing page: a centred header (eyebrow, title, copy, CTAs) over a responsive grid of rounded cards. Each card shows a cropped, fading illustration on top and a title with a two-line description below. The illustration can be a render function that receives `{ active }`, so a picture assembled from real kit components (ProgressTrack, Switch, Checkbox, Chip, Avatar, Kbd) can flip a switch, fill a bar or complete a step while the card is hovered or focused.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Landing grid of feature cards, each topped by a small illustration built from kit parts that plays a state change on hover or focus.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Active state: `FeatureCard` keeps `hovered` (pointerenter/leave) and `focused` (focus, and blur only when focus leaves the card, checked with `relatedTarget`) and ORs them into `active`. It writes `data-active` on the card and calls the illustration with `{ active }` when it is a function, so the artwork changes props on real components and their own transitions animate the change.
2. Artwork frame: the top area is a fixed 196px, `overflow-hidden`, with `mask-b-from-75%` so artwork that runs past the bottom fades out instead of being cut, and wider artwork is simply cropped at the card edge. While active the artwork lifts 4px on a 500ms ease-out curve.
3. The artwork is `aria-hidden` and `inert`: it is made of interactive kit components (checkboxes, switches, buttons) shown read-only, and inert keeps them out of the tab order and the accessibility tree, so the card is one stop with one name.
4. Card element: with `href` the whole card is an `<a>`, otherwise an `<article>`; both get the hover border and shadow lift and a focus-visible ring offset from the page background.
5. Grid: the `<section>` is an `@container/features`; columns step 1 → 2 (@xl) → 3 (@4xl) → 4 (@6xl) with the gap opening from 16 to 24px at four columns. `span={2}` widens a card from two columns up, for bento layouts.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `artwork height = 196px`
  About two thirds of a 300px-wide card, leaving room for a title and two lines of copy at a near-square card.
- `fade = mask-b-from-75%`
  Artwork can be taller than the frame and trail off; the last quarter fades into the card.
- `lift = -4px, 500ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)`
  Enough to read as a response, small enough that cropped artwork never reveals its top edge.
- `columns = 1 / 2 @xl / 3 @4xl / 4 @6xl`
  Keeps each card between roughly 260 and 340px wide at every container size.

## API

```ts
function FeatureCardGrid(props: { eyebrow?: ReactNode; title?: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; actions?: ReactNode; children: ReactNode; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function FeatureCard(props: { title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; illustration?: ReactNode | ((state: { active: boolean }) => ReactNode); href?: string; onClick?: MouseEventHandler; span?: 1 | 2; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `title: ReactNode`
  Card heading (rendered as h3).
- `description: ReactNode`
  Up to two lines of supporting copy.
- `illustration: ReactNode | ({ active }) => ReactNode`
  Artwork for the top frame; the function form reacts to hover and focus.
- `href: string`
  Makes the card a link.
- `span: 1 | 2` — default `1`
  Columns spanned from the two-column breakpoint up.
- `eyebrow / title / description / actions: ReactNode`
  FeatureCardGrid header slots; all optional.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * One tile of the grid. Hover and focus-within raise an `active` flag that is
 * handed to the illustration, so artwork built from kit parts can play a
 * small state change (a bar fills, a switch flips, a step completes) instead
 * of the whole card merely brightening. The artwork is `inert` and hidden from
 * assistive tech: it is a picture of a component, not a working one.
 */
export function FeatureCard({ title, description, illustration, href, onClick, span = 1, className }: FeatureCardProps) {
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false);
  const [focused, setFocused] = useState(false);
  const active = hovered || focused;
  const art = typeof illustration === "function" ? illustration({ active }) : illustration;

  const onBlur = (event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => {
    if (!event.currentTarget.contains(event.relatedTarget as Node | null)) setFocused(false);
  };

  const body = (
    <>
      <div
        aria-hidden="true"
        inert
        className="relative h-[196px] overflow-hidden mask-b-from-75% mask-b-to-100%"
      >
        <div
          className={cx(
            "h-full w-full transition-transform duration-500 ease-[cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)] motion-reduce:transition-none",
            active && "-translate-y-1 motion-reduce:translate-y-0",
          )}
        >
          {art}
        </div>
      </div>
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-1 px-5 pt-3 pb-5">
        <h3 className="text-headline-medium text-text-primary">{title}</h3>
        {description ? (
          <p className="line-clamp-2 text-body-regular text-text-tertiary">{description}</p>
        ) : null}
      </div>
    </>
  );

  const shared = {
    "data-active": active ? "true" : "false",
    onPointerEnter: () => setHovered(true),
    onPointerLeave: () => setHovered(false),
    onFocus: () => setFocused(true),
    onBlur,
    onClick,
    className: cx(
      "group/feature relative flex flex-col overflow-hidden rounded-3xl border bg-background-primary-default text-start",
      "border-border-button-default shadow-xs transition-[border-color,box-shadow] duration-200 ease-out",
      "hover:border-border-button-hover hover:shadow-md",
      "outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-background-full",
      span === 2 && "@xl/features:col-span-2",
      className,
    ),
  };

  return href ? (
    <a href={href} {...shared}>
      {body}
    </a>
  ) : (
    <article {...shared}>{body}</article>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No listeners, timers or effects; hover and focus state are plain React handlers on the card.

**Reduced motion.** The artwork lift and its transition are removed with `motion-reduce:` variants. State changes still happen on hover, they just snap; kit components drop their own transitions under the same preference.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Leaving the illustration interactive. Kit checkboxes and switches inside a card link nest focusable controls in a link and add a dozen tab stops; mark the frame `inert` and `aria-hidden`.
- Clearing focus state on every `blur`. Focus moving between elements inside the card fires blur; check `relatedTarget` against the card first.
- Using `md:`/`lg:` for the column count. The grid often sits in a narrower column than the window; container queries keep cards a sane width.
- Animating the illustration with its own timers. Reacting to `active` keeps every card still until a visitor points at it, which also costs nothing off screen.

## Notes

- The demo builds eight illustrations entirely from kit components and tokens: ProgressTrack bars that fill further, a Switch that flips, Checkboxes that select, a sidebar selection that moves.
- Pass a plain node as `illustration` for static artwork.

## Definition of done

At 1280px the section shows the install line, title, copy and two CTAs above four columns of cards. Hovering "Agent limits" raises the card and its context bar moves from 82% to 91%; hovering "Notification settings" flips the Mentions switch on; leaving restores both. Tab skips everything inside the artwork. In a narrow container the grid drops to two and then one column.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: File Upload

A 164px dashed drop zone that accepts a click, Enter or Space, or a dropped file. A bad extension or an oversized file swaps the prompt for a red message for 2.6 seconds; a good one fades the dashes out, draws an accent line clockwise around the rounded border from top centre as a percentage badge rises over the edge, and shows the file icon, name and size. The upload is simulated, so `onUploadComplete` is where the real storage call goes.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A drag-and-drop zone that validates type and size, traces progress around its own border, then reports the finished file.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The zone is a `div role="button"` (tabbable only when idle) holding a visually hidden `<input type="file">` whose `accept` is built from `allowedExtensions`. Click and Enter / Space call `input.click()`; `onDragOver` prevents the default and sets `dragOver`, `onDrop` takes `dataTransfer.files[0]`. The input clears its `value` after reading so choosing the same file again still fires `change`.
2. `startUpload` checks the lower-cased extension against `allowedExtensions` and the size against `maxBytes`, and on failure sets a rejection string that a 2600ms timeout clears. On success it stores the file, sets phase `uploading` and starts a self-scheduling `tick`: first after 250ms, then every 90ms, adding the next of `PROGRESS_STEPS` (3, 6, 4, 7, 2, 5 percent, cycled) until 100. At 100 the phase becomes `complete`, and 1600ms later it calls `onUploadComplete(file)` and returns to `idle`. Every timeout id goes into one ref that unmount clears.
3. A ResizeObserver keeps the measured box size in state. An SVG with `viewBox` equal to that size draws a 2px grey rounded rect and, over it, a path from `ringPath(width, height, 1, 15)`: start at top centre, run clockwise with 15px arcs, close. The path has `pathLength={100}`, so `strokeDasharray` is simply `${progress} 200` (102 once at 100, so the round caps overlap and close the loop) with a 200ms linear transition on `stroke-dasharray`.
4. The idle layer (icon disc, prompt, allowed types) and the busy layer (file icon, name, uploading / success line) are both always rendered on top of each other. `useStaggerState` turns a boolean into `shown`, `hiding` (200ms) or `hidden`, and the `.t-stagger` classes in the theme sheet animate each `.t-stagger-line` from 12px down, blurred 3px and transparent to rest over 500ms on `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`, with lines 2 and 3 delayed 40ms and 80ms. Hiding is a plain 200ms fade with no movement.
5. The "Uploading 1.7 MB..." and "Uploaded successfully!" lines share one 18px slot and cross-fade with the same three-state helper. The percentage badge sits at `-top-[9.5px]` centred on the border and enters by sliding 10px down while unblurring (opacity and blur 160ms, translate 300ms). The dashed border and the SVG ring cross-fade on `busy` over 300ms, and the background shifts from secondary to primary.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `defaults = maxBytes 8 * 1024 * 1024; extensions pdf, jpg, jpeg, png, xlsx`
  From the Figma copy ("PDF, JPG, PNG, XLSX (max 8 MB)"). JPEG is accepted but hidden from the label so the copy does not list JPG twice.
- `simulated progress = 250ms lead-in, 90ms ticks, +3 +6 +4 +7 +2 +5 percent cycled, 1600ms success hold`
  Averages a little under two seconds per file with uneven steps, so it reads like a network upload instead of a linear timer, and the success state stays up long enough to read. The steps are a fixed cycle rather than `Math.random()`, so every run (and every test) sees the same percentages.
- `ring geometry = inset 1, radius 15, strokeWidth 2, pathLength 100`
  The zone is `rounded-2xl` (16px); a 2px stroke centred 1px inside it needs a 15px radius to sit exactly on the border. `pathLength` lets progress map straight onto the dash length whatever the measured size.
- `closing dash = 102 at 100%`
  At exactly 100 the round caps leave a hairline gap at the top centre; overshooting by 2 closes the loop.
- `stagger = 500ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), 12px, blur 3px, 40ms per line; hide 200ms`
  The theme's shared text-reveal. A long ease-out reveal and a fast, motionless hide keep the swap from looking like content sliding back down.
- `rejection = 2600ms`
  Long enough to read a sentence-length message, short enough that the prompt comes back before the user tries again.

## API

```ts
function FileUpload(props: { onUploadComplete?: (file: File) => void; allowedExtensions?: readonly string[]; maxBytes?: number; renderFileIcon?: (file: File) => ReactNode; incomingFile?: File | null; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function formatFileSize(bytes: number): string
```

- `onUploadComplete: (file: File) => void`
  Called after the progress ring fills and the success line has shown for 1.6s.
- `allowedExtensions: readonly string[]` — default `["pdf", "jpg", "jpeg", "png", "xlsx"]`
  Extensions without dots; drives validation, `accept` and the hint line.
- `maxBytes: number` — default `8 * 1024 * 1024`
  Larger files are rejected with "That file is larger than 8 MB".
- `renderFileIcon: (file: File) => ReactNode`
  Custom icon for the file being uploaded.
- `incomingFile: File | null`
  Starts an upload of this file as if it were dropped (same validation; ignored while busy). Each new File object starts once.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the 164px zone, e.g. a width.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function FileUpload({
  onUploadComplete,
  allowedExtensions = DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS,
  maxBytes = DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES,
  renderFileIcon,
  incomingFile,
  className,
}: FileUploadProps) {
  const localize = useTemplateCopy();
  const [phase, setPhase] = useState<UploadPhase>("idle");
  const [progress, setProgress] = useState(0);
  const [file, setFile] = useState<File | null>(null);
  const [rejection, setRejection] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [dragOver, setDragOver] = useState(false);

  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const boxRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const [box, setBox] = useState({ width: 533, height: 164 });
  const timers = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>[]>([]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const element = boxRef.current;
    if (!element) return;
    const observer = new ResizeObserver(([entry]) => {
      if (!entry) return;
      const { width, height } = entry.contentRect;
      if (width > 0) setBox({ width, height });
    });
    observer.observe(element);
    return () => observer.disconnect();
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    const pending = timers.current;
    return () => pending.forEach(clearTimeout);
  }, []);

  const startUpload = (nextFile: File) => {
    const extension = extensionFor(nextFile.name);
    if (!allowedExtensions.map((value) => value.toLowerCase()).includes(extension)) {
      setRejection(`Only ${allowedExtensions.map((value) => value.toUpperCase()).join(", ")} files are supported`);
      timers.current.push(setTimeout(() => setRejection(null), 2600));
      return;
    }
    if (nextFile.size > maxBytes) {
      setRejection(`That file is larger than ${formatFileSize(maxBytes)}`);
      timers.current.push(setTimeout(() => setRejection(null), 2600));
      return;
    }

    setFile(nextFile);
    setProgress(0);
    setPhase("uploading");

    let value = 0;
    let step = 0;
    const tick = () => {
      value = Math.min(100, value + PROGRESS_STEPS[step++ % PROGRESS_STEPS.length]!);
      setProgress(Math.round(value));
      if (value < 100) {
        timers.current.push(setTimeout(tick, 90));
        return;
      }

      setPhase("complete");
      timers.current.push(
        setTimeout(() => {
          onUploadComplete?.(nextFile);
          setPhase("idle");
          setFile(null);
        }, 1600),
      );
    };
    timers.current.push(setTimeout(tick, 250));
  };

  const busy = phase !== "idle";

  // A new `incomingFile` behaves like a drop: ignored while an upload runs.
  // Keyed on the File object itself, so a re-render never restarts it.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (incomingFile && !busy) startUpload(incomingFile);
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [incomingFile]);

  const progressPath = ringPath(box.width, box.height, 1, 15);
  const idleReveal = useStaggerState(!busy);
  const busyReveal = useStaggerState(busy);
  const uploadingLine = useStaggerState(phase === "uploading");
  const completeLine = useStaggerState(phase === "complete");
  const allowedLabel = allowedExtensions
    .filter((extension) => extension.toLowerCase() !== "jpeg")
    .map((extension) => extension.toUpperCase())
    .join(", ");

  return localize(
    <div
      ref={boxRef}
      role="button"
      tabIndex={busy ? -1 : 0}
      aria-label="Upload a file"
      onClick={() => !busy && inputRef.current?.click()}
      onKeyDown={(event) => {
        if (!busy && (event.key === "Enter" || event.key === " ")) {
          event.preventDefault();
          inputRef.current?.click();
        }
      }}
      onDragOver={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        if (!busy) setDragOver(true);
      }}
      onDragLeave={() => setDragOver(false)}
      onDrop={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        setDragOver(false);
        const droppedFile = event.dataTransfer.files?.[0];
        if (droppedFile && !busy) startUpload(droppedFile);
      }}
      className={cx(
        "group relative h-[164px] w-full shrink-0 rounded-2xl outline-none",
        "transition-colors duration-300 ease-out",
        busy ? "bg-background-primary-default" : "cursor-pointer bg-background-secondary-default",
        "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
        className,
      )}
    >
      <input
        ref={inputRef}
        type="file"
        aria-label="Choose a file to upload"
        accept={allowedExtensions.map((extension) => `.${extension}`).join(",")}
        className="sr-only"
        tabIndex={-1}
        onChange={(event) => {
          const selectedFile = event.target.files?.[0];
          event.target.value = "";
          if (selectedFile) startUpload(selectedFile);
        }}
      />

      <div
        aria-hidden
        className={cx(
          "pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 rounded-2xl border-2 border-dashed",
          dragOver
            ? "border-border-button-active"
            : "border-border-checkbox-default group-hover:border-border-button-active",
          "transition-[opacity,border-color] duration-300 ease-out",
          busy ? "opacity-0" : "opacity-100",
        )}
      />

      <svg
        aria-hidden
        viewBox={`0 0 ${box.width} ${box.height}`}
        preserveAspectRatio="none"
        className={cx(
          "pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 size-full transition-opacity duration-300 ease-out",
          busy ? "opacity-100" : "opacity-0",
        )}
      >
        <rect
          x={1}
          y={1}
          width={box.width - 2}
          height={box.height - 2}
          rx={15}
          fill="none"
          stroke="var(--color-border-button-default)"
          strokeWidth={2}
        />
        <path
          d={progressPath}
          fill="none"
          stroke="var(--color-accent-400)"
          strokeWidth={2}
          strokeLinecap="round"
          pathLength={100}
          strokeDasharray={`${busy ? (progress >= 100 ? 102 : progress) : 0} 200`}
          className="transition-[stroke-dasharray] duration-200 ease-linear"
        />
      </svg>

      <div
        aria-hidden
        className={cx(
          "absolute -top-[9.5px] left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 rounded-md bg-accent-400 px-1.5 py-0.5",
          "text-caption-1-medium whitespace-nowrap text-white tabular-nums",
          "[transition:opacity_160ms_ease-out,filter_160ms_ease-out,translate_300ms_ease-out]",
          busy ? "translate-y-0 opacity-100 blur-none" : "-translate-y-2.5 opacity-0 blur-[2px]",
        )}
      >
        {progress}%
      </div>

      <div
        className={cx(
          "absolute inset-0 flex flex-col items-center justify-center gap-3.5",
          staggerContainer(idleReveal),
          busy && "pointer-events-none",
        )}
      >
        <span className="t-stagger-line t-stagger-line--1 flex size-10 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-file-upload-icon-background p-2.5">
          <RiUploadCloud2Line
            className="size-6 shrink-0 text-file-upload-icon-foreground transition-colors duration-150 ease group-hover:text-file-upload-icon-foreground-hover"
            aria-hidden
          />
        </span>
        <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-2 text-center">
          <p
            className={cx(
              "t-stagger-line t-stagger-line--2 text-body-medium",
              rejection ? "text-text-error-primary" : "text-text-secondary",
            )}
          >
            {rejection ?? (
              <>
                Drag and drop to upload or <span className="text-accent-500">select</span>
              </>
            )}
          </p>
          <p className="t-stagger-line t-stagger-line--3 text-body-2-regular text-text-tertiary">
            {allowedLabel} (max {formatFileSize(maxBytes)})
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div
        className={cx(
          "absolute inset-0 flex flex-col items-center justify-center",
          staggerContainer(busyReveal),
          !busy && "pointer-events-none",
        )}
      >
        <span className="t-stagger-line t-stagger-line--1 flex size-10 items-center justify-center rounded-full border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default p-2">
          {file && (renderFileIcon ? renderFileIcon(file) : <DefaultFileIcon file={file} />)}
        </span>
        <p className="t-stagger-line t-stagger-line--2 mt-3.5 max-w-[90%] truncate text-body-medium text-text-primary">
          {file?.name}
        </p>
        <div className="t-stagger-line t-stagger-line--3 relative mt-1 h-[18px] w-full">
          <p
            className={cx(
              "absolute inset-x-0 text-center text-body-2-regular text-text-secondary",
              staggerLine(uploadingLine),
            )}
          >
            Uploading {file ? formatFileSize(file.size) : ""}
            ...
          </p>
          <p
            className={cx(
              "absolute inset-x-0 text-center text-body-2-regular text-text-secondary",
              staggerLine(completeLine),
            )}
          >
            Uploaded successfully!
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The ResizeObserver disconnects on unmount, every upload and rejection timeout is cleared from the shared timer ref, and the 200ms hide timer in `useStaggerState` clears itself.

**Reduced motion.** The theme sheet sets `transition: none` on `.t-stagger-line` under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, so the text layers swap instantly with no rise or blur. The progress ring still fills (it carries the progress information) and the border, badge and background still cross-fade.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not mount and unmount the idle and busy layers. Both stay rendered and swap through the stagger classes; conditional rendering kills the exit fade and the blur-in.
- Do not leave the input's `value` set after reading it. The browser then fires no `change` when the same file is chosen again.
- Do not hard-code the ring path to the default 533 by 164 box. The path is rebuilt from the ResizeObserver size so the corners stay 15px at any width; a fixed path with `preserveAspectRatio="none"` would stretch the arcs.
- Do not schedule ticks without tracking them. Every `setTimeout` id is pushed to a ref and cleared on unmount, otherwise a navigation mid-upload sets state on an unmounted component and still fires `onUploadComplete`.
- Do not feed the zone a file with `new DataTransfer()` and a synthetic `change` event. The constructor is missing in older browsers, and assigning `input.files` bypasses the zone's busy check. Pass the File to `incomingFile` instead; a new File object starts one upload.
- Do not treat the progress as real. It is a timer; wire the actual upload in `onUploadComplete` or replace `tick` with your request's progress events.

## Notes

- `incomingFile` starts an upload as if that file had been dropped: same validation, ignored while busy, keyed on the File object so re-renders never restart it.
- `renderFileIcon(file)` replaces the default icon in the busy state (spreadsheet for xlsx, image for jpg/jpeg/png, document otherwise).
- `formatFileSize` is exported: KB below 1 MB (minimum 1 KB), one decimal under 10 MB, whole MB above.
- Strings go through `useTemplateCopy`, so the prompt and status lines can be translated by a `TemplateCopyProvider`.

## Definition of done

An idle dashed zone shows the upload icon, "Drag and drop to upload or select" and "PDF, JPG, PNG, XLSX (max 8 MB)". Dropping a .zip shows "Only PDF, JPG, JPEG, PNG, XLSX files are supported" in red, which clears after about 2.6s. Dropping a 1.7 MB PDF fades the dashes out, the icon, file name and "Uploading 1.7 MB..." rise in, an accent line runs clockwise from top centre around the border with a rising percentage badge, and at 100% the line closes and the status changes to "Uploaded successfully!". About 1.6s later `onUploadComplete` fires once and the zone returns to idle.

and where, so I can check them.

## What it does

- Category: block

## How it works

1. Spending uses the `labels` ring variant, so each ring names itself, innermost first from Subscriptions to Housing.
```tsx
export function FinanceDashboard({
  view,
  defaultView = 'finance',
  onViewChange,
  transactions: initialTransactions = FINANCE_TRANSACTIONS,
  today = '2026-11-05',
  defaultWidgets = ALL_WIDGETS,
  className,
}: FinanceDashboardProps) {
  const [innerView, setInnerView] = useState(defaultView);
  const current = view ?? innerView;
  const go = useCallback(
    (key: string) => {
      if (view === undefined) setInnerView(key);
      onViewChange?.(key);
    },
    [view, onViewChange],
  );

  const widgets = useWidgetToggles(ALL_WIDGETS, defaultWidgets);
  const shown = widgets.isShown;
  const [rows, setRows] = useState<Transaction[]>(() => [...initialTransactions]);
  const [added, setAdded] = useState<Transaction[]>([]);
  const [formOpen, setFormOpen] = useState(false);
  const nextId = useRef(1);


  // Only transactions added on this page move the cards; the sample rows are already in the bases.
  const kpis = useMemo<FinanceKpi[]>(() => {
    const inflow = added.reduce((sum, t) => sum + Math.max(0, t.amount), 0);
    const outflow = added.reduce((sum, t) => sum + Math.max(0, -t.amount), 0);
    const invested = added.reduce((sum, t) => sum + (t.category === 'investing' ? -t.amount : 0), 0);
    const balance = BASE.balance + inflow - outflow;
    return [
      { id: 'balance', label: 'Total balance', icon: WalletIcon, value: balance, change: 0.032, trend: [...TRENDS.balance, balance] },
      { id: 'income', label: 'Income', icon: IncomeIcon, value: BASE.income + inflow, change: 0.061, trend: [...TRENDS.income, BASE.income + inflow] },
      {
        id: 'expenses',
        label: 'Expenses',
        icon: CardIcon,
        value: BASE.expenses + outflow,
        change: 0.024,
        goodDirection: 'down',
        trend: [...TRENDS.expenses, BASE.expenses + outflow],
      },
      { id: 'invested', label: 'Invested', icon: InvestIcon, value: BASE.invested + invested, change: 0.084, trend: [...TRENDS.invested, BASE.invested + invested] },
    ];
  }, [added]);

  const addTransaction = (draft: Omit<Transaction, 'id' | 'date' | 'status'>) => {
    const tx: Transaction = { ...draft, id: `tx-new-${nextId.current++}`, date: today, status: 'completed' };
    setRows((prev) => [tx, ...prev]);
    setAdded((prev) => [...prev, tx]);
    setFormOpen(false);
    toast('Transaction added', { status: 'success', description: `${tx.name}: ${tx.amount > 0 ? '+' : '-'}${formatMoney(Math.abs(tx.amount))}` });
  };
```

# Build: Finance KPI Row

A responsive row of grey KPI cards. Each card has a white icon tile, a label, the value in a 24px medium figure, a percent delta chip and a 96×36 sparkline with a soft area fill and an end dot. The chip and line colour follow whether the move is good news, so rising expenses read rose while rising income reads lime. With `selectable`, the cards become pressed-state buttons that pick one metric for a chart.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Balance, income, expense and savings cards with a delta chip coloured by good or bad news and a tiny area sparkline.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Wrap the list in a `@container` and lay it out as a grid: one column, two from `@sm` (24rem) and four from `@3xl` (48rem), so the row wraps by its own width rather than the viewport. Below `@sm` each card collapses to one compact line (icon, figures, sparkline) by turning the top line into `display: contents` and reordering with `order`, so four cards fit a phone screen.
2. Classify each card with `toneOf(change, goodDirection)`: zero is flat, otherwise good when the sign of the change matches the good direction (`"up"` by default, `"down"` for expenses). Good maps to a lime chip and a chart-7 line, bad to rose and chart-3, flat to neutral.
3. Project the trend with `sparkPoints` into a 96×36 box with 3 units of padding: x steps evenly across the points, y is inverted against the series min and max, and a flat series sits on the middle line.
4. Draw a `M…L…` line path with a 1.75 stroke, close a copy down to the baseline for the area and fill it with a per-instance `useId` linear gradient from 28% to 0% of `currentColor`, then mark the last point with a 3-unit dot outlined in the card colour.
5. Format values with `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: "currency", maximumFractionDigits: 0 })` unless the item passes its own `format`, and deltas with a percent format using `signDisplay: "exceptZero"`; the chip also carries a screen-reader-only comparison label.
6. When `selectable`, render each card as a `<button aria-pressed>` and resolve the selection controlled (`selectedId`) or from local state seeded by `defaultSelectedId` or the first item; the selected card lifts to a white surface with a hairline ring.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `sparkline box = 96×36 with 3px padding`
  Fits the empty top-right corner beside the 32px icon tile without crowding the value line.
- `area gradient = 28% → 0% currentColor`
  Enough fill to read the shape at a glance, faint enough that the line stays the mark.
- `grid breakpoints = 1 col, 2 from @sm (24rem), 4 from @3xl (48rem)`
  A $84,230 figure plus its chip needs about 180px; below that the cards stack.
- `value type = text-title-1-medium (24px)`
  Matches the headline figures of the other dashboard cards.

```tsx
/** Map values onto the sparkline box: x spreads evenly, y is inverted so a
 *  larger value sits higher. A flat series draws along the middle. */
export function sparkPoints(values: number[], w = SPARK_W, h = SPARK_H, pad = SPARK_PAD): [number, number][] {
  if (values.length < 2) return [];
  const min = Math.min(...values);
  const max = Math.max(...values);
  const span = max - min;
  const step = (w - pad * 2) / (values.length - 1);
  return values.map((v, i) => [
    pad + i * step,
    span === 0 ? h / 2 : pad + (h - pad * 2) * (1 - (v - min) / span),
  ]);
}

function Sparkline({
  values,
  tone,
  label,
  className,
}: {
  values: number[];
  tone: "good" | "bad" | "flat";
  label: string;
  className?: string;
}) {
  const gradientId = useId();
  const pts = sparkPoints(values);
  const last = pts[pts.length - 1];
  const first = pts[0];
  if (!last || !first) return null;
  const line = pts.map(([x, y], i) => `${i ? "L" : "M"}${x.toFixed(2)} ${y.toFixed(2)}`).join(" ");
  const area = `${line} L${last[0].toFixed(2)} ${SPARK_H} L${first[0].toFixed(2)} ${SPARK_H} Z`;
  return (
    <svg
      role="img"
      aria-label={label}
      viewBox={`0 0 ${SPARK_W} ${SPARK_H}`}
      className={cx(
        "h-9 w-24 shrink-0 overflow-visible",
        className,
        tone === "good" ? "text-chart-7" : tone === "bad" ? "text-chart-3" : "text-chart-neutral",
      )}
    >
      <defs>
        <linearGradient id={gradientId} x1="0" x2="0" y1="0" y2="1">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor="currentColor" stopOpacity="0.28" />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor="currentColor" stopOpacity="0" />
        </linearGradient>
      </defs>
      <path d={area} fill={`url(#${gradientId})`} />
      <path d={line} fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth={1.75} strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" />
      <circle cx={last[0]} cy={last[1]} r={3} fill="currentColor" className="stroke-background-secondary-default" strokeWidth={1.5} />
    </svg>
  );
}

/** Good news is lime and bad news rose, whatever the sign: a rising expense
 *  line is bad, a falling one good. */
function toneOf(change: number, goodDirection: "up" | "down"): "good" | "bad" | "flat" {
  if (change === 0) return "flat";
  return (change > 0) === (goodDirection === "up") ? "good" : "bad";
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component has no timers, listeners or effects.

**Reduced motion.** The only motion is the 200ms surface change when a card is selected; it carries `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the selection switches instantly.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Colour the delta by good or bad news, not by sign. A +2.4% expense increase is bad and must not read lime.
- Give each sparkline gradient its own id (`useId`). A shared id makes every card paint with the first card's colour.
- A series with fewer than two points has no line; the sparkline is skipped rather than drawn as a dot.

## Notes

- Pass `format` per item for non-currency metrics such as a savings rate.
- Without `selectable` the cards are plain `<div>`s with no focus stops.
- `sparkPoints` is exported for reuse in other tiny charts.

## Definition of done

# Build: Floating Stickers

Playful stickers for a landing section, like the characters that peek over a footer line. Each sticker sits at a fractional position in its field and bobs on a slow float whose duration, phase, lift and sway come from a seed, so every load looks the same. Grab one with a pointer and it scales up, gains a deeper shadow and rises to the top of the stack. It follows the pointer through pointer capture and stays clamped to the field. Focused stickers move with the arrow keys.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Die-cut SVG characters that bob on seeded floats. Drag one and it lifts above the rest, clamped to the frame. Arrow keys nudge it.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The root is an `@container` field. Its `children` render in a `z-0` layer, and a `pointer-events-none` overlay above them holds the stickers. Each sticker is absolutely placed at `left: x%`, `top: y%` and centred with `translate(-50%, -50%)`. Its width is `min(size px, size/6.4 cqw)`, so it shrinks with a field narrower than 640px.
2. Every sticker has four layers. The outer layer carries the drag offset and the z-index. The lift layer scales to 1.1 and swaps `drop-shadow-md` for `drop-shadow-xl` while held. The float layer runs a Web Animations API loop, and the art layer holds the resting tilt. Because the float is WAAPI on `transform`, it runs on the compositor and never re-renders React.
3. Float parameters come from `createRng(`${seed}:${id}`)`: a duration of 4.2 to 7.4s, a negative start delay so the stickers start out of phase, 5 to 11px of lift, ±3px of drift and 1.5 to 4.5° of sway. The loop alternates with ease-in-out, and is paused on grab and resumed on drop.
4. On pointerdown the sticker calls `setPointerCapture`, records the start pointer and offset, and computes bounds once: the field rect minus the sticker's resting rect. A sticker placed partly outside the field keeps its current offset as a valid edge, so it never jumps. Pointermove clamps the offset into those bounds. Pointerup, pointercancel and lostpointercapture all end the drag through one handler.
5. Stacking is an order array in the parent, with the last id on top. Grabbing or key-nudging a sticker moves its id to the end, and each sticker's z-index is its rank + 1. The top sticker carries `data-top`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `float = 4200 to 7400ms, alternate, ease-in-out, lift 5 to 11px, sway 1.5 to 4.5°`
  At this pace the motion reads as idle breathing rather than a call to action, and differing durations keep the stickers from syncing up.
- `grab lift = scale 1.1, drop-shadow-md → drop-shadow-xl, 200ms ease-out`
  A sticker peeled off a page gets bigger and casts a softer, larger shadow. The scale is on its own layer, so it never fights the drag offset or the float.
- `key step = 10px, Shift 40px`
  Small enough to place precisely, and Shift crosses the field in a few presses.
- `responsive size = min(size px, size / 6.4 cqw)`
  Full size from a 640px field. At a 328px phone field an 88px sticker drops to about 45px and stays clear of the headline.

## API

```ts
function FloatingStickers(props: { stickers: StickerItem[]; seed?: string; draggable?: boolean; onGrab?: (id: string) => void; onMove?: (id: string, offset: { x: number; y: number }) => void; children?: ReactNode; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `stickers: StickerItem[]`
  `{ id, label, kind?, art?, x, y, size?, rotate? }`. x and y are 0 to 1 fractions of the field, `kind` is blob, star, cloud, heart or chart, and `art` is custom artwork.
- `seed: string` — default `"kinetic"`
  Seeds every float. Same seed, same motion.
- `draggable: boolean` — default `true`
  Enables pointer drag and arrow-key nudging. When false, the stickers are decorative and aria-hidden.
- `onGrab: (id) => void`
  Fires on pointer grab and key nudge.
- `onMove: (id, offset) => void`
  Fires on drop (if moved) and on each key nudge, with the offset in px from the resting place.
- `children: ReactNode`
  Section content beneath the stickers.
- `className: string`
  Field classes. Give it a height.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
function Sticker({ item, seed, draggable, reduced, z, top, fieldRef, raise, onMove }: StickerProps) {
  const [offset, setOffset] = useState<StickerOffset>({ x: 0, y: 0 });
  const [dragging, setDragging] = useState(false);
  const floatRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const anim = useRef<Animation | null>(null);
  const drag = useRef<{ pointer: number; sx: number; sy: number; ox: number; oy: number; x: number; y: number; b: Bounds } | null>(null);
  const size = item.size ?? 88;

  // The float runs on the compositor through WAAPI, so a bobbing sticker
  // never re-renders React. Reduced motion skips it: the sticker rests still.
  useEffect(() => {
    const el = floatRef.current;
    if (!el || reduced || typeof el.animate !== "function") return;
    const p = floatParams(seed, item.id);
    const a = el.animate(
      [
        { transform: `translate3d(0, 0, 0) rotate(${-p.sway}deg)` },
        { transform: `translate3d(${p.drift}px, ${-p.lift}px, 0) rotate(${p.sway}deg)` },
      ],
      { duration: p.duration, delay: p.delay, iterations: Infinity, direction: "alternate", easing: "ease-in-out" },
    );
    anim.current = a;
    return () => {
      a.cancel();
      anim.current = null;
    };
  }, [reduced, seed, item.id]);

  /** Allowed offsets that keep the sticker box inside the field. A sticker placed half outside may stay there. */
  const bounds = (el: HTMLElement): Bounds | null => {
    const field = fieldRef.current;
    if (!field) return null;
    const f = field.getBoundingClientRect();
    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    return {
      minX: Math.min(f.left - (r.left - offset.x), offset.x),
      maxX: Math.max(f.right - (r.right - offset.x), offset.x),
      minY: Math.min(f.top - (r.top - offset.y), offset.y),
      maxY: Math.max(f.bottom - (r.bottom - offset.y), offset.y),
    };
  };

  const onPointerDown = (event: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (!draggable || event.button !== 0 || drag.current) return;
    const b = bounds(event.currentTarget);
    if (!b) return;
    event.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId);
    drag.current = { pointer: event.pointerId, sx: event.clientX, sy: event.clientY, ox: offset.x, oy: offset.y, x: offset.x, y: offset.y, b };
    anim.current?.pause();
    setDragging(true);
    raise(item.id);
  };

  const onPointerMove = (event: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const d = drag.current;
    if (!d || d.pointer !== event.pointerId) return;
    d.x = clamp(d.ox + event.clientX - d.sx, d.b.minX, d.b.maxX);
    d.y = clamp(d.oy + event.clientY - d.sy, d.b.minY, d.b.maxY);
    setOffset({ x: d.x, y: d.y });
  };

  // Up, cancel and lost capture all land here; the first one wins.
  const end = (event: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const d = drag.current;
    if (!d || d.pointer !== event.pointerId) return;
    drag.current = null;
    anim.current?.play();
    setDragging(false);
    if (d.x !== d.ox || d.y !== d.oy) onMove?.(item.id, { x: Math.round(d.x), y: Math.round(d.y) });
  };

  const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const step = KEY_STEPS[event.key];
    if (!draggable || !step || drag.current) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    const b = bounds(event.currentTarget);
    if (!b) return;
    const by = event.shiftKey ? 40 : 10;
    const next = { x: clamp(offset.x + step[0] * by, b.minX, b.maxX), y: clamp(offset.y + step[1] * by, b.minY, b.maxY) };
    raise(item.id);
    if (next.x === offset.x && next.y === offset.y) return;
    setOffset(next);
    onMove?.(item.id, { x: Math.round(next.x), y: Math.round(next.y) });
  };

  return (
    <div
      data-sticker={item.id}
      data-top={top ? "" : undefined}
      data-dragging={dragging ? "" : undefined}
      role="img"
      aria-label={item.label}
      aria-roledescription={draggable ? "draggable sticker" : undefined}
      aria-keyshortcuts={draggable ? "ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight" : undefined}
      tabIndex={draggable ? 0 : undefined}
      onPointerDown={onPointerDown}
      onPointerMove={onPointerMove}
      onPointerUp={end}
      onPointerCancel={end}
      onLostPointerCapture={end}
      onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
      className={cx(
        "absolute aspect-square rounded-[28%] outline-none",
        draggable &&
          "pointer-events-auto cursor-grab touch-none select-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-background-primary-default",
        dragging && "cursor-grabbing",
      )}
      style={{
        left: `${item.x * 100}%`,
        top: `${item.y * 100}%`,
        width: `min(${size}px, ${(size / 6.4).toFixed(2)}cqw)`,
        zIndex: z,
        transform: `translate(-50%, -50%) translate3d(${offset.x}px, ${offset.y}px, 0)`,
      }}
    >
      <div
        className={cx(
          "size-full transition-[transform,filter] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
          dragging ? "scale-110 drop-shadow-xl" : "drop-shadow-md",
        )}
      >
        <div ref={floatRef} className="size-full">
          <div className="size-full" style={{ transform: `rotate(${item.rotate ?? 0}deg)` }}>
            {item.art ?? <StickerArtwork kind={item.kind ?? "blob"} className="size-full" />}
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Each float animation is cancelled in its effect cleanup, which runs on unmount, on a reduced-motion change or on a new seed. Pointer listeners are React props on the sticker, and pointer capture is released by the browser on pointerup. Lost capture ends the drag through the same handler, so no drag state outlives the gesture.

**Reduced motion.** With prefers-reduced-motion, `useReducedMotion` skips the WAAPI float, so every sticker rests still at its tilt. The lift scale and shadow apply instantly (`motion-reduce:transition-none`). Dragging and key nudging still work, because they follow the user's own input.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Putting the float and the drag on the same `transform`. Each would overwrite the other every frame, so the sticker snaps back mid-drag. Keep separate nested layers.
- Skipping `touch-action: none`. On touch screens the browser starts scrolling and fires pointercancel after a few pixels, so the drag dies. The draggable stickers carry `touch-none`.
- Seeding with `Math.random()`. The server and client would render different phases, so hydration fails and screenshots never match. Use the seeded rng.
- Clamping against bounds computed on every move. Reading layout in each pointermove is a forced reflow per frame. Bounds are computed once on pointerdown.

## Notes

- Pass `draggable={false}` for pure decoration. Stickers then ignore the pointer and are hidden from assistive tech.
- To reset positions, remount with a new `key` (the demo's Reset button does this). Offsets are internal state relative to each resting place.
- Give the field an explicit height. The overlay is `absolute inset-0`, so it covers whatever box the children produce.

## Definition of done

Five stickers (blob, star, chart, cloud, heart) bob out of sync around the "Make it yours" headline. Dragging the star moves it with the pointer, scales it up, puts it above the other stickers and keeps it inside the field, even when the pointer leaves it. The status line reads "Sleepy star moved +x, +y px". A focused sticker moves 10px per arrow key. Reset puts every sticker back. Under reduced motion nothing bobs. At 360px the stickers shrink and stay clear of the copy.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
