# Build: Funnel Chart Card

A dashboard card that draws a conversion funnel left to right. Every stage is a column whose band is sized to its share of the top stage and eases into the next stage's height, with a white share pill in the middle and a stat tile underneath. Hovering, focusing or tapping a stage dims the others, darkens it one tone and swaps the count-up headline for that stage's count with its step conversion from the stage before. A period select swaps the data and the bands re-grow from their old shape.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A horizontal conversion funnel: tapered SVG bands per stage with share pills, stat tiles and a headline that follows the hovered stage.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Each stage is a `<button>` in a flex row (`gap-0.5`, so the card surface shows as a 2px seam between columns). Inside it an absolutely positioned SVG uses `viewBox="0 0 100 {chartHeight}"` with `preserveAspectRatio="none"`: vertical units are pixels, horizontal units are 0-100 of the column, so the band stretches with the card while its heights stay exact.
2. Shares (`value / top`) go through `useTweenedValues`, a rAF tween with ease-out cubic over 520ms that starts from zeros on mount and from the current shares on every period change. Heights are `max(2, share * (chartHeight - 24))`, centred on `chartHeight / 2`.
3. `bandPath(h0, h1)` draws one column from its own height to the next stage's. Curved: flat to x=50, then two cubic Béziers with both control points at x=75 (horizontal tangents at both ends), so the edge is an S-curve. Sharp: a plain trapezoid. The last column uses its own height for both ends, so it runs flat.
4. Curved columns paint two halo copies of the band first, grown by 12px and 6px per side at 0.16 and 0.32 opacity, then the core. Sharp columns instead paint a 36px track rect at 0.18 opacity, so stages near 0% still have a visible lane.
5. The active stage is `hovered ?? pinned`. Pointer enter and focus set `hovered`; pointer leave and blur clear it; click toggles `pinned` (`aria-pressed`). Inactive columns and tiles fade to opacity 0.35 / 0.45 over 200ms, and the active core switches from `--color-chart-N` to `--color-chart-N-active`.
6. The header shows the title, `headline ?? top` and a lime/rose delta chip. With a stage active it shows the stage label, its value and a neutral chip reading "56% of Link opened" (step conversion) or "Top of funnel". The number counts through `useCountUp` (320ms) inside a `<p>` keyed by the active index, so the fade replays per swap.
7. Under the chart, `StatTiles` lays out one white tile per stage with a 2.5 swatch, label and value. Tiles take `flex-basis: calc((100% - gaps) / columns)` with a 120px minimum and `grow`, so a 360px card wraps to two per row. Hovering a tile sets the same active stage.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `EDGE / halo layers = 12px; layers +12px @ 0.16 and +6px @ 0.32`
  Leaves 136px of core in the default 160px chart, and the two soft layers give the curved shape its layered edge without a stroke.
- `FLAT = 50 (of 100 column units)`
  The band holds its height for the first half of its column, so the share pill always sits on a flat stretch, then eases into the next stage across the second half.
- `SHARP_TRACK = 36px at 0.18 opacity`
  Sharp trapezoids of 1% stages collapse to a line; the track keeps a lane to hover and read.
- `MIN_CORE = 2px`
  A stage with a tiny share still draws a visible line instead of vanishing.
- `tween = 520ms ease-out cubic, from 0 on mount`
  Long enough to read as growth, short enough that switching periods feels immediate. Shares are tweened rather than heights so `chartHeight` changes never animate.
- `dim opacity = columns 0.35, tiles 0.45, 200ms`
  Pushes the other stages back without hiding them, so the active stage still reads in context.

## API

```ts
function FunnelChartCard(props: { title?: string; ranges?: FunnelRange[]; stages?: FunnelStage[]; delta?: number; range?: string; defaultRange?: string; onRangeChange?: (id: string) => void; shape?: "curved" | "sharp"; mono?: boolean; chartHeight?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type FunnelStage = { label: string; value: number; color?: ChartColor }
type FunnelRange = { id: string; label: string; stages: FunnelStage[]; delta?: number; headline?: number }
```

- `title: string` — default `"Sign-up funnel"`
  Header label while no stage is active; also the card's accessible name.
- `ranges: FunnelRange[]` — default `SIGNUP_FUNNEL_RANGES`
  Periods with their own stages and delta. Two or more show the period select.
- `stages: FunnelStage[]`
  A single funnel, top stage first. Overrides `ranges` and hides the select.
- `delta: number`
  Headline chip percentage when `stages` is used.
- `range: string`
  Controlled period id.
- `defaultRange: string` — default `first range id`
  Initial period when uncontrolled.
- `onRangeChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called when the period select changes.
- `shape: "curved" | "sharp"` — default `"curved"`
  Eased taper with layered halo, or plain trapezoids over a faint track.
- `mono: boolean` — default `false`
  Paints every stage in the secondary text colour (primary when active) and hides tile swatches.
- `chartHeight: number` — default `160`
  Chart height in px including the 12px halo above and below.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function FunnelChartCard({
  title = "Sign-up funnel",
  ranges = SIGNUP_FUNNEL_RANGES,
  stages: stagesProp,
  delta: deltaProp,
  range: rangeProp,
  defaultRange,
  onRangeChange,
  shape = "curved",
  mono = false,
  chartHeight = 160,
  className,
}: FunnelChartCardProps) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const [innerRange, setInnerRange] = useState(defaultRange ?? ranges[0]?.id ?? "");
  const rangeId = rangeProp ?? innerRange;
  const activeRange = ranges.find((r) => r.id === rangeId) ?? ranges[0];
  const stages = stagesProp ?? activeRange?.stages ?? [];
  const delta = stagesProp ? deltaProp : activeRange?.delta;

  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const [pinned, setPinned] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const active = hovered ?? (pinned !== null && pinned < stages.length ? pinned : null);

  const top = stages[0]?.value ?? 0;
  const coreMax = chartHeight - EDGE * 2;
  const mid = chartHeight / 2;
  // Shares are tweened, not heights, so a new period re-grows from the old shape.
  const shares = useTweenedValues(
    stages.map((s) => (top > 0 ? s.value / top : 0)),
    { disabled: reduced },
  );
  const heights = shares.map((share) => Math.max(MIN_CORE, share * coreMax));

  const activeStage = active !== null ? stages[active] : undefined;
  const prevStage = active !== null && active > 0 ? stages[active - 1] : undefined;
  const headline = activeStage ? activeStage.value : (!stagesProp && activeRange?.headline) || top;

  const selectRange = (id: string) => {
    if (rangeProp === undefined) setInnerRange(id);
    setPinned(null);
    onRangeChange?.(id);
  };

  return (
    <ChartCardFrame className={className} aria-label={title}>
      <ChartCardHeader
        label={activeStage ? activeStage.label : title}
        value={headline}
        valueKey={active ?? "total"}
        delta={activeStage ? undefined : delta}
        note={
          activeStage
            ? prevStage
              ? `${pct(activeStage.value, prevStage.value)}% of ${prevStage.label}`
              : "Top of funnel"
            : undefined
        }
        action={
          !stagesProp && ranges.length > 1 ? (
            <PeriodSelect options={ranges} selectedId={activeRange?.id ?? ""} onChange={selectRange} />
          ) : undefined
        }
      />

      <div
        role="group"
        aria-label={`${title} stages`}
        className="flex gap-0.5 px-2"
        style={{ height: chartHeight }}
        onPointerLeave={() => setHovered(null)}
      >
        {stages.map((stage, index) => {
          const color = CHART_COLORS[chartColorAt(index, stage.color)];
          const isActive = active === index;
          const fill = mono ? (isActive ? "var(--color-text-primary)" : MONO_FILL) : isActive ? color.active : color.fill;
          const h0 = heights[index] ?? MIN_CORE;
          const h1 = heights[index + 1] ?? h0;
          const share = pct(stage.value, top);
          const prev = index > 0 ? stages[index - 1] : undefined;
          return (
            <button
              key={`${stage.label}-${index}`}
              type="button"
              aria-pressed={pinned === index}
              aria-label={`${stage.label}: ${formatInt(stage.value)}, ${share}% of ${stages[0]?.label ?? "top"}${
                prev ? `, ${pct(stage.value, prev.value)}% of ${prev.label}` : ""
              }`}
              onPointerEnter={() => setHovered(index)}
              onFocus={() => setHovered(index)}
              onBlur={() => setHovered(null)}
              onClick={() => setPinned((p) => (p === index ? null : index))}
              className={cx(
                "relative min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer rounded-md outline-none",
                "transition-opacity duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
                "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
                active !== null && !isActive && "opacity-35",
              )}
            >
              <svg
                aria-hidden
                viewBox={`0 0 100 ${chartHeight}`}
                preserveAspectRatio="none"
                className="absolute inset-0 size-full overflow-visible"
              >
                {shape === "sharp" ? (
                  <rect
                    x={0}
                    y={mid - SHARP_TRACK / 2}
                    width={100}
                    height={SHARP_TRACK}
                    style={{ fill: mono ? MONO_FILL : color.fill, opacity: 0.18 }}
                  />
                ) : (
                  LAYERS.map((layer) => (
                    <path
                      key={layer.grow}
                      d={bandPath(h0 + layer.grow * 2, h1 + layer.grow * 2, mid, shape)}
                      style={{ fill: mono ? MONO_FILL : color.fill, opacity: layer.opacity }}
                    />
                  ))
                )}
                <path
                  d={bandPath(h0, h1, mid, shape)}
                  className="transition-[fill] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none"
                  style={{ fill }}
                />
              </svg>
              <span
                aria-hidden
                className="absolute top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 rounded-full bg-background-primary-default px-1.5 py-px text-caption-1-medium text-text-primary tabular-nums shadow-xs"
              >
                {share}%
              </span>
            </button>
          );
        })}
      </div>

      <StatTiles
        columns={Math.max(1, stages.length)}
        activeIndex={active}
        onActiveChange={setHovered}
        items={stages.map((stage, index) => ({
          id: `${stage.label}-${index}`,
          label: stage.label,
          value: formatInt(stage.value),
          color: mono ? null : chartColorAt(index, stage.color),
        }))}
      />
    </ChartCardFrame>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The tween and `useCountUp` cancel their pending animation frame on every new target and on unmount. Hover state is plain React state; the Select's outside-press listener is removed by the Select itself when it closes or unmounts.

**Reduced motion.** `useTweenedValues` is disabled, so the bands render at their final shares on mount and jump on a period change. The headline count runs over 1ms (a single frame), the number fade and the opacity/fill transitions are removed with `motion-reduce:` variants.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using `preserveAspectRatio` other than `"none"`. The viewBox is 100 units wide but the column is not, so a uniform scale letterboxes the band and the columns stop meeting at their edges.
- Putting the share pill inside the SVG. With a non-uniform scale the text would stretch. The pill is an HTML span centred over the column.
- Tweening the path strings or the pixel heights. Interpolating shares keeps the shape correct at every frame and lets a new period start from wherever the previous tween had got to.
- Expecting Recharts' `<Funnel>`: it stacks vertical trapezoids and cannot draw the eased horizontal taper.

## Notes

- `SIGNUP_FUNNEL_RANGES`, `FunnelStage`, `FunnelRange` and `FunnelShape` are exported. Pass `stages` (and `delta`) for a single static funnel without the period select.
- The shell companion (`ChartCardFrame`, `ChartCardHeader`, `PeriodSelect`, `StatTiles`, `CHART_COLORS`, `useTweenedValues`) is shared by the other BoardUI chart cards in this batch.

## Definition of done

The card shows "Sign-up funnel", "197" and a lime "+5.2%" chip, four columns (lime, blue, purple, pink) with pills 100%, 56%, 39%, 19%, and tiles Link opened 197, Started 110, Completed 77, Converted 38. Hovering Started dims the other columns and tiles, and the header reads "Started", "110" and "56% of Link opened". Choosing "Last 30 days" re-grows the bands and the headline counts to 842. Clicking a stage sets its aria-pressed to true; clicking again clears it.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: GitHub Star Button

A compact pill button in the style of a repository star control, without any logo: a star glyph, a "Star" label and a count in an inset pill. Pressing it toggles starred: the outline star swaps to a filled amber one with a small springy pop, the label reads "Starred" and the count rolls up by one; pressing again rolls it back down.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A star toggle with a glyph, a Star label and a count pill. Starring pops the star and rolls the en-US formatted count by one.

- Category: action
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1, motion@^12.43.0, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. React Aria `ToggleButton` owns the state semantics: it renders a native button with `aria-pressed`, handles pointer, keyboard and touch presses, and exposes `data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed` and `data-focus-visible` for styling.
2. The shown total is `count + starred - defaultStarred`, so `count` is the number as loaded (including the viewer when they had already starred) and toggling moves it by exactly one in either direction.
3. The count is keyed by its value inside `AnimatePresence mode="popLayout"`. Each toggle stores a direction (+1 up, -1 down) and passes it as `custom`, so the old number exits upward while the new one enters from below on a star, and the reverse on an unstar. `popLayout` takes the exiting number out of flow so the two never stack.
4. The star glyph is a `motion.span` keyed by the starred state: starring remounts it from `scale 0.4, rotate -40deg` with a bouncy spring, unstarring from `scale 0.8` with no bounce.
5. All numbers use one `Intl.NumberFormat("en-US")`, so 999 to 1,000 gets its comma and the server and client strings always agree.
6. The accessible name is fixed text plus the current total ("Star kinetic, 12,481 stars"); the visible label and pill are `aria-hidden`, so the Star / Starred swap does not rename the control and `aria-pressed` carries the state.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `count roll = spring, 0.35s, bounce 0.2`
  Quick enough to feel like a counter tick, with a hint of overshoot so the new digit lands.
- `star pop = spring, 0.45s, bounce 0.55 from scale 0.4 / -40deg`
  Starring is the rewarding action and gets the expressive motion; unstarring settles without bounce.
- `press scale = 0.97`
  Tactile press feedback on `data-pressed` without shifting surrounding layout.

## API

```ts
function GithubStarButton(props: { count: number; defaultStarred?: boolean; onStarredChange?: (starred: boolean) => void; label?: string; starredLabel?: string; "aria-label"?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `count: number`
  Star total as loaded, including the viewer when `defaultStarred` is true.
- `defaultStarred: boolean` — default `false`
  Initial starred state.
- `onStarredChange: (starred: boolean) => void`
  Fires on every toggle.
- `label: string` — default `"Star"`
  Visible label when not starred.
- `starredLabel: string` — default `"Starred"`
  Visible label when starred.
- `aria-label: string`
  Accessible name; defaults to `label`. ", N stars" is appended.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the button.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function GithubStarButton({
  count,
  defaultStarred = false,
  onStarredChange,
  label = "Star",
  starredLabel = "Starred",
  "aria-label": ariaLabel,
  className,
}: GithubStarButtonProps) {
  const reduce = useReducedMotion();
  const [starred, setStarred] = useState(defaultStarred);
  // +1 for "count went up", -1 for "went down"; drives which way the digits roll.
  const [dir, setDir] = useState(1);
  const total = count + Number(starred) - Number(defaultStarred);
  const formatted = numberFormat.format(total);

  const toggle = (next: boolean) => {
    setDir(next ? 1 : -1);
    setStarred(next);
    onStarredChange?.(next);
  };

  const Icon = starred ? RiStarFill : RiStarLine;

  return (
    <ToggleButton
      isSelected={starred}
      onChange={toggle}
      aria-label={`${ariaLabel ?? label}, ${formatted} stars`}
      className={cx(
        "group inline-flex h-9 items-center gap-2 rounded-xl bg-background-primary-default pr-1.5 pl-3 text-body-2-medium text-text-primary shadow-xs ring-1 ring-separator-border outline-none select-none",
        "cursor-pointer transition-[background-color,box-shadow,scale] duration-150 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
        "data-hovered:bg-background-secondary-hover data-pressed:scale-[0.97] data-focus-visible:ring-2 data-focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
        className,
      )}
    >
      <span className="relative grid size-4 place-items-center">
        {reduce ? (
          <Icon aria-hidden className={cx("size-4", starred ? "text-status-yellow-text" : "text-foreground-icon-secondary")} />
        ) : (
          <motion.span
            key={String(starred)}
            initial={{ scale: starred ? 0.4 : 0.8, rotate: starred ? -40 : 0 }}
            animate={{ scale: 1, rotate: 0 }}
            transition={{ type: "spring", duration: 0.45, bounce: starred ? 0.55 : 0 }}
            className="grid place-items-center"
          >
            <Icon aria-hidden className={cx("size-4", starred ? "text-status-yellow-text" : "text-foreground-icon-secondary")} />
          </motion.span>
        )}
      </span>
      <span aria-hidden>{starred ? starredLabel : label}</span>
      <span
        aria-hidden
        data-count
        className="relative inline-flex h-6 items-center overflow-hidden rounded-lg bg-background-secondary-default px-2 text-caption-1-semibold text-text-secondary tabular-nums ring-1 ring-separator-border group-data-selected:text-text-primary"
      >
        {reduce ? (
          formatted
        ) : (
          <AnimatePresence mode="popLayout" initial={false} custom={dir}>
            <motion.span
              key={total}
              custom={dir}
              variants={roll}
              initial="enter"
              animate="center"
              exit="exit"
              transition={ROLL}
              className="inline-block"
            >
              {formatted}
            </motion.span>
          </AnimatePresence>
        )}
      </span>
    </ToggleButton>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers or listeners. Motion stops any running spring when its element unmounts, and AnimatePresence removes the exiting number when its exit finishes.

**Reduced motion.** With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (via `useReducedMotion`) the star and count render as plain elements without motion wrappers, so the glyph and number swap instantly; the press scale and colour transitions are removed with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Formatting with `toLocaleString()` and no locale. A German visitor sees "12.480" on the client after "12,480" from the server, which is a hydration mismatch; the locale is fixed to en-US.
- Computing the roll direction from the new value in the exit animation. The exiting element keeps its own props, so without `AnimatePresence custom` it exits using the previous toggle's direction.
- Changing the accessible name between "Star" and "Starred". A toggle button should keep its name and report state through `aria-pressed`.

## Notes

- Call your API in `onStarredChange`; the button updates optimistically and does not roll back on its own.
- For a real repo, link the surrounding card to GitHub and keep this control for in-app starring only.

## Definition of done

The first button reads "Star" with an outline star and 12,480. Clicking it sets aria-pressed="true", fills the star amber with a pop, changes the label to "Starred" and rolls the pill to 12,481 from below. Clicking again rolls back to 12,480 from above. The second button starts starred at 1,000 and unstarring rolls it to 999. Space and Enter toggle it from the keyboard with a visible focus ring. With reduced motion every change is instant.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: GitHub Stars CTA

A two-column landing block. The left side has a pill eyebrow, a large heading ("The free tier lives on GitHub" by default), a paragraph, a checklist and an optional secondary link. The right side is a repo card: an accent gradient band with a faded dot grid, a repository glyph tile overlapping the band, the owner / name in mono with a Public pill, the description, a stats panel with a large star count and a Star button, and a row of forks, license and language.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Open-source free tier section: copy and checklist beside a repo card with a counting star total, star button and repo facts.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The section is a size container. Below `@4xl` the copy and card stack; from `@4xl` they sit in a `minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,420px)` grid, so the layout follows the space it is given rather than the window.
2. The star total counts up once: `useCountUp` resets the shown value to 0 in a layout effect (before first paint), then an `IntersectionObserver` at 40% visibility starts a `requestAnimationFrame` loop that eases from 0 to `stars` over `COUNT_MS` with an ease-out cubic, `1 - (1 - t)^3`. The observer disconnects on first sight, so scrolling back does not replay it.
3. Only the small `StarCount` component re-renders per frame. Its visible digits are `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden sibling always holds the final "12,480 stars" text, so screen readers never hear the intermediate numbers.
4. All numbers go through one `Intl.NumberFormat("en-US")`, so server and client format the same way and hydration matches whatever the visitor locale is.
5. The band art is CSS only: a `bg-linear-to-br` accent gradient into the card surface, and a dot grid drawn with a `radial-gradient(currentColor ...)` background tinted `accent-500/35` and faded with `mask-l-from-10% mask-l-to-90%`.
6. Repo facts are a `dl` with icon `dt`s carrying sr-only labels (Forks, License, Language); missing fields are left out.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `COUNT_MS = 1200`
  Long enough to read as counting, short enough to finish before the eye moves to the button.
- `IntersectionObserver threshold = 0.4`
  The count starts once the stats panel is clearly on screen, not while it is a sliver at the fold.
- `card column = minmax(0, 420px)`
  A repo card wider than this turns into a long, sparse strip; the copy column takes the rest.

```ts
interface GithubRepo { owner: string; name: string; href: string; description?: string; stars: number; forks?: number; license?: string; language?: string }
```

- `repo: GithubRepo`
  Owner, name, link, star total and optional description, forks, license and language.
- `eyebrow: ReactNode` — default `"Open source"`
  Pill above the heading; pass null to hide it.

  Section heading.

  Paragraph under the heading; a default about the public MIT repo is provided.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Counts from 0 to `target` the first time `ref` is 40% visible. Reduced motion shows the target at once. */
function useCountUp(target: number, ref: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(target);

  // Layout effect: the reset to 0 lands before the first paint, so the final number never flashes first.
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const node = ref.current;
    const reduce = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
    if (!node || reduce || typeof IntersectionObserver === "undefined") {
      setValue(target);
      return;
    }
    setValue(0);
    let frame = 0;
    const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
      (entries) => {
        if (!entries.some((entry) => entry.isIntersecting)) return;
        observer.disconnect();
        const start = performance.now();
        const tick = (now: number) => {
          const t = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (now - start) / COUNT_MS));
          setValue(Math.round(target * (1 - (1 - t) ** 3)));
          if (t < 1) frame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
        };
        frame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
      },
      { threshold: 0.4 },
    );
    observer.observe(node);
    return () => {
      observer.disconnect();
      cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
    };
  }, [target, ref]);

  return value;
}

function StarCount({ stars }: { stars: number }) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);
  const value = useCountUp(stars, ref);
  return (
    <>
      <span ref={ref} aria-hidden className="tabular-nums">
        {numberFormat.format(value)}
      </span>
      <span className="sr-only">{numberFormat.format(stars)} stars</span>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The layout effect disconnects the IntersectionObserver and cancels any pending animation frame on unmount or when `stars` changes.

**Reduced motion.** With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the star count shows the final number straight away and no animation frame is requested. Nothing else on the block moves.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Starting the count in `useEffect` from the server-rendered final value. The real number paints for one frame and then jumps to 0; resetting in a layout effect avoids the flash.
- Formatting with the visitor locale (`toLocaleString()`). Server and browser can disagree ("12,480" vs "12.480") and React reports a hydration mismatch; the formatter is pinned to en-US.
- Announcing every frame of the count. The animated digits are hidden from assistive tech and the final total is exposed separately.

## Notes

- Pass a real star count from your build step or an API route; the component does no fetching.
- Use the GitHub URL as `repo.href`; the Star button is a plain link, so add `target` handling in your app if you want a new tab.

## Definition of done

The block shows the heading, paragraph and three checks on the left and the repo card on the right at 1280px, stacked at narrow widths. When the card comes into view the star total counts from 0 to 12,480 in about a second and stops there. Forks read "642 forks", license "MIT license". The Star button and the secondary link are links with visible focus rings. With reduced motion the total is 12,480 from the start. Light and dark both keep the gradient band and dot grid visible.

# Build: GPU Cubic-Bezier Burst

Concentric rings of dots turning slowly. Fire a sector — by clicking it, or by waiting for the automatic cycle — and its particles burst outward and fade, each one following its own cubic-bezier curve. The curve is the same four numbers CSS takes, but solved per vertex per frame by Newton's method, which is what lets two hundred particles carry two hundred different easings while the CPU only advances a clock.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Rings of dots that burst on click, every particle solving its own cubic-bezier easing in the vertex shader.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1

## How it works

1. A cubic bezier is parametric: for a parameter `t` it gives a point `(x(t), y(t))`. Easing needs `y` at a given *x*, and a cubic has no closed-form inverse, so the shader runs Newton's method — 8 iterations of `t -= (x(t) - target) / x'(t)`, seeded with `t = x` because the curve is monotonic in x — then evaluates `y(t)`.
2. The four control numbers ride in an `aBezier` attribute rather than a uniform. That is the whole reason to solve on the GPU: a uniform would give every particle in the burst one shared easing, and per-particle easing computed on the CPU would mean a buffer upload every frame.
3. Firing writes the current burst-clock time into a contiguous slice of the `aStart` attribute — one sector, one range, one `needsUpdate`. Each particle then computes `age = uBurstTime - aStart - delay` and animates only while `0 <= age <= uBurstDuration`; a start time of 0 means never fired, which is why the clock starts at 1.
4. Resting dots and burst particles live in the same buffer and the same draw call, distinguished by an `isBurst` flag. Burst particles sit invisible on the outer ring until fired, rather than the resting dots being displaced — displacing them would tear a hole in the ring and then pop it shut when the burst ended.
5. There are two clocks. `uRotation` accumulates from delta time only when motion is allowed; `uBurstTime` always accumulates. Under reduced motion the ring freezes at 0.35 rad and the automatic cycle stops, but a click still fires a full burst, and the frame loop is subscribed only for as long as one is in flight.
6. Flight direction is `angle + uRotation`, evaluated live rather than baked, so a burst stays radial to the ring while the ring keeps turning underneath it. Alpha fades linearly against the eased flight, and point size shrinks to 45%, so the particle dissipates instead of blinking out at full size.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `NEWTON_ITERATIONS = 8`
  Newton converges quadratically here, so 4 iterations already land inside a pixel. 8 is cheap insurance for control points near 0 or 1, where the derivative shrinks and convergence slows.
- `MIN_DERIVATIVE = 0.000001`
  Newton divides by the derivative. A curve with a flat segment divides by ~0, `t` becomes NaN, and the NaN propagates into `gl_Position` — the vertex silently disappears rather than erroring.
- `base curve = (0, 0.9, 0.5, 1)`
  A hard ease-out: almost all the distance is covered in the first third. Each particle jitters around it, with x-coordinates clamped to 0..1 because the solver needs monotonicity in x — the same constraint CSS puts on `cubic-bezier()`.
- `MAX_LAUNCH_DELAY = 0.09s`
  Particles all leaving on one frame read as a single expanding ring. Staggering launches over ~90ms reads as a spray, and staying well under `burstDuration` keeps the last launch ahead of the first landing.
- `burstDuration = 0.45s`
  Longer than the 0.25s a click ping wants, because at preview-card size the eye needs the extra frames to actually see the easing differ between particles. Shorten it toward 0.25 when the burst is real button feedback.
- `BURST_END_SIZE = 0.45`
  Particles shrink to 45% over the flight. Constant-size particles read as confetti; shrinking ones read as one thing dissipating.
- `STATIC_ROTATION = 0.35 rad`
  Angle the ring is frozen at under reduced motion. Off-axis, so the field does not look like it snapped to a grid the moment motion was disabled.
- `RING_DOT_SCALE / BURST_DOT_SCALE = 0.7 / 1.15`
  Burst particles are visibly larger than the resting field, so the burst reads as the event rather than as the ring shedding pixels.
- `flight fan = +/- 0.175 rad`
  Jitter added to each particle's radial direction. Pure radial launches leave on rails and the burst looks like a line drawing; more than ~0.3 rad and the sectors start to overlap.

## API

```ts
function GpuBezierBurst(props: { ringCount?: number; ringDots?: number; innerRadius?: number; groups?: number; burstDots?: number; spinSpeed?: number; chordInterval?: number; burstDuration?: number; burstRadius?: number; dotScale?: number; viewScale?: number; opacity?: number; color?: string; burstColor?: string; seed?: number | string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `ringCount: number` — default `4`
  Concentric rings in the resting field.
- `ringDots: number` — default `190`
  Dots on the outermost ring; inner rings scale down to keep density even.
- `innerRadius: number` — default `0.55`
  Radius of the innermost ring as a fraction of the outermost.
- `groups: number` — default `6`
  Sectors that can be fired independently.
- `burstDots: number` — default `34`
  Burst particles per sector.
- `spinSpeed: number` — default `0.18`
  Ambient ring rotation in radians per second.
- `chordInterval: number` — default `1.5`
  Seconds between automatic firings.
- `burstDuration: number` — default `0.45`
  Seconds a single particle's flight lasts.
- `burstRadius: number` — default `26`
  How far a particle travels, in CSS pixels.
- `dotScale: number` — default `1`
  Dot radius multiplier in CSS pixels.
- `viewScale: number` — default `0.4`
  Model-to-pixel scale as a fraction of the container short side.
- `opacity: number` — default `1`
  Multiplier applied to every dot.
- `color: string` — default `'#6f757e'`
  Resting dot colour.
- `burstColor: string` — default `'#ffffff'`
  Colour mixed in at the hot start of a flight.
- `seed: number | string` — default `'gpu-bezier-burst'`
  Seeds every curve, delay and fan angle for a stable, hydration-safe field.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the host element via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function GpuBezierBurst({
  ringCount = 4,
  ringDots = 190,
  innerRadius = 0.55,
  groups = 6,
  burstDots = 34,
  spinSpeed = 0.18,
  chordInterval = 1.5,
  burstDuration = 0.45,
  burstRadius = 26,
  dotScale = 1,
  viewScale = 0.4,
  opacity = 1,
  color = '#6f757e',
  burstColor = '#ffffff',
  seed = 'gpu-bezier-burst',
  className,
}: GpuBezierBurstProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);
  const [unsupported, setUnsupported] = useState(false);

  // Gates the frame loop under reduced motion: no ambient animation, but a
  // burst in flight still needs frames until it lands.
  const [burstLive, setBurstLive] = useState(false);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const size = useRef({ width, height });
  size.current = { width, height };

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  // Read inside the frame loop rather than closed over, so toggling the OS
  // setting does not tear down and rebuild the GL context.
  const reducedRef = useRef(reduced);
  reducedRef.current = reduced;

  const ready = width > 0 && height > 0;

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready) return;

    if (!hasWebGL()) {
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }

    let renderer: THREE.WebGLRenderer;
    try {
      renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: false, alpha: true });
    } catch {
      // A context can still be refused between the probe and the construction —
      // the tab may have hit the browser's live-context ceiling in between. three
      // throws rather than returning null, and an uncaught throw here takes the
      // page with it.
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }
    renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio());
    renderer.setClearAlpha(0);

    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const camera = new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0.1, 10);
    camera.position.z = 1;

    const rng = createRng(seed);

    const positions: number[] = [];
    const burstData: number[] = [];
    const bezier: number[] = [];

    /* ------------------------------------------------------------------
       Resting rings. Dot count scales with radius so the inner rings are
       not visibly denser than the outer ones — constant dots-per-ring is
       the classic tell of a generated field.
       ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
    for (let r = 0; r < ringCount; r += 1) {
      const t = ringCount === 1 ? 1 : r / (ringCount - 1);
      const radius = innerRadius + (1 - innerRadius) * t;
      const count = Math.max(8, Math.round(ringDots * radius));

      for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
        const angle = (i / count) * Math.PI * 2 + rng() * 0.01;
        positions.push(Math.cos(angle) * radius, Math.sin(angle) * radius, 0);
        // isBurst 0: these never move, so flight angle, delay and curve are unused.
        burstData.push(0, angle, RING_DOT_SCALE, 0);
        bezier.push(0, 0, 1, 1);
      }
    }

    /* ------------------------------------------------------------------
       Burst particles, grouped into contiguous sectors so firing one is a
       single contiguous write into the start-time buffer. They sit on the
       outer ring invisible until fired: displacing the resting dots
       instead would leave a hole in the ring, then pop them back.
       ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
    const groupRanges: { start: number; end: number }[] = [];
    const restingDots = positions.length / 3;
    const sector = (Math.PI * 2) / groups;

    for (let g = 0; g < groups; g += 1) {
      const start = positions.length / 3;
      const centre = g * sector;

      for (let i = 0; i < burstDots; i += 1) {
        const angle = centre + (rng() - 0.5) * sector * 0.9;
        const radius = 0.94 + rng() * 0.06;
        positions.push(Math.cos(angle) * radius, Math.sin(angle) * radius, 0);
        burstData.push(
          1,
          // Flight direction fans slightly off pure radial, so the burst
          // spreads instead of leaving on rails.
          angle + (rng() - 0.5) * 0.35,
          BURST_DOT_SCALE,
          rng() * MAX_LAUNCH_DELAY,
        );

        /* Each particle gets its own curve, jittered around an ease-out
           (0, 0.9, 0.5, 1). x-coordinates are clamped to 0..1 because the
           solver needs the curve monotonic in x — exactly the constraint
           CSS puts on cubic-bezier(). y is free to overshoot. */
        bezier.push(
          Math.min(1, Math.max(0, rng() * 0.25)),
          0.9 + (rng() - 0.5) * 0.3,
          Math.min(1, Math.max(0, 0.5 + (rng() - 0.5) * 0.4)),
          0.95 + rng() * 0.1,
        );
      }
      groupRanges.push({ start, end: positions.length / 3 });
    }

    const total = positions.length / 3;
    const starts = new Float32Array(total);

    const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
    geometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(Float32Array.from(positions), 3));
    geometry.setAttribute('aBurstData', new THREE.BufferAttribute(Float32Array.from(burstData), 4));
    geometry.setAttribute('aBezier', new THREE.BufferAttribute(Float32Array.from(bezier), 4));

    const startAttribute = new THREE.BufferAttribute(starts, 1);
    // The only buffer that changes at runtime, and only on a firing.
    startAttribute.setUsage(THREE.DynamicDrawUsage);
    geometry.setAttribute('aStart', startAttribute);

    const uniforms: Uniforms = {
      uBurstTime: { value: 0 },
      uRotation: { value: STATIC_ROTATION },
      uViewScale: { value: 1 },
      uPixelRatio: { value: renderer.getPixelRatio() },
      uDotScale: { value: dotScale },
      uOpacity: { value: opacity },
      uBurstDuration: { value: burstDuration },
      uBurstRadius: { value: burstRadius },
      uColor: { value: new THREE.Color(color) },
      uBurstColor: { value: new THREE.Color(burstColor) },
    };

    const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader: GPU_BEZIER_BURST_VERT,
      fragmentShader: GPU_BEZIER_BURST_FRAG,
      uniforms,
      transparent: true,
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
    });

    const points = new THREE.Points(geometry, material);
    // Vertices are unit-scale and the real placement happens in the shader, so
    // three's bounding sphere does not describe what is on screen.
    points.frustumCulled = false;
    scene.add(points);

    el.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
    renderer.domElement.style.display = 'block';
    renderer.domElement.style.width = '100%';
    renderer.domElement.style.height = '100%';

    /* -- the two clocks ------------------------------------------------ */
    let rotation = STATIC_ROTATION; // ambient; frozen under reduced motion
    let burstTime = 1; // feedback; always runs. Starts at 1 so a start
    //                    time of 0 can mean 'never fired'.
    let nextFire = chordInterval;
    let liveUntil = 0;
    let cursor = 0;

    const fire = (group: number) => {
      const range = groupRanges[group % groupRanges.length];
      if (!range) return;
      for (let i = range.start; i < range.end; i += 1) starts[i] = burstTime;
      startAttribute.needsUpdate = true;
      liveUntil = burstTime + burstDuration + MAX_LAUNCH_DELAY + 0.05;
      setBurstLive(true);
    };

    const render = () => renderer.render(scene, camera);

    const step = (dt: number) => {
      burstTime += dt;

      if (!reducedRef.current) {
        rotation += dt * spinSpeed;
        if (burstTime >= nextFire) {
          fire(cursor);
          cursor += 1;
          nextFire = burstTime + chordInterval;
        }
      } else if (burstTime > liveUntil) {
        // Nothing in flight and no ambient motion to draw: stand the loop
        // down. Idempotent, so this is safe to call every frame.
        setBurstLive(false);
      }

      uniforms.uRotation.value = rotation;
      uniforms.uBurstTime.value = burstTime;
      render();
    };

    const resize = (w: number, h: number) => {
      renderer.setSize(w, h, false);
      camera.left = -w / 2;
      camera.right = w / 2;
      camera.top = h / 2;
      camera.bottom = -h / 2;
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
      uniforms.uViewScale.value = Math.min(w, h) * viewScale;
      uniforms.uPixelRatio.value = renderer.getPixelRatio();
      render();
    };

    /* -- pointer: user-initiated, so it fires under reduced motion too -- */
    const onPointerDown = (event: PointerEvent) => {
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      const x = event.clientX - rect.left - rect.width / 2;
      // Screen y grows downward, model y grows upward.
      const y = rect.height / 2 - (event.clientY - rect.top);
      // Undo the ambient rotation so the sector under the cursor is the one
      // that fires, not the one that was there before the ring turned.
      const angle = Math.atan2(y, x) - rotation;
      const normalised = ((angle % (Math.PI * 2)) + Math.PI * 2) % (Math.PI * 2);
      fire(Math.round(normalised / sector) % groups);
    };
    el.addEventListener('pointerdown', onPointerDown);

    resize(size.current.width, size.current.height);
    stage.current = { resize, step };

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      el.removeEventListener('pointerdown', onPointerDown);
      disposeObject(scene);
      material.dispose();
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      renderer.domElement.remove();
    };
  }, [
    ready,
    ringCount,
    ringDots,
    innerRadius,
    groups,
    burstDots,
    spinSpeed,
    chordInterval,
    burstDuration,
    burstRadius,
    dotScale,
    viewScale,
    opacity,
    color,
    burstColor,
    seed,
  ]);

  useEffect(() => {
    stage.current?.resize(width, height);
  }, [width, height]);

  useRaf((dt) => stage.current?.step(dt), ready && !unsupported && (!reduced || burstLive));
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes the pointerdown listener, nulls the stage ref so a queued frame cannot touch a dead renderer, disposes the geometry via `disposeObject(scene)`, disposes the material, calls `disposeRenderer` for `dispose` + `forceContextLoss` + a zeroed backing store, and removes the canvas. `useRaf` unsubscribes on unmount, so a StrictMode double-invoke leaves no orphaned context.

**Reduced motion.** The ambient rotation freezes at 0.35 rad and the automatic firing cycle stops, so nothing moves unprompted. A pointer press still fires a full burst, because that is feedback for something the user did rather than decoration. The frame loop is subscribed only while a burst is actually in flight and unsubscribes as soon as the last particle lands, so the idle cost is zero.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Freezing the burst along with the ambient rotation under reduced motion. The component then stops answering clicks, which is a broken interface, not an accessible one — feedback for a user action is not decoration, hence the two separate clocks.
- Leaving the frame loop running under reduced motion to keep the burst alive. It burns a GPU-backed rAF forever for a static image; subscribe only while a burst is in flight and stand down when it lands.
- Passing the control points as a uniform. It compiles, it animates, and every particle in the burst moves identically — the effect collapses into one expanding ring and the GPU solve buys nothing.
- Omitting the derivative guard in the Newton loop. Certain control points produce a near-zero derivative, `t` goes NaN, and the affected vertices vanish with no error anywhere — the symptom is a burst that is missing particles at some curves and not others.
- Displacing the resting ring dots instead of using dedicated burst particles. The ring develops a gap for the duration of the burst and snaps shut at the end.
- Baking the flight direction at fire time. The ring keeps rotating during the 0.45s flight, so the particles visibly drift off-radial and appear to curve away from their launch point.
- Sizing burst radius in model units. It then scales with the container, and the burst that felt right on a large canvas barely leaves the ring on a small preview card — pixels are the right unit for an effect this small.

## Notes

- One draw call and one buffer for the resting field and every burst particle. The only runtime upload is the start-time attribute, written once per firing rather than once per frame.
- Clicking maps the pointer angle back through the current rotation, so the sector under the cursor is the one that fires.
- The automatic cycle exists so the component reads as alive in a preview grid; drop `chordInterval` handling if the burst is wired to real user actions.

## Definition of done

Concentric rings of dots turn slowly. Roughly every 1.5 seconds one sector throws a spray of brighter particles outward that fade as they travel, and the particles visibly do not move in lockstep — some shoot ahead and settle, others trail. Clicking a sector fires it immediately. The ring never develops a gap where a burst came from. With reduced motion the ring is still and nothing fires on its own, but a click still produces a full burst.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: GSAP Cursor Follower

A container hides its native cursor and draws its own: a small disc that lags the pointer by a settling tween, and swells into a labelled puck whenever it passes over an element marked `data-cursor-target`. The lag comes from GSAP rather than from a damped rAF loop, which is why the disc comes to rest when the pointer stops instead of asymptoting toward it forever.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A puck that replaces the arrow inside a panel, trailing 0.4s behind and swelling to a label over targets.

- Category: cursor
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. On mount the puck is centred on its own coordinates with `gsap.set(circle, { xPercent: -50, yPercent: -50 })` and the positioning wrapper is parked at `x: -999, y: -999`. From then on the follow tween writes raw x/y and the centring composes into the same matrix, so there is no per-move offset arithmetic and exactly one composited transform per node.
2. Every `pointermove` issues `gsap.to(wrapper, { x: e.clientX - rect.left, y: e.clientY - rect.top, duration, ease: "power2.out", overwrite: "auto" })`. `overwrite: "auto"` retires the previous tween so the ~120 events a second do not accumulate into ~120 concurrent tweens writing the same transform.
3. This is deliberately GSAP smoothing rather than `useSmoothPointer`. A tween re-eases from its current velocity to a *rest* at the target, so the puck decelerates into stillness the instant the pointer stops; an exponential `damp` never actually arrives. Reach for the damped hook when you want a value that is permanently chasing, and for this when you want it to settle.
4. `pointerenter` teleports first (`duration: 0`) and only then fades in, so re-entering the panel does not drag a visible streak across it from wherever the puck was last parked.
5. The hover state is delegated: one handler runs `e.target.closest("[data-cursor-target]")` per move and compares the result with the previous state, tweening `scale` on the disc and `autoAlpha`/`scale` on the label only on the transition. Scale — not width/height — keeps the resize on the compositor with no layout pass.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `PARK = -999`
  Initial x/y. The element exists from first paint but must be *nowhere*; at 0,0 it flashes in the top-left corner for the frames between mount and the first pointer event.
- `duration = 0.4`
  Seconds of catch-up. Below ~0.2 the puck is welded to the pointer and the trailing read disappears; past ~0.7 it feels detached from the hand and users start chasing it.
- `size = 16`
  Resting diameter. Small enough to point precisely with, large enough to see against a busy panel. Applied as `scale: size / targetSize` so only the transform changes.
- `targetSize = 112`
  Diameter over a target. It has to hold a short label at 14px with real breathing room — under ~90 the text touches the circle edge and the puck reads as a broken badge.
- `RESIZE_DURATION = 0.45`
  The swell. With `expo.out` this is almost all its motion in the first 120ms, which is what makes the state change feel like a snap rather than an inflation.
- `FADE_DURATION = 0.3`
  Enter/leave opacity. Fast enough that the puck is present before the user has moved a meaningful distance into the panel.

## API

```ts
function CursorFollower(props: { children: ReactNode; label?: string; duration?: number; size?: number; targetSize?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Panel content. Anything inside carrying `data-cursor-target` triggers the labelled state.
- `label: string` — default `'View'`
  Text revealed inside the puck over a target.
- `duration: number` — default `0.4`
  Seconds of catch-up on the follow tween.
- `size: number` — default `16`
  Resting diameter in px.
- `targetSize: number` — default `112`
  Diameter over a target, in px. Also the disc's laid-out size.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root container via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Far outside any container, so the puck is nowhere until a pointer exists. */
const PARK = -999;
const FADE_DURATION = 0.3;
const RESIZE_DURATION = 0.45;

export function CursorFollower({
  children,
  label = 'View',
  duration = 0.4,
  size = 16,
  targetSize = 112,
  className,
}: CursorFollowerProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const wrap = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const disc = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const text = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = root.current;
    const point = wrap.current;
    const circle = disc.current;
    const caption = text.current;
    if (!el || !point || !circle || !caption) return;

    // A coarse pointer has no hover state, so the puck could only ever exist
    // between pointerdown and pointerup — and `cursor: none` on a touch device
    // hides nothing while still suppressing the text-selection caret.
    if (!window.matchMedia('(pointer: fine)').matches) return;

    const reduced = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
    const follow = reduced ? 0 : duration;
    const fade = reduced ? 0 : FADE_DURATION;
    const resize = reduced ? 0 : RESIZE_DURATION;

    // Centre both layers on their own coordinates once. After this the follow
    // tween writes raw x/y and the centring composes into the same matrix —
    // no offset arithmetic per move, and one composited transform per node.
    gsap.set(point, { x: PARK, y: PARK, autoAlpha: 0 });
    gsap.set(circle, { xPercent: -50, yPercent: -50, scale: size / targetSize });
    gsap.set(caption, { xPercent: -50, yPercent: -50, autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.5 });

    // The puck *replaces* the arrow rather than accompanying it. Set from JS,
    // not from the class list, so a touch device never loses its cursor.
    const previousCursor = el.style.cursor;
    el.style.cursor = 'none';

    let overTarget = false;

    const place = (e: PointerEvent, instant: boolean) => {
      // Live rect: the container can scroll, resize, or be inside a
      // transformed ancestor. A rect cached on mount puts the puck at a
      // constant offset from the real pointer as soon as anything moves.
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      gsap.to(point, {
        x: e.clientX - rect.left,
        y: e.clientY - rect.top,
        duration: instant ? 0 : follow,
        ease: 'power2.out',
        // Each move REPLACES the last tween instead of queueing behind it.
        // Without it, ~120 events a second means ~120 live 0.4s tweens all
        // writing the same transform, and the puck visibly stutters.
        overwrite: 'auto',
      });
    };

    const onEnter = (e: PointerEvent) => {
      // Teleport on entry, then fade in. Tweening from wherever the puck was
      // parked draws a visible streak diagonally across the panel every time
      // the pointer re-enters.
      place(e, true);
      gsap.to(point, { autoAlpha: 1, duration: fade, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto' });
    };

    const onMove = (e: PointerEvent) => {
      place(e, false);

      const hit =
        e.target instanceof Element ? e.target.closest('[data-cursor-target]') : null;
      const next = hit !== null;
      // Only tween on the transition. Re-firing the same resize tween on every
      // move restarts its ease and the puck never reaches the target size.
      if (next === overTarget) return;
      overTarget = next;

      gsap.to(circle, {
        scale: next ? 1 : size / targetSize,
        duration: resize,
        ease: 'expo.out',
        overwrite: 'auto',
      });
      gsap.to(caption, {
        autoAlpha: next ? 1 : 0,
        scale: next ? 1 : 0.5,
        duration: resize,
        ease: 'expo.out',
        overwrite: 'auto',
      });
    };

    const onLeave = () => {
      gsap.to(point, { autoAlpha: 0, duration: fade, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto' });
    };

    el.addEventListener('pointerenter', onEnter);
    el.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove, { passive: true });
    el.addEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);

    return () => {
      el.removeEventListener('pointerenter', onEnter);
      el.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
      el.removeEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);
      el.style.cursor = previousCursor;
      // Kill before clearing, or an in-flight tween writes the transform
      // straight back onto a node React has already recycled.
      gsap.killTweensOf([point, circle, caption]);
      gsap.set([point, circle, caption], { clearProps: 'all' });
    };
  }, [duration, size, targetSize]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes the three container listeners, restores the container's previous inline `cursor`, calls `gsap.killTweensOf` on the wrapper, disc and label, then `gsap.set(..., { clearProps: "all" })`. Kill precedes clear so no in-flight tween can write the transform back after React has recycled the node.

**Reduced motion.** The puck still appears and still swells over targets — the affordance is preserved — but every duration collapses to 0, so it is welded to the pointer with no trailing lag and the size change is a hard cut. The native cursor stays hidden, because a container with no cursor at all would be worse than one that moves.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Calling `gsap.to` per pointermove without `overwrite: "auto"`. Sixty to a hundred and twenty 0.4s tweens end up live at once, all writing the same transform, and the puck stutters instead of gliding — the single most common way this effect is got wrong.
- Fading in without teleporting first. On every re-entry the puck tweens from its parked coordinates, drawing a diagonal streak across the whole panel before it reaches the pointer.
- Re-issuing the resize tween on every move instead of only on the hover transition. Each call restarts the `expo.out` ease from the beginning, so the puck creeps toward the target size and never gets there while the pointer keeps moving.
- Transitioning `width` and `height` for the swell. That is a layout write per frame on an element the compositor could otherwise leave alone; `scale` on a fixed-size disc is the same picture for free.
- Caching the container rect on mount. The panel scrolls, resizes, and may sit inside a transformed ancestor — a stale rect offsets the puck from the real pointer by a constant amount that never corrects itself.
- Putting `cursor: none` in the class list. It then applies on touch devices too, where it hides nothing but does suppress the text-selection caret; setting it from the effect means it only ever exists where the puck does.

## Notes

- Gated on `(pointer: fine)`. On touch nothing attaches: no listeners, no `cursor: none`, and the puck stays at `autoAlpha: 0` parked off-container, so a tap does not flash a disc at the touch point.
- Mark any element inside with `data-cursor-target` to trigger the labelled state — including elements nested arbitrarily deep, since the check is a `closest()` walk.
- The root sets `isolate`, so the puck stacks above the panel content without needing a page-level z-index.

## Definition of done

Move into the panel: the arrow disappears and a small disc arrives at the pointer without sweeping in from an edge, then trails about 0.4s behind as you move. Pass over a marked target and it swells into a labelled puck; leave and it shrinks back. Stop moving and it comes fully to rest rather than creeping. On a touch device the native cursor and all default behaviour are untouched.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Heatmap Chart Card

A grey dashboard card that lays out any two-axis data, such as weekday by hour or region by month, as a CSS grid of rounded cells. Each cell's colour is the accent mixed into the chart track by its share of the maximum, so the ramp follows the theme in light and dark. Hovering a cell, or moving to it with the arrow keys, rings it, darkens its row and column labels, floats a small tooltip and swaps the count-up headline to that cell with its gap to the average. A period pill switches between datasets and the cells pop in again on every switch.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A two-axis heatmap card on a plain CSS grid: cells mix the accent into the chart track, and hovering one rings it and swaps the headline.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Resolve the data: `ranges` wins, then `rows`; with neither, the card runs on `HEATMAP_RANGES`, three built-in weekday by two-hour datasets. Those come from a working-hours bell plus an evening bump, a weekday weight and a seeded `createRng` wobble, scaled so the cells sum to an exact total (1,892 for the last 7 days). The rounding residue goes onto the busiest cell.
2. One `useMemo` derives the total, the mean cell and the ceiling, which is `max` (prop or range) or else the largest value. A cell at value v paints `color-mix(in oklab, <accent> s%, var(--color-chart-track))` with `s = 10 + 90 * min(1, v / ceiling)`. The legend draws the same mix at 0.15, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1.
3. The grid is one CSS grid with `grid-template-columns: max-content repeat(n, minmax(0, 1fr))` and a 4px gap: a label column, then one track per column, and a last row of column labels. Row height is `floor((168 - (rows - 1) * 4) / rows)` clamped to 18–40px, which gives 20px cells for 7 rows and 39px cells for 4. The section is a size container, and when it is under 24rem with more than 8 columns, every other column label is hidden so the labels never touch.
4. Each cell has `.animate-cell-pop` (fade and scale from 0.5) with a delay of `c * 24 + r * 16` ms, so the grid fills in a diagonal sweep. The grid is keyed by the active range id, so a period switch remounts it and the sweep plays again.
5. Hovering a cell sets `active`. The cell gets a 2px `outline` in `--color-text-primary`, offset 1px and lifted with `z-10`, and its row and column labels turn from tertiary to primary text. A tooltip inside the cell shows the cell name and value, anchored left on the first two columns, right on the last two and centred elsewhere.
6. The header swaps `title` for the cell name ("Tue · 14:00" for the built-in data) and the total for the cell value through `useCountUp`. The value sits in a `<p>` keyed by the cell so `.animate-number-fade` replays. The chip changes from the period change to the cell's percent gap to the mean, with a "vs avg" suffix.
7. The grid is one tab stop (`role="group"`, `aria-roledescription="heatmap"`). Arrow keys move the active cell in two dimensions, Home and End jump to the row ends, and Escape, blur or leaving the grid with the pointer clears it. The header is an `aria-live="polite"` region, so the new cell is announced.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `MIX_FLOOR = 10%`
  A zero cell keeps a trace of the accent, so it still reads as part of the grid rather than as a hole in the card.
- `PLOT_HEIGHT / row clamp = 168px shared, rows 18–40px`
  Cards with 4 or 7 rows end up about the same height, so a dashboard row of heatmaps lines up without fixing the row count.
- `cell delay = c × 24ms + r × 16ms`
  The sweep runs left to right first, the way the eye reads time, and the whole 7 × 12 grid lands in about 700ms including the 380ms pop.
- `LEGEND_STEPS = 0.15, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1`
  Five evenly readable swatches. The first step is above the floor so the "Less" swatch is still visibly tinted.

## API

```ts
function HeatmapChartCard(props?: HeatmapChartCardProps): JSX.Element
type HeatmapRow = { label: string; values: number[] }
type HeatmapRange = { id: string; label: string; rows: HeatmapRow[]; columns?: string[]; max?: number; change?: number; headline?: number }
const HEATMAP_RANGES: HeatmapRange[]
const HEATMAP_HOURS: string[]
```

- `title: string` — default `"Active users"`
  Header label while no cell is active.
- `rows: HeatmapRow[]`
  One entry per row; `values` line up with `columns`. Ignored when `ranges` is passed.
- `columns: string[]` — default `HEATMAP_HOURS for the built-in data, else "1"…"n"`
  Column labels under the grid.
- `color: string` — default `"var(--color-chart-6)"`
  Ramp accent; any CSS colour.
- `max: number` — default `largest value`
  Value of a fully saturated cell.
- `change: number`
  Percent change for the chip when `ranges` is not used.
- `headline: number` — default `sum of all cells`
  Headline figure when `ranges` is not used.
- `periodLabel: string` — default `"This week"`
  Text of the static pill when no ranges are in play. An empty string hides it.
- `ranges: HeatmapRange[]` — default `HEATMAP_RANGES when no rows are passed`
  Periods for the dropdown pill; each brings its own rows.
- `range: string`
  Controlled active range id.
- `defaultRange: string` — default `first range`
  Uncontrolled starting range id.
- `onRangeChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called with the id picked from the period menu.
- `format: (value: number) => string` — default `rounded en-US number`
  Formats the headline and tooltip values.
- `cellLabel: (row: string, column: string) => string` — default `"Row · Column"`
  Names a cell in the header and tooltip.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

## Reference implementation of the core

```tsx
const model = useMemo(() => {
  const all = rows.flatMap((r) => r.values.slice(0, columns.length));
  const total = all.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  const largest = Math.max(0, ...all);
  const ceiling = maxProp ?? activeRange?.max ?? largest;
  return { total, mean: all.length ? total / all.length : 0, ceiling: ceiling > 0 ? ceiling : 1, largest };
}, [rows, columns.length, maxProp, activeRange]);

// Each cell mixes the accent into the chart track, so the ramp follows the theme.
const mix = (t: number) => {
  const share = MIX_FLOOR + (100 - MIX_FLOOR) * Math.min(1, Math.max(0, t));
  return `color-mix(in oklab, ${color} ${Math.round(share)}%, var(--color-chart-track))`;
};
const rowHeight = Math.max(
  ROW_HEIGHT[0],
  Math.min(ROW_HEIGHT[1], Math.floor((PLOT_HEIGHT - (rows.length - 1) * GAP) / Math.max(1, rows.length))),
);

const activeValue = active ? rows[active.r]?.values[active.c] : undefined;
const isActive = active !== null && activeValue !== undefined;
const headlineValue = isActive ? activeValue : (activeRange?.headline ?? headlineProp ?? model.total);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `useCountUp` cancels its animation frame when the target changes and on unmount. The dropdown removes its outside-press listener when it closes. Everything else is CSS and React event props, so nothing else needs tearing down.

**Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the cells appear at once (`motion-reduce:animate-none` on `.animate-cell-pop`, and no delays), the headline shows its value with no count-up and no fade, and the label colour and chevron changes are instant.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Building the ramp from opacity. A translucent accent over the grey card looks right in light mode but turns muddy in dark mode. Mixing into `--color-chart-track` gives an opaque colour that follows each theme.
- Leaving the hovered cell at the default stacking order. Every cell has a transform from the pop animation and so its own stacking context, and later cells would paint over an earlier cell's tooltip. The active cell gets `z-10`.
- Normalising each range by its own largest value when comparing periods. Pin `max` (prop or per range) when the colours have to mean the same thing across ranges.

## Notes

- `HEATMAP_RANGES` and `HEATMAP_HOURS` are exported, as are the `HeatmapRow` and `HeatmapRange` types. A range can carry its own `columns`, `max`, `change` and `headline`.
- Pass `cellLabel` to name cells differently in the header and tooltip, for example `(row, col) => `${col} ${row}``.

## Definition of done

The default card reads "Active users", "1,892" and a lime "+5.2%" chip with a "Last 7 days" pill. Below is a 7 × 12 blue grid, Mon–Sun by 00–22, darkest around midday on weekdays and lighter at night and on weekends, with a Less → More legend. Hovering a cell rings it, darkens its row and column labels, shows a tooltip and changes the header to "Tue · 14:00" style text with that cell's value and a "vs avg" chip. Picking "Last 30 days" pops the cells in again and shows "8,214". The emerald region card reads "963" and switches to H2 columns Jul–Dec.
