# Build: Meeting Scheduler

A compact "Schedule a meeting" button that opens a three-column booking panel: who you are meeting and what about on the left, a single-month calendar in the middle, and a timezone label, 12h / 24h switch and scrolling half-hour slots on the right. Choices are a draft until "Send meeting", which stays disabled until both a day and a time are picked, then commits and closes. The trigger is a plain button driving a controlled React Aria `Popover`, so the wide panel floats above the page and never pushes layout.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A Cal.com-style booking popover: host and meeting summary, a month calendar and a half-hour slot list, committed by "Send meeting".

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1, @internationalized/date@^3.12.4, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The trigger is a native `<button>` with the shared date-picker trigger styling and a chevron that rotates 180 degrees over 200ms while open. It toggles `isOpen` and, on opening, copies the committed value into `pendingValue`, so a draft abandoned last time never resurfaces.
2. The panel is a React Aria `Popover` wired with `triggerRef`, `isOpen` / `onOpenChange`, `placement="bottom end"`, `offset={8}` and `isNonModal`, so the page behind stays interactive. Non-modal popovers lose React Aria's outside-click dismissal, so `useDismissOnOutsidePress` adds a document `pointerdown` listener that closes it unless the press lands in the trigger or the panel.
3. Inside a `Dialog`, a React Aria `Calendar` bound to `pendingValue.date` wraps the whole 429px-tall row, so the shared `MonthPanel` (`offset={0}` with both arrows) renders the grid and day cells. Picking a day keeps any time already chosen; picking a slot keeps the day (falling back to today).
4. The left column (207px) shows the host avatar initial, name and email, the meeting title and description, then duration, language and conferencing rows pinned to the bottom. Under the calendar a chip shows the pending date and time ("Select a time" until one is picked) beside the "Send meeting" button.
5. The right column (170px) holds the timezone label, a weekday + day chip, a 12h / 24h switch (24h by default) and the slots: 09:00 to 18:30 every 30 minutes, generated once and shown as "2:30 PM" in 12h mode. The list scrolls inside a mask that fades the top 16px, and the chosen slot gets the tertiary background.
6. "Send meeting" calls `commit(pendingValue)`: uncontrolled, it stores the value internally; either way it calls `onChange({ date, time })` with `time` as 24-hour "HH:mm", and closes the popover.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `panel columns = 207px summary, 326px MonthPanel, 170px slots, gap-4, h-[429px]`
  From the Figma "Meeting" frame (node 3881:7618). A fixed height lets the slot column scroll while the summary and calendar stay put.
- `slots = 09:00 to 18:30, every 30 minutes (20 slots)`
  Replaces Figma's static mock (which repeated 14:00) with a generated working-day range.
- `popover = placement bottom end, offset 8, isNonModal`
  Right-aligned to the trigger so it can sit at the end of a toolbar; non-modal so the page stays scrollable and clickable while the panel is open.
- `slot mask = linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent, black 16px, black 100%)`
  Slots scrolled under the 24h toggle fade out instead of being cut off at a hard edge.
- `defaultOpen threshold = (min-width: 640px), applied after mount`
  If the ~735px panel is in the first paint, mobile Safari sizes its layout viewport to it and the page stays zoomed out after it closes.

## API

```ts
function MeetingScheduler(props: { host?: { name: string; email: string; avatarInitial: string }; meeting?: { title: string; description?: string; durationMinutes: number; language?: string; conferencing?: string }; timezone?: string; value?: MeetingSchedulerValue | null; defaultValue?: MeetingSchedulerValue | null; onChange?: (value: MeetingSchedulerValue | null) => void; defaultOpen?: boolean; className?: string; "aria-label"?: string; triggerLabel?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `value / defaultValue: { date: CalendarDate; time: string | null } | null`
  Controlled or initial booking. Without either, the draft starts on today with no time.
- `onChange: (value: MeetingSchedulerValue | null) => void`
  Fires once, when "Send meeting" is pressed.
- `host: MeetingSchedulerHost` — default `Jordan Lee`
  Name, email and avatar initial in the summary column.
- `meeting: MeetingSchedulerDetails` — default `30 min intro meeting`
  Title, description, duration, language and conferencing rows.
- `timezone: string` — default `"Amsterdam"`
  Label in the slot column header.
- `triggerLabel: string` — default `"Schedule a meeting"`
  Text on the trigger button.
- `defaultOpen: boolean` — default `false`
  Opens after mount on viewports 640px and wider.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Schedule meeting"`
  Names the dialog and the calendar grid.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function MeetingScheduler({
  host = DEFAULT_HOST,
  meeting = DEFAULT_MEETING,
  timezone = "Amsterdam",
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onChange,
  defaultOpen = false,
  className,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel = "Schedule meeting",
  triggerLabel = "Schedule a meeting",
}: MeetingSchedulerProps) {
  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const popoverRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
  const timeSlots = useTimeSlots();
  const isControlled = value !== undefined;
  const [internalValue, setInternalValue] = useState<MeetingSchedulerValue | null>(
    defaultValue ?? { date: today(getLocalTimeZone()), time: null },
  );
  const committedValue = isControlled ? value : internalValue;

  const [pendingValue, setPendingValue] = useState<MeetingSchedulerValue | null>(committedValue);
  const [use24h, setUse24h] = useState(true);
  // Never honor `defaultOpen` on the initial render: the ~700px-wide panel
  // being in the very first paint makes mobile Safari compute its layout
  // viewport from that width, permanently zooming the whole page out even
  // after the panel closes. Open it post-mount instead, and only on
  // viewports wide enough to show the panel without overflowing.
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!defaultOpen) return;
    if (window.matchMedia("(min-width: 640px)").matches) {
      setIsOpen(true);
    }
  }, [defaultOpen]);

  const commit = (next: MeetingSchedulerValue | null) => {
    if (!isControlled) setInternalValue(next);
    onChange?.(next);
    setIsOpen(false);
  };

  useDismissOnOutsidePress(isOpen, () => setIsOpen(false), [triggerRef, popoverRef]);

  const chip = pendingValue ? formatChipDateTime(pendingValue) : null;
  const dayChip = pendingValue
    ? {
        weekday: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { weekday: "short" }).format(pendingValue.date.toDate(getLocalTimeZone())).slice(0, 2),
        day: pendingValue.date.day,
      }
    : null;

  return (
    <>
      <button
        ref={triggerRef}
        type="button"
        onClick={() => {
          if (!isOpen) setPendingValue(committedValue);
          setIsOpen((open) => !open);
        }}
        className={cx(triggerButtonClassName, className)}
      >
        <RiCalendarLine className="size-5 shrink-0 text-foreground-icon-primary" aria-hidden />
        <span className="flex items-center justify-center whitespace-nowrap px-1 text-body-medium text-text-primary">
          {triggerLabel}
        </span>
        <ChevronDownSmall
          className={cx("size-4 shrink-0 text-text-secondary transition-transform duration-200 ease", isOpen && "rotate-180")}
        />
      </button>
      <Popover
        ref={popoverRef}
        triggerRef={triggerRef}
        isOpen={isOpen}
        onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
        placement="bottom end"
        offset={8}
        isNonModal
        className={popoverClassName}
      >
        <Dialog aria-label={ariaLabel} className="outline-none">
          <Calendar
            aria-label={ariaLabel}
            value={pendingValue?.date ?? null}
            onChange={(date) => setPendingValue((prev) => ({ date, time: prev?.time ?? null }))}
          >
            <div className="flex h-[429px] gap-4">
              {/* Host + meeting summary */}
              <div className="flex w-[207px] shrink-0 flex-col gap-4 py-4 ps-4">
                <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-2">
                  <Avatar size="md" color="blue" initials={host.avatarInitial} />
                  <div className="flex flex-col text-body-medium">
                    <span className="text-text-primary">{host.name}</span>
                    <span className="text-text-secondary">{host.email}</span>
                  </div>
                </div>
                <div className="flex flex-col gap-1">
                  <p className="text-title-3-medium text-text-primary">{meeting.title}</p>
                  {meeting.description && (
                    <p className="text-body-2-medium text-text-secondary">{meeting.description}</p>
                  )}
                </div>
                <div className="mt-auto flex flex-col gap-3">
                  <InfoRow icon={<GlyphIcon icon={RiGlobalLine} />}>{meeting.durationMinutes} minutes</InfoRow>
                  {meeting.language && <InfoRow icon={<GlyphIcon icon={RiFlagLine} />}>{meeting.language}</InfoRow>}
                  {meeting.conferencing && <InfoRow icon={<GoogleMeetIcon />}>{meeting.conferencing}</InfoRow>}
                </div>
              </div>

              {/* Calendar + footer */}
              <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 pt-2 pb-3">
                <MonthPanel offset={0} showPrev showNext />
                <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
                  <span className="flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-2lg border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default px-2 py-2 text-body-medium text-text-primary shadow-xs">
                    {chip && (
                      <>
                        <span>{chip.date}</span>
                        <span className="text-text-secondary">{chip.time}</span>
                      </>
                    )}
                  </span>
                  <Button onClick={() => commit(pendingValue)} disabled={!pendingValue?.time}>
                    Send meeting
                  </Button>
                </div>
              </div>

              {/* Timezone + hour format + time slots */}
              <div className="flex h-full w-[170px] shrink-0 flex-col gap-3 overflow-hidden pt-4 pe-4">
                <button
                  type="button"
                  className="flex cursor-pointer items-center justify-between rounded-2lg outline-none"
                >
                  <span className="flex items-center gap-[5px] text-body-medium text-text-primary">
                    <RiGlobalLine className="size-5 shrink-0 text-foreground-icon-primary" aria-hidden />
                    {timezone}
                  </span>
                  <ChevronDownSmall className="size-4 shrink-0 text-text-secondary" />
                </button>

                <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
                  {dayChip && (
                    <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-[3px] rounded-2lg bg-background-tertiary-default px-2 py-1 text-body-medium">
                      <span className="text-text-primary">{dayChip.weekday}</span>
                      <span className="text-text-secondary">{dayChip.day}</span>
                    </span>
                  )}
                  <HourFormatToggle use24h={use24h} onChange={setUse24h} />
                </div>

                <div
                  className="flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-2 overflow-y-auto pb-3"
                  style={{
                    maskImage: "linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent, black 16px, black 100%)",
                    WebkitMaskImage: "linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent, black 16px, black 100%)",
                  }}
                >
                  {timeSlots.map((slot) => (
                    <button
                      key={slot}
                      type="button"
                      onClick={() =>
                        setPendingValue((prev) => ({ date: prev?.date ?? today(getLocalTimeZone()), time: slot }))
                      }
                      className={cx(
                        "w-full shrink-0 cursor-pointer rounded-2lg px-2 py-1.5 text-center text-body-medium text-text-primary transition-colors duration-150 ease",
                        pendingValue?.time === slot
                          ? "bg-background-tertiary-default"
                          : "hover:bg-background-secondary-hover",
                      )}
                    >
                      {formatTime(slot, use24h)}
                    </button>
                  ))}
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
          </Calendar>
        </Dialog>
      </Popover>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The outside-press hook removes its document listener when the panel closes or the component unmounts, and React Aria tears down the popover's positioning and focus handling on close. No timers.

**Reduced motion.** The component does not branch on `prefers-reduced-motion`. The motion is the shared popover entrance (150ms opacity, scale and blur), the 200ms chevron turn and 150ms colour fades on slots and the hour toggle, all brief and none needed to understand the state.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not open the panel during the first render. `defaultOpen` is applied in an effect and only on viewports of 640px or wider; rendering a ~735px overlay in the first paint zooms mobile Safari out permanently.
- Do not commit on every click. Date and slot edits go to `pendingValue`; only "Send meeting" calls `onChange`, so closing the panel discards the draft.
- Do not leave `isNonModal` without the outside-press hook. React Aria skips light dismiss for non-modal popovers, so clicking the page would leave the panel stuck open.
- Do not rely on the uncontrolled default in server-rendered pages. With no `value` or `defaultValue` it seeds today's date, which can differ between server and client around midnight; pass a value.

## Notes

- The value is `{ date: CalendarDate; time: string | null }`; `time` is always 24-hour "HH:mm" regardless of the 12h / 24h display.
- The timezone row is a label with a chevron, not a working selector; wire your own picker there if you need one.
- The trigger keeps `triggerLabel` ("Schedule a meeting") after booking; show the booked time elsewhere, as the demo does.
- BoardUI ships a Google Meet bitmap for conferencing; this port uses a Remix video icon.

## Definition of done

A "Schedule a meeting" button with a calendar icon and chevron. Clicking it opens a panel below, right-aligned, with the host card and meeting rows, a month calendar and a slot column from 09:00 to 18:30; "Send meeting" is disabled. Picking a day updates the chip and the weekday badge, picking a slot highlights it and fills the chip, and "Send meeting" becomes enabled. Toggling 12h shows "9:00 AM" style labels. Pressing "Send meeting" closes the panel and calls `onChange` with the date and the 24-hour time; clicking outside instead closes it without calling `onChange`.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Meter

A labelled rail that shows a quantity within a known range: storage used, seats taken, API quota. It is React Aria's `Meter`, so it is announced as `role="meter"` (a level, not a task heading towards done), and it is drawn on Progress's `ProgressTrack`, sharing the same rail and eased translate fill. A `tone` recolours the fill from semantic tokens so a meter can turn amber or red as it nears its limit.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A level within a known range (storage, seats, quotas) with accent, success, warning and error tones, on React Aria Meter.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Map `tone` to a text-colour class in a `sortCx` map: `accent` → `text-accent-500`, `success` → `text-notification-success-foreground`, `warning` → `text-chart-8-active`, `error` → `text-notification-error-foreground`. The fill paints in `currentColor`, so a text class is all it takes.
2. Render `AriaMeter` with every React Aria prop passed through (`value`, `minValue`, `maxValue`, `valueLabel`, `formatOptions`) and `flex w-full flex-col gap-1.5` on the root.
3. Use the render props `{ percentage, valueText }`. When there is a label or the value is shown, render a `flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3` row: the kit `Label` (truncated) and `valueText` in `text-body-medium text-text-secondary tabular-nums`. `showValueLabel` defaults to `label != null`.
4. Render `<ProgressTrack percentage={percentage} size={size} className={tones[tone]} />`: a `bg-border-button-default` rail 4 / 6 / 8px tall whose full-width fill is shifted by `translate` and eases over 500ms on `cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)` when the value changes.
5. Render the optional `description` underneath in `text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `tone tokens = accent-500; success lime-600 (dark lime-300); warning yellow-500 (chart-8-active); error rose-600 (dark rose-300)`
  Semantic tokens rather than palette classes, so the fill keeps its contrast on dark cards, where success and error lighten to the 300 step.
- `track = h-1 / h-1.5 / h-2 (4 / 6 / 8px), default md`
  Shared with ProgressBar so a meter and a progress bar stacked on one card are identical rails.
- `fill easing = 500ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) on translate`
  Inherited from ProgressTrack: a value change eases in on the compositor instead of animating width.

## API

```ts
type MeterTone = "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "error"
interface MeterProps extends Omit<AriaMeterProps, "children" | "className"> { label?: ReactNode; showValueLabel?: boolean; description?: ReactNode; tone?: MeterTone; size?: ProgressSize; className?: string }
function Meter(props: MeterProps): JSX.Element
```

- `value: number` — default `0`
  Current level (React Aria).
- `minValue / maxValue: number` — default `0 / 100`
  The range the value sits in (React Aria).
- `valueLabel: ReactNode`
  Custom value text instead of the formatted percentage (React Aria).
- `label: ReactNode`
  Label above the rail; also turns the value label on by default.
- `showValueLabel: boolean`
  Show the value at the end of the label row. Defaults to `label != null`.
- `description: ReactNode`
  Helper text under the rail.
- `tone: "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "error"` — default `"accent"`
  Colour of the fill.
- `size: "sm" | "md" | "lg"` — default `"md"`
  4, 6 or 8px rail.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const tones = sortCx({
  accent: "text-accent-500",
  success: "text-notification-success-foreground",
  warning: "text-chart-8-active",
  error: "text-notification-error-foreground",
});

export interface MeterProps extends Omit<AriaMeterProps, "children" | "className"> {
  label?: ReactNode;
  /** Show the formatted value at the end of the label row. Default: shown with a label. */
  showValueLabel?: boolean;
  /** Helper text under the bar. */
  description?: ReactNode;
  /** Colour of the fill. Default `accent`. */
  tone?: MeterTone;
  /** Track thickness: 4, 6 (default), or 8px. */
  size?: ProgressSize;
  className?: string;
}

export function Meter({
  label,
  showValueLabel,
  description,
  tone = "accent",
  size = "md",
  className,
  ...props
}: MeterProps) {
  const showValue = showValueLabel ?? label != null;
  return (
    <AriaMeter {...props} className={cx("flex w-full flex-col gap-1.5", className)}>
      {({ percentage, valueText }) => (
        <>
          {label != null || showValue ? (
            <div className="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3">
              {label != null ? <Label className="min-w-0 truncate">{label}</Label> : <span />}
              {showValue ? (
                <span className="shrink-0 text-body-medium text-text-secondary tabular-nums">{valueText}</span>
              ) : null}
            </div>
          ) : null}
          <ProgressTrack percentage={percentage} size={size} className={tones[tone]} />
          {description ? <span className="text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary">{description}</span> : null}
        </>
      )}
    </AriaMeter>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component is stateless apart from React Aria's render props; there are no listeners or timers.

**Reduced motion.** The fill's 500ms translate transition is removed by ProgressTrack's `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so a new value appears immediately.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not use a Meter for a task in progress (an upload, an import). That is a ProgressBar; Meter is announced as a level and has no indeterminate state.
- Do not pass a raw count without `maxValue`. React Aria assumes 0..100, so `value={19}` for 19 of 20 seats renders as 19% full.
- Do not encode the status only in the tone colour. Put the number or a description next to it ("1 seat left").
- Do not recolour the fill with `bg-*` classes. The fill is `bg-current`; set a text colour (or `tone`) instead.

## Notes

- `valueLabel` (React Aria) replaces the formatted percentage with custom text, e.g. "7.2 of 10 GB".
- Tone thresholds are the caller's decision; the component never switches tone by itself.

## Definition of done

`<Meter label="Seats" value={19} maxValue={20} tone="warning" />` renders "Seats" with "95%" on the right and a 6px rail filled 95% in amber, exposed as `role="meter"` with aria-valuenow 19. `valueLabel="7.2 of 10 GB"` replaces the percentage text. Changing the value eases the fill to its new length over half a second, and the error tone fill is rose in light mode and a lighter rose in dark mode.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Mixed Scrub Depth Layers

Elements marked with a depth index get two things from that index: how far they travel, and how much they lag. The travel is ordinary parallax; the lag — a different `scrub` value per depth — is what keeps the planes visibly apart while the eye is moving and lets them converge at rest. Works on a vertical page and, given a horizontal strip's tween, along that strip instead.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Layers separate while you scroll and converge when you stop, because each depth has its own scrub.

- Category: scroll
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. Each `[data-depth]` element is read once: `depth = clamp(parseInt(dataset.depth), 0, ladder.length - 1)`, so bad or missing markup lands on the nearest plane rather than throwing.
2. Distance comes from the normalised depth: `amount = (depth / (ladder.length - 1)) * travel`, tweened `fromTo(-amount → +amount)` in `yPercent` so it is relative to the element's own height and survives any layout.
3. Lag comes from the ladder: `scrub = ladder[depth]`, giving 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 seconds of catch-up across four planes. Depth 0 uses `scrub: true` rather than `scrub: 0`, because ScrollTrigger reads 0 as falsy and would drop scrubbing entirely.
4. The trigger window is the element's full crossing — `top bottom` to `bottom top` — so nothing is ever caught mid-tween on load and every layer is at a defined offset for any scroll position.
5. Passing a `containerAnimation` swaps the position keywords to `left right` / `right left`, so the same ladder drives layers riding a pinned horizontal strip.
6. The ladder array is serialised to a string for the effect dependency list, so a caller passing a fresh literal every render does not rebuild every trigger every render.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `DEFAULT_LADDER = [0, 0.25, 0.5, 1]`
  Seconds of catch-up per plane. Four values is the most the eye separates reliably; a fifth reads as the same distance as the fourth. Doubling at each step keeps the ratio between adjacent planes constant, which is what makes them read as evenly spaced.
- `travel = 26`
  yPercent at the deepest plane, so a tile moves just over a quarter of its own height across the whole crossing. Past ~40 the tiles visibly leave their grid cells and the layout looks broken; below ~10 the parallax is invisible once the lag is doing the work.
- `scrub for depth 0 = true`
  ScrollTrigger treats `scrub: 0` as falsy and turns scrubbing off, which makes the nearest plane a toggle animation instead of a locked one. `true` is the documented spelling of "no catch-up".
- `trigger window = 'top bottom' → 'bottom top'`
  The element's entire crossing of the scroller. A shorter window leaves the layer frozen at a partial offset above and below it, which shows up as a jump the first time it enters.

## API

```ts
function MixedScrubLayers(props: { children: ReactNode; scroller?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; containerAnimation?: gsap.core.Animation | null; ladder?: number[]; travel?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Markup containing `[data-depth]` elements; 0 is nearest.
- `scroller: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>`
  Scroll container the triggers read. Omit for the document.
- `containerAnimation: gsap.core.Animation | null`
  A horizontal strip tween to measure along. `null` defers until it exists.
- `ladder: number[]` — default `[0, 0.25, 0.5, 1]`
  Seconds of catch-up per depth index. Length defines how many planes exist.
- `travel: number` — default `26`
  yPercent travel at the deepest plane.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the wrapper.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function MixedScrubLayers({
  children,
  scroller,
  containerAnimation,
  ladder = DEFAULT_LADDER,
  travel = 26,
  className,
}: MixedScrubLayersProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  // Serialised so a fresh array literal from the caller does not rebuild
  // every trigger on every render.
  const ladderKey = ladder.join(',');

  useEffect(() => {
    const rootEl = root.current;
    if (!rootEl || reduced) return;
    if (containerAnimation === null) return;

    const steps = ladderKey.split(',').map(Number);
    const last = Math.max(1, steps.length - 1);
    const scrollerEl = scroller?.current ?? undefined;
    const horizontal = containerAnimation !== undefined;

    const ctx = gsap.context(() => {
      for (const el of Array.from(rootEl.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-depth]'))) {
        const raw = Number.parseInt(el.dataset.depth ?? '0', 10);
        const depth = clamp(Number.isFinite(raw) ? raw : 0, 0, last);
        // Normalised depth drives distance; the ladder drives lag. Distance
        // alone collapses the moment the scroll stops — the lag is what keeps
        // the planes apart while the eye is still moving.
        const amount = (depth / last) * travel;
        const scrub = steps[depth] ?? 0;

        gsap.fromTo(
          el,
          { yPercent: -amount },
          {
            yPercent: amount,
            ease: 'none',
            scrollTrigger: {
              trigger: el,
              scroller: scrollerEl,
              // Full-crossing window: the layer starts moving as it enters
              // and stops as it leaves, so no layer is ever mid-jump on load.
              start: horizontal ? 'left right' : 'top bottom',
              end: horizontal ? 'right left' : 'bottom top',
              scrub: scrub === 0 ? true : scrub,
              ...(containerAnimation ? { containerAnimation } : {}),
            },
          },
        );
      }
    }, rootEl);

    return () => ctx.revert();
  }, [scroller, containerAnimation, ladderKey, travel, reduced]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `ctx.revert()` on unmount and on any dependency change kills each layer's tween and ScrollTrigger and strips the inline `transform` GSAP wrote, so a remount measures the authored layout rather than the previous run's offsets.

**Reduced motion.** No triggers are created, so every layer sits at its natural document position with no transform at all. The grid is the same grid — it simply does not separate, which is the point of the setting.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Building parallax from distance alone. Every layer lands on its final offset on the same frame, so the depth cue vanishes the instant scrolling stops and the composition flattens.
- Writing `scrub: 0` for the locked plane. It is falsy, so ScrollTrigger disables scrubbing and the layer plays as a one-shot toggle animation — the one plane that was supposed to be rock solid becomes the one that pops.
- Using `y` in pixels instead of `yPercent`. The offsets stop being proportional to the tiles, so a layout that reads well at desktop width has layers sliding out of their cells on a phone.
- Recreating triggers on every render because the ladder is a fresh array literal in the caller's JSX. The triggers are torn down and rebuilt mid-scroll and the layers snap back to their start offsets.
- Indexing the ladder without a bound. `data-depth="7"` on a four-value ladder yields `undefined`, which GSAP coerces into a scrub of `NaN` and the layer stops responding to scroll entirely.
- Keeping vertical position keywords when a `containerAnimation` is supplied. The trigger measures along the container's axis, so vertical keywords resolve to a position the element never reaches and the layer never moves.

## Notes

- Depth 0 is deliberately motionless. Something in the frame has to be still, or the whole composition reads as drift rather than depth.
- Combine with `pinned-horizontal-track` by feeding its `onTrack` payload's `animation` into `containerAnimation`.

## Definition of done

Scroll through the grid at speed: the tiles visibly separate into distinct planes, the depth-0 tile stays locked to the grid, and the deepest tiles trail furthest behind. Stop scrolling and, within about a second, everything settles into an aligned composition. Scroll backwards and the separation reverses rather than replaying.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Modal

A centred dialog built on React Aria's `ModalOverlay`, `Modal` and `Dialog`: focus is trapped and returned to the trigger, the page behind stops scrolling, and Escape or a backdrop press dismisses it. The panel fades in from scale 0.85 with a 4px blur on the iOS sheet curve and plays the same transition in reverse before it unmounts. `ModalHeader`, `ModalBody` and `ModalFooter` lay out the content, and `AlertDialog` is the destructive-confirm preset whose async `onConfirm` keeps it open and busy until the promise settles.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Dialog over a dimmed page with a header, scrolling body and actions, plus an alert dialog for destructive confirms.

- Category: overlay
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `ModalTrigger` splits its children with `Children.toArray`: the first child is the trigger and is wrapped in React Aria's `Pressable`, so any kit button that forwards its ref and spreads props opens the dialog; the rest (the `Modal`) are passed through to `DialogTrigger`. Without a trigger, `Modal` is controlled from outside with `isOpen` / `onOpenChange`.
2. `Modal` renders `ModalOverlay` (`fixed inset-x-0 top-0 z-100`, height `h-(--visual-viewport-height)`, centred with `p-4 sm:p-6`) with `isDismissable` defaulting to true and `dir` from `useDirection()`. Inside it sits an `aria-hidden` backdrop div (`absolute inset-0 bg-black/70`) and the `AriaModal` panel, whose width comes from the `size` map: sm 400, md 480, lg 640, xl 800px.
3. Motion is pure CSS keyed on React Aria's `data-entering` / `data-exiting` attributes. The overlay is a `group/modal`, so the backdrop fades with `group-data-[entering]/modal:opacity-0` over `duration-300 ease-out`. The panel transitions `opacity, scale, filter` over 300ms on `cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)` from `opacity-0` plus, under `motion-safe:` only, `scale-[0.85]` and `blur-[4px]`. React Aria waits for the exit transition before unmounting, so closing replays the entrance in reverse.
4. `ModalDialog` (shared with Drawer) renders the `AriaDialog` surface: `rounded-3xl border border-separator-border bg-background-full shadow-xs`, `py-6`, `gap-4`, and `overflow-clip` rather than `overflow-hidden`. It owns a `useId()` description id and a `described` flag in context; `ModalHeader` sets that flag in a `useLayoutEffect` when it has a description, so `aria-describedby` points at the description only while one is rendered.
5. `ModalHeader` renders an optional 40px icon circle (tinted with the notification-error tokens when `tone="danger"`), the title as a React Aria `Heading slot="title"` so it names the dialog, the description, and a `CloseButton` that calls `useModalClose()` (which reads `OverlayTriggerStateContext`). `ModalBody` is the only scroller (`overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain`) and shows a `ScrollFade` once scrolled; `ModalFooter` stacks actions `flex-col-reverse` on phones and becomes a trailing row from `sm`.
6. `AlertDialog` renders `Modal` with `role="alertdialog"`, `size="sm"` and `isDismissable` false by default. Its confirm handler calls `onConfirm`; if that returns a thenable it sets `pending`, disables Cancel, turns the confirm button `aria-busy` with a spinner and `pendingLabel`, blocks Escape (`isKeyboardDismissDisabled`) and backdrop dismissal, closes on resolve and stays open on reject. Cancel carries `autoFocus`, so focus lands on the safe action.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `panel widths = sm 400 / md 480 / lg 640 / xl 800 px`
  `md` is the default for forms; `AlertDialog` defaults to `sm` because a confirm holds one sentence and two buttons, and a wider panel stretches the line length past comfortable reading.
- `entrance / exit = 300ms, cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), scale 0.85, blur 4px`
  The iOS sheet curve front-loads the motion so the panel arrives fast and settles; the blur hides the scaled-up rasterisation of the first frames. The same values run in reverse on exit.
- `backdrop = bg-black/70, 300ms ease-out opacity`
  Dark enough to separate the panel from a busy page in both themes, and timed with the panel so the two arrive together.
- `icon circle = size-10 (40px) with a size-5 (20px) glyph, mb-4`
  Matches the Settings Modal header so dialogs across the kit share one header rhythm.

## API

```ts
function ModalTrigger(props: Omit<DialogTriggerProps, "children"> & { children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
function Modal(props: Omit<ModalOverlayProps, "children" | "className" | "style"> & { size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"; role?: "dialog" | "alertdialog"; "aria-label"?: string; className?: string; overlayClassName?: string; children: ReactNode | ((renderProps: DialogRenderProps) => ReactNode) }): JSX.Element
function ModalHeader(props: { title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; icon?: IconComponent; tone?: "default" | "danger"; showCloseButton?: boolean; closeLabel?: string; className?: string; children?: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
function ModalBody(props: { className?: string; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
function ModalFooter(props: { className?: string; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
function AlertDialog(props: AlertDialogProps): JSX.Element
function useModalClose(): () => void
```

- `size: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"` — default `"md"`
  Panel max width: 400, 480, 640 or 800px. AlertDialog defaults to "sm".
- `isDismissable: boolean` — default `true (Modal) / false (AlertDialog)`
  Whether a press on the backdrop closes the dialog.
- `isOpen / onOpenChange: boolean / (isOpen: boolean) => void`
  Controlled open state when the Modal is used without a ModalTrigger.
- `children: ReactNode | ((renderProps: DialogRenderProps) => ReactNode)`
  Dialog content; the function form receives `close`.
- `overlayClassName: string`
  Classes on the full-screen overlay, e.g. to pin the panel to the top.
- `ModalHeader.description: ReactNode`
  Supporting copy under the title, wired to the dialog's `aria-describedby`.
- `ModalHeader.tone: "default" | "danger"` — default `"default"`
  Danger tints the 40px icon circle with the error tokens.
- `AlertDialog.onConfirm: () => void | Promise<unknown>`
  Return a promise to keep the dialog open and busy until it settles; it closes on resolve and stays open on reject.
- `AlertDialog.variant: "danger" | "default"` — default `"danger"`
  Danger pairs the warning icon tint with a danger confirm button.
- `AlertDialog.isConfirmDisabled: boolean` — default `false`
  Disables the confirm action, e.g. until a confirmation phrase is typed.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function Modal({
  size = "md",
  role,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel,
  className,
  overlayClassName,
  isDismissable = true,
  children,
  ...props
}: ModalProps) {
  const direction = useDirection();

  return (
    <AriaModalOverlay {...props} dir={direction} isDismissable={isDismissable} className={cx(styles.overlay, overlayClassName)}>
      <div aria-hidden className={styles.backdrop} />
      <AriaModal className={cx(styles.modal, styles.size[size])}>
        <ModalDialog role={role} aria-label={ariaLabel} className={className}>
          {children}
        </ModalDialog>
      </AriaModal>
    </AriaModalOverlay>
  );
}

export interface ModalDialogProps {
  role?: "dialog" | "alertdialog";
  "aria-label"?: string;
  /** Classes merged onto the panel surface. */
  className?: string;
  children: ReactNode | ((renderProps: DialogRenderProps) => ReactNode);
}

/**
 * The panel surface and dialog element shared by Modal and Drawer: the
 * ModalHeader title names it and the description is wired to
 * aria-describedby. Render it inside a React Aria Modal.
 */
export function ModalDialog({ role, "aria-label": ariaLabel, className, children }: ModalDialogProps) {
  const descriptionId = useId();
  const [described, setDescribed] = useState(false);

  return (
    <AriaDialog
      role={role}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      aria-describedby={described ? descriptionId : undefined}
      className={cx(styles.dialog, className)}
    >
      {(renderProps) => (
        <ModalContext.Provider value={{ descriptionId, setDescribed }}>
          {typeof children === "function" ? children(renderProps) : children}
        </ModalContext.Provider>
      )}
    </AriaDialog>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** React Aria releases the focus trap, restores focus to the trigger, and removes the scroll lock when the overlay unmounts after its exit transition. The ModalHeader layout effect resets the `described` flag on unmount. No timers or listeners of its own.

**Reduced motion.** The panel's scale and blur are behind `motion-safe:` and are dropped under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`; the backdrop and panel still fade over 300ms, so opening and closing remain perceptible without movement.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not use `overflow-hidden` on the dialog surface. A hidden box is still programmatically scrollable, so focusing a field clipped by the body scroller can scroll the whole panel; `overflow-clip` cannot be scrolled.
- Do not let the panel or the header scroll. Only `ModalBody` scrolls (`min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto`), so the title and the actions stay put on a short viewport.
- Do not animate the panel with JS or a keyframe that ignores `data-exiting`. React Aria only delays unmount for a CSS transition or animation on the exiting element, which is what makes the close replay the entrance.
- Do not hard-code `aria-describedby`. It is set only while `ModalHeader` renders a description, otherwise it would point at an id that does not exist.
- Do not make an `AlertDialog` dismissable by default or put the initial focus on the destructive button. An alert asks for an answer, and Enter on a focused Delete is an accident waiting to happen.

## Notes

- `useModalClose()` is exported so deep children (a form submit handler, a list row) can close the surrounding Modal, Drawer or AlertDialog without threading `close` down.
- Reduced motion keeps the opacity fade and only drops the scale and blur, because those are behind `motion-safe:`.
- The surface uses `bg-background-full`: page white in light mode and, in dark mode, a ground darker than the inputs and menus inside, so they keep an edge.

## Definition of done

Pressing "Invite teammates" fades in a dimmed backdrop and a panel that grows from slightly smaller and blurred to sharp; Tab cycles only inside the panel, Escape or a click on the backdrop closes it with the reverse animation, and focus returns to the trigger. In the delete AlertDialog, focus starts on Cancel, a backdrop click does nothing, and Delete shows a spinner with "Deleting…" while Cancel is disabled, then closes when the promise resolves.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Model Select

A model picker for chat composers, built on the kit Select so it keeps React Aria listbox behaviour: arrow keys, typeahead, Escape and screen-reader selection state. Each row shows a tinted two-letter monogram, the model name with optional New and Pro badges, a muted description and a check on the selected model. The trigger shows a small monogram and the name; the ghost variant sits flat in a toolbar, and the outline variant is the regular bordered field.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Model picker on the kit Select. Rows show a tinted monogram, name, description, New/Pro badges and a check on the current model.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. The kit `Select` is driven through `selectedKey` and `onSelectionChange`. When `value` is passed the component is controlled; otherwise it keeps its own pick in state, seeded from `defaultValue` or the first enabled model. `onChange` receives both the id and the full model object.
2. Rows are kit `SelectItem`s (React Aria `ListBoxItem`) with `textValue` set to the model name, so typing "de" jumps to Deep 1 even though the row also holds badges and a description.
3. Inside each row the name and badges sit in a React Aria `Text slot="label"` and the description in `Text slot="description"`. The option is labelled by the name and described by the line under it, so the description is announced as a hint, not as part of the name.
4. The monogram is the `monogram` field or, when it is missing, the first character of the first two words of the name ("Deep 1" becomes "D1"). Its square takes a `status-*-background` / `status-*-text` token pair from `tone`, which the kit theme defines for light and dark.
5. The check is always rendered and switches between `opacity-0` and `opacity-100`, so rows never shift width when the selection moves. React Aria already sets `aria-selected` on the option, so the icon is `aria-hidden`.
6. `renderValue` puts a 20px monogram and the name in the trigger. `compact` makes the name `sr-only`, leaving only the monogram on screen while the trigger keeps its accessible text.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `popover size = 320px wide, list up to 336px tall`
  Wide enough for a name with both badges and a description of about 34 characters on one line; the kit menu surface caps it at `100vw - 32px` on phones. The kit listbox stops at 240px, which would hide the fifth two-line row, so the popover lifts that cap through a `[&_[role=listbox]]` variant and longer lists scroll past 336px.
- `monogram = 32px rows / 20px trigger, two characters`
  Two characters keep model families apart ("S2" and "SM") without becoming a logo. 32px matches the height of the two-line text block, so rows stay centred.
- `GHOST_TRIGGER = transparent border, background and shadow; secondary surface on hover or press`
  Inside a composer toolbar a bordered field reads as a form input. The ghost trigger looks like a label until it is pointed at.

## API

```ts
function ModelSelect(props: { models?: ModelOption[]; value?: string; defaultValue?: string; onChange?: (id: string, model: ModelOption) => void; variant?: "ghost" | "outline"; size?: "sm" | "md"; label?: ReactNode; "aria-label"?: string; isDisabled?: boolean; compact?: boolean; className?: string }): JSX.Element
interface ModelOption { id: string; name: string; description?: string; monogram?: string; tone?: ModelTone; badges?: ("new" | "pro")[]; isDisabled?: boolean }
```

- `models: ModelOption[]` — default `MODEL_OPTIONS`
  Rows of the menu, in order.
- `value: string`
  Selected model id. Passing it makes the select controlled.
- `defaultValue: string`
  Starting model when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first enabled model.
- `onChange: (id: string, model: ModelOption) => void`
  Called with the new id and its model when a row is chosen.
- `variant: "ghost" | "outline"` — default `"ghost"`
  Flat trigger for toolbars, or the kit's bordered field.
- `size: "sm" | "md"` — default `"md"`
  Trigger and row density, passed to the kit Select. `sm` also shrinks the row monograms.
- `label: ReactNode`
  Visible label above the trigger. Without it the select is named by `aria-label`.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Model"`
  Accessible name when there is no visible label.
- `isDisabled: boolean`
  Disables the whole select.
- `compact: boolean` — default `false`
  Shows only the monogram in the trigger; the name stays for screen readers.
- `className: string`
  Classes for the select wrapper.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function ModelSelect({
  models = MODEL_OPTIONS,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onChange,
  variant = "ghost",
  size = "md",
  label,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel = "Model",
  isDisabled,
  compact = false,
  className,
}: ModelSelectProps) {
  const fallback = models.find((m) => !m.isDisabled)?.id ?? models[0]?.id ?? null;
  const [internal, setInternal] = useState<string | null>(defaultValue ?? fallback);
  // Controlled when `value` is passed; otherwise the select keeps its own pick.
  const selectedId = value ?? internal;
  const selected = models.find((m) => m.id === selectedId);

  return (
    <Select<ModelOption>
      label={label}
      aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}
      size={size}
      isDisabled={isDisabled}
      selectedKey={selectedId}
      disabledKeys={models.filter((m) => m.isDisabled).map((m) => m.id)}
      onSelectionChange={(key) => {
        if (key == null) return;
        const id = String(key);
        const model = models.find((m) => m.id === id);
        if (!model) return;
        if (value === undefined) setInternal(id);
        onChange?.(id, model);
      }}
      className={cx("w-fit", className)}
      triggerClassName={variant === "ghost" ? GHOST_TRIGGER : undefined}
      // The kit listbox caps at 240px; five two-line rows need about 300px.
      popoverClassName="w-[320px] [&_[role=listbox]]:max-h-[336px]"
      renderValue={
        selected ? (
          <>
            <ModelMonogram model={selected} small />
            <span data-model-name className={cx("truncate", compact && "sr-only")}>{selected.name}</span>
          </>
        ) : (
          <span className="text-text-placeholder">Choose a model</span>
        )
      }
    >
      {models.map((model) => {
        const isSelected = model.id === selectedId;
        return (
          <SelectItem key={model.id} id={model.id} textValue={model.name} className="gap-2.5">
            <ModelMonogram model={model} small={size === "sm"} />
            <span className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-0.5">
              <Text slot="label" className="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-1.5">
                <span className="truncate">{model.name}</span>
                <ModelBadges badges={model.badges} />
              </Text>
              {model.description && (
                <Text slot="description" className="truncate text-body-2-regular text-text-tertiary">
                  {model.description}
                </Text>
              )}
            </span>
            <RiCheckLine
              aria-hidden
              className={cx(
                "size-4 shrink-0 text-accent-500 transition-opacity duration-150 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
                isSelected ? "opacity-100" : "opacity-0",
              )}
            />
          </SelectItem>
        );
      })}
    </Select>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The component adds no timers or listeners of its own. Open state, outside-press dismissal and focus restore belong to the kit Select and React Aria.

**Reduced motion.** The check fades with `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so it switches instantly. The popover open animation and chevron turn come from the kit Select.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Leaving out `textValue` on rows with rich content. React Aria then cannot build typeahead text or the trigger's accessible value from the row.
- Putting the description inside the label. Screen readers then read "Deep 1 Slower, reasons for longer" as the model's name; the `description` slot keeps it as a hint.
- Mounting the check only on the selected row. The text column then reflows as the check appears; toggling opacity keeps every row the same width.

## Notes

- The model list, names and descriptions are sample data. Pass your own `models`; badges are any mix of `"new"` and `"pro"`.
- Disabled models go to the kit Select as `disabledKeys`, and the uncontrolled default skips them.
- The kit Select places its popover below the trigger and flips it above when there is no room, which is what happens at the foot of a chat.

## Definition of done

The trigger shows a tinted monogram and the model name. Opening it lists five models with descriptions; Atlas 3 and Lumen 1 carry New, Deep 1 and Lumen 1 carry Pro. The current model has a check. Choosing a row closes the menu, moves the check and updates the trigger and the demo sentence. Arrow keys and typeahead work, and Escape closes the menu.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Models Picker

The model list from an agent's settings. Each row shows a small tinted provider monogram, the model name and a control on the right. In `single` mode the rows form one radio group and the chosen row sits on a soft grey fill, the way an active-model menu reads. In `multiple` mode every row is a switch that adds the model to the composer, and the header keeps an "N of M enabled" count. A search field filters by name and provider, and `children` render under a divider for things like an effort slider.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A card of models with provider monograms: pick one with radios, or enable several with switches, a search filter and a live count.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Split the props into a discriminated union on `selectionMode`: `single` takes `value: string` and `onChange(id)`, `multiple` takes `value: string[]` and `onChange(ids)`. Both are controlled-or-uncontrolled: local state seeds from `defaultValue` and `value` wins when given.
2. Single mode renders a react-aria `RadioGroup` whose `Radio`s ARE the rows (monogram, name, kit `RadioDot`), so one Tab stop enters the list, arrow keys move and select, and the selected row gets `bg-background-secondary-default`.
3. Multiple mode renders each row as a react-aria `Switch` with the kit `SwitchTrack` on the right, inside a `role="group"` named by the label. Toggling rebuilds the value by filtering `models` in their own order, so the array is stable no matter which order rows were flipped.
4. The search query is trimmed, lowercased and matched against `name + provider + description`; the filtered list replaces the rows, and an empty result prints "No models match …" instead. The count in the header always counts the whole list, not the filtered rows.
5. The monogram is a 28px rounded square with one or two letters (`monogram` or the provider's first letter) on a status tint, `aria-hidden`; the provider name is added as visually hidden text so the radio or switch is announced as "Fable 5, Anthropic".

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `monogram = size-7, rounded 8px, caption-1 semibold`
  Big enough for two letters at a glance, small enough that the model name stays the first thing read.
- `row padding = px-2.5 py-2, rounded-2lg, 2px gap`
  The selected fill needs air around it inside the 6px card padding, and a 2px gap keeps adjacent hover fills from merging.
- `searchable default = more than 5 models`
  A short list is faster to scan than to search; past a screenful, a filter pays for its height.

## API

```ts
function ModelsPicker(props: ({ selectionMode?: "single"; value?: string; defaultValue?: string; onChange?: (id: string) => void } | { selectionMode: "multiple"; value?: string[]; defaultValue?: string[]; onChange?: (ids: string[]) => void }) & { models: ModelOption[]; label?: ReactNode; searchable?: boolean; searchPlaceholder?: string; children?: ReactNode; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type ModelOption = { id: string; name: string; provider: string; monogram?: string; tone?: ModelMonogramTone; description?: string; isDisabled?: boolean }
```

- `models: ModelOption[]`
  Rows in display order: id, name, provider, optional monogram letters, tint, caption and disabled flag.
- `selectionMode: "single" | "multiple"` — default `"single"`
  Radio rows for one active model, or switch rows for an enabled set.
- `value: string | string[]`
  Controlled selection: an id in single mode, an id array in multiple mode.
- `defaultValue: string | string[]`
  Initial selection when uncontrolled.
- `onChange: (id: string) => void | (ids: string[]) => void`
  Called with the new id or the new id array, in the models' order.
- `label: ReactNode` — default `"Models"`
  Header title; a string also names the radio group or switch group.
- `searchable: boolean` — default `models.length > 5`
  Show the search field above the rows.
- `searchPlaceholder: string` — default `"Search models"`
  Placeholder of the search field.
- `children: ReactNode`
  Footer content under a divider, e.g. an effort control.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function ModelsPicker(props: ModelsPickerProps) {
  const { models, label = "Models", searchPlaceholder = "Search models", children, className } = props;
  const multiple = props.selectionMode === "multiple";
  const searchable = props.searchable ?? models.length > 5;

  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
  const [single, setSingle] = useState<string | undefined>(
    props.selectionMode === "multiple" ? undefined : props.defaultValue,
  );
  const [many, setMany] = useState<string[]>(
    props.selectionMode === "multiple" ? (props.defaultValue ?? []) : [],
  );

  const selectedOne = props.selectionMode === "multiple" ? undefined : (props.value ?? single);
  const selectedMany = props.selectionMode === "multiple" ? (props.value ?? many) : [];

  const pick = (id: string) => {
    if (props.selectionMode === "multiple") return;
    setSingle(id);
    props.onChange?.(id);
  };

  const toggle = (id: string, on: boolean) => {
    if (props.selectionMode !== "multiple") return;
    // Keep the models' own order so the value is stable however it was toggled.
    const next = models.filter((m) => (m.id === id ? on : selectedMany.includes(m.id))).map((m) => m.id);
    setMany(next);
    props.onChange?.(next);
  };

  const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();
  const shown = q
    ? models.filter((m) => `${m.name} ${m.provider} ${m.description ?? ""}`.toLowerCase().includes(q))
    : models;

  const groupLabel = typeof label === "string" ? label : "Models";
  const count = multiple
    ? `${models.filter((m) => selectedMany.includes(m.id)).length} of ${models.length} enabled`
    : `${models.length} available`;

  const empty = (
    <p className="px-2.5 py-6 text-center text-caption-1-medium text-text-tertiary">
      No models match “{query.trim()}”
    </p>
  );

  return (
    <section
      className={cx(
        // Dark: primary and tertiary are both neutral-800, so the card drops to
        // secondary or the off switch tracks and the search field disappear.
        "flex w-full min-w-0 flex-col gap-1 rounded-2xl border border-border-table bg-background-primary-default p-1.5 shadow-xs dark:bg-background-secondary-default",
        className,
      )}
    >
      <header className="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3 px-2.5 pt-1.5 pb-1">
        <h3 className="text-body-medium text-text-secondary">{label}</h3>
        <span className="text-caption-1-medium text-text-tertiary tabular-nums" aria-live="polite">
          {count}
        </span>
      </header>

      {searchable ? (
        <SearchField
          aria-label={`Search ${groupLabel.toLowerCase()}`}
          placeholder={searchPlaceholder}
          size="small"
          value={query}
          onChange={setQuery}
          className="px-1 pb-1"
        />
      ) : null}

      {multiple ? (
        <div role="group" aria-label={groupLabel} className="flex flex-col gap-0.5">
          {shown.length === 0
            ? empty
            : shown.map((m) => (
                <AriaSwitch
                  key={m.id}
                  isSelected={selectedMany.includes(m.id)}
                  isDisabled={m.isDisabled}
                  onChange={(on) => toggle(m.id, on)}
                  className={({ isHovered, isDisabled }) =>
                    cx(
                      row,
                      isDisabled ? "cursor-not-allowed opacity-50" : "cursor-pointer",
                      isHovered && "bg-background-primary-hover",
                    )
                  }
                >
                  {(state) => (
                    <>
                      <ModelMonogram model={m} />
                      <ModelText model={m} />
                      <SwitchTrack state={state} size="sm" />
                    </>
                  )}
                </AriaSwitch>
              ))}
        </div>
      ) : (
        <AriaRadioGroup
          aria-label={groupLabel}
          value={selectedOne ?? null}
          onChange={pick}
          className="flex flex-col gap-0.5"
        >
          {shown.length === 0
            ? empty
            : shown.map((m) => (
                <AriaRadio
                  key={m.id}
                  value={m.id}
                  isDisabled={m.isDisabled}
                  className={({ isSelected, isHovered, isDisabled }) =>
                    cx(
                      row,
                      isDisabled ? "cursor-not-allowed opacity-50" : "cursor-pointer",
                      isSelected
                        ? "bg-background-secondary-default dark:bg-background-primary-default"
                        : isHovered && "bg-background-primary-hover",
                    )
                  }
                >
                  {({ isSelected, isFocusVisible }) => (
                    <>
                      <ModelMonogram model={m} />
                      <ModelText model={m} />
                      <RadioDot selected={isSelected} focusVisible={isFocusVisible} />
                    </>
                  )}
                </AriaRadio>
              ))}
        </AriaRadioGroup>
      )}

      {children != null && children !== false ? (
        <>
          <hr className="mx-1 mt-1 border-border-table" />
          <div className="px-2.5 pt-1.5 pb-2">{children}</div>
        </>
      ) : null}
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up: state is the query and the uncontrolled selection, with no timers, listeners or observers.

**Reduced motion.** The only motion is the 150ms row hover and selected fill, plus the kit switch thumb; rows carry `motion-reduce:transition-none` and the switch track follows its own reduced-motion rule.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Wrapping a radio input in a clickable div. The row must BE the radio (or switch) so the whole row is the hit target and the accessible name covers the model, not just the dot.
- Counting the filtered rows. "2 of 8 enabled" must not drop to "1 of 3" while a search is typed.
- Drawing provider logos. The glyph is letters on a tint, which avoids trademark artwork and still tells providers apart.

## Notes

- Pass `searchable` explicitly to force the field on a short list or hide it on a long one.
- The demo puts the kit `Slider` (0–3, no tooltip) under the active-model list as an effort control with Faster and Smarter labels.

## Definition of done

Left card: "Fable 5" is selected; clicking "Sonnet 5" moves the grey fill and the radio, and ArrowDown from it wraps to "Composer 2.5". Pressing ArrowRight on the Effort slider changes "Medium" to "High". Right card reads "4 of 8 enabled"; switching on Gemini makes it "5 of 8"; typing "anthropic" leaves 3 rows with the count unchanged, and "zzz" shows "No models match".

# Build: Month Stepper

The calendar header's month switcher: a 36px bordered pill with a chevron button at each end and the formatted month centred between them. The label is a focusable spinbutton, so the whole control is usable from the keyboard without tabbing between the buttons. Each step slides the new label in from the side it came from.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A bordered month label between prev/next chevrons, with spinbutton keys: arrows step a month, Page Up/Down a year, Home/End the bounds.

- Category: navigation
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @internationalized/date@^3.12.4, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. State is a `CalendarDate` from `@internationalized/date`, normalised with `startOfMonth`. `value` makes it controlled; otherwise `defaultValue` (or the current month) seeds internal state. Every change is emitted as the first day of the month.
2. Bounds and comparisons use `monthIndex(date) = year * 12 + month - 1`, a monotonic integer. `step(n)` clamps `current + n` to `[min, max]`, does nothing when the clamped target equals the current month, and otherwise calls `month.add({ months: target - current })`. The chevrons are disabled at the bounds.
3. The label is a `role="spinbutton"` span with `aria-valuenow` set to the month index and `aria-valuetext` set to the formatted label. Its key handler maps ArrowUp and the reading-direction arrow to +1, ArrowDown and the opposite arrow to -1, PageUp/PageDown to ±12, and Home/End to the min/max when they are set. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight swap under RTL.
4. The label text comes from a `DateFormatter(locale, { month: "long", year: "numeric", ...formatOptions, timeZone: "UTC" })` applied to `month.toDate("UTC")`, so server and client format the same instant and hydration matches.
5. An effect compares the new month index with the previous one and runs `element.animate()` on the inner label: opacity 0 → 1 and translateX(±8px) → 0 over 180ms, with the sign from the step direction (mirrored in RTL). The effect returns `animation.cancel()`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `height = 36px medium / 32px small`
  Matches the kit's icon buttons and inputs, so the stepper lines up with the notification and inbox buttons beside it in the calendar header.
- `button box = 34px / 30px inside a 1px border`
  The chevron hit area fills the pill's inner height exactly, so the hover tint touches the border with a 9px (or 7px) radius that follows the outer 10px (or 8px) corner.
- `default width = w-80 (320px)`
  The calendar header gives the stepper a fixed width so the chevrons do not jump as the month name changes length (May vs September).
- `label slide = 8px, 180ms, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`
  Enough travel to show which way the month moved without the text leaving the pill. Short enough that holding an arrow key stays readable.

## API

```ts
function MonthStepper(props: { value?: CalendarDate; defaultValue?: CalendarDate; onChange?: (month: CalendarDate) => void; minValue?: CalendarDate; maxValue?: CalendarDate; locale?: string; formatOptions?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions; size?: "medium" | "small"; "aria-label"?: string; previousLabel?: string; nextLabel?: string; isDisabled?: boolean; className?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function monthIndex(date: CalendarDate): number
```

- `value: CalendarDate`
  Controlled month. Any day in the month works.
- `defaultValue: CalendarDate` — default `current month`
  Uncontrolled starting month.
- `onChange: (month: CalendarDate) => void`
  Called with the first day of the newly shown month.
- `minValue / maxValue: CalendarDate`
  Inclusive month bounds. The chevrons disable and Home/End jump to them.
- `locale: string` — default `"en-US"`
  Locale for the month label.
- `formatOptions: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` — default `{ month: "long", year: "numeric" }`
  Overrides for the label format, e.g. `{ month: "short" }`.
- `size: "medium" | "small"` — default `"medium"`
  36px or 32px tall.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Month"`
  Name of the group and the spinbutton.
- `previousLabel / nextLabel: string` — default `"Previous month" / "Next month"`
  Accessible names of the chevron buttons.
- `isDisabled: boolean` — default `false`
  Disables both buttons and removes the label from the tab order.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function MonthStepper({
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onChange,
  minValue,
  maxValue,
  locale = "en-US",
  formatOptions,
  size = "medium",
  "aria-label": ariaLabel = "Month",
  previousLabel = "Previous month",
  nextLabel = "Next month",
  isDisabled = false,
  className,
  ref,
}: MonthStepperProps) {
  const direction = useDirection();
  const reducedMotion = useReducedMotion();
  const [uncontrolled, setUncontrolled] = useState<CalendarDate>(() =>
    startOfMonth(defaultValue ?? today(getLocalTimeZone())),
  );
  const month = startOfMonth(value ?? uncontrolled);
  const current = monthIndex(month);
  const min = minValue ? monthIndex(minValue) : -Infinity;
  const max = maxValue ? monthIndex(maxValue) : Infinity;

  const formatter = useMemo(
    () => new DateFormatter(locale, { month: "long", year: "numeric", ...formatOptions, timeZone: "UTC" }),
    [locale, formatOptions],
  );
  const label = formatter.format(month.toDate("UTC"));

  const step = (months: number) => {
    const target = Math.min(max, Math.max(min, current + months));
    if (isDisabled || target === current) return;
    const next = month.add({ months: target - current });
    setUncontrolled(next);
    onChange?.(next);
  };

  // Slide the label in from the side the user stepped towards. The Web
  // Animations API needs no keyframes in the stylesheet and cancels cleanly.
  const labelRef = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);
  const previous = useRef(current);
  useEffect(() => {
    const delta = current - previous.current;
    previous.current = current;
    const el = labelRef.current;
    if (!el || delta === 0 || reducedMotion || typeof el.animate !== "function") return;
    const from = (delta > 0 ? 8 : -8) * (direction === "rtl" ? -1 : 1);
    const animation = el.animate(
      [
        { opacity: 0, transform: `translateX(${from}px)` },
        { opacity: 1, transform: "translateX(0)" },
      ],
      { duration: 180, easing: "cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)" },
    );
    return () => animation.cancel();
  }, [current, reducedMotion, direction]);

  const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLSpanElement>) => {
    const forward = direction === "rtl" ? "ArrowLeft" : "ArrowRight";
    const back = direction === "rtl" ? "ArrowRight" : "ArrowLeft";
    let delta: number | null = null;
    if (event.key === "ArrowUp" || event.key === forward) delta = 1;
    else if (event.key === "ArrowDown" || event.key === back) delta = -1;
    else if (event.key === "PageUp") delta = 12;
    else if (event.key === "PageDown") delta = -12;
    else if (event.key === "Home" && Number.isFinite(min)) delta = min - current;
    else if (event.key === "End" && Number.isFinite(max)) delta = max - current;
    if (delta === null) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    step(delta);
  };

  const s = sizes[size];
  const buttonClass = cx(
    "inline-flex shrink-0 cursor-pointer items-center justify-center text-foreground-icon-primary",
    "transition-colors duration-150 ease-out hover:bg-background-primary-hover active:bg-background-primary-active",
    "outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
    "disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:text-foreground-disabled disabled:hover:bg-transparent",
    s.button,
  );

  return (
    <div
      ref={ref}
      role="group"
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      data-disabled={isDisabled || undefined}
      className={cx(
        "inline-flex w-80 max-w-full items-center justify-between gap-1 border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default shadow-xs",
        "data-[disabled]:opacity-60",
        s.root,
        className,
      )}
    >
      <button
        type="button"
        aria-label={previousLabel}
        disabled={isDisabled || current <= min}
        onClick={() => step(-1)}
        className={buttonClass}
      >
        <RiArrowLeftSLine aria-hidden className={cx(s.icon, "rtl:rotate-180")} />
      </button>
      <span
        role="spinbutton"
        tabIndex={isDisabled ? -1 : 0}
        aria-label={ariaLabel}
        aria-valuenow={current}
        aria-valuetext={label}
        aria-valuemin={Number.isFinite(min) ? min : undefined}
        aria-valuemax={Number.isFinite(max) ? max : undefined}
        aria-disabled={isDisabled || undefined}
        onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
        className={cx(
          "min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-default select-none overflow-hidden rounded-md text-center text-text-primary outline-none",
          "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
          s.label,
        )}
      >
        <span ref={labelRef} className="block truncate tabular-nums" aria-hidden>
          {label}
        </span>
      </span>
      <button
        type="button"
        aria-label={nextLabel}
        disabled={isDisabled || current >= max}
        onClick={() => step(1)}
        className={buttonClass}
      >
        <RiArrowRightSLine aria-hidden className={cx(s.icon, "rtl:rotate-180")} />
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The slide effect returns `animation.cancel()`, so a fast second step or an unmount stops the running animation. There are no listeners, timers or observers.

**Reduced motion.** The label slide is skipped entirely: `useReducedMotion()` gates the `element.animate()` call, so the new month replaces the old one instantly. Button hover tints still change colour.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Comparing months with `CalendarDate.compare`. Day-of-month differences make 2026-08-15 "after" 2026-08-01 even though they are the same month. Compare `monthIndex` values instead.
- Formatting with the runtime's local time zone. `toDate(getLocalTimeZone())` can land on the previous day in UTC on the server, and the label hydrates as July. Format a UTC date with `timeZone: "UTC"`.
- Stepping with `.set({ month: month + 1 })`. It does not roll the year over; `.add({ months })` does.
- Animating on every render. The effect must compare with the previous month index, or a parent re-render replays the slide.

## Notes

- Without `value` or `defaultValue` the stepper starts on the current month in the viewer's time zone. Pass a fixed date when the markup is server rendered.
- The chevron buttons stay in the tab order for pointer-first users of assistive tech, and the spinbutton covers keyboard stepping.

## Definition of done

The stepper shows "August 2026". Clicking the right chevron shows "September 2026" and the label slides in from the right; the left chevron goes back. Focusing the label and pressing ArrowRight steps forward, PageUp jumps to the same month next year. A stepper bounded to January–December 2026 disables its next chevron on December and ignores further ArrowUp presses; Home jumps to January.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
