# Build: Month View Grid

The month page of the calendar template: a grey frame, weekday headers and six rows of rounded day cells. Days before and after the month are muted but keep their events in full colour. Each day lists its events as compact kit chips at the bottom of the cell; past `maxVisible` the rest collapse into a "+N more" button on the date line, which selects the day and calls `onShowMore`. The selected day gets an accent pill and today an accent number. It is an ARIA grid with a single tab stop: arrows, Home / End and Page Up / Page Down move focus and turn the month when needed. Below 560px of its own width the cells swap chips for colour dots. `renderEvent` wraps chips, for example in an EventDetailPopover, and `eventsOnDay` feeds an agenda panel.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Six-week month calendar: muted outside days, event chips per day with "+N more", a selected-day pill and full arrow-key navigation.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @internationalized/date@^3.12.4

## How it works

1. The grid always shows 42 days starting at `startOfWeek(startOfMonth(month), locale, firstDayOfWeek)`, so every month has the same six rows and the layout never jumps. `month`, `selectedDate` and the focused day are each controlled or uncontrolled independently.
2. One memoised pass sorts the events (all-day first, then start, longer first) and buckets them by every visible day they touch; an event ending exactly at midnight stops the day before, so all-day events stored midnight to midnight cover the right days. Each cell shows the first `maxVisible` and counts the rest for "+N more", which sits on the number line so it never costs a chip row.
3. Roving focus: exactly one gridcell has `tabIndex=0`, the focused day if it is on screen, else the selected day, else today, else the 1st. The chips and "+N more" inside that cell are tabbable; all others are `-1`, so Tab enters the grid once and leaves after the active day.
4. A single `onKeyDown` on the grid acts only when the target is a gridcell (keys on chips, buttons and portaled popovers are left alone). It reads the day from `data-date`, moves ±1 day (mirrored in RTL), ±7 days, to `startOfWeek` / `endOfWeek`, or ±1 month (Shift: ±1 year), calls `onMonthChange` when the target leaves the month, and sets a flag so an effect focuses `[data-date=…]` after the new month renders.
5. Cells carry `--cell-min-h = 34 + 24 × maxVisible` px and use it only at container widths of 560px and up (`@min-[560px]:min-h-(--cell-min-h)`); narrower, they drop to 48px with up to three colour dots and the header shows narrow weekday letters.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `weeks = 6 (42 days)`
  Months span four to six weeks; always drawing six keeps the grid height fixed when paging.
- `maxVisible = 3 (demo 2)`
  Three 22px chips fill a ~110px cell; the demo uses two so six rows fit in 560px.
- `cell min height = 34 + 24 × maxVisible px`
  12px padding, the 20px number line, a 4px gap and 22px chips with 2px gaps.
- `compact breakpoint = 560px container width`
  Below ~80px per column a chip cannot show a title, so cells switch to colour dots.

## API

```ts
function MonthViewGrid(props: { events: CalendarEvent[]; month?: CalendarDate; defaultMonth?: CalendarDate; onMonthChange?: (month: CalendarDate) => void; selectedDate?: CalendarDate | null; defaultSelectedDate?: CalendarDate | null; onSelectedDateChange?: (date: CalendarDate) => void; today?: CalendarDate; firstDayOfWeek?: DayOfWeek; selectedEventId?: string | null; maxVisible?: number; onShowMore?: (date: CalendarDate, events: CalendarEvent[]) => void; onEventClick?: (event: CalendarEvent) => void; renderEvent?: (event: CalendarEvent, chip: ReactElement, day: CalendarDate) => ReactNode; locale?: string; hourCycle?: 12 | 24; "aria-label"?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function eventsOnDay(events: CalendarEvent[], day: CalendarDate): CalendarEvent[]
```

- `events: CalendarEvent[]`
  Timed and all-day events; multi-day events appear on each day.
- `month / defaultMonth / onMonthChange: CalendarDate`
  Any day in the month to show; called with the 1st when keyboard navigation leaves the month.
- `selectedDate / defaultSelectedDate / onSelectedDateChange: CalendarDate | null` — default `null`
  The day with the accent pill; set by click, Enter, Space or "+N more".
- `today: CalendarDate`
  Accent number and initial tab stop. Never read from the clock inside.
- `firstDayOfWeek: 'sun' | 'mon' | … | 'sat'` — default `locale`
  First column.
- `maxVisible: number` — default `3`
  Chips per day before "+N more".
- `onShowMore: (date, events) => void`
  "+N more" was pressed; the day is selected too.
- `selectedEventId: string | null`
  Rings the matching chip.
- `onEventClick: (event) => void`
  Called when a chip is pressed.
- `renderEvent: (event, chip, day) => ReactNode`
  Wrap each chip, for example in an EventDetailPopover; key open state on the day too, since multi-day events render once per day.
- `hourCycle: 12 | 24` — default `24`
  Chip times.
- `locale: string` — default `"en-US"`
  Weekday names, first day of week, labels.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function MonthViewGrid({
  events,
  month: controlledMonth,
  defaultMonth,
  onMonthChange,
  selectedDate: controlledSelected,
  defaultSelectedDate = null,
  onSelectedDateChange,
  today,
  firstDayOfWeek,
  selectedEventId,
  maxVisible = 3,
  onShowMore,
  onEventClick,
  renderEvent,
  locale = "en-US",
  hourCycle = 24,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel,
  className,
  ref,
}: MonthViewGridProps) {
  const [ownMonth, setOwnMonth] = useState<CalendarDate | undefined>(defaultMonth);
  const [ownSelected, setOwnSelected] = useState<CalendarDate | null>(defaultSelectedDate);
  const [focused, setFocused] = useState<CalendarDate | null>(null);
  const gridRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const moveFocus = useRef(false);

  const selected = controlledSelected !== undefined ? controlledSelected : ownSelected;
  const first = events[0];
  const month = startOfMonth(
    controlledMonth ?? ownMonth ?? selected ?? today ?? (first ? toCalendarDate(first.start) : parseDate("2026-01-01")),
  );
  const gridStart = startOfWeek(month, locale, firstDayOfWeek);
  // Always six weeks, so the grid keeps its height from month to month.
  const days = useMemo(() => Array.from({ length: 42 }, (_, i) => gridStart.add({ days: i })), [gridStart.toString()]); // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  const gridEnd = days[41] ?? gridStart;

  // Bucket events by the visible days they touch (multi-day events repeat on each day).
  const byDay = useMemo(() => {
    const map = new Map<string, CalendarEvent[]>();
    for (const event of [...events].sort(byStart)) {
      let day = toCalendarDate(event.start);
      if (day.compare(gridStart) < 0) day = gridStart;
      const last = lastDayOf(event);
      for (; day.compare(last) <= 0 && day.compare(gridEnd) <= 0; day = day.add({ days: 1 })) {
        const key = day.toString();
        const list = map.get(key);
        if (list) list.push(event);
        else map.set(key, [event]);
      }
    }
    return map;
  }, [events, gridStart.toString()]); // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps

  // One tab stop: the focused day if it is on screen, else the selected day
  // in this month, else today in this month, else the 1st.
  const inGrid = (d: CalendarDate | null | undefined): d is CalendarDate =>
    !!d && d.compare(gridStart) >= 0 && d.compare(gridEnd) <= 0;
  const tabStop = inGrid(focused)
    ? focused
    : selected && isSameMonth(selected, month)
      ? selected
      : today && isSameMonth(today, month)
        ? today
        : month;

  // After a keyboard move (possibly to another month) focus the new cell
  // once it has rendered.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!moveFocus.current || !focused) return;
    moveFocus.current = false;
    gridRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-date="${focused.toString()}"]`)?.focus();
  }, [focused, month]);

  const changeMonth = (next: CalendarDate) => {
    const start = startOfMonth(next);
    if (start.compare(month) === 0) return;
    setOwnMonth(start);
    onMonthChange?.(start);
  };
  const select = (date: CalendarDate) => {
    setOwnSelected(date);
    onSelectedDateChange?.(date);
  };

  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const cell = e.target as HTMLElement;
    const iso = cell.dataset.date;
    // Keys pressed on a chip or "+N more" belong to that button.
    if (!iso || cell.getAttribute("role") !== "gridcell") return;
    const from = parseDate(iso);
    if (e.key === "Enter" || e.key === " ") {
      e.preventDefault();
      select(from);
      return;
    }
    if (!NAV_KEYS.has(e.key)) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    const rtl = getComputedStyle(cell).direction === "rtl";
    const step = { ArrowLeft: rtl ? 1 : -1, ArrowRight: rtl ? -1 : 1, ArrowUp: -7, ArrowDown: 7 } as Record<string, number>;
    let to: CalendarDate;
    if (e.key in step) to = from.add({ days: step[e.key] ?? 0 });
    else if (e.key === "Home") to = startOfWeek(from, locale, firstDayOfWeek);
    else if (e.key === "End") to = endOfWeek(from, locale, firstDayOfWeek);
    else to = from.add(e.shiftKey ? { years: e.key === "PageUp" ? -1 : 1 } : { months: e.key === "PageUp" ? -1 : 1 });
    moveFocus.current = true;
    setFocused(to);
    if (!isSameMonth(to, month)) changeMonth(to);
  };

  const weekdays = days.slice(0, 7);
  const rows = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, r) => days.slice(r * 7, r * 7 + 7));
  // 12px padding + 20px number line + 4px gap + 22px chips with 2px gaps.
  const cellStyle = { "--cell-min-h": `${34 + maxVisible * 24}px` } as CSSProperties;

  return (
    <div
      ref={ref}
      className={cx("@container w-full rounded-[20px] bg-background-secondary-default p-1.5", className)}
    >
      <div
        ref={gridRef}
        role="grid"
        aria-label={ariaLabel ?? formatDay(month, locale, { month: "long", year: "numeric" })}
        onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
        className="flex flex-col gap-1"
      >
        <div role="row" className="grid grid-cols-7 gap-1 @min-[560px]:gap-x-1.5">
          {weekdays.map((day) => (
            <div
              key={day.toString()}
              role="columnheader"
              aria-label={formatDay(day, locale, { weekday: "long" })}
              className="py-1 text-center text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary"
            >
              <span className="@min-[560px]:hidden">{formatDay(day, locale, { weekday: "narrow" })}</span>
              <span className="hidden @min-[560px]:inline">{formatDay(day, locale, { weekday: "short" })}</span>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>

        {rows.map((week) => (
          <div key={week[0]?.toString()} role="row" className="grid grid-cols-7 gap-1 @min-[560px]:gap-x-1.5">
            {week.map((day) => {
              const key = day.toString();
              const list = byDay.get(key) ?? [];
              const outside = !isSameMonth(day, month);
              const isSelected = !!selected && isSameDay(day, selected);
              const isToday = !!today && isSameDay(day, today);
              const isStop = isSameDay(day, tabStop);
              // "+N more" shares the number's line, so it never costs a chip row.
              const shown = list.slice(0, maxVisible);
              const hidden = list.length - shown.length;
              const name = `${formatDay(day, locale, { weekday: "long", month: "long", day: "numeric" })}${
                isToday ? ", today" : ""
              }${list.length ? `, ${list.length} ${list.length === 1 ? "event" : "events"}` : ""}`;

              return (
                <div
                  key={key}
                  role="gridcell"
                  data-date={key}
                  data-outside-month={outside || undefined}
                  data-today={isToday || undefined}
                  aria-selected={isSelected}
                  aria-label={name}
                  tabIndex={isStop ? 0 : -1}
                  style={cellStyle}
                  onClick={() => {
                    setFocused(day);
                    select(day);
                  }}
                  onFocus={(e) => {
                    if (e.target === e.currentTarget) setFocused(day);
                  }}
                  className={cx(
                    "flex min-h-10 min-w-0 cursor-default flex-col gap-1 rounded-lg p-1 outline-none @min-[560px]:min-h-(--cell-min-h) @min-[560px]:rounded-xl @min-[560px]:p-1.5",
                    "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
                    outside
                      ? "bg-background-tertiary-default dark:bg-background-inner-default"
                      : "bg-background-primary-default",
                  )}
                >
                  <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-1">
                    <span
                      aria-hidden
                      className={cx(
                        "flex h-5 min-w-6 items-center justify-center rounded-full px-1.5 tabular-nums",
                        isToday ? "text-body-2-semibold" : "text-body-2-medium",
                        isSelected
                          ? "bg-accent-500 text-text-white"
                          : isToday
                            ? "text-accent-500"
                            : outside
                              ? "text-text-secondary"
                              : "text-text-primary",
                      )}
                    >
                      {day.day}
                    </span>
                    {hidden > 0 ? (
                      <button
                        type="button"
                        tabIndex={isStop ? 0 : -1}
                        aria-label={`${hidden} more on ${formatDay(day, locale, { month: "long", day: "numeric" })}`}
                        onClick={(e) => {
                          e.stopPropagation();
                          setFocused(day);
                          select(day);
                          onShowMore?.(day, list);
                        }}
                        className="hidden h-5 truncate rounded-md px-1 text-caption-2-semibold text-text-secondary outline-none transition-colors duration-150 ease-out hover:bg-background-secondary-default hover:text-text-primary focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring motion-reduce:transition-none @min-[560px]:block"
                      >
                        +{hidden} more
                      </button>
                    ) : null}
                  </div>

                  {list.length > 0 ? (
                    <>
                      <ul className="mt-auto hidden min-w-0 flex-col gap-0.5 @min-[560px]:flex">
                        {shown.map((event) => {
                          const chip = (
                            <CalendarEventChip
                              title={event.title}
                              color={event.color}
                              start={event.start}
                              end={event.end}
                              allDay={event.allDay}
                              locale={locale}
                              hourCycle={hourCycle}
                              selected={selectedEventId === event.id}
                              tabIndex={isStop ? 0 : -1}
                              onClick={onEventClick ? () => onEventClick(event) : undefined}
                            />
                          );
                          return (
                            <li key={event.id} className="flex min-w-0">
                              {renderEvent ? renderEvent(event, chip, day) : chip}
                            </li>
                          );
                        })}
                      </ul>
                      <div aria-hidden className="mt-auto flex justify-center gap-0.5 pb-0.5 @min-[560px]:hidden">
                        {list.slice(0, 3).map((event) => (
                          <span key={event.id} className={cx("size-1.5 rounded-full", calendarEventColorStyles[event.color].dot)} />
                        ))}
                      </div>
                    </>
                  ) : null}
                </div>
              );
            })}
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** One effect focuses the new cell after a keyboard move and returns nothing; there are no listeners, timers or observers outside React handlers. Formatters are cached in a module-level map.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing moves: paging swaps the cells instantly and focus jumps without scrolling animation. The only transitions are 150ms colour changes on "+N more" (dropped under `motion-reduce`) and the kit chip hover brightness and selection ring, which change no position or size.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Importing `compareDate` from @internationalized/date. It is not exported from the package entry; use `a.compare(b)` on the dates instead.
- Handling arrow keys for every keydown in the grid. React bubbles events from portaled popovers through their React parent, so a popover opened from a chip would move the grid focus; check that the target is a gridcell.
- Making every cell and chip tabbable. 42 cells and their chips turn Tab into a trap; keep one tab stop and move it with the arrows.
- Calling `.focus()` right after changing the month. The new cell is not in the DOM yet; set the focused day and focus it in an effect after the render.
- Formatting weekday names from a local `Date`. Server and browser zones can disagree about the day; the grid formats a fixed UTC noon built from the calendar fields.

## Notes

- Clicking a muted outside day selects it without turning the month; arrowing onto it does turn the month, as a focused cell must stay in the visible month to keep the tab stop predictable.
- `eventsOnDay(events, day)` is exported and uses the same multi-day and midnight rules, for agenda or side panels.
- Pass `selectedEventId` to ring the chip whose popover is open.
- Multi-day events render a chip on every day they touch. When wrapping chips in popovers, key the open state on the event and the `day` argument, or one click opens a popover per day.

## Definition of done

August 2026 opens with Jul 26 to Sep 5 in six rows, July and September days muted with their Coffee, Payday and Payday chips still coloured. Thursday the 20th shows a selected pill, two chips and "+4 more"; the side panel lists its six events. Clicking a cell moves the pill and the panel. With a cell focused, ArrowRight / ArrowDown move by a day and a week, Page Down turns to September and focuses the same date, and Page Up returns. Holidays repeats on the 11th to 13th. Clicking a chip opens its details popover; Delete removes it, updates "+N more" and offers Undo. At 360px the cells show colour dots.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Letter Scramble

Every character flips through a handful of wrong glyphs and then lands on the right one, each character starting a tenth of a second after the one before it, so the resolution sweeps left to right across the word. Each successive flip is held slightly longer than the last, which is what makes it read as settling rather than as a spinner that was switched off. Character widths are frozen to their final glyph before the first substitution, so the word does not breathe while it scrambles.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A word assembles out of noise — each character flips through wrong glyphs, decelerating onto the right one.

- Category: text
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. The word is split in JSX to one `inline-block` span per character, each carrying `data-final` with its resolved glyph. React owns every node; nothing is injected into the DOM.
2. A single `gsap.timeline` schedules `tl.call()` at absolute times. For character `i` the start time is `START_DELAY + i * stagger`; for flip `f` the time advances by `baseFlip + f * flipGrowth`, so hold durations grow 0.08, 0.105, 0.13, 0.155 … That arithmetic progression is the deceleration.
3. Each `call` assigns `c.textContent = randomGlyph`. After the last flip a final `call` writes `c.dataset.final`, and a `fromTo(c, { opacity: DIM }, { opacity: 1, duration: settle, ease: "power3.out" })` runs at the same time — the fade is what separates "resolved" from "one more wrong glyph".
4. Glyphs come from a seeded PRNG (`createRng(seed ?? text + ":" + run)` and `randInt`), never `Math.random`. The glyph sequence decides what is painted on the first client frame, and a server/client disagreement about that is a hydration mismatch.
5. Before the timeline is built, every character box is pinned with `c.style.width = getBoundingClientRect().width + "px"`, measured from the *final* glyph that is currently in the DOM. Proportional type gives `i` and `W` wildly different advance widths, so an unpinned word visibly breathes and every element after it on the line shudders in sympathy. A final `tl.call` at position `">"` clears the widths so the word reflows normally afterwards.
6. The whole build is deferred behind `document.fonts.ready`, because measuring before the webfont lands pins every box to a fallback-font width.
7. The real word is rendered once in an `sr-only` span and the animated characters are `aria-hidden`, since mid-flight they are literal garbage.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `GLYPHS = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789#%&@$*'`
  The substitution pool. Uppercase and figures keep the visual weight even; adding lowercase mixes x-height and cap-height so the word appears to jitter vertically as well as horizontally. The punctuation adds texture without introducing very narrow glyphs.
- `FLIPS = 7`
  Wrong glyphs per character before resolving. Below ~4 there is no sense of searching; past ~10 the tail characters of a long word are still churning after the reader has looked away.
- `STAGGER = 0.1`
  Seconds between adjacent characters starting. Roughly the flip interval, so the sweep front is a couple of characters wide. Much smaller and the whole word scrambles as a block, losing the left-to-right read.
- `BASE_FLIP = 0.08`
  Seconds the first wrong glyph is held. About five frames at 60Hz — fast enough to be a blur, slow enough that the substitution is not skipped entirely on a slow frame.
- `FLIP_GROWTH = 0.025`
  Seconds added to each successive hold. This is the deceleration and it is the whole character of the effect: at 0 the flipping is constant-interval and reads as a slot machine that stopped, rather than as a search converging.
- `SETTLE = 0.45`
  Seconds of the opacity fade landing with the final glyph. Long enough to be a distinct beat after 0.08s flips; a shorter fade is indistinguishable from another substitution.
- `DIM = 0.35`
  Opacity the settle fade starts from. Fading from 0 makes the character disappear for a frame between the last wrong glyph and the right one, which reads as a dropped frame.
- `START_DELAY = 0.25`
  Seconds before the first character begins. Gives the page a moment to settle, so the scramble is not competing with layout for the reader's attention.
- `VIEW_THRESHOLD = 0.4`
  Fraction visible before the timeline runs, so a headline low on the page has actually arrived before it scrambles.

## API

```ts
function LetterScramble(props: { text: string; glyphs?: string; flips?: number; stagger?: number; baseFlip?: number; flipGrowth?: number; settle?: number; replayOnHover?: boolean; startOnView?: boolean; seed?: number | string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `text: string`
  The resolved word. Rendered as-is for SSR, reduced motion, and assistive technology.
- `glyphs: string` — default `'A-Z0-9#%&@$*'`
  Substitution pool. Keep to glyphs of similar visual weight.
- `flips: number` — default `7`
  Wrong glyphs shown per character before it resolves.
- `stagger: number` — default `0.1`
  Seconds between adjacent characters starting.
- `baseFlip: number` — default `0.08`
  Seconds the first wrong glyph is held.
- `flipGrowth: number` — default `0.025`
  Seconds added to each successive hold. This is the deceleration.
- `settle: number` — default `0.45`
  Seconds of the fade that lands with the final glyph.
- `replayOnHover: boolean` — default `true`
  Re-run on pointer enter, on fine pointers only.
- `startOnView: boolean` — default `true`
  Run when scrolled into view rather than on mount.
- `seed: number | string`
  Any string or number. The same seed gives the same sequence on every render.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the outer span via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const GLYPHS = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789#%&@$*';
const FLIPS = 7;
const STAGGER = 0.1;
const BASE_FLIP = 0.08;
const FLIP_GROWTH = 0.025;
const SETTLE = 0.45;
const START_DELAY = 0.25;
const DIM = 0.35;
const VIEW_THRESHOLD = 0.4;

export function LetterScramble({
  text,
  glyphs = GLYPHS,
  flips = FLIPS,
  stagger = STAGGER,
  baseFlip = BASE_FLIP,
  flipGrowth = FLIP_GROWTH,
  settle = SETTLE,
  replayOnHover = true,
  startOnView = true,
  seed,
  className,
}: LetterScrambleProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const { inView } = useInView(root, { threshold: VIEW_THRESHOLD, once: true });
  const [run, setRun] = useState(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = root.current;
    if (!el || reduced) return;
    if (startOnView && !inView) return;

    const chars = Array.from(el.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-char]'));
    if (chars.length === 0 || glyphs.length === 0) return;

    // Seeded, never Math.random: the glyph sequence decides what is painted
    // on the first client frame, and a server/client disagreement about that
    // is a hydration mismatch.
    const rng = createRng(seed ?? `${text}:${run}`);

    let cancelled = false;
    let tl: gsap.core.Timeline | null = null;

    const restore = () => {
      for (const c of chars) {
        c.textContent = c.dataset.final ?? '';
        c.style.width = '';
        c.style.opacity = '';
      }
    };

    const build = () => {
      if (cancelled) return;

      // Measured after fonts are ready, and measured from the *final* glyph,
      // which is what is in the DOM right now. Measuring a substituted glyph
      // would lock in the wrong box.
      for (const c of chars) {
        c.style.width = `${c.getBoundingClientRect().width}px`;
      }

      tl = gsap.timeline();

      chars.forEach((c, i) => {
        const final = c.dataset.final ?? '';
        let t = START_DELAY + i * stagger;

        for (let f = 0; f < flips; f += 1) {
          const g = glyphs.charAt(randInt(rng, 0, glyphs.length));
          tl?.call(
            () => {
              c.textContent = g;
            },
            undefined,
            t,
          );
          t += baseFlip + f * flipGrowth;
        }

        tl?.call(
          () => {
            c.textContent = final;
          },
          undefined,
          t,
        );
        // The fade is what separates "resolved" from "one more wrong glyph".
        tl?.fromTo(
          c,
          { opacity: DIM },
          { opacity: 1, duration: settle, ease: 'power3.out' },
          t,
        );
      });

      // Release the frozen widths once nothing is substituting any more, so
      // the word reflows normally if the viewport or the font changes later.
      tl?.call(
        () => {
          for (const c of chars) c.style.width = '';
        },
        undefined,
        '>',
      );
    };

    // Splitting or measuring before the webfont lands measures the fallback,
    // and every character box is then frozen to the wrong width.
    void document.fonts.ready.then(build);

    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
      tl?.kill();
      restore();
    };
  }, [
    text,
    glyphs,
    flips,
    stagger,
    baseFlip,
    flipGrowth,
    settle,
    seed,
    startOnView,
    inView,
    reduced,
    run,
  ]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** A `cancelled` flag guards the async `document.fonts.ready` boundary so a build cannot start after unmount. Teardown kills the timeline and then restores every character: `textContent` back to `data-final`, and `style.width` and `style.opacity` cleared. Without that restore, unmounting mid-scramble would leave the word frozen as garbage inside pinned boxes.

**Reduced motion.** The effect returns before building anything, so the word stays exactly as React rendered it — the resolved text, at full opacity, on first paint. Hover replay is also disabled. Nothing is scrambled, hidden, or left mid-substitution.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using `Math.random()` for the glyph sequence. The server and the client pick different glyphs, React reports a hydration mismatch, and the first frame flickers as the tree is patched.
- Not freezing the character widths. Every substitution changes the advance width, so the word pulses and everything after it on the line jitters for the whole animation.
- Measuring those widths before `document.fonts.ready`. Each box is then pinned to a fallback-font width, and when the real font arrives the glyphs are clipped or swimming inside boxes that are visibly the wrong size — the same failure mode described in `font-safe-text-split`.
- Measuring the width of a substituted glyph rather than the final one. The box is locked to the wrong character forever.
- Never releasing the frozen widths. The word cannot reflow on a viewport change or a late font swap, so it breaks out of its container at narrow widths.
- Constant-interval flipping. Without the growing hold the effect reads as a slot machine that was switched off rather than as a search that converged.
- Leaving the scrambling characters in the accessibility tree. A screen reader announces the random glyphs as they change; the real word must be exposed separately and the animated spans hidden.
- Re-running the effect from a `Math.random`-seeded value or an inline callback prop. The dependency array must contain only stable values or the scramble restarts on every parent render.

## Notes

- The original technique used GSAP MorphSVGPlugin to morph hand-drawn letter paths into random variants. MorphSVG is a paid GSAP Club plugin, so this is the dependency-free equivalent: character substitution from a glyph set on a per-character timeline, preserving the two things that actually make the original read the way it does — the 0.1s stagger and the `0.08 + n * 0.025` deceleration.
- No text-splitting library either. The split is declarative JSX; `SplitText` is reserved for the components whose subject is SplitText itself.
- Hover replay is gated on `(pointer: fine)` and on reduced motion being off — on touch there is no hover, so it would only fire on press and read as a glitch.

## Definition of done

On entering the viewport each character flips through several wrong glyphs and lands on the right one, left to right. Time the flips: the last is visibly slower than the first. The word occupies exactly the same width throughout, and nothing on the same line moves. Reload repeatedly with a fixed `seed` and the identical glyph sequence appears every time, with no hydration warning in the console. Unmount mid-scramble and remount, and the word is correct. With reduced motion enabled the resolved word is present on first paint.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Most Active Days Card

A grey dashboard card with the visible month's step total, a month pill with previous and next arrows, and a fixed-height white panel that scrolls through all twelve months of the year. Every day is a numbered cell with a 26px stack of three concentric progress rings; days after "today" show faded empty tracks and cannot be picked. Scrolling updates the pill and the total to the month in view, the arrows scroll smoothly to the neighbouring month, and picking a day (click or arrow keys) reports it so a paired Activity Rings Card can show that day.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A scrolling year calendar where each day is a mini activity ring, with a month pill that follows the scroll and selectable days.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @internationalized/date@^3.12.4, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. One memoised pass builds the year: for each month, `getDaysInMonth` gives the day count, each `CalendarDate` gets its data from `getActivity` (default `sampleDayActivity`, seeded by `createRng(date.toString())` so every date is stable across renders and server/client), and each month sums `steps` for days on or before `today` into its total.
2. Each month is a section with a sticky 44px heading ("Jul") over a 7-column grid of day buttons that simply runs 1–7, 8–14 and so on, like the reference, rather than aligning to weekdays. A cell is 42×74px: the number above `MiniActivityRings`, an SVG where each ring is a tinted track (ring colour mixed 22% into `--color-chart-track`) plus a `pathLength={100}` arc with `stroke-dasharray: pct 100`, rotated -90° to start at twelve o'clock.
3. Scroll-spy: the scroller's `onScroll` schedules one `requestAnimationFrame`, which picks the last month section whose `offsetTop` is at or above `scrollTop + 35%` of the viewport (or December once the scroll is at the end). That month names the pill and its total; both are keyed spans, so `.animate-number-fade` replays as the label walks along.
4. The arrows call `scrollTo({ top: section.offsetTop })` on the scroller (smooth, or instant under reduced motion) and let the spy update the label as the scroll passes. On mount, and again whenever `height` changes, an isomorphic layout effect sets `scrollTop` to the focused day's month (the selection, else `today`) and reveals that day before paint.
5. Selection is controlled (`selected` + `onSelectedChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultSelected`, else `today`). Day buttons use a roving tabindex: arrow keys move ±1 or ±7 days, Home and End go to the month's first and last day, Page Up and Page Down move a month, clamped to January 1 and `today`; the focused button is revealed inside the scroller (never the page) below the sticky heading. Enter or Space picks it.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `RING_SIZE / RING_STROKE / RING_GAP = 26px / 2.75px / 1px`
  Three rings fit in a day cell with a visible hole in the middle and still read as separate bands at a glance.
- `HEADING_H = 44px`
  Height of the sticky month heading; a revealed day is kept below it so keyboard focus never hides under "Jul".
- `SPY_LINE = 0.35`
  The pill switches once the next month's heading is a third of the way up the panel, so the label changes while that month is clearly arriving rather than at the very top.
- `height = 232px`
  Shows two full weeks of cells and the start of a third, which hints that the panel scrolls.

## API

```ts

function MiniActivityRings(props: { rings: ActivityRing[]; empty?: boolean; size?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element

```

- `title: string` — default `"Most active days"`
  Header label.
- `totalLabel: string` — default `"total steps"`
  Unit after the month total.
- `year: number` — default `today.year`
  Year on show; all twelve months scroll in one column.
- `today: CalendarDate` — default `parseDate("2026-07-10")`
  Later days are empty and disabled, and totals stop here.
- `getActivity: (date: CalendarDate) => DayActivity` — default `sampleDayActivity`
  Steps and ring values per day.

  Controlled selected day.
- `defaultSelected: CalendarDate | null` — default `today`
  Uncontrolled initial selection.
- `onSelectedChange: (date: CalendarDate) => void`
  Called when a day is picked by click, Enter or Space.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Scroll the calendar so `el` sits fully below the sticky month heading.
const reveal = (el: HTMLElement, behavior: ScrollBehavior) => {
  const scroller = scrollerRef.current;
  if (!scroller) return;
  const top = el.offsetTop - HEADING_H;
  const bottom = el.offsetTop + el.offsetHeight + 8;
  if (top < scroller.scrollTop) scroller.scrollTo({ top, behavior });
  else if (bottom > scroller.scrollTop + scroller.clientHeight)
    scroller.scrollTo({ top: bottom - scroller.clientHeight, behavior });
};

// Scroll-spy: the month whose top has passed SPY_LINE of the viewport names the pill.
const spy = () => {
  const scroller = scrollerRef.current;
  if (!scroller) return;
  const atEnd = scroller.scrollTop + scroller.clientHeight >= scroller.scrollHeight - 1;
  const line = scroller.scrollTop + scroller.clientHeight * SPY_LINE;
  let month = 1;
  monthRefs.current.forEach((section, i) => {
    if (section && section.offsetTop <= line) month = i + 1;
  });
  setVisibleMonth(atEnd ? 12 : month);
};

const onScroll = () => {
  cancelAnimationFrame(spyFrame.current);
  spyFrame.current = requestAnimationFrame(spy);
};

const goToMonth = (month: number) => {
  const section = monthRefs.current[month - 1];
  const scroller = scrollerRef.current;
  if (!section || !scroller) return;
  scroller.scrollTo({ top: section.offsetTop, behavior: reduced ? "auto" : "smooth" });
};
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The pending scroll-spy animation frame is cancelled on every new scroll event and on unmount. Scrolling, clicks and keys use React event props, so there are no listeners to remove.

**Reduced motion.** With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the month arrows and keyboard reveal scroll instantly instead of smoothly, the pill label and total no longer fade in (`motion-reduce:animate-none`), and the cell hover and selection border changes are instant.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using `scrollIntoView` to reveal the focused day. In a preview frame or a scrolled page it also scrolls every ancestor; setting `scrollTop` on the panel only moves the calendar.
- Setting the pill label straight from the arrow click. The spy would then flip it back for a few frames while the smooth scroll is still short of the line; letting the spy own the label keeps it in step with what is on screen.
- Passing a fresh `CalendarDate` for `today` each render rebuilds the whole year. The memo is keyed on `today.toString()` so equal dates reuse it.

## Notes

- Exports `MostActiveDaysCard`, `MiniActivityRings`, `sampleDayActivity`, `formatLongDate` and the `DayActivity` type (`{ steps, rings: ActivityRing[] }`). The rings use the `ActivityRing` shape from the Activity Rings Card, so a day's rings can be passed straight to it.
- The demo pairs the two cards: the selected day drives the Activity Rings Card's title ("Activity for July 10, 2026") and rings, which glide to the new values. On screens under 640px the demo stacks the cards and passes a 168px calendar `height` and a 120px ring `size` so both fit.

## Definition of done

The default card reads "Most active days", "39,919 total steps" and a pill showing "July", with the panel opened on July: days 1–10 have three-colour mini rings, 11–31 are faded empty tracks and disabled, and the 10th has a grey outline. Clicking the next arrow scrolls smoothly to August and the pill then reads "August" with a total of 0; scrolling back up changes it to "July" again. Clicking July 3 outlines it and fires `onSelectedChange` (in the demo the Activity card title becomes "Activity for July 3, 2026" and its rings move); with July 3 focused, Arrow Right moves focus to July 4 and Arrow Down to July 10, but not past it.

# Build: Multi Agent Chat

A full multi-agent chat for a 1280 × 800 frame. The left card lists conversations with stacked agent avatars, a marketplace button, support, settings and a workspace switcher. The middle pane is the open conversation: send one message and every agent in it answers in turn, each thinking for a moment before its reply streams in. The right panel edits any agent with the full agent creator, creates new ones, browses the workspace file tree with who last touched each file, and shows the progress of the current round of replies.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A group chat with a team of agents who reply in turn, plus a workspace switcher and a panel to edit agents and browse files.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. All state lives in `MultiAgentChat`: agents, conversations, workspaces, the open conversation, the single active run, the last run per conversation, the side panel tab and the open modal. The conversation view and side panel are controlled components in their own files.
2. A run is `{ queue, index, phase, full, shown, paused }`. One effect keyed on the run arms one timeout: thinking waits on the agent's model (500, 900 or 1600ms, scaled by the composer model), streaming appends a chunk every 24ms scaled by the agent's speed, and a finished reply holds 380ms, is committed to the conversation and hands the turn to the next agent. Cleanup clears that timeout, so Stop, Pause, deleting the chat or unmounting never leaves a callback.
3. The run lives in the page, not the conversation, so it keeps going while another conversation is open. That conversation's list row says who is replying and collects unread replies, and other composers stay disabled until the round ends.
4. Each reply is written by `replyFor` from the agent's role label, the prompt and a counter, so the same agent answers differently on each turn. Plan mode in the composer makes every agent say it changed nothing.
5. The participant row above the composer toggles agents in and out of the open conversation; the next round only queues the agents still in it. Clicking an agent avatar in the thread, or a file owner in the Files tab, opens that agent in the editor.
6. Edits in the agent editor update the agent everywhere at once, because messages store only the agent id. The editor snapshots the agent on open and remounts after Save so its Reset returns to the saved version.
7. The Activity tab drives the run through `AgentDetailPanel`: Pause holds the current timer off, Resume re-arms it, Stop keeps the partial reply, and Run again replays the last prompt with the same agents.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `THINK_MS = swift 500ms, balanced 900ms, deep 1600ms`
  Deeper models visibly think longer, so a mixed team answers at different rhythms instead of in lockstep.
- `MODEL_PACE = Swift 2 Mini 0.5, Swift 2 1, Deep 1 1.6`
  The composer's model choice scales every agent's thinking so it has a felt effect.
- `stream tick = 3 characters every 24ms times the agent speed`
  About 125 characters a second at speed 1; a three-agent round finishes in under ten seconds.
- `HAND_OFF_MS = 380ms`
  A short beat on each finished reply makes the change of speaker readable.
- `side panel width = 356px`
  Fits the agent creator's pickers while leaving about 600px for the conversation next to the 272px list.

## API

```ts
function MultiAgentChat(props: MultiAgentChatProps): JSX.Element
interface MultiAgentChatProps { agents?: MacAgent[]; conversations?: MacConversation[]; workspaces?: Workspace[]; defaultWorkspaceId?: string; defaultConversationId?: string; className?: string }
```

- `agents: MacAgent[]` — default `MAC_AGENTS`
  The team: each agent is an AgentDraft with an id.
- `conversations: MacConversation[]` — default `MAC_CONVERSATIONS`
  Seed conversations; each names its workspace, its agents and its messages.
- `workspaces: Workspace[]` — default `MAC_WORKSPACES`
  Workspaces offered by the switcher.
- `defaultWorkspaceId: string` — default `"board"`
  Workspace selected on first render.
- `defaultConversationId: string` — default `"group"`
  Conversation open on first render.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root, which is h-full w-full.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// One timeout at a time drives the run. Thinking waits on the agent's model,
// streaming appends a chunk per tick, and a finished reply is committed to
// the conversation before the next agent in the queue starts thinking.
// Every change to the run re-arms the effect, so cleanup always clears the
// only pending timer: Stop, Pause, deleting the chat or unmounting is safe.
useEffect(() => {
  if (!run || run.paused) return;
  const agent = agents.find((a) => a.id === run.queue[run.index]);
  const advance = () => {
    const index = run.index + 1;
    if (index < run.queue.length) {
      record(run, index, "running");
      setRun({ ...run, index, phase: "thinking", full: "", shown: 0 });
    } else {
      record(run, run.queue.length, "done");
      setRun(null);
    }
  };
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;
  if (!agent) {
    timer = setTimeout(advance, 0);
  } else if (run.phase === "thinking") {
    timer = setTimeout(() => {
      const full = replyFor(agent, run.prompt, run.id + run.index, run.plan);
      setRun({ ...run, phase: "streaming", full, shown: reduced ? full.length : 0 });
    }, (THINK_MS[agent.model] ?? 900) * run.pace);
  } else if (run.shown < run.full.length) {
    const step = Math.max(1, Math.round(CHUNK * Number(agent.speed || 1)));
    timer = setTimeout(() => setRun({ ...run, shown: Math.min(run.full.length, run.shown + step) }), TICK_MS);
  } else {
    timer = setTimeout(() => {
      commit(run, run.full);
      advance();
    }, HAND_OFF_MS);
  }
  return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  // record and commit only read state through setters and refs.
  // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
}, [run, agents, reduced]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The single run timeout is cleared on every run change, on pause and on unmount. The share and support copied-state timers clear on unmount.

**Reduced motion.** Under reduced motion each reply appears whole once its agent has thought, avatars stop floating and blinking, the thinking label drops its shimmer, and hover transitions use motion-reduce:transition-none. Turn-taking and its timing stay so the order of speakers is still readable.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Running replies inside the conversation component. Switching conversations would unmount it and drop the round; the page owns the run and passes the live reply only to the conversation it belongs to.
- Storing agent names or colours on messages. Renaming an agent would leave old messages stale; messages keep the agent id and look the agent up at render.
- Passing the live agent as the creator's default. Its Reset would revert to whatever was typed last; snapshot on open and remount on Save.
- Letting a deleted or cleared conversation keep its run. The timer would commit a reply into a conversation that no longer has it; both actions end the run first.

## Notes

- Replies are canned and local: nothing is sent anywhere. The share link, support address and workspace data are fictional.
- Adding a bot from the marketplace also adds it to the open conversation and opens it in the editor.

## Definition of done

At 1280 × 800 a conversation list, a conversation and a side panel fill the frame. Typing a message and pressing Enter adds a bubble, then each agent in the conversation thinks and replies in turn. Toggling an agent in the participant row removes it from the next round. The Files tab shows the workspace tree and who last edited each file; the Activity tab pauses, stops and replays the round. Renaming an agent in the editor renames it in the thread. The workspace switcher swaps the conversation list, and the marketplace adds a bot to the team.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Multipass Offscreen Composite

A hero field built the way a compositor builds one: a background ramp and three additive gradient fills are accumulated into an offscreen target, a bright-pass and blur run into a second target at half size, and a final pass adds them together with a vignette and a dither. The canvas is written exactly once, by the last pass. It is a small piece of art in its own right and a complete, disposable template for any offscreen chain.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Four passes into two render targets — ramp, additive fills, half-size bloom — and one composite that writes the canvas once.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1

## How it works

1. Passes 1 and 2 share one target. `renderer.autoClear = false` is set at construction, the scene target is cleared explicitly once with `renderer.clear(true, false, false)`, and the ramp and the fills are then rendered back to back. The absence of a clear between those two renders is the entire composite.
2. The ramp is a clip-space quad. Each fragment projects onto the ramp axis with `dot(uv - 0.5, dir) / (abs(dir.x) + abs(dir.y)) + 0.5`; the divisor is the largest that projection can reach inside the unit square, so the ramp reaches its end colour exactly at the far corner for any angle rather than saturating early.
3. The fills are three `PlaneGeometry(1, 1)` meshes in one rotated group, each drawn with a Gaussian falloff `exp(-d * d * uSoftness)` and `AdditiveBlending`. They travel around ellipses of different radii at speeds of 0.05, -0.08 and 0.11 revolutions per second, so the arrangement takes about 200 seconds to return to its start.
4. Both targets are `HalfFloatType`. Three additive fills overlap well past 1.0, and on an unsigned-byte target that overlap clips flat before the bright-pass runs — the bloom would then be told the image is uniformly hot wherever any two fills cross.
5. Pass 3 renders into a target at `bloomScale` (0.5) of the scene target. The bright-pass is a soft knee, `smoothstep(uThreshold, uThreshold + 0.25, luma)`, and the blur is a 3x3 tent with weights 4 / 2 / 1 normalised by 16. Its offsets are measured in the half-size target's texels, so the blur reaches twice as far across the image for the same nine taps.
6. Pass 4 reads both targets, adds `bloom * uBloomStrength`, multiplies by a vignette measured in a square space so it stays circular in a wide box, and adds triangular-PDF dither — the difference of two hashes, about 1/255 — to break the 8-bit banding a smooth ramp otherwise shows as hard contour lines.
7. Resizing calls `setSize` on both targets and rewrites `uResolution` and the bloom `uTexel`. Nothing is reallocated, and because no pass reads its own previous contents there is no clear-and-settle: the next frame redraws all four passes from scratch.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `renderer.autoClear = false`
  The one line that makes multipass possible in three. Left at its default, every `render()` clears its target first, so pass 2 wipes pass 1 and the layering silently collapses into whatever was drawn last — with no error and no warning.
- `bloomScale = 0.5`
  Quarter the pixels for the blur pass, and the tent's texel-sized offsets cover twice the distance. Below about 0.35 the half-resolution grid becomes visible as a soft blockiness in the upsample; at 1.0 the pass costs four times as much for a tighter, less useful glow.
- `BLOOM_RADIUS = 1.4`
  Tap spacing in bloom-target texels, so 2.8 scene pixels. Above roughly 2 the nine taps no longer overlap and the tent starts sampling a sparse grid, which shows up as a faint cross-shaped ringing around bright cores.
- `bloomThreshold = 0.34`
  Luma where the bright-pass starts. The ramp peaks near 0.18, so this sits above the background and below the fills: the glow comes from the lights, not from the whole frame. Drop it under the ramp and the bloom becomes a flat wash that just raises exposure.
- `knee width = 0.25`
  The smoothstep span above the threshold. With a hard step, a pixel pops into the bright set the instant it crosses the cut, so the bloom boundary crawls as the fills drift — the most common giveaway of a hand-rolled bloom.
- `DISC_SOFTNESS = 3.1`
  The k in `exp(-d*d*k)`, which puts the fill at 4.5% of peak at the edge of its own quad. Much lower and the Gaussian is still bright where the geometry stops, giving a visible square edge; much higher and the fill shrinks to a hard dot inside an oversized quad.
- `DITHER = 0.004`
  One 8-bit code. The ramp crosses only a few hundred codes over a thousand pixels, and without a sub-LSB perturbation that gradient bands into visible contour lines on any display. Larger values are perceptible as noise rather than as smoothness.
- `REVEAL_START / REVEAL_SPAN = 0.7 / 0.2`
  The source ties the fills to scroll with exactly this ramp: nothing until 70% of the progress, full by 90%, held after. The dead zone is deliberate — the ramp establishes the space first, and the light arrives as a separate event.
- `DISC_SQUASH / PLANE_TILT = 0.62 / -0.19 rad`
  The fills are round in their own plane; squashing them and rotating their shared group is what makes three moving blobs read as one ellipse seen at an angle instead of three unrelated circles.
- `STATIC_ELAPSED = 6.2 s`
  The frame drawn when motion is suppressed. At t = 0 all three fills sit at their starting phases; six seconds in, the composition is spread out and reads as a designed still rather than as a default state.
- `maxDpr = 2`
  Four full-screen passes are already 2.5 screens of fragments per frame (1 + 1 + 0.25 + 1). At a 3x backing store that is over twenty million fragment invocations per frame on a phone, for no visible gain over 2x.

## API

```ts
function MultipassOffscreenComposite(props: { reveal?: number; bloomStrength?: number; bloomThreshold?: number; bloomScale?: number; vignette?: number; drift?: number; rampAngle?: number; rampColors?: readonly [string, string, string]; fillColors?: readonly [string, string, string]; maxDpr?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `reveal: number` — default `1`
  Progress 0..1. The fills fade in between 0.7 and 0.9 and hold; the ramp is always drawn.
- `bloomStrength: number` — default `0.85`
  How much of the blurred bright-pass is added back in the composite.
- `bloomThreshold: number` — default `0.34`
  Luminance where the bright-pass begins to contribute, with a 0.25 knee above it.
- `bloomScale: number` — default `0.5`
  Bloom target size relative to the scene target. Changing it rebuilds both targets.
- `vignette: number` — default `0.38`
  Corner darkening in the composite, 0..1.
- `drift: number` — default `1`
  Multiplier on the fills' orbital speeds. 0 freezes them without stopping the passes.
- `rampAngle: number` — default `141`
  Ramp direction in degrees, counter-clockwise from +x.
- `rampColors: readonly [string, string, string]` — default `['#0a0f1a', '#16283c', '#070a12']`
  Start, bend and end stops of the background ramp.
- `fillColors: readonly [string, string, string]` — default `['#3f7ae0', '#2fd0b4', '#a866f0']`
  Colours of the three additive fills, largest first.
- `maxDpr: number` — default `2`
  Backing-store cap. Both targets follow the drawing buffer.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the host element via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function MultipassOffscreenComposite({
  reveal = 1,
  bloomStrength = 0.85,
  bloomThreshold = 0.34,
  bloomScale = 0.5,
  vignette = 0.38,
  drift = 1,
  rampAngle = 141,
  rampColors = RAMP_COLORS,
  fillColors = FILL_COLORS,
  maxDpr = 2,
  className,
}: MultipassOffscreenCompositeProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const { inView } = useInView(host, { threshold: 0 });
  const visible = useVisibility();
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  const [supported, setSupported] = useState(true);
  useEffect(() => setSupported(hasWebGL()), []);

  /* Everything that only feeds a uniform lives here and is read inside the
     draw loop. None of it belongs in the effect's dependency list: rebuilding
     two render targets because a vignette changed by 0.01 would drop frames. */
  const live = useRef({ reveal, bloomStrength, bloomThreshold, vignette, drift });
  live.current = { reveal, bloomStrength, bloomThreshold, vignette, drift };

  const ready = width > 1 && height > 1 && supported;

  /* Joined, not spread. Array props are compared by identity, so an inline
     literal would be a new value every render and the effect would thrash. */
  const colorKey = `${rampColors.join('|')}/${fillColors.join('|')}`;

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready) return;

    let renderer: THREE.WebGLRenderer;
    try {
      renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({
        antialias: false,
        // Opaque. Pass 4 covers every pixel with alpha 1, so an alpha channel
        // would only cost bandwidth and force the compositor to blend.
        alpha: false,
        depth: false,
        stencil: false,
      });
    } catch {
      // A context can still be refused between the probe and the construction —
      // the tab may have hit the browser's live-context ceiling in between. three
      // throws rather than returning null, and an uncaught throw here takes the
      // page with it.
      setSupported(false);
      return;
    }
    renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio(maxDpr));
    renderer.setSize(el.clientWidth, el.clientHeight, false);
    renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 1);
    // The single most important line in the file. See the header.
    renderer.autoClear = false;
    renderer.domElement.style.display = 'block';
    renderer.domElement.style.width = '100%';
    renderer.domElement.style.height = '100%';
    el.appendChild(renderer.domElement);

    const buffer = new THREE.Vector2();
    renderer.getDrawingBufferSize(buffer);
    const bufferW = Math.max(2, Math.round(buffer.x));
    const bufferH = Math.max(2, Math.round(buffer.y));
    const bloomW = Math.max(2, Math.round(bufferW * bloomScale));
    const bloomH = Math.max(2, Math.round(bufferH * bloomScale));

    const sceneTarget = makeTarget(bufferW, bufferH);
    const bloomTarget = makeTarget(bloomW, bloomH);

    // Two cameras. The flat one is for the clip-space quads, whose vertex
    // shader ignores both matrices; the ortho one gives the fills a stable
    // -aspect..aspect x -1..1 space to move in.
    const flatCamera = new THREE.Camera();
    const contentCamera = new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0, 10);
    contentCamera.position.z = 1;

    const flatGeometry = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(2, 2);
    const discGeometry = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(1, 1);

    const [rampA = '#000000', rampB = '#000000', rampC = '#000000'] = rampColors;
    const rampUniforms: RampUniforms = {
      uResolution: { value: new THREE.Vector2(bufferW, bufferH) },
      uAngle: { value: (rampAngle * Math.PI) / 180 },
      uColorA: { value: new THREE.Color(rampA) },
      uColorB: { value: new THREE.Color(rampB) },
      uColorC: { value: new THREE.Color(rampC) },
    };
    const rampMaterial = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader: MULTIPASS_FLAT_VERT,
      fragmentShader: MULTIPASS_RAMP_FRAG,
      uniforms: rampUniforms,
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
    });
    const rampScene = new THREE.Scene();
    const rampQuad = new THREE.Mesh(flatGeometry, rampMaterial);
    rampQuad.frustumCulled = false;
    rampScene.add(rampQuad);

    const fillScene = new THREE.Scene();
    // One group, rotated once: the fills share a plane, and tilting the group
    // is what makes their paths read as one ellipse seen at an angle rather
    // than three unrelated circles.
    const fillGroup = new THREE.Group();
    fillGroup.rotation.z = PLANE_TILT;
    fillScene.add(fillGroup);

    const discMaterials: THREE.ShaderMaterial[] = [];
    const discMeshes: THREE.Mesh[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < DISCS.length; i++) {
      const spec = DISCS[i];
      if (!spec) continue;
      const uniforms: DiscUniforms = {
        uColor: { value: new THREE.Color(fillColors[i] ?? '#ffffff') },
        uIntensity: { value: 0 },
        uSoftness: { value: DISC_SOFTNESS },
      };
      const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
        vertexShader: MULTIPASS_DISC_VERT,
        fragmentShader: MULTIPASS_DISC_FRAG,
        uniforms,
        transparent: true,
        blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending,
        depthTest: false,
        depthWrite: false,
      });
      const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(discGeometry, material);
      mesh.scale.set(spec.size, spec.size * DISC_SQUASH, 1);
      mesh.frustumCulled = false;
      fillGroup.add(mesh);
      discMaterials.push(material);
      discMeshes.push(mesh);
    }

    const bloomUniforms: BloomUniforms = {
      uSource: { value: sceneTarget.texture },
      uTexel: { value: new THREE.Vector2(1 / bloomW, 1 / bloomH) },
      uThreshold: { value: bloomThreshold },
      uRadius: { value: BLOOM_RADIUS },
    };
    const bloomMaterial = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader: MULTIPASS_FLAT_VERT,
      fragmentShader: MULTIPASS_BLOOM_FRAG,
      uniforms: bloomUniforms,
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
    });
    const bloomScene = new THREE.Scene();
    const bloomQuad = new THREE.Mesh(flatGeometry, bloomMaterial);
    bloomQuad.frustumCulled = false;
    bloomScene.add(bloomQuad);

    const compositeUniforms: CompositeUniforms = {
      uScene: { value: sceneTarget.texture },
      uBloom: { value: bloomTarget.texture },
      uResolution: { value: new THREE.Vector2(bufferW, bufferH) },
      uBloomStrength: { value: bloomStrength },
      uVignette: { value: vignette },
      uDither: { value: DITHER },
    };
    const compositeMaterial = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader: MULTIPASS_FLAT_VERT,
      fragmentShader: MULTIPASS_COMPOSITE_FRAG,
      uniforms: compositeUniforms,
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
    });
    const compositeScene = new THREE.Scene();
    const compositeQuad = new THREE.Mesh(flatGeometry, compositeMaterial);
    compositeQuad.frustumCulled = false;
    compositeScene.add(compositeQuad);

    stage.current = {
      resize(w, h) {
        renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio(maxDpr));
        renderer.setSize(w, h, false);
        renderer.getDrawingBufferSize(buffer);
        const bw = Math.max(2, Math.round(buffer.x));
        const bh = Math.max(2, Math.round(buffer.y));

        const aspect = w / h;
        contentCamera.left = -aspect;
        contentCamera.right = aspect;
        contentCamera.updateProjectionMatrix();

        // setSize, never new. Allocating a pair of half-float targets is a
        // synchronous driver call; doing it from a ResizeObserver during a
        // window drag is how a smooth resize turns into a slideshow — and the
        // old targets would leak unless every one of them were disposed.
        sceneTarget.setSize(bw, bh);
        rampUniforms.uResolution.value.set(bw, bh);
        compositeUniforms.uResolution.value.set(bw, bh);

        const sw = Math.max(2, Math.round(bw * bloomScale));
        const sh = Math.max(2, Math.round(bh * bloomScale));
        bloomTarget.setSize(sw, sh);
        // Texel size is per target, and this one is not the canvas. Leaving it
        // at the old size makes the blur radius drift with the window.
        bloomUniforms.uTexel.value.set(1 / sw, 1 / sh);
      },

      draw(elapsed) {
        const state = live.current;

        // The source ties the fills to scroll with exactly this ramp.
        const fade = clamp((state.reveal - REVEAL_START) / REVEAL_SPAN, 0, 1);

        for (let i = 0; i < discMeshes.length; i++) {
          const mesh = discMeshes[i];
          const spec = DISCS[i];
          const material = discMaterials[i];
          if (!mesh || !spec || !material) continue;
          const angle = spec.phase + elapsed * spec.speed * state.drift * Math.PI * 2;
          mesh.position.set(Math.cos(angle) * spec.radius, Math.sin(angle) * spec.radius, 0);
          const intensity = material.uniforms.uIntensity;
          if (intensity) intensity.value = spec.intensity * fade;
        }

        // Passes 1 and 2 — one clear, two renders. The absence of a clear
        // between them IS the composite.
        renderer.setRenderTarget(sceneTarget);
        renderer.clear(true, false, false);
        renderer.render(rampScene, flatCamera);
        renderer.render(fillScene, contentCamera);

        // Pass 3 — bright-pass and blur at bloomScale. Nothing accumulates, so
        // this target never needs to survive a frame.
        bloomUniforms.uThreshold.value = state.bloomThreshold;
        renderer.setRenderTarget(bloomTarget);
        renderer.clear(true, false, false);
        renderer.render(bloomScene, flatCamera);

        // Pass 4 — the only write to the canvas.
        compositeUniforms.uBloomStrength.value = state.bloomStrength;
        compositeUniforms.uVignette.value = state.vignette;
        renderer.setRenderTarget(null);
        renderer.clear(true, false, false);
        renderer.render(compositeScene, flatCamera);
      },
    };

    stage.current.resize(el.clientWidth, el.clientHeight);
    stage.current.draw(0);

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      // Explicit, not disposeObject over the scenes: flatGeometry is shared by
      // three of them, and a traversal would dispose it three times.
      flatGeometry.dispose();
      discGeometry.dispose();
      rampMaterial.dispose();
      bloomMaterial.dispose();
      compositeMaterial.dispose();
      for (const material of discMaterials) material.dispose();
      // Both targets. Nothing walks a render target for you — each holds a
      // half-float texture and a framebuffer object.
      sceneTarget.dispose();
      bloomTarget.dispose();
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      renderer.domElement.remove();
    };
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [ready, colorKey, rampAngle, bloomScale, maxDpr]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const current = stage.current;
    if (!current || width < 1 || height < 1) return;
    current.resize(width, height);
    // No pass reads its own previous contents, so a resized target needs no
    // clear-and-settle — but a still frame does need redrawing, since resizing
    // a target discards what it held.
    if (reduced) current.draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);
  }, [width, height, reduced]);

  useRaf(
    (_dt, elapsed) => {
      stage.current?.draw(elapsed);
    },
    ready && inView && visible && !reduced,
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nulls the stage ref, disposes both `PlaneGeometry` instances, all six materials, and — separately, because nothing traverses them — both render targets. Then `disposeRenderer` performs `dispose` + `forceContextLoss` + a zeroed drawing buffer, and the canvas is removed from the DOM. The canvas is created inside the effect by three and appended per effect run, so a StrictMode remount builds a fresh context rather than reattaching the one that was just force-lost. `useRaf` releases its own subscription; the component adds no listeners of its own.

**Reduced motion.** The component reads `useReducedMotion` itself and never subscribes to rAF when it is set. All four passes still run, once, at a fixed elapsed of 6.2 seconds, and again after any resize — so the artwork is complete, correctly exposed and fully bloomed, it simply does not drift. A hero background is composition first and motion second; deleting it under reduced motion would leave a hole in the page, and freezing it at t = 0 would show an arrangement nobody designed.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Leaving `autoClear` at its default and wondering why only the last pass appears. Nothing errors; the ramp is simply gone, and the usual next move — reordering the renders — makes it worse.
- Setting `autoClear = false` and then forgetting to clear at all. The first target accumulates frame over frame, so the fills smear into permanent trails that look almost intentional for about two seconds.
- Recreating render targets in the resize handler. Allocating a pair of half-float framebuffers is a synchronous driver call; doing it on every ResizeObserver callback turns a window drag into a slideshow, and every previous pair leaks unless it is explicitly disposed.
- Disposing the renderer but not the targets. Render targets are not part of any scene graph, so nothing traverses them — each surviving one holds a full-resolution half-float texture plus a framebuffer object until the tab is closed.
- Using an 8-bit target for anything that feeds a bright-pass. Additive overlap clips at 1.0, so the bloom sees a plateau instead of a peak and the glow spreads uniformly across the crossing region.
- Premultiplying alpha in a shader that uses three's `AdditiveBlending`. That blend is already `(SrcAlpha, One)`, so multiplying in the shader squares the alpha and the fills all but vanish — then get "fixed" by tripling the intensity, which clips the cores.
- Reusing one `uTexel` or `uResolution` uniform across passes that render into differently sized targets. Everything looks right at one window size and the blur radius drifts as the window changes.
- Reading a colour buffer while it is still bound as the render target. It is undefined behaviour in WebGL and shows as tearing, black, or a correct image depending on the driver — which is why the bright-pass needs an offscreen target and cannot run on the canvas.
- Letting three convert colour space in the middle of the chain. Its output conversion is injected into built-in materials only, so a chain that mixes `ShaderMaterial` and `MeshBasicMaterial` converts at some passes and not others; this component uses `ShaderMaterial` everywhere and converts nowhere.

## Notes

- The renderer is created with `alpha: false`. Pass 4 covers every pixel at full alpha, so an alpha channel would only cost bandwidth and force the compositor to blend the canvas over the page.
- `reveal` is deliberately a plain number rather than an internal scroll listener. Drive it from whatever already tracks progress — `useInView`'s ratio, a scroll library, or a constant — and the component stays a renderer.
- The array props are compared through a joined string key, so passing an inline `[a, b, c]` literal does not tear down the GL stack on every render. Values that only feed a uniform (`reveal`, `bloomStrength`, `vignette`, `drift`) are read from a ref inside the draw loop and never appear in a dependency list.
- Geometries are disposed by hand rather than through `disposeObject` over each scene: the clip-space quad is shared by three scenes, and a traversal would dispose it three times.
- To extend the chain, add a target and a pass — the structure does not change. The costly mistakes are all in the two rules this file already follows: clear deliberately, and resize rather than reallocate.

## Definition of done

Three soft coloured lights drift across a dark angled ramp with a halo that is clearly wider and softer than the lights themselves, corners falling off, and no banding anywhere in the gradient — tilt a laptop screen and the ramp stays smooth. Resize the window continuously: the image tracks the box with no stutter, no flash of black, and the halo keeps the same apparent width. Set `reveal` to 0.5 and only the ramp is visible; sweep it to 1 and the lights come up over the last third. With reduced motion the full composition, bloom included, is present and still.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
