# Build: Notification

A card for one event (a deploy finished, someone commented, a build failed) with a round status icon or an avatar with presence, a title, timestamp, description, small action buttons and a close button. It can dismiss itself after a set time, showing a 3px countdown bar along its bottom edge that pauses and resumes with the timer. `NotificationViewport` portals a fixed stack to any corner or bottom/top centre, and cards entering or leaving it make the others glide into place on a spring.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Dismissible notification card with status icon or avatar, actions and a pausable countdown bar, stacked in a corner viewport.

- Category: overlay
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, motion@^12.43.0, react-aria@^3.53.1

## How it works

1. `Notification` keeps its own `dismissedState`, ORed with the `dismissed` prop, and renders a `motion.div` inside `AnimatePresence onExitComplete={onDismiss}`. Dismissing (close button, timer or `dismissed`) plays the exit (opacity 0, y 8, scale 0.96, `blur(3px)`, 0.18s easeOut) and only then calls `onDismiss`, so the parent removes the item after the card has gone. A ref marks the card dismissed at once: AnimatePresence keeps rendering the exiting element with its old handlers, so a second press of the close button during the exit does nothing instead of firing `onDismissStart` again.
2. The entrance plays only when `introDelay` is defined: `initial` is opacity 0, y 12, scale 0.97, `blur(4px)`, animating to rest over 0.25s easeOut after `introDelay` seconds. Without it, `initial={false}` renders the card in place.
3. With `autoDismissDuration`, the countdown bar is a native Web Animation (`element.animate` from `scaleX(1)` to `scaleX(0)`, linear, `fill: "forwards"`, delayed by the intro) on a `h-[3px] bg-accent-600` span anchored `origin-left` (`rtl:origin-right`). A second effect owns the timer: `remaining` starts at duration plus intro delay, and each run plays the bar and sets a timeout for `remaining`. On `paused` it pauses the bar, and its cleanup subtracts the elapsed time, so a held countdown resumes where it stopped.
4. The card is `relative flex items-start gap-3 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl border p-4 pe-11` on the primary background with `shadow-dropdown`; `pe-11` reserves room for the `xs` `CloseButton` at `top-3 end-3`. The visual is the avatar (36px Avatar forced to `size-10`, plus a 12px presence dot: lime online, rose busy, grey offline) or a 40px round badge with `icon ?? STATUS_ICON[status]` tinted by status. Actions are small Buttons; without a `variant`, the first is secondary and the rest primary.
5. The card's `role` defaults to "alert" for `status="error"` and "status" otherwise, so screen readers announce errors assertively and the rest politely.
6. `NotificationViewport` waits for hydration (`useSyncExternalStore` returns false on the server), then `createPortal`s a `motion.div layoutRoot` to React Aria's portal container (`useUNSAFE_PortalContext().getContainer`) or `document.body`. The layer is `pointer-events-none fixed z-100 w-[min(400px,calc(100vw-24px))] flex-col gap-3`, positioned 12px from the edges (24px from `sm`). Each child is wrapped in a `pointer-events-auto` `motion.div layout`, keyed by the child's key, inside `AnimatePresence initial={false} mode="popLayout"`, with a layout spring of stiffness 520, damping 42 and mass 0.7.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `layout spring = stiffness 520, damping 42, mass 0.7`
  Quick and almost without overshoot, so the rest of the stack closes the gap promptly when a card leaves without bouncing.
- `enter / exit = enter 0.25s: y 12, scale 0.97, blur 4px / exit 0.18s: y 8, scale 0.96, blur 3px`
  The exit is shorter than the entrance so a dismissed card gets out of the way faster than a new one arrives.
- `countdown bar = 3px, bg-accent-600, linear`
  Linear makes the bar's length a true reading of the time left; 3px is visible along the bottom edge without crowding the actions.
- `viewport width and inset = w-[min(400px,calc(100vw-24px))], 12px inset (24px from sm)`
  A comfortable width for a title, two-line description and actions, while keeping a 12px gutter on each side of a phone.
- `z-index = z-100`
  The overlay layer shared with Modal and Drawer, so notifications sit above page content.

## API

```ts
function Notification(props: Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "title" | "onDrag" | "onDragStart" | "onDragEnd" | "onAnimationStart" | "onAnimationEnd"> & { title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; timestamp?: ReactNode; status?: "neutral" | "information" | "success" | "error"; icon?: IconComponent; avatar?: Omit<AvatarProps, "size"> & { presence?: "online" | "busy" | "offline" }; actions?: { label: ReactNode; onClick?: () => void; variant?: ButtonProps["variant"] }[]; dismissible?: boolean; closeLabel?: string; onDismiss?: () => void; onDismissStart?: () => void; autoDismissDuration?: number; paused?: boolean; dismissed?: boolean; introDelay?: number; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function NotificationViewport(props: HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { children?: ReactNode; position?: NotificationPosition; placement?: "bottom-left" | "bottom-right" }): ReactPortal | null
```

- `title / description / timestamp: ReactNode`
  The card's copy; the timestamp sits after the title.
- `status: "neutral" | "information" | "success" | "error"` — default `"neutral"`
  Badge tint and default icon; "error" also makes the card an alert.
- `icon: IconComponent`
  Replaces the status icon.
- `avatar: AvatarProps & { presence?: "online" | "busy" | "offline" }`
  Shown instead of the icon, with an optional presence dot.
- `actions: { label; onClick?; variant? }[]`
  Small buttons under the message; first secondary, others primary by default.
- `dismissible / closeLabel: boolean / string` — default `true / "Dismiss notification"`
  Show the close button and name it.
- `autoDismissDuration: number (ms)`
  Dismiss after this long, with the countdown bar.
- `paused: boolean` — default `false`
  Hold the countdown and its bar.
- `dismissed: boolean` — default `false`
  Dismiss from outside; the exit plays, then `onDismiss` runs.
- `introDelay: number (s)`
  Enables the entrance animation, after this delay.
- `onDismiss: () => void`
  Called after the exit animation completes.
- `onDismissStart: () => void`
  Called once when the card closes itself (close button or countdown), as the exit starts.
- `NotificationViewport.position: NotificationPosition` — default `"bottom-end"`
  Corner or centre edge the stack is anchored to.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function Notification({
  title,
  description,
  timestamp,
  status = "neutral",
  icon,
  avatar,
  actions,
  dismissible = true,
  closeLabel = "Dismiss notification",
  onDismiss,
  onDismissStart,
  autoDismissDuration,
  paused = false,
  dismissed: dismissedProp = false,
  introDelay,
  className,
  ref,
  role,
  ...props
}: NotificationProps) {
  const [dismissedState, setDismissed] = useState(false);
  const dismissed = dismissedProp || dismissedState;
  // The countdown can fire long after the render that scheduled it, so it
  // reads the latest callback.
  const onDismissStartRef = useRef(onDismissStart);
  useEffect(() => {
    onDismissStartRef.current = onDismissStart;
  });
  // While a card exits, AnimatePresence keeps rendering its last element,
  // whose close button still holds this handler. The ref makes a second press
  // (or the countdown) during the exit a no-op instead of a second
  // onDismissStart.
  const dismissedRef = useRef(dismissed);
  useEffect(() => {
    dismissedRef.current = dismissed;
  });
  const dismiss = () => {
    if (dismissedRef.current) return;
    dismissedRef.current = true;
    setDismissed(true);
    onDismissStartRef.current?.();
  };
  const Icon = icon ?? STATUS_ICON[status];
  const hasIntro = introDelay !== undefined;
  const introDelayMs = (introDelay ?? 0) * 1000;
  const timed = Boolean(autoDismissDuration && autoDismissDuration > 0);

  // The countdown bar runs as one native Web Animation so `paused` can hold
  // and resume it in step with the timer below. (Motion's standalone
  // animate() on this child cancelled the card's own enter animation.)
  const barRef = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);
  const bar = useRef<Animation | null>(null);
  const remaining = useRef((autoDismissDuration ?? 0) + introDelayMs);

  useEffect(() => {
    const element = barRef.current;
    if (!timed || !element) return;
    bar.current = element.animate(
      [{ transform: "scaleX(1)" }, { transform: "scaleX(0)" }],
      { duration: autoDismissDuration, delay: introDelayMs, easing: "linear", fill: "forwards" },
    );
    return () => bar.current?.cancel();
  }, [timed, autoDismissDuration, introDelayMs]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!timed || dismissed) return;
    if (paused) {
      bar.current?.pause();
      return;
    }
    bar.current?.play();
    const startedAt = performance.now();
    const timer = window.setTimeout(dismiss, remaining.current);
    return () => {
      window.clearTimeout(timer);
      remaining.current = Math.max(0, remaining.current - (performance.now() - startedAt));
    };
  }, [timed, paused, dismissed]);

  return (
    <AnimatePresence onExitComplete={onDismiss}>
      {!dismissed ? (
        <motion.div
          ref={ref}
          role={role ?? (status === "error" ? "alert" : "status")}
          initial={
            hasIntro
              ? { opacity: 0, y: 12, scale: 0.97, filter: "blur(4px)" }
              : false
          }
          animate={
            hasIntro
              ? {
                  opacity: 1,
                  y: 0,
                  scale: 1,
                  filter: "blur(0px)",
                  transition: {
                    duration: 0.25,
                    delay: introDelay,
                    ease: "easeOut",
                  },
                }
              : undefined
          }
          exit={{
            opacity: 0,
            y: 8,
            scale: 0.96,
            filter: "blur(3px)",
            transition: { duration: 0.18, ease: "easeOut" },
          }}
          className={cx(styles.card, className)}
          {...props}
        >
          {avatar ? (
            <NotificationAvatarVisual {...avatar} />
          ) : (
            <span className={cx(styles.visual, styles.status[status])}>
              <Icon className={styles.icon} aria-hidden />
            </span>
          )}

          <div className={styles.content}>
            <div className={styles.header}>
              <p className={styles.title}>{title}</p>
              {timestamp ? <span className={styles.timestamp}>{timestamp}</span> : null}
            </div>
            {description ? <p className={styles.description}>{description}</p> : null}

            {actions?.length ? (
              <div className={styles.actions}>
                {actions.map((action, index) => (
                  <Button
                    key={index}
                    size="small"
                    variant={action.variant ?? (index === 0 ? "secondary" : "primary")}
                    onClick={action.onClick}
                  >
                    {action.label}
                  </Button>
                ))}
              </div>
            ) : null}
          </div>

          {dismissible ? (
            <CloseButton
              size="xs"
              aria-label={closeLabel}
              onClick={dismiss}
              className={styles.close}
            />
          ) : null}

          {timed ? (
            <span
              ref={barRef}
              aria-hidden
              className="absolute inset-x-0 bottom-0 h-[3px] origin-left rtl:origin-right bg-accent-600"
            />
          ) : null}
        </motion.div>
      ) : null}
    </AnimatePresence>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The countdown Web Animation is cancelled and the dismiss timeout cleared by their effect cleanups (the timer cleanup also banks the elapsed time). The viewport portal unmounts with its owner.

**Reduced motion.** The component does not read `prefers-reduced-motion`: the 0.25s entrance, the 0.18s exit and the layout spring run regardless. A host can wrap the app in Motion's `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"`. The countdown bar also runs, since it shows how much time is left.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not drive the countdown bar with Motion's standalone `animate()`. On this child it cancelled the card's own enter animation; a native Web Animation can be paused and played in step with the timer.
- Do not remove a card from your list to dismiss it. Set `dismissed` (or let the timer or close button do it) and remove it in `onDismiss`, or it vanishes without its exit animation.
- Do not leave out `introDelay` and expect an entrance. Without it `initial` is `false`; pass `introDelay={0}` for cards that arrive while the page is open.
- Do not key the viewport's children by array index. The wrapper falls back to the index when a child has no key, so removing a card from the middle would animate the wrong ones.

## Notes

- `paused` is meant for a stack held by hover or focus; the demo sets it from `onPointerEnter` / `onPointerLeave` on the viewport.
- `position` accepts logical (`top-start`, `bottom-end`) and physical (`top-left`, `bottom-center`, …) corners; `placement` is a deprecated alias for the two bottom corners.
- The viewport defaults to `aria-label="Notifications"` and `position="bottom-end"`.

## Definition of done

Nothing shows until a button is pressed. "Deploy finished" brings a green success card into the bottom-right stack with a blue bar shrinking over 5 seconds; hovering the stack holds the bar, leaving resumes it, and at the end the card blurs out while the others glide into place. "New comment" shows the LS avatar with a green presence dot and Mark read / Reply buttons, either of which closes the card. "Build failed" is announced as an alert. The position control moves the stack to the top or bottom centre, and a fifth card pushes the oldest out with its exit animation.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Notification Bell Badge

The dashboard header bell: a 36px bordered button with a small red count badge over the glyph. Pressing it opens the kit Popover with the notification list; each row toggles its own read state and "Mark all as read" clears them, and the badge, the trigger's accessible name and the "N unread" line all come from the same list.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Bell button with a red unread badge that opens a notification popover; mark one or all read and the badge follows.

- Category: action
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. State is one notifications array (controlled via notifications + onNotificationsChange, or uncontrolled via defaultNotifications); unread is derived as items.filter(!read).length and never stored separately.
2. BellButton is a plain <button> that forwards its ref and spreads props, styled with the kit buttonStyles base and secondary variant at 36px (or 32px), so it can be the first child of PopoverTrigger.
3. Its aria-label reads "Notifications, N unread"; the visual badge is aria-hidden, absolutely positioned at top-1 start-[18px] and scales from 50% plus fades out when the count hits 0.
4. While fading out the badge keeps its last non-zero number (a setState-during-render sync that only updates on non-zero counts), so it never flashes an empty red dot.
5. Each row's toggle button flips between "Mark as read" and "Mark as unread" and calls setRead(id, !read), mapping a new array; "Mark all as read" maps every unread item to read.
6. Neither control unmounts or becomes disabled after use (the mark-all button turns aria-disabled), so keyboard focus stays inside the popover; the unread line is aria-live so screen readers hear the new count.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `badge position = top-1 start-[18px], h-3.5 min-w-3.5`
  Sits on the bell glyph's top-right shoulder inside the 36px button, matching the dashboard shot.
- `badge ring = ring-2 ring-background-primary-default`
  A 2px ring in the button's own fill cuts the badge out of the glyph outline in both themes.
- `max = 9`
  A 14px badge holds two characters; larger counts read 9+.
- `popover width = 360px (max 100vw - 32px)`
  Fits a two-line title, a description and the toggle button without wrapping the time row.
- `list height = max-h-[min(340px,60vh)]`
  About five rows before the list scrolls, and never taller than a phone viewport allows.

## API

```ts
export function NotificationBellBadge({ notifications, defaultNotifications, onNotificationsChange, isOpen, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, max, size, label, emptyState, footer, placement, className, popoverClassName }: NotificationBellBadgeProps): JSX.Element
export function BellButton({ count, max, size, label, className, ref, ...props }: BellButtonProps): JSX.Element
```

- `notifications: readonly BellNotification[]`
  Controlled list: { id, title, description?, time, read?, icon?, tone? }.
- `defaultNotifications: readonly BellNotification[]` — default `[]`
  Initial list when uncontrolled.
- `onNotificationsChange: (next: BellNotification[]) => void`
  Receives the whole updated list after a mark-one or mark-all change.
- `isOpen / defaultOpen / onOpenChange: boolean / boolean / (isOpen: boolean) => void`
  Popover open state, controlled or not.
- `max: number` — default `9`
  Counts above this show as max+.
- `size: 'medium' | 'small'` — default `'medium'`
  36px or 32px bell.
- `label: string` — default `'Notifications'`
  Trigger accessible name base and popover title.
- `emptyState: ReactNode` — default `'You are all caught up.'`
  Shown when the list is empty.
- `footer: ReactNode`
  Content under the list, e.g. a "View all" link.
- `placement: 'bottom' | 'bottom start' | 'bottom end'` — default `'bottom end'`
  Popover placement relative to the bell.
- `BellButton.count: number`
  Unread count shown in the standalone bell; the badge hides at 0.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function NotificationBellBadge({
  notifications,
  defaultNotifications = [],
  onNotificationsChange,
  isOpen,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  max = 9,
  size = 'medium',
  label = 'Notifications',
  emptyState = 'You are all caught up.',
  footer,
  placement = 'bottom end',
  className,
  popoverClassName,
}: NotificationBellBadgeProps) {
  const [uncontrolled, setUncontrolled] = useState<readonly BellNotification[]>(defaultNotifications);
  const items = notifications ?? uncontrolled;
  const unread = items.filter((item) => !item.read).length;

  const commit = (next: BellNotification[]) => {
    setUncontrolled(next);
    onNotificationsChange?.(next);
  };
  const setRead = (id: string, read: boolean) =>
    commit(items.map((item) => (item.id === id ? { ...item, read } : item)));
  const markAllRead = () => {
    if (unread === 0) return;
    commit(items.map((item) => (item.read ? item : { ...item, read: true })));
  };

  return (
    <PopoverTrigger isOpen={isOpen} defaultOpen={defaultOpen} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>
      <BellButton count={unread} max={max} size={size} label={label} className={className} />
      <Popover placement={placement} className={cx('w-[360px]', popoverClassName)} dialogClassName="gap-1.5 p-1">
        <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-3 px-2 pt-1.5 pb-1">
          <PopoverHeader
            title={label}
            description={<span aria-live="polite">{unread > 0 ? `${unread} unread` : 'No unread notifications'}</span>}
          />
          <Button
            variant="ghost"
            size="xs"
            leadingIcon={RiCheckDoubleLine}
            aria-disabled={unread === 0 || undefined}
            onClick={markAllRead}
            className="mt-px"
          >
            Mark all as read
          </Button>
        </div>

        {items.length === 0 ? (
          <p className="px-2 py-6 text-center text-body-2-regular text-text-tertiary">{emptyState}</p>
        ) : (
          <ul className="flex max-h-[min(340px,60vh)] flex-col gap-0.5 overflow-y-auto" aria-label={label}>
            {items.map((item) => {
              const Icon = item.icon ?? RiNotification3Line;
              return (
                <li
                  key={item.id}
                  className={cx(
                    'flex items-start gap-3 rounded-xl px-2 py-2.5 transition-colors duration-150 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none',
                    item.read ? 'bg-transparent' : 'bg-background-secondary-default',
                  )}
                >
                  <span
                    aria-hidden
                    className={cx('flex size-8 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full', styles.tone[item.tone ?? DEFAULT_TONE])}
                  >
                    <Icon className="size-4" aria-hidden />
                  </span>
                  <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-0.5">
                    <p className={cx('text-body-2-medium', item.read ? 'text-text-secondary' : 'text-text-primary')}>
                      {item.title}
                      {item.read ? null : <span className="sr-only"> (unread)</span>}
                    </p>
                    {item.description ? <p className="text-caption-1-regular text-text-tertiary">{item.description}</p> : null}
                    <p className="flex items-center gap-1 text-caption-1-regular text-text-tertiary">
                      {item.read ? null : <StatusDot color="indigo" className="-ms-[3px]" />}
                      {item.time}
                    </p>
                  </div>
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    className={styles.toggle}
                    aria-label={item.read ? `Mark "${item.title}" as unread` : `Mark "${item.title}" as read`}
                    title={item.read ? 'Mark as unread' : 'Mark as read'}
                    onClick={() => setRead(item.id, !item.read)}
                  >
                    {item.read ? <RiMailLine aria-hidden className="size-4" /> : <RiCheckLine aria-hidden className="size-4" />}
                  </button>
                </li>
              );
            })}
          </ul>
        )}
        {footer ? <div className="border-t border-separator-border px-2 pt-2 pb-1">{footer}</div> : null}
      </Popover>
    </PopoverTrigger>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing of its own to release: no timers or listeners. The kit PopoverTrigger owns and removes its outside-press listener.

**Reduced motion.** The badge and row highlight change instantly (motion-reduce:transition-none); the kit Popover drops its scale and blur entry and only fades.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not remove the per-row button once a notification is read: focus would drop to <body> mid-popover. Flip its label instead.
- Do not disable "Mark all as read" with the disabled attribute for the same reason; use aria-disabled and no-op the handler.
- Do not wrap IconButton in a span as the PopoverTrigger child: the trigger must be the focusable element that receives the forwarded ref and press props.
- Do not keep a separate unread counter in state; derive it from the list or the badge and the list will drift apart.

## Notes

- BellButton is exported on its own for headers that open a different surface (a drawer or a full notification center).
- Pass isOpen / onOpenChange to control the popover, e.g. to close it after navigating to a notification.

## Definition of done

With 5 unread, the bell reads "Notifications, 5 unread"; marking one read in the popover makes it "4 unread", and "Mark all as read" hides the badge and leaves the name "Notifications".

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Notification Center

A 430px inbox card: a header with the unread count and "Mark all read", a segmented control filtering All / Mentions / System with a count on each tab, and a scrolling list of notification rows. Each row shows an avatar or a tinted status icon, title, timestamp, an unread dot, the description and optional action buttons. Read state is tracked inside the component, so pressing an action or "Mark all read" clears the dots without the parent rewriting its data; the tab can be controlled or left uncontrolled.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Tabbed activity inbox with unread counts, avatars or status icons, inline action buttons and a mark-all-read control.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Tab state bridges controlled and uncontrolled use: `activeTab = tab ?? internalTab`, and `setTab` only writes `internalTab` when `tab` is undefined before calling `onTabChange`. The `SegmentedControl` (`selectedKeys={[activeTab]}`) reads the first key of the selection set and ignores an empty selection, so a tab can never be deselected.
2. Read state is a `Set` of ids in local state. `isUnread(item)` is `item.unread === true && !readIds.has(item.id)`; the header shows "N unread" or "No unread notifications", and "Mark all read" (a small ghost Button, disabled at zero) replaces the set with every `unread` id. Pressing any action button adds that row's id before calling `onAction(notificationId, actionId)`.
3. Tab counts and the visible list are `useMemo`s over `notifications`: All shows everything, Mentions and System filter by `category`. Items with `category: "activity"` only appear under All. Each tab label renders its count in a `bg-badge-neutral-background` pill.
4. `NotificationVisual` renders the `avatar` (Avatar `size="lg"` forced to `size-10`) when present, else a 40px round badge with `icon ?? STATUS_ICON[status]` tinted by `status`: neutral (tertiary background), information, success and error (`bg-notification-*-background` / `text-notification-*-foreground`).
5. The list sits in a padded well (`p-1.5` around a `rounded-2xl bg-background-secondary-default` box) whose inner div is `max-h-[516px] overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain`, so long inboxes scroll inside the card without scrolling the page. Rows are `<article>`s with `rounded-notification-card` (10px) on the primary background; the unread dot is an 8px `bg-accent-500` span labelled "Unread". With no visible rows it shows an empty state with `RiNotificationOffLine` and `emptyMessage`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `card width = w-full max-w-[430px], rounded-3xl`
  Fits a notification row with two inline buttons and a timestamp on one line, and fits the 440px bell popover in the app shell with its border.
- `list height = max-h-[516px]`
  Caps the list so the card stays inside a laptop viewport when it is opened from a header bell; longer inboxes scroll inside it.
- `row card radius = --radius-notification-card: 10px`
  Smaller than the 16px (`rounded-2xl`) well around the rows, so the nested corners read as nested inside its 8px padding.
- `visual size = size-10 (40px), icon size-5`
  Avatars and status icons share one footprint, so titles line up whatever the row's visual is.

## API

```ts
function NotificationCenter(props: Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "onChange"> & { notifications: NotificationCenterItem[]; defaultTab?: "all" | "mentions" | "system"; tab?: "all" | "mentions" | "system"; onTabChange?: (tab: NotificationCenterTab) => void; onAction?: (notificationId: string, actionId: string) => void; title?: string; emptyMessage?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
type NotificationCenterItem = { id: string; category: "mentions" | "system" | "activity"; group: string; title: string; description: string; timestamp: string; unread?: boolean; status?: "neutral" | "information" | "success" | "error"; icon?: IconComponent; avatar?: Pick<AvatarProps, "src" | "alt" | "initials" | "color">; actions?: { id: string; label: string; variant?: ButtonProps["variant"] }[] }
```

- `notifications: NotificationCenterItem[]`
  The inbox, rendered in array order.
- `defaultTab: "all" | "mentions" | "system"` — default `"all"`
  Initial tab when uncontrolled.
- `tab / onTabChange: NotificationCenterTab / (tab) => void`
  Controlled tab.
- `onAction: (notificationId: string, actionId: string) => void`
  Called when a row's action button is pressed; the row is marked read first.
- `title: string` — default `"Notifications"`
  Heading and accessible name of the section.
- `emptyMessage: string` — default `"You’re all caught up."`
  Shown when the active tab has no rows.
- `item.status: "neutral" | "information" | "success" | "error"` — default `"neutral"`
  Tint and default icon of the round badge when there is no avatar.
- `item.actions[].variant: ButtonProps["variant"]` — default `"secondary"`
  Button style of an inline action.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function NotificationCenter({
  notifications,
  defaultTab = "all",
  tab,
  onTabChange,
  onAction,
  title = "Notifications",
  emptyMessage = "You’re all caught up.",
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: NotificationCenterProps) {
  const localize = useTemplateCopy();
  const [internalTab, setInternalTab] = useState<NotificationCenterTab>(defaultTab);
  const [readIds, setReadIds] = useState<Set<string>>(() => new Set());
  const activeTab = tab ?? internalTab;

  const setTab = (nextTab: NotificationCenterTab) => {
    if (tab === undefined) setInternalTab(nextTab);
    onTabChange?.(nextTab);
  };

  const isUnread = (item: NotificationCenterItem) => item.unread === true && !readIds.has(item.id);
  const unreadCount = notifications.filter(isUnread).length;

  const tabCounts = useMemo(
    () => ({
      all: notifications.length,
      mentions: notifications.filter((item) => item.category === "mentions").length,
      system: notifications.filter((item) => item.category === "system").length,
    }),
    [notifications],
  );

  const visibleNotifications = useMemo(
    () =>
      activeTab === "all"
        ? notifications
        : notifications.filter((item) => item.category === activeTab),
    [activeTab, notifications],
  );

  const markAllRead = () => {
    setReadIds(new Set(notifications.filter((item) => item.unread).map((item) => item.id)));
  };

  return localize((
    <section
      ref={ref}
      aria-label={title}
      className={cx(
        "flex w-full max-w-[430px] flex-col overflow-hidden rounded-3xl border border-border-button-default bg-notification-center-background shadow-dropdown",
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 p-4 pb-1.5">
        <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-4">
          <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-0.5">
            <h2 className="text-title-3-medium text-text-primary">{title}</h2>
            <p className="text-body-regular text-text-secondary">
              {unreadCount === 0 ? "No unread notifications" : `${unreadCount} unread`}
            </p>
          </div>
          <Button
            variant="ghost"
            size="small"
            onClick={markAllRead}
            disabled={unreadCount === 0}
          >
            Mark all read
          </Button>
        </div>

        <SegmentedControl
          aria-label="Notification category"
          selectedKeys={[activeTab]}
          onSelectionChange={(keys) => {
            const next = [...(keys as Set<string>)][0] as NotificationCenterTab | undefined;
            if (next) setTab(next);
          }}
          className="flex w-full"
        >
          {TABS.map(({ id, label }) => (
            <SegmentedControlItem
              key={id}
              id={id}
              className="flex-1"
            >
              <TabLabel label={label} count={tabCounts[id]} />
            </SegmentedControlItem>
          ))}
        </SegmentedControl>
      </div>

      <div className="bg-notification-center-background p-1.5">
        <div className="overflow-hidden rounded-2xl bg-background-secondary-default">
          <div className="max-h-[516px] overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain bg-background-secondary-default p-2">
            {visibleNotifications.length === 0 ? (
              <div className="flex min-h-64 flex-col items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-2xl bg-background-primary-default px-6 text-center">
                <span className="flex size-11 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-background-secondary-default text-foreground-icon-secondary">
                  <RiNotificationOffLine className="size-5" aria-hidden />
                </span>
                <p className="text-body-medium text-text-primary">{emptyMessage}</p>
                <p className="max-w-64 text-body-regular text-text-secondary">
                  New activity will appear here when it arrives.
                </p>
              </div>
            ) : (
              <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
                {visibleNotifications.map((item) => {
                  const unread = isUnread(item);
                  return (
                    <article
                      key={item.id}
                      className="group/item relative flex gap-3 rounded-notification-card bg-background-primary-default px-3 py-3"
                    >
                      <NotificationVisual item={item} />
                      <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-0.5">
                        <div className="flex min-w-0 items-start justify-between gap-3">
                          <p className="min-w-0 text-body-medium text-text-primary">{item.title}</p>
                          <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center gap-2">
                            <span className="text-caption-1-medium whitespace-nowrap text-text-tertiary">
                              {item.timestamp}
                            </span>
                            {unread ? (
                              <span
                                className="size-2 rounded-full bg-accent-500"
                                aria-label="Unread"
                              />
                            ) : null}
                          </div>
                        </div>
                        <p className="text-body-regular text-text-secondary">{item.description}</p>
                        {item.actions?.length ? (
                          <div className="mt-1.5 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
                            {item.actions.map((action) => (
                              <Button
                                key={action.id}
                                size="small"
                                variant={action.variant ?? "secondary"}
                                onClick={() => {
                                  setReadIds((current) => new Set(current).add(item.id));
                                  onAction?.(item.id, action.id);
                                }}
                              >
                                {action.label}
                              </Button>
                            ))}
                          </div>
                        ) : null}
                      </div>
                    </article>
                  );
                })}
              </div>
            )}
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  ));
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** None: state only (tab, read ids), no listeners or timers.

**Reduced motion.** The component adds no motion of its own; tab and button transitions come from SegmentedControl and Button and follow their reduced-motion rules.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not expect `unread: false` to be written back to your data. Read state lives in the component's `readIds` set; persist it in `onAction` (or a "mark all" handler of your own) if it must survive a remount.
- Do not rely on `group` for headings. It is part of the item type for your own data, but the list renders flat rows in array order; sort the array yourself.
- Do not pass `tab` without `onTabChange`. A controlled tab never changes on its own, so the segmented control would appear stuck.
- Do not give an item both `avatar` and `icon` expecting the icon; the avatar wins.

## Notes

- The fixed copy (tab names, "Mark all read", the empty-state line) runs through `useTemplateCopy()`'s `localize`, so localized templates translate it.
- The section is labelled by `title` (`aria-label`), and the h2 shows the same text.
- Used by the app shell's notification bell, which renders it inside a non-modal popover.

## Definition of done

The card reads "4 unread" with tab counts All 6, Mentions 2, System 3. Choosing System shows the three system rows and "Viewing System" in the activity panel. Pressing Retry removes that row's blue dot, drops the count to 3 and logs "Retry" beside the card. "Mark all read" clears every dot, reads "No unread notifications" and disables itself. The list scrolls inside the card when it is taller than 516px.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Number Field

A number typed or stepped, such as seats, a price or a percentage. It puts Input's field shell (`InputBase`, with the same hover, focus, invalid and disabled states) inside React Aria's `NumberField` and adds minus and plus buttons at the trailing end. React Aria formats and parses the value for the locale, clamps it to `minValue` and `maxValue` on blur, disables a stepper at its limit, and handles arrow keys, Home and End, the scroll wheel and press-and-hold repeat.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Input's field shell plus minus and plus steppers on React Aria NumberField: locale currency, percent and unit formats, clamped to limits.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `NumberField` renders `AriaNumberField` as `group flex w-full flex-col items-start gap-1`. All React Aria number props (`value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `minValue`, `maxValue`, `step`, `formatOptions`, `isWheelDisabled`, `isDisabled`, `isInvalid`) pass straight through. Without a `label` or `aria-label`, the `placeholder` becomes the `aria-label`.
2. Its render function shows `Label` (with the asterisk when `isRequired`) when `label` is set, then `InputBase` from the Input item, then `HintText` (red when invalid) when `hint` is set. Because `InputBase` renders React Aria's `Group` and `Input`, they pick up `NumberField`'s context: the group gets the field's state for the ring and fill classes, and the input gets the formatted value, `inputMode` and key handling. The input adds `tabular-nums` so digits do not shift width while stepping.
3. The steppers go in `InputBase`'s `trailingAddon`: a `-my-1 -me-1 flex gap-0.5` span with two React Aria `Button`s, `slot="decrement"` (`RiSubtractLine`) and `slot="increment"` (`RiAddLine`). The slots connect them to the field, so React Aria disables each at its limit, repeats the step while it is held, and keeps focus in the input on press.
4. Each stepper is `rounded-md` in `text-foreground-icon-secondary`, `size-6` (or `size-5` at `small`) with a 16px icon. Hover and press set `bg-background-tertiary-hover` with a 150ms colour transition; keyboard focus draws `ring-2 ring-border-focus-ring`; disabled switches to the disabled text colour and a `not-allowed` cursor with no hover fill.
5. `hideSteppers` drops the buttons entirely; Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End still step the value from the keyboard.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `stepper size = size-6 (24px) at medium, size-5 (20px) at small; icon size-4 (16px)`
  Fits inside the 36px or 32px shell without changing its height, and leaves the 16px icon a 4px hover margin on every side.
- `stepper inset = -my-1 -me-1`
  Pulls the button pair 4px into the shell's padding, so their hover fill sits closer to the edge while the text keeps Input's inset.
- `stepper gap = gap-0.5 (2px)`
  Keeps minus and plus as separate hover targets without reading as two distant controls.
- `hover transition = transition-colors duration-150 ease-out`
  The same 150ms as the field shell (`--input-transition-ms`), so a stepper and the ring around it change together.

## API

```ts
function NumberField(props: Omit<AriaNumberFieldProps, "className" | "children"> & { label?: ReactNode; hint?: ReactNode; tooltip?: boolean | string; placeholder?: string; size?: "medium" | "small"; leadingIcon?: IconComponent; hideSteppers?: boolean; className?: string; fieldClassName?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `value / defaultValue: number`
  Controlled or uncontrolled numeric value.
- `onChange: (value: number) => void`
  Called with the parsed number, after clamping; `NaN` when cleared.
- `minValue / maxValue: number`
  Limits. The value is clamped on blur and the matching stepper disables at each limit.
- `step: number` — default `1`
  Amount per stepper press or arrow key.
- `formatOptions: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`
  Currency, percent, unit or decimal formatting for the locale.
- `label / hint: ReactNode`
  Label above and caption below, as on Input.
- `size: "medium" | "small"` — default `"medium"`
  36px or 32px shell; 24px or 20px steppers.
- `hideSteppers: boolean` — default `false`
  Removes the minus and plus buttons.
- `leadingIcon: ComponentType`
  20px icon before the value.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function NumberField({
  label,
  hint,
  tooltip,
  placeholder,
  size = "medium",
  leadingIcon,
  hideSteppers = false,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel,
  className,
  fieldClassName,
  ...props
}: NumberFieldProps) {
  const stepper = cx(STEPPER, size === "small" ? "size-5" : "size-6");

  return (
    <AriaNumberField
      {...props}
      aria-label={ariaLabel ?? (!label ? placeholder : undefined)}
      className={cx("group flex w-full flex-col items-start gap-1", className)}
    >
      {({ isInvalid }) => (
        <>
          {label ? (
            <Label isRequired={props.isRequired} isInvalid={isInvalid} tooltip={tooltip}>
              {label}
            </Label>
          ) : null}
          <InputBase
            size={size}
            placeholder={placeholder}
            leadingIcon={leadingIcon}
            fieldClassName={fieldClassName}
            className="tabular-nums"
            trailingAddon={
              hideSteppers ? undefined : (
                <span className="-my-1 -me-1 flex shrink-0 items-center gap-0.5">
                  <AriaButton slot="decrement" className={stepper}>
                    <RiSubtractLine aria-hidden className="size-4" />
                  </AriaButton>
                  <AriaButton slot="increment" className={stepper}>
                    <RiAddLine aria-hidden className="size-4" />
                  </AriaButton>
                </span>
              )
            }
          />
          {hint ? <HintText isInvalid={isInvalid}>{hint}</HintText> : null}
        </>
      )}
    </AriaNumberField>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component holds no state of its own; React Aria owns the value and the press-and-hold timer.

**Reduced motion.** The component does not check `prefers-reduced-motion`. Its only motion is the 150ms colour transition on the steppers and the shell, which a global rule that removes transitions makes instant.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not render steppers as plain `<button>`s with your own `onClick`. Only React Aria `Button`s with `slot="increment"` and `slot="decrement"` get the limit disabling, hold-to-repeat and focus handling from the field.
- Do not format the value yourself and pass a string. Pass a number and `formatOptions` (for example `{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }`); React Aria formats it for display and parses typed text back.
- Do not forget that `onChange` can give `NaN` when the field is cleared. Guard any total you compute from it.
- Do not use `step` for a percent field in whole numbers. With `style: "percent"`, 10% is the value 0.1, so a 5% step is `step={0.05}`.

## Notes

- The field imports `InputBase` from Input, and `Label` and `HintText` from Input's companion files, so install Input alongside it.

## Definition of done

A "Seats" field shows 5 with minus and plus at its end. Pressing plus shows 6; holding it keeps stepping. At the maximum the plus button greys out and stops responding. Typing 80 into a field with a maximum of 50 and tabbing away snaps it to 50. A currency field shows "$12.00" and a percent field "10%"; Up and Down step them. Hover on a stepper fills it softly; focus on the field draws Input's inset ring.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: On This Page TOC

The table of contents that sits to the right of a docs article. A thin rail runs down the list and a 2px bar slides to the section currently in view, which also turns its label from tertiary to primary. Clicking a label scrolls the article to that section and moves focus there. It watches any scroll container, not only the window, so it works inside panels and previews.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Right-hand "On this page" list that tracks the section you are reading with an IntersectionObserver and a sliding active bar.

- Category: navigation
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Items are `{ id, label, depth? }`, where `id` is the id of a section element. One IntersectionObserver is created with `root` set to the `scrollRoot` element (or the viewport when omitted) and observes every section.
2. The observer's `rootMargin` shrinks the root to an activation band: `-offset px` from the top and `-(1 - activationRatio)` from the bottom (by default the top 30%). Callbacks add or remove ids from an in-band set, and the active item is the last id in TOC order that is in the band, which is the section whose heading most recently scrolled into it. When nothing is in the band, the last active id is kept.
3. A passive scroll listener on the same root only checks for reaching the end: once `scrollTop + clientHeight` hits `scrollHeight`, the last item wins, because a short final section can never reach the band.
4. Clicking an item prevents the hash jump, computes the target offset relative to the root with `getBoundingClientRect`, and calls `root.scrollTo` (smooth unless reduced motion). The clicked id is committed at once and observer updates are locked until `scrollend` or a 900ms fallback, so the bar does not stutter through the sections the scroll passes.
5. The indicator is one absolutely positioned span whose `translateY` and height are copied from the active link's `offsetTop` / `offsetHeight` in a layout effect. A ResizeObserver on the list re-measures when wrapping changes, and the first placement skips the transition so it does not slide in from the top.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `activation band = top 30% of the root (activationRatio 0.3)`
  A section counts as "being read" once its top crosses into the upper part of the view; a band that is too low flips the TOC before the heading is visible.
- `offset = 16px`
  Used for both the observer's top margin and the scroll target, so a clicked section lands where the observer already treats it as active.
- `click lock = until scrollend, max 900ms`
  Long enough for a smooth scroll across the article; the timeout covers browsers without `scrollend` and clicks on the section already in place.
- `indicator = 2px bar on a 1px rail, 300ms ease-out`
  Matches the reference: a light rail with a darker bar beside the active label.
- `end tolerance = 2px`
  Fractional scroll positions on high-DPI screens can stop a pixel short of `scrollHeight`.

## API

```ts
function OnThisPageToc(props: { items: TocItem[]; scrollRoot?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; activeId?: string | null; defaultActiveId?: string | null; onActiveChange?: (id: string) => void; title?: ReactNode; offset?: number; activationRatio?: number; focusTarget?: boolean; "aria-label"?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type TocItem = { id: string; label: string; depth?: 0 | 1 | 2 }
```

- `items: TocItem[]`
  Entries in document order; `id` is the section element id and `depth` indents sub-sections.
- `scrollRoot: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>` — default `window`
  Scroll container holding the sections. Becomes the observer root and the element scrolled on click.
- `activeId / defaultActiveId: string | null` — default `first item`
  Active section, controlled or initial.
- `onActiveChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called when scrolling or a click changes the active section.
- `title: ReactNode` — default `"On this page"`
  Heading above the list; pass null to hide it.
- `offset: number` — default `16`
  Px between the root top and a section after a jump; also the top of the activation band.
- `activationRatio: number` — default `0.3`
  Fraction of the root height, from the top, in which a section counts as active.
- `focusTarget: boolean` — default `true`
  Moves focus to the section after a jump (adds `tabindex="-1"` if needed).
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the nav.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Scrollspy: the active section is the last one (in TOC order) inside a band
// from `offset` px below the root's top down to `activationRatio` of its
// height, i.e. the section whose heading most recently entered the band.
// Scrolled to the very end, the last section wins even when it is too short
// to ever reach the band.
useEffect(() => {
  const root = scrollRoot?.current ?? null;
  const order = ids.split("|").filter(Boolean);
  const targets = order
    .map((id) => document.getElementById(id))
    .filter((el): el is HTMLElement => el !== null);
  if (targets.length === 0 || typeof IntersectionObserver === "undefined") return;

  const inBand = new Set<string>();
  const atEnd = () =>
    root
      ? root.scrollTop + root.clientHeight >= root.scrollHeight - 2
      : window.scrollY + window.innerHeight >= document.documentElement.scrollHeight - 2;
  const pick = () => {
    if (lockRef.current) return;
    const last = order[order.length - 1];
    const scrolled = (root ? root.scrollTop : window.scrollY) > 0;
    if (last && scrolled && atEnd()) return commit(last);
    let current: string | undefined;
    for (const id of order) if (inBand.has(id)) current = id;
    if (current) commit(current);
  };

  const bottomInset = Math.round((1 - activationRatio) * 100);
  const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
    (entries) => {
      for (const entry of entries) {
        if (entry.isIntersecting) inBand.add(entry.target.id);
        else inBand.delete(entry.target.id);
      }
      pick();
    },
    { root, rootMargin: `-${offset}px 0px -${bottomInset}% 0px`, threshold: 0 },
  );
  for (const target of targets) observer.observe(target);

  let wasAtEnd = atEnd();
  const scroller: HTMLElement | Window = root ?? window;
  const onScroll = () => {
    const end = atEnd();
    if (end !== wasAtEnd) {
      wasAtEnd = end;
      pick();
    }
  };
  scroller.addEventListener("scroll", onScroll, { passive: true });

  return () => {
    observer.disconnect();
    scroller.removeEventListener("scroll", onScroll);
  };
}, [ids, scrollRoot, offset, activationRatio, commit]);

const jumpTo = (event: ReactMouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement>, id: string) => {
  const target = document.getElementById(id);
  if (!target) return;
  event.preventDefault();
  const root = scrollRoot?.current ?? null;
  const behavior: ScrollBehavior = reduced ? "auto" : "smooth";

  // Hold the clicked item while the smooth scroll passes other sections.
  releaseRef.current?.();
  lockRef.current = id;
  commit(id);
  const scroller: HTMLElement | Window = root ?? window;
  const release = () => {
    lockRef.current = null;
    scroller.removeEventListener("scrollend", release);
    window.clearTimeout(timer);
    releaseRef.current = null;
  };
  const timer = window.setTimeout(release, 900);
  scroller.addEventListener("scrollend", release);
  releaseRef.current = release;

  if (root) {
    const top = root.scrollTop + target.getBoundingClientRect().top - root.getBoundingClientRect().top - offset;
    root.scrollTo({ top, behavior });
  } else {
    window.scrollTo({ top: window.scrollY + target.getBoundingClientRect().top - offset, behavior });
  }
  if (focusTarget) {
    if (!target.hasAttribute("tabindex")) target.setAttribute("tabindex", "-1");
    target.focus({ preventScroll: true });
  }
};
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The IntersectionObserver is disconnected and the scroll listener removed when the component unmounts or its items, root, offset or ratio change. A pending click lock removes its `scrollend` listener and clears its timeout on release and on unmount. The ResizeObserver lives in `useResizeObserver` and disconnects itself.

**Reduced motion.** With reduced motion the click jump uses `behavior: "auto"` (an instant scroll) and the bar and label colour transitions carry `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so the indicator moves without sliding.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Observing with the default viewport root while the sections live in an inner scroll container. The sections never leave the viewport, so the TOC never changes; pass the container as `root`.
- Picking the entry with the largest `intersectionRatio`. Tall sections have tiny ratios, so the TOC jumps to short neighbours; track which ids are in the band and choose the last one in document order instead.
- Letting the observer drive the TOC during a click-initiated smooth scroll. The bar runs through every section in between; lock it to the clicked id until the scroll ends.
- Using `scrollIntoView` for the jump. It scrolls every ancestor, so the page under an embedded article moves too.
- Forgetting the end-of-scroll rule. A final section shorter than the band never becomes active and the last TOC item is unreachable by scrolling.

## Notes

- Section ids in the demo are prefixed with `useId` so two copies on one page do not share targets.
- Prefer the section wrapper as the target over its heading: the wrapper stays intersecting while its body is read.

## Definition of done

Preview is active on load with the bar beside it. Scrolling the article moves the bar to Installation, Usage and so on; scrolling to the bottom activates Accessibility. Clicking Tokens scrolls the article so Tokens sits near the top, the Tokens link gets `aria-current="location"`, and the page around the demo does not move.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Single-Draw Orbit Rings

Five concentric orbits of static path dots, each carrying one brighter dot that travels it. Every dot in the system is a vertex of one `THREE.Points` object, so ring count and dot count cost buffer memory but never a second draw call. The outer rings are dimmer than the inner ones, which reads as depth even though the camera is orthographic and nothing is actually further away.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Concentric rings of dots, one bright marker travelling each ring, all of it in a single draw call.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1

## How it works

1. Each dot packs its whole identity into one attribute, `aPointData = vec4(kind, ringIndex, angle, dotRadius)`, where `kind` is 0 for a path dot and 1 for the orbiting marker. `position` is zeroed for every vertex and carries no information at all.
2. The vertex shader derives the ring radius as `uBaseRadius * scale * uExtent * 0.5` with `scale = 1.0 - (uRingCount - 1.0 - ringIndex) * 0.1`, so rings step 10% apart with the outermost at full radius, and `uExtent = min(width, height)` keeps the structure inside a preview of any aspect.
3. Path dots sit at `vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle)) * ringRadius`; markers use `angle - PI * 0.5 + uElapsed * uSpeed` instead, so the phase offset baked into the attribute becomes a starting position and the clock does the travelling.
4. Depth is faked with a focal length that no camera uses: `alpha = 0.15 + 0.65 * FOCAL_LENGTH / (FOCAL_LENGTH + ringRadius)` dims a ring in proportion to its size, so wider rings recede.
5. `gl_PointSize` is clamped to a 2px floor and the fragment alpha is then divided by the area that clamping invented — `vAlphaScale = unclamped² / clamped²` — so a dot forced twice as wide comes out four times fainter and the field looks identical at 1x and 3x device pixel ratio.
6. The fragment shader turns each square point sprite into a disc with `1.0 - smoothstep(0.43, 0.5, length(gl_PointCoord - 0.5))` and discards anything fully transparent, so the renderer is created with `antialias: false`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `RING_STEP = 0.1`
  10% radius difference between adjacent rings. Below ~0.06 the rings visually merge into a band at preview size; above ~0.15 the innermost ring collapses to a dot when ringCount is 5.
- `FOCAL_LENGTH = 800.0`
  Not a camera property — the denominator of the alpha falloff. At 800 the outermost ring lands about 30% dimmer than the innermost at typical preview sizes: enough to read as depth, not enough to read as a fade-out. At 200 the outer rings vanish.
- `MIN_POINT_SIZE = 2.0`
  Hardware floor. Below roughly 1px most GPUs rasterise nothing at all, so a 1px dot at DPR 1 would simply be missing on some machines rather than faint.
- `UNCLAMPED_MIN_POINT_SIZE = 1.0`
  The size the dot *would* have had. It is the numerator of the area correction — without a separate constant there is nothing to compare the clamped size against and the compensation cannot be computed.
- `disc edge = smoothstep(0.43, 0.5, d)`
  A soft band 7% of the point radius wide. Narrower and a 2px dot aliases into a square; wider and every dot looks blurred rather than small.
- `baseRadius = 0.75`
  Outermost ring diameter as a fraction of the container short side. At 1.0 the ring touches the edge and the marker clips as it passes; 0.75 leaves a margin the marker can travel through.
- `dotsPerRing = 170`
  Dense enough that the path reads as a continuous line at 320px wide, sparse enough that the innermost ring is not a solid filled circle.
- `speed = 0.3`
  Radians per second — one lap every ~21s. Linear, no easing: a constant angular rate is what makes it read as a mechanism rather than an animation.

## API

```ts
function OrbitRingPoints(props: { ringCount?: number; dotsPerRing?: number; speed?: number; baseRadius?: number; dotRadius?: number; markerRadius?: number; opacity?: number; color?: string; markerColor?: string; seed?: number | string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `ringCount: number` — default `5`
  Concentric rings. Each gets exactly one travelling marker.
- `dotsPerRing: number` — default `170`
  Static path dots per ring.
- `speed: number` — default `0.3`
  Marker angular speed in radians per second.
- `baseRadius: number` — default `0.75`
  Outermost ring diameter as a fraction of the container short side.
- `dotRadius: number` — default `1`
  Path dot radius in CSS pixels, before pixel-ratio scaling.
- `markerRadius: number` — default `3`
  Marker radius in CSS pixels.
- `opacity: number` — default `1`
  Multiplier applied to every dot in the vertex shader.
- `color: string` — default `'#8a8f98'`
  Path dot colour, any value `THREE.Color` accepts.
- `markerColor: string` — default `'#ffffff'`
  Travelling marker colour.
- `seed: number | string` — default `'orbit-ring-points'`
  Seeds the angular scatter, so the ring is identical on server and client.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the host element via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function OrbitRingPoints({
  ringCount = 5,
  dotsPerRing = 170,
  speed = 0.3,
  baseRadius = 0.75,
  dotRadius = 1,
  markerRadius = 3,
  opacity = 1,
  color = '#8a8f98',
  markerColor = '#ffffff',
  seed = 'orbit-ring-points',
  className,
}: OrbitRingPointsProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);
  const [unsupported, setUnsupported] = useState(false);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const size = useRef({ width, height });
  size.current = { width, height };

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const ready = width > 0 && height > 0;

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready) return;

    if (!hasWebGL()) {
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }

    // `antialias: false` is deliberate: the fragment shader anti-aliases each
    // disc itself with a smoothstep, so MSAA would pay for a whole extra
    // sample buffer to solve a problem that is already solved.
    let renderer: THREE.WebGLRenderer;
    try {
      renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: false, alpha: true });
    } catch {
      // A context can still be refused between the probe and the construction —
      // the tab may have hit the browser's live-context ceiling in between. three
      // throws rather than returning null, and an uncaught throw here takes the
      // page with it.
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }
    renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio());
    renderer.setClearAlpha(0);

    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    // Orthographic and 1:1 with CSS pixels, so `gl_PointSize` in the shader is
    // a real pixel count and the ring radii are real pixel radii.
    const camera = new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0.1, 10);
    camera.position.z = 1;

    const rng = createRng(seed);
    const perRing = dotsPerRing + 1; // path dots + one marker
    const total = ringCount * perRing;

    const positions = new Float32Array(total * 3); // stays all zeros
    const pointData = new Float32Array(total * 4);

    let at = 0;
    for (let ring = 0; ring < ringCount; ring += 1) {
      // Sorting the angles is not cosmetic. Points are drawn in buffer order,
      // and an unsorted ring interleaves near and far dots so the alpha blend
      // stipples along the path instead of reading as one continuous line.
      const angles = new Float32Array(dotsPerRing);
      for (let i = 0; i < dotsPerRing; i += 1) angles[i] = rng() * Math.PI * 2;
      angles.sort();

      for (let i = 0; i < dotsPerRing; i += 1) {
        pointData[at] = 0;
        pointData[at + 1] = ring;
        pointData[at + 2] = angles[i] ?? 0;
        pointData[at + 3] = dotRadius;
        at += 4;
      }

      pointData[at] = 1;
      pointData[at + 1] = ring;
      pointData[at + 2] = rng() * Math.PI * 2;
      pointData[at + 3] = markerRadius;
      at += 4;
    }

    const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
    geometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(positions, 3));
    geometry.setAttribute('aPointData', new THREE.BufferAttribute(pointData, 4));

    const uniforms: Uniforms = {
      uElapsed: { value: 0 },
      uExtent: { value: 1 },
      uPixelRatio: { value: renderer.getPixelRatio() },
      uOpacity: { value: opacity },
      uRingCount: { value: ringCount },
      uSpeed: { value: speed },
      uBaseRadius: { value: baseRadius },
      uColor: { value: new THREE.Color(color) },
      uMarkerColor: { value: new THREE.Color(markerColor) },
    };

    const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader: ORBIT_RING_POINTS_VERT,
      fragmentShader: ORBIT_RING_POINTS_FRAG,
      uniforms,
      transparent: true,
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
    });

    const points = new THREE.Points(geometry, material);
    // Every vertex sits at the origin, so three computes a bounding sphere of
    // radius zero and culls the entire object the moment the camera is not
    // looking straight at (0,0,0). Displacement happens in the shader, which
    // the culler cannot see.
    points.frustumCulled = false;
    scene.add(points);

    el.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
    renderer.domElement.style.display = 'block';
    renderer.domElement.style.width = '100%';
    renderer.domElement.style.height = '100%';

    const resize = (w: number, h: number) => {
      renderer.setSize(w, h, false);
      camera.left = -w / 2;
      camera.right = w / 2;
      camera.top = h / 2;
      camera.bottom = -h / 2;
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
      // Ring radii scale off the SHORT side. Off the height alone, a wide
      // preview leaves the rings floating in a sea of empty space; off the
      // width alone, a tall one clips them.
      uniforms.uExtent.value = Math.min(w, h);
      uniforms.uPixelRatio.value = renderer.getPixelRatio();
    };

    const draw = (elapsed: number) => {
      uniforms.uElapsed.value = elapsed;
      renderer.render(scene, camera);
    };

    resize(size.current.width, size.current.height);
    stage.current = { renderer, scene, camera, uniforms, resize, draw };
    draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      // Order matters: release the scene graph's GPU objects while the
      // context is still alive, then hand the context back.
      disposeObject(scene);
      material.dispose();
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      renderer.domElement.remove();
    };
  }, [
    ready,
    ringCount,
    dotsPerRing,
    speed,
    baseRadius,
    dotRadius,
    markerRadius,
    opacity,
    color,
    markerColor,
    seed,
  ]);

  // Resize is its own effect so a container reflow costs a `setSize` call
  // rather than a full teardown and rebuild of the buffer.
  useEffect(() => {
    stage.current?.resize(width, height);
    if (reduced) stage.current?.draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);
  }, [width, height, reduced]);

  useRaf((_dt, elapsed) => stage.current?.draw(elapsed), ready && !reduced && !unsupported);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Clears the stage ref first so no queued frame can touch a dead renderer, then `disposeObject(scene)` for the geometry, `material.dispose()`, `disposeRenderer(renderer)` for `dispose` + `forceContextLoss` + zeroing the drawing buffer, and finally removes the canvas from the DOM. The rAF subscription is released by `useRaf` on unmount.

**Reduced motion.** The rAF subscription is never opened. One frame is drawn at `uElapsed = 0`, which parks every marker at twelve o'clock on its ring, so the full structure is visible and only the orbiting stops. Resizing still redraws that frame.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Leaving `frustumCulled` at its default. Every vertex sits at the origin, so three computes a bounding sphere of radius zero; the displacement is invisible to the culler and the entire object disappears the moment the camera is not pointed exactly at (0,0,0).
- Not sorting the angles within a ring before writing them into the buffer. Points are blended in buffer order with depth testing off, so an unsorted ring stipples — the path visibly breaks into a dotted texture instead of reading as one line.
- Clamping `gl_PointSize` without correcting the alpha. The clamp is invisible at DPR 3 and doubles the covered area at DPR 1, so the same component looks twice as bright on a cheap monitor as on a retina laptop.
- Turning on `antialias: true` to smooth the dots. The fragment shader already anti-aliases each disc; MSAA then allocates a multisample buffer the size of the canvas to solve nothing.
- Rebuilding the renderer on every resize. The buffer is size-independent — only the camera frustum and `uExtent` change — so a container reflow should cost a `setSize` call, not a teardown that drops and re-acquires a GL context.
- Calling `renderer.dispose()` and stopping there. It frees GPU objects but leaves the context alive; `disposeRenderer` also calls `forceContextLoss`, without which a grid of previews silently blacks out the oldest one at around sixteen contexts.

## Notes

- The camera is orthographic and spans the canvas 1:1 in CSS pixels, so `gl_PointSize` is a real pixel count and ring radii are real pixel radii. That is what makes the pixel-ratio compensation expressible at all.
- Ring count and dots per ring are both free at draw time. A hundred rings is one draw call and one buffer upload.

## Definition of done

Five rings of dots with one brighter dot travelling each, all at the same angular rate, the outer rings visibly dimmer than the inner ones. Resize the container and the rings rescale without flicker or a dropped context. Zoom the browser to 200% and the dots stay the same apparent brightness rather than getting denser. With reduced motion on, the rings render fully and the markers sit still at the top.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
