# Build: Pointer-Variable Gradient

A radial gradient declared once in CSS reads its centre from `--pointer-x` and `--pointer-y`. The pointer handler does nothing but write those two properties as percentages. There is no animation frame, no tween library and no `background` string assembled in JavaScript.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A soft glow tracks the pointer through two CSS custom properties. No rAF, no tween, no string rebuilding.

- Category: cursor
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The gradient — its size, colour, stops and the layer underneath it — is declared once on the element. The only thing JavaScript ever writes is two custom properties, so the style engine invalidates the paint of one gradient rather than re-parsing a `background` shorthand it has already parsed thousands of times.
2. Values are written as percentages, not pixels. A percentage in a gradient position resolves against the element box, so the glow stays put relative to the panel across a resize with no resize listener and no recomputation — the value that was correct before the resize is still correct after it.
3. There is deliberately no `requestAnimationFrame`. A custom-property write is not a layout read, so there is nothing to batch away from; the browser already coalesces style changes into the next paint. Wrapping this in a frame loop adds one frame of latency and buys nothing measurable.
4. There is deliberately no tween. Smoothing the glow would mean owning a value between the pointer and the gradient, which means a frame loop, which is the cost this component exists to avoid. A 38rem glow is so diffuse that a few pixels of jitter are invisible — the smoothing would be paying for something no one can see.
5. Leaving removes the properties rather than writing the rest position back, so the fallback declared in the inline `style` takes over and the resting position is stated in exactly one place.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `REST_X / REST_Y = '50%' / '38%'`
  Where the glow sits before any pointer has been seen, and where it returns to on leave. Slightly above centre because a glow that sits dead-centre behind a headline reads as a lighting mistake, while one a little high reads as a source above the frame.
- `glowWidth / glowHeight = '38rem' / '30rem'`
  Wider than tall, matching the aspect of most content blocks. Sizing in rem rather than % means the glow keeps its physical size on a small panel instead of shrinking to a hotspot — a percentage-sized gradient in a 320px preview looks like a different effect entirely.
- `intensity = 0.09`
  Peak accent opacity at the centre. Under ~0.05 it is indistinguishable from a gradient banding artefact; over ~0.2 it stops being ambient light and becomes a coloured blob that competes with the text it is behind.
- `transparent 68% = 68%`
  Where the glow reaches zero. Ending short of 100% keeps the falloff inside the gradient box so the edge is never visible as a circle boundary against the panel edge.

## API

```ts
function PointerVarGradient(props: { children?: ReactNode; glowWidth?: string; glowHeight?: string; intensity?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Content rendered over the gradient.
- `glowWidth: string` — default `'38rem'`
  Horizontal radius of the glow, any CSS length.
- `glowHeight: string` — default `'30rem'`
  Vertical radius of the glow, any CSS length.
- `intensity: number` — default `0.09`
  Peak accent opacity at the glow centre, 0..1.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root container via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Where the glow sits before the pointer has ever been seen. */
const REST_X = '50%';
const REST_Y = '38%';

export function PointerVarGradient({
  children,
  glowWidth = '38rem',
  glowHeight = '30rem',
  intensity = 0.09,
  className,
}: PointerVarGradientProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = root.current;
    if (!el) return;

    /* Fine pointers only. On touch a `pointermove` exists only during a drag,
       so the glow would be pinned under the finger that is scrolling the page
       and then abandoned there on lift — worse than not moving at all. The
       rest position set in the inline style stays, so touch users still get a
       composed gradient. */
    if (!window.matchMedia('(pointer: fine)').matches) return;

    const onMove = (e: PointerEvent) => {
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      /* Percentages, not px. The gradient position resolves against the
         element box, so a percentage survives a resize with no listener and
         no recalculation — the glow stays where it was relative to the panel
         even if the panel changes size between moves. */
      el.style.setProperty(
        '--pointer-x',
        `${((e.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width) * 100}%`,
      );
      el.style.setProperty(
        '--pointer-y',
        `${((e.clientY - rect.top) / rect.height) * 100}%`,
      );
    };

    const onLeave = () => {
      /* Removing the property rather than writing the rest value back lets the
         inline `style` fallback take over, so the resting position is declared
         in exactly one place. */
      el.style.removeProperty('--pointer-x');
      el.style.removeProperty('--pointer-y');
    };

    el.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove, { passive: true });
    el.addEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);

    return () => {
      el.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
      el.removeEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);
      el.style.removeProperty('--pointer-x');
      el.style.removeProperty('--pointer-y');
    };
  }, []);

  /* The gradient definition lives here and only here. The handler above never
     mentions colours, sizes or stops — it only moves the centre.

     No `transition`: an unregistered custom property is an untyped token, so
     the browser cannot interpolate it and a transition on the gradient would
     silently do nothing. Making the leave ease would mean registering the
     properties with `@property { syntax: '<percentage>' }` in a stylesheet,
     which is a real option but not a free one. The snap back is acceptable
     here because the glow at rest is barely above the background. */
  const style = {
    '--pointer-x': REST_X,
    '--pointer-y': REST_Y,
    backgroundImage: `radial-gradient(${glowWidth} ${glowHeight} at var(--pointer-x) var(--pointer-y), color-mix(in oklab, var(--k-accent) ${Math.round(
      intensity * 100,
    )}%, transparent), transparent 68%)`,
  } as CSSProperties;
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes the two pointer listeners and removes both custom properties from the element, so a remount starts from the declared rest position rather than inheriting the last pointer location. Nothing else was ever allocated — no frame loop, no tween, no observer.

**Reduced motion.** Unchanged, and intentionally so. Nothing here animates: the gradient centre tracks the pointer one-to-one with no easing, no inertia and no continuing motion after input stops. Suppressing it would remove a hover affordance rather than a motion effect.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Rebuilding the whole `background` string in JavaScript on every move. The browser re-parses every layer, including the static one, and you have moved a CSS declaration into a hot event handler where it will drift out of sync with the stylesheet.
- Expecting a `transition` on the gradient to smooth the leave. An unregistered custom property is an untyped token and cannot be interpolated, so the transition silently does nothing and there is no warning anywhere. Smoothing requires `@property { syntax: "<percentage>"; inherits: false; initial-value: 50% }` in a real stylesheet.
- Writing pixel values instead of percentages. They are correct only until the element resizes, at which point the glow is offset by however much the box changed and stays wrong until the next pointer move.
- Wrapping the write in `requestAnimationFrame`. It adds a frame of latency to a write that was never the bottleneck. rAF batching is for handlers that read layout; this one does not.
- Setting the properties on `document.documentElement` instead of the element. Every subtree that uses the same variable names then responds to a pointer that is nowhere near it, and two instances on one page fight over the same two globals.
- Reading `getBoundingClientRect()` and caching it. The rect is cheap here because nothing in this component writes layout, so there is no forced reflow to avoid — but a cached rect goes stale on scroll, which is the actual bug people ship trying to optimise this.

## Notes

- Gated on `(pointer: fine)`. On touch no listener attaches at all: `pointermove` only fires mid-drag, so the glow would follow the finger that is scrolling and be abandoned wherever it lifted. The inline rest position remains, so touch users get a composed static gradient rather than a blank panel.
- No reduced-motion branch is needed and none is present. There is no animation to reduce — the glow does not move on its own, does not ease, and does not persist after the pointer leaves. It is a hover state that happens to be continuous.
- The glow colour is `color-mix(in oklab, var(--k-accent) N%, transparent)` so it follows the category accent and the light/dark theme without a second code path.
- This is the cheapest component in the cursor category. If an effect can be expressed this way it should be, and the interesting question about any pointer effect is why it cannot.

## Definition of done

Move across the panel and a soft accent glow follows the pointer exactly, with no lag and no easing. Leave and it snaps back above centre. Resize the panel while the pointer is stationary and the glow stays in the same relative position rather than sliding. Open DevTools and confirm the element has exactly two inline custom properties changing and that no `background` or `background-image` value is being rewritten. On touch the glow never moves.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Pooled Cursor Image Trail

Sweeping the pointer across the panel drops a trail of tiles behind it, each fading up over 220ms, holding, and fading out — total life 520ms. The tiles come from a fixed ring of 22 nodes created once at mount and reused by index, and a new one is only released when the pointer has travelled more than 130px since the last. Those two rules are the component; the tween values are decoration.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Tiles drop behind the cursor from a fixed ring of 22 reused nodes, one every 130px of travel.

- Category: cursor
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. A ring of `poolSize` absolutely-positioned canvases is rendered once, all with `will-change: transform` so layer promotion has already happened before the first spawn. Nothing is ever created or removed after mount.
2. `plateCount` gradient plates are painted into offscreen canvases at mount — the registry ships no image assets, so the "photographs" are drawn. A spawn is then a single `drawImage` blit, which keeps the gradient and text work off the frame where a tween starts.
3. On `pointermove` the handler measures `Math.hypot(x - anchor.x, y - anchor.y)` against the last spawn point and returns early below `threshold`. The very first move only seeds the anchor and spawns nothing, so entering from an edge does not drop a tile before any real movement has happened.
4. A spawn takes slot `spawned % poolSize`, picks a plate with a seeded RNG plus a one-line no-repeat guard (`if (i === last) i = (i + 1) % n`), blits it, then `gsap.killTweensOf(node)` before `gsap.set` reinitialises x, y, rotation, scale 0.92, opacity 0 and `zIndex: spawned`.
5. `zIndex` is the monotonically increasing spawn counter, so the newest tile always paints over older ones with no stacking logic at all. At ten spawns a second it would take roughly 285,000 years to reach `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.
6. The life is one timeline: in over 220ms with `power2.out`, hold 100ms, out over 200ms with `power2.in`. The pool is sized so a slot's 520ms life always expires before the ring wraps back around to it.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `threshold = 130`
  Pixels of travel per tile, and the single most load-bearing number here. A deliberate sweep across a hero yields 8-10 readable tiles; small jitters yield none. Drop it toward 20 and a flick produces a solid smear of overlapping tiles; raise it past ~250 and normal mouse movement never triggers the effect at all.
- `poolSize = 22`
  The ring must not wrap while a tile is still visible. At 520ms of life you would have to move 22 x 130 = 2860px in 520ms to catch your own tail — a flick nobody performs by accident.
- `plateCount = 17`
  Deliberately coprime with the 22 slots, so the plate-to-slot pairing never settles into a short repeating pattern as the ring advances. Also fewer plates than slots, so the memory cost is bounded independently of pool size.
- `IN_DURATION / HOLD / OUT_DURATION = 0.22 / 0.1 / 0.2`
  520ms total. Fast in with `power2.out` (arrives), a beat of stillness so the tile is actually readable, then a `power2.in` exit (leaves). Collapse the hold and the trail reads as a blur instead of as a sequence of pictures.
- `START_SCALE = 0.92`
  An 8% growth on entry. Enough to read as arriving, small enough not to pop — at 0.7 it looks like a modal opening.
- `TILT = 7`
  Degrees of seeded rotation either way. Perfectly square tiles read as UI panels; a few degrees reads as prints dropped on a table. Past ~12 the corners of successive tiles collide and the trail looks untidy.
- `PLATE_SCALE = 2`
  Backing-store multiplier for the plate canvases. Fixed rather than `devicePixelRatio` so the drawn output is byte-identical on every machine and a visual regression is actually visible.

## API

```ts
function PooledImageTrail(props: { children?: ReactNode; threshold?: number; poolSize?: number; plateCount?: number; tileWidth?: number; tileHeight?: number; seed?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Content rendered above the trail layer.
- `threshold: number` — default `130`
  Pixels of pointer travel required before another tile is released.
- `poolSize: number` — default `22`
  Number of reusable nodes in the ring.
- `plateCount: number` — default `17`
  Distinct plates painted at mount. Keep coprime with poolSize.
- `tileWidth: number` — default `236`
  Tile width in CSS px.
- `tileHeight: number` — default `160`
  Tile height in CSS px.
- `seed: string` — default `'pooled-image-trail'`
  Seeds plate choice and tilt so the sequence is deterministic.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root container via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const IN_DURATION = 0.22;
const HOLD = 0.1;
const OUT_DURATION = 0.2;
const START_SCALE = 0.92;
const TILT = 7;

export function PooledImageTrail({
  children,
  threshold = 130,
  poolSize = 22,
  plateCount = 17,
  tileWidth = 236,
  tileHeight = 160,
  seed = 'pooled-image-trail',
  className,
}: PooledImageTrailProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const slots = useRef<Array<HTMLCanvasElement | null>>([]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = root.current;
    if (!el) return;

    const nodes: HTMLCanvasElement[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < poolSize; i++) {
      const node = slots.current[i];
      if (node) nodes.push(node);
    }
    if (nodes.length === 0) return;

    const bw = tileWidth * PLATE_SCALE;
    const bh = tileHeight * PLATE_SCALE;

    // Paint every plate once, offscreen. A spawn is then a single blit; if the
    // plate were drawn at spawn time the gradient + text work would land on
    // the same frame as the tween start, which is the one frame that must not
    // drop.
    const plates: HTMLCanvasElement[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < plateCount; i++) {
      const plate = document.createElement('canvas');
      plate.width = bw;
      plate.height = bh;
      const pctx = plate.getContext('2d');
      if (!pctx) break;
      pctx.scale(PLATE_SCALE, PLATE_SCALE);
      paintPlate(pctx, tileWidth, tileHeight, i);
      plates.push(plate);
    }
    if (plates.length === 0) return;

    const contexts = nodes.map((node) => {
      node.width = bw;
      node.height = bh;
      return node.getContext('2d');
    });

    const reduced = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
    const fine = window.matchMedia('(pointer: fine)').matches;

    gsap.set(nodes, { xPercent: 0, yPercent: 0, opacity: 0, force3D: true });

    if (reduced || !fine) {
      // Poster fallback: three plates fanned in the middle, drawn once. The
      // panel is composed rather than empty, and nothing ever moves.
      const shown = Math.min(3, nodes.length, plates.length);
      for (let i = 0; i < shown; i++) {
        const ctx = contexts[i];
        const plate = plates[i % plates.length];
        const node = nodes[i];
        if (!ctx || !plate || !node) continue;
        ctx.drawImage(plate, 0, 0);
        gsap.set(node, {
          x: el.clientWidth / 2 - tileWidth / 2 + (i - 1) * tileWidth * 0.42,
          y: el.clientHeight / 2 - tileHeight / 2 + (i - 1) * 14,
          rotate: (i - 1) * 4,
          opacity: 1,
          zIndex: i,
        });
      }
      return () => {
        gsap.killTweensOf(nodes);
        gsap.set(nodes, { clearProps: 'all' });
      };
    }

    const rng = createRng(seed);
    /** Monotonic. Doubles as the ring index and as the z-index. */
    let spawned = 0;
    /** Where the last tile was dropped. `null` until the first move seeds it. */
    let anchor: { x: number; y: number } | null = null;
    let lastPlate = -1;

    const onMove = (e: PointerEvent) => {
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      const x = e.clientX - rect.left;
      const y = e.clientY - rect.top;

      // First move seeds the anchor and spawns nothing. Otherwise the initial
      // distance is measured from (0, 0) and entering from the right-hand side
      // of a wide panel drops a tile immediately, before any real movement.
      if (anchor === null) {
        anchor = { x, y };
        return;
      }
      if (Math.hypot(x - anchor.x, y - anchor.y) < threshold) return;
      anchor = { x, y };

      const slot = spawned % nodes.length;
      const node = nodes[slot];
      const ctx = contexts[slot];
      if (!node || !ctx) return;
      spawned++;

      // One-line no-repeat guard. It does not attempt a uniform distribution,
      // because the only thing the eye actually notices is the same picture
      // twice in a row.
      let plateIndex = Math.floor(rng() * plates.length);
      if (plateIndex === lastPlate) plateIndex = (plateIndex + 1) % plates.length;
      lastPlate = plateIndex;
      const plate = plates[plateIndex];
      if (!plate) return;

      ctx.clearRect(0, 0, bw, bh);
      ctx.drawImage(plate, 0, 0);

      // Kill before reuse. A slot recycled while still fading out would carry
      // two competing tweens on `opacity` and visibly flicker.
      gsap.killTweensOf(node);
      gsap.set(node, {
        x: x - tileWidth / 2,
        y: y - tileHeight / 2,
        rotate: randRange(rng, -TILT, TILT),
        scale: START_SCALE,
        opacity: 0,
        // Monotonic z-index: the newest tile always paints over older ones and
        // there is no stacking logic to maintain.
        zIndex: spawned,
      });

      gsap
        .timeline()
        .to(node, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: IN_DURATION, ease: 'power2.out' })
        .to(node, { opacity: 0, duration: OUT_DURATION, ease: 'power2.in' }, `+=${HOLD}`);
    };

    el.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove, { passive: true });

    return () => {
      el.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
      gsap.killTweensOf(nodes);
      gsap.set(nodes, { clearProps: 'all' });
    };
  }, [threshold, poolSize, plateCount, tileWidth, tileHeight, seed]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes the single `pointermove` listener, calls `gsap.killTweensOf` on every pool node — which also kills the per-spawn timelines, since they only target those nodes — then `gsap.set(nodes, { clearProps: "all" })`. The offscreen plate canvases are plain locals and are collected with the closure; nothing was allocated that needs revoking.

**Reduced motion.** No listener attaches and nothing animates. Three plates are drawn once into the first three pool slots, fanned across the centre with a few degrees of rotation each, so the panel is a composed still of what the effect produces rather than an empty rectangle.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Creating an element per spawn. A fast sweep across a wide hero allocates a hundred nodes, each forcing a style recalc, a layer promotion and a paint at the exact moment the main thread is busiest — the trail stutters precisely when it is being used hardest.
- Spawning on every `pointermove` instead of on distance travelled. Events fire on sub-pixel movement, so a flick produces a solid smear and a slow drift produces a dense clump; "moved" and "moved enough" are different predicates.
- Measuring the first move against a zeroed anchor. The distance from (0, 0) to wherever the pointer entered is usually well over the threshold, so a tile fires the instant the pointer crosses the boundary, before any movement has happened.
- Reusing a slot without `gsap.killTweensOf(node)` first. If the ring wraps onto a tile that is still fading out, two tweens fight over `opacity` and it flickers rather than restarting cleanly.
- Recomputing z-order from tile ages. A monotonic counter is correct, free, and cannot get out of sync; sorting is a whole class of bug bought for nothing.
- Painting the gradient plate at spawn time. The gradient fill, the radial sheen and the text layout all land on the same frame as the tween start, which is the one frame in the effect that must not drop. Paint once at mount and blit.
- Omitting `will-change: transform` from the pool. The browser promotes the tile to its own layer partway through its 220ms entry, so the first frames of every spawn are visibly cheaper-looking than the rest.

## Notes

- Gated on `(pointer: fine)`. On touch a `pointermove` only exists during a drag, so the trail would appear only under a finger that is already covering it and would then be stranded mid-life on lift. The touch path renders the same static fan as reduced motion.
- The tiles sit behind the content layer (`z-0` under a `z-10` child wrapper) so headline copy stays readable while the trail passes under it.
- Plate choice runs on `createRng(seed)`, never `Math.random()`, so the sequence is identical on every load and across a server render.

## Definition of done

Sweep the pointer slowly across the panel and tiles drop behind it roughly every 130px, each readable for about half a second before fading. Jiggle the pointer in place and nothing spawns. Flick as fast as you can and you get a spaced trail, not a smear, and no tile ever restarts mid-fade with a flicker. Enter the panel from an edge and no tile appears until you have actually moved. On touch or with reduced motion you see three static fanned plates.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Popover

A non-modal surface for a share link, a short form or the explanation behind an info icon, anchored to its trigger with React Aria's `DialogTrigger`, `Popover` and `Dialog`. It positions and flips itself, Escape closes it and focus returns to the trigger. It opens with the menu family's 150ms fade, 0.95 scale and 2px blur, grown from the point nearest the trigger, and can draw Tooltip's caret pointing back at it.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Free-form content anchored to a trigger, with an optional arrow, smart positioning and the menu family's motion, built on React Aria.

- Category: overlay
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `PopoverTrigger` owns the open state (controlled `isOpen` or uncontrolled `defaultOpen`) and keeps two refs in context: `triggerRef` on a `Pressable` wrapped around the first child (so any kit button that forwards its ref works as the trigger) and `popoverRef`, which `Popover` attaches to the surface. The remaining children go through to `AriaDialogTrigger`.
2. The popover is non-modal (`isNonModal` whenever it sits inside `PopoverTrigger`): React Aria's modal popovers lock page scroll and the reflow shunts sticky layout. Because non-modal popovers lose outside-press dismissal, `useDismissOnOutsidePress` adds a capture-phase `pointerdown` listener on `document` that closes it when a press lands outside both refs.
3. `useTriggerToggle` watches for a `pointerdown` on the trigger while open and swallows the reopen that would follow, so `onOpenChange` is gated by `allowOpenChange(next)` and pressing the trigger again closes the popover instead of flickering it closed and open.
4. `Popover` renders `AriaPopover` with `placement` defaulting to "bottom", `offset` 10 with the arrow or 8 without, `dir` from `useDirection()`, and the surface classes `z-110 w-80 max-w-[calc(100vw-32px)] rounded-[20px] border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default p-1.5 shadow-dropdown`.
5. Motion is CSS on React Aria's state attributes: `origin-(--trigger-anchor-point)` grows the surface from the point nearest the trigger, `transition-[opacity,scale,filter] duration-150 ease-out`, `data-[entering]` / `data-[exiting]` set `opacity-0`, and `motion-safe:` adds `scale-95` and `blur-[2px]`. React Aria keeps the popover mounted until the exit transition finishes.
6. With `showArrow`, an `OverlayArrow` render prop reads the resolved `placement` and draws the matching SVG path from `TOOLTIP_CARETS` (imported from Tooltip) with `fill-background-primary-default stroke-border-button-default` and a placement-specific 5% black drop shadow, so the caret flips with the popover. The content sits in an `AriaDialog` with `flex flex-col gap-3 p-2.5`; `PopoverHeader` renders the title as `Heading slot="title"` so it names the dialog.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `offset = 8px, or 10px with the arrow`
  The extra 2px makes room for the caret so its tip, not the surface, sits 8px from the trigger.
- `width = w-80 (320px), max-w-[calc(100vw-32px)]`
  A comfortable measure for a sentence or a short form; the cap keeps a 16px gutter on each side on a phone.
- `motion = 150ms ease-out, scale 0.95, blur 2px`
  The same values as Select and Dropdown so every anchored surface in the kit opens alike; small scale and blur read as "growing out of the trigger" without drifting.
- `surface = rounded-[20px], p-1.5 outer + p-2.5 inner`
  The composer permission popover's recipe: the outer 6px padding lets menu-like rows (with `dialogClassName="p-0"`) sit inset with their own radius.
- `z-index = z-110`
  Above Modal and Drawer overlays (z-100), so a popover opened from inside a dialog is not hidden behind it.

## API

```ts
function PopoverTrigger(props: { isOpen?: boolean; defaultOpen?: boolean; onOpenChange?: (isOpen: boolean) => void; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
function Popover(props: Pick<AriaPopoverProps, "placement" | "offset" | "crossOffset" | "shouldFlip" | "containerPadding" | "triggerRef" | "isOpen" | "onOpenChange"> & { showArrow?: boolean; "aria-label"?: string; className?: string; dialogClassName?: string; children: ReactNode | ((renderProps: DialogRenderProps) => ReactNode) }): JSX.Element
function PopoverHeader(props: { title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function PopoverFooter(props: { className?: string; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
```

- `showArrow: boolean` — default `false`
  Draw a caret pointing at the trigger; bumps the offset from 8 to 10px.
- `placement: Placement` — default `"bottom"`
  Preferred side; React Aria flips it when there is no room.
- `offset: number` — default `8 (10 with arrow)`
  Distance from the trigger in pixels.
- `className: string`
  Classes on the surface, e.g. a width other than the default 320px.
- `dialogClassName: string`
  Classes on the inner dialog; `p-0` suits menu-like rows that pad themselves.
- `aria-label: string`
  Accessible name when the content has no PopoverHeader title.
- `PopoverTrigger.isOpen / onOpenChange: boolean / (isOpen: boolean) => void`
  Controlled open state; `defaultOpen` for uncontrolled.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function PopoverTrigger({ isOpen: controlledOpen, defaultOpen = false, onOpenChange, children }: PopoverTriggerProps) {
  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
  const popoverRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
  const [uncontrolledOpen, setUncontrolledOpen] = useState(defaultOpen);
  const isOpen = controlledOpen ?? uncontrolledOpen;
  const setOpen = (next: boolean) => {
    setUncontrolledOpen(next);
    onOpenChange?.(next);
  };

  useDismissOnOutsidePress(isOpen, () => setOpen(false), [triggerRef, popoverRef]);
  // Pressing the trigger while open closes the popover instead of reopening it.
  const allowOpenChange = useTriggerToggle(isOpen, triggerRef);

  const [trigger, ...rest] = Children.toArray(children);
  return (
    <PopoverContext.Provider value={{ popoverRef }}>
      <AriaDialogTrigger isOpen={isOpen} onOpenChange={(next) => allowOpenChange(next) && setOpen(next)}>
        {isValidElement(trigger) ? (
          <Pressable ref={triggerRef}>{trigger as ReactElement<Record<string, unknown>, string>}</Pressable>
        ) : (
          trigger
        )}
        {rest}
      </AriaDialogTrigger>
    </PopoverContext.Provider>
  );
}

export interface PopoverProps
  extends Pick<AriaPopoverProps, "placement" | "offset" | "crossOffset" | "shouldFlip" | "containerPadding" | "triggerRef" | "isOpen" | "onOpenChange"> {
  /** Draw a caret pointing at the trigger. */
  showArrow?: boolean;
  /** Accessible name when the content has no PopoverHeader title. */
  "aria-label"?: string;
  /** Classes on the surface, e.g. a width (default 320px). */
  className?: string;
  /** Classes on the inner dialog; `p-0` suits menu-like rows that pad themselves. */
  dialogClassName?: string;
  children: ReactNode | ((renderProps: DialogRenderProps) => ReactNode);
}

export function Popover({
  showArrow = false,
  placement = "bottom",
  offset,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel,
  className,
  dialogClassName,
  children,
  ...props
}: PopoverProps) {
  const context = useContext(PopoverContext);
  const direction = useDirection();

  return (
    <AriaPopover
      {...props}
      ref={context?.popoverRef}
      dir={direction}
      // Standalone (triggerRef + isOpen) popovers keep React Aria's own
      // dismissal; inside PopoverTrigger the trigger restores it.
      isNonModal={context != null}
      placement={placement}
      offset={offset ?? (showArrow ? 10 : 8)}
      className={cx(
        "z-110 w-80 max-w-[calc(100vw-32px)]",
        "rounded-[20px] border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default p-1.5 shadow-dropdown",
        "origin-(--trigger-anchor-point) transition-[opacity,scale,filter] duration-150 ease-out",
        "data-[entering]:opacity-0 data-[exiting]:opacity-0",
        "motion-safe:data-[entering]:scale-95 motion-safe:data-[entering]:blur-[2px]",
        "motion-safe:data-[exiting]:scale-95 motion-safe:data-[exiting]:blur-[2px]",
        className,
      )}
    >
      {showArrow ? (
        <AriaOverlayArrow>
          {({ placement: side }) => {
            const caret = TOOLTIP_CARETS[side as keyof typeof TOOLTIP_CARETS] ?? TOOLTIP_CARETS.top;
            return (
              <svg
                width={caret.width}
                height={caret.height}
                viewBox={`0 0 ${caret.width} ${caret.height}`}
                className="block overflow-visible fill-background-primary-default stroke-border-button-default"
                style={{ filter: `drop-shadow(${caret.shadow} rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05))` }}
              >
                <path d={caret.path} />
              </svg>
            );
          }}
        </AriaOverlayArrow>
      ) : null}
      <AriaDialog aria-label={ariaLabel} className={cx("flex flex-col gap-3 p-2.5 outline-none", dialogClassName)}>
        {children}
      </AriaDialog>
    </AriaPopover>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The two `pointerdown` capture listeners on `document` are added only while the popover is open and removed in their effect cleanups when it closes or unmounts. React Aria restores focus to the trigger on close.

**Reduced motion.** The scale and blur are behind `motion-safe:`, so under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the popover only fades in and out over 150ms.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not switch the popover to modal to get outside-press dismissal. Modal popovers lock page scroll and shift sticky layout; dismissal comes from the capture-phase `pointerdown` listener instead.
- Do not drop the trigger toggle. Without `useTriggerToggle`, pressing the trigger of an open popover closes it on the outside press and immediately reopens it.
- Do not put the transform origin at the centre. `origin-(--trigger-anchor-point)` is what makes it grow from the trigger after a flip.
- Do not hard-code the caret to one side. The arrow must read `placement` from `OverlayArrow` because React Aria can flip the popover when there is no room.

## Notes

- A standalone `Popover` (outside `PopoverTrigger`, positioned with `triggerRef` and `isOpen`) keeps React Aria's own modal dismissal, because `isNonModal` is only set when the context exists.
- The caret geometry is shared with Tooltip through the exported `TOOLTIP_CARETS` map, so both overlays draw the same arrow.

## Definition of done

Pressing "Details" grows a 320px popover with a caret out of the button over about 150ms; pressing the button again, clicking anywhere outside, or pressing Escape closes it with the reverse motion and focus returns to the button. The page stays scrollable while it is open. The Share popover opens above its button and flips below when there is no room, with "Copy link" and "Done" inside.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Pre-Scatter Horizontal Gallery

A pinned horizontal strip whose media is deliberately off-grid: every item gets a small seeded resting offset, then rides in from ahead of its slot and runs out behind it, rotating through zero on the way past. Two `fromTo` pairs per item — one entry, one exit — measured against the strip's own tween rather than against scroll position, so the choreography is a property of where an item is in the container, not of where the page is.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A pinned strip where each item rests slightly off its slot, flies in from ahead and peels away behind.

- Category: scroll
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. The component owns a `PinnedHorizontalTrack` and captures its `onTrack` payload in state. The strip's tween is built in the child's effect and therefore arrives one commit late, which is why it is state and not a ref — the arrival has to re-run the builder.
2. Every `[data-scatter]` element draws one value from `createRng(seed)`: `rest = (rng() - 0.5) * scatter`, a resting `xPercent` offset. It is applied with `gsap.set` for every item whether or not it animates, so the composition is identical with motion on and off.
3. The entry is `fromTo(el, { xPercent: rest + sweep, yPercent: dir * lift, rotation: dir * rotation }, { xPercent: rest, yPercent: 0, rotation: 0 })` scrubbed over `left 110%` to `left 65%` — the item lags behind its slot and catches up as it crosses the container.
4. The exit is the mirror: `fromTo(el, { xPercent: rest, yPercent: 0, rotation: 0 }, { xPercent: rest - sweep, yPercent: -dir * lift, rotation: -dir * rotation })` over `right 35%` to `right -10%`, with `immediateRender: false` so it does not overwrite the entry's from-state at creation.
5. `dir` alternates by index parity, so odd items throw up and rotate clockwise while even items do the opposite, and the rotation passes continuously through zero between the two ranges.
6. Both triggers take `containerAnimation: track.animation` and horizontal position keywords, so ScrollTrigger measures each item along the strip's timeline instead of down the page.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `scatter = 32`
  Total resting spread as a percentage of the item's own width, i.e. ±16%. Below ~10 the grid still reads as a grid and the effect is invisible; above ~50 items collide with their neighbours' captions and it reads as a layout bug rather than a composition.
- `sweep = 400`
  Horizontal lag on entry and lead on exit, as a percentage of item width. Four widths is enough that the item is genuinely off-stage at the start of its range, so the catch-up is a travel rather than a nudge. Under ~150 the item is already visible when its tween begins and appears to jerk into place.
- `lift = 150`
  Vertical throw as a percentage of item height. At 100 the item starts exactly one height away, so its edge is still touching the frame; 150 clears the frame with margin, which is what makes it read as flying in rather than sliding.
- `rotation = 40°`
  Peak tilt. Under ~15° the rotation is mistaken for a rendering artefact; past ~60° the item is legibly upside-down at the extremes and text inside it becomes unreadable during the travel.
- `ENTER_START / ENTER_END = 'left 110%' / 'left 65%'`
  The item's leading edge, measured along the container. Starting past 100% means the tween begins before the item is visible, so nothing pops in already moving. Ending at 65% leaves the middle third of the crossing settled.
- `EXIT_START / EXIT_END = 'right 35%' / 'right -10%'`
  The trailing edge. Ending below 0% carries the item fully past the left frame before the tween completes, so it never freezes half-visible at the edge. The two ranges cannot overlap for any item narrower than 1.3 containers.
- `item scrub = true`
  Locked to the container animation, not a number. These triggers read the strip's progress, and the strip already scrubs with a second of catch-up, so a numeric scrub here smooths an already-smoothed signal and the items swim behind the panels they belong to.

## API

```ts
function PrescatterHorizontalGallery(props: { children: ReactNode; scroller?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; seed?: number | string; scatter?: number; rotation?: number; lift?: number; sweep?: number; scrub?: number; className?: string; trackClassName?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Panels for the strip. Give each a width and `shrink-0`, and mark the media inside `data-scatter`.
- `scroller: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>`
  Scroll container the triggers read. Omit for the document.
- `seed: number | string` — default `'gallery'`
  Anything hashable. The same seed rebuilds the same composition.
- `scatter: number` — default `32`
  Total resting spread as a percentage of item width.
- `rotation: number` — default `40`
  Peak tilt in degrees, alternating by index.
- `lift: number` — default `150`
  Vertical throw as a percentage of item height.
- `sweep: number` — default `400`
  Horizontal lag and lead as a percentage of item width.
- `scrub: number` — default `1`
  Seconds of catch-up on the strip, forwarded to the pinned track.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the gallery wrapper.
- `trackClassName: string`
  Merged onto the moving strip.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * The item's leading edge crosses the container from just off the right
 * (110%) to two thirds in (65%), and its trailing edge leaves from a third in
 * (35%) to just past the left (-10%). The two ranges cannot overlap for any
 * item narrower than 1.3 containers, so every item gets a settled window in
 * the middle where it is simply itself.
 */
const ENTER_START = 'left 110%';
const ENTER_END = 'left 65%';
const EXIT_START = 'right 35%';
const EXIT_END = 'right -10%';

export function PrescatterHorizontalGallery({
  children,
  scroller,
  seed = 'gallery',
  scatter = 32,
  rotation = 40,
  lift = 150,
  sweep = 400,
  scrub = 1,
  className,
  trackClassName,
}: PrescatterHorizontalGalleryProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  // The strip's tween is built in a child's effect, so it arrives one commit
  // late. State, not a ref: the arrival has to re-run the builder below.
  const [track, setTrack] = useState<PinnedTrack | null>(null);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  useEffect(() => {
    const rootEl = root.current;
    if (!rootEl) return;

    const containerAnimation = track?.animation;
    const scrollerEl = scroller?.current ?? undefined;

    const ctx = gsap.context(() => {
      const targets = Array.from(rootEl.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-scatter]'));
      const rng = createRng(seed);

      targets.forEach((el, i) => {
        // Drawn for every item whether or not it animates, so adding motion
        // never shifts the resting composition.
        const rest = (rng() - 0.5) * scatter;
        // Parity, not the generator: alternating up/down and cw/ccw is a
        // rhythm, and a random sign clumps three the same way and looks broken.
        const dir = i % 2 === 0 ? 1 : -1;

        gsap.set(el, { xPercent: rest });
        // The resting scatter is layout. Under reduced motion the composition
        // survives and only the flight is dropped.
        if (reduced || !containerAnimation) return;

        gsap.fromTo(
          el,
          { xPercent: rest + sweep, yPercent: dir * lift, rotation: dir * rotation },
          {
            xPercent: rest,
            yPercent: 0,
            rotation: 0,
            ease: 'none',
            scrollTrigger: {
              trigger: el,
              scroller: scrollerEl,
              containerAnimation,
              start: ENTER_START,
              end: ENTER_END,
              // `true`, not a number. The strip already scrubs with catch-up,
              // and these triggers read the strip's progress rather than the
              // scrollbar, so they inherit that smoothing. A second scrub
              // value smooths the smoothed signal and the items swim.
              scrub: true,
            },
          },
        );

        gsap.fromTo(
          el,
          { xPercent: rest, yPercent: 0, rotation: 0 },
          {
            xPercent: rest - sweep,
            yPercent: -dir * lift,
            rotation: -dir * rotation,
            ease: 'none',
            // The single most important line here. A `fromTo` renders its
            // from-state at creation, so without this the exit immediately
            // overwrites the entry's from-state — every item starts on the
            // grid instead of off-stage, and the entry appears not to exist.
            immediateRender: false,
            scrollTrigger: {
              trigger: el,
              scroller: scrollerEl,
              containerAnimation,
              start: EXIT_START,
              end: EXIT_END,
              scrub: true,
            },
          },
        );
      });
    }, rootEl);

    return () => ctx.revert();
  }, [track, scroller, seed, scatter, rotation, lift, sweep, reduced]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** One `gsap.context` scoped to the root holds the `set` calls and both tweens per item, so `ctx.revert()` kills every tween, kills every ScrollTrigger, and strips the inline transforms back off the media. It runs on unmount and on every dependency change, including the commit where the strip's tween arrives.

**Reduced motion.** The resting scatter is still applied — it is layout, not motion, and the gallery is supposed to look deliberately off-grid. What is dropped is the flight: no entry or exit triggers are created, so every item sits at its offset from first paint. The pinned track also declines to pin, so the strip becomes a horizontally scrollable row and every item stays reachable.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using `gsap.to` for the exit. A `to` records its start values when it is created, which is after the entry has already rendered its from-state — so the exit animates from `xPercent: rest + sweep` and the item never returns to its slot.
- Using a second `fromTo` for the exit without `immediateRender: false`. A `fromTo` writes its from-state immediately, so the later tween wins and every item starts on the grid: the entry animation exists, runs, and is invisible.
- Keeping vertical position keywords with a `containerAnimation`. `start: "top 110%"` on a horizontal container resolves to a position the element never occupies. No error, no warning, no animation — the items simply arrive pre-placed.
- Measuring the scatter in pixels off the container width. It has to be recomputed on every ScrollTrigger refresh or the composition creeps as the window resizes; expressed as `xPercent` it resolves against the element and never needs invalidating.
- `Math.random()` for the offsets. The server and the client disagree at hydration, and the composition is different on every reload, so nobody can tell a regression from a reroll.
- Building the item triggers before the strip's tween exists. Treating `undefined` as "no container animation" builds a full set of vertical triggers on horizontal content and tears them down on the next commit — a visible flash of items that were already in place.
- Alternating direction from the generator instead of from the index. A random sign lands three items the same way often enough to look like a bug, where parity always reads as rhythm.

## Notes

- Mark the media, not the panel: `data-scatter` on an inner element lets the panel keep the caption on the grid while the image drifts off it.
- ScrollTrigger forbids `pin` on a trigger that has a `containerAnimation`. The strip's section is pinned by `PinnedHorizontalTrack`; the items riding it are never pinned.
- Panels need `overflow: visible` for the sweep to be seen. Clipping happens once, at the pinned section's edge.

## Definition of done

Scroll into the section: it pins, the strip travels sideways, and each item swings in from ahead of its slot, straightens, holds through the middle of the crossing, then tilts the other way and runs out to the left. Scroll back up and every item reverses along the same path. Note that no two items rest exactly on the grid, and that reloading gives the identical composition. With reduced motion on, the items are already at their offsets and the strip can be swiped by hand.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Preview Code Tabs

The two-tab frame that sits at the top of a component docs page. A grey pill track holds "Preview" and "Code" tabs, with a white thumb that slides to the selected tab. Below it, a bordered stage renders the live example centred, or a code block shows the example source with line numbers and copy. The preview stays mounted while the code tab is open, so whatever the reader did to the example survives a look at the code.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Docs Preview / Code switcher: a pill tab track with a sliding thumb over a bordered live stage and a highlighted, copyable source.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. React Aria `Tabs`, `TabList`, `Tab` and `TabPanel` supply the roles, `aria-controls` wiring, roving focus and arrow, Home and End keys. Selection is controlled through `selectedTab` or uncontrolled through `defaultSelectedTab`, and only the two known keys reach `onSelectedTabChange`.
2. A collection can only contain `Tab` children, so the thumb is a sibling of the `TabList` inside a positioned track. A layout effect reads the selected tab's `offsetLeft`, `offsetTop`, `offsetWidth` and `offsetHeight` and applies them as a translate plus width and height, which a 200ms `ease-out` transition animates.
3. A `MutationObserver` filtered to `data-selected` re-measures on every selection change, controlled or not. A `ResizeObserver` on the track and each tab re-measures when fonts load or labels change. The state setter returns the previous object when nothing moved, so the observers never cause a render loop.
4. The preview `TabPanel` uses `shouldForceMount`. While the code tab is selected, React Aria marks it `inert` and the render-prop class adds `hidden`, so it leaves focus order and layout but keeps its React state.
5. The code tab renders the kit `CodeBlock` (TSX tokenizer, line numbers, wrap toggle, copy) with the `filename` chip and a `codeMaxHeight` cap. The `actions` slot at the end of the tab row takes extra controls such as a copy or open-in-new-tab button.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `thumb transition = 200 ms ease-out on transform, width, height`
  Fast enough to keep up with arrow-key presses, and slow enough that the eye can follow the thumb between two tabs of different widths.
- `track / thumb radii = rounded-xl track, p-1, rounded-lg thumb`
  The thumb sits 4px inside the track, so a 12px outer and 8px inner radius stay concentric.
- `stage = rounded-[20px], border-button-default, background-full, p-6 to p-10, minHeight 320 (code panel too)`
  The code panel shares the floor so the page does not jump between tabs. A calm, slightly rounder frame than the cards it shows, with room on every side so a centred example never touches the edge.
- `codeMaxHeight = 420 px`
  Long sources scroll inside the panel rather than pushing the rest of the page down when the reader switches tabs.

## API

```ts
type PreviewCodeTab = "preview" | "code";
function PreviewCodeTabs(props: { children: ReactNode; code: string; filename?: string; language?: "tsx" | "plain"; selectedTab?: PreviewCodeTab; defaultSelectedTab?: PreviewCodeTab; onSelectedTabChange?: (tab: PreviewCodeTab) => void; actions?: ReactNode; previewLabel?: string; codeLabel?: string; "aria-label"?: string; minHeight?: number; codeMaxHeight?: number; onCopied?: (code: string) => void; previewClassName?: string; className?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  The live example, centred in the preview stage.
- `code: string`

- `filename: string`

- `minHeight: number` — default `320`
  Minimum height of the preview stage, in px.
- `codeMaxHeight: number` — default `420`
  Height cap of the code panel, in px.
- `onCopied: (code: string) => void`
  Called after the code panel copies.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// The thumb is a sibling of the TabList (a collection can only hold Tabs), so
// it is positioned from the selected tab's offset box inside the track. A
// ResizeObserver catches font loading and label changes; a MutationObserver
// on `data-selected` catches selection, controlled or not.
useIsomorphicLayoutEffect(() => {
  const track = trackRef.current;
  if (!track) return;
  const measure = () => {
    const selected = track.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[role="tab"][data-selected]');
    if (!selected) return;
    setThumb((prev) => {
      const next = {
        left: selected.offsetLeft,
        top: selected.offsetTop,
        width: selected.offsetWidth,
        height: selected.offsetHeight,
      };
      return prev &&
        prev.left === next.left &&
        prev.top === next.top &&
        prev.width === next.width &&
        prev.height === next.height
        ? prev
        : next;
    });
  };
  measure();
  const ro = new ResizeObserver(measure);
  ro.observe(track);
  track.querySelectorAll('[role="tab"]').forEach((tab) => ro.observe(tab));
  const mo = new MutationObserver(measure);
  mo.observe(track, { attributes: true, subtree: true, attributeFilter: ["data-selected"] });
  return () => {
    mo.disconnect();
    ro.disconnect();
  };
}, []);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The layout effect disconnects its `ResizeObserver` and `MutationObserver` on unmount. There are no timers. The code panel copy timer belongs to `CodeBlock` and is cleared there.

**Reduced motion.** The only movement is the thumb slide. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the thumb has `motion-reduce:transition-none` and jumps straight to the selected tab. The tab text colour change stays because it is not motion.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Putting the thumb inside `TabList`. React Aria builds the tab collection from its children, and anything that is not a `Tab` breaks the collection. The thumb lives next to the list, in the positioned track.
- Unmounting the preview on tab change. Any state the reader built up in the example (a toggled option, a typed value) would reset every time they glanced at the code. `shouldForceMount` together with `hidden` on `isInert` avoids this.
- Measuring with `getBoundingClientRect` relative to the viewport. Page scroll and transforms on ancestors would leak into the thumb position. Offsets relative to the track do not have that problem.

## Notes

- Labels are props (`previewLabel`, `codeLabel`), and the list name defaults to "Example view".
- Pass `language="plain"` for examples that are not TSX, such as CSS or shell output.

## Definition of done

The Preview tab is selected on load and the white thumb sits under it. Clicking Code, or pressing the Right arrow with the list focused, slides the thumb under Code (200ms, instant with reduced motion), shows the highlighted source and sets `aria-selected="true"` on the Code tab. Returning to Preview shows the example with its state intact. The code panel copy button puts the exact `code` string on the clipboard.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Pricing Plan Cards

A pricing section: an optional icon tile, heading and copy, a Monthly / Yearly segmented control, and a responsive grid of plan cards. Each card is a grey shell holding two white panels (name and description on top, features below) with the price and CTA sitting on the shell between them. Switching the cycle rolls every price to its new per-month figure, strikes through the monthly price and swaps the caption for the yearly saving.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Plan cards with a monthly/yearly switch that rolls the prices, shows yearly savings, highlights one plan and lists features with icons.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The cycle is controlled-or-uncontrolled: `cycle ?? inner`, where `inner` starts at `defaultCycle`. The kit `SegmentedControl` (a React Aria single-select toggle group) feeds `onSelectionChange`, and the handler only accepts the keys "monthly" and "yearly" before calling `setInner` (when uncontrolled) and `onCycleChange`.
2. Each plan stores `price.monthly` and the annual total `price.yearly`. `perMonth()` returns the monthly price, or `yearly / 12` on the yearly cycle; `yearlySavings()` is `monthly * 12 - yearly`, clamped at 0. The best saving across paid plans, as a rounded percentage, becomes the "-21%" chip inside the Yearly segment.
3. `useTweenedNumber` rolls the displayed price from where it currently is to the new target over 360ms with an ease-out cubic in a `requestAnimationFrame` loop, writing the in-flight value back to a ref so a toggle mid-roll restarts from what is on screen. The rolling digits are `aria-hidden`; an `sr-only` sibling always holds the final formatted price.
4. Prices format through two cached `Intl.NumberFormat` instances (whole and two-decimal) built from the fixed `locale` and `currency` props, so the server and client print the same string. A plan with 0 / 0 prices renders `freeLabel` instead of a number.
5. On the yearly cycle a paid plan with a saving shows the monthly price struck through (with a hidden "was" for screen readers) and replaces the second caption line with "Save €48 a year" in the success colour. A plan with its own `caption` keeps it on both cycles.
6. The card grid is driven by a container query (`@container` on the section): one column, two from `@2xl` (42rem) and four from `@5xl` (64rem), so the block reflows by the width it is given rather than the viewport. A highlighted plan gets the primary CTA, an accent ring and its badge pill; the others use the secondary button.
7. The CTA is a `ButtonLink` when the plan has `cta.href`; otherwise a `Button` that calls `onSelectPlan(plan.id, cycle)`. Features render as a list with the given icon, a check when no icon is given, or a dash plus struck text and an "Not included:" prefix for screen readers when `included` is false.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `TWEEN_MS = 360`
  Long enough to read as the price rolling to its new value, short enough that a quick double toggle never feels laggy.
- `ease = 1 - (1 - t)^3`
  Ease-out cubic: the number moves fast first and settles, so the final digits are readable almost immediately.
- `grid breakpoints = @2xl (42rem) → 2 cols, @5xl (64rem) → 4 cols`
  Four cards need about 250px each for the feature labels to wrap at most once; container queries keep that true inside narrow hosts.
- `panel radius = shell rounded-3xl (24px), panels 20px, shell padding 4px`
  Inner radius = outer radius minus the padding, so the nested panels stay concentric with the shell.
- `CTA = h-11 rounded-full`
  Matches the reference: a 44px pill across the full card width, taller than the kit default 36px button.

## API

```ts
function PricingPlanCards(props: { plans: PricingPlan[]; cycle?: BillingCycle; defaultCycle?: BillingCycle; onCycleChange?: (cycle: BillingCycle) => void; onSelectPlan?: (planId: string, cycle: BillingCycle) => void; currency?: string; locale?: string; freeLabel?: string; heading?: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; icon?: IconComponent; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type BillingCycle = "monthly" | "yearly"
interface PricingPlan { id: string; name: string; description: ReactNode; icon?: IconComponent; price: { monthly: number; yearly: number }; caption?: [ReactNode, ReactNode]; badge?: string; highlighted?: boolean; cta: { label: string; icon?: IconComponent; href?: string }; features: PricingPlanFeature[] }
```

- `plans: PricingPlan[]`
  Cards in display order. `price.yearly` is the annual total.
- `cycle: "monthly" | "yearly"`
  Controlled billing cycle.
- `defaultCycle: "monthly" | "yearly"` — default `"monthly"`
  Initial cycle when uncontrolled.
- `onCycleChange: (cycle: BillingCycle) => void`
  Fires when the segmented control changes.
- `onSelectPlan: (planId: string, cycle: BillingCycle) => void`
  Called by CTAs of plans without `cta.href`.
- `currency: string` — default `"EUR"`
  ISO 4217 currency for every price.
- `locale: string` — default `"en-US"`
  Fixed formatting locale, so SSR and client output match.
- `freeLabel: string` — default `"Free"`
  Shown instead of a number for 0 / 0 plans.
- `heading: ReactNode`
  Section heading.
- `description: ReactNode`
  Copy under the heading.
- `icon: ComponentType`
  Glyph drawn in a tile above the heading.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
function PlanPrice({
  plan,
  cycle,
  format,
  freeLabel,
  reduced,
}: {
  plan: PricingPlan;
  cycle: BillingCycle;
  format: (n: number) => string;
  freeLabel: string;
  reduced: boolean;
}) {
  const target = perMonth(plan, cycle);
  const shown = useTweenedNumber(target, reduced);
  const free = plan.price.monthly === 0 && plan.price.yearly === 0;
  const savings = yearlySavings(plan);
  const wholeOnly = Number.isInteger(target) && Number.isInteger(plan.price.monthly);
  const display = format(wholeOnly ? Math.round(shown) : Math.round(shown * 100) / 100);
  const [line1, line2] = plan.caption ?? [
    "per month",
    cycle === "yearly" ? `billed ${format(plan.price.yearly)} yearly` : "billed monthly",
  ];

  return (
    <div className="flex min-h-12 items-center gap-2.5">
      {free ? (
        <span className="text-display-4-medium tracking-tight text-text-primary">{freeLabel}</span>
      ) : (
        <span className="flex items-baseline gap-1.5">
          {cycle === "yearly" && savings > 0 && (
            <s className="text-title-1-regular text-text-tertiary tabular-nums decoration-1">
              <span className="sr-only">was </span>
              {format(plan.price.monthly)}
            </s>
          )}
          <span aria-hidden className="text-display-4-medium tracking-tight text-text-primary tabular-nums">
            {display}
          </span>
          <span className="sr-only">{format(target)}</span>
        </span>
      )}
      <span className="flex flex-col text-caption-1-regular leading-tight">
        <span className="text-text-secondary">{line1}</span>
        {cycle === "yearly" && savings > 0 && !plan.caption ? (
          <span className="text-state-success-text">Save {format(savings)} a year</span>
        ) : (
          <span className="text-text-tertiary">{line2}</span>
        )}
      </span>
    </div>
  );
}

function PlanCard({
  plan,
  cycle,
  format,
  freeLabel,
  reduced,
  onSelectPlan,
}: {
  plan: PricingPlan;
  cycle: BillingCycle;
  format: (n: number) => string;
  freeLabel: string;
  reduced: boolean;
  onSelectPlan?: (planId: string, cycle: BillingCycle) => void;
}) {
  const titleId = useId();
  const Icon = plan.icon;
  const variant = plan.highlighted ? "primary" : "secondary";
  const ctaClass = "h-11 w-full rounded-full text-body-medium";

  return (
    <article
      aria-labelledby={titleId}
      data-highlighted={plan.highlighted || undefined}
      className={cx(
        "flex flex-col rounded-3xl bg-background-secondary-default p-1 ring-1 ring-separator-border",
        plan.highlighted && "ring-accent-200 dark:ring-accent-900",
      )}
    >
      <div className="relative rounded-[20px] bg-background-primary-default px-5 pt-5 pb-5 shadow-xs">
        {Icon && <Icon aria-hidden className="mb-3 size-5 text-text-primary" />}
        {plan.badge && (
          <span className="absolute top-4 right-4 inline-flex items-center rounded-md bg-badge-new-background px-1.5 py-0.5 text-caption-1-medium text-badge-new-text">
            <span aria-hidden className="absolute -top-1 -left-1 size-1 rounded-full bg-accent-300" />
            <span aria-hidden className="absolute -right-1 -bottom-1 size-1 rounded-full bg-accent-300" />
            {plan.badge}
          </span>
        )}
        <h3 id={titleId} className="text-title-2-regular text-text-primary">
          {plan.name}
        </h3>
        <p className="mt-1 text-body-regular text-text-secondary [&_strong]:font-semibold [&_strong]:text-text-primary">
          {plan.description}
        </p>
      </div>

      <div className="flex flex-col gap-4 px-4 pt-5 pb-5">
        <PlanPrice plan={plan} cycle={cycle} format={format} freeLabel={freeLabel} reduced={reduced} />
        {plan.cta.href ? (
          <ButtonLink href={plan.cta.href} variant={variant} leadingIcon={plan.cta.icon} className={ctaClass}>
            {plan.cta.label}
          </ButtonLink>
        ) : (
          <Button
            variant={variant}
            leadingIcon={plan.cta.icon}
            className={ctaClass}
            aria-describedby={titleId}
            onClick={() => onSelectPlan?.(plan.id, cycle)}
          >
            {plan.cta.label}
          </Button>
        )}
      </div>

      <ul className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-3.5 rounded-[20px] bg-background-primary-default px-5 py-5 shadow-xs">
        {plan.features.map((feature, i) => {
          const included = feature.included !== false;
          const Glyph = included ? (feature.icon ?? RiCheckLine) : RiSubtractLine;
          return (
            <li key={i} className={cx("flex items-start gap-2.5 text-body-regular", included ? "text-text-secondary" : "text-text-tertiary")}>
              <Glyph aria-hidden className={cx("mt-px size-[18px] shrink-0", included ? "text-foreground-icon-tertiary" : "text-foreground-icon-quaternary")} />
              <span className={cx(!included && "line-through decoration-1")}>
                {!included && <span className="sr-only">Not included: </span>}
                {feature.label}
              </span>
              {feature.action && (
                <a
                  href={feature.action.href}
                  className="-my-0.5 ml-0.5 shrink-0 rounded-md bg-background-secondary-default px-1.5 py-0.5 text-caption-1-medium text-text-primary outline-none transition-colors duration-150 ease-out hover:bg-background-secondary-hover focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring motion-reduce:transition-none"
                >
                  {feature.action.label}
                </a>
              )}
            </li>
          );
        })}
      </ul>
    </article>
  );
}

export function PricingPlanCards({
  plans,
  cycle: cycleProp,
  defaultCycle = "monthly",
  onCycleChange,
  onSelectPlan,
  currency = "EUR",
  locale = "en-US",
  freeLabel = "Free",
  heading,
  description,
  icon: HeadingIcon,
  className,
}: PricingPlanCardsProps) {
  const [inner, setInner] = useState<BillingCycle>(defaultCycle);
  const cycle = cycleProp ?? inner;
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const format = useMoney(currency, locale);

  const bestPercent = useMemo(() => {
    let best = 0;
    for (const p of plans) {
      if (p.price.monthly > 0) best = Math.max(best, yearlySavings(p) / (p.price.monthly * 12));
    }
    return Math.round(best * 100);
  }, [plans]);

  const setCycle = (next: BillingCycle) => {
    if (cycleProp === undefined) setInner(next);
    onCycleChange?.(next);
  };

  return (
    <section className={cx("@container flex flex-col items-center", className)}>
      {HeadingIcon && (
        <span className="mb-5 grid size-14 place-items-center rounded-2xl bg-background-primary-default shadow-sm ring-1 ring-separator-border">
          <HeadingIcon aria-hidden className="size-7 text-text-primary" />
        </span>
      )}
      {heading && (
        <h2 className="max-w-2xl text-center text-display-3-medium tracking-tight text-balance text-text-primary">{heading}</h2>
      )}
      {description && (
        <p className="mt-3 max-w-md text-center text-body-regular text-pretty text-text-secondary">{description}</p>
      )}

      <SegmentedControl
        aria-label="Billing cycle"
        className="mt-6"
        selectedKeys={new Set([cycle])}
        onSelectionChange={(keys) => {
          const next = [...keys][0];
          if (next === "monthly" || next === "yearly") setCycle(next);
        }}
      >
        <SegmentedControlItem id="monthly">Monthly</SegmentedControlItem>
        <SegmentedControlItem id="yearly">
          Yearly
          {bestPercent > 0 && (
            <span className="ml-1.5 rounded-sm bg-badge-new-background px-1 text-caption-2-semibold text-badge-new-text">
              -{bestPercent}%
            </span>
          )}
        </SegmentedControlItem>
      </SegmentedControl>

      <div className="mt-8 grid w-full grid-cols-1 gap-4 @2xl:grid-cols-2 @5xl:grid-cols-4">
        {plans.map((plan) => (
          <PlanCard
            key={plan.id}
            plan={plan}
            cycle={cycle}
            format={format}
            freeLabel={freeLabel}
            reduced={reduced}
            onSelectPlan={onSelectPlan}
          />
        ))}
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The price tween cancels its pending `requestAnimationFrame` when the target changes or the card unmounts. There are no other listeners or timers.

**Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the price roll is skipped: `useTweenedNumber` returns the target directly and starts no animation frame. The "Join now" pill hover transition is removed with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Formatting with the browser locale (`toLocaleString()` without a locale). The server and client may print different separators and React reports a hydration mismatch; the `locale` prop pins it.
- Tweening the accessible text. Screen readers would announce every intermediate number; the rolling figure is `aria-hidden` and an `sr-only` copy carries the final price.
- Storing the yearly price as a per-month value. Savings and the "billed €180 yearly" caption need the annual total; the per-month figure is derived.
- Using viewport breakpoints for the grid. Inside a narrow container (a docs preview, a modal) four cards would squeeze; the grid uses container queries instead.

## Notes

- Pass `cycle` and `onCycleChange` to keep the switch in the URL or in shared state; omit both to let the component own it.
- Rich descriptions are allowed: `<strong>` inside `description` is styled as the primary text colour, matching the reference card copy.

## Definition of done

The section renders four cards in a row at 1280px and one column at 360px. Monthly is selected and the Pro card reads €19 per month. Clicking Yearly rolls Pro to €15, strikes €19 through, and the caption reads "Save €48 a year"; the Yearly segment carries a "-21%" chip. The highlighted Team card has a blue CTA and a "Most popular" pill. Clicking a CTA reports the plan and current cycle through `onSelectPlan`. Under reduced motion prices change instantly.

and where, so I can check them.
