# Build: Priority Badge

The priority pill from the project board cards: "Low" on blue, "Medium" on yellow, "High" on orange and "Urgent" on rose, drawn from the kit's status tokens so it flips cleanly in dark mode. A small three-bar glyph (one, two or three lit bars, an alert tile for urgent) can ride in front of the label so the level still reads for people who cannot tell the colours apart. Sorting helpers (`PRIORITIES`, `PRIORITY_RANK`) ship with it.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Urgent, high, medium and low ticket pills with a signal-bars glyph, in tinted, plain and icon-only looks.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Four levels map to four status token pairs in one `sortCx` table: urgent → `status-rose`, high → `status-orange`, medium → `status-yellow`, low → `status-blue`, each as `bg-status-*-background text-status-*-text`. The dark sheet redefines those tokens as 60% colour-mixed 950 fills with brighter text, so the pill needs no `dark:` classes.
2. `PriorityGlyph` is a 16×16 SVG in `currentColor`: three 3px-wide bars at x = 2, 6.5, 11 with heights 4.5, 8 and 11.5, bottom-aligned at y = 14.5. `LIT_BARS` decides how many are lit (low 1, medium 2, high 3) and the rest draw at 30% opacity. Urgent replaces the bars with a 13px rounded tile and an exclamation cut out in `--color-background-primary-default`, so it reads as a hole in light and dark.
3. The `soft` variant tints the whole pill. The `plain` variant drops the fill, writes the label in `text-text-secondary` and tints only the glyph with the level's text token, for dense lists where five coloured pills in a row get loud.
4. `iconOnly` hides the visible label but keeps "<Level> priority" in an `sr-only` span, so the glyph never becomes an unlabeled image. `label` overrides the visible text for localized copy, and `data-priority` is stamped on the root for styling hooks and tests.
5. `PRIORITIES` lists the levels highest first and `PRIORITY_RANK` gives weights 4…1, so a board can sort with `PRIORITY_RANK[b] - PRIORITY_RANK[a]` without string comparisons.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `md pill = px-1.5 py-px, 14/20 body-regular, radius 6px`
  Measured off the board card: a 22px tall pill with the label in regular weight, the same height as the bordered project tag beside it, so the two sit on one line.
- `sm pill = px-1 py-px, 12/16 caption-1-medium, 12px glyph`
  For table rows and pickers. The glyph shrinks with the type so it never towers over the label.
- `unlit bar opacity = 0.3`
  Enough to show the empty slots (so "low" reads as one of three, not just one bar) while staying clearly off in both themes.
- `PRIORITY_RANK = low 1, medium 2, high 3, urgent 4`
  Integer weights make the board's sort a subtraction and keep "urgent above high" true even if labels are translated.

## API

```ts
type Priority = "urgent" | "high" | "medium" | "low";
function PriorityBadge(props: Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, "children"> & { priority: Priority; variant?: "soft" | "plain"; size?: "sm" | "md"; showIcon?: boolean; iconOnly?: boolean; label?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLSpanElement> }): JSX.Element
function PriorityGlyph(props: { priority: Priority; className?: string }): JSX.Element
const PRIORITIES: readonly Priority[]; const PRIORITY_LABELS: Record<Priority, string>; const PRIORITY_RANK: Record<Priority, number>
```

- `priority: "urgent" | "high" | "medium" | "low"`
  Level to show. Picks the token pair, glyph and default label.
- `variant: "soft" | "plain"` — default `"soft"`
  Tinted pill, or no fill with a tinted glyph and muted label.
- `size: "sm" | "md"` — default `"md"`
  18px caption pill or 22px body pill.
- `showIcon: boolean` — default `true`
  Draw the bars glyph before the label. Always on for `plain` and `iconOnly`.
- `iconOnly: boolean` — default `false`
  Glyph only; the label moves into an sr-only span.
- `label: string`
  Replaces the visible text, e.g. for localized copy.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** 3-bar signal glyph in `currentColor`; unlit bars sit at 30% opacity. */
export function PriorityGlyph({ priority, className }: PriorityGlyphProps) {
  if (priority === "urgent") {
    return (
      <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden className={cx("size-3.5 shrink-0", className)}>
        <rect x="1.5" y="1.5" width="13" height="13" rx="3.5" fill="currentColor" />
        <path d="M8 4.5v4.25" stroke="var(--color-background-primary-default)" strokeWidth="1.75" strokeLinecap="round" />
        <circle cx="8" cy="11.25" r="1" fill="var(--color-background-primary-default)" />
      </svg>
    );
  }
  const lit = LIT_BARS[priority];
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden className={cx("size-3.5 shrink-0", className)}>
      {[0, 1, 2].map((i) => (
        <rect
          key={i}
          x={2 + i * 4.5}
          y={10 - i * 3.5}
          width="3"
          height={4.5 + i * 3.5}
          rx="1"
          fill="currentColor"
          opacity={i < lit ? 1 : 0.3}
        />
      ))}
    </svg>
  );
}

const styles = sortCx({
  base: "inline-flex shrink-0 items-center whitespace-nowrap rounded-md",
  size: {
    sm: "gap-0.5 px-1 py-px text-caption-1-medium",
    md: "gap-1 px-1.5 py-px text-body-regular",
  },
  soft: {
    urgent: "bg-status-rose-background text-status-rose-text",
    high: "bg-status-orange-background text-status-orange-text",
    medium: "bg-status-yellow-background text-status-yellow-text",
    low: "bg-status-blue-background text-status-blue-text",
  },
  /** Plain: no fill, label in secondary text, only the glyph is tinted. */
  plainGlyph: {
    urgent: "text-status-rose-text",
    high: "text-status-orange-text",
    medium: "text-status-yellow-text",
    low: "text-status-blue-text",
  },
});

export interface PriorityBadgeProps extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, "children"> {
  priority: Priority;
  /** `soft` = tinted pill (board cards); `plain` = glyph + muted label (dense lists). */
  variant?: PriorityBadgeVariant;
  size?: PriorityBadgeSize;
  /** Draw the bars glyph before the label. Forced on for `plain`. */
  showIcon?: boolean;
  /** Hide the visible label (glyph only). The label stays as the accessible name. */
  iconOnly?: boolean;
  /** Override the visible text (e.g. localized copy). */
  label?: string;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLSpanElement>;
}

export function PriorityBadge({
  priority,
  variant = "soft",
  size = "md",
  showIcon = true,
  iconOnly = false,
  label,
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: PriorityBadgeProps) {
  const text = label ?? PRIORITY_LABELS[priority];
  const glyph = showIcon || iconOnly || variant === "plain";
  return (
    <span
      ref={ref}
      data-priority={priority}
      className={cx(
        styles.base,
        styles.size[size],
        variant === "soft" ? styles.soft[priority] : "px-0 text-text-secondary",
        iconOnly && (size === "sm" ? "px-0.5" : "px-1"),
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      {glyph && (
        <PriorityGlyph
          priority={priority}
          className={cx(size === "sm" && "size-3", variant === "plain" && styles.plainGlyph[priority])}
        />
      )}
      {iconOnly ? <span className="sr-only">{`${text} priority`}</span> : text}
    </span>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up: no state, effects, listeners or timers.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing animates in the badge itself; it is static markup. The demo's row and picker colour transitions are dropped with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Hard-coding blue/yellow/orange/rose shades. The status tokens are redefined for dark mode as translucent fills with lighter text; raw shades leave bright pastel blocks on dark cards.
- Relying on colour alone. Yellow and orange are close for many people; keep `showIcon` on wherever the badge is the only priority cue.
- Rendering `iconOnly` without a label. The SVG is `aria-hidden`, so the `sr-only` "<Level> priority" span is the only thing a screen reader hears.
- Sorting by label string. "Urgent" < "Low" alphabetically is meaningless; sort with `PRIORITY_RANK`.

## Notes

- The board cards in BoardUI's template show the text-only pill; pass `showIcon={false}` for that look. Kanban Card does exactly that.
- The urgent tile's cut-out uses the primary surface token, so on a non-white custom surface pass a `className` to the glyph if the hole should match that surface.
- Below 768px the demo shows only the triage queue so it fits a phone screen; the Levels grid joins it from `md` up.

## Definition of done

Four pills render in rose, orange, yellow and blue with labels Urgent, High, Medium, Low; the glyph lights 1, 2 and 3 bars for low, medium and high and shows an alert tile for urgent. In the demo, selecting FE-82 and choosing Urgent changes that row's badge to "Urgent" and, with Priority sort on, moves it to the top of the list; switching to Recent reorders by date. In dark mode every pill keeps readable contrast.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Pro Access Card

The card a docs page shows in place of a paid component. A brushed-metal lock tile, the heading and licence copy sit on top with a "Pro access" pill; below, inside a grey inset, the real preview is rendered blurred and desaturated under a "locked" chip, and a footer carries the upsell line with a get-access button. When `locked` turns false the blur lifts, the chip fades and the footer swaps to your unlocked content.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Pro-locked component placeholder: metallic lock tile, a blurred inert preview, upsell copy and a get-access action that lifts the veil.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Layout: a rounded-3xl bordered section; the header is a flex row of a lock tile (40px, 56px from `sm`) and a title column; the title has a 14rem flex-basis, so in narrow cards the pill wraps under it instead of squeezing the heading. A `bg-background-secondary-default` inset with 4px padding holds the preview stage (rounded-[20px], primary background) and the footer, which reads as two nested surfaces like the docs install panel.
2. The veil is the preview wrapper itself: while locked it gets `blur-[6px] saturate-50 opacity-60 scale-[1.03]`, `pointer-events-none select-none`, the `inert` attribute and `aria-hidden`, so the preview cannot be focused, clicked, selected or read out. The slight scale pushes the blurred edge outside the clipped stage so no soft halo shows at the corners.
3. Unlocking sets the wrapper back to `blur-none` and identity scale/opacity with a 500ms `transition-[filter,opacity,scale]`, while the absolutely positioned lock chip runs a 300ms `transition-[opacity,visibility]` to `invisible opacity-0` so it leaves the tab order and the accessibility tree once faded.
4. The footer is an `aria-live="polite"` region: locked, it shows the title/description and the action (a `ButtonLink` with `actionHref`, else a `Button`); `pending` swaps the icon for a spinner glyph and sets `aria-disabled` (not `disabled`, so focus stays on the button) and `aria-busy` on the card; unlocked, it renders `unlockedFooter`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `veil = blur 6px, saturate 50%, opacity 60%, scale 1.03`
  Enough to hide detail and colour while the silhouette still sells the component; the scale hides the blur halo at the clipped edge.
- `unveil = 500ms ease-out (chip 300ms)`
  The chip is gone before the preview finishes sharpening, so the reveal reads as one motion.
- `lock tile = 56px (40px below sm), rx 14`
  Matches the icon tile in the reference header and the card's rounded-3xl rhythm.
- `inset = p-1 (4px), stage radius 20px`
  Outer radius 24px minus the 4px inset keeps the nested corners concentric.

## API

```ts
function ProAccessCard(props: { title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; badge?: ReactNode; unlockedBadge?: ReactNode; icon?: ReactNode; preview?: ReactNode; lockedLabel?: ReactNode; locked?: boolean; footerTitle?: ReactNode; footerDescription?: ReactNode; unlockedFooter?: ReactNode; actionLabel?: ReactNode; actionIcon?: IconComponent; actionHref?: string; onAction?: () => void; pending?: boolean; titleAs?: "h2" | "h3" | "h4"; previewClassName?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function ProLockTile(props: { className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `title: ReactNode`
  Heading, e.g. "Line Chart Card is a Pro component."; labels the section.
- `description: ReactNode`
  Licence copy under the title.
- `preview: ReactNode`
  The component preview, veiled while locked.
- `locked: boolean` — default `true`
  Blurs and disables the preview and shows the call to action.
- `pending: boolean` — default `false`
  Spinner in the action, `aria-disabled`, and `aria-busy` on the card.
- `onAction / actionHref: () => void / string`
  Click handler, or a link target that renders the action as an anchor.
- `actionLabel / actionIcon: ReactNode / IconComponent` — default `"Get access" / RiVipCrown2Line`
  Action text and leading icon.
- `badge / unlockedBadge: ReactNode` — default `"Pro access" / "Unlocked"`
  Pill text for each state.
- `lockedLabel: ReactNode` — default `"Preview locked"`
  Chip over the blurred preview.
- `footerTitle / footerDescription: ReactNode` — default `"This component is included in Pro"`
  Upsell copy beside the action.
- `unlockedFooter: ReactNode`
  Replaces the footer once unlocked.
- `icon: ReactNode` — default `<ProLockTile />`
  Header icon.
- `titleAs: "h2" | "h3" | "h4"` — default `"h3"`
  Heading level for the title.
- `previewClassName: string` — default `"p-3 sm:p-6"`
  Classes for the preview stage.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// The veil: blur + desaturate + inert while locked, so the preview teases
// the component but cannot be tabbed into, clicked or read out. Unlocking
// transitions filter, opacity and scale back to identity in one 500ms pass,
// while the lock chip fades out over 300ms and then turns `invisible`.
const veilClass = cx(
  "origin-center transition-[filter,opacity,scale] duration-500 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
  locked ? "pointer-events-none scale-[1.03] opacity-60 blur-[6px] saturate-50 select-none" : "blur-none",
  previewClassName ?? "p-3 sm:p-6",
);
const overlayClass = cx(
  "absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center bg-background-primary-default/30",
  "transition-[opacity,visibility] duration-300 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
  locked ? "visible opacity-100" : "invisible opacity-0",
);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The component holds no timers or listeners. The demo's simulated activation is a `setTimeout` inside an effect keyed on the status and cleared in its cleanup.

**Reduced motion.** Every transition (veil filter/opacity/scale, chip fade, pill colour) carries `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so the preview snaps between veiled and clear.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Blurring a preview that is still interactive. Without `inert` keyboard users tab into invisible-looking controls and screen readers read the hidden component; add `inert` and `aria-hidden` together.
- Fading the overlay with opacity only. It stays clickable and announced; pair it with `visibility` in the same transition.
- Setting `disabled` on the action while pending. The focused button loses focus to `<body>`; use `aria-disabled` and ignore clicks instead.
- Writing `blur-0` to clear the filter in Tailwind v4: it emits nothing. Use `blur-none`.

## Notes

- The card does not own the licence state: pass `locked` from wherever you check it, and `pending` while an activation request is in flight.
- The lock tile colours are fixed SVG artwork (brushed metal reads the same in both themes); pass `icon` to use your own.

## Definition of done

The demo loads with a blurred revenue chart, an "Unlock to use this component" chip, a "Pro access" pill and a "Get Pro" button; nothing in the preview is focusable. Clicking Get Pro shows "Activating…" with a spinner and aria-disabled for about 900ms, then the chart sharpens, the chip fades, the pill reads "Unlocked", the footer says the licence is active and focus lands on "Lock again". Clicking Lock again restores the veil and the Get Pro button.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Pro Upsell Toast

The card that appears when someone reaches for a paid feature, such as installing a Pro template. A 300px white card floats in the corner with a soft wash of blue and pink light across its top, a brushed-metal app tile, a title, one line of copy, a full-width "Get Pro" button and a round dismiss button. It is controlled with `isOpen`, rises in from the corner, closes on the dismiss button or Escape and hands focus back to the control that opened it.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A floating Upgrade-to-Pro card with a grainy pastel wash, app tile, dismiss and a full-width CTA; it rises in and returns focus on close.

- Category: overlay
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: motion@^12.43.0

## How it works

1. The card is a `motion.div` inside `AnimatePresence`, so it can play an exit before it unmounts. It enters from 16px lower at 96% scale over 340ms on an ease-out curve (0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) with its transform origin at the bottom, and leaves 8px down at 98% over 160ms.
2. It is a non-modal `role="dialog"` named by its title and described by its copy. When it opens with `autoFocus`, an effect remembers `document.activeElement` and focuses the card itself (`tabIndex={-1}`), so a screen reader reads the title and copy and the next Tab reaches the button. Nothing else on the page is blocked.
3. When `isOpen` turns false the card is still in the DOM for its exit animation, so the same effect can check whether focus is inside it. If it is, focus goes back to the remembered element; if the user had already moved on, focus is left where it is.
4. Escape is handled by a `keydown` on the card, not on the window, so it only closes the toast while focus is inside it and never fights a modal or menu elsewhere on the page. The dismiss button and Escape both call `onOpenChange(false)`; the call to action calls `onCta` and leaves closing to the parent.
5. The wash is inline SVG: five blurred vertical ellipses in pastel blue, violet and pink, a fractal-noise grain at 12% and a gradient mask that fades the lot out by the middle of the card. It is stretched with `preserveAspectRatio="none"` and drops to 55% opacity in dark mode so it glows instead of glaring.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `card = 300px wide (never wider than the container minus 2rem), radius 24px, 16px padding, 16px from the corner`
  Wide enough for the title on one line and the copy on two, narrow enough to leave the page usable beside it on a laptop.
- `enter = 340ms, y 16 → 0, scale 0.96 → 1, ease (0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`
  A fast start with a long settle reads as the card arriving from the corner without bouncing; the small scale keeps the motion near the corner it grows from.
- `exit = 160ms, y +8, scale 0.98, ease-in`
  Leaving is half the length of arriving, so dismissing feels immediate and the page underneath is usable again at once.
- `wash = blur 12, grain 12%, faded to transparent by 100% of a 112px band; 55% in dark mode`
  Enough colour to mark the card as special, kept above the text so the copy sits on plain white.

## API

```ts
function ProUpsellToast(props: ProUpsellToastProps): JSX.Element
interface ProUpsellToastProps { isOpen: boolean; onOpenChange?: (isOpen: boolean) => void; title?: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; ctaLabel?: ReactNode; onCta?: () => void; icon?: ReactNode; autoFocus?: boolean; className?: string }
```

- `isOpen: boolean`
  Shows the card. It animates in and out on change.
- `onOpenChange: (isOpen: boolean) => void`
  Called with false by the dismiss button and by Escape.
- `title: ReactNode` — default `"This template is part of Pro"`
  Dialog title.
- `description: ReactNode` — default `"Buy once and install the full source with the CLI."`
  One line under the title; also the dialog description.
- `ctaLabel: ReactNode` — default `"Get Pro"`
  Label of the full-width button.
- `onCta: () => void`
  Called by the button. Close the card yourself if the action leaves the page state.
- `icon: ReactNode`
  Replaces the default metal Pro tile.
- `autoFocus: boolean` — default `true`
  Focus the card when it opens and return focus when it closes.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card; the default placement is `fixed end-4 bottom-4 z-50`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function ProUpsellToast({
  isOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  title = "This template is part of Pro",
  description = "Buy once and install the full source with the CLI.",
  ctaLabel = "Get Pro",
  onCta,
  icon,
  autoFocus = true,
  className,
}: ProUpsellToastProps) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const cardRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const returnTo = useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null);
  const titleId = useId();
  const descriptionId = useId();

  useEffect(() => {
    if (isOpen) {
      if (!autoFocus) return;
      const active = document.activeElement;
      returnTo.current = active instanceof HTMLElement ? active : null;
      cardRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true });
      return;
    }
    // The card is still mounted while it animates out, so this sees where
    // focus is. Only pull it back if it was inside the card.
    if (cardRef.current?.contains(document.activeElement)) returnTo.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true });
    returnTo.current = null;
  }, [isOpen, autoFocus]);

  const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (event.key !== "Escape") return;
    event.stopPropagation();
    onOpenChange?.(false);
  };

  return (
    <AnimatePresence>
      {isOpen ? (
        <motion.div
          key="pro-upsell-toast"
          ref={cardRef}
          role="dialog"
          aria-labelledby={titleId}
          aria-describedby={descriptionId}
          tabIndex={-1}
          onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
          initial={reduced ? { opacity: 0 } : { opacity: 0, y: 16, scale: 0.96 }}
          animate={{
            opacity: 1,
            y: 0,
            scale: 1,
            transition: reduced ? { duration: 0.15 } : { duration: 0.34, ease: ENTER_EASE },
          }}
          exit={
            reduced
              ? { opacity: 0, transition: { duration: 0.12 } }
              : { opacity: 0, y: 8, scale: 0.98, transition: { duration: 0.16, ease: EXIT_EASE } }
          }
          className={cx(
            "fixed end-4 bottom-4 z-50 w-[min(300px,calc(100%-2rem))] origin-bottom overflow-hidden",
            "rounded-3xl bg-background-primary-default p-4 shadow-lg ring-1 ring-border-ai-profile-card outline-none",
            "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
            className,
          )}
        >
          <ProWash className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-x-0 top-0 h-28 w-full dark:opacity-55" />

          <div className="relative flex flex-col">
            <span className="mb-4 flex">{icon ?? <ProTile />}</span>
            <h2 id={titleId} className="pe-8 text-body-medium text-text-primary">
              {title}
            </h2>
            <p id={descriptionId} className="mt-1 text-body-2-regular text-text-secondary">
              {description}
            </p>
            <Button variant="primary" size="medium" className="mt-4 w-full justify-center" onClick={onCta}>
              {ctaLabel}
            </Button>
          </div>

          <CloseButton
            size="sm"
            aria-label="Dismiss"
            onClick={() => onOpenChange?.(false)}
            className="absolute end-3 top-3 dark:bg-background-quaternary-default"
          />
        </motion.div>
      ) : null}
    </AnimatePresence>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** There are no timers or global listeners. The Escape handler is a React `onKeyDown` on the card, the focus effect only reads and moves focus, and motion stops the exit animation if the component unmounts mid-way.

**Reduced motion.** With prefers-reduced-motion the card does not move or scale: it fades in over 150ms and out over 120ms. The wash and tile are static in every mode.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Clearing the remembered element or skipping the focus return when the parent closes the toast. Keyboard users are left on `<body>` at the top of the page. The effect returns focus whenever the card closes with focus inside it, whoever closed it.
- Listening for Escape on `window`. It would close the toast while a modal or a select popover is open, and one keypress would close both. The listener lives on the card.
- Making it a modal or trapping focus. An upsell is optional; a trap turns a suggestion into a wall. Use `autoFocus={false}` when the card appears on its own, so it does not steal focus from someone typing.
- Placing it `fixed` inside a transformed parent. The parent becomes the containing block and the card lands in the wrong place. Render it near the root, or pass `absolute` to pin it inside a positioned frame as the demo does.

## Notes

- Pass `icon` to swap the default tile for your product mark, and `title`, `description` and `ctaLabel` for your own plan.
- For several toasts at once use the kit Toaster; this card is a single, specific prompt.

## Definition of done

Nothing floats at first. "Install template" opens a 300px card in the bottom-right corner of the frame that rises in with a blue-and-pink grainy glow across its top, a metal tile, "This template is part of Pro", "Buy once and install the full source with the CLI." and a blue "Get Pro" button. Focus lands on the card; Tab reaches Get Pro and then the round dismiss button. Escape or the dismiss button lowers it away and the status reads "Dismissed", with focus back on "Install template". Get Pro closes it and the status reads "Checkout opened".

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Profile Cover Header

The card at the top of a profile page. A wide cover band of soft gradient artwork runs across the top, an 80px initials avatar sits half over its bottom edge, and below it come the name, the handle with small badges, inline follower counts and an underline tab strip. Visitors get Share and a Follow toggle; the owner gets Share and Edit.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Profile identity card: gradient cover, overlapping initials avatar, name, handle and badges, Follow or Edit actions and underline tabs.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The root is a `section` labelled by the name heading, with a 16px radius, a 1px `border-ai-profile-card` border and `overflow-hidden`, so the cover is clipped to the top corners without its own radius.
2. The cover band is 112px tall on phones and 160px from `sm` up. By default it holds `ProfileCoverArt`: an inline SVG (viewBox 680x170, `xMidYMid slice`) with a sky gradient, a radial sun halo, three blurred haze ellipses, a 24px sun and two rows of rounded forms. Its gradient ids come from `useId`, so several headers can share a page. Pass `cover` to put any node there instead.
3. Under the cover, one flex row puts the avatar on the left and the actions on the right. The kit Avatar is enlarged to 80px with 28px initials and pulled up with `-mt-10`, so half of it overlaps the cover; a 4px ring in the card background cuts it out of the artwork. The actions sit 12px below the cover edge.
4. Follow is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`. It works controlled (`isFollowing` + `onFollowingChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultFollowing`): the click computes the next value, stores it only when uncontrolled, and always reports it. The button swaps from a primary "Follow" with a user-add icon to a secondary "Following" with a user-check icon, at a 104px minimum width from `sm` up so the row does not jump. Below `sm` the Share button keeps its icon and hides its label (its `aria-label` stays "Share"), so avatar and both actions fit one row at 360px.
5. With `isOwner` the Follow toggle is replaced by an Edit button; Share appears whenever `onShare` is passed. Name (20px medium), handle (16px secondary), tone-coloured badges (11px semibold) and an optional bio and `dl` of stats stack below with 4px gaps.
6. Tabs use the kit Tabs (react-aria): arrow keys move between tabs and each has a `TabPanel` filled by `renderPanel(id)`. The strip sits in an `overflow-x-auto` wrapper with `min-w-max`, so four tabs with counts scroll sideways on a phone instead of wrapping.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `cover height = 112px (h-28) below sm, 160px (h-40) from sm`
  Wide enough to read as a banner on a laptop; on a phone it shrinks so the name and actions stay above the fold.
- `avatar = 80px, -40px top margin, 4px ring, 28px initials`
  Exactly half the avatar overlaps the cover, the classic profile silhouette; the ring keeps the circle readable over any artwork.
- `follow button = min-width 104px from sm; Share label hidden below sm`
  "Following" is wider than "Follow"; the minimum stops the Share button shifting when the state flips. On phones the icon-only Share leaves room for the wider label without wrapping.
- `card padding = 16px sides, 16px panel padding`
  Lines the avatar, name and tab labels up on one left edge.

## API

```ts
function ProfileCoverHeader(props: ProfileCoverHeaderProps): JSX.Element
```

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Follow works controlled (`isFollowing`) or uncontrolled (`defaultFollowing`).
const [innerFollowing, setInnerFollowing] = useState(defaultFollowing);
const following = isFollowing ?? innerFollowing;
const toggleFollow = () => {
  const next = !following;
  if (isFollowing === undefined) setInnerFollowing(next);
  onFollowingChange?.(next);
};
const avatarText = (initials ?? name.trim().charAt(0)).toUpperCase();

const actions = (
  <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center justify-end gap-2">
    {onShare && (
      <Button
        variant="secondary"
        size="small"
        leadingIcon={RiUpload2Line}
        aria-label="Share"
        onClick={onShare}
      >
        <span className="max-sm:hidden">Share</span>
      </Button>
    )}
    {isOwner ? (
      <Button variant="secondary" size="small" leadingIcon={RiEditBoxLine} onClick={onEdit}>
        Edit
      </Button>
    ) : (
      <Button
        variant={following ? "secondary" : "primary"}
        size="small"
        aria-pressed={following}
        leadingIcon={following ? RiUserFollowLine : RiUserAddLine}
        onClick={toggleFollow}
        className="sm:min-w-[104px]"
      >
        {following ? "Following" : "Follow"}
      </Button>
    )}
  </div>
);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The component owns no timers, listeners or observers. The tab strip uses the kit TabList, which disconnects its own resize and mutation observers on unmount.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing animates on its own. The only motion is the kit tab underline sliding and the buttons changing colour, both short CSS transitions; the artwork is static. In dark mode the cover is dimmed to 85% brightness so it does not glare.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Giving the cover its own top radius instead of clipping it with the card. At fractional zoom the two curves drift apart and a hairline of background shows. Clip with `overflow-hidden` on the card.
- Hard-coding SVG gradient ids. Two headers on one page then share the first gradient and the second cover renders the wrong tone. The art builds its ids from `useId`.
- Toggling the visible label without exposing the state. Screen readers hear a new label but no relationship to the old one; `aria-pressed` tells them it is the same toggle, now on.
- Letting the tab strip wrap on narrow screens. The underline is measured from the selected tab and lands under the wrong row; scroll the strip instead.

## Notes

- Swap the artwork tone with `coverTone` ("sky", "dusk", "aurora") or pass a photo or your own SVG as `cover`.
- Follower counts are plain `stats`; update them in `onFollowingChange` as the demo does.

## Definition of done

A card shows a blue sky cover, an 80px "M" avatar overlapping its bottom edge, "Mira Okafor", "@miraok" with a PRO pill, "1,284 followers" and four tabs. Clicking Follow turns it into a pressed secondary "Following" button and the count reads 1,285; clicking again reverts. Switching the view to Owner swaps Follow for Edit. Arrow keys move between tabs and the panel below changes; at 360px wide the tab strip scrolls instead of wrapping.

# Build: Profile Stat Tiles

The contributions block of an AI profile: a caption, a large headline figure with a purple trend chip, and a row of small grey tiles such as lifetime tokens, peak tokens, longest task and top streak. Each tile shows its value, its label and an optional up or down change. The headline rolls to new values, and the tiles can become toggle buttons so one metric can drive another view.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A rolling headline figure with a trend chip over a row of grey stat tiles (value, label, trend) that can act as toggles.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The headline value runs through the kit `useCountUp` hook (480ms, ease-out cubic via requestAnimationFrame), so switching the dataset rolls the number instead of snapping. The rolling text is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden copy carries the final formatted value, so screen readers never hear the intermediate numbers.
2. The default formatter is an `Intl.NumberFormat` for whole US dollars; pass `formatValue` for tokens, hours or anything else. Trends are formatted by `formatTrend`: one decimal at most, a leading plus for gains and a true minus sign (U+2212) for losses.
3. The headline trend is a kit Chip at caption size: purple for gains, rose for losses, neutral for zero. Inside tiles the trend is smaller: a 12px arrow icon and the unsigned percentage (`formatTrend(trend, false)`) in the same purple or rose text, with a visually hidden "up" or "down" so the direction is not conveyed by colour and icon alone.
4. Tiles sit in a `role="group"` grid: two columns on phones and `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(132px, 1fr))` from `sm`, so four tiles share one row on a card and fold cleanly when the card narrows. Each tile is a 10px-radius block on `background-secondary` with 10px padding, the value in 14px medium and the label in 13px secondary text.
5. Selection is opt-in: when `onSelectionChange` or `selectedId` is passed, the tiles render as `button`s with `aria-pressed`; clicking the selected one clears it. The selected tile lifts to the primary background with a 1px ring and a small shadow. It works controlled (`selectedId`) or uncontrolled (`defaultSelectedId`).

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `count-up = 480ms, ease-out cubic`
  Long enough to read as a change of dataset, short enough to finish before the eye has moved on to the tiles.
- `tile grid = 2 columns below sm, auto-fit minmax(132px, 1fr) from sm, 8px gap`
  132px is the narrowest width that keeps "Lifetime tokens" and "562.7M ↑ 8.1%" on single lines.
- `tile = 10px radius, 10px padding, 14px value, 13px label`
  Small, quiet tiles that sit under a 24px headline without competing with it.

## API

```ts
function ProfileStatTiles(props: ProfileStatTilesProps): JSX.Element
interface ProfileStatTilesProps extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "children" | "onSelect"> { label?: ReactNode; value?: number; formatValue?: (value: number) => string; trend?: number; tiles: StatTile[]; selectedId?: string | null; defaultSelectedId?: string | null; onSelectionChange?: (id: string | null) => void; tilesLabel?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }
interface StatTile { id: string; label: string; value: ReactNode; trend?: number }
```

- `label: ReactNode`
  Caption above the headline.
- `value: number`
  Headline number; rolls when it changes. Omit to show only the tiles.
- `formatValue: (value: number) => string` — default `whole US dollars`
  Formats the headline.
- `trend: number`
  Headline percent change, shown as a chip.
- `tiles: StatTile[]`
  The tiles: id, label, value and optional trend.
- `selectedId: string | null`
  Controlled selected tile. Passing it makes tiles toggle buttons.
- `defaultSelectedId: string | null` — default `null`
  Initial selection when uncontrolled.
- `onSelectionChange: (id: string | null) => void`
  Called with the tile id, or null when the selected tile is clicked again.
- `tilesLabel: string` — default `"Stats"`
  Accessible name of the tile group.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Tiles are toggle buttons only when someone listens or controls them.
const selectable = onSelectionChange !== undefined || selectedId !== undefined;
const [innerSelected, setInnerSelected] = useState<string | null>(defaultSelectedId);
const current = selectedId !== undefined ? selectedId : innerSelected;
const toggle = (id: string) => {
  const next = current === id ? null : id;
  if (selectedId === undefined) setInnerSelected(next);
  onSelectionChange?.(next);
};

const tileBase =
  "flex min-w-0 flex-col items-start gap-0.5 rounded-[10px] px-2.5 py-2.5 text-start transition-[background-color,box-shadow] duration-150 ease-out";
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The count-up hook cancels its requestAnimationFrame when the value changes again or the component unmounts. There are no other timers or listeners.

**Reduced motion.** With prefers-reduced-motion the headline shows its final value immediately instead of rolling. Tile hover and selection keep their 150ms colour change, which does not move anything.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Announcing the rolling number. A live headline that changes every frame floods a screen reader; the animated text is hidden and only the final value is exposed.
- Showing direction by colour alone. Purple and rose are hard to tell apart for many people; the arrow icon and the hidden "up" or "down" carry the meaning.
- Rendering tiles as buttons when nothing listens to them. They would be focus stops that do nothing; tiles are plain blocks unless selection is wired up.
- Using a hyphen for negative trends. "-3.2%" looks lighter than "+3.2%" and may break onto a new line; the U+2212 minus sign is the width of a plus.

## Notes

- Omit `value` to render only the tiles, for example inside another card that already has its own headline.
- Wire `onSelectionChange` to a heatmap or chart to filter it by the chosen metric.

## Definition of done

The card shows "Contributions this year", "$7,462" with a purple "+14.8%" chip and four tiles: 9B Lifetime tokens, 562.7M Peak tokens, 12h 54m Longest task (rose, down 3.2%) and 62 days Top streak. Clicking a tile presses it and the hint names that metric; clicking it again clears it. Choosing 2024 rolls the headline to $5,954 with a rose "−2.5%" chip and updates every tile. At 360px wide the tiles form two columns.

# Build: Progress

How far along a task is, as a rounded rail or a small ring. Both are React Aria `ProgressBar`s, so they are announced with their label and a locale-formatted value. The bar's fill moves by `translate` and eases to each new value over 500ms; the indeterminate bar sweeps a band of light (crisp core, tight glow, wide bloom) along the rail, and the indeterminate ring is the Spinner's orbiting light.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Progress bar and ring, determinate or indeterminate, with an eased translate fill and a layered light sweep, on React Aria.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `ProgressTrack` draws the rail: `relative w-full rounded-full bg-border-button-default text-accent-500` at `h-1`, `h-1.5` or `h-2` for sm / md / lg. The fill colour is `currentColor`, so a text class recolours it.
2. Determinate: inside an `overflow-hidden rounded-full` clip, a full-width `bg-current` span is shifted by `translate: -(100 - p)% 0` (positive in RTL, read from `useDirection()`), with `p` clamped to 0..100. `transition-[translate] duration-500` with `cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)` eases each change on the compositor instead of animating `width`.
3. Indeterminate (`Sweep`): a wrapper clipped with `[clip-path:inset(-8px_0_round_9999px)]` keeps the light inside the rail's length but lets it bleed 8px past its thickness. A `w-2/5` band runs `bui-progress-sweep` (translate -100% to 250%) over 1.6s `cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)`, reversed in RTL.
4. The band holds three right-anchored `bg-linear-to-r from-transparent to-current` layers: a bloom (`-inset-y-[5px] right-[10px]`, opacity 30%, `blur-[5px]`), a glow (`-inset-y-[1.5px] right-[4px] left-[25%]`, opacity 60%, `blur-[2px]`) and a crisp core (`right-0 left-[35%]`). Pulling the soft layers back from the right edge is what keeps the sharp head in front.
5. `ProgressBar` wraps `AriaProgressBar` and uses its render props `{ percentage, valueText }`: a label row (the kit `Label`, truncated, and `valueText` in `tabular-nums`), the track, and an optional caption description. The value label shows by default only when there is a label and the bar is determinate.
6. `ProgressCircle` maps sm / md / lg to box 16 / 24 / 32 and line 2 / 2.5 / 3. It draws a `-rotate-90` SVG with a `stroke-border-button-default` track circle and a `currentColor` arc whose `strokeDashoffset = circumference × (1 - p/100)`, transitioned over 500ms. Indeterminate, it renders `SpinnerGlyph` at sm / lg / xl.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `track heights = sm h-1 (4px), md h-1.5 (6px), lg h-2 (8px)`
  Md is the default rail of the agent-limits card; sm fits inside dense rows and lg reads as a primary step indicator.
- `fill easing = 500ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) on translate`
  A strong ease-out lands each new value softly. Moving by `translate` keeps the change on the compositor; animating `width` relayouts every frame.
- `sweep = band w-2/5, 1.6s cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1), translate -100% to 250%; 4s under reduced motion`
  250% of a 40% band carries it fully past the rail's end, so the band leaves before it re-enters on the left.
- `sweep bleed = clip-path inset(-8px 0 round 9999px); bloom -5px, glow -1.5px`
  The glow and bloom are taller than the 6px rail. Clipping only horizontally lets the light halo above and below while it still stops at the rail ends.
- `ring sizes = sm 16/2, md 24/2.5, lg 32/3 (box/line px); indeterminate uses SpinnerGlyph sm / lg / xl`
  Ring and spinner share box sizes, so a ring can swap between determinate and indeterminate in place without moving its neighbours.

## API

```ts
type ProgressSize = "sm" | "md" | "lg"
interface ProgressBarProps extends Omit<AriaProgressBarProps, "children" | "className"> { label?: ReactNode; showValueLabel?: boolean; description?: ReactNode; size?: ProgressSize; className?: string }
function ProgressBar(props: ProgressBarProps): JSX.Element
interface ProgressTrackProps { percentage: number; size?: ProgressSize; isIndeterminate?: boolean; className?: string }
function ProgressTrack(props: ProgressTrackProps): JSX.Element
interface ProgressCircleProps extends Omit<AriaProgressBarProps, "children" | "className"> { size?: ProgressSize; className?: string }
function ProgressCircle(props: ProgressCircleProps): JSX.Element
```

- `value: number` — default `0`
  Current value between `minValue` and `maxValue` (React Aria).
- `isIndeterminate: boolean` — default `false`
  Show the light sweep (bar) or the orbiting spinner (ring) instead of a value.
- `label: ReactNode`
  Bar only. Label above the rail; also turns the value label on by default.
- `showValueLabel: boolean`
  Bar only. Show the formatted value at the end of the label row. Defaults to on when there is a label and a value.
- `description: ReactNode`
  Bar only. Helper text under the rail.
- `size: "sm" | "md" | "lg"` — default `"md"`
  Bar: 4 / 6 / 8px rail. Ring: 16 / 24 / 32px box.
- `className: string`
  Bar: classes on the root. Ring: arc colour via a text class (default accent).

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** The sweeping band of light for an indeterminate bar. */
function Sweep() {
  return (
    // The clip keeps the light inside the rail's length but lets the glow
    // and bloom bleed past its thickness.
    <span aria-hidden className="absolute inset-0 [clip-path:inset(-8px_0_round_9999px)]">
      <span
        className={cx(
          "absolute inset-y-0 left-0 w-2/5",
          "animate-[bui-progress-sweep_1.6s_cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)_infinite]",
          "rtl:[animation-direction:reverse] motion-reduce:[animation-duration:4s]",
        )}
      >
        <span className="absolute inset-0 rtl:-scale-x-100">
          <span className="absolute -inset-y-[5px] right-[10px] left-0 rounded-full bg-linear-to-r from-transparent to-current opacity-30 blur-[5px]" />
          <span className="absolute -inset-y-[1.5px] right-[4px] left-[25%] rounded-full bg-linear-to-r from-transparent to-current opacity-60 blur-[2px]" />
          <span className="absolute inset-y-0 right-0 left-[35%] rounded-full bg-linear-to-r from-transparent to-current" />
        </span>
      </span>
    </span>
  );
}

export interface ProgressTrackProps {
  /** 0 to 100. */
  percentage: number;
  size?: ProgressSize;
  /** Draw the indeterminate sweep instead of a fill. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean;
  /** Colour of the fill, from the text colour. Default accent. */
  className?: string;
}

/** The rail and its fill, shared by ProgressBar and Meter. */
export function ProgressTrack({ percentage, size = "md", isIndeterminate = false, className }: ProgressTrackProps) {
  const direction = useDirection();
  return (
    // The rail is File Upload's ring track colour, which keeps an edge on
    // every surface in both themes (chart-track matches dark cards).
    <div className={cx("relative w-full rounded-full bg-border-button-default text-accent-500", styles.track[size], className)}>
      {isIndeterminate ? (
        <Sweep />
      ) : (
        <span className="absolute inset-0 overflow-hidden rounded-full">
          <span
            className={cx("absolute inset-0 rounded-full bg-current transition-[translate] duration-500 motion-reduce:transition-none", EASE)}
            style={{ translate: `${(direction === "rtl" ? 1 : -1) * (100 - Math.min(100, Math.max(0, percentage)))}% 0` }}
          />
        </span>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. Motion is CSS transitions and keyframes; there are no listeners, timers or effects.

**Reduced motion.** Fill and ring transitions are removed (`motion-reduce:transition-none`), so values jump straight to their new position. The indeterminate sweep keeps running but slows from 1.6s to 4s, and the indeterminate ring inherits Spinner's slower 2.4s orbit, because a stopped loader reads as a hang.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not animate the fill's `width`. The component translates a full-width span inside an `overflow-hidden` clip; width transitions cause layout on every frame.
- Do not forget RTL. The fill offset flips sign with `useDirection()` and the sweep reverses; a hard-coded negative translate fills from the wrong edge in Arabic or Hebrew.
- Do not replace the sweep's `clip-path` with `overflow: hidden`. It would cut the glow off at the rail's 6px thickness.
- Do not render a ring or an unlabelled bar without `aria-label`. React Aria warns and screen readers announce an unnamed progress bar.

## Notes

- `ProgressTrack` is exported and shared with Meter, which reuses the same rail and fill.
- Values are React Aria's: `value`, `minValue` (0), `maxValue` (100) and `formatOptions`; `valueText` is formatted for the locale.

## Definition of done

`<ProgressBar label="Uploading" value={64} />` shows "Uploading" with "64%" on the right and a 6px rail filled 64% in the accent colour; raising the value to 90 slides the fill smoothly over half a second. An indeterminate bar shows a glowing band crossing the rail left to right every 1.6s, with its glow spilling slightly above and below the rail but never past its ends. Rings show a clockwise arc from 12 o'clock proportional to the value, and an indeterminate ring shows the spinner. Each exposes `role="progressbar"` with its name.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Project Board

The Project Board template as one working page. Five columns (Backlog, To do, In progress, Review, Done) show count against a work-in-progress limit; cards drag between and within columns with an insertion line, open a side panel with editable status, priority, project, assignees, a token usage chart and comments, and the header carries an activity inbox, sort, filter, a panel toggle and New ticket.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A full kanban page: drag tickets across five columns, open a side panel to edit them, create, sort and filter, with an activity inbox.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Every ticket lives in one ordered array; a column is that array filtered by `stage`, then filtered by the active `BoardFilter` and optionally sorted for display. Counts in the column header use the unfiltered stage list, so `3/8` stays true while filters hide cards.
2. `moveTicket(id, stage, beforeId)` removes the ticket, restamps its stage (moving into Done stamps a completion day, moving out clears it) and splices it back in front of `beforeId`, or after the last ticket already in the target stage when `beforeId` is null. Drag, the Alt+Arrow keys, the panel's Status select and the column menu all go through it.
3. Drag and drop is native HTML5. A card sets `text/plain` to its id on `dragstart`. Each card's `dragover` compares the pointer to its vertical midpoint and reports `{stage, beforeId}` (itself, or the next card); the column's own `dragover` only claims the end slot when the pointer first enters it. `drop` reads the id and calls `moveTicket`; `dragend` clears the indicator either way.
4. Each card is an `article` with a stretched title button (`after:absolute after:inset-0`), so the whole card opens the detail panel while the hit area stays one real button. Alt+ArrowLeft/Right on that button moves the ticket one stage and an `aria-live` region announces it.
5. The side panel shows `TicketPanel` (keyed by ticket id so the title draft resets) or, with nothing open, a board overview of column load and total tokens. Every edit appends an entry to the activity log that feeds the Inbox popover; closing the popover marks entries read.
6. Sidebar rows are `href="#"` links; one `onClickCapture` on the root maps the link's `aria-label` to a `DASHBOARD_NAV` key and switches the view in state. Other keys show a placeholder with "Back to Project board".

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `column width = 268px`
  Fits "KEY > epic" plus a three-avatar stack on one line; the board scrolls sideways when the side panel takes 332px.
- `WIP limits = 8 / 5 / 4 / 3 / 6`
  Backlog to Done. Going over turns the count rose so overload is visible at a glance.
- `TODAY = 15 (Sep)`
  Fixed day stamped on created tickets and on tickets moved into Done, so renders never read the clock.
- `drop midpoint = rect.top + rect.height / 2`
  Upper half inserts before the hovered card, lower half after it, matching where the line is drawn.
- `activity cap = 30 entries`
  Keeps the inbox list short and the state small during long sessions.

## API

```ts
function ProjectBoard(props: { tickets?: Ticket[]; defaultNotifications?: BellNotification[]; defaultView?: string; defaultPanelOpen?: boolean; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `tickets: Ticket[]` — default `BOARD_TICKETS`
  Tickets in board order (13 samples). Moves, edits, comments and deletes change a local copy.
- `defaultNotifications: BellNotification[]` — default `BOARD_NOTIFICATIONS`
  Initial bell contents; unread items drive the badge count.
- `defaultView: string` — default `"project-board"`
  Sidebar key shown first. Any other key shows the placeholder view.
- `defaultPanelOpen: boolean` — default `false`
  Show the side panel (board overview) on first render. Opening a ticket always opens it.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// The sidebar rows are `href="#"` links: one capture listener turns any of
// them into a local view switch so the host URL never changes.
const onNavClickCapture = (event: MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
  if (!(event.target instanceof Element)) return;
  const link = event.target.closest('a[href="#"]');
  if (!link) return;
  event.preventDefault();
  const item = DASHBOARD_NAV.find((entry) => entry.label === link.getAttribute("aria-label"));
  if (item) setView(item.key);
};

// One ordered array holds every ticket. Moving = remove it, restamp its
// stage (Done gets a completion day), then splice it back in front of
// `beforeId`, or after the last ticket already in the target stage.
const moveTicket = (id: string, stage: StageId, beforeId: string | null) => {
  const ticket = tickets.find((t) => t.id === id);
  if (!ticket) return;
  if (beforeId === id) {
    if (ticket.stage === stage) return;
    beforeId = null;
  }
  setTickets((list) => {
    const current = list.find((t) => t.id === id);
    if (!current) return list;
    const rest = list.filter((t) => t.id !== id);
    let at = beforeId ? rest.findIndex((t) => t.id === beforeId) : -1;
    if (at < 0) {
      at = rest.length;
      for (let i = rest.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        if (rest[i]?.stage === stage) {
          at = i + 1;
          break;
        }
      }
    }
    return [...rest.slice(0, at), withStage(current, stage), ...rest.slice(at)];
  });
  const label = stageOf(stage).label;
  const message = ticket.stage === stage ? `Reordered ${id} in ${label}` : `${id} moved to ${label}`;
  if (ticket.stage !== stage) log(`Jordan moved ${id} to ${label}`);
  setAnnouncement(message);
};

const onDropTicket = (id: string) => {
  const target = drop;
  setDragId(null);
  setDrop(null);
  if (target) moveTicket(id, target.stage, target.beforeId);
};
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers, observers or global listeners: drag state lives in React state set by element drag events and is cleared on `dragend` and `drop`. Overlays and the Toaster clean up their own listeners.

**Reduced motion.** The ticket entry fade, token bar height and column-load width transitions all carry `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so changes apply instantly. Dragging uses the browser's own drag image and has no added animation.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Calling `preventDefault` only on the column. Cards sit on top of it, so each card must also cancel `dragover` (and stop it bubbling) or the drop is refused over cards.
- Clearing the drop target on every `dragleave`. The event fires when the pointer crosses into a child card; ignore it while `relatedTarget` is still inside the column.
- Counting the visible cards for the WIP limit. Filters would make a full column look under its limit; count the stage before filtering.
- Reordering inside a sorted view. With a sort active the display order is derived, so dropping still moves stage but the manual order only shows again under "Manual order".
- Wrapping a `PopoverTrigger` child in a plain `span`. The trigger must be an element that forwards its ref and props (a native `button` here) or the popover cannot anchor.

## Notes

- Composed from kit items: `DashboardSidebar`, `DashboardPageHeader`, `NotificationBellBadge`, `AvatarStack`, `PriorityBadge`, `Dropdown`, `Popover`, `Modal`, `Select`, `Input`, `Textarea`, `Checkbox` and `Toaster`. The board, panel and toolbar are this item's own files.
- New tickets slide in with a CSS `@starting-style` fade and lift (`starting:opacity-0 starting:translate-y-1`), switched off under `motion-reduce`.

## Definition of done

At 1280x800 the sidebar shows Project board selected and the board shows Backlog 3/8, To do 3/5, In progress 2/4, Review 1/3 and Done 4/6. Dragging FE-76 onto Done makes Review 0/3 and Done 5/6 with "Completed 15 Sep" on the card. New ticket with a title adds it to the top of Backlog (4/8) and toasts. Clicking a card opens its panel; changing Status moves the card; posting a comment adds it to the list. Filter by Urgent leaves only DS-31 visible. Clicking Calendar in the sidebar shows the placeholder and "Back to Project board" returns.

# Build: Props Table

A documentation table for a component API: prop name in a grey code chip, the TypeScript type in the purple command colour, the default in muted code and a plain-language description. Required and deprecated props get small tinted tags. When the slot it sits in is narrower than 42rem, the same table re-flows into one bordered card per prop with Type and Default labels.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

API props table with code-styled names, types and defaults; long unions collapse, and narrow slots stack each prop into a card.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The root is an `@container`; every layout switch uses `@2xl:` container variants, so the table reacts to the width of the column it lives in (a sidebar, a modal, a phone) rather than the viewport.
2. Mobile-first, the `<table>`, `<tbody>` and `<tr>` are `block` / `flex flex-col` and each row is a rounded bordered card; from `@2xl` they return to `table`, `table-row-group` and `table-row` with a top separator instead of a card border. Explicit `role="table|rowgroup|row|columnheader|rowheader|cell"` attributes keep the semantics that `display` overrides strip in some engines.
3. The header row is `sr-only` in card mode (`@2xl:not-sr-only` brings it back) and each cell carries its own `aria-hidden` label ("Type", "Default") that is `@2xl:hidden`, so sighted users get labels in cards while screen readers keep the column headers.
4. A string `type` is split by `splitUnion`, which walks the string and only splits on `|` at depth 0 outside quotes (tracking `([{<` and ignoring the `>` of `=>`). Unions with more than `maxUnionMembers` members show the first ones plus a "+N more" button with `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`; the expanded rows are kept in a `Set` keyed by prop name.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `stack breakpoint = @2xl (42rem / 672px container width)`
  Below this the four columns squeeze descriptions into 2-3 words per line; the card layout reads better.
- `maxUnionMembers = 4 (demo uses 3)`
  Four literal members fit one line of a 30% column; longer unions wrap into a wall of code.
- `column widths = 22% / 30% / 14% / rest`
  Types need the most room after descriptions; defaults are short literals.
- `cell padding = px-4 py-3, header py-2.5`
  Matches the 16px inset of the docs preview cards and keeps rows at a ~44px minimum.

## API

```ts
function PropsTable(props: { rows: PropsTableRow[]; caption?: string; maxUnionMembers?: number; labels?: PropsTableLabels; idPrefix?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type PropsTableRow = { name: string; type: string | ReactNode; default?: string | ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; required?: boolean; deprecated?: boolean }
function splitUnion(type: string): string[]
```

- `rows: PropsTableRow[]`
  One entry per prop: name, type, optional default, description, required and deprecated flags.
- `caption: string`
  Visually hidden `<caption>` naming the table.
- `maxUnionMembers: number` — default `4`
  Unions longer than this collapse behind a "+N more" toggle; 0 never collapses.
- `labels: PropsTableLabels` — default `{ name: "Prop", type: "Type", default: "Default", description: "Description", ... }`
  Header and tag wording, for localisation.
- `idPrefix: string`
  Gives each row an id of `<idPrefix>-<name>` for deep links.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the container element.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * Splits a type string on `|` at nesting depth 0, so
 * `"a" | Array<"b" | "c"> | (() => void)` yields three members.
 */
export function splitUnion(type: string): string[] {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  let depth = 0;
  let quote: string | null = null;
  let start = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < type.length; i++) {
    const ch = type[i];
    if (quote) {
      if (ch === quote && type[i - 1] !== "\\") quote = null;
      continue;
    }
    if (ch === '"' || ch === "'" || ch === "`") quote = ch;
    else if (ch === "(" || ch === "[" || ch === "{" || ch === "<") depth++;
    else if (ch === ")" || ch === "]" || ch === "}" || (ch === ">" && type[i - 1] !== "=")) depth = Math.max(0, depth - 1);
    else if (ch === "|" && depth === 0) {
      parts.push(type.slice(start, i).trim());
      start = i + 1;
    }
  }
  parts.push(type.slice(start).trim());
  return parts.filter(Boolean);
}

function TypeCell({
  type,
  max,
  expanded,
  onToggle,
  controlsId,
}: {
  type: PropsTableRow["type"];
  max: number;
  expanded: boolean;
  onToggle: () => void;
  controlsId: string;
}) {
  if (typeof type !== "string") return <>{type}</>;
  const members = splitUnion(type);
  const collapsible = max > 0 && members.length > max;
  const shown = collapsible && !expanded ? members.slice(0, max) : members;
  return (
    <span className="inline-flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-x-1 gap-y-0.5">
      <code id={controlsId} className="font-mono text-caption-1-regular break-words text-docs-command-accent">
        {shown.map((member, i) => (
          <span key={`${member}-${i}`}>
            {i > 0 ? <span className="text-text-tertiary"> | </span> : null}
            {member}
          </span>
        ))}
      </code>
      {collapsible ? (
        <button
          type="button"
          aria-expanded={expanded}
          aria-controls={controlsId}
          onClick={onToggle}
          className={cx(
            "cursor-pointer rounded-md px-1 text-caption-1-medium text-text-tertiary outline-none",
            "transition-colors duration-150 ease-out hover:bg-background-secondary-hover hover:text-text-primary motion-reduce:transition-none",
            "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
          )}
        >
          {expanded ? "Show less" : `+${members.length - max} more`}
        </button>
      ) : null}
    </span>
  );
}

const CELL_LABEL = "w-20 shrink-0 text-caption-1-medium text-text-tertiary @2xl:hidden";

export function PropsTable({
  rows,
  caption,
  maxUnionMembers = 4,
  labels: labelsProp,
  idPrefix,
  className,
}: PropsTableProps) {
  const labels = { ...DEFAULT_LABELS, ...labelsProp };
  const baseId = useId();
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState<ReadonlySet<string>>(() => new Set());
  const toggle = (name: string) =>
    setExpanded((prev) => {
      const next = new Set(prev);
      if (next.has(name)) next.delete(name);
      else next.add(name);
      return next;
    });

  // Explicit ARIA roles keep table semantics while the narrow layout sets
  // every element to block/flex (display overrides strip implicit roles in
  // some engines). The layout switch is a container query, so it follows the
  // width of the slot the table sits in, not the viewport.
  return (
    <div className={cx("@container w-full", className)}>
      <div className="@2xl:overflow-hidden @2xl:rounded-2xl @2xl:border @2xl:border-border-component-detail-container @2xl:bg-background-primary-default">
        <table role="table" className="block w-full border-collapse text-start @2xl:table">
          {caption ? <caption className="sr-only">{caption}</caption> : null}
          <thead role="rowgroup" className="sr-only @2xl:not-sr-only @2xl:table-header-group">
            <tr role="row" className="@2xl:bg-background-secondary-default">
              {[
                [labels.name, "w-[22%]"],
                [labels.type, "w-[30%]"],
                [labels.default, "w-[14%]"],
                [labels.description, ""],
              ].map(([label, width]) => (
                <th
                  key={label}
                  role="columnheader"
                  scope="col"
                  className={cx("px-4 py-2.5 text-start align-middle text-caption-1-medium text-text-tertiary", width)}
                >
                  {label}
                </th>
              ))}
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody role="rowgroup" className="flex flex-col gap-2 @2xl:table-row-group">
            {rows.map((row) => {
              const typeId = `${baseId}-${row.name}-type`;
              return (
                <tr
                  key={row.name}
                  role="row"
                  id={idPrefix ? `${idPrefix}-${row.name}` : undefined}
                  className={cx(
                    "flex scroll-mt-20 flex-col gap-2 rounded-2xl border border-border-component-detail-container bg-background-primary-default p-4",
                    "@2xl:table-row @2xl:rounded-none @2xl:border-0 @2xl:border-t @2xl:border-border-table @2xl:bg-transparent @2xl:p-0",
                    "@2xl:target:bg-background-secondary-default",
                  )}
                >
                  <th role="rowheader" scope="row" className="block text-start font-normal @2xl:table-cell @2xl:px-4 @2xl:py-3 @2xl:align-top">
                    <span className="inline-flex flex-wrap items-center gap-1.5">
                      <code
                        className={cx(
                          "rounded-md bg-background-secondary-default px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-caption-1-medium text-text-primary",
                          row.deprecated && "text-text-tertiary line-through",
                        )}
                      >
                        {row.name}
                      </code>
                      {row.required ? (
                        <span className="rounded-sm bg-status-rose-background px-1 text-caption-2-medium text-status-rose-text">
                          {labels.required}
                        </span>
                      ) : null}
                      {row.deprecated ? (
                        <span className="rounded-sm bg-status-yellow-background px-1 text-caption-2-medium text-status-yellow-text">
                          {labels.deprecated}
                        </span>
                      ) : null}
                    </span>
                  </th>
                  <td role="cell" className="flex gap-3 @2xl:table-cell @2xl:px-4 @2xl:py-3 @2xl:align-top">
                    <span aria-hidden className={CELL_LABEL}>
                      {labels.type}
                    </span>
                    <TypeCell
                      type={row.type}
                      max={maxUnionMembers}
                      expanded={expanded.has(row.name)}
                      onToggle={() => toggle(row.name)}
                      controlsId={typeId}
                    />
                  </td>
                  <td role="cell" className="flex gap-3 @2xl:table-cell @2xl:px-4 @2xl:py-3 @2xl:align-top">
                    <span aria-hidden className={CELL_LABEL}>
                      {labels.default}
                    </span>
                    {row.default === undefined ? (
                      <span className="text-caption-1-regular text-text-tertiary">
                        <span aria-hidden>—</span>
                        <span className="sr-only">{labels.none}</span>
                      </span>
                    ) : typeof row.default === "string" ? (
                      <code className="font-mono text-caption-1-regular break-words text-text-secondary">{row.default}</code>
                    ) : (
                      row.default
                    )}
                  </td>
                  <td
                    role="cell"
                    className={cx(
                      "block text-body-regular text-text-secondary @2xl:table-cell @2xl:border-0 @2xl:px-4 @2xl:py-3 @2xl:align-top",
                      row.description ? "border-t border-border-table pt-3" : "hidden",
                    )}
                  >
                    {row.description}
                  </td>
                </tr>
              );
            })}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to release: no timers, listeners or observers. Container queries are pure CSS.

**Reduced motion.** Only the "+N more" button has a 150ms colour transition, removed with `motion-reduce:transition-none`. The layout switch is instant.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using viewport breakpoints (`md:`) for the stack switch. A props table in a narrow docs column on a wide screen would stay a cramped table; a container query follows the slot.
- Setting `display: block` on table elements without explicit ARIA roles. Some browsers then expose a flat list of text with no row or column relationships.
- Splitting union types on every `|`. Pipes inside generics, tuples, object types or string literals belong to one member.
- Labelling card cells with visible text that screen readers also hear next to the real column header. Mark the inline labels `aria-hidden`.

## Notes

- Pass a ReactNode as `type` or `default` to skip union splitting and render your own markup (links to type docs, for example).
- With `idPrefix`, each row gets `id="<prefix>-<name>"` and `scroll-mt-20`, and a `:target` row is highlighted in table mode.
