# Build: Proximity Snap Track

A scrollable rail whose items may be any width. `scroll-snap-type: x proximity` snaps to an item only when the scroll comes to rest near one, so free scanning stays free. `scroll-snap-stop: always` caps a single fling at one item, so a hard swipe cannot launch the user past six cards. No JavaScript runs during the scroll.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A horizontal rail of variable-width cards that snaps only when you stop near one, and never skips past two at once.

- Category: layout
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The container is `overflow-x: auto` with `scroll-snap-type: x proximity`. `proximity` means the browser only adjusts the resting position when the natural end of the scroll already falls close to a snap point; anywhere else, it leaves the position exactly where the user left it.
2. Each item declares `scroll-snap-align: start` (or `center`) — this is what makes it a snap point at all — and `scroll-snap-stop: always`, which forbids the browser from passing more than one snap point per gesture no matter how much momentum the fling carried.
3. `scroll-padding-inline` is set alongside `padding-inline` to the same gutter. They are different properties: `padding` insets the content, `scroll-padding` insets the *snapport* — the rectangle a snap position is measured against. With padding alone, a `start`-aligned item comes to rest flush against the container border and the inset the design asked for vanishes at every rest position.
4. `overscroll-behavior-x: contain` stops a horizontal fling that reaches the end of the rail from chaining to an ancestor scroller or triggering the browser's back-navigation gesture.
5. `scroll-behavior` is `smooth` normally and `auto` under reduced motion, which affects programmatic and keyboard-initiated scrolls. The snap adjustment itself is the browser's own and already respects the OS setting.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `snapType = 'proximity'`
  The whole argument of this component. With `mandatory`, the browser must always come to rest on a snap point, so on a rail of variable-width items it is physically impossible to stop between two of them — every attempt to park somewhere gets yanked. Worse, on a long rail `mandatory` plus a short flick can leave the user unable to reach a position at all. `proximity` snaps when it helps and gets out of the way when it does not.
- `snapStop = 'always'`
  Without it, a hard fling on a trackpad passes every snap point and lands on whichever item the momentum ran out over — which on a rail of 20 cards means the user has no way to advance by exactly one. `always` turns each item into a gate.
- `snapAlign = 'start'`
  Correct default for variable-width items: their left edges line up at rest, which reads as a column of starts. `center` is right only when items are uniform, because with mixed widths a centred rest position puts every item's left edge somewhere different.
- `gutter = 16`
  Set on both `padding-inline` and `scroll-padding-inline`. The two must match or the resting inset and the visual inset disagree by exactly this many pixels, which looks like a rounding bug.
- `gap = 12`
  Large enough that two adjacent cards read as separate snap targets, small enough that the next card is clearly a continuation of the row rather than a separate section.

## API

```ts
function ProximitySnapTrack(props: { children: ReactNode; snapType?: 'proximity' | 'mandatory'; snapAlign?: 'start' | 'center'; snapStop?: 'normal' | 'always'; gutter?: number; gap?: number; className?: string; itemClassName?: string; 'aria-label'?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  One item per child. Widths may differ.
- `snapType: 'proximity' | 'mandatory'` — default `'proximity'`
  Snap strictness. `mandatory` is exposed so the difference can be felt, not because it is usually right here.
- `snapAlign: 'start' | 'center'` — default `'start'`
  Which edge of an item lines up with the snapport.
- `snapStop: 'normal' | 'always'` — default `'always'`
  `always` caps one gesture at one item.
- `gutter: number` — default `16`
  Inset in px, applied to both `padding-inline` and `scroll-padding-inline`.
- `gap: number` — default `12`
  Gap between items in px.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the scroll container.
- `itemClassName: string`
  Merged onto each item cell.
- `aria-label: string` — default `'Track'`
  Label for the focusable scroll region.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const trackStyle: CSSProperties = {
  scrollSnapType: `x ${snapType}`,
  // `scroll-padding` is what a snap position is measured against, and it is
  // a separate property from `padding`. With padding alone, a `start`-aligned
  // item snaps flush to the container's border and the inset the design asked
  // for silently disappears at every rest position.
  scrollPaddingInline: `${gutter}px`,
  paddingInline: `${gutter}px`,
  gap: `${gap}px`,
  // Programmatic scrolls (anchor jumps, `scrollIntoView`, arrow keys in some
  // engines) animate unless told not to. Snapping itself is not affected —
  // it is the browser's own transition and honours the OS setting already.
  scrollBehavior: reduced ? 'auto' : 'smooth',
};

const itemStyle: CSSProperties = {
  scrollSnapAlign: snapAlign,
  scrollSnapStop: snapStop,
};
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to release. All behaviour is declarative CSS on nodes React owns; the only subscription is `useReducedMotion`, which removes its own `matchMedia` listener on unmount. No listeners, no timers, no rAF.

**Reduced motion.** The rail behaves identically — it is a scroll container, and scrolling is the user moving, not the interface animating. The one change is `scroll-behavior: auto` instead of `smooth`, so keyboard and programmatic scrolls jump rather than glide. The snap adjustment is the browser's own transition and already follows the OS setting without any help.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory` on a track with variable-width items. It makes it impossible to rest between items: every release is pulled to a snap point, so the user cannot park where they want, and on a long rail with wide items they end up fighting the browser for the whole length of the track. `proximity` is the correct choice whenever the items are not uniform or the track is long.
- Setting `padding-inline` without `scroll-padding-inline`. Every rest position then puts the item flush against the container edge, so the gutter appears while scrolling and disappears the instant you let go.
- Omitting `scroll-snap-stop: always`. A single hard swipe lands eight cards along, which makes stepping by one impossible and makes the rail feel slippery rather than mechanical.
- Hiding the scrollbar without making the container focusable. The rail becomes invisible to keyboard users and to anyone who was relying on the scrollbar as the affordance. `tabIndex={0}` and a `role`/`aria-label` restore arrow-key scrolling, and Chrome stops warning about a non-focusable scroll container.
- Leaving `overscroll-behavior-x` at `auto`. Flinging past the end chains into the page or, in Safari and Chrome, triggers the swipe-to-go-back gesture and the user loses the page.
- Reaching for a JS carousel because "the design has arrows". A snap track already has momentum, rubber-banding, keyboard support and accessible scroll semantics; arrows are one `scrollBy` call on top, not a reason to replace the mechanism.

## Notes

- Snap is a layout-level contract, not an animation. Everything here runs on the compositor and continues to work when the main thread is blocked, which is the reason to prefer it over a JS track whenever the interaction is genuinely "a scrollable row".
- Items are `shrink-0`. Without it, flex would compress them to fit the container and the track would never overflow, so there would be nothing to snap.
- `scroll-snap-stop` is ignored during programmatic scrolls in every engine — it only constrains user gestures. Arrows implemented with `scrollTo` can therefore still jump several items at once by design.

## Definition of done

Scroll the rail slowly and stop between two cards — it stays where you left it. Stop just past a card's edge and it eases onto that card. Fling as hard as you can and it advances exactly one card. Tab to the rail and press the arrow keys: it scrolls and snaps the same way. At every rest position the leading card sits inset from the container edge by the gutter, not flush against it.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Questionnaire

A chat-thread card that walks through a few questions, one at a time. Multiple-select questions are checkbox rows; single-select questions number their rows, and a click or the digit key picks and moves on after a short beat so the choice is seen landing. An optional Other row takes free text. The footer has a pill per question for jumping around plus Previous and Next, which reads Done on the last step. Questions slide in the direction of travel while the card eases to the new height.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

The questions an agent asks before it plans: one per step, checkbox or numbered rows, a free-text Other and step pills.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: motion@^12.43.0

## How it works

1. Answers are keyed by question id as { values, other? }: values keep option order, and other exists only while the Other row is selected. Typed text is kept in a separate drafts map so unticking Other and ticking it again restores it.
2. answers and step are each controllable: the prop wins when given, otherwise internal state holds it, and the change callback fires either way.
3. A single-select pick writes { values: [value] } and schedules goTo(step + 1) after advanceDelay; the timeout is cleared by any other navigation and on unmount. When the pick moves the card on, focus lands on the next question's first row.
4. goTo records the direction (+1 or -1, mirrored in RTL); AnimatePresence in popLayout mode hands it to both the entering and the exiting panel so they slide opposite ways at once.
5. The exiting panel is popped out of flow, so a shared ResizeObserver on the panel wrapper reports the new question's height right away, and an outer motion.div animates its height to it with overflow hidden.
6. One keydown handler on the card maps 1-9 to rows (the last digit focuses the Other input) and ArrowUp/ArrowDown to moving focus between rows; it ignores typing inside the input, where Enter sends the free text.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `advanceDelay = 180ms`
  Long enough to see the row and its key turn selected, short enough that picking feels like one action.
- `slide = 28px, 320ms, cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), 2px blur`
  A short travel distance keeps the two overlapping panels readable while they cross.
- `height = 300ms on the same curve`
  Finishes with the slide so the footer settles once.

## API

```ts
<Questionnaire questions={[{ id: "permission", select: "single", question: "How should the permission pill behave?", options: [{ value: "lock", label: "Lock it" }], other: true }]} onComplete={(answers) => plan(answers)} onDismiss={() => setOpen(false)} />
```

- `questions: readonly QuestionnaireQuestion[]`
  Each has id, question, options ({ value, label, description? }), optional other (true or { label, placeholder }), select and stepLabel.
- `select: "single" | "multiple"` — default `"multiple"`
  Default mode for questions that do not set their own.
- `advanceDelay: number` — default `180`
  Milliseconds before a single-select pick moves to the next question.
- `answers: QuestionnaireAnswers`
  Controlled answers keyed by question id.
- `defaultAnswers: QuestionnaireAnswers` — default `{}`
  Initial answers when uncontrolled.
- `onAnswersChange: (answers: QuestionnaireAnswers) => void`
  Fires on every pick, untick or keystroke in Other.
- `step: number`
  Controlled index of the visible question.
- `defaultStep: number` — default `0`
  Initial question when uncontrolled.
- `onStepChange: (step: number) => void`
  Fires when Previous, Next, a pill or an auto-advance changes the question.
- `onComplete: (answers: QuestionnaireAnswers) => void`
  Fires when Done is pressed on the last question, or Enter is pressed in its Other field.
- `onDismiss: () => void`
  Shows the corner dismiss button when set.
- `labels: QuestionnaireLabels`
  previous, next, complete, other, otherPlaceholder, dismiss and steps.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Questions"`
  Accessible name of the card.
- `className: string`
  Classes on the card.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function Questionnaire({
  questions,
  select = 'multiple',
  advanceDelay = 180,
  answers: answersProp,
  defaultAnswers,
  onAnswersChange,
  step: stepProp,
  defaultStep = 0,
  onStepChange,
  onComplete,
  onDismiss,
  labels = {},
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Questions',
  className,
}: QuestionnaireProps) {
  const uid = useId();
  const reduce = useReducedMotion();
  const rtl = useDirection() === 'rtl';
  const [answers, setAnswers] = useControlled<QuestionnaireAnswers>(answersProp, defaultAnswers ?? {}, onAnswersChange);
  const [rawStep, setStep] = useControlled<number>(stepProp, defaultStep, onStepChange);
  const last = Math.max(questions.length - 1, 0);
  const step = Math.min(Math.max(rawStep, 0), last);
  const q = questions[step];

  // Direction of travel: +1 forward, -1 back. Read by both the entering and the exiting panel.
  const [dir, setDir] = useState(1);
  // Free text survives unticking Other, so ticking it again restores what was typed.
  const [drafts, setDrafts] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const bodyRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const { height } = useResizeObserver(bodyRef);
  const timer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
  const focusAfter = useRef(false);

  const clearTimer = () => {
    if (timer.current !== null) clearTimeout(timer.current);
    timer.current = null;
  };
  useEffect(() => clearTimer, []);

  const goTo = (next: number, refocus = false) => {
    clearTimer();
    const target = Math.min(Math.max(next, 0), last);
    if (target === step) return;
    setDir(target > step ? 1 : -1);
    focusAfter.current = refocus;
    setStep(target);
  };

  // A pick that moves the card on unmounts the focused row; land focus on the next question's first row.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!focusAfter.current) return;
    focusAfter.current = false;
    rootRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-step="${step}"] [data-q-row]`)?.focus({ preventScroll: true });
  }, [step]);

  if (!q) return null;
  const mode = q.select ?? select;
  const other = otherConfig(q, labels);
  const answer = answers[q.id] ?? EMPTY;
  const otherOn = answer.other !== undefined;
  const isLast = step === last;

  const write = (next: QuestionnaireAnswer) => setAnswers({ ...answers, [q.id]: next });

  const toggle = (value: string) => {
    const on = answer.values.includes(value);
    const values = q.options.map((o) => o.value).filter((v) => (v === value ? !on : answer.values.includes(v)));
    write({ ...answer, values });
  };

  const pick = (value: string) => {
    write({ values: [value] });
    clearTimer();
    if (isLast) return;
    const from = step;
    timer.current = setTimeout(() => goTo(from + 1, true), advanceDelay);
  };

  const setOtherText = (text: string) => {
    setDrafts((d) => ({ ...d, [q.id]: text }));
    const filled = text.trim().length > 0;
    if (mode === 'single') write(filled ? { values: [], other: text } : { values: [] });
    else write(filled ? { ...answer, other: text } : { values: answer.values });
  };

  const toggleOther = () => {
    if (otherOn) write({ values: answer.values });
    else write({ ...answer, other: drafts[q.id] ?? '' });
  };

  const advance = () => {
    if (isLast) {
      clearTimer();
      onComplete?.(answers);
    } else goTo(step + 1);
  };

  const otherInputId = `${uid}-other`;
  const rowCount = q.options.length + (other ? 1 : 0);

  const onKeyDown = (event: ReactKeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (event.altKey || event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey) return;
    const target = event.target as HTMLElement;
    if (target.tagName === 'INPUT' || target.tagName === 'TEXTAREA') return;
    if (event.key === 'ArrowDown' || event.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      const rows = Array.from(
        rootRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(`[data-step="${step}"] [data-q-row]`) ?? [],
      );
      const at = rows.indexOf(target);
      if (at < 0) return;
      event.preventDefault();
      rows[(at + (event.key === 'ArrowDown' ? 1 : -1) + rows.length) % rows.length]?.focus();
      return;
    }
    if (!/^[1-9]$/.test(event.key)) return;
    const index = Number(event.key) - 1;
    if (index >= rowCount) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    const option = q.options[index];
    if (option) {
      if (mode === 'single') pick(option.value);
      else toggle(option.value);
    } else {
      document.getElementById(otherInputId)?.focus();
    }
  };

  const shift = reduce ? 0 : rtl ? -28 : 28;
  const variants: Variants = {
    enter: (d: number) => ({ x: d * shift, opacity: 0, filter: reduce ? 'none' : 'blur(2px)' }),
    center: { x: 0, opacity: 1, filter: reduce ? 'none' : 'blur(0px)' },
    exit: (d: number) => ({ x: -d * shift, opacity: 0, filter: reduce ? 'none' : 'blur(2px)' }),
  };
  const slide = reduce ? { duration: 0.12 } : { duration: 0.32, ease: EASE_OUT };

  return (
    <div
      ref={rootRef}
      role="group"
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
      className={cx(
        'relative w-full rounded-2xl bg-background-primary-default p-3 shadow-sm ring-1 ring-border-button-default',
        className,
      )}
    >
      {onDismiss ? (
        <CloseButton aria-label={labels.dismiss ?? 'Dismiss questions'} onClick={onDismiss} className="absolute end-3 top-3 z-10" />
      ) : null}

      <motion.div
        initial={false}
        animate={{ height: height > 0 ? height : 'auto' }}
        transition={reduce ? { duration: 0 } : { duration: 0.3, ease: EASE_OUT }}
        className="overflow-hidden"
      >
        <div ref={bodyRef} className="relative">
          <AnimatePresence initial={false} mode="popLayout" custom={dir}>
            <motion.div
              key={step}
              data-step={step}
              custom={dir}
              variants={variants}
              initial="enter"
              animate="center"
              exit="exit"
              transition={slide}
              className="flex w-full flex-col gap-2"
            >
              <p id={`${uid}-q${step}`} className={cx('px-0.5 pb-0.5 text-body-medium text-text-primary', onDismiss && 'pe-8')}>
                {q.question}
              </p>
              <div
                role={mode === 'single' ? 'radiogroup' : 'group'}
                aria-labelledby={`${uid}-q${step}`}
                className="flex flex-col gap-2"
              >
                {q.options.map((option, i) => {
                  const on = answer.values.includes(option.value);
                  const id = `${uid}-${step}-${i}`;
                  return (
                    <button
                      key={option.value}
                      type="button"
                      data-q-row
                      role={mode === 'single' ? 'radio' : 'checkbox'}
                      aria-checked={on}
                      aria-labelledby={`${id}-l`}
                      aria-describedby={option.description ? `${id}-d` : undefined}
                      aria-keyshortcuts={String(i + 1)}
                      onClick={() => (mode === 'single' ? pick(option.value) : toggle(option.value))}
                      className={cx(
                        ROW,
                        on ? 'border-border-button-hover bg-background-primary-hover' : 'border-border-button-default',
                      )}
                    >
                      <RowText id={id} label={option.label} description={option.description} />
                      {mode === 'single' ? <NumberKey n={i + 1} on={on} /> : tick(on)}
                    </button>
                  );
                })}

                {other ? (
                  <div
                    onClick={(event) => {
                      if ((event.target as HTMLElement).closest('input,button')) return;
                      document.getElementById(otherInputId)?.focus();
                    }}
                    className={cx(
                      ROW,
                      'cursor-text focus-within:ring-2 focus-within:ring-inset focus-within:ring-border-focus-ring',
                      otherOn ? 'border-border-button-hover bg-background-primary-hover' : 'border-border-button-default',
                    )}
                  >
                    <span className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col">
                      <label htmlFor={otherInputId} className="text-body-medium text-text-primary">
                        {other.label}
                      </label>
                      <input
                        id={otherInputId}
                        data-q-row
                        value={drafts[q.id] ?? answer.other ?? ''}
                        placeholder={other.placeholder}
                        onChange={(event) => setOtherText(event.target.value)}
                        onKeyDown={(event) => {
                          if (event.key !== 'Enter') return;
                          event.preventDefault();
                          if (mode === 'single' && !otherOn) return;
                          advance();
                        }}
                        aria-keyshortcuts={String(rowCount)}
                        className="w-full min-w-0 bg-transparent p-0 text-body-regular text-text-primary outline-none placeholder:text-text-placeholder"
                      />
                    </span>
                    {mode === 'single' ? (
                      <NumberKey n={rowCount} on={otherOn} />
                    ) : (
                      <button
                        type="button"
                        role="checkbox"
                        aria-checked={otherOn}
                        aria-label={other.label}
                        onClick={toggleOther}
                        className="rounded-sm outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2"
                      >
                        {tick(otherOn)}
                      </button>
                    )}
                  </div>
                ) : null}
              </div>
            </motion.div>
          </AnimatePresence>
        </div>
      </motion.div>

      <div className="mt-3 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-1 gap-y-2">
        <div role="group" aria-label={labels.steps ?? 'Steps'} className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-1">
          {questions.map((item, i) => (
            <button
              key={item.id}
              type="button"
              aria-current={i === step ? 'step' : undefined}
              onClick={() => goTo(i)}
              className={cx(
                'rounded-full px-2 py-1 text-body-regular outline-none',
                'transition-colors duration-150 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none',
                'focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring',
                i === step
                  ? 'bg-status-blue-background text-status-blue-text'
                  : 'text-text-secondary hover:bg-background-primary-hover hover:text-text-primary',
              )}
            >
              {item.stepLabel ?? `Step ${i + 1}`}
            </button>
          ))}
        </div>
        <div className="ms-auto flex items-center gap-2">
          <Button variant="secondary" size="small" disabled={step === 0} onClick={() => goTo(step - 1)}>
            {labels.previous ?? 'Previous'}
          </Button>
          <Button variant="primary" size="small" onClick={advance}>
            {isLast ? (labels.complete ?? 'Done') : (labels.next ?? 'Next')}
          </Button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <span aria-live="polite" className="sr-only">
        {`Question ${step + 1} of ${questions.length}`}
      </span>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The pending auto-advance timeout is cleared on every navigation and on unmount; the height observer is released on unmount. Keyboard handling is a React handler on the card, so no global listeners are attached.

**Reduced motion.** Questions swap with a 120ms crossfade instead of the slide and blur, the card height changes instantly, and row colour transitions are off. Single-select picks still wait advanceDelay so the choice is visible.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Give every question a stable, unique id: answers and drafts are stored by it.
- A pick on the last single-select question does not complete on its own; Done fires onComplete, so a stray click cannot send the answers.
- When you control step, keep it inside 0..questions.length - 1; out-of-range values are clamped for display only.
- Digit keys only work while focus is inside the card, so they never steal keys from the rest of the page.

## Notes

- select on a question overrides the card-level select, so one card can mix checkbox and numbered questions.
- labels rewords Previous, Next, Done, the Other row, the dismiss button and the steps group.
- onComplete receives the answers as they stand; questions left unanswered are absent or have empty values.

## Definition of done

Ticking two rows on step 1 sets both checkboxes and Next moves to step 2 with the card sliding left; pressing 2 there highlights Queue the change and moves to step 3 on its own; Previous returns with the pick still highlighted; typing in Other ticks it; the pills jump straight to any step; Done on step 4 shows the summary, Edit answers comes back with every answer intact and Start over clears them.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Quick Search Button

The search entry point for an app or docs header. It looks like a small search field (magnifier, "Search..." and a ⌘ K key hint) but is a button. Clicking it, or pressing ⌘K / Ctrl+K anywhere on the page, opens the existing CommandPalette with whatever sections and items you pass as children; running an item closes the palette and reports its id.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A "Search..." field-style trigger with a ⌘K hint that opens the kit command palette, and a global ⌘K / Ctrl+K shortcut that toggles it.

- Category: action
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The trigger is a native `button` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-keyshortcuts` ("Meta+K" on Apple platforms, "Control+K" elsewhere). The key hint is two kit `Kbd` elements marked `aria-hidden`, since the shortcut is already exposed through `aria-keyshortcuts`.
2. Open state lives here and is passed to `CommandPalette` as `isOpen` / `onOpenChange`, with the palette's own shortcut turned off (`shortcut={false}`), so exactly one keyboard listener exists. The query is controlled too (`inputValue` / `onInputChange`) and cleared on every open, because the palette only resets it when it opens itself.
3. A single `keydown` listener on `window`, added in an effect and removed in its cleanup, accepts ⌘ or Ctrl plus `shortcutKey` (default "k"), ignores Alt, Shift and auto-repeat, calls `preventDefault` so the browser address-bar shortcut does not fire, and toggles the palette.
4. The ⌘ versus Ctrl glyph comes from `useSyncExternalStore` with a server snapshot of "Apple", so server HTML and the hydration pass agree and Windows or Linux visitors see "Ctrl" right after hydration with no mismatch warning.
5. Everything inside the palette (filtering, arrow-key navigation, Escape, focus return to the trigger, the modal scrim) is the kit CommandPalette built on React Aria Autocomplete and Menu.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `shortcutKey = "k"`
  ⌘K / Ctrl+K is the convention people already try first for search and command menus.
- `trigger width = w-full, max 16rem`
  Wide enough to read as a field in a header, and it shrinks with a truncating label in tight bars.

## API

```ts
function QuickSearchButton(props: { label?: string; shortcutKey?: string; placeholder?: string; paletteLabel?: string; onAction?: (key: Key) => void; children: ReactNode; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `label: string` — default `"Search..."`
  Trigger text.
- `shortcutKey: string` — default `"k"`
  Letter pressed with ⌘ or Ctrl to toggle the palette; also shown in the key hint.
- `placeholder: string`
  Palette input placeholder; the palette default is used when omitted.
- `paletteLabel: string` — default `"Search"`
  Accessible name of the palette dialog.
- `onAction: (key: Key) => void`
  Called with the id of the item that was run.
- `children: ReactNode`
  CommandPaletteSection and CommandPaletteItem elements.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the trigger button.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function QuickSearchButton({
  label = "Search...",
  shortcutKey = "k",
  placeholder,
  paletteLabel = "Search",
  onAction,
  children,
  className,
}: QuickSearchButtonProps) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  // The query is controlled here: the palette only clears it when it opens itself, and here it is opened from outside.
  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
  // Server and first hydration render use the Mac glyph; the real platform lands right after without a mismatch.
  const apple = useSyncExternalStore(noop, isApple, () => true);
  const key = shortcutKey.toLowerCase();

  // One global listener for ⌘K / Ctrl+K. It toggles, so the same chord closes an open palette.
  useEffect(() => {
    const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (!(event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) || event.altKey || event.shiftKey) return;
      if (event.key.toLowerCase() !== key || event.repeat) return;
      event.preventDefault();
      setQuery("");
      setOpen((current) => !current);
    };
    window.addEventListener("keydown", onKeyDown);
    return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKeyDown);
  }, [key]);

  return (
    <>
      <button
        type="button"
        onClick={() => {
          setQuery("");
          setOpen(true);
        }}
        aria-haspopup="dialog"
        aria-expanded={open}
        aria-keyshortcuts={`${apple ? "Meta" : "Control"}+${key.toUpperCase()}`}
        className={cx(
          "group inline-flex h-9 w-full max-w-64 min-w-0 cursor-pointer items-center gap-2 rounded-xl bg-background-primary-default pr-1.5 pl-3 text-start shadow-xs ring-1 ring-separator-border outline-none",
          "transition-[background-color,box-shadow] duration-150 ease-out hover:bg-background-secondary-default focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring motion-reduce:transition-none",
          className,
        )}
      >
        <RiSearchLine
          aria-hidden
          className="size-4 shrink-0 text-foreground-icon-tertiary transition-colors group-hover:text-foreground-icon-secondary motion-reduce:transition-none"
        />
        <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-body-2-regular text-text-tertiary transition-colors group-hover:text-text-secondary motion-reduce:transition-none">
          {label}
        </span>
        <span aria-hidden className="flex shrink-0 items-center gap-0.5">
          <Kbd className="min-w-5">{apple ? "⌘" : "Ctrl"}</Kbd>
          <Kbd className="min-w-5">{key.toUpperCase()}</Kbd>
        </span>
      </button>

      <CommandPalette
        isOpen={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        shortcut={false}
        aria-label={paletteLabel}
        placeholder={placeholder}
        inputValue={query}
        onInputChange={setQuery}
        onAction={onAction}
      >
        {children}
      </CommandPalette>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The window `keydown` listener is removed when the component unmounts or `shortcutKey` changes. The palette is closed state, not a portal left behind.

**Reduced motion.** The trigger's hover colour transitions use `motion-reduce:transition-none`. The palette's open and close motion is handled by the kit CommandPalette.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Leaving the palette's built-in shortcut on while adding your own. Both listeners toggle on the same keypress and the palette opens and closes in one event; this component passes `shortcut={false}`.
- Reading `navigator` during render to choose ⌘ or Ctrl. The server has no navigator and the markup mismatches on hydration; `useSyncExternalStore` with a server snapshot avoids it.
- Controlling `isOpen` but not the query. The palette clears its own query only when it opens itself, so a palette opened from outside would come back showing the last search; the query is reset here on each open.
- Forgetting `preventDefault` on Ctrl+K. In Chrome and Firefox on Windows and Linux it focuses the browser search bar instead.

## Notes

- Children are ordinary `CommandPaletteSection` / `CommandPaletteItem` elements, so items can have icons, descriptions and shortcut hints.
- Mount one per page. Two instances would each register the global shortcut.

## Definition of done

The demo header shows a "Search..." field with a ⌘ K hint and no dialog open. Clicking it opens the palette with Pages and Actions sections and focus in the input. Typing "pri" leaves only Pricing; Enter runs it, closes the palette, returns focus to the trigger and the demo shows "Ran: Pricing". Pressing Ctrl+K (or ⌘K) opens it again with an empty query and pressing it a second time closes it. Escape also closes it.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: quickTo Cursor Preview

Hovering a row fades in a preview panel that then trails the pointer with a full second of catch-up, so it reads as a heavy object being dragged rather than a tooltip pinned to the cursor. Position comes from exactly two `gsap.quickTo` setters created once at mount; the hovered row is the only thing that ever enters React state.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A preview panel drifts a full second behind the pointer, driven by two reused quickTo tweens.

- Category: cursor
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. `gsap.quickTo(box, "x", { duration, ease })` returns a setter backed by ONE tween whose end value is mutated in place. A `pointermove` handler firing 60-120 times a second therefore allocates nothing after the first frame, where the `gsap.to()` equivalent allocates and garbage-collects a tween object per event and leaves each new tween fighting the last for the same property.
2. Hovered row is React state because it changes a handful of times a second and drives real DOM structure (text colour, stroke, offset). Panel position is never state: it changes on every pointer event, and a re-render per move would cost more than the animation it is driving.
3. `duration: 1` is roughly five times a normal cursor follow, and that is the entire design. Under `power3` the panel covers most of the gap early and then creeps, so it always reads as heading for the pointer without ever arriving — which is what makes it feel like mass rather than lag.
4. The first move after entry calls `xTo(x, x)` — quickTo's second argument is the tween's START value, so the panel is teleported rather than eased. Without it, re-entering the list sends the panel sailing diagonally across the whole component over a full second before it becomes useful.
5. Position is centred with `xPercent: -50, yPercent: -50` set once at mount, so `x`/`y` are raw pointer coordinates and no offset arithmetic appears in the hot handler.
6. Every preview is a gradient plate painted into an offscreen canvas at mount — the registry ships no image assets. Switching rows is one `drawImage` blit, so the gradient, band and text work never lands on the frame where the fade-in starts.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `duration = 1`
  Seconds of catch-up, and the whole character of the component. At 0.2 it is an ordinary tooltip that happens to be smooth; at 1 it is an object with weight. Past ~1.6 the panel is still crossing the list when the pointer has already left it, and the effect reads as broken rather than heavy.
- `ease: 'power3' = power3 (in-out)`
  In-out, not `.out`. Because the end value is remutated on every event, the tween is permanently restarting from its own midpoint; the symmetric curve means direction changes are absorbed smoothly instead of snapping to a new outward ramp each time.
- `FADE_DURATION = 0.35`
  Fade and scale on row change. Long enough to register as a cross-fade rather than a cut, short enough that dragging down a list of eight rows does not leave the panel permanently mid-transition.
- `scale 0.94 -> 1 = 0.94`
  A 6% growth on appear. Paired with opacity it reads as arriving from behind the page; without it the fade alone looks like a stuck render.
- `DOCK_INSET = 20`
  Pixels of margin when the panel docks to the right edge on touch or reduced motion. Clamped against `panelWidth / 2` so a panel wider than its container still lands fully inside rather than half off-screen.
- `PLATE_SCALE = 2`
  Backing-store multiplier for the plate canvases. Fixed rather than `devicePixelRatio` so the drawn output is identical on every machine and a visual regression is actually visible in a screenshot diff.

## API

```ts
function QuickToCursorPreview(props: { items: PreviewItem[]; duration?: number; panelWidth?: number; panelHeight?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `items: PreviewItem[]`
  Rows to render. `{ id, title, meta? }`; one plate is painted per item.
- `duration: number` — default `1`
  Seconds of catch-up on the follow. The defining value of the effect.
- `panelWidth: number` — default `260`
  Preview panel width in CSS px.
- `panelHeight: number` — default `180`
  Preview panel height in CSS px.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root container via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const PLATE_SCALE = 2;
const FADE_DURATION = 0.35;
const DOCK_INSET = 20;

/**
 * True when the panel must NOT follow: no fine pointer (a `pointermove` on
 * touch only exists during a drag, so the panel would live under the finger
 * that is dragging it), or reduced motion (a full second of drift is precisely
 * what that user opted out of). One predicate, so the two effects below can
 * never disagree about which mode the component is in.
 */
function docked(): boolean {
  return (
    !window.matchMedia('(pointer: fine)').matches ||
    window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches
  );
}

export function QuickToCursorPreview({
  items,
  duration = 1,
  panelWidth = 260,
  panelHeight = 180,
  className,
}: QuickToCursorPreviewProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const panel = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const surface = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement>(null);
  const plates = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement[]>([]);

  /* Hovered row is React state because it changes a handful of times a
     second. Panel position is never state — it changes 120 times a second and
     a re-render per pointermove would dwarf the animation itself. */
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(root);

  const count = items.length;

  /* Paint every plate once. Drawing at hover time would put a gradient fill,
     four band rects and a text layout on the same frame as the fade-in. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const bw = panelWidth * PLATE_SCALE;
    const bh = panelHeight * PLATE_SCALE;
    const built: HTMLCanvasElement[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const plate = document.createElement('canvas');
      plate.width = bw;
      plate.height = bh;
      const ctx = plate.getContext('2d');
      if (!ctx) break;
      ctx.scale(PLATE_SCALE, PLATE_SCALE);
      paintPlate(ctx, panelWidth, panelHeight, i);
      built.push(plate);
    }
    plates.current = built;

    const canvas = surface.current;
    if (canvas) {
      canvas.width = bw;
      canvas.height = bh;
    }
    return () => {
      plates.current = [];
    };
  }, [count, panelWidth, panelHeight]);

  /* Centre the panel on its own coordinates ONCE, at mount. Doing it with a
     negative margin or `left: -130px` instead means the offset and the
     transform fight, and the panel sits half a width off. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const box = panel.current;
    if (!box) return;
    gsap.set(box, { xPercent: -50, yPercent: -50, autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.94 });
    return () => {
      gsap.killTweensOf(box);
      gsap.set(box, { clearProps: 'all' });
    };
  }, []);

  /* With no fine pointer — or with reduced motion, where a second of drift is
     exactly what the user opted out of — the panel docks to the right edge and
     only cross-fades as rows change. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const box = panel.current;
    if (!box || width === 0 || height === 0) return;
    if (!docked()) return;
    gsap.set(box, {
      x: Math.max(width - panelWidth / 2 - DOCK_INSET, panelWidth / 2),
      y: height / 2,
    });
  }, [width, height, panelWidth]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = root.current;
    const box = panel.current;
    if (!el || !box || docked()) return;

    // ONE tween per property, reused for the lifetime of the component.
    const xTo = gsap.quickTo(box, 'x', { duration, ease: 'power3' });
    const yTo = gsap.quickTo(box, 'y', { duration, ease: 'power3' });
    let seeded = false;

    const onMove = (e: PointerEvent) => {
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      const x = e.clientX - rect.left;
      const y = e.clientY - rect.top;
      if (seeded) {
        xTo(x);
        yTo(y);
        return;
      }
      // Second argument is quickTo's `start` value: it snaps rather than
      // easing. Without it the panel sails in from wherever it was left,
      // taking a full second to cross the list on every re-entry.
      seeded = true;
      xTo(x, x);
      yTo(y, y);
    };

    const onLeave = () => {
      seeded = false;
    };

    el.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove, { passive: true });
    el.addEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);

    /* Deliberately NOT clearing props here. `xPercent`, `yPercent` and
       `autoAlpha` belong to the mount effect; wiping them whenever `duration`
       changes would un-centre the panel and pop it to full opacity mid-hover.
       Teardown of those lives in the effect that set them. */
    return () => {
      el.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
      el.removeEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);
      gsap.killTweensOf(box);
    };
  }, [duration]);

  /* Visibility and content follow the hovered row, not the pointer. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const box = panel.current;
    const canvas = surface.current;
    if (!box || !canvas) return;

    const reduced = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

    if (hovered !== null) {
      const plate = plates.current[hovered];
      const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
      if (plate && ctx) {
        ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
        ctx.drawImage(plate, 0, 0);
      }
    }

    gsap.to(box, {
      autoAlpha: hovered === null ? 0 : 1,
      scale: hovered === null ? 0.94 : 1,
      duration: reduced ? 0 : FADE_DURATION,
      ease: 'power3.out',
      // Only the fade is overwritten; the quickTo tweens own x and y and must
      // keep running underneath, which is exactly what 'auto' guarantees.
      overwrite: 'auto',
    });
  }, [hovered]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The follow effect removes both listeners and calls `gsap.killTweensOf(box)`, which disposes the two quickTo tweens. The mount effect separately kills tweens and runs `clearProps: "all"`, restoring the centring transform and opacity it set. The offscreen plate canvases are dropped by nulling the ref array; they are plain canvases, never object URLs, so there is nothing to revoke.

**Reduced motion.** No `pointermove` listener attaches. The panel docks to the right edge, vertically centred, and hovering a row swaps its plate with a zero-duration cross-fade. The preview still works; it simply never moves.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Calling `gsap.to()` in the `pointermove` handler. It allocates a tween per event and every new one competes with the still-running previous tween for `x`, so the panel judders under fast movement — exactly when the follow is most visible.
- Putting the panel position in React state. Every pointer event becomes a render of the whole list; the follow gets slower the more rows you add, which is a scaling failure with no obvious cause at the call site.
- Omitting the start value on the first call after entry. The panel eases in from wherever it was abandoned, so re-entering the list gives a full second of a panel flying across the layout before it means anything.
- Centring with a negative margin or `left: -130px` as well as `xPercent: -50`. The two offsets compose and the panel sits half a width away from the pointer — a bug that looks like a follow-lag problem and is not one.
- Running `clearProps: "all"` in the cleanup of an effect that only owns `x` and `y`. Any dependency change then wipes the `xPercent`/`yPercent` centring and the `autoAlpha` state owned by a different effect, and the panel jumps or flashes to full opacity mid-hover. Each effect must tear down only what it set.
- Using `overwrite: true` on the fade tween. It kills the quickTo tweens that own `x` and `y`, and the panel freezes in place the moment you move between rows. `overwrite: "auto"` only claims the properties the fade actually animates.
- Transitioning `all` on the row text. The panel and rows share a stacking context, and a blanket transition catches `transform`, which then fights whatever else is animating it.

## Notes

- Gated on `(pointer: fine)`. On touch there is no hover and a `pointermove` only exists mid-drag, so the panel would live directly under the finger dragging it. The touch path docks the panel to the right edge and cross-fades on row change instead, which keeps the preview useful without pretending there is a cursor.
- Reduced motion takes the same docked path — a second of drift is precisely what that user opted out of — and the cross-fade duration drops to 0.
- Both branches read the same `docked()` predicate, so the follow effect and the dock effect can never disagree about which mode the component is in.
- The panel is `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events-none`: it is decoration for the row title, which remains the accessible content.

## Definition of done

Hover a row and the panel fades up over ~350ms while scaling from 0.94. Move the pointer and it follows with about a second of lag, always heading toward the pointer and never quite catching it. Move fast between rows and the image cross-fades while the follow keeps running underneath — the panel never freezes. Leave and re-enter the list and the panel appears at the pointer, not sailing in from the far side. On touch or with reduced motion the panel sits docked at the right edge and only its contents change.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Radar Chart Card

A grey dashboard card that plots six months of visitors as a Recharts radar on a hexagonal polar grid, with the range total counted up in the header next to a chip comparing it with the range before, and a white tile per month underneath. A calendar pill swaps between H1 2024, H2 2024 and the full year. Hovering an axis pulses a dot on that vertex, opens a tooltip with the value and its share, and switches the header to that month. Four looks are built in: a filled polygon, a light fill with vertex dots, an outline only, and a fill with a centre score disc that turns rose when the value it shows is low.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A "Visitors" card with a lime radar on a hexagon grid; hovering an axis pulses its vertex and counts the header to that month.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: recharts@^3.10.1

## How it works

1. A `RadarChart` draws a `PolarGrid` with `gridType="polygon"` in `--color-chart-track`, a `PolarAngleAxis` keyed on the month label for the outer labels, and a hidden `PolarRadiusAxis` (no ticks, no line) with its domain set to `[0, "auto"]` so the polygon always grows from the centre.
2. Hover state comes from Recharts' own store. `RadarActiveAxis` is a child of the chart that reads `useIsTooltipActive()` and `useActiveTooltipLabel()` and passes the active label (or null) up in an effect. Reading the store, rather than the chart's `onMouseMove` payload, means the header is right on the very first pointer event over the chart and follows the chart's arrow-key focus too.
3. The hovered label is looked up in the current range by name, so after a range switch a stale label simply finds nothing and the header falls back to the total. With an axis active the header shows that axis value and hides the chip; at rest it shows the sum against `previous` through `describeDelta`.
4. The `Radar` keeps one 2px outline in the tone's `-active` colour and changes only `fillOpacity` per look: 0.6 filled, 0.2 dots, 0 lines, 0.35 score. The dots look adds 3.5px vertex dots ringed in the card colour; every look uses the shared `PulseDot` as `activeDot`, which pings unless motion is reduced.
5. The score disc is an absolutely centred HTML circle over the plot. The chart margins match on opposite sides (12px top and bottom, 40px left and right), which keeps the polar centre at the middle of the plot box, so `top-1/2 left-1/2` with a translate lands on it. It shows the axis average at rest and the hovered value on hover, and its text and border switch to the rose status colour below `lowThreshold`.
6. The tooltip uses a dashed radial cursor and renders `ChartTooltipCard` from `activeIndex` (mapped from `null` to -1 first) with the value and its share of the range total.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `outer radius = 78% of the plot half-size, 280px plot height`
  The radius is a share of the smaller plot side, so on a wide card the 280px height sets it and on a 360px screen the narrowed width does, leaving room for "February" and "September" at the side vertices.
- `fill per look = filled 0.6, dots 0.2, lines 0, score 0.35`
  The solid look matches the preview; the dots look needs a lighter fill so the dots carry the shape; the score look stays light enough for the disc to read on top.
- `chart margin = 12px top and bottom, 40px left and right`
  Matching opposite margins keep the polar centre at the middle of the box, where the score disc is positioned with plain CSS; the wider sides shrink the radius only when the card is narrow, so the side labels are never cut off.
- `low threshold = 200`
  With the default data, January (186) is the only month under it, so hovering it shows the rose disc while the 237 average stays neutral.
- `motion = polygon 500ms, tooltip 160ms, disc colour 200ms, count-up 320ms`
  Quick enough to sweep round six axes, and all of it is off under reduced motion.

## API

```ts
function RadarChartCard(props?: RadarChartCardProps): JSX.Element
type RadarChartCardProps = { title?: string; ranges?: RadarRange[]; range?: string; defaultRange?: string; onRangeChange?: (id: string) => void; variant?: "filled" | "dots" | "lines" | "score"; tone?: ChartTone; lowThreshold?: number; rangeControl?: "segmented" | "select"; hideTiles?: boolean; className?: string }
type RadarRange = { id: string; label: string; data: { label: string; value: number }[]; previous?: number }
```

- `title: string` — default `"Visitors"`
  Header label and series name.
- `ranges: RadarRange[]` — default `RADAR_RANGES`
  Data sets for the pill, one point per axis clockwise from the top; `previous` feeds the chip.
- `range: string`
  Controlled range id.
- `defaultRange: string` — default `first range id`
  Initial range when uncontrolled.
- `onRangeChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called with the chosen range id.
- `variant: "filled" | "dots" | "lines" | "score"` — default `"filled"`
  Solid polygon, light fill with vertex dots, outline only, or fill with a centre score disc.
- `tone: ChartTone` — default `2`
  Series hue; the outline, dots and active dot use its `-active` step.
- `lowThreshold: number` — default `200`
  Score look only: the disc turns rose below this value.
- `rangeControl: "segmented" | "select"` — default `"select"`
  Calendar pill with a listbox, or a segmented switch.
- `hideTiles: boolean` — default `false`
  Hide the per-axis tiles under the chart.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function RadarChartCard({
  title = "Visitors",
  ranges = RADAR_RANGES,
  range,
  defaultRange,
  onRangeChange,
  variant = "filled",
  tone = 2,
  lowThreshold = 200,
  rangeControl = "select",
  hideTiles = false,
  className,
}: RadarChartCardProps = {}) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const [innerRange, setInnerRange] = useState(defaultRange ?? ranges[0]?.id ?? "");
  const rangeId = range ?? innerRange;
  const active = ranges.find((r) => r.id === rangeId) ?? ranges[0];
  const data = active?.data ?? [];
  const [hoveredLabel, setHoveredLabel] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const total = data.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.value, 0);
  const hoveredIndex = hoveredLabel === null ? -1 : data.findIndex((p) => p.label === hoveredLabel);
  const hovered = data[hoveredIndex];

  // At rest the header is the range total against the range before; on an axis it is that axis alone.
  const headline = hovered ? hovered.value : total;
  const delta = hovered ? null : describeDelta(total, active?.previous);
  const average = data.length > 0 ? total / data.length : 0;
  const score = hovered ? hovered.value : average;
  const low = score < lowThreshold;

  const selectRange = (id: string) => {
    if (range === undefined) setInnerRange(id);
    onRangeChange?.(id);
  };

  return (
    <section aria-label={`${title} radar chart`} className={cx(CHART_CARD_FRAME, "gap-3", className)}>
      <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-3 px-2 pt-2">
        <ChartHeadline
          label={hovered ? `${title} · ${hovered.label}` : title}
          value={headline}
          delta={delta}
          swapKey={`${rangeId}-${hovered?.label ?? "total"}`}
          reducedMotion={reduced}
        />
        {ranges.length > 1 ? (
          <ChartPeriodControl
            options={ranges}
            value={rangeId}
            onChange={selectRange}
            variant={rangeControl}
            label={`${title} range`}
            className="shrink-0"
          />
        ) : null}
      </div>

      <div className="relative h-[280px] w-full">
        <ResponsiveContainer width="100%" height="100%" initialDimension={{ width: 420, height: 280 }}>
          <RadarChart data={data} margin={RADAR_MARGIN} outerRadius={RADAR_OUTER_RADIUS}>
            <RadarActiveAxis onChange={setHoveredLabel} />
            <PolarGrid gridType="polygon" stroke={GRID_STROKE} />
            <PolarRadiusAxis domain={[0, "auto"]} tick={false} axisLine={false} />
            <PolarAngleAxis dataKey="label" tick={AXIS_TICK} tickLine={false} />
            <Tooltip
              cursor={CHART_CURSOR}
              offset={16}
              isAnimationActive={!reduced}
              animationDuration={160}
              wrapperStyle={{ outline: "none", zIndex: 10 }}
              content={({ active: isActive, activeIndex }) => {
                const at = data[activeIndex == null ? -1 : Number(activeIndex)];
                if (!isActive || !at) return null;
                return (
                  <ChartTooltipCard
                    title={at.label}
                    rows={[
                      { key: "value", label: title, tone, value: formatNumber(at.value) },
                      { key: "share", label: "Share", value: `${formatNumber((at.value / (total || 1)) * 100, 1)}%` },
                    ]}
                  />
                );
              }}
            />
            <Radar
              dataKey="value"
              name={title}
              fill={toneColor(tone)}
              fillOpacity={VARIANT_FILL[variant]}
              stroke={toneActiveColor(tone)}
              strokeWidth={2}
              strokeLinejoin="round"
              dot={
                variant === "dots"
                  ? {
                      r: 3.5,
                      fill: toneActiveColor(tone),
                      fillOpacity: 1,
                      stroke: "var(--color-background-secondary-default)",
                      strokeWidth: 1.5,
                    }
                  : false
              }
              activeDot={<PulseDot color={toneActiveColor(tone)} pulse={!reduced} />}
              isAnimationActive={!reduced}
              animationDuration={500}
            />
          </RadarChart>
        </ResponsiveContainer>

        {variant === "score" ? (
          <div
            aria-hidden
            className={cx(
              "pointer-events-none absolute top-1/2 left-1/2 flex size-14 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 flex-col items-center justify-center rounded-full border-2 bg-background-primary-default transition-colors duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
              low ? "text-status-rose-text" : "text-text-primary",
            )}
            style={{ borderColor: low ? "var(--color-status-rose-text)" : toneActiveColor(tone) }}
          >
            <span className="text-body-medium tabular-nums">{formatNumber(score)}</span>
            <span className="max-w-12 truncate text-[10px] leading-3 text-text-tertiary">
              {hovered ? hovered.label : "avg"}
            </span>
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </div>

      {hideTiles ? null : (
        <ChartStatTiles
          columns={3}
          tiles={data.map((p) => ({ key: p.label, label: p.label, value: formatNumber(p.value) }))}
        />
      )}
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `RadarActiveAxis` only runs an effect that calls the setter, `useCountUp` cancels its animation frame on target change and unmount, `useReducedMotion` unsubscribes its media-query listener, `ResponsiveContainer` disconnects its resize observer, and the kit `Select` tears down its popover when closed. The card adds no listeners or timers of its own.

**Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `useReducedMotion` turns off `isAnimationActive` on the Radar and the Tooltip, the header shows its value without counting, the active dot drops its ping, and the number fade and disc colour transition are disabled with `motion-reduce:` variants.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Driving the header from the chart `onMouseMove` payload alone. In testing, a single pointer event that entered the chart opened the tooltip but left that payload inactive, so the header stayed on the total; the store hooks update on the same event.
- Using different margins on opposite sides with the centred disc. The polar centre follows the plot area, not the box, and the disc would sit off the hub.
- Reading `activeIndex` with `Number()` directly. Recharts passes `null` when inactive and `Number(null)` is 0, which would pin the tooltip to January.

## Notes

- `RADAR_RANGES`, `RADAR_MARGIN`, `RADAR_OUTER_RADIUS`, `RadarActiveAxis` and the `RadarRange`, `RadarAxisPoint` and `RadarVariant` types are exported; Radar Comparison Card reuses them. H1 2024 totals 1,424 against 1,354 ("+5.2%"), H2 2024 1,598 ("+12.2%") and 2024 3,022 against 2,780 ("+8.7%").
- The full-year range uses two-month buckets so every range keeps six axes and six tiles.
- The frame, header, range pill, tooltip card, tiles and pulse dot come from `line-chart-card-parts.tsx`.

## Definition of done

The card shows "Visitors", "1,424" with a lime "+5.2%" chip, an "H1 2024" pill, a lime filled hexagon radar labelled January to June on a grey polygon grid, and six tiles January 186, February 305, March 237, April 273, May 209 and June 214.
