# Build: Radar Comparison Card

A grey "Visitors" dashboard card that overlays two outline-only Recharts radars, Desktop in lime and Mobile in blue, on one hexagonal grid. The header counts up the lead series total with a chip against the range before, a calendar pill swaps between H1 2024, H2 2024 and the full year, and a tile per axis sits underneath. The legend under the chart is live: it shows each series total at rest and its value on the hovered axis, and every entry is a toggle button that hides or shows its outline, with the last visible series locked on.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Desktop and Mobile as lime and blue radar outlines on one grid, with a live legend whose entries toggle each series on and off.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: recharts@^3.10.1

## How it works

1. Each series is a `Radar` with `fillOpacity={0}` and a 2px outline in its tone's `-active` colour, so overlapping shapes stay readable. The range data is stored as `{ label, values: { desktop, mobile } }` and spread into flat chart rows, one `dataKey` per series key.
2. Hiding a series sets the Radar `hide` prop instead of unmounting it. The hidden `PolarRadiusAxis` gets a fixed domain of `[0, max]`, where `max` is taken over every series in the range, so turning one outline off never rescales the other.
3. The legend is a list of native buttons with `aria-pressed`. A click builds the next key list in series order and, when `visible` is uncontrolled, stores it; `onVisibleChange` gets it either way. If the clicked series is the only one shown, the click is ignored and the button carries `aria-disabled` and a title saying why.
4. Hover state comes from Recharts' store through `RadarActiveAxis` from Radar Chart Card, so it is right on the first pointer event and follows the chart's arrow-key focus. With an axis active, the header shows the lead series value for it and hides the chip, and every legend entry swaps its total for its value on that axis.
5. The lead series is the first visible one. The header total, the chip (`describeDelta` against `previous[lead]`) and the tiles all follow it, and the tiles carry its colour square so it is clear which series they show.
6. The tooltip lists only visible series, each with its colour dot, and every Radar uses the shared `PulseDot` as `activeDot`, so each visible outline pulses on the hovered axis.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `radius domain = [0, largest value of any series in the range]`
  A shared, fixed scale keeps side-by-side reads honest and stops the remaining outline jumping when one is hidden.
- `outline = 2px stroke, fill opacity 0`
  Outline-only shapes let the smaller series show through the larger one, as in the preview.
- `hidden legend entry = 50% opacity, hollow square`
  Shows the series is off while keeping its value readable and the button easy to find again.
- `plot size = 260px high, 78% outer radius, margins 12px top and bottom and 40px left and right`
  The same geometry as Radar Chart Card, a little shorter to make room for the legend row.
- `motion = outlines 500ms, tooltip 160ms, legend fade 150ms, count-up 320ms`
  Quick enough to sweep round six axes, and all of it is off under reduced motion.

## API

```ts
function RadarComparisonCard(props?: RadarComparisonCardProps): JSX.Element
type RadarComparisonCardProps = { title?: string; series?: RadarSeries[]; ranges?: RadarComparisonRange[]; range?: string; defaultRange?: string; onRangeChange?: (id: string) => void; visible?: string[]; defaultVisible?: string[]; onVisibleChange?: (keys: string[]) => void; rangeControl?: "segmented" | "select"; hideTiles?: boolean; className?: string }
type RadarSeries = { key: string; label: string; tone: ChartTone }
type RadarComparisonRange = { id: string; label: string; data: { label: string; values: Record<string, number> }[]; previous?: Record<string, number> }
```

- `title: string` — default `"Visitors"`
  Header label.
- `series: RadarSeries[]` — default `RADAR_COMPARISON_SERIES`
  Series keys, legend labels and tones; the first visible one leads the header and tiles.
- `ranges: RadarComparisonRange[]` — default `RADAR_COMPARISON_RANGES`
  Data sets for the pill, one point per axis with a value per series key; `previous` feeds the chip.
- `range: string`
  Controlled range id.
- `defaultRange: string` — default `first range id`
  Initial range when uncontrolled.
- `onRangeChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called with the chosen range id.
- `visible: string[]`
  Controlled list of visible series keys.
- `defaultVisible: string[]` — default `every series`
  Initial visible keys when uncontrolled.
- `onVisibleChange: (keys: string[]) => void`
  Called with the next visible keys after a legend click.
- `rangeControl: "segmented" | "select"` — default `"select"`
  Calendar pill with a listbox, or a segmented switch.
- `hideTiles: boolean` — default `false`
  Hide the per-axis tiles under the chart.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function RadarComparisonCard({
  title = "Visitors",
  series = RADAR_COMPARISON_SERIES,
  ranges = RADAR_COMPARISON_RANGES,
  range,
  defaultRange,
  onRangeChange,
  visible,
  defaultVisible,
  onVisibleChange,
  rangeControl = "select",
  hideTiles = false,
  className,
}: RadarComparisonCardProps = {}) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const [innerRange, setInnerRange] = useState(defaultRange ?? ranges[0]?.id ?? "");
  const [innerVisible, setInnerVisible] = useState<string[]>(defaultVisible ?? series.map((s) => s.key));
  const [hoveredLabel, setHoveredLabel] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const rangeId = range ?? innerRange;
  const active = ranges.find((r) => r.id === rangeId) ?? ranges[0];
  const data = active?.data ?? [];
  const rows = data.map((p) => ({ label: p.label, ...p.values }));

  // Never render an empty chart: if nothing valid is visible, the first series stays on.
  const visibleKeys = visible ?? innerVisible;
  const picked = series.filter((s) => visibleKeys.includes(s.key));
  const shown = picked.length > 0 ? picked : series.slice(0, 1);
  const isShown = (key: string) => shown.some((s) => s.key === key);
  const lead = shown[0];

  const valueOf = (p: RadarComparisonPoint | undefined, key: string) => p?.values[key] ?? 0;
  const totalOf = (key: string) => data.reduce((sum, p) => sum + valueOf(p, key), 0);
  // One radius scale for every series, so hiding one never rescales the other.
  const max = Math.max(0, ...data.flatMap((p) => series.map((s) => valueOf(p, s.key))));

  const hovered = hoveredLabel === null ? undefined : data.find((p) => p.label === hoveredLabel);
  const leadKey = lead?.key ?? "";
  const leadTotal = totalOf(leadKey);
  const leadPrevious = active?.previous?.[leadKey];
  const headline = hovered ? valueOf(hovered, leadKey) : leadTotal;
  const delta = hovered || leadPrevious === undefined ? null : describeDelta(leadTotal, leadPrevious);

  const selectRange = (id: string) => {
    if (range === undefined) setInnerRange(id);
    onRangeChange?.(id);
  };

  const toggle = (key: string) => {
    const on = isShown(key);
    if (on && shown.length <= 1) return;
    const next = series.filter((s) => (s.key === key ? !on : isShown(s.key))).map((s) => s.key);
    if (visible === undefined) setInnerVisible(next);
    onVisibleChange?.(next);
  };

  return (
    <section aria-label={`${title} radar comparison`} className={cx(CHART_CARD_FRAME, "gap-3", className)}>
      <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-3 px-2 pt-2">
        <ChartHeadline
          label={hovered ? `${title} · ${hovered.label}` : title}
          value={headline}
          delta={delta}
          swapKey={`${rangeId}-${leadKey}-${hovered?.label ?? "total"}`}
          reducedMotion={reduced}
        />
        {ranges.length > 1 ? (
          <ChartPeriodControl
            options={ranges}
            value={rangeId}
            onChange={selectRange}
            variant={rangeControl}
            label={`${title} range`}
            className="shrink-0"
          />
        ) : null}
      </div>

      <div className="h-[260px] w-full">
        <ResponsiveContainer width="100%" height="100%" initialDimension={{ width: 420, height: 260 }}>
          <RadarChart data={rows} margin={RADAR_MARGIN} outerRadius={RADAR_OUTER_RADIUS}>
            <RadarActiveAxis onChange={setHoveredLabel} />
            <PolarGrid gridType="polygon" stroke={GRID_STROKE} />
            <PolarRadiusAxis domain={[0, max || 1]} tick={false} axisLine={false} />
            <PolarAngleAxis dataKey="label" tick={AXIS_TICK} tickLine={false} />
            <Tooltip
              cursor={CHART_CURSOR}
              offset={16}
              isAnimationActive={!reduced}
              animationDuration={160}
              wrapperStyle={{ outline: "none", zIndex: 10 }}
              content={({ active: isActive, activeIndex }) => {
                const at = data[activeIndex == null ? -1 : Number(activeIndex)];
                if (!isActive || !at) return null;
                return (
                  <ChartTooltipCard
                    title={at.label}
                    rows={shown.map((s) => ({ key: s.key, label: s.label, tone: s.tone, value: formatNumber(valueOf(at, s.key)) }))}
                  />
                );
              }}
            />
            {series.map((s) => (
              <Radar
                key={s.key}
                dataKey={s.key}
                name={s.label}
                hide={!isShown(s.key)}
                fillOpacity={0}
                stroke={toneActiveColor(s.tone)}
                strokeWidth={2}
                strokeLinejoin="round"
                dot={false}
                activeDot={<PulseDot color={toneActiveColor(s.tone)} pulse={!reduced} />}
                isAnimationActive={!reduced}
                animationDuration={500}
              />
            ))}
          </RadarChart>
        </ResponsiveContainer>
      </div>

      <ul aria-label={`${title} series`} className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1 px-2">
        {series.map((s) => {
          const on = isShown(s.key);
          const locked = on && shown.length <= 1;
          return (
            <li key={s.key}>
              <button
                type="button"
                aria-pressed={on}
                aria-disabled={locked || undefined}
                title={locked ? "At least one series stays visible" : undefined}
                onClick={() => toggle(s.key)}
                className={cx(
                  "flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md px-1.5 py-0.5 text-body-2-regular text-text-secondary outline-none transition-opacity duration-150 ease-out focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring motion-reduce:transition-none",
                  on ? "opacity-100" : "opacity-50",
                  locked ? "cursor-default" : "cursor-pointer hover:bg-background-primary-hover",
                )}
              >
                <span
                  aria-hidden
                  className={cx("size-2.5 shrink-0 rounded-[3px]", on ? TONE_DOT[s.tone] : "ring-1 ring-current ring-inset")}
                />
                {s.label}
                <span className="text-body-2-medium text-text-primary tabular-nums">
                  {formatNumber(hovered ? valueOf(hovered, s.key) : totalOf(s.key))}
                </span>
              </button>
            </li>
          );
        })}
      </ul>

      {hideTiles ? null : (
        <ChartStatTiles
          columns={3}
          tiles={data.map((p) => ({ key: p.label, label: p.label, value: formatNumber(valueOf(p, leadKey)), tone: lead?.tone }))}
        />
      )}
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `RadarActiveAxis` only runs an effect that calls the setter, `useCountUp` cancels its animation frame on target change and unmount, `useReducedMotion` unsubscribes its media-query listener, `ResponsiveContainer` disconnects its resize observer, and the kit `Select` tears down its popover when closed. The card adds no listeners or timers of its own.

**Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `useReducedMotion` turns off `isAnimationActive` on every Radar and the Tooltip, the header shows its value without counting, the active dots drop their ping, and the legend fade is disabled with a `motion-reduce:` variant.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Leaving the radius domain on "auto". Recharts then scales to the visible data only, so hiding Desktop makes Mobile balloon to fill the grid and the comparison is lost.
- Unmounting a hidden Radar instead of using `hide`. The series order, colours and the tooltip rows then shift as series come and go.
- Letting every series be turned off. An empty grid has no lead series for the header or tiles, so the last visible entry is locked.
- Reading `activeIndex` with `Number()` directly. Recharts passes `null` when inactive and `Number(null)` is 0, which would pin the tooltip to January.

## Notes

- H1 2024 is Desktop 1,424 against 1,354 ("+5.2%") and Mobile 860 against 800 ("+7.5%"); H2 2024 is 1,598 ("+12.2%") and 1,100 ("+27.9%"); 2024 is 3,022 ("+8.7%") and 1,960 ("+15.3%") in two-month buckets.
- Imports `RADAR_MARGIN`, `RADAR_OUTER_RADIUS` and `RadarActiveAxis` from `radar-chart-card.tsx`, and the frame, header, range pill, tooltip card, tiles and pulse dot from `line-chart-card-parts.tsx`.
- With Desktop hidden, Mobile becomes the lead series: the header shows "860" with "+7.5%" and the tiles show the Mobile values.

The card shows "Visitors", "1,424" with a lime "+5.2%" chip and an "H1 2024" pill, a lime and a blue radar outline on a grey hexagon grid labelled January to June, a legend reading "Desktop 1,424" and "Mobile 860", and six tiles January 186 to June 214. Hovering an axis pulses both vertices, opens a tooltip with both values and switches the header and legend to that month. Clicking "Desktop" hides the lime outline, and the header reads "860" with "+7.5%"; clicking "Mobile" then does nothing. Picking "H2 2024" shows "1,598" and "+12.2%".

# Build: Radial Chart Card

A dashboard card that draws one rounded arc per item over its own track ring, smallest item innermost, every arc starting at twelve o'clock and running clockwise. The arcs sweep in on mount and to their new lengths on every period or look change. Hovering, focusing or tapping a ring darkens it one tone, fades the others, floats a tooltip on the arc's tip and swaps the count-up headline to that item. Four looks come from one prop: plain rings, names set along each arc, rings over a circular grid, and a single gauge of the total against a goal with the percentage in the centre.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Concentric radial bars in the dashboard card shell, with a tooltip on the arc tip, a count-up headline that follows hover, and stat tiles.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The chart is an inline SVG drawn 1:1 in a 216px square. `layoutRings` puts the outermost ring flush with the edge (radius 108 − 2 − stroke/2) and steps inwards by the pitch (stroke + gap, 8 + 4 for rings). If the rings would come closer than 26px to the centre, the pitch shrinks to fit.
2. Each arc is a `<circle>` rotated −90° about the centre, with `pathLength=100` and `strokeLinecap="round"`. Its dash is just `fraction × 100`, so no arc maths is needed. The fraction is `value / max`, where max defaults to the largest item ÷ 0.9, so the biggest ring sweeps 324°.
3. The fractions go through `useTweenedValues`: a 520ms ease-out cubic tween that starts from 0 on mount and from the current sweeps on a new period or look. So the arcs grow, shrink and re-proportion in one motion.
4. Each ring is a `<g role="button" tabIndex=0>` holding the track, the arc, an optional name and a transparent hit circle as wide as the pitch, so the gaps between rings still hover. Pointer enter and focus set the active ring, click or Enter/Space toggle a pin (`aria-pressed`), and leaving the square clears the hover.
5. The active arc switches to the darker `--color-chart-N-active` tone. The other arcs fade to 0.3 opacity over 200ms, and so do the stat tiles (to 0.45). A keyboard focus also draws a focus-ring halo under that ring.
6. The tooltip is a plain absolutely positioned div. It sits on the arc's tip, at `(C + r·cos θ, C + r·sin θ)` with θ = fraction × 2π − π/2. Its x is clamped 52px inside the square so it never clips, and it is lifted 10px above the tip.
7. The `labels` look writes each name in 8px white type on a `<textPath>` that follows a closed circle path starting at twelve o'clock. A name only shows once its arc is longer than the text (about 4.9px per character plus 10px of padding and the stroke), so short arcs never spill their label.
8. `gauge` folds the items into one ring of their total against the range's `goal` (or `max`), with the percentage and a caption in the centre. Its tiles show the total, the goal and what is still to go.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `SIZE = 216px square, drawn 1:1`
  Matches the preview's ring diameter, and keeps tooltip positions in plain CSS px with no viewBox scaling.
- `LOOKS = rings 8/4, labels 12/2, grid 8/4 without track, gauge 16 (stroke/gap px)`
  Five rings fit with a 50px hole on the plain look. The labelled look needs a 12px band for 8px type.
- `HEADROOM = 0.9`
  The largest item sweeps 324° instead of a closed circle, so every ring still shows where it ends.
- `MIN_HOLE = 26px`
  With many items the pitch shrinks so the innermost ring never collapses into the centre.
- `TIP_INSET = 52px`
  Keeps the roughly 110px-wide tooltip inside the chart square at the ring's far left or right.
- `tween = 520ms ease-out cubic (useTweenedValues)`
  Sweeps are tweened as fractions, so a period or look change starts from wherever the arcs are.

## API

```ts
function RadialChartCard(props: { title?: string; variant?: "rings" | "labels" | "grid" | "gauge"; ranges?: RadialRange[]; items?: RadialItem[]; delta?: number; max?: number; range?: string; defaultRange?: string; onRangeChange?: (id: string) => void; tiles?: boolean; showCenter?: boolean; gaugeCaption?: string; formatValue?: (value: number) => string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type RadialItem = { label: string; value: number; color?: ChartColor }
type RadialRange = { id: string; label: string; items: RadialItem[]; delta?: number; goal?: number }
```

- `title: string` — default `"Visitors"`
  Header label while nothing is active. Also the gauge's item name and the card's accessible name.
- `variant: "rings" | "labels" | "grid" | "gauge"` — default `"rings"`
  Plain rings, names along each arc, rings over a circular grid, or one total against a goal.
- `ranges: RadialRange[]` — default `RADIAL_RANGES`
  Periods with their own items, delta and goal. Two or more show the period select.
- `items: RadialItem[]`
  A single item list, innermost first. Overrides `ranges` and hides the select.
- `delta: number`
  Headline chip percentage when `items` is used.
- `max: number` — default `largest ÷ 0.9 (rings), range goal (gauge)`
  The value of a full circle.
- `range: string`
  Controlled period id.
- `defaultRange: string` — default `first range id`
  Initial period when uncontrolled.
- `onRangeChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called when the period select changes.
- `tiles: boolean` — default `true`
  Stat tiles under the chart, three per row; hovering one focuses its ring.
- `showCenter: boolean` — default `false`
  Shows the active value (or the total) in the hole of the ring looks.
- `gaugeCaption: string` — default `"of goal"`
  Caption under the gauge's centre percentage.
- `formatValue: (value: number) => string` — default `en-US integer`
  Formats the headline, tooltip, tiles and the accessible labels.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * One ring: track, arc, optional name on a text path, and a transparent hit
 * stroke as wide as the ring pitch so the gaps between rings still hover.
 * The arc is a circle rotated to twelve o'clock with `pathLength=100`, so its
 * dash is simply the tweened fraction × 100 and round caps close it off.
 */
function RingView({
  item,
  index,
  ring,
  fraction,
  color,
  variant,
  active,
  pinned,
  focusVisible,
  label,
  pathId,
  onTarget,
  onFocusVisible,
  onTogglePin,
}: RingViewProps) {
  const tone = CHART_COLORS[color];
  const isActive = active === index;
  const dimmed = active !== null && !isActive;
  const look = LOOKS[variant];
  const dash = clamp01(fraction) * 100;
  const arcLength = clamp01(fraction) * 2 * Math.PI * ring.r;
  const showName =
    variant === "labels" && arcLength >= item.label.length * LABEL_CHAR + LABEL_OFFSET * 2 + ring.stroke;

  const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent<SVGGElement>) => {
    if (event.key !== "Enter" && event.key !== " ") return;
    event.preventDefault();
    onTogglePin();
  };

  return (
    <g
      role="button"
      tabIndex={0}
      aria-label={label}
      aria-pressed={pinned}
      data-ring={item.label}
      className="cursor-pointer outline-none"
      onPointerEnter={() => onTarget(index)}
      onFocus={(event) => {
        onTarget(index);
        onFocusVisible(event.currentTarget.matches(":focus-visible") ? index : null);
      }}
      onBlur={() => {
        onTarget(null);
        onFocusVisible(null);
      }}
      onClick={onTogglePin}
      onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
    >
      {focusVisible ? (
        <circle
          cx={C}
          cy={C}
          r={ring.r}
          fill="none"
          stroke="var(--color-border-focus-ring)"
          strokeWidth={ring.stroke + Math.min(4, ring.pitch - ring.stroke + 2)}
        />
      ) : null}
      {look.track ? (
        <circle cx={C} cy={C} r={ring.r} fill="none" stroke="var(--color-chart-track)" strokeWidth={ring.stroke} />
      ) : null}
      {dash > 0 ? (
        <circle
          cx={C}
          cy={C}
          r={ring.r}
          fill="none"
          stroke={isActive ? tone.active : tone.fill}
          strokeWidth={ring.stroke}
          strokeLinecap="round"
          pathLength={100}
          strokeDasharray={`${dash} 100`}
          transform={`rotate(-90 ${C} ${C})`}
          opacity={dimmed ? 0.3 : 1}
          className="transition-[stroke,opacity] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none"
        />
      ) : null}
      {variant === "labels" ? (
        <>
          <path id={pathId} d={circlePath(ring.r)} fill="none" stroke="none" />
          <text
            aria-hidden
            fontSize={LABEL_FONT}
            fontWeight={600}
            fill="#fff"
            dominantBaseline="central"
            opacity={showName ? (dimmed ? 0.5 : 1) : 0}
            className="pointer-events-none select-none transition-opacity duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none"
          >
            <textPath href={`#${pathId}`} startOffset={LABEL_OFFSET}>
              {item.label}
            </textPath>
          </text>
        </>
      ) : null}
      <circle
        cx={C}
        cy={C}
        r={ring.r}
        fill="none"
        stroke="transparent"
        strokeWidth={ring.pitch}
        pointerEvents="stroke"
      />
    </g>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The sweep tween and the headline's `useCountUp` cancel their animation frame on every new target and on unmount. Hover, focus and pin are plain React state on SVG elements, with no document listeners.

**Reduced motion.** `useTweenedValues` is disabled, so the arcs render at their final sweeps and jump on a change. The stroke/opacity fades on arcs and names use `motion-reduce:transition-none`. The headline count runs over 1ms, and the number fade is off.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Drawing arcs with SVG `A` commands. A full or near-full sweep then needs special cases, because start and end coincide. A rotated circle with `pathLength=100` and a dash covers 0–100% with one formula.
- Hit-testing only the visible stroke. The 4px gaps between rings then flicker the hover off as the pointer crosses them. A transparent stroke as wide as the pitch makes the whole band one target.
- Showing ring names regardless of arc length. The name of a short arc then runs on past its end over the bare track. Hide it until the arc is longer than the text.

## Notes

- `RADIAL_RANGES`, `RadialItem`, `RadialRange` and `RadialVariant` are exported. Pass `items` (and `delta`) for one static list without the period select.
- `showCenter` writes the active item's value (or the total) in the hole of the ring looks.
- The frame, header, period select and stat tiles come from `funnel-chart-card-shell`.

## Definition of done

# Build: Radial Mask Spotlight

A stacked layer is masked by a radial gradient whose centre follows the pointer, so content is lit rather than uncovered. The mask string is rewritten once per animation frame from a damped pointer position, and both the prefixed and unprefixed `mask-image` properties are set.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A layer masked to a soft disc follows the pointer, with a flat core that makes it read as a beam.

- Category: cursor
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The gradient stops are the design: solid black to 30% of the radius, then a ramp to transparent at 72%. That flat core gives the beam a lit region with an actual size. A gradient that begins falling off at 0% has no lit area at all — just a bright point that fades, which the eye reads as blur rather than as light.
2. A px radius is used rather than a percentage. A percentage radius in a radial gradient resolves against the element box, so the same declaration produces a beam of a different physical size in every panel it is dropped into, and the effect stops being reusable.
3. Position comes from `useSmoothPointer` with a very low smoothing factor, so the beam has a small amount of drag. `damp` is frame-rate independent — the smoothing constant is the fraction of the gap left after one full second — so the same value produces the same feel at 60Hz and 144Hz rather than the beam arriving twice as fast on a fast display.
4. The mask is written in a `useRaf` callback, not in the pointer handler. Setting `mask-image` invalidates paint for the layer, and a fast pointer delivers two or three events per frame, so a per-event write does the same expensive work several times to produce one visible result.
5. The layer is seeded with a mask parked two radii off-panel, so the first painted frame — before rAF has run once — cannot show the layer unmasked. Nothing is written until `pointer.active` is true, which is what stops the beam flashing at the hook's centre-parked seed position on mount.
6. Both `maskImage` and `WebkitMaskImage` are set. This is not defensive habit: released Safari versions mishandle gradient masks without the prefix, and the failure mode is the layer being fully visible or fully invisible rather than slightly wrong.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `radius = 220`
  Beam radius in px, giving a 132px solid core and a 92px falloff. Below ~120 the core is too small to hold a line of text and the effect becomes a magnifier; above ~350 in a small panel the falloff never completes inside the box and the beam reads as an uneven wash.
- `CORE_STOP = 0.3`
  Where the solid region ends. This is the single number that separates "a light" from "a smudge". At 0 there is no lit area, only a peak; past ~0.5 the edge becomes hard enough that it reads as a cut-out hole instead of illumination.
- `EDGE_STOP = 0.72`
  Where the falloff reaches zero. Short of 100% so the gradient completes inside its own radius and the beam never shows a visible circular boundary at the edge of the declared circle.
- `smoothing = 0.0006`
  Fraction of the remaining distance still uncovered after one second — so the beam is effectively caught up within about 100ms. Enough drag to give the light some weight, not enough for the beam to visibly trail behind the thing you are pointing at, which would make it useless for reading.
- `FADE_MS = 260`
  Enter and leave fade on the whole layer. Long enough that the beam does not blink on and off as the pointer crosses the edge, short enough that leaving does not leave a light hanging in an unhovered panel.
- `rest mask offset = -radius * 2`
  Where the seeded mask sits before the first frame. Two radii guarantees no part of the falloff is inside the box at any panel size, so nothing is lit before the pointer has been seen.

## API

```ts
function RadialMaskSpotlight(props: { children: ReactNode; radius?: number; smoothing?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Content of the lit layer. Should have a transparent background.
- `radius: number` — default `220`
  Beam radius in CSS px. Core is 30% of this, falloff completes at 72%.
- `smoothing: number` — default `0.0006`
  Fraction of the gap remaining after one second. Lower is tighter.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root container via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Where the solid core ends, as a fraction of `radius`. */
const CORE_STOP = 0.3;
/** Where the falloff reaches full transparency, as a fraction of `radius`. */
const EDGE_STOP = 0.72;
const FADE_MS = 260;

export function RadialMaskSpotlight({
  children,
  radius = 220,
  smoothing = 0.0006,
  className,
}: RadialMaskSpotlightProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const lit = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const enabled = useRef(false);
  const visible = useRef(false);

  const pointer = useSmoothPointer({
    target: root,
    smoothing,
    // Touch is explicitly off: this component is fine-pointer only, and
    // letting touch drags drive the mask would move the beam under the finger.
    touch: false,
  });

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = root.current;
    const layer = lit.current;
    if (!el || !layer) return;

    const fine = window.matchMedia('(pointer: fine)').matches;
    const reduced = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

    if (!fine) {
      /* No pointer to track. Rather than leaving a masked layer invisible, the
         mask is removed entirely so the lit layer simply shows in full — the
         content stays readable and nothing is hidden behind an effect that
         cannot be operated. */
      layer.style.maskImage = '';
      layer.style.webkitMaskImage = '';
      layer.style.opacity = '1';
      return;
    }

    enabled.current = !reduced;

    if (reduced) {
      /* Reduced motion keeps the spotlight — it is a hover affordance, not
         gratuitous movement — but pins it. A beam that chases the pointer with
         inertia is the part that was objected to, so the mask is written once,
         parked, and never updated again. */
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      writeMask(layer, rect.width * 0.5, rect.height * 0.45, radius);
      layer.style.opacity = '1';
      return;
    }

    const onEnter = () => {
      visible.current = true;
      layer.style.opacity = '1';
    };
    const onLeave = () => {
      visible.current = false;
      layer.style.opacity = '0';
    };

    el.addEventListener('pointerenter', onEnter);
    el.addEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);

    return () => {
      el.removeEventListener('pointerenter', onEnter);
      el.removeEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);
      enabled.current = false;
      layer.style.maskImage = '';
      layer.style.webkitMaskImage = '';
      layer.style.opacity = '';
    };
  }, [radius]);

  useRaf(() => {
    const layer = lit.current;
    if (!layer || !enabled.current) return;
    const p = pointer.current;
    // `active` is false until a real pointer has been seen. Writing before
    // that would place the beam at the hook's centre-parked seed value, which
    // flashes a spotlight the user never asked for.
    if (!p.active) return;
    writeMask(layer, p.x, p.y, radius);
  });

  return (
    <div ref={root} className={cn('relative isolate overflow-hidden', className)}>
      <div
        ref={lit}
        className="absolute inset-0"
        style={{
          opacity: 0,
          transition: `opacity ${FADE_MS}ms ease-out`,
          // Seeded off-panel so the very first painted frame cannot show an
          // unmasked layer before rAF runs.
          maskImage: restMask(radius),
          WebkitMaskImage: restMask(radius),
        }}
      >
        {children}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

function maskFor(x: number, y: number, radius: number): string {
  /* `circle <radius>px at <x>px <y>px` — an explicit px radius rather than a
     percentage, because a percentage radius in a radial gradient resolves
     against the box and would make the beam a different physical size on
     every panel it is dropped into. */
  return `radial-gradient(circle ${radius}px at ${x}px ${y}px, #000 0%, #000 ${
    CORE_STOP * 100
  }%, transparent ${EDGE_STOP * 100}%)`;
}

function restMask(radius: number): string {
  return maskFor(-radius * 2, -radius * 2, radius);
}

function writeMask(layer: HTMLElement, x: number, y: number, radius: number) {
  const value = maskFor(x, y, radius);
  /* Both spellings. Safari has shipped unprefixed `mask-image` for years but
     still mishandles gradient masks without `-webkit-` in enough released
     versions that dropping the prefix means the layer is either fully visible
     or fully gone on those browsers — a total failure, not a degraded one. */
  layer.style.maskImage = value;
  layer.style.webkitMaskImage = value;
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes the enter and leave listeners, flips the enabled flag so any in-flight frame is a no-op, and clears the inline `maskImage`, `WebkitMaskImage` and `opacity`. `useRaf` and `useSmoothPointer` unsubscribe themselves. Nothing was allocated beyond the two strings written per frame.

**Reduced motion.** The spotlight is still drawn — it is a hover affordance and removing it would hide content — but it never moves. The mask is written once at 50% across and 45% down, the rAF loop is left disabled, and no pointer listeners attach.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- A linear falloff from 0%. Without a flat core there is no lit region, just a bright centre that fades continuously, and the result reads as a blurred blob rather than a light. This is the most common way this effect is built and the most common reason it looks cheap.
- Setting only `maskImage`. Released Safari versions mishandle gradient masks without `-webkit-mask-image`, and the failure is total — the layer is either always visible or never visible — so it does not look like a mask bug when reported.
- Writing the mask in the `pointermove` handler. Every write invalidates paint for the layer, and a fast pointer produces several events per frame, so the same paint is thrown away two or three times before anything reaches the screen.
- A percentage radius. `circle 30% at ...` resolves against the element box, so the beam is a different size in every container and the constant that looked right in the design mock is wrong everywhere else.
- Writing the mask before the pointer has actually been seen. `useSmoothPointer` parks at the element centre so the first movement eases out sensibly, but that seed is not a real position — treating it as one flashes a spotlight in the middle of the panel on mount.
- Masking a layer containing interactive elements. `mask-image` does not clip hit testing, so links in the dark region are still clickable while being invisible. Either keep the masked layer non-interactive or accept that the mask is purely decorative.
- Putting the effect on a layer with its own background. The mask reveals the layer, and a masked opaque background is a visible disc of colour, not a light. The lit layer needs a transparent background so the beam shows content, not a shape.

## Notes

- Gated on `(pointer: fine)`. On touch the mask is removed entirely and the lit layer shows in full rather than staying hidden — an effect that cannot be operated must not be allowed to hide content. `useSmoothPointer` is also configured with `touch: false` so a scroll drag can never move the beam.
- Reduced motion keeps the spotlight but pins it: the mask is written once, centred slightly above middle, and never updated. The affordance survives; the chasing does not.
- Scoped to its own container and measured against its rect, so several instances can appear on one page without interfering.
- The masked layer is decorative by construction. If it holds links, remember that a mask hides paint but not hit testing.

## Definition of done

Move across the panel and a soft round beam follows the pointer with a slight drag, lighting the content under it. The centre of the beam is evenly lit rather than brightest at one point — cover the middle third with a finger and the light should look flat, not peaked. Enter and leave and the whole layer fades over about a quarter of a second rather than blinking. On first load, before you move, nothing is lit. Check in Safari that the beam appears at all. On touch the layer is fully visible with no mask.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Radial Ripple Dot Cloud

Several thousand dots in one draw call, with a wave travelling outward from a point left of centre. The displacement is a sine in radius minus a phase in time, attenuated exponentially, so the field is violent near the source and nearly still at the rim — which is what gives the motion an origin rather than making it a screensaver. Dot density along the radius is a hand-placed cubic B-spline, so the rings and gaps in the layout are drawn rather than derived from a formula.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A dot field with a travelling wave running out of one off-centre point, its density drawn by hand as a B-spline.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1

## How it works

1. Rest positions are baked once, in field units, into an `aOrigin` attribute: the field spans ±16/9 horizontally and ±1 vertically. The draw-time uniform `uCover = max(1, aspect / (16/9))` scales that field to cover the camera, so a resize writes one float instead of rebuilding a buffer.
2. Density along the radius comes from a uniform cubic B-spline over eight hand-placed control points — five spans — evaluated in JS at bake time. `bsplineWeights(t)` returns the four basis values `[(1-t)³, 4-6t²+3t³, 1+3t+3t²-3t³, t³] / 6` and `sampleRamp` blends control points `i..i+3`. The curve is C2 and does not pass through its control points, which is what lets a hand-placed sequence stay smooth.
3. Positions are chosen by rejection sampling: a seeded candidate uniform over the field rectangle is kept with probability `ramp(dist / maxRadius)`, where `maxRadius` is the distance from the ripple source to the farthest field corner. That is the only way to realise an arbitrary drawn radial density from a uniform PRNG without inverting the curve analytically.
4. The same ramp value is baked into `aScale` (0.55 + 0.75d) and `aAlpha` (0.3 + 0.7d), so a sparse band is also a dim band. Two independent curves would let them disagree and the field would read as noise with holes in it.
5. The vertex shader computes `dist = length(origin - uCenter)`, `wave = sin(dist * uFrequency - uElapsed * uSpeed)` — a travelling wave, because the time term is subtracted from the radius term — and `attenuated = wave * exp(-dist * uDecay)`, then displaces each dot along its own outward direction by `attenuated * uAmplitude`.
6. The direction is guarded: `dir = dist > 1e-5 ? delta / dist : vec2(0.0)`, because normalising a zero vector at the exact source yields NaN and one NaN vertex takes the whole point with it.
7. `gl_PointSize` is floored at 2 device pixels and the alpha is divided by the area that flooring invented, so the cloud has the same density on a 1x monitor as on a 3x phone. The fragment shader cuts a disc with `1 - smoothstep(0.42, 0.5, d)` and tints toward `uCrestColor` by the signed wave, so only the outgoing crest lights up.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `FIELD_HALF_W = 16 / 9`
  Half-width of the baked field, with the field 2 units tall. Baking at one fixed aspect is what makes a resize a single uniform write; 16:9 is the aspect most containers are near, so `uCover` is usually 1 and nothing is scaled at all.
- `DENSITY_RAMP = [1, 1, 0.34, 0.28, 0.92, 0.5, 0, -0.15]`
  Eight control points, so five spans. Sampled it reads 0.89 / 0.44 / 0.40 / 0.74 / 0.49 / 0.06 — dense core, gap, secondary band at ~60% radius, empty rim. The last point is negative deliberately: a control point is not a value, and pulling it below zero is what makes the tail actually reach zero instead of settling around 0.15.
- `centerX = 0.4`
  Ripple source at 40% of the width rather than 50%. A centred radial wave is bilaterally symmetric and the eye reads symmetry as a screensaver; a source off the axis reads as an impact somewhere in the scene.
- `frequency = 6.5 rad per field unit`
  Wavelength 2π/6.5 ≈ 0.97 units, about half the field height, so roughly two and a half crests fit between the source and the far corner. Past ~12 the rings alias against the dot spacing and the field boils; below ~3 there is only one crest and no ripple to read.
- `speed = 2.4 rad per second`
  Crest speed is speed / frequency = 0.37 field units per second, so a crest crosses the field in about six seconds. Fast enough to be motion, slow enough that the eye can follow a single ring outward.
- `decay = 0.85 per field unit`
  Amplitude is 43% at one unit from the source and 13% at the far corner, which gives the wave a source without a visible boundary. A linear falloff reaches exactly zero at a fixed radius and draws a hard circle there.
- `amplitude = 0.045 field units`
  2.25% of the field height — around 25px on a 1100px-tall field, in the same range as the 18px the technique was observed at. Past ~0.12 dots cross each other and the cloud shears instead of rippling.
- `size = 2.6 CSS pixels`
  Base diameter, scaled 0.55..1.3 per dot. Under ~2 the hardware point-size floor kicks in for most dots and the alpha compensation is doing all the work; over ~5 the dense core fills solid and the ripple stops being legible.
- `count = 6000`
  One interleaved-free buffer, one draw call. At this size the field is vertex-bound rather than fill-bound, and 6000 is roughly where the core reads as continuous without the gaps needing more dots to hide them.
- `MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_DOT = 24`
  Rejection-sampling budget. The mean of the ramp is about 0.45, so ~2.2 attempts per kept dot; a 24x budget absorbs a much sparser custom curve and still terminates rather than spinning forever if someone authors a ramp that is zero everywhere.
- `STATIC_ELAPSED = 3.4 s`
  The frame drawn under reduced motion. Far enough in that two crests have left the source, so the still frame shows the ripple structure rather than the undisturbed lattice.

## API

```ts
function RadialRippleDotCloud(props: { count?: number; size?: number; frequency?: number; speed?: number; decay?: number; amplitude?: number; centerX?: number; centerY?: number; color?: string; crestColor?: string; opacity?: number; seed?: number | string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `count: number` — default `6000`
  Dots kept after density rejection. One draw call regardless.
- `size: number` — default `2.6`
  Base dot diameter in CSS pixels, before the per-dot density scale.
- `frequency: number` — default `6.5`
  Radians of wave per field unit; wavelength is 2π / frequency.
- `speed: number` — default `2.4`
  Radians of phase per second. Crest speed is speed / frequency.
- `decay: number` — default `0.85`
  Exponential attenuation per field unit of radius.
- `amplitude: number` — default `0.045`
  Peak displacement in field units, where the field is 2 units tall.
- `centerX: number` — default `0.4`
  Ripple source across the field, 0..1. Deliberately not centred.
- `centerY: number` — default `0.5`
  Ripple source down the field, 0..1.
- `color: string` — default `'#5d6b7a'`
  Dot colour in the troughs.
- `crestColor: string` — default `'#eaf2ff'`
  Dot colour on an outgoing crest.
- `opacity: number` — default `1`
  Multiplier applied after the per-dot area compensation.
- `seed: number | string` — default `'radial-ripple-dot-cloud'`
  Seeds rejection sampling, so the layout is stable across reloads and matches the server.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the host element via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Uniform cubic B-spline basis at parameter `t` within one span. */
function bsplineWeights(t: number): [number, number, number, number] {
  const t2 = t * t;
  const t3 = t2 * t;
  return [
    (1 - 3 * t + 3 * t2 - t3) / 6,
    (4 - 6 * t2 + 3 * t3) / 6,
    (1 + 3 * t + 3 * t2 - 3 * t3) / 6,
    t3 / 6,
  ];
}

/**
 * Sample the density curve at `u` in 0..1. `n` control points give `n - 3`
 * spans; the curve is C2 and does NOT pass through its control points, which
 * is the property that lets a hand-placed sequence stay smooth.
 */
function sampleRamp(ramp: readonly number[], u: number): number {
  const spans = ramp.length - 3;
  if (spans < 1) return clamp(ramp[0] ?? 0, 0, 1);
  const s = clamp(u, 0, 1) * spans;
  const span = Math.min(Math.floor(s), spans - 1);
  const weights = bsplineWeights(s - span);
  let total = 0;
  for (let k = 0; k < 4; k += 1) {
    total += (ramp[span + k] ?? 0) * (weights[k] ?? 0);
  }
  return clamp(total, 0, 1);
}

export function RadialRippleDotCloud({
  count = 6000,
  size = 2.6,
  frequency = 6.5,
  speed = 2.4,
  decay = 0.85,
  amplitude = 0.045,
  centerX = 0.4,
  centerY = 0.5,
  color = '#5d6b7a',
  crestColor = '#eaf2ff',
  opacity = 1,
  seed = 'radial-ripple-dot-cloud',
  className,
}: RadialRippleDotCloudProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);
  const [unsupported, setUnsupported] = useState(false);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const size2 = useRef({ width, height });
  size2.current = { width, height };

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const visible = useVisibility();
  const { inView } = useInView(host, { threshold: 0 });
  const ready = width > 0 && height > 0;

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready) return;

    if (!hasWebGL()) {
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }

    let renderer: THREE.WebGLRenderer;
    try {
      renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: false, alpha: true });
    } catch {
      // A context can still be refused between the probe and the construction —
      // the tab may have hit the browser's live-context ceiling in between. three
      // throws rather than returning null, and an uncaught throw here takes the
      // page with it.
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }
    renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio());
    renderer.setClearAlpha(0);

    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const camera = new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0.1, 10);
    camera.position.z = 1;

    // Field-unit centre of the ripple. Baked alongside the origins so the
    // normalised radius each dot stores is measured from the same point the
    // shader will use.
    const cx = (centerX * 2 - 1) * FIELD_HALF_W;
    const cy = 1 - centerY * 2;

    /* The farthest corner from the source. Normalising radius by this is what
       makes the density ramp aspect-independent: the tail of the curve lands on
       the corner of the field rather than at some arbitrary unit distance. */
    const maxRadius = Math.max(
      Math.hypot(FIELD_HALF_W - cx, 1 - cy),
      Math.hypot(FIELD_HALF_W + cx, 1 - cy),
      Math.hypot(FIELD_HALF_W - cx, 1 + cy),
      Math.hypot(FIELD_HALF_W + cx, 1 + cy),
    );

    /* Rejection sampling against the density curve. Candidates are uniform over
       the field rectangle and kept with probability `ramp(r)`, which is the only
       way to get an arbitrary hand-drawn radial density out of a uniform PRNG
       without inverting the curve analytically. Seeded, so the layout is
       identical on the server, on the client, and on every reload. */
    const rng = createRng(seed);
    const wanted = Math.max(1, Math.round(count));
    const origins: number[] = [];
    const scales: number[] = [];
    const alphas: number[] = [];

    let attempts = 0;
    const budget = wanted * MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_DOT;
    while (origins.length < wanted * 2 && attempts < budget) {
      attempts += 1;
      const x = (rng() * 2 - 1) * FIELD_HALF_W;
      const y = rng() * 2 - 1;
      const density = sampleRamp(DENSITY_RAMP, Math.hypot(x - cx, y - cy) / maxRadius);
      if (rng() > density) continue;
      origins.push(x, y);
      // The ramp is reused for weight as well as for density, so a sparse band
      // is also a dim one. Two curves would let them disagree and the field
      // would read as noise with holes in it.
      scales.push(0.55 + 0.75 * density);
      alphas.push(0.3 + 0.7 * density);
    }

    const kept = scales.length;
    const positions = new Float32Array(kept * 3); // zeros; the shader positions
    const originAttr = new Float32Array(kept * 2);
    const scaleAttr = new Float32Array(kept);
    const alphaAttr = new Float32Array(kept);
    for (let i = 0; i < kept; i += 1) {
      originAttr[i * 2] = origins[i * 2] ?? 0;
      originAttr[i * 2 + 1] = origins[i * 2 + 1] ?? 0;
      scaleAttr[i] = scales[i] ?? 1;
      alphaAttr[i] = alphas[i] ?? 1;
    }

    const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
    geometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(positions, 3));
    geometry.setAttribute('aOrigin', new THREE.BufferAttribute(originAttr, 2));
    geometry.setAttribute('aScale', new THREE.BufferAttribute(scaleAttr, 1));
    geometry.setAttribute('aAlpha', new THREE.BufferAttribute(alphaAttr, 1));

    const uniforms: Uniforms = {
      uElapsed: { value: 0 },
      uCover: { value: 1 },
      uCenter: { value: new THREE.Vector2(cx, cy) },
      uFrequency: { value: frequency },
      uSpeed: { value: speed },
      uDecay: { value: decay },
      uAmplitude: { value: amplitude },
      uSize: { value: size },
      uPixelRatio: { value: renderer.getPixelRatio() },
      uColor: { value: new THREE.Color(color) },
      uCrestColor: { value: new THREE.Color(crestColor) },
      uOpacity: { value: opacity },
    };

    const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader: RADIAL_RIPPLE_VERT,
      fragmentShader: RADIAL_RIPPLE_FRAG,
      uniforms,
      transparent: true,
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
      // Additive, because overlapping dots in the dense core should read as
      // brighter rather than as a flat plate of the same colour.
      blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending,
    });

    const points = new THREE.Points(geometry, material);
    // Every vertex is displaced in the shader, so three's bounding sphere is
    // wrong by construction and culling against it can blank the whole cloud.
    points.frustumCulled = false;
    scene.add(points);

    el.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
    renderer.domElement.style.display = 'block';
    renderer.domElement.style.width = '100%';
    renderer.domElement.style.height = '100%';

    const resize = (w: number, h: number) => {
      if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) return;
      renderer.setSize(w, h, false);
      const aspect = w / h;
      camera.left = -aspect;
      camera.right = aspect;
      camera.top = 1;
      camera.bottom = -1;
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix();

      /* Cover, not contain. Past 16:9 the baked field is narrower than the
         camera, so it is scaled up until it reaches both edges; the alternative
         is a visible vertical seam where the dots stop. The centre is scaled by
         the same factor so the ripple stays put relative to the field. */
      const cover = Math.max(1, aspect / FIELD_HALF_W);
      uniforms.uCover.value = cover;
      uniforms.uCenter.value.set(cx * cover, cy * cover);
      // Re-read: moving a window between displays changes devicePixelRatio
      // without changing the CSS size, and dot sizes are specified in CSS px.
      uniforms.uPixelRatio.value = renderer.getPixelRatio();
    };

    const draw = (elapsed: number) => {
      uniforms.uElapsed.value = elapsed;
      renderer.render(scene, camera);
    };

    resize(size2.current.width, size2.current.height);
    stage.current = { resize, draw };
    draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      disposeObject(scene);
      material.dispose();
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      renderer.domElement.remove();
    };
  }, [
    ready,
    count,
    size,
    frequency,
    speed,
    decay,
    amplitude,
    centerX,
    centerY,
    color,
    crestColor,
    opacity,
    seed,
  ]);

  useEffect(() => {
    stage.current?.resize(width, height);
    // A resize clears the drawing buffer, so the frozen frame has to be
    // redrawn or a reduced-motion visitor sees an empty box after any reflow.
    if (reduced) stage.current?.draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);
  }, [width, height, reduced]);

  useRaf(
    (_dt, elapsed) => stage.current?.draw(elapsed),
    ready && inView && visible && !reduced && !unsupported,
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nulls the stage ref, walks the scene with `disposeObject` to release the geometry and its four attribute buffers, disposes the ShaderMaterial explicitly, then calls `disposeRenderer` — `dispose` plus `forceContextLoss` plus a zeroed drawing buffer — and removes the canvas. The canvas is created inside the effect and appended imperatively rather than being owned by a React ref, so a StrictMode double-mount builds a fresh context instead of handing back the one that was just killed.

**Reduced motion.** The component reads `useReducedMotion` itself and opens no rAF subscription. One frame is drawn at `uElapsed = 3.4`, by which point two crests have left the source — so the still image shows the ripple structure and the drawn density bands, not the undisturbed lattice. The layout, the colours and the crest tinting are all present; only the travel stops. The frame is re-drawn on resize because a canvas resize clears the buffer.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Writing `sin(dist * frequency) * sin(elapsed * speed)`. That is a standing wave: the rings pulse in place and never travel. Subtracting the phase from the radius inside one sine is what makes crests move outward — and adding it instead sends them inward, which reads as a drain rather than an impact.
- Normalising the offset vector without guarding the source. At `dist == 0` the division produces NaN, the vertex is discarded by the rasteriser, and on some drivers the whole primitive goes with it — an intermittently missing dot that is very hard to attribute.
- Attenuating the radius instead of the wave, or using a linear falloff. Linear reaches zero at a fixed radius and draws a visible circle across the field; the exponential never quite reaches zero and has no edge.
- Rebuilding the position buffer on resize. It reallocates hundreds of kilobytes during a window drag and, if the layout is re-sampled, re-randomises every dot mid-motion. Baking in field units and scaling by one `uCover` uniform avoids both.
- Leaving `frustumCulled` at its default. Every vertex is displaced in the shader, so three's bounding sphere — computed from the undisplaced attribute — is wrong, and the whole cloud can vanish when the camera or the container changes.
- Using `Math.random()` for the layout. The server and the client disagree, so React logs a hydration mismatch, and the composition a designer approved is not the one the next visitor sees.
- Treating the B-spline control points as points on the curve. The curve does not pass through them — the value at the start of the first span is `(P0 + 4P1 + P2) / 6`. Authoring the ramp as if it were interpolating produces a flatter, wrong curve and hours of confusion.
- Driving dot brightness from a second curve independent of the density curve. Where they disagree the field reads as random noise with holes in it rather than as drawn bands.
- Forgetting that a resize clears the drawing buffer. Under reduced motion nothing redraws afterwards, so the component is blank after any reflow unless the frozen frame is re-rendered.

## Notes

- The camera is orthographic, ±aspect by ±1, so field units are directly comparable to the container height: 1 unit is half the visible height.
- `uCover` implements cover, not contain. Past 16:9 the baked field would otherwise stop short of the container edge and leave a visible vertical seam where the dots end.
- The ripple runs on absolute elapsed time from the shared rAF clock, so several instances on one page stay in phase with each other.

## Definition of done

Rings of dots visibly travel outward from a point left of centre, roughly two crests visible at a time, brightening as each crest passes and dimming behind it. The rim of the field barely moves. The layout has obvious drawn structure — a dense core, a gap, a second band — and is identical after a reload and after resizing the window. With reduced motion the field renders in full and holds a frozen mid-ripple frame.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Radio

A `RadioGroup` and `Radio` on React Aria, plus the bare `RadioDot` glyph they draw. The dot is three stacked circles: a bordered white surface, the accent gradient surface on top of it, and a small white centre. Selecting cross-fades the two surfaces over 200ms while the centre scales up from nothing, which gives a gradient fill a smooth transition even though CSS cannot animate gradients.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

React Aria radio group with a gradient selected dot that cross-fades in while the white centre scales up, in two sizes.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `RadioGroup` spreads its props onto `AriaRadioGroup` (single selection, arrow-key roving between radios, form `name` and `value`, label association) and lays the radios out as `flex flex-col gap-2`. `className` accepts a string or React Aria's state function.
2. `Radio` renders `AriaRadio`, a `<label>` around a visually hidden `<input type="radio">`, as `group inline-flex items-center select-none gap-2`. Its children render function passes `isSelected` and `isFocusVisible` to `RadioDot`, then renders `children` (when not null or undefined) in the size's label type in `text-text-primary`. Disabled adds `cursor-not-allowed opacity-50`.
3. `RadioDot` is a `relative rounded-full` span marked `aria-hidden`, sized by `dotStyles[size]`. Layer one is the default surface (`border-border-checkbox-default bg-background-primary-default shadow-xs`). Layer two is the selected surface: `bg-gradient-to-b from-accent-500 to-accent-600` with an inset 1px accent ring and an inset 2px white top highlight at 25% opacity. Only one of them is at full opacity at a time, and both have `transition-opacity duration-200`.
4. Layer three is the inner dot (`bg-control-indicator-background`, white), positioned with `absolute top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2` rather than flex centring, because fractional sizes such as 5px can land on half pixels under flex. It transitions `scale` and `opacity` over 200ms between `scale-0 opacity-0` and `scale-100 opacity-100`.
5. Focus draws `ring-2 ring-border-focus-ring ring-offset-2` on the dot only while React Aria reports `isFocusVisible`, so a mouse click does not show a ring.
6. `RadioDot` is exported on its own for menu rows that already manage selection (for example a dropdown acting as a radio group). It has no role or focus, so it can sit inside a menu item without nesting one interactive control in another.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `md = size-4 dot (16px), size-1.5 centre (6px), text-body-medium`
  The Figma radio for forms. The 6px centre leaves a 5px gradient ring around it at 16px, which reads as a ring instead of a filled disc.
- `sm = size-3.5 dot (14px), 5px centre, 0.875px border, text-body-2-medium`
  The AI chat model picker (node 4035:6925). Every stroke is scaled by 14/16 (0.875) so the small dot looks like the medium one shrunk, not thinner.
- `crossfade = 200ms opacity on both surfaces, 200ms scale + opacity on the centre`
  Gradient backgrounds cannot transition, so the motion is carried by opacity on stacked layers. All three layers share one duration so the fill and the centre arrive together.
- `selected inset shadow = inset 0 0 0 1px accent-500, inset 0 2px 0 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.25)`
  The first is a crisp edge where a border would shift the layout; the second is the top highlight that matches the primary button's gradient.

## API

```ts
function RadioGroup(props: Omit<AriaRadioGroupProps, "children"> & { children?: ReactNode; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function Radio(props: Omit<AriaRadioProps, "children"> & { children?: ReactNode; size?: "sm" | "md"; ref?: Ref<HTMLLabelElement> }): JSX.Element
function RadioDot(props: { selected?: boolean; size?: "sm" | "md"; focusVisible?: boolean; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `RadioGroup.value / defaultValue: string`
  Controlled or uncontrolled selected value, from React Aria.
- `RadioGroup.onChange: (value: string) => void`
  Called with the newly selected radio's `value`.
- `RadioGroup.aria-label: string`
  Accessible name when the group has no visible label.
- `Radio.value: string`
  Value this radio contributes to the group.
- `Radio.size: "sm" | "md"` — default `"md"`
  16px dot with body label, or 14px dot with the 13px body-2 label.
- `Radio.isDisabled: boolean`
  Half opacity, not-allowed cursor, skipped by arrow keys.
- `RadioDot.selected: boolean` — default `false`
  Shows the gradient surface and the white centre.
- `RadioDot.size: "sm" | "md"` — default `"sm"`
  Same size table as `Radio`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function RadioDot({ selected = false, size = "sm", focusVisible = false, className }: RadioDotProps) {
  const s = dotStyles[size];
  return (
    <span
      aria-hidden
      className={cx(
        "relative flex shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full",
        s.dot,
        focusVisible && "ring-2 ring-border-focus-ring ring-offset-2",
        className,
      )}
    >
      {/* Default surface */}
      <span
        className={cx(
          "absolute inset-0 rounded-full border-border-checkbox-default bg-background-primary-default shadow-xs",
          "transition-opacity duration-200 ease",
          s.border,
          selected && "opacity-0",
        )}
      />
      {/* Selected gradient surface */}
      <span
        className={cx(
          "absolute inset-0 rounded-full",
          "transition-opacity duration-200 ease",
          s.selected,
          !selected && "opacity-0",
        )}
      />
      {/* Inner dot: absolutely centered (flex centering of fractional sizes can
          land on subpixels) and no drop shadow — a downward shadow makes the
          dot read as sitting below center. */}
      <span
        className={cx(
          "absolute top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 rounded-full bg-control-indicator-background",
          "transition-[scale,opacity] duration-200 ease",
          s.inner,
          selected ? "scale-100 opacity-100" : "scale-0 opacity-0",
        )}
      />
    </span>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component holds no state, listeners or timers of its own; React Aria owns the group state.

**Reduced motion.** The component does not check `prefers-reduced-motion`. The 200ms opacity crossfade and the centre scale are CSS transitions, so a global rule that removes transitions makes the dot switch instantly.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not swap the gradient with a conditional `background-image` on one element. It snaps. The crossfade needs the two surfaces as separate layers.
- Do not centre the inner dot with flexbox. At 5px it can land on a half pixel and look off-centre. Keep the absolute `top-1/2 left-1/2` plus translate.
- Do not give the inner dot a drop shadow. A downward shadow makes it look like it sits below the centre of the ring.
- Do not put a `Radio` inside a menu item. Use `RadioDot`, which is presentational, and let the menu own selection and focus.
- Do not leave `RadioGroup` without a visible `label` or an `aria-label`. React Aria warns about a radio group with no accessible name.

## Notes

- `RadioDot` defaults to `size="sm"` (it is mostly used in compact menus), while `Radio` defaults to `size="md"`.

## Definition of done

Three radios stack vertically with Weekly selected: its dot is a blue gradient with a white centre. Clicking Monthly fades Weekly back to a white bordered circle while Monthly's gradient fades in and its centre grows from nothing, in about 200ms. Arrow keys move the selection within the group. Tab shows a focus ring around the dot, a mouse click does not. The small size renders a slightly smaller dot and label with the same look.

# Build: Radio Card

The radio counterpart of Checkbox Card: a 10px-radius bordered card with a title, an optional description and the 16px `RadioDot` on the trailing edge. It is a React Aria `Radio`, so it must sit in a `RadioGroup`, which gives single selection and arrow-key movement between cards. Selecting a card cross-fades its dot to the accent gradient while the white centre grows in.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Bordered option card with title, description and the kit radio dot on the right; inside a RadioGroup a click anywhere selects it.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `RadioCard` renders `AriaRadio` directly. React Aria makes it a `<label>` around a visually hidden `<input type="radio">`, so the whole card is the click target and the card reads its selection, focus and disabled state from the surrounding `RadioGroup` context. All Aria radio props (`value`, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) pass through.
2. The card class is computed from the render state: `flex w-full items-center justify-between gap-3 rounded-2lg border border-border-button-default py-3 pe-5 ps-4 select-none` with `transition-colors duration-150`. Hovered and not disabled gives `bg-background-primary-hover`, otherwise `bg-background-primary-default`. Disabled adds `cursor-not-allowed opacity-50`.
3. The text column (`flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-0.5`) holds the title in `text-body-medium text-text-primary` and, when `description` is not null or undefined, a line in `text-body-regular text-text-secondary`. Both truncate to one line.
4. The trailing slot (`shrink-0 py-1`) renders `<RadioDot size="md" selected={state.isSelected} focusVisible={state.isFocusVisible} />`, the same glyph `Radio` uses: a bordered white disc and an accent gradient disc cross-fading over 200ms, with a 6px white centre that scales from 0 to 1. The focus ring appears on the dot for keyboard focus only.
5. Because the cards are radios in one group, Tab enters the group once (on the selected card) and the arrow keys move both focus and selection between cards, which is the standard radio pattern.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `padding = ps-4 pe-5 py-3 (16 / 20 / 12px)`
  The Figma checkbox item spec (node 3793:2966), reused so radio and checkbox cards are interchangeable in one settings page. The wider trailing padding gives the dot breathing room in its corner.
- `dot size = RadioDot size="md" (16px, 6px centre)`
  Fixed to medium so the dot matches the 16px checkbox box in Checkbox Card. It is not a prop.
- `radius = rounded-2lg (10px)`
  The kit's radius for card-level controls, shared with Checkbox Card and Switch Card.

## API

```ts
function RadioCard(props: Omit<AriaRadioProps, "children"> & { title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; ref?: Ref<HTMLLabelElement> }): JSX.Element
```

- `value: string`
  Value this card contributes to the surrounding `RadioGroup`.
- `title: ReactNode`
  Main label in body medium. Also the accessible name of the radio.
- `description: ReactNode`
  Optional secondary line, truncated to one line.
- `isDisabled: boolean`
  Half opacity, not-allowed cursor, skipped by arrow keys.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of

```tsx

    <AriaRadio
      ref={ref}
      {...props}

            : "bg-background-primary-default",

          </span>
        </>
      )}
```

## Requirements

With a card focused, the arrow keys move the selection between cards. Hover tints a card's background. A disabled card is at half opacity and cannot be selected.
