# Build: Rotary Drag Carousel

Items sit at fixed stations around a circle whose hub is below the frame, so only the top arc is ever visible. The gesture is measured in angle rather than pixels: `atan2(y - cy, x - cx)`, differenced through a shortest-signed wrap, so a hand sweeping the top of the wheel turns it by the amount it actually travelled around the hub. Release and it keeps going at the speed it left at, then stops with a station facing up — one motion, no corrective hop.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A wheel of cards you grab and spin. Angular drag, projected inertia, and it always lands on a station.

- Category: layout
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. Layout is a pure function of one number. For wheel angle `A`, station `i` sits at screen angle `theta = A + i * (360 / count) - 90`, at `(cx + R cos theta, cy + R sin theta)`, rotated by the shortest signed distance to the top, `away = wrapRange(theta + 90, -180, 180)`. `A` is unbounded and may be -4000 without consequence, because `away` is the only value that ever needs wrapping.
2. The radius is floored at `1.25 x containerHeight`, which forces the hub `cy = topInset * height + R` strictly below the box. That is a correctness constraint, not a look: `atan2` about a point the user can touch converts a two-pixel wobble near the hub into a hundred degrees of spin.
3. Each `pointermove` computes the pointer's own angle about the hub and adds `wrapRange(current - previous, -180, 180)` to `A`. The wrap is what keeps a drag across the 180° seam from reading as a 359° jerk backwards.
4. Release velocity is measured over a rolling ~70 ms window of `(angle, time)` rather than off the final delta. Because a stationary finger produces no `pointermove` events, the window never advances while the hand is still, and the measured speed decays toward zero on its own — "drag, pause, lift" therefore does not throw.
5. Inertia without a plugin: `power3.out` is `p(t) = 1 - (1 - t)^3`, so `p'(0) = 3`. A tween of duration `D` covering `delta` degrees departs at `3 * delta / D` deg/s, so setting `delta = v * D / 3` makes a plain `gsap.to` continue the gesture at exactly the speed the hand left.
6. That projected landing angle is rounded to a multiple of the station spacing *before* the tween is created, so the throw and the snap are the same tween. Snapping afterwards is a second animation starting from rest — the small hop that gives away a hand-rolled dial.
7. Pointer capture is taken on `pointerdown`, and the release path is one idempotent `finish` guarded on the stored `pointerId`, wired to `pointerup`, `pointercancel` and `lostpointercapture` alike. A drag that ends off-screen still lands.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `MIN_RADIUS_HEIGHT_RATIO = 1.25`
  Radius floor as a multiple of container height, so the hub is always below the visible box. At 1.0 the hub lands exactly on the bottom edge and a press there divides by a near-zero radius; below 1.0 it is reachable and the wheel spins wildly for a pointer that barely moved.
- `POWER3_OUT_SLOPE = 3`
  The initial derivative of `power3.out`, and the divisor in `delta = v * D / 3`. It is exact, not tuned: change the ease and this number changes with it — `power2.out` needs 2, `power4.out` needs 4. Leave it at 3 with a different ease and the throw either undershoots or overshoots by a constant factor.
- `throwDuration = 1.1`
  Seconds of inertial travel. Under ~0.6 s the wheel stops so abruptly that a fast fling feels like it hit a wall; over ~1.6 s the tail is so slow it reads as broken rather than as momentum, and it delays the settle callback past the point anyone is still watching.
- `maxThrow = 260`
  Degrees one throw may carry, applied to the projected distance before snapping. Without a cap, a 900 deg/s fling projects 330° and the wheel makes most of a revolution from a flick — past about 270° the user loses track of which way it went and which station is coming.
- `VELOCITY_WINDOW = 0.07`
  Seconds of gesture history the release speed is averaged over. Shorter and it is effectively the last delta, which is noisy at 120 Hz and jitters the throw distance between identical gestures; much longer and a deliberate slow-down before release is averaged away, so the wheel throws when the user meant to place it.
- `MAX_VELOCITY = 900`
  Degrees per second the measured speed is clamped to. A pointer that jumps (a tab switch mid-drag, a synthetic event, a coalesced move across the hub) can report thousands of deg/s; clamping keeps one bad sample from spinning the wheel several turns.
- `DRAG_THRESHOLD = 5`
  Pixels of travel before a press becomes a drag. Below ~3 the hand tremor in a normal tap counts as a drag, so every tap is swallowed as a gesture; above ~10 a small deliberate nudge of the wheel does nothing at all.
- `CULL_DEG = 96`
  Stations more than this far from the top are `visibility: hidden`. Just past 90° they are behind the horizontal through the hub and outside the box in every supported aspect ratio, so painting them is pure cost; culling at exactly 90° makes the boundary coincide with the fade reaching its floor and items visibly wink out.
- `radiusRatio = 0.78`
  Radius as a fraction of container width, before the height floor. Larger flattens the arc until the wheel reads as a straight row; much smaller pulls the hub up toward the box and the visible arc bends so hard that only three stations fit.
- `fade = 0.85`
  Opacity lost per 90° off the top. The station one step out stays clearly legible, which is the affordance that says the wheel turns; at 1.0 the neighbours reach zero exactly at the cull angle and the wheel looks like it holds one card.

## API

```ts
function RotaryDragCarousel(props: { children: ReactNode; radiusRatio?: number; topInsetRatio?: number; snapDeg?: number; throwDuration?: number; maxThrow?: number; fade?: number; scaleFalloff?: number; initialIndex?: number; className?: string; itemClassName?: string; onIndexChange?: (index: number) => void; 'aria-label'?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  One item per child. Each gets a station on the wheel.
- `radiusRatio: number` — default `0.78`
  Wheel radius as a fraction of container width, floored against height so the hub stays below the box.
- `topInsetRatio: number` — default `0.08`
  Where the top of the wheel sits, as a fraction of container height.
- `snapDeg: number`
  Degrees the wheel snaps to. Defaults to one station, `360 / count`.
- `throwDuration: number` — default `1.1`
  Seconds of inertial travel after release.
- `maxThrow: number` — default `260`
  Hard cap on how far one throw may carry, in degrees.
- `fade: number` — default `0.85`
  Opacity lost per 90° away from the top station.
- `scaleFalloff: number` — default `0.22`
  Scale lost at 90° away from the top station.
- `initialIndex: number` — default `0`
  Station facing up on mount. Seeded once, never re-applied.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the drag surface.
- `itemClassName: string`
  Merged onto every station. Size the items here.
- `onIndexChange: (index: number) => void`
  Fires with the wrapped index of the station that lands facing up.
- `aria-label: string` — default `'Carousel'`
  Label for the focusable wheel, which also takes arrow keys.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * Write one transform per station from the current wheel angle. A pure
 * function of `angleRef.current` and the box size — nothing accumulates in
 * here, so interrupting the throw tween mid-flight cannot desynchronise it.
 */
const layout = useCallback(() => {
  const host = hostRef.current;
  if (!host || count === 0) return;

  const width = host.clientWidth;
  const height = host.clientHeight;
  if (width < 1 || height < 1) return;

  const radius = Math.max(radiusRatio * width, height * MIN_RADIUS_HEIGHT_RATIO);
  const cx = width / 2;
  const cy = topInsetRatio * height + radius;
  const angle = angleRef.current;

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
    const station = stationsRef.current[i];
    if (!station) continue;

    // Station i's screen angle. `UP_DEG` puts station 0 at the top when the
    // wheel is at 0, so the maths and the visual agree at rest.
    const theta = angle + i * step + UP_DEG;
    // Shortest signed distance to the top, in (-180, 180]. The wheel is a
    // real circle, so this is the only place wrapping is needed at all —
    // `angle` itself may be -4000 without consequence.
    const away = wrapRange(theta - UP_DEG, -180, 180);
    const distance = Math.abs(away);

    if (distance > CULL_DEG) {
      station.style.visibility = 'hidden';
      continue;
    }

    const rad = theta * DEG_TO_RAD;
    const x = cx + radius * Math.cos(rad);
    const y = cy + radius * Math.sin(rad);
    const t = Math.min(distance / 90, 1);

    station.style.visibility = 'visible';
    // Counter-rotating by `-away` would keep the cards upright; leaving the
    // rotation in is what makes it read as one rigid wheel rather than a row
    // of cards travelling along an arc.
    station.style.transform =
      `translate(-50%, -50%) translate(${x.toFixed(2)}px, ${y.toFixed(2)}px) ` +
      `rotate(${away.toFixed(2)}deg) ` +
      `scale(${(1 - scaleFalloff * t).toFixed(3)})`;
    station.style.opacity = clamp(1 - fade * t, 0, 1).toFixed(3);
    station.style.zIndex = String(100 - Math.round(distance));
  }
}, [count, step, radiusRatio, topInsetRatio, fade, scaleFalloff]);

/** Angle at which station `index` faces up: `angle + index * step = 0`. */
const angleForIndex = useCallback((index: number) => -index * step, [step]);

const report = useCallback(() => {
  if (count === 0) return;
  // `angle = -i * step` puts station i up, so `i = -angle / step`.
  const index = wrapIndex(Math.round(-angleRef.current / step), count);
  if (index === reportedRef.current) return;
  reportedRef.current = index;
  notify.current?.(index);
}, [count, step]);

/**
 * Land the wheel. `velocity` is degrees per second at the moment of release;
 * pass 0 for a keyboard step or a tap.
 */
const settle = useCallback(
  (velocity: number) => {
    const projected =
      angleRef.current +
      clamp(
        (velocity * throwDuration) / POWER3_OUT_SLOPE,
        -maxThrow,
        maxThrow,
      );
    // Round to a station BEFORE tweening. Snapping afterwards is a second
    // animation that starts from rest, which is the little hop that gives
    // away every hand-rolled dial.
    const landing = Math.round(projected / snap) * snap;

    gsap.killTweensOf(angleRef);

    if (reduced || Math.abs(landing - angleRef.current) < 0.01) {
      angleRef.current = landing;
      layout();
      report();
      return;
    }

    gsap.to(angleRef, {
      current: landing,
      duration: throwDuration,
      ease: 'power3.out',
      overwrite: true,
      onUpdate: layout,
      onComplete: report,
    });
  },
  [throwDuration, maxThrow, snap, reduced, layout, report],
);

useEffect(() => {
  const host = hostRef.current;
  if (!host) return;

  let pointerId: number | null = null;
  let lastPointerAngle = 0;
  let pressX = 0;
  let pressY = 0;
  let moved = false;
  let swallowClick = false;
  let swallowTimer: number | null = null;

  // The gate expires. A throw released over a gap between cards, or one the
  // browser cancels, produces no click at all — and a gate left armed eats
  // the visitor's next real click, however long afterwards it lands.
  const disarmSwallow = () => {
    swallowClick = false;
    if (swallowTimer !== null) {
      window.clearTimeout(swallowTimer);
      swallowTimer = null;
    }
  };
  /** Rolling window: the wheel angle and clock at the start of the window. */
  let sampleAngle = 0;
  let sampleTime = 0;

  const now = () => performance.now() / 1000;

  const pointerAngle = (clientX: number, clientY: number) => {
    const rect = host.getBoundingClientRect();
    const radius = Math.max(
      radiusRatio * rect.width,
      rect.height * MIN_RADIUS_HEIGHT_RATIO,
    );
    const cx = rect.left + rect.width / 2;
    const cy = rect.top + topInsetRatio * rect.height + radius;
    return Math.atan2(clientY - cy, clientX - cx) / DEG_TO_RAD;
  };

  const onPointerDown = (e: PointerEvent) => {
    // One pointer owns the wheel. A second finger arriving mid-throw would
    // otherwise reset the origin angle and the wheel would jump.
    if (pointerId !== null || !e.isPrimary) return;
    if (e.pointerType === 'mouse' && e.button !== 0) return;

    // A new press means the previous gesture is over and whatever click it
    // was owed never came.
    disarmSwallow();
    pointerId = e.pointerId;
    pressX = e.clientX;
    pressY = e.clientY;
    moved = false;
    lastPointerAngle = pointerAngle(e.clientX, e.clientY);
    sampleAngle = angleRef.current;
    sampleTime = now();

    // Capture on press, not once the threshold is crossed: by then the
    // pointer may already have left the element, and `pointermove` would
    // have stopped arriving.
    host.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId);
    gsap.killTweensOf(angleRef);
  };

  const onPointerMove = (e: PointerEvent) => {
    if (pointerId !== e.pointerId) return;

    const current = pointerAngle(e.clientX, e.clientY);
    // Shortest signed step. Without the wrap, dragging across the 180°
    // seam reads as a 359° jerk in the wrong direction.
    const delta = wrapRange(current - lastPointerAngle, -180, 180);
    lastPointerAngle = current;

    if (!moved) {
      if (Math.hypot(e.clientX - pressX, e.clientY - pressY) < DRAG_THRESHOLD) return;
      moved = true;
    }

    angleRef.current += delta;
    layout();

    // Retire the velocity window once it is full. Measuring over a window
    // rather than off the last delta is what stops "drag, pause, lift" from
    // throwing the wheel: with no movement there are no events, the window
    // never advances, and the measured speed decays toward zero on its own.
    const t = now();
    if (t - sampleTime > VELOCITY_WINDOW) {
      sampleAngle = angleRef.current;
      sampleTime = t;
    }
  };

  /**
   * Idempotent. Called from `pointerup`, `pointercancel` and
   * `lostpointercapture`, all three of which can be the last event a gesture
   * produces, and at least one of which will always arrive — including when
   * the pointer is released outside the window, or the OS takes it away for
   * a gesture of its own. Guarding on `pointerId` makes the extra calls
   * no-ops instead of a double throw.
   */
  const finish = (e: PointerEvent) => {
    if (pointerId !== e.pointerId) return;
    const id = pointerId;
    pointerId = null;

    const elapsed = now() - sampleTime;
    const velocity =
      moved && elapsed > 0
        ? clamp((angleRef.current - sampleAngle) / elapsed, -MAX_VELOCITY, MAX_VELOCITY)
        : 0;

    disarmSwallow();
    if (moved) {
      swallowClick = true;
      swallowTimer = window.setTimeout(disarmSwallow, SWALLOW_TIMEOUT_MS);
    }
    moved = false;

    if (host.hasPointerCapture(id)) host.releasePointerCapture(id);
    settle(velocity);
  };

  // Capture phase, ahead of any child's own handler. A throw ends with a
  // `click` on whatever happens to be under the pointer, so without this the
  // gesture that spins the wheel also activates a card.
  const onClick = (e: MouseEvent) => {
    if (!swallowClick) return;

    // Enter or Space on a focused card dispatches a click with `detail === 0`
    // and no pointer sequence behind it. Nothing was thrown, and swallowing
    // it is what makes the wheel keyboard-inoperable.
    if (e.detail === 0) return;

    disarmSwallow();
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();
  };

  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    const direction =
      e.key === 'ArrowRight' || e.key === 'ArrowDown'
        ? -1
        : e.key === 'ArrowLeft' || e.key === 'ArrowUp'
          ? 1
          : 0;
    if (direction === 0) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    gsap.killTweensOf(angleRef);
    angleRef.current = Math.round(angleRef.current / snap) * snap + direction * snap;
    settle(0);
  };

  host.addEventListener('pointerdown', onPointerDown);
  host.addEventListener('pointermove', onPointerMove);
  host.addEventListener('pointerup', finish);
  host.addEventListener('pointercancel', finish);
  host.addEventListener('lostpointercapture', finish);
  host.addEventListener('click', onClick, true);
  host.addEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);

  return () => {
    host.removeEventListener('pointerdown', onPointerDown);
    host.removeEventListener('pointermove', onPointerMove);
    host.removeEventListener('pointerup', finish);
    host.removeEventListener('pointercancel', finish);
    host.removeEventListener('lostpointercapture', finish);
    host.removeEventListener('click', onClick, true);
    // Or the timer outlives the effect and a remount starts life armed.
    disarmSwallow();
    host.removeEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);
    if (pointerId !== null && host.hasPointerCapture(pointerId)) {
      host.releasePointerCapture(pointerId);
    }
    pointerId = null;
  };
}, [layout, settle, snap, radiusRatio, topInsetRatio]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes `pointerdown`, `pointermove`, `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, `lostpointercapture`, the capture-phase `click` and `keydown`; releases pointer capture if a gesture is still live at unmount; and kills the throw tween on the angle ref via a separate effect so an in-flight `gsap.to` cannot call `onUpdate` against detached nodes. The shared resize observer unregisters. Nothing but inline styles on the stations remains, and those die with the nodes.

**Reduced motion.** Dragging is unchanged — it is the user's own motion, tracked one-to-one, and removing it would remove the component. What goes away is everything the component would have animated by itself: the inertial throw is not created, so release rounds the current angle to the nearest station and assigns it in one frame, and an arrow key moves one station instantly. The wheel never travels further than the hand did.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Driving the rotation from `deltaX` instead of from an angle. A linear delta turns the wheel by the same amount wherever you grab it, so a drag near the left edge feels geared wrong and a drag straight down the middle does nothing at all. Angular input is what makes it feel like a physical wheel.
- Differencing raw `atan2` output. Crossing the ±180° seam gives a delta of about -359° instead of +1°, and the wheel snaps a full turn backwards once per revolution. Every angle difference here goes through `wrapRange(d, -180, 180)`.
- Putting the hub inside the container. Near the hub the pointer's angular change per pixel goes to infinity, so a press within a few pixels of it and a one-pixel jitter spins the wheel a hundred degrees. The radius floor makes that geometrically impossible rather than guarding it after the fact.
- Taking the release velocity from the last `pointermove`. Drag, hold still for half a second, lift, and the wheel flies off at the speed from before the pause, because the last event recorded was the last time the hand moved. A rolling time window measured against `performance.now()` at release decays to zero on its own.
- Snapping after the inertial tween instead of before it. The throw finishes, comes to rest between two stations, and a second tween hops it into place — two eases back to back, and it is instantly recognisable as fake momentum.
- Calling `setPointerCapture` only after the drag threshold is crossed. By then a fast gesture has already left the element, `pointermove` has stopped arriving, and the wheel sticks at the angle it had when the pointer crossed the boundary.
- Handling only `pointerup`. Release outside the window, let the OS claim the gesture, or have the element re-parented mid-drag and no `pointerup` arrives; the wheel stays captured and frozen mid-throw. `pointercancel` and `lostpointercapture` both route to the same idempotent finish, guarded on the stored `pointerId` so the duplicate is a no-op rather than a second throw.
- Letting the click through. A throw ends with a `click` dispatched on whatever card is under the pointer, so spinning the wheel also opens a project. The click is swallowed in the capture phase, once, only when the gesture actually moved.
- Reaching for `InertiaPlugin`. It is a Club GreenSock plugin — not redistributable, and not installable from a public registry — so a component that depends on it fails to build for most consumers. The `v * D / 3` projection reproduces the throw with the free core.
- Re-seeding `initialIndex` on resize. Rotate a phone mid-gesture and the wheel teleports back to its opening station. The seed is guarded by a ref and runs exactly once.

## Notes

- The counter-rotation is deliberately absent: each card is rotated *with* the wheel by `away`, so the whole thing reads as one rigid disc. Cancelling that rotation keeps labels upright but turns it into a row of cards sliding along an arc, which is a different and much weaker effect.
- The snap grid is a multiple of `360 / count`, so a station always lands facing up. The source of this technique snapped to a fixed 10°, which only coincides with item positions when `360 / count` is itself a multiple of 10 — with 7 or 9 items it lands between cards.
- Arrow keys step one station and route through the same settle path, so keyboard and pointer cannot disagree about where the wheel rests.

## Definition of done

Grab anywhere in the box and drag in an arc: the wheel follows your hand around the hub, and a drag near the left or right edge turns it less than the same pixel distance across the top. Fling and release — it keeps going, decelerates, and comes to rest with one card exactly upright, in a single continuous motion with no hop at the end. Drag, hold still for a second, then lift: it settles to the nearest station without throwing. Start a drag, move the pointer off the window, and release outside — the wheel still lands rather than freezing. Release over a card and no click reaches it; tap the same card without moving and the click goes through. Arrow keys step one card at a time.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Rotating Word Hero

The landing page opener: an announcement pill, a two-line headline whose key word cycles through a list ("for Finance / Healthcare / Agentic Interface"), a subcopy paragraph, a CTA row and a "built with" badges row. Each swap slides the old word up through a blur while the next rises from below, and the word slot animates its width so the centred line re-balances smoothly. A dotted rule under the word signals that it changes. `RotatingWord` is exported on its own for headlines laid out differently.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Landing hero whose key word slides and blurs through a list while the line glides to each new width, with CTAs and a stack badges row.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: motion@^12.43.0

## How it works

1. Slot sizing: inside the word slot sits an in-flow, invisible `inline-block` copy of the current word. It gives the slot its line height and baseline, and a ResizeObserver on it reports its border-box inline size. That number becomes the slot's explicit `width`, which has `transition-[width] duration-500 ease-out`, so the rest of the centred line glides instead of jumping. The first measurement replaces `auto` and therefore does not animate.
2. Word swap: the visible word is a `motion.span` keyed by index inside `AnimatePresence initial={false}`, absolutely positioned at the slot's top-left. Enter is `y 45% → 0, opacity 0 → 1, blur 8px → 0`; exit is `y 0 → -45%` with the same fade and blur, 550ms on `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`. Both run at once, so the words cross mid-slot.
3. Rotation clock: one `setInterval` advances the index every `interval` ms (2600 by default). The effect only runs while `running` is true: more than one word, not `paused`, no reduced-motion preference, not hovered, tab visible (`useVisibility`) and slot on screen (`useInView`). Any of these flipping clears the interval, so a hidden tab never queues swaps.
4. Measurement uses ResizeObserver layout sizes, never `getBoundingClientRect`, because the hero is often rendered inside a CSS-scaled preview and a rect would report the scaled width.
5. Accessibility: the animated layers are `aria-hidden`; a `sr-only` span holds the first word, so assistive tech reads one stable headline ("React Design System for Finance Interface") rather than a sentence that mutates every few seconds. Hovering the word pauses it for reading.
6. Layout: the `<section>` is an `@container/hero`; the headline steps from display-4 to display-2 at `@xl` and to the 64px large title at `@4xl`, so a narrow column gets a smaller heading even on a wide window. The optional glow is four blurred token-coloured bars behind the headline, masked off toward the bottom.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `interval = 2600ms`
  Long enough to read a word and the line it completes, short enough that a visitor sees at least two swaps before scrolling.
- `swap = 550ms, y ±45%, blur 8px`
  Under half the slot height keeps both words partly in the slot while they cross, and the blur hides the overlap.
- `width transition = 500ms ease-out`
  Slightly shorter than the swap so the line settles before the incoming word fully sharpens.
- `dot rule = 0.15em × 0.1em tiles, 0.032em dots`
  Em units scale the dotted underline with every headline size step.

## API

```ts
function RotatingWordHero(props: { words: string[]; before?: ReactNode; after?: ReactNode; announcement?: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; actions?: ReactNode; badges?: { label: string; version?: string; icon?: ComponentType }[]; interval?: number; paused?: boolean; glow?: boolean; children?: ReactNode; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function RotatingWord(props: { words: string[]; interval?: number; paused?: boolean; underline?: boolean; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function HeroAnnouncement(props: { tag?: string; href?: string; onClick?: MouseEventHandler; children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
```

- `words: string[]`
  Words cycled in the headline slot. One word renders static.
- `before / after: ReactNode`
  Headline text around the rotating word.
- `interval: number` — default `2600`
  Milliseconds per word.
- `paused: boolean` — default `false`
  Holds the current word.
- `announcement: ReactNode`
  Pill above the headline, usually a `HeroAnnouncement`.
- `description: ReactNode`
  Subcopy under the headline (max 620px).
- `actions: ReactNode`
  CTA row, e.g. a primary and a secondary kit Button.
- `badges: HeroBadgeItem[]` — default `[]`
  `{ label, version?, icon? }` items separated by dots.
- `glow: boolean` — default `true`
  Soft accent light bars behind the headline.
- `children: ReactNode`
  Content below the badges row, e.g. a product shot.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * A word that swaps in place: the outgoing word slides up and blurs out while
 * the next rises from below. An in-flow invisible copy of the current word
 * gives the slot its height and baseline; a ResizeObserver on that copy feeds
 * an explicit width, so the surrounding line glides to the new length instead
 * of jumping. The rotation stops under reduced motion, while hovered, off
 * screen and in a hidden tab.
 */
export function RotatingWord({ words, interval = 2600, paused = false, underline = true, className }: RotatingWordProps) {
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);
  const sizerRef = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);
  const [index, setIndex] = useState(0);
  const [width, setWidth] = useState<number | undefined>(undefined);
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const visible = useVisibility();
  const { inView } = useInView(rootRef);

  const count = words.length;
  const word = words[index % Math.max(count, 1)] ?? "";
  const running = count > 1 && !paused && !reduced && !hovered && visible && inView;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!running) return;
    const id = window.setInterval(() => setIndex((i) => (i + 1) % count), interval);
    return () => window.clearInterval(id);
  }, [running, interval, count]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const sizer = sizerRef.current;
    if (!sizer || typeof ResizeObserver === "undefined") return;
    // Layout size, not getBoundingClientRect: the hero may sit inside a scaled preview.
    const ro = new ResizeObserver((entries) => {
      const box = entries[0]?.borderBoxSize?.[0];
      setWidth(box ? box.inlineSize : sizer.offsetWidth);
    });
    ro.observe(sizer);
    return () => ro.disconnect();
  }, []);

  return (
    <span
      ref={rootRef}
      data-word={word}
      onPointerEnter={() => setHovered(true)}
      onPointerLeave={() => setHovered(false)}
      className={cx(
        "relative inline-block whitespace-nowrap",
        !reduced && "transition-[width] duration-500 ease-out",
        className,
      )}
      style={width === undefined ? undefined : { width }}
    >
      <span className="sr-only">{words[0]}</span>
      <span ref={sizerRef} aria-hidden="true" className="invisible inline-block">
        {word}
      </span>
      <span aria-hidden="true" className="absolute inset-0">
        <AnimatePresence initial={false}>
          <motion.span
            key={`${index}-${word}`}
            className="absolute top-0 left-0 inline-block"
            initial={reduced ? false : { y: "45%", opacity: 0, filter: "blur(8px)" }}
            animate={{ y: "0%", opacity: 1, filter: "blur(0px)" }}
            exit={reduced ? { opacity: 0, transition: { duration: 0 } } : { y: "-45%", opacity: 0, filter: "blur(8px)" }}
            transition={{ duration: 0.55, ease: EASE_OUT }}
          >
            {word}
          </motion.span>
        </AnimatePresence>
      </span>
      {underline ? (
        <span
          aria-hidden="true"
          className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-x-0 -bottom-[0.08em] h-[0.1em] bg-[radial-gradient(circle,currentColor_0.032em,transparent_0.042em)] bg-size-[0.15em_0.1em] bg-repeat-x text-text-placeholder opacity-70"
        />
      ) : null}
    </span>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The interval is cleared whenever the rotation stops or the hero unmounts; the ResizeObserver is disconnected on unmount. useInView and useVisibility unsubscribe their shared observers.

**Reduced motion.** The rotation stops entirely and the headline shows its current word. The width transition is removed, and the word renders without enter/exit motion.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Measuring an inline `<span>`: ResizeObserver reports 0x0 for non-replaced inline elements. The sizer must be `inline-block`.
- Letting the slot width follow its content: CSS cannot transition `width: auto`, so the line snaps. Feed a measured pixel width instead.
- Leaving the interval running in a background tab: when the tab returns, the browser fires the backlog and the word flickers through several swaps.
- Putting `aria-live` on the word. Screen readers then announce a new word every 2.6 seconds; keep the animated part hidden and expose one stable word.

## Notes

- Pass `paused` to hold the word, e.g. while a modal is open over the hero.
- The `before` slot accepts any node; the demo wraps "React Design System" in a block span to force the two-line split.
- `HeroAnnouncement` renders an anchor when given `href`, otherwise a static pill.

## Definition of done

The headline reads "React Design System / for Finance Interface" with a dotted rule under Finance. About every 2.6s the word slides up and blurs out while the next (Healthcare, Agentic, …) rises in, and "Interface" glides to its new position. Hovering the word pauses it. With reduced motion the word never changes. Light and dark both show the pill, CTAs and four badges.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Row Actions

The action cluster from the BoardUI finance table rows: a 32px bordered kebab that opens the kit Dropdown with Edit, Duplicate and Delete. Delete never fires straight away; it opens the kit AlertDialog with a row-specific title and focus on Cancel. With inline, delete and edit also appear as 32px icon buttons in front of the kebab, as in the reference, and fold into the kebab on phones. The component owns no row data: it calls onEdit, onDuplicate and onDelete and the table updates itself.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Kebab menu at the end of a table row with Edit, Duplicate and a red Delete that asks first through the kit AlertDialog.

- Category: overlay
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. The kebab is the kit DropdownTrigger styled with the exported buttonStyles (secondary, small, icon-only), so it matches the inline kit Buttons beside it; while the menu is open it keeps the pressed background and border.
2. The menu is the kit Dropdown (non-modal React Aria popover with outside-press dismissal) narrowed to w-48 with p-1.5 and denser px-2 py-1.5 rows; only actions with a handler are rendered, and Delete sits under a divider in text-error-primary with a tertiary-error hover.
3. Choosing a row first focuses the kebab, then closes the panel and runs the action. Any dialog opened next (the caller's edit form, the confirm) therefore records the kebab as its restore target instead of a menu row that is about to unmount.
4. Delete, from the menu or the inline trash button, only sets confirmOpen. The kit AlertDialog (role=alertdialog, no backdrop dismissal, focus on Cancel) calls onDelete on confirm, and an async onDelete keeps it open with a busy Delete button until the promise settles.
5. Inline buttons carry max-sm:hidden, so below 640px the row keeps a single kebab that still holds every action.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `button size = 32px (kit Button small icon-only), gap-2`
  Matches the finance table's trash / edit / kebab squares and keeps a comfortable touch target.
- `menu width = w-48, p-1.5`
  Three short verbs do not need the 266px kit default; the narrow panel stays inside the row on phones.
- `placement = 'bottom end', offset 4`
  The kebab is the last cell, so the panel grows leftwards into the table instead of off the edge.
- `danger row = text-error-primary, bg-background-tertiary-error on hover`
  Marks the destructive verb in both themes before the confirm even appears.

## API

```ts
export function RowActions({ name, onEdit, onDuplicate, onDelete, inline, confirmTitle, confirmDescription, confirmLabel, placement, className }: RowActionsProps): JSX.Element
```

- `name: string`
  Row name used in the kebab, inline and dialog labels.
- `onEdit: () => void`
  Adds Edit to the menu (and the inline pencil).
- `onDuplicate: () => void`
  Adds Duplicate to the menu.
- `onDelete: () => void | Promise<unknown>`
  Adds Delete and runs after confirmation; a promise keeps the dialog busy.
- `inline: boolean` — default `false`
  Show delete and edit as icon buttons before the kebab from 640px up.
- `confirmTitle: ReactNode` — default ``Delete ${name}?``
  Confirm dialog title.
- `confirmDescription: ReactNode`
  Confirm dialog body; defaults to a generic cannot-undo line.
- `confirmLabel: ReactNode` — default `'Delete'`
  Label of the danger button.
- `placement: 'bottom end' | 'bottom start' | 'top end' | 'top start'` — default `'bottom end'`
  Menu placement relative to the kebab.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function RowActions({
  name,
  onEdit,
  onDuplicate,
  onDelete,
  inline = false,
  confirmTitle,
  confirmDescription,
  confirmLabel = 'Delete',
  placement = 'bottom end',
  className,
}: RowActionsProps) {
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const [menuOpen, setMenuOpen] = useState(false);
  const [confirmOpen, setConfirmOpen] = useState(false);

  // Park focus on the kebab before the panel unmounts: whatever opens next
  // (the caller's edit form, the confirm dialog) then records the kebab as
  // the element to restore focus to, instead of a detached menu row.
  const run = (action: (() => void) | undefined) => {
    rootRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-row-actions-trigger]')?.focus();
    setMenuOpen(false);
    action?.();
  };
  const askDelete = () => setConfirmOpen(true);
  const hasMenuAbove = Boolean(onEdit || onDuplicate);

  return (
    <div ref={rootRef} className={cx('inline-flex items-center gap-2', className)}>
      {inline && onDelete ? (
        <Button
          variant="secondary"
          size="small"
          iconOnly
          leadingIcon={RiDeleteBinLine}
          aria-label={`Delete ${name}`}
          onClick={askDelete}
          className="max-sm:hidden"
        />
      ) : null}
      {inline && onEdit ? (
        <Button
          variant="secondary"
          size="small"
          iconOnly
          leadingIcon={RiPencilLine}
          aria-label={`Edit ${name}`}
          onClick={onEdit}
          className="max-sm:hidden"
        />
      ) : null}

      <Dropdown isOpen={menuOpen} onOpenChange={setMenuOpen}>
        <DropdownTrigger data-row-actions-trigger aria-label={`Actions for ${name}`} className={cx(KEBAB, menuOpen && KEBAB_OPEN)}>
          <RiMore2Fill aria-hidden className={buttonStyles.icon.small} />
        </DropdownTrigger>
        <DropdownPopover aria-label={`Actions for ${name}`} placement={placement} className="w-48 p-1.5" dialogClassName="gap-0.5">
          {onEdit ? (
            <DropdownItem onSelect={() => run(onEdit)} className="px-2 py-1.5">
              <ItemLabel icon={RiPencilLine}>Edit</ItemLabel>
            </DropdownItem>
          ) : null}
          {onDuplicate ? (
            <DropdownItem onSelect={() => run(onDuplicate)} className="px-2 py-1.5">
              <ItemLabel icon={RiFileCopyLine}>Duplicate</ItemLabel>
            </DropdownItem>
          ) : null}
          {onDelete ? (
            <>
              {hasMenuAbove ? <DropdownDivider className="-mx-1.5 my-1" /> : null}
              <DropdownItem onSelect={() => run(askDelete)} className={cx('px-2 py-1.5', DANGER_ITEM)}>
                <ItemLabel icon={RiDeleteBinLine} danger>
                  Delete
                </ItemLabel>
              </DropdownItem>
            </>
          ) : null}
        </DropdownPopover>
      </Dropdown>

      {onDelete ? (
        <AlertDialog
          isOpen={confirmOpen}
          onOpenChange={setConfirmOpen}
          icon={RiDeleteBinLine}
          title={confirmTitle ?? `Delete ${name}?`}
          description={confirmDescription ?? 'This row will be removed from the table. You can’t undo this.'}
          confirmLabel={confirmLabel}
          onConfirm={onDelete}
        />
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers or listeners of its own. The kit Dropdown removes its outside-press listener on close and unmount, and the modal releases its scroll lock when it unmounts.

**Reduced motion.** The kit Dropdown drops its fade, scale and blur under reduced motion and the kit AlertDialog keeps only its fade; RowActions adds no motion of its own.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Deleting the row unmounts the focused controls and the open dialog with it; move focus to a neighbouring row (the demo uses its kebab) or focus drops to <body>.
- Do not pass a ref to DropdownTrigger: it would replace the Dropdown's own trigger ref and break outside-press and toggle handling. RowActions finds the kebab through data-row-actions-trigger instead.
- Give every row a distinct name; the labels ("Actions for Ana Carter", "Delete Ana Carter?") are the only thing that tells repeated buttons apart.

## Notes

- Leave out onDuplicate (or onEdit) to drop that row from the menu; without onDelete there is no divider and no dialog.
- Pass confirmDescription with the row's details ("The $640 payment from Jun 12 ...") so the confirm says exactly what goes away.

## Definition of done

Opening "Actions for Mia Chen" shows Edit, Duplicate and Delete; Duplicate inserts "Mia Chen (copy)" below it and the count reads 6 payments; Delete asks "Delete Mia Chen?" with focus on Cancel, Cancel keeps the row, Delete removes it, the count drops and focus lands on the next row's kebab.

# Build: Preloader That Cannot Hang

Every hand-rolled preloader eventually ships the same bug: a signal that never arrives — a 404 on a font, a decode that fails on iOS, an image behind a dead CDN — and the site is a permanent opaque rectangle nobody can see through or tab past. This inverts the contract. A hard ceiling guarantees the page is visible by a fixed time and the load signal only ever makes it sooner; a floor stops a warm cache turning the overlay into a two-frame flash; a session flag keeps it an introduction rather than a toll booth.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

An intro overlay with a hard ceiling, a minimum visible time and a once-per-session flag, so a stalled load cannot trap the page.

- Category: transition
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. A three-state phase machine — `holding`, `leaving`, `gone` — drives the render. It starts at `holding` on both server and client so the markup matches, and the session check runs in a `useLayoutEffect`, before paint, so a returning visitor never sees a single frame of the overlay.
2. THE CEILING: `setTimeout(reveal, ceilingMs)` is armed in an effect on mount, before anything subscribes to a load signal, and nothing clears it except a successful reveal or unmount. This is not a fallback — it is the actual guarantee, and the load signal is the optimisation.
3. THE FLOOR: when the signal does arrive, the remaining hold is `Math.max(0, floorMs - (performance.now() - started))` and the reveal is deferred by that much. Measured from mount, not from the signal, so the floor overlaps the load instead of being added to it.
4. The signal is `ready` when the prop is passed, otherwise the browser's own: `document.readyState === "complete"` is checked first and only then is a one-shot `load` listener attached, because if the document has already finished the event has been and gone and a listener alone would wait forever.
5. ONCE: on reveal, `sessionStorage[sessionKey] = "1"`, wrapped in try/catch because `setItem` throws in Safari private browsing and a preloader is not worth taking the page down for. Both the read and the write are guarded.
6. `reveal()` guards on a ref, not on state, so the ceiling and the floor firing in the same tick still reveal exactly once. It sets `leaving` — a CSS opacity transition on `[data-leaving="true"]` — and schedules the actual removal `fadeMs` later, so the node is never pulled out of the tree mid-transition. `onDone` fires from that same timer, after the overlay is gone.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `ceilingMs = 4000`
  The reveal deadline. Long enough that a genuinely slow first paint on a cold 3G connection is not cut off mid-load, short enough that a user staring at a broken overlay gives up after it rather than before. Past ~6s people reload, which restarts the same stall.
- `floorMs = 700`
  Minimum visible time. On a warm cache the signal resolves in about 40ms; without a floor the overlay appears and vanishes inside two frames, which reads as a rendering fault rather than an introduction. Below ~400ms the fade has no room to be perceived as deliberate.
- `fadeMs = 420`
  Fade-out duration, passed to CSS as `--k-safe-fade` and used as the removal delay so the two can never disagree. Long enough that the page underneath is already composited and visible through the fade; past ~700ms the user is looking at content they cannot yet click.
- `fade easing = cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`
  Heavily front-loaded, so most of the opacity is gone in the first third and the perceived wait is shorter than the measured one. A linear fade of the same length feels about twice as long.
- `scan bar = 1.4s cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1) infinite`
  A determinate progress bar would be a lie — nothing here knows a byte count. This is an indeterminate scan whose cycle is slow enough not to read as urgency and fast enough to prove the page is not frozen. The in-out curve keeps the ends from clipping at the container edges.
- `sessionKey = 'k-preloader'`
  Session, not local, storage. Local storage would mean the introduction plays once ever, so a returning visitor months later gets no reveal and QA can never see it again without clearing site data.

## API

```ts
function SafePreloader(props: { children?: ReactNode; ready?: boolean; ceilingMs?: number; floorMs?: number; fadeMs?: number; sessionKey?: string; once?: boolean; onDone?: () => void; position?: 'fixed' | 'absolute'; className?: string }): JSX.Element | null
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  Overlay content. Defaults to a label and an indeterminate scan bar.
- `ready: boolean`
  The load signal. Leave undefined to use the browser's own `load` event and `readyState`.
- `ceilingMs: number` — default `4000`
  Hard ceiling. The reveal happens by this time whether or not the signal ever arrives.
- `floorMs: number` — default `700`
  Minimum time the overlay stays up, measured from mount.
- `fadeMs: number` — default `420`
  Fade-out duration in ms. Also the delay before the node is removed.
- `sessionKey: string` — default `'k-preloader'`
  sessionStorage key used by the once-per-session gate.
- `once: boolean` — default `true`
  Set false to replay on every load, for development.
- `onDone: () => void`
  Fires after the overlay has finished leaving and unmounted.
- `position: 'fixed' | 'absolute'` — default `'fixed'`
  Absolute lets the overlay be scoped to a container instead of the viewport.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the overlay via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const reveal = useCallback(() => {
  if (revealed.current) return;
  revealed.current = true;
  clearTimers();
  if (once) markShown(sessionKey);
  setPhase('leaving');
  // The node is removed only after the fade has actually run, so nothing is
  // pulled out of the tree mid-transition.
  timers.current.push(
    setTimeout(
      () => {
        setPhase('gone');
        done.current?.();
      },
      reduced ? 0 : fadeMs,
    ),
  );
}, [clearTimers, fadeMs, once, reduced, sessionKey]);

useLayoutEffect(() => {
  if (once && wasShown(sessionKey)) {
    revealed.current = true;
    setPhase('gone');
    return;
  }
  started.current = performance.now();
}, [once, sessionKey]);

// THE CEILING. Armed on mount, before any load signal is subscribed to, and
// never cancelled by anything except a successful reveal. If the signal
// never comes, this is what saves the page.
useEffect(() => {
  if (revealed.current) return;
  const id = setTimeout(reveal, ceilingMs);
  timers.current.push(id);
  return () => clearTimeout(id);
}, [ceilingMs, reveal]);

// THE FLOOR. When the signal arrives, wait out whatever is left of the
// minimum so a warm cache does not produce a two-frame black flash.
useEffect(() => {
  if (revealed.current) return;

  const settle = () => {
    const elapsed = performance.now() - started.current;
    const remaining = Math.max(0, (reduced ? 0 : floorMs) - elapsed);
    const id = setTimeout(reveal, remaining);
    timers.current.push(id);
  };

  if (ready !== undefined) {
    if (ready) settle();
    return;
  }

  // No `ready` prop: use the browser's own signal. If the document has
  // already finished loading, the event has been and gone — check first.
  if (document.readyState === 'complete') {
    settle();
    return;
  }
  window.addEventListener('load', settle, { once: true });
  return () => window.removeEventListener('load', settle);
}, [floorMs, ready, reduced, reveal]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Every timeout is pushed into a ref array and cleared on unmount, the ceiling effect clears its own id, and the one-shot `load` listener is removed by its effect. Because the removal timer is cleared, `setPhase` cannot run on a dead component and `onDone` cannot fire for a page that has already gone. No rAF, no observers, no global state beyond the session flag.

**Reduced motion.** The overlay still appears and the ceiling still applies — withholding content is a behaviour, not an animation, so it is not skipped. What goes away is the motion: the floor collapses to 0 so nothing is held longer than it must be, the removal delay drops to 0 and the CSS transition to 1ms, and the scanning bar becomes a static full-width rule via `animation: none; transform: scaleX(1)` rather than a pulsing one. The result is a brief still plate, not a zero-duration version of the animated one.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Having no ceiling at all. One 404 on a font or a decode that fails only on iOS, and the overlay stays up forever: the content is not visible, not scrollable, and not reachable by keyboard, and it happens to a fraction of users you will never hear from.
- Clearing the ceiling when the load signal is subscribed to, or when it fires. Whatever the signal hands off to — a floor timer, a promise chain, a decode — can itself stall, and the one thing that guaranteed a reveal has already been thrown away.
- Attaching a `load` listener without checking `document.readyState` first. On a warm cache or after a client-side navigation the event has already fired, so the listener never runs; the ceiling silently does all the work and you only discover it the day someone shortens the ceiling.
- Shipping without a floor. The overlay appears and vanishes inside two frames on a fast connection, producing a black flash on every load that reads as a broken paint and is nearly impossible to reproduce on a throttled dev machine.
- Starting the floor clock when the signal arrives instead of at mount. The floor is then added to the load time rather than overlapping it, so a 2s load becomes a 2.7s hold for no benefit.
- Using state for the reveal-once guard. The ceiling and the floor can both fire before React re-renders, so `reveal` runs twice and the second call re-arms the fade on a node that is already leaving. A ref flips synchronously and cannot be raced.
- Unmounting the overlay in the same commit that starts the fade. The node leaves the tree before the transition can run a single frame, so the overlay simply disappears and the fade you wrote never happens.
- Reading `sessionStorage` in `useEffect` instead of `useLayoutEffect`. The overlay gets one painted frame before the effect runs, so a returning visitor sees a flash of it on every single navigation.
- Initialising state from `sessionStorage` during render. The server has no session storage, so it renders `holding` while the client renders `gone`, and React logs a hydration mismatch and re-renders the tree.
- Calling `sessionStorage.setItem` unguarded. It throws in Safari private browsing, and an unhandled throw inside the reveal path leaves the overlay up permanently — the exact failure the component exists to prevent.
- Replaying it on every visit. A preloader is an introduction; on the fourth arrival in the same session it is a toll booth, and the fix is one flag rather than a shorter animation.
- Leaving timers pending on unmount. The removal timer fires after the route has changed, so `setPhase` runs on a dead component and `onDone` fires for a page that is no longer mounted.

## Notes

- `position` defaults to `fixed` for real page use and can be switched to `absolute` so the overlay can be demonstrated, or used, inside a bounded container.
- The overlay is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`, so a screen reader announces the loading state once rather than reading a decorative bar, and the announcement is not interrupted by the reveal.
- `once={false}` exists for development and for the demo. In production the default keeps the overlay to one appearance per tab session.

## Definition of done

Simulate a signal that never arrives and the page is nonetheless visible and interactive at the ceiling. Reload with a warm cache and the overlay is visible for at least the floor — never a single-frame flash. Reload again in the same tab and no overlay is painted at all, not even one frame. Watch the reveal and the overlay fades rather than vanishing, with the content already composited underneath. Navigate away mid-hold and no state update warning appears and `onDone` never fires. With reduced motion on, the plate appears static and leaves immediately.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Sankey Chart Card

A Sankey diagram in the BoardUI chart card shell. The layout is computed in the component: columns by link depth, nodes stacked to one shared scale, ribbons ordered so they only cross where the data does. Each ribbon takes its source node's colour, sources are labelled with name and value on the left, sinks with their share on the right. Hovering or focusing a node, or hovering a ribbon, lights the whole path through it, dims everything else and swaps the headline for that node or flow.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Source-to-sink flows as tinted SVG ribbons in a dashboard card: hover a node or ribbon to isolate its path while the headline follows.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Links reference nodes by name or index. Unknown references, self-links and non-positive values are dropped. Depths are relaxed across the links (a node sits one column right of its deepest source), with the passes capped at the node count so a cycle cannot loop forever.
2. A node's value is the larger of its inflow and outflow. Each column needs `(height - 14px * (n - 1)) / sum` px per unit; the smallest of those is used for every column, so equal hours are equal heights everywhere. Each column is then centred vertically.
3. Ribbons leave a source stacked in the vertical order of their targets and arrive at a target stacked in the order of their sources. Each is a filled path: two cubic Béziers whose control points sit at the horizontal midpoint, so the band keeps its thickness at both ends and eases between them.
4. The chart width comes from `useResizeObserver`. The label gutters are `clamp(14% of width, 72, 96)` on the left and `clamp(26%, 104, 168)` on the right. Below 440px the labels drop to 12px names and the sink labels stack the share under the name.
5. Hover is `{ kind: "node" | "link", index }`. `litPath` walks upstream and downstream from the node (or from the ribbon's two ends), collecting links and nodes. Lit ribbons go to 0.65 fill-opacity, the rest to 0.1 (0.4 at rest), and unlit nodes and labels fade over 200ms.
6. The labels are absolutely positioned `<button>`s carrying a full description ("Focus: 32h, 37% of total. to Browsing 9h, …"), so keyboard and screen-reader users get every flow. Focus lights the same path as hover.
7. A clipPath rect sweeps from the first column to the right edge over 800ms (ease-out cubic) on mount and on every period change. `useSweep` resets to 0 during render when the key changes, so no frame shows the old ribbons at full width.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `NODE_W = 12px, rx 3`
  Wide enough to read as a bar and to hover, narrow enough that the ribbons carry the picture.
- `NODE_GAP = 14px`
  At the default 340px height with seven sinks, this leaves 256px for 86h (about 3px per hour) and room for a two-line label beside a 7h node.
- `RIBBON = rest 0.4, lit 0.65, dim 0.1 fill-opacity`
  At rest overlaps stay readable; on hover the lit path stands out and the rest almost disappears without vanishing.
- `SWEEP_MS = 800ms ease-out cubic`
  The sweep reads as flow from sources to sinks. A new period redraws instead of morphing, because node order and counts can change between ranges.
- `COMPACT_W = 440px`
  Below it, "Everything else · 13%" no longer fits the right gutter on one line, so the share moves under a 12px name.
- `chartHeight = 340px`
  Matches the preview's proportion with seven sinks.

## API

```ts
function SankeyChartCard(props: { title?: string; ranges?: FlowRange[]; nodes?: FlowNode[]; links?: FlowLink[]; delta?: number; range?: string; defaultRange?: string; onRangeChange?: (id: string) => void; formatValue?: (value: number) => string; sourceCaption?: string; targetCaption?: string; chartHeight?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type FlowNode = { name: string; color?: ChartColor }
type FlowLink = { source: string | number; target: string | number; value: number }
```

- `title: string` — default `"Tracked time"`
  Header label while nothing is hovered; also the card's accessible name.
- `ranges: FlowRange[]` — default `TRACKED_TIME_RANGES`
  Periods with their own nodes, links and optional delta/headline. Two or more show the period select.
- `nodes: FlowNode[]`
  Static nodes; used with `links` instead of `ranges`.
- `links: FlowLink[]`
  Static links `{ source, target, value }`, by node name or index.
- `delta: number`
  Headline chip percentage for static data.
- `range: string`
  Controlled period id.
- `defaultRange: string` — default `first range id`
  Initial period when uncontrolled.
- `onRangeChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called when the period select changes.
- `formatValue: (value: number) => string` — default `whole hours, e.g. "86h"`
  Formats the headline, the source labels and the screen-reader descriptions.
- `sourceCaption: string` — default `"Tracked time"`
  Caption under the left column.
- `targetCaption: string` — default `"Share of tracked time"`
  Caption under the right column.
- `chartHeight: number` — default `340`
  Chart height in px.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card section.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * Columns come from link depth (a node sits one column right of its deepest
 * source). Every column is stacked to the same px-per-unit scale, the
 * tightest one any column allows, then centred. Ribbons leave a node in the
 * vertical order of their targets and arrive in the order of their sources,
 * so they only cross where the data makes them.
 */
function layoutSankey(
  nodesIn: readonly FlowNode[],
  linksIn: readonly FlowLink[],
  box: { width: number; height: number; left: number; right: number },
): Layout {
  const byName = new Map(nodesIn.map((node, index) => [node.name, index] as const));
  const resolve = (ref: string | number) =>
    typeof ref === "number" ? (ref >= 0 && ref < nodesIn.length ? ref : -1) : (byName.get(ref) ?? -1);
  const links = linksIn
    .map((link) => ({ source: resolve(link.source), target: resolve(link.target), value: link.value }))
    .filter((link) => link.source >= 0 && link.target >= 0 && link.source !== link.target && link.value > 0);

  const count = nodesIn.length;
  const depth = new Array<number>(count).fill(0);
  // Relax depths; capping the passes at the node count keeps a cycle from looping forever.
  for (let pass = 0; pass < count; pass++) {
    let changed = false;
    for (const link of links) {
      const next = (depth[link.source] ?? 0) + 1;
      if (next > (depth[link.target] ?? 0) && next < count) {
        depth[link.target] = next;
        changed = true;
      }
    }
    if (!changed) break;
  }
  const maxDepth = Math.max(0, ...depth);

  const inSum = new Array<number>(count).fill(0);
  const outSum = new Array<number>(count).fill(0);
  for (const link of links) {
    outSum[link.source] = (outSum[link.source] ?? 0) + link.value;
    inSum[link.target] = (inSum[link.target] ?? 0) + link.value;
  }
  const values = nodesIn.map((_, i) => Math.max(inSum[i] ?? 0, outSum[i] ?? 0));

  const columns: number[][] = Array.from({ length: maxDepth + 1 }, () => []);
  depth.forEach((d, i) => columns[d]?.push(i));

  let scale = Infinity;
  for (const column of columns) {
    const sum = column.reduce((acc, i) => acc + (values[i] ?? 0), 0);
    if (sum > 0) scale = Math.min(scale, (box.height - NODE_GAP * (column.length - 1)) / sum);
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(scale) || scale < 0) scale = 0;

  const span = Math.max(0, box.width - box.left - box.right - NODE_W);
  let firstOrdinal = 0;
  const nodes: LaidNode[] = nodesIn.map((node, index) => {
    const d = depth[index] ?? 0;
    const colorKey = node.color ?? (d === 0 ? chartColorAt(firstOrdinal++) : null);
    return {
      index,
      name: node.name,
      colorKey,
      fill: colorKey ? CHART_COLORS[colorKey].fill : NEUTRAL_FILL,
      depth: d,
      value: values[index] ?? 0,
      x: box.left + (maxDepth > 0 ? (d / maxDepth) * span : 0),
      y0: 0,
      y1: 0,
    };
  });

  for (const column of columns) {
    const used =
      column.reduce((acc, i) => acc + (values[i] ?? 0) * scale, 0) + NODE_GAP * Math.max(0, column.length - 1);
    let y = (box.height - used) / 2;
    for (const i of column) {
      const node = nodes[i];
      if (!node) continue;
      node.y0 = y;
      node.y1 = y + node.value * scale;
      y = node.y1 + NODE_GAP;
    }
  }

  const top = (i: number) => nodes[i]?.y0 ?? 0;
  const outOffset = nodes.map((node) => node.y0);
  const inOffset = nodes.map((node) => node.y0);
  const sy = new Array<number>(links.length).fill(0);
  const ty = new Array<number>(links.length).fill(0);
  const order = links.map((_, i) => i);
  for (const i of [...order].sort((a, b) => top(links[a]!.target) - top(links[b]!.target) || a - b)) {
    const link = links[i]!;
    sy[i] = outOffset[link.source] ?? 0;
    outOffset[link.source] = sy[i]! + link.value * scale;
  }
  for (const i of [...order].sort((a, b) => top(links[a]!.source) - top(links[b]!.source) || a - b)) {
    const link = links[i]!;
    ty[i] = inOffset[link.target] ?? 0;
    inOffset[link.target] = ty[i]! + link.value * scale;
  }

  const laidLinks: LaidLink[] = links.map((link, index) => {
    const from = nodes[link.source]!;
    const to = nodes[link.target]!;
    const h = link.value * scale;
    const x0 = r2(from.x + NODE_W);
    const x1 = r2(to.x);
    const xm = r2((x0 + x1) / 2);
    const s0 = r2(sy[index] ?? 0);
    const s1 = r2((sy[index] ?? 0) + h);
    const t0 = r2(ty[index] ?? 0);
    const t1 = r2((ty[index] ?? 0) + h);
    return {
      index,
      source: link.source,
      target: link.target,
      value: link.value,
      fill: from.fill,
      d: `M${x0} ${s0}C${xm} ${s0} ${xm} ${t0} ${x1} ${t0}V${t1}C${xm} ${t1} ${xm} ${s1} ${x0} ${s1}Z`,
    };
  });

  const total = nodes.filter((node) => node.depth === 0).reduce((acc, node) => acc + node.value, 0);
  return { nodes, links: laidLinks, maxDepth, total };
}

/** Everything upstream and downstream of the hovered node, or of the hovered ribbon's ends. */
function litPath(hover: Hover, layout: Layout) {
  if (!hover) return null;
  const nodes = new Set<number>();
  const links = new Set<number>();
  const walk = (start: number, dir: "up" | "down") => {
    const queue = [start];
    while (queue.length) {
      const at = queue.shift()!;
      for (const link of layout.links) {
        const from = dir === "down" ? link.source : link.target;
        const to = dir === "down" ? link.target : link.source;
        if (from !== at || links.has(link.index)) continue;
        links.add(link.index);
        nodes.add(to);
        queue.push(to);
      }
    }
  };
  if (hover.kind === "node") {
    nodes.add(hover.index);
    walk(hover.index, "up");
    walk(hover.index, "down");
  } else {
    const link = layout.links[hover.index];
    if (!link) return null;
    links.add(link.index);
    nodes.add(link.source).add(link.target);
    walk(link.source, "up");
    walk(link.target, "down");
  }
  return { nodes, links };
}

/** 0 to 1 eased progress that restarts whenever `key` changes; 1 throughout when disabled. */
function useSweep(key: string, disabled: boolean) {
  const [progress, setProgress] = useState(0);
  const [lastKey, setLastKey] = useState(key);
  if (lastKey !== key) {
    setLastKey(key);
    setProgress(0);
  }
  useEffect(() => {
    if (disabled) return;
    const start = performance.now();
    let raf = 0;
    const tick = (now: number) => {
      // rAF's timestamp is the frame's start, which can precede the effect's
      // performance.now() after a long commit; unclamped, t < 0 gives a
      // negative clip width.
      const t = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (now - start) / SWEEP_MS));
      setProgress(easeOutCubic(t));
      if (t < 1) raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    };
    raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    return () => cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
  }, [key, disabled]);
  return disabled ? 1 : progress;
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The sweep's and the count-up's animation frames are cancelled on every restart and on unmount. `useResizeObserver` unobserves the chart box on unmount.

**Reduced motion.** `useSweep` is disabled, so the ribbons are drawn in full at once on mount and on a period change. The headline count runs over 1ms, and the opacity transitions and number fade are removed with `motion-reduce:` variants.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Stroking a centre line with `stroke-width` for ribbons. The stroke keeps its width perpendicular to the curve, so on a slope the band visibly thins and the ends no longer match the node slices. Filled ribbons keep exact heights at both ends.
- Scaling each column to fill the height on its own. A column with fewer nodes would get a bigger px-per-unit than its neighbours, and ribbons would change thickness between columns.
- Sorting a node's outgoing ribbons by value instead of by target position. Ribbons then cross right next to the node and the diagram turns to noise.
- Leaving the old ribbons visible for a frame when the period changes. `useSweep` resets its progress during render, not in an effect.

## Notes

- Pass `nodes` and `links` for one static data set (no period select), or `ranges` for a select. `TRACKED_TIME_RANGES`, `FlowNode`, `FlowLink` and `FlowRange` are exported.
- More than two columns work: middle nodes are labelled on their right with their share of the total. Labels of very small neighbouring nodes can overlap; raise `chartHeight` for dense columns.
- The frame, header and period select come from `funnel-chart-card-shell`.

## Definition of done

The card reads "Tracked time" and "86h" with a "This week" select. Sources Focus 32h (emerald), Meetings 18h (purple), Breaks 12h (yellow), Admin 14h (blue) and Learning 10h (pink) sit on the left. On the right are grey sinks Browsing · 22%, Writing · 18%, Messaging · 13%, Productivity · 12%, Email · 8%, Video calls · 14% and Everything else · 13%. Hovering Focus dims the other sources' ribbons and the header shows "Focus", "32h" and "37% of total". Hovering a ribbon shows e.g. "Focus → Browsing". Choosing "Last week" redraws the ribbons with a sweep, and the headline becomes 79h.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
