# Build: Pixels-Per-Second Marquee

A looping strip of content whose speed is expressed in pixels per second and whose duration is derived from it, never the other way round. A fixed `duration` means a 900px strip crawls while a 4000px strip sprints, so two marquees on the same page visibly disagree about how fast scrolling is — and adding one word to either changes its speed. The loop distance is exactly one content set plus its gap, so the wrap frame is pixel-identical to the frame before it and the seam is invisible.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A marquee whose duration is derived from measured width and a px/second speed, so every strip moves at the same rate.

- Category: text
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. A `ResizeObserver` on the first content copy gives `copyWidth`; the repeating unit is `setWidth = copyWidth + gap`, because the gap that follows a copy is part of the unit — omit it and the rhythm at the seam is one gap tighter than everywhere else, which reads as a stutter once per cycle.
2. Duration is `setWidth / speed` — seconds = px / (px per second). Every marquee on the site then moves at the same rate regardless of how much content is in it.
3. The number of copies is `Math.max(2, Math.ceil(rootWidth / setWidth) + 1)`, from a second `ResizeObserver` on the container. The `+1` covers the gap that the translation itself opens up; with the exact ceiling a blank wedge appears at the right edge on the last frame of every cycle.
4. The tween is `gsap.fromTo(track, { x: 0 }, { x: -setWidth, duration, ease: "none", repeat: -1 })`. `ease: "none"` is mandatory — any easing makes the strip accelerate and decelerate once per cycle, which turns the seam into a visible pulse.
5. Pausing lives in a *separate* effect that calls `tween.paused(!(visible && inView))`, driven by `useVisibility` (tab hidden) and `useInView` (scrolled away). Rebuilding the tween on a visibility flip would snap the strip back to x = 0.
6. Hover ramps the timeScale rather than toggling paused: `gsap.to(tween, { timeScale: 0 | 1, duration: 0.35, overwrite: true })`. The tween object is itself a valid GSAP target, so the strip glides to a stop instead of stopping dead.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `SPEED = 60`
  Pixels per second. Around 60px/s a 12px word takes a fifth of a second to cross its own width — readable while moving. Past ~120px/s the copy is decorative texture; below ~30px/s viewers assume it is stuck.
- `GAP = 48`
  Pixels between items and between the last item and the next copy. It must be identical in both places or the seam is visibly a different rhythm from the interior. Below ~24px adjacent items read as one phrase.
- `HOVER_RAMP = 0.35`
  Seconds to ramp `timeScale` between 1 and 0. Zero (a hard pause) reads as a broken animation; past ~0.6s the strip keeps drifting long enough that a user trying to read an item has to chase it.
- `copies = max(2, ceil(rootWidth / setWidth) + 1)`
  The floor of 2 covers content wider than the container, where the ceiling alone yields 1 and there is nothing to wrap into. The `+1` covers the width the translation itself vacates.

## API

```ts
function SeamlessMarquee(props: { children: ReactNode; speed?: number; direction?: 'left' | 'right'; gap?: number; pauseOnHover?: boolean; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  One content set. Cloned as many times as the container width requires.
- `speed: number` — default `60`
  Pixels per second. Identical for every marquee whatever its width.
- `direction: 'left' | 'right'` — default `'left'`
  Travel direction.
- `gap: number` — default `48`
  Pixels between items and between copies.
- `pauseOnHover: boolean` — default `true`
  Ramp `timeScale` to 0 on pointer enter and back to 1 on leave.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the clipping container via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const SPEED = 60;
const GAP = 48;
const HOVER_RAMP = 0.35;

export function SeamlessMarquee({
  children,
  speed = SPEED,
  direction = 'left',
  gap = GAP,
  pauseOnHover = true,
  className,
}: SeamlessMarqueeProps) {
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const track = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const copy = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const tween = useRef<gsap.core.Tween | null>(null);

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const visible = useVisibility();
  const { inView } = useInView(root);
  const { width: rootWidth } = useResizeObserver(root);
  const { width: copyWidth } = useResizeObserver(copy);

  // The loop distance is one copy *plus* the gap that follows it — the gap is
  // part of the repeating unit. Leave it out and the rhythm of the seam is one
  // gap tighter than the rhythm everywhere else, which reads as a stutter.
  const setWidth = copyWidth + gap;
  const measured = copyWidth > 0;
  const copies =
    reduced || !measured ? 1 : Math.max(2, Math.ceil(rootWidth / setWidth) + 1);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = track.current;
    if (!el || reduced || !measured) return;

    const duration = setWidth / speed;
    const t = gsap.fromTo(
      el,
      { x: direction === 'left' ? 0 : -setWidth },
      {
        x: direction === 'left' ? -setWidth : 0,
        duration,
        ease: 'none',
        repeat: -1,
      },
    );
    tween.current = t;

    return () => {
      tween.current = null;
      // Kill the hover timeScale tweens too — they target the tween object
      // itself, so killTweensOf(el) would not reach them.
      gsap.killTweensOf(t);
      t.kill();
      gsap.set(el, { clearProps: 'transform' });
    };
  }, [setWidth, measured, speed, direction, reduced]);

  // Separate effect so a visibility flip pauses in place instead of rebuilding
  // the tween, which would snap the strip back to its start position.
  useEffect(() => {
    const t = tween.current;
    if (!t) return;
    t.paused(!(visible && inView));
  }, [visible, inView, setWidth, measured, speed, direction, reduced]);

  const ramp = useCallback(
    (to: number) => {
      const t = tween.current;
      if (!pauseOnHover || !t) return;
      gsap.to(t, { timeScale: to, duration: HOVER_RAMP, overwrite: true });
    },
    [pauseOnHover],
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The build effect clears the tween ref, calls `gsap.killTweensOf(tween)` to catch in-flight hover `timeScale` ramps that target the tween object, then `tween.kill()`, then `gsap.set(track, { clearProps: "transform" })`. Both `ResizeObserver` instances are disconnected by their hooks.

**Reduced motion.** Renders a single, un-cloned content set with no tween created at all. The content is fully visible and static — the strip is not left mid-translation and nothing is clipped out of view.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Specifying `duration` instead of a px/second speed. Two marquees on one page then move at different rates, and editing the copy silently changes the speed of the one you edited.
- Translating by the copy width and forgetting the gap. The seam arrives one gap early every cycle — a small, regular hitch that is very hard to diagnose from the code.
- Hardcoding the clone count at 2. On a wide viewport with short content the strip runs out and a blank band sweeps through once per cycle.
- Any ease other than `none`. The strip speeds up and slows down once per loop, so the seam that is geometrically invisible becomes obvious from the velocity change alone.
- Rebuilding the tween when visibility or hover changes. The `fromTo` restarts at x = 0 and the strip teleports backwards.
- Killing only `killTweensOf(trackElement)` on unmount. The hover ramps target the *tween object*, not the element, so they survive and keep writing `timeScale` to a dead tween — `gsap.killTweensOf(t)` before `t.kill()` is what catches them.
- Leaving the cloned copies exposed to assistive technology. A screen reader reads the same six items three times; every clone past the first is `aria-hidden`.

## Notes

- Reduced motion renders exactly one copy with no tween and no transform, so the content sits statically at the left edge and remains fully readable.
- No text splitting is involved — the marquee moves whole content sets, so no split library dependency is imposed on consumers.

## Definition of done

Watch the seam for a full cycle: no jump, no blank wedge, no change in spacing as one copy hands over to the next. Put two marquees with very different content lengths side by side and both move at visibly the same speed. Hover and the strip glides to a stop over about a third of a second rather than halting. Switch browser tabs and back, and the strip resumes from where it was rather than restarting. With reduced motion the content is static and readable.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Search Field

A query field for filtering a list or searching a table. It puts Input's field shell inside React Aria's `SearchField`, rounds it into a pill by default, and adds a search icon at the start and a small clear button at the end that scales and fades in once there is text. `isLoading` cross-fades the icon into Spinner's orbiting light in the same 20px box. Escape clears the text and Enter calls `onSubmit`.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Pill or rounded search input on React Aria SearchField: Escape clears, a clear button scales in with text, and the icon fades to a spinner.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `SearchField` renders `AriaSearchField` as `group flex w-full flex-col items-start gap-1` and always passes it a `value`: the controlled `value` when given, otherwise its own `uncontrolledValue` state. Its `change` function updates that state and calls `onChange`, so the clear button can work in both modes. With no `label` or `aria-label`, the `placeholder` becomes the `aria-label`.
2. The render function shows `Label` when `label` is set, then Input's `InputBase` with `fieldClassName` set to `rounded-full` for `shape="pill"` (the default; `rounded` keeps Input's 10px corners), then `HintText` when `hint` is set. The input hides the browser's own WebKit cancel button so only the kit's clear button shows.
3. The `leadingAddon` is one `aria-hidden` 20px box holding two absolutely positioned layers: the `icon` (default `RiSearchLine`) and `SpinnerGlyph size="sm"`. Both transition `opacity` and `scale` over 200ms. When `isLoading` the icon goes to `scale-75 opacity-0` and the spinner comes in; otherwise the spinner is faded out and its spin is paused with `[animation-play-state:paused]` on its children, so it stays mounted for the fade but does no work.
4. The `trailingAddon` is a `CloseButton size="2xs"` (16px) on `bg-background-tertiary-hover`. While the field is empty or disabled it is `pointer-events-none scale-50 opacity-0` and `aria-hidden`; once there is text it transitions to `scale-100 opacity-100` over 150ms. It has `tabIndex={-1}`, because Escape already clears from the keyboard.
5. Clicking the clear button runs `clear`: `change("")`, `onClear`, then focus back to the input. Its `onMouseDown` calls `preventDefault`, so the input never loses focus while the pointer is down. React Aria's own Escape handling clears through the same `change` and `onClear`.
6. The clear button's accessible name goes through `useTemplateCopy`, which returns the string unchanged unless a template copy provider is present, so the default "Clear search" can be localised.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `icon box = size-5 (20px), ms-1`
  The icon and the spinner share one box and cross-fade in place, so the text never moves when loading starts. A leading addon drops the shell's start padding to 4px (`ps-1`), so the 4px margin brings the icon back to the 8px inset of a plain field.
- `icon / spinner fade = 200ms opacity + scale, hidden at scale-75`
  A short shrink while fading reads as one glyph turning into the other rather than two overlapping.
- `clear button = CloseButton 2xs (16px), 150ms opacity + scale from scale-50`
  Small enough to sit inside the 36px shell. Scaling in from half size makes it appear as the first character is typed without a jump in the layout, since it always occupies its slot.
- `shape = pill (rounded-full) by default, rounded (Input's rounded-2lg) as the option`
  The pill marks the field as search at a glance; `rounded` keeps Input's corners so it lines up with other fields in a form.

## API

```ts
function SearchField(props: Omit<AriaSearchFieldProps, "className" | "children"> & { label?: ReactNode; hint?: ReactNode; placeholder?: string; size?: "medium" | "small"; shape?: "pill" | "rounded"; isLoading?: boolean; icon?: IconComponent; clearLabel?: string; className?: string; fieldClassName?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `value / defaultValue / onChange: string / (value: string) => void`
  Controlled or uncontrolled query.
- `onSubmit: (value: string) => void`
  Called on Enter, from React Aria.
- `onClear: () => void`
  Called when Escape or the clear button empties the field.
- `shape: "pill" | "rounded"` — default `"pill"`
  Fully rounded, or Input's 10px corners.
- `size: "medium" | "small"` — default `"medium"`
  36px or 32px shell.
- `isLoading: boolean` — default `false`
  Cross-fades the icon into a spinner.
- `icon: ComponentType` — default `RiSearchLine`
  Replaces the search icon.
- `clearLabel: string` — default `"Clear search"`
  Accessible name of the clear button.
- `label / hint: ReactNode`
  Label above and caption below, as on Input.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function SearchField({
  label,
  hint,
  placeholder,
  size = "medium",
  shape = "pill",
  isLoading = false,
  icon: Icon = RiSearchLine,
  clearLabel = "Clear search",
  value: controlledValue,
  defaultValue = "",
  onChange,
  onClear,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel,
  className,
  fieldClassName,
  ...props
}: SearchFieldProps) {
  const localize = useTemplateCopy();
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const [uncontrolledValue, setUncontrolledValue] = useState(defaultValue);
  const value = controlledValue ?? uncontrolledValue;

  const change = (next: string) => {
    setUncontrolledValue(next);
    onChange?.(next);
  };

  const clear = () => {
    change("");
    onClear?.();
    inputRef.current?.focus();
  };

  return (
    <AriaSearchField
      {...props}
      value={value}
      onChange={change}
      onClear={onClear}
      aria-label={ariaLabel ?? (!label ? placeholder : undefined)}
      className={cx("group flex w-full flex-col items-start gap-1", className)}
    >
      {({ isEmpty, isDisabled, isInvalid }) => (
        <>
          {label ? (
            <Label isRequired={props.isRequired} isInvalid={isInvalid}>
              {label}
            </Label>
          ) : null}
          <InputBase
            ref={inputRef}
            size={size}
            placeholder={placeholder}
            fieldClassName={cx(shape === "pill" && "rounded-full", fieldClassName)}
            className="[&::-webkit-search-cancel-button]:hidden"
            leadingAddon={
              // The icon and the light share one 20px box and cross-fade.
              <span aria-hidden className="relative ms-1 size-5 shrink-0">
                <Icon
                  className={cx(
                    "absolute inset-0 size-5 transition-[opacity,scale] duration-200 ease-out",
                    isLoading && "scale-75 opacity-0",
                  )}
                />
                <span
                  className={cx(
                    "absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center transition-[opacity,scale] duration-200 ease-out",
                    // Hidden, the light stays mounted for the fade but stops turning.
                    !isLoading && "scale-75 opacity-0 [&_*]:[animation-play-state:paused]",
                  )}
                >
                  <SpinnerGlyph size="sm" />
                </span>
              </span>
            }
            trailingAddon={
              <CloseButton
                size="2xs"
                aria-label={localize(clearLabel)}
                aria-hidden={isEmpty || undefined}
                tabIndex={-1}
                disabled={isDisabled}
                // Keep focus in the input while the pointer clears it.
                onMouseDown={(event) => event.preventDefault()}
                onClick={clear}
                className={cx(
                  "me-0.5 bg-background-tertiary-hover transition-[opacity,scale,color] duration-150 ease-out",
                  isEmpty || isDisabled ? "pointer-events-none scale-50 opacity-0" : "scale-100 opacity-100",
                )}
              />
            }
          />
          {hint ? <HintText isInvalid={isInvalid}>{hint}</HintText> : null}
        </>
      )}
    </AriaSearchField>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component keeps one piece of state and a ref; the spinner's CSS animation is paused while hidden.

**Reduced motion.** The fades are CSS transitions and the component does not check `prefers-reduced-motion` itself. Spinner's glyph does: under `motion-reduce` its spin slows from 900ms to 2400ms per turn.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not unmount the spinner when not loading. It stays mounted at `opacity-0` with its animation paused so it can fade in and out; unmounting would make it pop.
- Do not put the clear button in the tab order. Escape already clears from the keyboard, and a tabbable 16px button would add an extra stop on every search.
- Do not remove the `onMouseDown` `preventDefault` on the clear button. Without it, pressing the button blurs the input first, which closes any results popover tied to focus.
- Do not leave the field with no `label`, `aria-label` or string `placeholder`. Nothing would name it.

## Notes

- The field imports `InputBase` from Input, `Label` and `HintText` from Input's companions, `CloseButton` from Close Button and `SpinnerGlyph` from Spinner, so install those items alongside it.
- The clear button always occupies its slot, even when hidden, so the text area width does not change when text is typed.

## Definition of done

An empty pill field shows a search icon and no clear button. Typing a letter scales the clear button in at the end; clicking it empties the field and keeps the caret in it. Escape also clears it. While `isLoading` is true the search icon shrinks away and a spinning light takes its place, then swaps back when loading ends. With `shape="rounded"` the corners match Input. Tab never lands on the clear button.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Segmented Control

A single-select segmented control on React Aria's ToggleButtonGroup, so arrow keys move focus, Space or Enter selects, and the selection can never be emptied. Instead of each segment painting its own background, one absolutely positioned thumb is measured off the selected button and slides between segments over 200ms. A `plain` variant drops the track and the thumb and marks the selection with text weight and colour alone.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A pill switcher for Weekly / Monthly / Yearly choices: one white thumb, measured from the DOM, slides under the selected segment.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `SegmentedControl` renders an `AriaToggleButtonGroup` with `selectionMode="single"` and `disallowEmptySelection` fixed, then spreads the caller's props (`selectedKeys`, `defaultSelectedKeys`, `onSelectionChange`, `aria-label`, ...). The `solid` track is `inline-flex gap-0.5 rounded-2lg p-1` on `bg-segmented-control-background`.
2. In a layout effect (a plain effect on the server) it queries the group for the `[data-selected]` button that React Aria marks and stores its `offsetLeft`, `offsetTop`, `offsetWidth` and `offsetHeight`. A 0px width (the control is hidden or not laid out yet) or no selection stores no thumb, and equal measurements keep the previous state so observer callbacks cannot re-render in a loop. Offsets are relative to the group because the group is `relative`, so the thumb needs no `getBoundingClientRect` arithmetic.
3. The thumb is a single `aria-hidden` span at `left-0 top-0`, placed with `transform: translate(left, top)` and sized with explicit `width` / `height`, with `transition-[transform,width,height] duration-200`. Moving between segments of different widths therefore slides and resizes in one motion.
4. Re-measuring is event driven, never polled: a ResizeObserver watches the group and every button (labels can change width when fonts load or text changes), and a MutationObserver on the subtree re-observes new buttons and re-measures when `data-selected` or the children change. Both disconnect on cleanup; the effect re-runs when the document direction flips.
5. Each `SegmentedControlItem` is a `relative z-10` React Aria `ToggleButton` above the thumb: `px-2.5 py-1 rounded-md`, `text-body-medium text-text-primary` when selected and `text-body-regular text-text-secondary` otherwise, with a 200ms colour transition, a focus-visible ring and 50% opacity when disabled. Until the thumb exists (the server render, or a hidden control) a context flag gives the selected segment the thumb's own `bg-segmented-control-selected-background shadow-2xs`, so first paint already shows the white pill; once the thumb is measured the segment drops it and the thumb takes over and slides.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `thumb transition = 200ms on transform, width and height`
  Long enough to read as one object moving to the new choice, short enough that rapid clicking never lags behind the selection.
- `track = p-1, gap-0.5, rounded-2lg (10px); segments rounded-md (6px)`
  From the Figma switch (node 3731:3096). A 4px inset with a 6px inner radius keeps the thumb's corners concentric with the 10px track.
- `segment padding = px-2.5 py-1`
  Compact enough to sit in a card header next to a title without dominating it.
- `thumb shadow = shadow-2xs: 0 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.16)`
  A single-pixel bottom edge lifts the white thumb off the light-grey track without a blurred shadow.

## API

```ts
function SegmentedControl(props: Omit<ToggleButtonGroupProps, "selectionMode" | "disallowEmptySelection"> & { variant?: "solid" | "plain"; children?: ReactNode; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function SegmentedControlItem(props: Omit<ToggleButtonProps, "children"> & { children?: ReactNode; ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement> }): JSX.Element
```

- `selectedKeys / defaultSelectedKeys: Iterable<Key>`
  Controlled or initial selection; holds exactly one item id.
- `onSelectionChange: (keys: Set<Key>) => void`
  Fires with the new one-key set.
- `variant: "solid" | "plain"` — default `"solid"`
  `plain` drops the track background and the thumb.
- `aria-label: string`
  Names the group for assistive technology.
- `isDisabled: boolean`
  On the group or a single `SegmentedControlItem`; disabled items drop to 50% opacity.
- `id: Key`
  SegmentedControlItem only. The key reported in the selection set.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function SegmentedControl({ className, children, variant = "solid", ref, ...props }: SegmentedControlProps) {
  const direction = useDirection();
  const innerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const [thumb, setThumb] = useState<Thumb | null>(null);

  useIsomorphicLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = innerRef.current;
    if (!el) return;
    const measure = () => {
      const selected = el.querySelector<HTMLElement>("[data-selected]");
      // Nothing selected, or a 0px box (display: none, not laid out yet):
      // drop the thumb so the segment's own fill shows. The ResizeObserver
      // measures again once the segment has a size.
      const next =
        selected && selected.offsetWidth > 0
          ? {
              left: selected.offsetLeft,
              top: selected.offsetTop,
              width: selected.offsetWidth,
              height: selected.offsetHeight,
            }
          : null;
      // Skip equal values so observer callbacks never re-render in a loop.
      setThumb((prev) =>
        prev && next && prev.left === next.left && prev.top === next.top && prev.width === next.width && prev.height === next.height
          ? prev
          : next,
      );
    };
    measure();
    const ro = new ResizeObserver(measure);
    ro.observe(el);
    const observeItems = () => el.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(item => ro.observe(item));
    observeItems();
    const mo = new MutationObserver(() => { observeItems(); measure(); });
    mo.observe(el, { attributes: true, childList: true, characterData: true, subtree: true, attributeFilter: ["data-selected"] });
    return () => {
      mo.disconnect();
      ro.disconnect();
    };
  }, [direction]);

  const setRefs = (node: HTMLDivElement | null) => {
    innerRef.current = node;
    if (typeof ref === "function") ref(node);
    else if (ref) (ref as { current: HTMLDivElement | null }).current = node;
  };

  return (
    <AriaToggleButtonGroup
      ref={setRefs}
      selectionMode="single"
      disallowEmptySelection
      {...props}
      className={(state) =>
        cx(
          "relative inline-flex items-start gap-0.5 rounded-2lg",
          variant === "solid" && "bg-segmented-control-background p-1",
          typeof className === "function" ? className(state) : className,
        )
      }
    >
      {variant === "solid" && thumb && (
        <span
          aria-hidden
          className="pointer-events-none absolute left-0 top-0 rounded-md bg-segmented-control-selected-background shadow-2xs transition-[transform,width,height] duration-200 ease"
          style={{
            transform: `translate(${thumb.left}px, ${thumb.top}px)`,
            width: thumb.width,
            height: thumb.height,
          }}
        />
      )}
      <SelectedFillContext.Provider value={variant === "solid" && !thumb}>{children}</SelectedFillContext.Provider>
    </AriaToggleButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The layout effect disconnects its ResizeObserver and MutationObserver when the control unmounts or the direction changes. No timers or window listeners.

**Reduced motion.** The component does not branch on `prefers-reduced-motion`. The only motion is the 200ms thumb slide plus colour fades on the labels, and the selected state is also carried by text weight and colour, so turning transitions off loses nothing.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not give each selected segment its own background once the thumb is measured. The point is a single thumb that travels; per-segment backgrounds jump with no motion. The segment fill is only the stand-in before the first measurement.
- Do not measure with `getBoundingClientRect` against the viewport. The thumb is positioned inside the `relative` group, so `offsetLeft` / `offsetTop` are already in the right space and survive page scroll.
- Do not measure only once on mount. Web fonts, translated labels and a direction flip all change segment widths; without the ResizeObserver and MutationObserver the thumb drifts off its segment.
- Do not pass `selectionMode` or `disallowEmptySelection`. Both are fixed by the component and omitted from its props; a segmented control that can be emptied leaves the thumb parked on nothing.

## Notes

- Selection uses React Aria's key sets: `selectedKeys={new Set(["monthly"])}` with `onSelectionChange={(keys) => ...}`, where each item's `id` is its key.
- Give the group an `aria-label` ("Period", "View"); React Aria renders it as `role="radiogroup"` with radio items in single-selection mode.
- The thumb renders only after the first measurement. Before that (on the server, or while the control is hidden) the selected segment paints the same white fill itself, so server HTML and first paint match the measured look.

## Definition of done

A grey pill track holds Weekly, Monthly and Yearly with a white thumb under the selected one. Clicking another segment slides and resizes the thumb to it in about 200ms while its label turns medium weight and primary colour. Arrow keys move focus between segments and Space selects; clicking the selected segment keeps it selected. The `plain` variant shows no track or thumb, only the weight and colour change, and a disabled item is dimmed and cannot be chosen.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Select

React Aria's `Select` with BoardUI's trigger and menu chrome: a 10px-radius bordered button whose 16px chevron turns 180° while open, and a 266px popover that shares the Dropdown recipe (radius 2xl, shadow-dropdown, 150ms fade, scale and blur). The popover is deliberately non-modal so opening a select never locks page scroll, and the component restores the outside-press dismissal and trigger toggle that React Aria drops in that mode. Rows take any content, so a status dot, avatar or flag sits beside the text.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A React Aria select: bordered trigger with a turning chevron, non-modal popover on the shared menu surface, free-form rows.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Open state is controlled locally (`isOpen` in `useState`) and passed to `AriaSelect`. The `AriaPopover` is `isNonModal` with `offset={4}`, which skips React Aria's scroll lock: that lock sets `overflow: hidden` on `<html>` and, under an `h-full` root, makes the page jump each time a select opens.
2. `isNonModal` also turns off React Aria's outside-press dismissal, so `useDismissOnOutsidePress(isOpen, close, [triggerRef, popoverRef])` adds a capture-phase `pointerdown` listener on `document` while open and closes when the press lands outside both refs.
3. Pressing the trigger while open makes React Aria call `onOpenChange(false)` then `onOpenChange(true)` in the same press. `useTriggerToggle` watches for that pointerdown and swallows the reopen, so `onOpenChange={(o) => allowOpenChange(o) && setIsOpen(o)}` turns the trigger into a true toggle.
4. The trigger is an `AriaButton` holding `AriaSelectValue` (the selected row's own content, or `renderValue`) and `ChevronDownSmall`, which gets `rotate-180` from the render-prop `isOpen` and animates with `transition-transform duration-200`. The button itself transitions background, border, shadow, padding and font size over 200ms, so hover and a `size` switch both ease.
5. The popover combines `MENU_POPOVER_WIDTH` (266px), `MENU_POPOVER_SURFACE` and `p-2`. The surface's `data-[entering]` and `data-[exiting]` classes run opacity 0, `scale-95` and `blur-[2px]` over 150ms ease-out, with `transform-origin` taken from `data-placement`. Inside, an `AriaListBox` scrolls past `max-h-[240px]`.
6. `size` goes down to the rows through `SelectSizeContext`. `SelectItem` reads it to pick `text-body-medium` (md) or `px-2 py-1.5 text-body-2-medium` (sm), and applies `MENU_ITEM_ACTIVE` when the row is focused or selected.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `popover offset = 4px`
  The gap between trigger and menu. It is enough to show the trigger border and shadow, and close enough that the menu reads as belonging to that trigger.
- `menu width = w-[266px] (MENU_POPOVER_WIDTH)`
  Shared with Dropdown so every menu in the kit has the same width. Pass `popoverClassName` to narrow it, for example to the trigger width in a filter bar.
- `list height = max-h-[240px]`
  About six rows at 36px plus 4px gaps. Longer lists scroll inside the popover instead of running past the viewport.
- `trigger padding = md px-2.5 py-2, gap-1.5 / sm px-[7px] py-1, gap-1`
  From Figma: md gives a 38px trigger that lines up with Input, and sm gives a 28px trigger for compact table toolbars.
- `motion = chevron 200ms rotate; popover 150ms opacity/scale-95/blur-2px`
  The menu is quicker than the chevron so the list is readable by the time the chevron settles. The 2px blur hides the scale step on the first frame.

## API

```ts
function Select<T extends object>(props: Omit<AriaSelectProps<T>, "children"> & { label?: ReactNode; className?: string; triggerClassName?: string; popoverClassName?: string; size?: "sm" | "md"; children: ReactNode; items?: Iterable<T>; renderValue?: ReactNode | ((values: AriaSelectValueRenderProps<T>) => ReactNode); ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element; function SelectItem(props: Omit<AriaListBoxItemProps, "children"> & { children?: ReactNode }): JSX.Element
```

- `label: ReactNode`
  Visible label above the trigger. React Aria wires it as the accessible name. Without it, pass `aria-label`.
- `size: "sm" | "md"` — default `"md"`
  Trigger padding and type size. Rows read the same size through context.
- `placeholder: string`
  React Aria's placeholder, shown in the trigger until something is selected.
- `value / defaultValue / onChange: Key | null`
  React Aria's selection value, controlled or uncontrolled. The older `selectedKey` props still work but are deprecated in React Aria.
- `renderValue: ReactNode | ((values) => ReactNode)`
  Custom trigger content. Falls back to the selected row's children.
- `className: string`
  Classes on the root, for example a fixed width.
- `triggerClassName: string`
  Classes on the trigger button.
- `popoverClassName: string`
  Classes on the popover, for example a narrower width.
- `items: Iterable<T>`
  Optional dynamic collection, rendered with a children function inside the listbox.
- `children: ReactNode`
  `SelectItem` rows, each with an `id` and a `textValue`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function Select<T extends object>({
  label,
  className,
  triggerClassName,
  popoverClassName,
  size = "md",
  children,
  items,
  renderValue,
  ref,
  ...props
}: SelectProps<T>) {
  // The popover is `isNonModal`: react-aria's modal scroll lock puts
  // `overflow: hidden` on <html>, which — with this app's `h-full` root —
  // collapses the page scroll position and visibly yanks the sticky
  // sidebar upward every time a select opens. Non-modal skips the lock,
  // but also disables react-aria's outside-press dismissal (`isDismissable`
  // is hard-coupled to `!isNonModal` in usePopover), so open state is
  // controlled here and dismissal restored manually — the same fix as the
  // date-picker family (see utils/use-dismiss-on-outside-press.ts).
  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const popoverRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
  useDismissOnOutsidePress(isOpen, () => setIsOpen(false), [triggerRef, popoverRef]);
  // Pressing the trigger while open closes the popover instead of reopening
  const allowOpenChange = useTriggerToggle(isOpen, triggerRef);

  return (
    <AriaSelect
      ref={ref}
      {...props}
      isOpen={isOpen}
      onOpenChange={(o) => allowOpenChange(o) && setIsOpen(o)}
      className={cx("group flex flex-col", label ? "gap-1" : undefined, className)}
    >
      {({ isOpen, isRequired }) => (
        <>
          {label ? <Label isRequired={isRequired}>{label}</Label> : null}
          <AriaButton
            ref={triggerRef}
            className={cx(
              "flex w-full cursor-pointer items-center justify-between rounded-2lg",
              "border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default shadow-xs",
              "text-text-primary",
              "transition-[background-color,border-color,box-shadow,padding,font-size] duration-200 ease",
              "hover:bg-background-primary-hover hover:border-border-button-hover",
              "outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
              "disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:bg-background-primary-disabled disabled:text-text-tertiary disabled:shadow-none",
              size === "sm"
                ? "gap-1 px-[7px] py-1 text-body-2-medium"
                : "gap-1.5 px-2.5 py-2 text-body-medium",
              triggerClassName,
            )}
          >
            <AriaSelectValue
              className={cx(
                "flex min-w-0 items-center truncate",
                size === "sm" ? "gap-1" : "gap-[5px]",
              )}
            >
              {renderValue as never /* RAC accepts node or render-prop */}
            </AriaSelectValue>
            <ChevronDownSmall
              className={cx(
                "shrink-0 text-text-secondary transition-transform duration-200 ease",
                size === "sm" ? "size-3.5" : "size-4",
                isOpen && "rotate-180",
              )}
            />
          </AriaButton>
          <AriaPopover
            ref={popoverRef}
            isNonModal
            offset={4}
            className={cx(
              MENU_POPOVER_WIDTH,
              MENU_POPOVER_SURFACE,
              // Listbox rows already space themselves 4px apart, so the
              // surface sits a touch tighter than the action-menu Dropdown.
              "p-2",
              popoverClassName,
            )}
          >
            <AriaListBox
              items={items}
              className={cx(MENU_ITEMS_CONTAINER, "max-h-[240px] overflow-auto")}
            >
              <SelectSizeContext.Provider value={size}>{children}</SelectSizeContext.Provider>
            </AriaListBox>
          </AriaPopover>
        </>
      )}
    </AriaSelect>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The outside-press listener is added in an effect only while the popover is open and removed in that effect's cleanup, both on close and on unmount. `useTriggerToggle` clears its 400ms safety timeout the same way. React Aria owns the popover portal and removes it on close.

**Reduced motion.** The chevron rotation, the trigger colour transitions and the popover fade, scale and blur are CSS transitions of 150–200ms with no JavaScript tween. They do not change position on screen, so they run under `prefers-reduced-motion` too. Add `motion-reduce:transition-none` through `popoverClassName` and `triggerClassName` to remove them.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Leaving out both `label` and `aria-label`. React Aria then logs an accessibility warning and screen readers announce an unnamed button. Pass one of them.
- Removing `isNonModal` to get dismissal for free. The modal popover's scroll lock returns and the page jumps under an `h-full` root on every open.
- Giving a `SelectItem` rich children with no `textValue`. Typeahead and the accessible name then fall back to an empty string, so pass `textValue` whenever children are not plain text.
- Passing `isOpen` or `onOpenChange` from outside. The component controls open state itself, and the spread comes before its own props, so outside values are overwritten.

## Notes

- The trigger value is the selected row's own content, so a row with a status dot shows the dot in the trigger too. Use `renderValue` when the trigger needs a more compact form, such as a flag and a dial code.
- Like the other BoardUI controls, `className` and `triggerClassName` merge through tailwind-merge, so `w-[240px]` replaces the default width cleanly.

## Definition of done

Clicking the trigger opens a 266px menu 4px below it with a short fade and scale, and the chevron turns 180°. Picking a row closes the menu and shows that row's content, status dot included, in the trigger. Clicking the trigger again, clicking outside, or pressing Escape closes the menu, and the page does not scroll or jump. Arrow keys move the highlight, and typing a letter jumps to the matching `textValue`. No accessibility warning appears in the console when `label` or `aria-label` is passed.

# Build: Self-Parking RAF

An eased value never arrives. Closing 12% of the remaining gap each frame closes it 100% never — the distance decays asymptotically and `current !== target` stays true for the life of the page, so a loop conditioned on that comparison never stops. One line fixes it: below a threshold, assign the target outright. The equality test can now succeed, the loop reaches its own stopping condition, and it unsubscribes itself. The frame callback exists only while something is genuinely moving.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

An epsilon snap lets a damped value reach its target exactly, so the frame loop hits its exit test and dies.

- Category: primitive
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The damped step is `damp(current, target, smoothing, dt)`, which is `current + (target - current) * (1 - smoothing^dt)`. The exponent is what makes it frame-rate independent: the naked `* 0.12` from the source converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz, so the same code feels different on different hardware and visibly speeds up whenever the browser drops frames.
2. After the step, `Math.abs(target - next) < epsilon` assigns `next = target` exactly. This is the entire technique. Without it the loop's exit condition — `next === target` — is unreachable, because exponential decay produces 1e-8, then 1e-9, then a denormal, and never a clean zero.
3. Parking is expressed as React state, not as a local flag: `setRunning(false)` drops the `useRaf` subscription, and when the last subscriber leaves the shared loop calls `cancelAnimationFrame` and stops scheduling frames at all. The saving is the whole callback plus the paint it would have dirtied, not merely the arithmetic.
4. Waking is driven by a `target` change in an effect, guarded by `value.current === target`. The guard is load-bearing: without it any unrelated re-render that happens to pass the same target restarts a loop that had already parked, which is how "self-parking" quietly degrades back into an always-on loop.
5. Because `perFrameToSmoothing(0.12)` is `0.88^60 ≈ 0.00047`, the value retains 0.047% of its gap after a second — so the settle time is a few hundred milliseconds and the epsilon is crossed within roughly twenty frames rather than being an escape hatch from a genuinely long tail.
6. A hidden tab and reduced motion both take the same short path: `park()` assigns the target, emits one `onFrame`, and never starts a loop. No observer means no reason to interpolate, and the value stays correct either way.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `per-frame rate = 0.12`
  Fraction of the remaining gap closed per frame at 60fps, converted through `perFrameToSmoothing`. It settles in about 300 ms — fast enough that a scrubber feels attached to the click, slow enough to read as motion. Above ~0.3 the damping is barely visible and the loop may as well be a jump; below ~0.05 the tail is long enough that a user beats it with the next click.
- `EPSILON = 0.0002`
  Snap threshold, in the units of the value. For the 0-1 normalised scrub position of the source this is a fifth of a pixel on a 1000 px track — invisible. Set it to 0 and the loop never parks, which is the exact bug this component exists to fix. Set it far too large and the last visible fraction of the travel is skipped as a jump.
- `MAX_DT = 0.1`
  Inherited from `useRaf`. A tab returning from the background delivers a multi-second delta; unclamped, `smoothing^dt` underflows to 0, the damp closes the entire gap in one frame, and the "settle" is a teleport.

## API

```ts
function useSelfParkingRaf(target: number, options: { smoothing?: number; epsilon?: number; onFrame: (value: number) => void }): { running: boolean; value: RefObject<number>; park: () => void }
```

- `target: number`
  The value to settle toward. Changing it wakes the loop; it is the only trigger.
- `smoothing: number` — default `perFrameToSmoothing(0.12)`
  Fraction of the gap remaining after one second. Smaller is snappier.
- `epsilon: number` — default `0.0002`
  Distance below which the value snaps to the target and the loop parks. Must match the unit of the value.
- `onFrame: (value: number) => void`
  Called with the damped value every frame while running, and once when it parks. For DOM writes.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * `0.12` of the gap per frame, measured at 60fps, expressed as the retention
 * factor `damp` wants. Using the raw 0.12 with a per-frame multiply would run
 * twice as fast on a 120 Hz display; this converges in the same wall-clock
 * time on any refresh rate.
 */
const SMOOTHING = perFrameToSmoothing(0.12);
/** The snap threshold. This single line is what allows the loop to end. */
const EPSILON = 0.0002;

/**
 * A damped value that runs a frame loop only while it is moving.
 *
 * `target` is a plain prop: changing it wakes the loop, and the loop parks
 * itself once it arrives. There is no `start`, and there is no
 * `requestAnimationFrame` running when the value is at rest.
 */
export function useSelfParkingRaf(
  target: number,
  options: SelfParkingOptions,
): SelfParkingValue {
  const { smoothing = SMOOTHING, epsilon = EPSILON } = options;
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const visible = useVisibility();

  const value = useRef(target);
  const [running, setRunning] = useState(false);

  const config = useRef({ smoothing, epsilon, target, options });
  config.current = { smoothing, epsilon, target, options };

  const park = useCallback(() => {
    const cfg = config.current;
    value.current = cfg.target;
    cfg.options.onFrame(value.current);
    setRunning(false);
  }, []);

  // Waking the loop is the only thing a target change does. The guard matters:
  // without it, any unrelated re-render that happens to pass the same target
  // restarts a loop that had already parked.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (value.current === target) return;
    // Nothing to interpolate: reduced motion wants the end state, and a hidden
    // tab has no observer, so both arrive in one write instead of a loop.
    if (reduced || !visible) {
      park();
      return;
    }
    setRunning(true);
  }, [target, reduced, visible, park]);

  useRaf((dt) => {
    const cfg = config.current;
    let next = damp(value.current, cfg.target, cfg.smoothing, dt);

    // The whole technique. Asymptotic approach means `next` would otherwise
    // never equal `cfg.target`, so the exit test below could never pass.
    if (Math.abs(cfg.target - next) < cfg.epsilon) next = cfg.target;

    value.current = next;
    cfg.options.onFrame(next);

    // Parking flips `running`, which drops the `useRaf` subscription. When the
    // last subscriber goes, the shared loop cancels its frame entirely.
    if (next === cfg.target) setRunning(false);
  }, running);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** `useRaf` removes the subscription when `running` goes false or the component unmounts, and cancels the shared frame when it was the last subscriber — so an unmount mid-settle leaves nothing scheduled. The visibility and media-query listeners belong to `useVisibility` and `useReducedMotion`, which detach their own. No timers and no direct `requestAnimationFrame` handles are held.

**Reduced motion.** No loop is started at all. A target change calls `park()`, which assigns the target and emits a single `onFrame`, so the value lands on its final position in one write. That is the still, correct state rather than a zero-duration animation: `onFrame` still fires, so the DOM the consumer writes is identical to the end of a full settle, and `running` never goes true.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Omitting the epsilon snap. The value approaches the target forever, the exit test never passes, and one hover or one scrub leaves a rAF running for the rest of the session. It is invisible in a demo and shows up as a battery complaint.
- Expressing epsilon in the wrong unit. The threshold is compared against the value, so 0.0002 is correct for a 0-1 progress value and absurd for a pixel offset — at pixel scale it costs dozens of extra frames to cross, and the loop appears not to park.
- Keeping the loop alive to "avoid the cost of restarting it". Subscribing to a shared rAF is a `Set.add`; a frame callback plus the paint it dirties is orders of magnitude more. Restarting is free, running is not.
- Using `current += (target - current) * 0.12` directly. Frame-rate dependent: the same settle takes 300 ms at 60 Hz and 150 ms at 120 Hz, and speeds up mid-motion whenever a long task drops frames — the animation gets faster precisely when the page is struggling.
- Waking the loop without comparing against the current value. Every re-render that re-supplies the same target restarts the loop, which parks on its first frame and restarts on the next render — a loop that thrashes instead of resting.
- Calling `setState` from `onFrame`. That re-renders on every frame of the settle, which costs far more than the loop being parked ever saved. `onFrame` is for DOM writes.
- Reading the returned `value` ref during render. It changes between renders without notifying React, so the rendered output and the ref disagree; read it inside a frame callback or an event handler only.
- Forgetting that the loop is asleep when the target is set imperatively. Anything that mutates the underlying source without changing the `target` prop leaves the value stale, because nothing is polling — the trade for not running a loop is that changes must be declared.

## Notes

- The natural pairing is with an invalidate-driven renderer: a WebGL scene that renders only on demand plus a value that only moves on demand gives a page that is genuinely idle at rest, not merely cheap.
- The `park()` escape hatch exists for handoffs — a drag that takes over the value, or a route change that should not animate the old position. It emits one final `onFrame` so the DOM is left in the correct end state rather than mid-travel.
- `running` is exposed because parking is otherwise unobservable, and a component that claims to park should be able to prove it. The demo prints it beside a frame count that freezes.
- For several values settling together, one hook per value is fine — they all share the single `useRaf` loop, and the last one to park is the one that stops it.

## Definition of done

Click a timecode. The bar and the readout race to it and stop, and the status line goes from "rAF live" to "rAF parked" with the frame count frozen at roughly twenty — not climbing. Leave it alone for a minute: the count does not move. Open DevTools performance and record while idle after a seek; there are no animation frames. Click the timecode that is already active and nothing wakes. Switch tabs mid-settle and come back — the bar is already at its target with no catch-up sweep. With reduced motion on, a seek moves the bar in one step, the count reads 1, and the status never leaves "parked".

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Settings Modal

A controlled `SettingsModal` (`isOpen` / `onClose`) portals an 871×614 panel with a grouped section rail on the left and a scrolling page on the right. It ships four pages built from shared row primitives: General (a plan card with a WebGL "burning flag" artwork, pull-request and notification preferences), Profile (fields that save on Enter or blur and trigger a "Saved" toast), Tools (MCP servers by scope) and Storage (a sortable, filterable, paginated file table with uploads). The open and close are the same transition run in reverse. The DOM is kept mounted until the close has finished.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A controlled settings dialog with a section rail and General, Profile, Tools and Storage pages. It scales in from 85% with a light blur.

- Category: block
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria@^3.53.1, react-aria-components@^1.22.1, @internationalized/date@^3.12.4

## How it works

1. Opening runs in two phases. `mounted` puts the portal in the DOM at its hidden pose (`scale-[0.85] opacity-0 blur-[4px]`), and a double `requestAnimationFrame` flips `visible` one frame after that pose has been committed. Without the second frame the browser merges both class sets into one style recalc and skips the transition. Closing clears `visible` straight away and only unmounts after a 320ms timer, so the 300ms exit plays in full.
2. The backdrop and the panel transition separately. The backdrop is a `bg-black/70` `<button>` (`tabIndex={-1}`, clicking it closes) that fades its opacity over 300ms. The wrapper carries `transform-gpu transition-[opacity,transform,filter]` on `cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)`, a fast start that settles softly. The "Saved" toast lives in this same wrapper, outside the panel's clip, so it scales with the panel while sitting across its bottom edge.
3. The portal target is `useUNSAFE_PortalContext().getContainer?.() ?? document.body`. Hosts that clip fixed children, such as a scaled preview frame, can hand it their own container. Opening focuses the panel (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `tabIndex={-1}`), and a document `keydown` listener closes it on Escape. That listener only exists while `isOpen` is true.
4. The rail renders `NAV_GROUPS` as Settings, Desktop app and Customize. Only entries that carry a `page` navigate. The others (Appearance, Billing, Plugins…) are inert rows that complete the layout. Marketplace only appears when a `marketplace` node is passed. Each open resets the page to `defaultPage`. Switching pages resets the scroll fade, an `h-10` gradient over the top of the scroller that fades in over 200ms once `scrollTop > 0`.
5. The Saved toast is a three-phase state machine: `hidden → shown → leaving → hidden`. Each phase has its own offset: it rises in from 12px below its resting spot, stays for 2000ms, then drifts 10px up while fading and blurring. After 220ms it is quietly reset to the bottom start, so the next save rises in again instead of falling back down. A new save within the window restarts the timer.
6. General's plan art is `PlanArtFlame`. It is a fullscreen-quad fragment shader that ripples the artwork like a flag, with the most movement at the edges, and burns it away with 4-octave fbm noise behind an ember rim and three layers of rising flakes. The pointer hotspot is eased toward the cursor every frame. With no `planArtSrc` it burns built-in blobs painted from theme colour tokens. If WebGL is unavailable it falls back to a static DOM blur.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `enter / exit pose = scale 0.85, opacity 0, blur 4px → 1, 1, 0 over 300ms`
  An 85% start reads as the dialog coming forward rather than popping. The blur was 8px until the close stuttered. Re-filtering an 8px blur over the whole 871×614 panel every frame of the scale-down was the cost, and 4px with GPU promotion stays smooth.
- `unmount delay = 320ms`
  20ms longer than the 300ms transition, so the last frame of the exit lands before the portal is removed. If it is equal or shorter, the panel can vanish one frame early on a busy main thread.
- `panel size = 871 × 614 px, capped at calc(100vw-32px) × calc(100dvh-32px)`
  Taken from the Figma frame. The caps keep a 16px gutter on small screens, and the rail falls back to icons only (`w-14`) below `sm` so the page still has room.
- `saved toast timing = 2000ms shown, 200ms transitions, 220ms reset`
  Two seconds is enough to notice and still gone before the next edit. The reset waits 20ms past the fade so the jump back to the start offset happens at opacity 0 and is never seen.
- `storage table = 1,262 rows (mulberry32 seed 26), 6 per page, 400ms row enter / 225ms row exit`
  A seeded PRNG generates the same inventory on the server and the client, so there is no hydration mismatch. The exit is shorter than the enter because removing a row should feel immediate, while a new row needs time to be noticed.
- `flame pointer easing = position 0.12, strength 0.07 per frame`
  Position follows quickly enough that the heat clearly tracks the cursor. Strength eases about half as fast, so the burn swells and cools gradually instead of switching on and off at the canvas edge.

## API

```ts
type SettingsPage = "general" | "profile" | "storage" | "tools" | "marketplace"
function SettingsModal(props: { isOpen: boolean; onClose: () => void; defaultPage?: SettingsPage; planArtSrc?: string; marketplace?: ReactNode }): ReactPortal | null
```

- `isOpen: boolean`
  Controlled open state. Flipping it to false plays the exit and unmounts 320ms later.
- `onClose: () => void`
  Called by the backdrop, the close button and Escape. The parent sets `isOpen` back to false.
- `defaultPage: SettingsPage` — default `"general"`
  Page shown each time the dialog opens. Read on the open transition only.
- `planArtSrc: string`
  Image burned by the plan card's WebGL artwork. Omit it to burn the built-in token-coloured blobs.
- `marketplace: ReactNode`
  Content for an optional Marketplace page. The rail entry is hidden unless this is provided.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Mount/visible two-phase state so both the enter and the exit play the
// full fade + blur + scale transition before the DOM goes away.
const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(false);
const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false);
const unmountTimer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
const panelRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

// "Saved" toast — floats half-out of the panel's bottom edge for ~2s
// whenever a profile field commits a change (Enter / blur). Three phases
// so the motion is directional: it rises in from below ("hidden" starting
// offset) and keeps drifting upward while fading out ("leaving" offset).
const [savedPhase, setSavedPhase] = useState<"hidden" | "shown" | "leaving">("hidden");
const savedTimer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
const showSavedToast = () => {
  if (savedTimer.current) clearTimeout(savedTimer.current);
  setSavedPhase("shown");
  savedTimer.current = setTimeout(() => {
    setSavedPhase("leaving");
    // Reset to the below-the-edge start once the fade-out finished, so the
    // next save rises in from the bottom again (invisible: opacity 0 → 0).
    savedTimer.current = setTimeout(() => setSavedPhase("hidden"), 220);
  }, 2000);
};

// Top fade over the scrolling page so rows dissolve under the title row
// instead of cutting sharply (same recipe as the medical alerts feed).
const [contentScrolled, setContentScrolled] = useState(false);

useEffect(() => {
  if (isOpen) {
    if (unmountTimer.current) clearTimeout(unmountTimer.current);
    setPage(defaultPage);
    setMounted(true);
    // Double rAF: the panel must commit its hidden state before the
    // transition to visible starts, or the browser skips the animation.
    requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(() => setVisible(true)));
  } else {
    setVisible(false);
    setSavedPhase("hidden");
    unmountTimer.current = setTimeout(() => setMounted(false), 320);
  }
  return () => {
    if (unmountTimer.current) clearTimeout(unmountTimer.current);
    if (savedTimer.current) clearTimeout(savedTimer.current);
  };
  // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps -- defaultPage only matters at the open transition
}, [isOpen]);

// Escape closes; focus moves into the dialog on open.
useEffect(() => {
  if (!isOpen) return;
  const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (event.key === "Escape") onClose();
  };
  document.addEventListener("keydown", onKeyDown);
  panelRef.current?.focus();
  return () => document.removeEventListener("keydown", onKeyDown);
}, [isOpen, onClose]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Closing clears the Saved-toast timers and schedules the unmount timer. Unmounting clears both. The Escape listener is removed whenever `isOpen` goes false. `PlanArtFlame` cancels its rAF, removes its window `pointermove` listener, calls `WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext()` and removes its canvas. The canvas is created inside the effect, so StrictMode's re-run gets a fresh context rather than the dead one. The Storage page clears its pending row-delete and just-added timers on unmount.

**Reduced motion.** Not handled in JavaScript. The open and close transitions, the Saved toast and the scroll fade all run at full duration under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, and the plan card's WebGL flame keeps animating. Only the Storage row enter and exit animations are cut to 1ms by the theme sheet. To honour the setting, add `motion-reduce:transition-none` to the wrapper and backdrop, and gate `PlanArtFlame`'s rAF loop on the media query, drawing one frame instead.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Setting `visible` in the same commit as `mounted`. The panel never renders its hidden pose, so the open snaps in. The double rAF is not a superstition.
- Using `overflow-hidden` on the panel instead of `overflow-clip`. A hidden-overflow box is still programmatically scrollable, so focusing a switch's visually hidden input in a row clipped by the inner scroller scrolls the whole panel and shifts the modal with no way back. `clip` forbids scrolling outright.
- Passing an inline arrow as `onClose` and expecting the Escape listener to stay put. The effect depends on `onClose`, so a new function every render re-binds the listener and re-focuses the panel. Memoise it if the parent re-renders while the dialog is open.
- Rendering the modal inside a transformed or `overflow-hidden` ancestor without a portal container. `fixed inset-0` becomes relative to the transformed ancestor and the dialog is clipped to it. Provide an `UNSAFE_PortalProvider` container or let it fall back to `document.body`.
- Opening many settings dialogs at once in a gallery. Each General page creates its own WebGL context, and Chromium silently drops the oldest one at about 16.

## Notes

- The rows (`SettingsCard`, `SettingsRow`, `SettingsSectionLabel`, `SettingsValueField`) live in `settings-rows.tsx`, so a new page can be added with the same rhythm: 52px rows, a 202px value column and a hairline between rows.
- The Storage page uses data-URI SVGs from `settings-storage-icons.ts` in place of BoardUI's `/public` artwork, so the item works without static assets.
- `SettingsProfile` uses `@internationalized/date` for its birth-date picker. That is why the date package is a direct dependency even though the modal shell never touches dates.

## Definition of done

Nothing is on screen until the trigger is clicked. Opening scales the dialog up from about 85% while it fades in and sharpens, behind a 70% black backdrop. Clicking the backdrop, the round close button or pressing Escape plays the same motion in reverse, and the DOM is gone afterwards. Rail items with pages switch the content and highlight the selected row. Scrolling a page fades in a gradient under the title. On General, the plan card's artwork ripples and burns at the edges, and the burn intensifies near the cursor. On Profile, changing a name and pressing Enter shows a "Saved" pill that rises in across the bottom edge and drifts up and away after about 2 seconds. On Storage, sorting, filtering, paging, selecting and deleting rows all work, and deleted rows collapse upward.
