# Build: Slider

One shared `SliderBase` drawn over React Aria's `Slider`, exported as `Slider` (one thumb) and `RangeSlider` (two). React Aria owns the value model, pointer dragging, keyboard steps, hidden range inputs, RTL and thumb collision. The component owns the look: a 6px rail, an accent gradient fill between the thumbs, 20px thumbs that grow while dragged, and an exact-value bubble with a pointer that lifts while its thumb is active.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Single and min/max sliders on React Aria: a gradient fill, thumbs that grow while dragged, and a value bubble above each thumb.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `AriaSlider` gets the consumer's props plus a forced `orientation="horizontal"`. Its render prop exposes `state`, and `isRange` is simply `state.values.length > 1`.
2. The fill is a positioned span. Its `insetInlineStart` is `state.getThumbPercent(0)` for a range or 0 for a single slider, and its `insetInlineEnd` is `1 - getThumbPercent(last)`. Logical insets make the fill grow from the right in RTL with no extra code.
3. Each value in `state.values` renders an `AriaSliderThumb` with `index`. Its `aria-label` comes from `thumbLabels[index]` (default "Value", or "Minimum" and "Maximum"), so each thumb is named for what it changes and not by its position.
4. Thumb states come from React Aria's render props. Hover gives `scale-105` and a darker border. Dragging gives `scale-110`, an accent border, an accent-tinted shadow and `z-20`, so the active thumb sits above the other where they overlap. All of it eases over 150ms via `transition-[scale,box-shadow,border-color]`.
5. With `showTooltip` (the default), each thumb holds a bubble at `bottom-[calc(100%+9px)]` that shows `formatValue(value, index)`, or `state.getThumbValueLabel(index)` when there is no formatter. A rotated 8px square draws its pointer. While the thumb is dragged or focused the bubble rises 2px (`-translate-y-0.5`) and picks up `shadow-dropdown`. The track adds `mt-8` so the bubble has room above it.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `track = h-8 hit area, h-1.5 rail`
  The visible rail is 6px, but the track element is 32px tall, so a click slightly above or below the rail still moves the thumb.
- `thumb = size-5 (20px) with an 8px accent dot; scale 1.05 hover, 1.1 drag`
  Twenty pixels is the Figma size and a comfortable pointer target. The grow-on-drag is small enough to keep the thumb centred on the value and still visible under a finger.
- `bubble offset = bottom-[calc(100%+9px)], h-7, lift -2px`
  Nine pixels clears the thumb's scaled size plus the pointer. The 2px lift shows which bubble belongs to the thumb you are holding.
- `transition = 150ms ease`
  Short enough that the thumb still feels attached to the pointer while scale and shadow change underneath it.

## API

```ts
function Slider(props: Omit<AriaSliderProps<number>, "children" | "className" | "orientation"> & { label?: ReactNode; showTooltip?: boolean; formatValue?: (value: number, index: number) => ReactNode; className?: string; thumbLabel?: string }): JSX.Element; function RangeSlider(props: Omit<AriaSliderProps<number[]>, "children" | "className" | "orientation"> & { label?: ReactNode; showTooltip?: boolean; formatValue?: (value: number, index: number) => ReactNode; className?: string; thumbLabels?: [string, string] }): JSX.Element
```

- `label: ReactNode`
  Visible label above the track, wired to every thumb.
- `value / defaultValue / onChange: number | number[]`
  React Aria value props. `Slider` takes a number, `RangeSlider` a two-item array.
- `onChangeEnd: (value) => void`
  Fires once when a drag or key press ends. Use it for saving.
- `minValue / maxValue / step: number` — default `0 / 100 / 1`
  Range and step size.
- `showTooltip: boolean` — default `true`
  Show the value bubble above each thumb.
- `formatValue: (value: number, index: number) => ReactNode`
  Visual text for the bubble only.
- `thumbLabel: string` — default `"Value"`
  `Slider` only: accessible name for the thumb.
- `thumbLabels: [string, string]` — default `["Minimum", "Maximum"]`
  `RangeSlider` only: accessible names for the two thumbs.
- `isDisabled: boolean`
  Dims to 50% and shows a not-allowed cursor.
- `className: string`
  Classes on the root column.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
function SliderBase<T extends SliderValue>({
  className,
  label,
  showTooltip = true,
  formatValue,
  thumbLabels,
  ...props
}: SliderBaseInternalProps<T>) {
  return (
    <AriaSlider
      {...props}
      orientation="horizontal"
      className={({ isDisabled }) =>
        cx(
          "group flex w-full min-w-0 flex-col gap-2",
          isDisabled && "cursor-not-allowed opacity-50",
          className,
        )
      }
    >
      {({ state }) => {
        const isRange = state.values.length > 1;
        const startPercent = isRange ? state.getThumbPercent(0) : 0;
        const endPercent = state.getThumbPercent(state.values.length - 1);

        return (
          <>
            {label != null && (
              <AriaLabel className="text-body-medium text-text-primary">
                {label}
              </AriaLabel>
            )}

            <AriaSliderTrack
              className={cx(
                "relative h-8 w-full touch-none",
                showTooltip && "mt-8",
              )}
            >
              {({ isHovered }) => (
                <>
                  <span
                    aria-hidden
                    className={cx(
                      "absolute top-1/2 end-0 start-0 h-1.5 -translate-y-1/2 rounded-full",
                      "bg-background-tertiary-default shadow-[inset_0_1px_1px_rgb(0_0_0/0.06)]",
                      "transition-colors duration-150 ease",
                      isHovered && "bg-background-tertiary-hover",
                    )}
                  />
                  <span
                    aria-hidden
                    className={cx(
                      "absolute top-1/2 h-1.5 -translate-y-1/2 rounded-full",
                      "bg-linear-to-r from-accent-500 to-accent-600",
                      "shadow-[inset_0_1px_0_rgb(255_255_255/0.24),0_1px_2px_rgb(4_80_226/0.16)]",
                    )}
                    style={{
                      insetInlineStart: `${startPercent * 100}%`,
                      insetInlineEnd: `${(1 - endPercent) * 100}%`,
                    }}
                  />

                  {state.values.map((value, index) => {
                    const valueLabel =
                      formatValue?.(value, index) ??
                      state.getThumbValueLabel(index);

                    return (
                      <AriaSliderThumb
                        key={index}
                        index={index}
                        aria-label={
                          thumbLabels[index] ??
                          (isRange ? `Value ${index + 1}` : "Value")
                        }
                        className={({
                          isDragging,
                          isHovered: isThumbHovered,
                          isFocusVisible,
                          isDisabled,
                        }) =>
                          cx(
                            "top-1/2 size-5 rounded-full border border-border-button-default outline-none",
                            "flex items-center justify-center bg-control-indicator-background",
                            "shadow-[0_2px_4px_rgb(0_0_0/0.10),inset_0_1px_0_rgb(255_255_255/0.8)]",
                            "transition-[scale,box-shadow,border-color] duration-150 ease",
                            isThumbHovered && !isDragging && "scale-105 border-border-button-hover",
                            isDragging && "z-20 scale-110 border-accent-500 shadow-[0_3px_8px_color-mix(in_srgb,var(--color-accent-600)_22%,transparent)]",
                            isFocusVisible && "ring-2 ring-border-focus-ring ring-offset-2",
                            isDisabled ? "cursor-not-allowed" : "cursor-grab active:cursor-grabbing",
                          )
                        }
                      >
                        {({ isDragging, isFocused }) => (
                          <>
                            {showTooltip && (
                              <span
                                aria-hidden
                                className={cx(
                                  "pointer-events-none absolute bottom-[calc(100%+9px)] left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2",
                                  "flex h-7 min-w-8 items-center justify-center rounded-lg border border-border-button-default",
                                  "bg-background-primary-default px-2 text-caption-1-medium whitespace-nowrap text-text-primary shadow-xs",
                                  "transition-[translate,box-shadow] duration-150 ease",
                                  (isDragging || isFocused) && "-translate-y-0.5 shadow-dropdown",
                                )}
                              >
                                {valueLabel}
                                <span
                                  aria-hidden
                                  className="absolute -bottom-[4.5px] left-1/2 size-2 -translate-x-1/2 rotate-45 border-r border-b border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default"
                                />
                              </span>
                            )}
                            <span
                              aria-hidden
                              className={cx(
                                "size-2 rounded-full bg-linear-to-b from-accent-500 to-accent-600",
                                "shadow-[inset_0_1px_0_rgb(255_255_255/0.24)] transition-[filter] duration-150 ease",
                                (isDragging || isFocused) && "brightness-110",
                              )}
                            />
                          </>
                        )}
                      </AriaSliderThumb>
                    );
                  })}
                </>
              )}
            </AriaSliderTrack>
          </>
        );
      }}
    </AriaSlider>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No effects or listeners of its own. React Aria attaches its pointer move and up listeners on drag start and removes them when the drag ends or the slider unmounts.

**Reduced motion.** The thumb follows the pointer directly, with no tween, so dragging is the same under any setting. The hover and drag scale, shadow and bubble lift are 150ms CSS transitions of a few pixels. They are kept under `prefers-reduced-motion` because they report state, and `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the root removes them.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Leaving out both `label` and `aria-label`. React Aria logs a warning and the group is unnamed. `thumbLabel` names only the thumb, not the slider.
- Setting `showTooltip={false}` and expecting the space above to stay. The track drops its `mt-8`, so any layout that depended on that height moves up.
- Returning a long string from `formatValue`. The bubble is `whitespace-nowrap`, so wide text spreads sideways and can collide with the other thumb's bubble when the values are close.

## Notes

- `RangeSlider` keeps the thumbs from crossing because React Aria clamps each one to its neighbour. `minValue`, `maxValue`, `step` and `formatOptions` pass straight through.
- The value bubble is `aria-hidden`. Screen readers hear React Aria's value text from the hidden range input, so use `formatOptions` when the spoken value should be formatted too (currency, percent).

## Definition of done

Dragging the volume thumb moves the bubble and fill with it, the thumb grows slightly and its border turns accent, and the summary line updates on every frame. The range thumbs cannot cross, the fill always runs between them, and the dragged thumb sits above the other where they overlap. Tab focuses a thumb and lifts its bubble, and the arrow keys step by 100 on the budget. In RTL the fill grows from the right. No accessibility warning appears in the console.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Slow Idle Float

The ambient motion you put on a hero image, a floating card or a badge so the page does not feel frozen. Fourteen pixels over five seconds is under the threshold at which the eye tracks it as movement — you read it as presence. Because it animates `translate` rather than `transform`, the element can still carry a hover scale or a tilt without the two fighting.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A 14px rise and fall over 5 seconds, on the independent translate property so hover transforms still work.

- Category: primitive
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. A two-pose keyframe: `0%, 100% { translate: 0 0 }` and `50% { translate: var(--kx-float-x) var(--kx-float-y) }`. Both endpoints of the round trip are the resting position, so the loop has no seam and the element always returns to exactly its layout position.
2. The animated property is `translate`, not `transform`. They are separate properties that compose in the order translate, rotate, scale, transform — so a consumer can put `hover:scale-105` (a `transform`) on the same element and both apply. An animation on `transform` would instead override any transition on `transform` for its entire duration, and the hover would appear dead.
3. Direction comes from custom properties rather than separate keyframe blocks: `axis="y"` writes `--kx-float-y: -14px` and leaves X at 0, `axis="x"` does the reverse. One keyframe block covers both axes and any diagonal a consumer wants to set by hand.
4. `phase` is applied as a negative `animation-delay` — `-durationMs * phase`. A negative delay means the animation is treated as having already been running for that long, so an element starts mid-flight on its first painted frame. A positive delay would make it sit dead still until its turn came round, which is exactly what makes staggered idle animations look broken on load.
5. `ease-in-out` is what makes it buoyant. The element decelerates into both extremes and hangs there; `linear` gives constant velocity and reads as a mechanical lift.
6. `will-change: translate` names the property that is actually animating. `will-change: transform` — the reflex — hints at a property this component never touches.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `distance = 14px`
  Peak travel. Average speed works out at roughly 11px per second, which is below the rate at which the eye starts tracking an object instead of just registering it. Under about 6px the motion is invisible on a 1x display; over about 24px it reads as a balloon on a string and pulls focus from the content.
- `durationMs = 5000`
  The round trip. Faster than about 3s and it becomes a pulse that competes with real feedback in the UI; slower than about 8s and the element appears to have simply drifted out of position rather than to be floating.
- `timing function = ease-in-out`
  Buoyancy comes from the hold at the two extremes. `linear` moves at constant velocity, which reads as a machine; `ease-out` alone makes the return leg abrupt and the loop develops a visible tick at 100%.
- `phase sign = negative`
  Negative delay starts the animation partway through its first cycle instead of postponing it. With a positive delay a staggered group is motionless for the first phase*duration milliseconds after mount — on a five-second cycle with four items that is several seconds of a page that looks frozen.

## API

```ts
function SlowFloatIdle(props: { children: ReactNode; distance?: number; durationMs?: number; axis?: 'x' | 'y'; phase?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  What floats. Wrapped in a block-level element that owns the `translate`.
- `distance: number` — default `14`
  Peak travel in pixels, reached at the midpoint of the cycle.
- `durationMs: number` — default `5000`
  Full round trip in milliseconds.
- `axis: 'x' | 'y'` — default `'y'`
  Direction of travel. `y` rises then falls; `x` drifts right then back.
- `phase: number` — default `0`
  Start position in the cycle, 0-1. Applied as a negative `animation-delay`.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the wrapper via `cn`. Safe to use `transform`-based utilities here — the float does not use `transform`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const FLOAT_CSS = `
@keyframes kx-float-idle {
  0%, 100% { translate: 0 0; }
  50%      { translate: var(--kx-float-x, 0px) var(--kx-float-y, -14px); }
}

.kx-float {
  display: block;
  animation: kx-float-idle var(--kx-float-duration, 5s) ease-in-out infinite;
  animation-delay: var(--kx-float-delay, 0s);
  /* Names the property that is actually animating. 'will-change: transform'
     is the reflex here and it hints at the wrong property entirely. */
  will-change: translate;
}

/* No motion: the element rests at its natural layout position, not at the
   midpoint of the float. The hint is released too — a promoted layer for an
   animation that is not running is pure GPU memory. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .kx-float {
    animation: none;
    will-change: auto;
  }
}
`;

export function SlowFloatIdle({
  children,
  distance = 14,
  durationMs = 5000,
  axis = 'y',
  phase = 0,
  className,
}: SlowFloatIdleProps) {
  const style: StyleWithVars = {
    '--kx-float-duration': `${durationMs}ms`,
    // Negative: the animation is treated as having already run for this long,
    // so a set of floats is out of phase from the very first frame.
    '--kx-float-delay': `${-durationMs * phase}ms`,
    // Rise, not fall: negative Y is up. X drifts right on the positive side.
    '--kx-float-x': axis === 'x' ? `${distance}px` : '0px',
    '--kx-float-y': axis === 'y' ? `${-distance}px` : '0px',
  };

  return (
    <>
      <style href="kinetic-slow-float-idle" precedence="medium">
        {FLOAT_CSS}
      </style>
      <div className={cn('kx-float', className)} style={style}>
        {children}
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. No listeners, no timers, no animation frames. Unmounting removes the element and its CSS animation; React removes the hoisted `<style>` when the last instance unmounts.

**Reduced motion.** A `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block sets `animation: none` and `will-change: auto`. The element rests at its natural layout position — not at the top of the float — so nothing shifts and no gap appears where the animation used to be.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Animating `transform` instead of `translate`. Animations beat transitions on the same property for as long as they run, so a `transition: transform` hover on the same element never has a visible effect — the hover looks broken and the cause is a keyframe elsewhere in the file.
- Animating `top` or `margin-top` for the float. Those are layout properties: the ancestor reflows on every frame and any sibling laid out after it jitters. Only `translate`, `transform`, `opacity` and `filter` stay off the layout path.
- Staggering a group with positive `animation-delay`. Every element holds at its 0% pose until its delay expires, so the group starts as a static row and comes alive one item at a time — most visible right after a page load, which is the worst possible moment.
- Setting `will-change: transform` for an animation on `translate`. The hint names a property that never changes; the browser may still promote the layer for other reasons, so the mistake produces no error and no benefit.
- Leaving `will-change` on when reduced motion is active. The element keeps a dedicated compositor layer for an animation that has been switched off — cost with no motion in exchange.
- Parking the element at the midpoint of the float for reduced motion. The float exists to add life, not to reposition anything; freezing it 14px above its layout position leaves a permanent, unexplained gap under the element.

## Notes

- The independent `translate`, `rotate` and `scale` properties need Chrome 104+, Safari 14.1+ and Firefox 72+. In an older engine the declaration is dropped and the element simply does not float — the layout is unaffected.
- The wrapper is a `div` with `display: block`. To float an inline element, pass `className="inline-block"`; a floated `display: inline` box would have nothing to translate.
- For a group, give each instance a different `phase` — 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 for four items. Equal phases make the group move as one rigid object, which is more noticeable than no motion at all.

## Definition of done

The element rises about 14px, hangs, and settles back over five seconds with no visible tick at the loop point. Add a `hover:scale-110` to the same element and the scale still works while the float continues. Give three instances phases 0, 0.33 and 0.66 and all three are already at different heights on the first painted frame. With reduced motion on, the element sits exactly where the layout puts it.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Social Button

A "Continue with …" button where the brand is named rather than passed as artwork: `brand="github"` pulls the glyph, the brand colour and the label from one table, so a stack of providers cannot drift out of sync. Three appearances share one shape: `colorful` fills with a gradient derived from the brand colour, `black` is solid high-contrast, and `white` is the outlined secondary surface that shows each provider's real multi-colour mark. Passing `href` renders an anchor, because starting OAuth is a navigation.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Sign-in button for 24 named providers: one brand prop supplies logo, colour and label, in colourful, black or outlined styles.

- Category: action
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. `SOCIAL_PROVIDERS` maps 24 providers to `{ label, brand, viewBox, path }`. The glyphs are monochrome single paths painted with `currentColor` (Simple Icons, CC0, on a 24 grid; Bootstrap Icons, MIT, on a 16 grid for LinkedIn, Slack, Microsoft and Amazon). Each keeps its own `viewBox`, and the button scales whichever grid it gets into the same 18 or 16px box.
2. For `appearance="white"` the button looks up `SOCIAL_COLOR_LOGOS` instead: real multi-path marks with their own fills (gilbarbara/logos, CC0), injected with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` from a build-time constant. Amazon has no plain mark upstream, so it falls back to the monochrome glyph tinted with its brand colour. Apple, GitHub and X are drawn near-black, so in dark mode `dark:[&_path]:fill-white` repaints them white.
3. `colorful` builds its gradient inline per brand: `linear-gradient(180deg, fill, oklch(from fill calc(l − 0.04) calc(c + 0.01) h))`. The second stop is the brand colour 4% darker and slightly more saturated, which is the same step the kit's primary button takes from blue-500 to blue-600. Hover and press adjust `brightness` (1.06 and 0.95) instead of swapping gradients.
4. A brand whose colour is a CSS variable (Google is `var(--color-accent-500)`) skips the inline gradient and takes `bg-button-primary`, so it is exactly the kit's primary button, including its hover gradient layer, rather than an approximation of it.
5. Sizes copy `Button` to the pixel (36px with a 10px radius, 32px with 8px) and add a fixed width (300 or 250px) so a column of providers lines up without a wrapper; `fullWidth` swaps that for `w-full`. With `iconOnly` the label is hidden and the element receives `aria-label="Continue with <Label>"` so it is never announced unlabelled.
6. `brand="custom"` takes `config: { icon, label, color }` for anything not built in. The label defaults to "SSO" and the colour to black.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `gradient end stop = oklch(from fill calc(l - 0.04) calc(c + 0.01) h)`
  Darkening in OKLCH keeps the hue stable. Mixing toward black in sRGB would wash out saturated brands such as Spotify green or Twitch purple and turn them muddy at the bottom edge.
- `hover and press brightness = 1.06 / 0.95`
  A per-brand hover gradient would need 24 more colours. A brightness filter gives every brand a consistent, subtle lift and dip from the one colour it already has.
- `fixed widths = 300px (medium) / 250px (small)`
  "Continue with Microsoft" is the longest built-in label and fits at both sizes. A fixed width lets a stack of providers align without each caller adding a wrapper.
- `glyph sizes = 18px / 16px`
  One step below Button's 20 / 18px icons. A filled brand mark is denser than a line icon and reads heavier at the same size.

## API

```ts
function SocialButton(props: SocialButtonProps | SocialButtonLinkProps): JSX.Element
// shared: { brand: SocialProvider | "custom"; config?: { icon: ReactNode; label?: string; color?: string }; size?: "medium" | "small"; appearance?: "colorful" | "black" | "white"; iconOnly?: boolean; fullWidth?: boolean; children?: ReactNode; className?: string }
// SocialButtonProps: Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "children" | "color"> & { href?: never; ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement> }
// SocialButtonLinkProps: Omit<AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement>, "children" | "color"> & { href: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLAnchorElement> }
const SOCIAL_PROVIDERS: Record<SocialProvider, { label: string; brand: string; viewBox: string; path: string }>
```

- `brand: SocialProvider | "custom"`
  Required. One of 24 providers (google, apple, github, gitlab, microsoft, x, facebook, linkedin, discord, slack, figma, notion, dropbox, spotify, twitch, reddit, tiktok, instagram, telegram, whatsapp, amazon, bitbucket, auth0, okta) or `custom`.
- `appearance: "colorful" | "black" | "white"` — default `"colorful"`
  Brand-colour gradient with a white glyph, solid black, or the outlined surface with the full-colour mark.
- `size: "medium" | "small"` — default `"medium"`
  36px tall and 300px wide, or 32px and 250px.
- `iconOnly: boolean` — default `false`
  Square logo-only button. The label moves to `aria-label`.
- `fullWidth: boolean` — default `false`
  Fill the container instead of the fixed width.
- `config: { icon: ReactNode; label?: string; color?: string }`
  Required for `brand="custom"`, ignored otherwise.
- `href: string`
  Renders an `<a>` instead of a `<button>`, for OAuth redirects.
- `children: ReactNode` — default `"Continue with <Label>"`
  Overrides the visible label.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function SocialButton({ href, ...props }: SocialButtonProps | SocialButtonLinkProps) {
  const {
    brand,
    config,
    size = "medium",
    appearance = "colorful",
    iconOnly = false,
    fullWidth = false,
    children,
    className,
    ref,
    ...rest
  } = props as SocialButtonBaseProps & {
    ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement & HTMLAnchorElement>;
  } & Record<string, unknown>;

  const custom = brand === "custom";
  const meta = custom ? undefined : SOCIAL_PROVIDERS[brand as SocialProvider];
  const label = custom ? (config?.label ?? "SSO") : meta!.label;
  const fill = custom ? (config?.color ?? "#000000") : meta!.brand;

  // The outlined treatment is where the real multi-colour mark belongs: on a
  // brand or black fill it would fight the background. Not every provider has
  // one upstream (see social-color-logos.ts), so a missing mark falls back to
  // the monochrome glyph tinted with the brand colour.
  const colorLogo =
    appearance === "white" && !custom
      ? SOCIAL_COLOR_LOGOS[brand as SocialProvider]
      : undefined;

  const glyph = custom ? (
    <span className={cx(styles.glyph[size], "inline-flex items-center justify-center")}>
      {config?.icon}
    </span>
  ) : colorLogo ? (
    <svg
      viewBox={colorLogo.viewBox}
      aria-hidden
      className={cx(
        styles.glyph[size],
        DARK_INVERTED_BRANDS.has(brand) && "dark:[&_path]:fill-white",
      )}
      // The mark carries its own fills, so it goes in as markup. This is a
      // build-time constant from this repo, never caller- or user-supplied.
      dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: colorLogo.body }}
    />
  ) : (
    <svg
      viewBox={meta!.viewBox}
      aria-hidden
      className={styles.glyph[size]}
      // On the filled appearances the glyph rides the white label; outlined
      // falls back to the brand colour so it is not a grey smudge.
      style={appearance === "white" ? { color: meta!.brand } : undefined}
    >
      <path d={meta!.path} fill="currentColor" />
    </svg>
  );

  const content = (
    <>
      {glyph}
      {iconOnly ? null : <span className="truncate">{children ?? `Continue with ${label}`}</span>}
    </>
  );

  // A brand whose colour is a system token (Google) hands the fill straight
  // to `bg-button-primary`, so it is the primary button, gradient, hover and
  // active included, rather than an approximation of it. Every other brand
  // gets that gradient's shape derived from its own colour: down in
  // lightness and up slightly in chroma, which is what blue-500 → blue-600
  // does. Mixing toward black instead would wash the second stop out.
  const systemFill = appearance === "colorful" && fill.startsWith("var(");

  const classes = cx(
    styles.base,
    iconOnly ? styles.iconOnlySize[size] : styles.size[size],
    styles.appearance[appearance],
    // `bg-button-primary` carries its own hover and active gradients; the
    // derived brands need the brightness shift instead.
    systemFill
      ? "bg-button-primary"
      : appearance === "colorful" && "hover:brightness-[1.06] active:brightness-95",
    fullWidth && !iconOnly && "w-full",
    className,
  );

  // The visible label already names the brand; when it is hidden the element
  // needs that name back, or the control announces as unlabelled.
  const accessibleName = iconOnly ? `Continue with ${label}` : undefined;

  const inlineStyle =
    appearance === "colorful" && !systemFill
      ? {
          backgroundImage: `linear-gradient(180deg, ${fill} 0%, oklch(from ${fill} calc(l - 0.04) calc(c + 0.01) h) 100%)`,
        }
      : undefined;

  if (href !== undefined) {
    return (
      <a
        ref={ref as Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>}
        href={href}
        aria-label={accessibleName}
        className={classes}
        style={inlineStyle}
        {...(rest as AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement>)}
      >
        {content}
      </a>
    );
  }

  return (
    <button
      ref={ref as Ref<HTMLButtonElement>}
      type="button"
      aria-label={accessibleName}
      className={classes}
      style={inlineStyle}
      {...(rest as ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>)}
    >
      {content}
    </button>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component is stateless markup with no listeners, timers or effects.

**Reduced motion.** The press scale from `button-press-motion` is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Hover still brightens or changes the fill, because that colour feedback carries meaning and does not move anything.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Passing a `style` prop. It is spread after the computed inline style, so it replaces the brand gradient and the colourful button turns transparent with white text.
- Relying on the colourful gradient in older browsers. Relative colour syntax (`oklch(from …)`) is invalid where unsupported, which drops the whole `background-image`. Use `appearance="white"` or `black` if you must support those engines.
- Writing the label yourself as "Sign in with Google" in only some buttons. Leave `children` empty and every provider gets the same "Continue with <Label>" wording.
- Using `brand="custom"` without `config`. The button then renders "Continue with SSO" on a black fill with no logo.
- Shipping without checking each provider's brand guidelines. Google and Apple in particular publish rules on wording, colour and clear space for sign-in buttons.

## Notes

- The outlined `white` appearance with full-colour marks is what most sign-in screens use. `colorful` suits a single prominent provider; `black` suits monochrome layouts.
- `SOCIAL_PROVIDERS` and the `SocialProvider` type are re-exported, so a settings page can list connected accounts with the same glyphs and labels.

## Definition of done

The outlined stack shows Google's four-colour G, Apple and GitHub marks that turn white in dark mode, and three equal-width rows reading "Continue with …". The filled column shows Google in the kit's exact primary-button blue, Discord in its own purple, slightly darker at the bottom edge, and Apple in solid black. Hover brightens Discord without a colour jump. Icon-only buttons are 36px squares, and a screen reader announces "Continue with GitHub". At 360px wide nothing overflows the frame.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Speedometer Chart Card

A dashboard card with a half gauge that opens at the bottom. The `segments` look stacks one round-capped segment per item around a gray track, with a small gap between neighbours, and writes the primary item's share in the centre ("47%" over "Desktop"). The segments sweep in from the left end on mount and re-proportion on a period change. Hovering, focusing or tapping a segment darkens it one tone, fades the others, swaps the count-up headline to that item and moves the centre to its share; a click or Enter makes it the primary. The `needle` look draws one value arc in the item's colour over a tick scale, with a needle that swings to every new value, the value under the hub and min/max labels at the arc ends.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A 220° half gauge in the dashboard card shell: stacked segments with the main share in the centre, or a value arc and needle.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. The gauge is an inline SVG drawn 1:1 in a 280 × 212 box, centred on (140, 134) with a 110px radius. Angles run clockwise from twelve o'clock, from −110° to +110° (a 220° sweep), and `polar(θ, r)` maps them to `(140 + r·sin θ, 134 − r·cos θ)`. `arcPath` writes one SVG `A` command between two angles, with the large-arc flag set past 180°.
2. For `segments`, the items become cumulative boundaries (0..1 of the total) that go through `useTweenedValues`, a 520ms ease-out cubic tween from 0 on mount and from the current boundaries on a period change. `layoutSegments` turns them into angles: a 6px gap (6/110 rad) between neighbours, scaled by the last boundary so the gaps open as the gauge sweeps in, and the rest of the sweep shared by value.
3. Each segment path is inset by the round cap's half-width (14/110 rad) at both ends, so the caps land exactly on the segment's extent and the gaps stay clean. The gray track is inset the same way, so no track shows past the first and last segments. A segment too short for its two caps becomes a dot centred on its extent, as wide as the extent (at least 4px).
4. Each segment is a `<g role="button" tabIndex=0 aria-pressed>`. Pointer enter and focus set the active item, leaving the gauge or blurring clears it, and click or Enter/Space call `onPrimaryChange` (or set the uncontrolled primary). The active segment switches to the darker `--color-chart-N-active` tone, the others fade to 0.35 opacity over 200ms, and a keyboard focus draws a focus-ring halo under the segment.
5. The centre is an HTML overlay over the SVG with `aria-live="polite"`. It shows the share of the hovered item, or else the primary item, in `text-display-4`, and remounts on every change so the shell's number fade plays. The header shows the total and the delta chip at rest; on hover it shows the item, its value and "x% of total".
6. For `needle`, the value is the `value` prop or else the shown item's share in percent, mapped to 0..1 of `min`..`max`. The fraction goes through `useTweenedValues` over 700ms. The value arc runs from the left end to the needle angle in the shown item's colour, and the needle polygon is drawn pointing up and rotated about the hub by that angle, so the arc and the needle move together. Eleven ticks mark every 10% (the 0, 50 and 100% ticks are longer), and the min/max labels sit under the arc ends.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `W × H = 280 × 212px, centre (140, 134), radius 110`
  Drawn 1:1 so the centre overlay is placed in plain CSS px with no viewBox scaling, and the arc ends and their labels fit under the hub.
- `START / SWEEP = −110° / 220°`
  Opens the gauge at the bottom like the preview, with room for the centre value inside the arc.
- `SEG_STROKE / NEEDLE_STROKE = 28px / 16px`
  Thick segments read as a stacked gauge; the needle look uses a thinner band so the ticks and needle stay the focus.
- `GAP_PX = 6px`
  A visible break between round-capped neighbours. It is scaled by the sweep progress so it does not show before the gauge fills.
- `NEEDLE_MS = 700ms ease-out cubic`
  Slower than the 520ms segment tween, so the needle reads as a swing rather than a jump.

## API


## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * One stacked segment. Its visible extent is [from, to]; the path is inset
 * by the cap's half-width at both ends so the round caps land exactly on the
 * extent and neighbours keep a clean gap. Too short for its caps, it becomes
 * a dot as wide as the extent allows, centred on it.
 */
function SegmentView({
  item,
  index,
  segment,
  color,
  active,
  primary,
  focusVisible,
  label,
  onTarget,
  onFocusVisible,
  onSelect,
}: SegmentViewProps) {
  const span = segment.to - segment.from;
  if (span <= 0.0001) return null;
  const tone = CHART_COLORS[color];
  const isActive = active === index;
  const dimmed = active !== null && !isActive;
  const cap = SEG_STROKE / 2 / R;
  const fits = span > cap * 2;
  const mid = (segment.from + segment.to) / 2;
  const d = fits ? arcPath(segment.from + cap, segment.to - cap, R) : arcPath(mid, mid, R);
  const width = fits ? SEG_STROKE : Math.max(4, span * R);

  const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent<SVGGElement>) => {
    if (event.key !== "Enter" && event.key !== " ") return;
    event.preventDefault();
    onSelect();
  };

  return (
    <g
      role="button"
      tabIndex={0}
      aria-label={label}
      aria-pressed={primary}
      data-segment={item.label}
      className="cursor-pointer outline-none"
      onPointerEnter={() => onTarget(index)}
      onFocus={(event) => {
        onTarget(index);
        onFocusVisible(event.currentTarget.matches(":focus-visible") ? index : null);
      }}
      onBlur={() => {
        onTarget(null);
        onFocusVisible(null);
      }}
      onClick={onSelect}
      onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
    >
      {focusVisible ? (
        <path d={d} fill="none" stroke="var(--color-border-focus-ring)" strokeWidth={width + 6} strokeLinecap="round" />
      ) : null}
      <path
        d={d}
        fill="none"
        stroke={isActive ? tone.active : tone.fill}
        strokeWidth={width}
        strokeLinecap="round"
        opacity={dimmed ? 0.35 : 1}
        className="transition-[stroke,opacity] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none"
      />
    </g>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The segment and needle tweens and the headline's count-up cancel their animation frame on every new target and on unmount. Hover, focus and the primary are plain React state on SVG elements, with no document listeners.

**Reduced motion.** `useTweenedValues` is disabled for both looks, so the segments render at their final extents and the needle sits at its value, jumping on a change. The stroke/opacity fades use `motion-reduce:transition-none`, and the centre number fade is off (`motion-reduce:animate-none`).

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Drawing round-capped segments edge to edge. The caps then overlap the neighbours by half the stroke on each side. Inset each path by the cap's half-width so the visible extent is exactly the segment.
- Opening the gaps from the first frame. On mount every segment then starts as a dot at its gap position. Scaling the gap with the last boundary makes the whole gauge sweep in from one end.
- Rotating the needle with a CSS transition while the arc is tweened in JS. The two then drift apart mid-swing. Drive both from the same tweened fraction.

## Notes

- `SPEEDOMETER_RANGES`, `GaugeItem`, `GaugeRange` and `SpeedometerVariant` are exported. Pass `items` (and `delta`) for one static list without the period select.
- Pass `value` with `min`/`max` to use the needle look as a plain gauge for any number, and `formatGaugeValue` for the units.
- The frame, header, period select and stat tiles come from `funnel-chart-card-shell`.

## Definition of done

The card shows "Visitors", "2,500", a lime "+5.2%" chip and a "Last 7 days" select. Under it is a half gauge with lime, blue, purple and pink segments (Desktop, Mobile, Tablet, TV) separated by small gaps, with "47%" over "Desktop" in the centre, and four tiles: Desktop 1,180, Mobile 620, Tablet 380 and TV 320. Hovering the Mobile tile fades the other segments and tiles, the header reads "Mobile", "620" and "25% of total", and the centre reads "25%" over "Mobile". In the Needle look the needle and a lime arc point at 47%, "0%" and "100%" sit under the arc ends, and picking Mobile swings the needle back to 25%. "Last 30 days" re-proportions the segments, and the headline counts to 10,000.

# Build: Spinner

A spinner for work of unknown length, drawn as a comet of light: the same arc at three scales (a crisp line with a rounded head, a tight glow and a wide bloom), each softer layer shorter and a few degrees behind, over a faint full-circle track. Everything paints in `currentColor`, so a text class sets the colour. `Spinner` is announced as an indeterminate React Aria progress bar labelled "Loading"; `SpinnerGlyph` is the bare visual.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

An orbiting light in three layers (crisp arc, tight glow, wide bloom) in five sizes and any text colour, announced as loading.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Look up the box and line width from `SIZES`: xs 12/1.5, sm 16/2, md 20/2, lg 24/2.5, xl 32/3 px. Render a `relative inline-flex shrink-0 text-accent-500` span at that box size.
2. If `track` is on, draw the full circle as an `absolute inset-0 rounded-full border-current opacity-15` span with `borderWidth: line`.
3. Each `Arc` paints `conic-gradient(transparent ${360 - arc}deg, currentColor 360deg)` so the arc ends at 12 o'clock, then masks it to a ring with a `radial-gradient` that is opaque between `center ± width/2` (with `center = box/2 - line/2`). Its wrapper is grown by `bleed = max(0, outer + blur*2 - box/2)` on every side so the blur never clips, then gets `filter: blur()`, `opacity` and `rotate: -lag deg`.
4. Stack three arcs inside one `animate-spin [animation-duration:900ms]` layer: bloom (width line×4, blur line×1.6, opacity 0.32, 110°, 22° behind), glow (width line×2, blur line×0.6, opacity 0.6, 200°, 9° behind) and crisp (width line, no blur, opacity 1, 290°, 0°). The shorter, lagging soft layers make the glow gather just behind the sharp head.
5. Finish the head with a `line × line` `rounded-full bg-current` dot at `left-1/2 top-0` (`translate: -50% 0`), the leading end of the crisp arc.
6. `Spinner` wraps the glyph in React Aria's `<ProgressBar isIndeterminate aria-label="Loading">`, giving it `role="progressbar"`. With `aria-hidden` it returns the bare `SpinnerGlyph`, for when a parent control already announces the wait.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `SIZES = xs 12/1.5, sm 16/2, md 20/2, lg 24/2.5, xl 32/3 (box/line px)`
  Sm and md match the kit's 16px and 20px icon slots, so a spinner can replace a button icon without changing the button height. Line width grows slower than the box so small spinners do not turn into solid discs.
- `layers = bloom 4×line, blur 1.6×line, 0.32, 110°, lag 22° / glow 2×line, blur 0.6×line, 0.6, 200°, lag 9° / crisp 1×line, 1, 290°, lag 0°`
  Shorter and later soft layers keep the bright head in front and the glow trailing like a comet's tail. Scaling everything by `line` keeps the look identical from 12 to 32px.
- `orbit = 900ms per turn; 2400ms under reduced motion`
  Under a second reads as active work. The reduced-motion orbit slows rather than stops, because a frozen spinner reads as a hang.
- `track = opacity-15 border in currentColor`
  Faint enough to sit behind the light, but it completes the circle so the 290° arc never reads as a broken ring.

## API

```ts

interface SpinnerProps { size?: SpinnerSize; track?: boolean; "aria-label"?: string; "aria-hidden"?: boolean; className?: string }
function SpinnerGlyph(props: Omit<SpinnerProps, "aria-label" | "aria-hidden">): JSX.Element
function Spinner(props: SpinnerProps): JSX.Element
```

- `size: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"` — default `"md"`
  12, 16, 20, 24 or 32px box with a matching line width.
- `track: boolean` — default `true`
  Draw the faint full circle under the light.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Loading"`
  Accessible name of the progress bar.
- `aria-hidden: boolean`
  Render only the glyph, with no progress-bar role, when a parent already announces the wait.
- `className: string`
  Colour via a text class (default `text-accent-500`) and extra layout classes.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Box size and line width in px. */
const SIZES: Record<SpinnerSize, { box: number; line: number }> = {
  xs: { box: 12, line: 1.5 },
  sm: { box: 16, line: 2 },
  md: { box: 20, line: 2 },
  lg: { box: 24, line: 2.5 },
  xl: { box: 32, line: 3 },
};

/** One scale of the light: a conic arc masked to a ring, blurred by its wrapper. */
function Arc({
  box,
  line,
  width,
  blur,
  opacity,
  arc,
  lag,
}: {
  box: number;
  line: number;
  /** Ring thickness, px. */
  width: number;
  blur: number;
  opacity: number;
  /** Arc length in degrees; the head sits at 12 o'clock before the turn. */
  arc: number;
  /** Degrees this layer trails the crisp head. */
  lag: number;
}) {
  const center = box / 2 - line / 2;
  const inner = center - width / 2;
  const outer = center + width / 2;
  // The wrapper is grown to hold the ring plus its blur, so nothing clips.
  const bleed = Math.max(0, outer + blur * 2 - box / 2);
  const ring = `radial-gradient(circle, transparent ${inner}px, #000 ${inner + 0.5}px, #000 ${outer - 0.5}px, transparent ${outer}px)`;
  const style: CSSProperties = {
    inset: -bleed,
    filter: blur > 0 ? `blur(${blur}px)` : undefined,
    opacity,
    rotate: `${-lag}deg`,
  };
  return (
    <span aria-hidden className="absolute" style={style}>
      <span
        className="absolute inset-0"
        style={{
          background: `conic-gradient(transparent ${360 - arc}deg, currentColor 360deg)`,
          maskImage: ring,
          WebkitMaskImage: ring,
        }}
      />
    </span>
  );
}

export interface SpinnerProps {
  /** 12, 16, 20 (default), 24, or 32px. */
  size?: SpinnerSize;
  /** Draw the faint full circle under the light. Default true. */
  track?: boolean;
  /** Accessible name. Default "Loading". */
  "aria-label"?: string;
  /** Hide it from assistive technology when a parent already announces the wait. */
  "aria-hidden"?: boolean;
  /** Colour comes from the text colour, e.g. `text-white`. Default accent. */
  className?: string;
}

export function SpinnerGlyph({ size = "md", track = true, className }: Omit<SpinnerProps, "aria-label" | "aria-hidden">) {
  const { box, line } = SIZES[size];
  return (
    <span
      aria-hidden
      className={cx("relative inline-flex shrink-0 text-accent-500", className)}
      style={{ width: box, height: box }}
    >
      {track ? (
        <span className="absolute inset-0 rounded-full border-current opacity-15" style={{ borderWidth: line }} />
      ) : null}
      <span className="absolute inset-0 animate-spin [animation-duration:900ms] motion-reduce:[animation-duration:2400ms]">
        <Arc box={box} line={line} width={line * 4} blur={line * 1.6} opacity={0.32} arc={110} lag={22} />
        <Arc box={box} line={line} width={line * 2} blur={line * 0.6} opacity={0.6} arc={200} lag={9} />
        <Arc box={box} line={line} width={line} blur={0} opacity={1} arc={290} lag={0} />
        {/* The crisp line's rounded head, at the arc's leading end. */}
        <span
          className="absolute left-1/2 top-0 rounded-full bg-current"
          style={{ width: line, height: line, translate: "-50% 0" }}
        />
      </span>
    </span>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The orbit is a CSS animation; there are no listeners, timers or effects.

**Reduced motion.** The orbit keeps turning but slows from 900ms to 2400ms per revolution (`motion-reduce:[animation-duration:2400ms]`), since a stopped spinner would read as a frozen app.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not rotate each arc separately. All three share one spinning parent; their offsets come from a static `rotate: -lag`, so the comet shape never drifts apart.
- Do not set the wrapper to `overflow: hidden` or trim the `bleed` inset. The blurred layers extend past the box and would be cut into a square.
- Do not colour it with `fill` or `stroke`. Everything paints in `currentColor`; set a text colour such as `text-white` instead.
- Do not leave both a busy button label and the spinner announced. Pass `aria-hidden` to the spinner inside a pending button so screen readers do not hear "Loading" twice.

## Notes

- The default colour is `text-accent-500`; override it with any `text-*` class.
- `SpinnerGlyph` is exported for places that need the visual without the progress-bar role.

## Definition of done

A md spinner renders a 20px accent ring with a bright arc and rounded head turning clockwise about once every 0.9s, with a soft glow trailing behind the head and a faint full circle underneath. `className="text-white"` turns every layer white. The default spinner exposes `role="progressbar"` named "Loading" with no value; with `aria-hidden` no progressbar role is rendered. Nothing is clipped at any of the five sizes.
