# Build: Switch

A skeuomorphic on/off switch built on React Aria `Switch`. Off, the track is a flat neutral surface; on, it fills with the accent gradient plus an inset ring and top highlight. The white thumb slides across over 200ms and carries a tiny embossed chip in its centre that turns from white to blue. The visual lives in an exported `SwitchTrack`, so Switch Card renders exactly the same control.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

React Aria toggle with a gradient track, a white thumb that slides 200ms, and an embossed chip that turns blue when on; 3 sizes, 2 shapes.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `Switch` renders `AriaSwitch`, a `<label>` around a visually hidden `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`, as `group inline-flex items-center gap-2 select-none`. Its children render function passes the state to `<SwitchTrack state={state} size={size} shape={shape} />` and renders `children` (when not null or false) as a `text-body-medium text-text-primary` label. The cursor is `not-allowed` when disabled.
2. Every dimension comes from the `switchSizes` table, keyed by `sm`, `md` and `lg`: track size, track and thumb radius per shape, the on-state shadow, thumb size, the thumb's resting `offset`, its `travel`, and the chip size, border and shadow. `shape` only chooses between the `pill` and `rectangle` radii in each tier.
3. The track is a `relative` `aria-hidden` span with `transition-colors duration-200`. Off: `bg-background-tertiary-default`. On: `bg-linear-to-b from-accent-500 to-accent-600` plus the tier's `onShadow`, an inset white top highlight at 25% and an inset accent-500 hairline ring. At `lg` that shadow is exactly the shared `shadow-checkbox-selected` token; `md` and `sm` scale the highlight to 1.5px and 1px and the ring to 0.75px and 0.5px.
4. The thumb is absolutely positioned at the tier's `offset` (for example `start-[3px] top-[3px]` at md) with a near-white vertical gradient (`from-control-indicator-background from-[43.837%] to-control-indicator-background-subtle`) and a soft contact shadow. When selected it gets the tier's `travel` class (`translate-x-[18px] rtl:-translate-x-[18px]` at md) and `transition-transform duration-200` slides it. Positioning uses the logical `start-*` and the travel flips sign under `rtl:`, so the switch mirrors in RTL.
5. Inside the thumb, the chip is a bottom-to-top gradient (`bg-linear-to-t`) rather than a flipped element, so it stays pixel-snapped and its own drop shadow points down. Off it uses `switch-off-chip-start/end` with a half-opacity button border; on it uses `switch-on-chip-start/end` with an `accent-600` border.
6. Disabled dims only the track (`opacity-50`). Keyboard focus draws `ring-2 ring-border-focus-ring ring-offset-2` on the track while `isFocusVisible` is true.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `track sizes = sm 28×16 · md 42×24 · lg 56×32 px`
  1:1 with the Figma "Toogles" frame (node 3856:3807). Thumb = track height minus twice the padding: 12, 18 and 24px.
- `travel = sm 12px · md 18px · lg 24px`
  Track width minus thumb minus both paddings (28 − 12 − 4, 42 − 18 − 6, 56 − 24 − 8). Any other value leaves the thumb short of, or overlapping, the far edge.
- `duration = 200ms on the track colour and the thumb transform`
  Both run on one clock so the fill and the thumb arrive together. Short enough that a quick double toggle never shows the thumb lagging behind the track colour.
- `thumb gradient stop = from-[43.837%]`
  Copied from the Figma gradient: the top 44% of the thumb is solid white before it falls off to neutral-100, which is what makes it read as a rounded physical knob.

## API

```ts
function Switch(props: Omit<AriaSwitchProps, "children"> & { children?: ReactNode; size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg"; shape?: "pill" | "rectangle"; ref?: Ref<HTMLLabelElement> }): JSX.Element
function SwitchTrack(props: { state: { isSelected: boolean; isDisabled: boolean; isFocusVisible: boolean }; size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg"; shape?: "pill" | "rectangle" }): JSX.Element
```

- `isSelected / defaultSelected: boolean`
  Controlled or uncontrolled on state, from React Aria.
- `onChange: (isSelected: boolean) => void`
  Called when the switch is toggled.
- `size: "sm" | "md" | "lg"` — default `"md"`
  28×16, 42×24 or 56×32 track.
- `shape: "pill" | "rectangle"` — default `"pill"`
  Fully rounded, or a squarer track and thumb with small radii.
- `children: ReactNode`
  Optional label after the track in body medium. Without it, pass `aria-label`.
- `isDisabled: boolean`
  Dims the track to 50% and ignores input.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function SwitchTrack({
  state,
  size = "md",
  shape = "pill",
}: {
  state: SwitchVisualState;
  size?: SwitchSize;
  shape?: SwitchShape;
}) {
  const s = switchSizes[size];

  return (
    <span
      aria-hidden
      className={cx(
        "relative shrink-0 transition-colors duration-200 ease",
        s.track,
        s.trackRadius[shape],
        state.isSelected
          ? cx("bg-linear-to-b from-accent-500 to-accent-600", s.onShadow)
          : "bg-background-tertiary-default",
        state.isDisabled && "opacity-50",
        state.isFocusVisible && "ring-2 ring-border-focus-ring ring-offset-2",
      )}
    >
      {/* Thumb */}
      <span
        className={cx(
          "absolute flex items-center justify-center",
          "bg-linear-to-b from-control-indicator-background from-[43.837%] to-control-indicator-background-subtle",
          "shadow-[0_3px_3px_0_rgb(0_0_0/0.03),0_0.75px_0_0_rgb(0_0_0/0.05)]",
          "transition-transform duration-200 ease",
          s.thumb,
          s.thumbRadius[shape],
          s.offset,
          state.isSelected && s.travel,
        )}
      >
        {/* Embossed inner chip. Gradient runs bottom→top (`to-t`) — equivalent
            to the Figma layer's vertical flip — but WITHOUT a transform, so the
            chip stays pixel-snapped/centred (no blurry 1px shift at sub-pixel
            sizes) and its drop shadow points down instead of up. */}
        <span
          className={cx(
            "border-solid bg-linear-to-t from-[43.837%]",
            s.chip,
            s.chipRadius[shape],
            state.isSelected
              ? "border-accent-600 from-switch-on-chip-start to-switch-on-chip-end"
              : "border-border-button-default/50 from-switch-off-chip-start to-switch-off-chip-end",
          )}
        />
      </span>
    </span>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The component holds no state, listeners or timers of its own; React Aria owns the toggle state.

**Reduced motion.** The component does not check `prefers-reduced-motion`. The thumb slide and the track colour change are 200ms CSS transitions, so a global rule that removes transitions makes the thumb jump straight to the other end.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not animate the thumb with `left`. It is placed once with `start-*` and moved with `translate-x`, which stays on the compositor and mirrors with `rtl:-translate-x-*`.
- Do not flip the chip with `rotate-180` or `-scale-y-100` to reverse its gradient. A transform at sub-pixel sizes blurs it and points its shadow upward. Use the reversed gradient direction.
- Do not mix travel values across tiers. Each size's `travel` equals its own track width minus thumb and padding, so changing a track width means recomputing it.
- Do not ship a switch with no label and no `aria-label`. React Aria warns, and screen readers would announce only "switch".

## Notes

- `SwitchTrack` and `switchSizes` are exported, so another control (Switch Card, a menu row) can render the identical visual with its own input.

## Definition of done

An off switch shows a flat grey track with the white thumb at the start. Clicking it, or pressing Space when focused, slides the thumb to the end in about 200ms while the track fills with the blue gradient and the chip in the thumb turns blue. Clicking again reverses both. All three sizes and both shapes keep the thumb inset by the same proportion at both ends. In RTL the thumb starts on the right and slides left. Tab shows a focus ring around the track.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Switch Card

The switch counterpart of Checkbox Card: a 12px-radius bordered row with an optional 24px icon, a title, an optional description and the kit `SwitchTrack` on the trailing edge. The whole card is the React Aria `Switch` label, so a click anywhere toggles it and the thumb slides across in 200ms. Size and shape pass straight through to the track.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Bordered settings row with an optional icon, title and description; a click anywhere on the card flips the kit switch on its trailing edge.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `SwitchCard` renders `AriaSwitch` directly. React Aria makes it a `<label>` around a visually hidden `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`, so the entire card is the hit area and Space toggles it when focused. All Aria switch props (`isSelected`, `defaultSelected`, `onChange`, `isDisabled`, `name`) pass through.
2. The card class is computed from the render state: `group flex w-full items-center justify-between gap-3 rounded-xl border border-border-button-default py-3 pe-5 ps-4 select-none` with `transition-colors duration-150`. Hovered and not disabled gives `bg-background-primary-hover`, otherwise `bg-background-primary-default`. Disabled adds `cursor-not-allowed opacity-50`. A `className` function is called with the same state and merged last.
3. The leading block is `flex min-w-0 items-center gap-3`: the optional `icon` component rendered at `size-6` in `text-foreground-icon-secondary` with `aria-hidden`, then a `flex-col gap-0.5` column with the title in `text-body-medium text-text-primary` and, when `description` is not null or undefined, a line in `text-body-regular text-text-secondary`. Both lines truncate.
4. The trailing slot (`flex shrink-0 items-center`) renders `<SwitchTrack state={state} size={size} shape={shape} />` from the Switch item with the card's own render state, so selection, disabled dimming and the keyboard focus ring all show on the track exactly as on a plain `Switch`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `padding = ps-4 pe-5 py-3 (16 / 20 / 12px)`
  The same chrome as Checkbox Card, so the two can share a settings page. The extra 4px on the trailing side gives the 42px track room from the border.
- `radius = rounded-xl (12px)`
  The one deliberate difference from Checkbox Card, which uses rounded-2lg (10px); the source header calls it out as "mirrors CheckboxCard, but with rounded-xl (12px) corners".
- `hover fade = transition-colors duration-150`
  Same hover fade as Checkbox Card and Radio Card, so every selectable card in the kit tints at one speed. The track itself keeps its own 200ms transition.
- `icon = size-6 (24px), text-foreground-icon-secondary`
  Matches the 24×24 Remix Icon grid. The component takes the icon component itself (`RiMailLine`), not an element, so it controls size and colour.

## API

```ts
function SwitchCard(props: Omit<AriaSwitchProps, "children"> & { title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; icon?: ComponentType<{ className?: string; "aria-hidden"?: boolean | "true" | "false" }>; size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg"; shape?: "pill" | "rectangle"; ref?: Ref<HTMLLabelElement> }): JSX.Element
```

- `title: ReactNode`
  Main label in body medium. Also the accessible name of the switch.
- `description: ReactNode`
  Optional secondary line, truncated to one line.
- `icon: ComponentType`
  Optional leading 24px icon component, rendered `aria-hidden`.
- `isSelected / defaultSelected: boolean`
  Controlled or uncontrolled on state, from React Aria.
- `onChange: (isSelected: boolean) => void`
  Called when the card is toggled.
- `size: "sm" | "md" | "lg"` — default `"md"`
  Track size, passed to `SwitchTrack`.
- `shape: "pill" | "rectangle"` — default `"pill"`
  Track shape, passed to `SwitchTrack`.
- `isDisabled: boolean`
  Half opacity, not-allowed cursor, ignores input.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function SwitchCard({
  className,
  title,
  description,
  icon: Icon,
  size = "md",
  shape = "pill",
  ref,
  ...props
}: SwitchCardProps) {
  return (
    <AriaSwitch
      ref={ref}
      {...props}
      className={(state) =>
        cx(
          "group flex w-full items-center justify-between gap-3 rounded-xl border border-border-button-default py-3 pe-5 ps-4 select-none",
          "transition-colors duration-150 ease",
          state.isHovered && !state.isDisabled
            ? "bg-background-primary-hover"
            : "bg-background-primary-default",
          state.isDisabled ? "cursor-not-allowed opacity-50" : "cursor-pointer",
          typeof className === "function" ? className(state) : className,
        )
      }
    >
      {(state) => (
        <>
          <span className="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-3">
            {Icon && <Icon className="size-6 shrink-0 text-foreground-icon-secondary" aria-hidden />}
            <span className="flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-0.5">
              <span className="truncate text-body-medium text-text-primary">{title}</span>
              {description !== undefined && description !== null && (
                <span className="truncate text-body-regular text-text-secondary">{description}</span>
              )}
            </span>
          </span>
          <span className="flex shrink-0 items-center">
            <SwitchTrack state={state} size={size} shape={shape} />
          </span>
        </>
      )}
    </AriaSwitch>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The card holds no state, listeners or timers of its own; React Aria owns the toggle state.

**Reduced motion.** The component does not check `prefers-reduced-motion`. The 150ms card tint and the 200ms track and thumb are CSS transitions, so a global rule that removes transitions makes them switch instantly.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not pass an element to `icon` (`<RiMailLine />`). It expects the component (`RiMailLine`) and renders it itself.
- Do not put links or buttons in `title` or `description`. The card is a `<label>`, so clicks inside it toggle the switch.
- Do not add a separate `Switch` inside the card. The trailing track is already the visual for this card's own input; a second one would nest two controls.
- Do not give the card a fixed height. The description truncates to one line, but the title and description stack, so a fixed height clips the second line.

## Notes

- The track comes from `registry/ui/switch.tsx` (`SwitchTrack`), so install the Switch item alongside this one.

## Definition of done

A stack of setting cards each shows an icon, a title, a one-line description and a switch on the right. Clicking anywhere on a card, including its description, slides its thumb across and fills the track blue in about 200ms; clicking again reverses it. Hover tints the card. Tab focuses the card and shows the ring on the track; Space toggles it. A disabled card is at half opacity and ignores clicks.

# Build: Table

The static table primitive behind BoardUI's dashboard tables. Only the root is wrapped: `Table` adds a horizontal scroll container and a density flag around React Aria's `Table`. `TableHeader`, `TableColumn`, `TableBody`, `TableRow` and `TableCell` are React Aria's collection components re-exported untouched, because wrapping them would break React Aria's collection building. All visual styling (header band, row separators, cell padding, focus ring) lives in CSS scoped to `.bui-table`, so the markup stays real `<table>`, `<th>`, `<tr>` and `<td>` with keyboard navigation for free.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Semantic table on React Aria with a scroll container, an md/sm density flag and dashboard styling from one scoped stylesheet.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Wrap the table in `<div className="w-full overflow-x-auto">` (plus `containerClassName`), so a wide table scrolls sideways inside its card instead of stretching the page.
2. Render `AriaTable` with every React Aria prop passed through (`aria-label`, `selectionMode`, `sortDescriptor`, …), the forwarded `ref`, and `className = cx("bui-table", size === "sm" && "bui-table-sm", className)`.
3. Re-export `TableHeader`, `Column as TableColumn`, `TableBody`, `Row as TableRow` and `Cell as TableCell` from react-aria-components unchanged, so React Aria can still introspect the collection.
4. In the theme sheet, `.bui-table` is `w-full border-collapse text-start`. Header cells get `px-3 py-2.5 text-body-medium text-text-tertiary whitespace-nowrap`, the secondary background and a separator border above and below; body cells get `px-3 py-2.5 text-body-medium text-text-primary`.
5. Rows are separated by `tbody tr:not(:last-child) { border-bottom }` only, so the last row never doubles up with the container edge or a pagination footer. `tr[data-focus-visible]` draws an inset 2px focus ring.
6. `.bui-table-sm` drops cells to `px-2.5 py-1.5 text-body-2-medium`; padding and font-size carry a 200ms ease transition, so switching density animates.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `cell padding = md px-3 py-2.5 (12 / 10px); sm px-2.5 py-1.5 (10 / 6px)`
  The two dashboard densities. Both are set on th and td together, so header and body stay aligned.
- `density transition = padding 200ms ease, font-size 200ms ease`
  Toggling `size` reflows the rows smoothly instead of snapping.
- `separators = 1px solid var(--color-separator-border)`
  One token for the header band edges and the between-row rules, set with plain CSS because `@apply` drops border and background on row-group cells.

## API

```ts
type TableSize = "sm" | "md"
interface TableProps extends Omit<AriaTableProps, "className"> { size?: TableSize; className?: string; containerClassName?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLTableElement> }
function Table(props: TableProps): JSX.Element
export { TableHeader, Column as TableColumn, TableBody, Row as TableRow, Cell as TableCell } from "react-aria-components"
```

- `size: "sm" | "md"` — default `"md"`
  Row density. `sm` adds `bui-table-sm` for tighter padding and the smaller body type.
- `aria-label: string`
  Accessible name for the table (React Aria). Required unless `aria-labelledby` is set.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the `<table>` after `bui-table`.
- `containerClassName: string`
  Class for the `overflow-x-auto` scroll wrapper.
- `ref: Ref<HTMLTableElement>`
  Forwarded to the `<table>` element.
- `...props: AriaTableProps`
  Selection, sorting and every other React Aria Table prop.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function Table({ size = "md", className, containerClassName, ref, ...props }: TableProps) {
  return (
    <div className={cx("w-full overflow-x-auto", containerClassName)}>
      <AriaTable
        ref={ref}
        {...props}
        className={cx("bui-table", size === "sm" && "bui-table-sm", className)}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

export {
  TableHeader,
  Column as TableColumn,
  TableBody,
  Row as TableRow,
  Cell as TableCell,
};
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. The wrapper is stateless; React Aria owns focus and selection state and removes its own listeners on unmount.

**Reduced motion.** The only motion is the 200ms padding and font-size transition when `size` changes, plus a 150ms colour transition on rows. Neither is gated by prefers-reduced-motion; both are short, non-spatial reflows. Add `motion-reduce:transition-none` through `className` if a product needs them off.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not wrap `TableColumn`, `TableRow` or `TableCell` in your own components. React Aria builds the collection by introspecting these exact elements; restyle through `.bui-table` CSS or `className` instead.
- Do not forget `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) on `Table`. Without one the grid has no accessible name.
- Mark exactly one column `isRowHeader`, usually the name column, so screen readers announce each row by it.
- Do not put the header background or borders on `<thead>`. With `border-collapse` the browser does not paint them on the row group, which is why the sheet puts them on `th`.

## Notes

- Sorting, filtering and pagination are not built in. Pair the primitive with @tanstack/react-table (or your own state) and pass `sortDescriptor` / `onSortChange` through to React Aria.
- The component file's doc comment mentions h-16 / h-12 rows and a `data-size` attribute; the shipped code uses the `bui-table-sm` class and padding-driven heights instead.

## Definition of done

A `<Table aria-label="Team members">` with a header row and four body rows renders a real `<table>` inside a horizontally scrolling div. Header cells sit on the secondary background between two hairlines in tertiary text; body rows are separated by hairlines with none under the last row. Tabbing into the table and pressing the arrow keys moves a visible inset ring between rows. Switching `size` to "sm" tightens every cell from 12/10px to 10/6px padding over 200ms. At 360px the table scrolls sideways inside its container without widening the page.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Table Filter Bar

The filter row that sits on top of a BoardUI table: a "Total Results" count on the left, then one kit Select per filter ("All prices", "All products", "All regions") and a pill SearchField. Every active filter and a non-empty search become removable chips with a Clear all button. The bar never touches rows: it reports values and the query, the caller filters and passes back the result count, which is announced politely.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Strip above a data table: "All ..." select filters, a pill search, removable active-filter chips, Clear all and a live result count.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. State is a FilterValues record (filter id -> option id, a missing key means "All") plus a query string; both are controlled (values / query) or uncontrolled (defaultValues / defaultQuery) and every change is reported through onValuesChange / onQueryChange.
2. Each filter renders a kit Select whose first SelectItem has the sentinel id __all__ and the allLabel text; selectedKey is values[id] ?? __all__, and choosing __all__ deletes the key instead of storing it.
3. Active chips are derived on render: filters.flatMap finds the option matching values[filter.id]; a trimmed non-empty query adds a "Search: ..." chip. The chip row (role=group "Active filters") only mounts while something is active.
4. Chip remove buttons and Clear all set a refocus ref before updating state; an effect after the re-render moves focus to the next [data-filter-chip-remove] button or, if none is left, to the search input, so focus never falls to <body>.
5. resultCount renders under totalLabel inside an aria-live="polite" aria-atomic paragraph so assistive tech hears "4 orders" after each change; omit the prop to hide the count block.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `ALL sentinel = '__all__'`
  Keeps "All ..." a real listbox option so the trigger shows its label, while the stored values stay free of reset entries.
- `search width = w-full, sm:w-[200px]`
  Full row on phones; a fixed 200px pill beside the selects from 640px up, as in the finance table header.
- `layout breakpoint = lg:flex-row`
  Below 1024px the count stacks above the controls so three selects plus search can wrap without squeezing the count.
- `chip remove target = size-5 rounded-full, 14px icon`
  A round 20px hit area inside a caption chip, with hover and focus-ring states from the kit tokens.
- `gap = gap-2.5 controls, gap-2 chips`
  10px between bordered selects matches the reference spacing; chips sit slightly tighter.

## API

```ts
export function TableFilterBar({ filters, values, defaultValues, onValuesChange, query, defaultQuery, onQueryChange, searchPlaceholder, resultCount, resultLabel, totalLabel, showActiveFilters, clearLabel, className }: TableFilterBarProps): JSX.Element
```

- `filters: readonly FilterDefinition[]`
  Each { id, label, allLabel, options: { id, label }[] } renders one select.
- `values / defaultValues: Record<string, string>` — default `{}`
  Selected option per filter id, controlled or initial.
- `onValuesChange: (values: FilterValues) => void`
  Called with the whole record after any select, chip or Clear all change.
- `query / defaultQuery: string` — default `''`
  Search text, controlled or initial.
- `onQueryChange: (query: string) => void`
  Called on each keystroke and on clear.
- `searchPlaceholder: string` — default `'Search'`
  Placeholder and accessible name of the search field.
- `resultCount: number`
  Rows left after filtering; omit to hide the count block.
- `resultLabel: string` — default `'results'`
  Noun after the count.
- `totalLabel: ReactNode` — default `'Total Results'`
  Caption above the count.
- `showActiveFilters: boolean` — default `true`
  Show the removable chip row while anything is active.
- `clearLabel: string` — default `'Clear all'`
  Label of the reset button.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function TableFilterBar({
  filters,
  values,
  defaultValues = EMPTY,
  onValuesChange,
  query,
  defaultQuery = '',
  onQueryChange,
  searchPlaceholder = 'Search',
  resultCount,
  resultLabel = 'results',
  totalLabel = 'Total Results',
  showActiveFilters = true,
  clearLabel = 'Clear all',
  className,
}: TableFilterBarProps) {
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const [innerValues, setInnerValues] = useState<FilterValues>(defaultValues);
  const [innerQuery, setInnerQuery] = useState(defaultQuery);
  const current = values ?? innerValues;
  const search = query ?? innerQuery;

  const setValues = (next: FilterValues) => {
    setInnerValues(next);
    onValuesChange?.(next);
  };
  const setSearch = (next: string) => {
    setInnerQuery(next);
    onQueryChange?.(next);
  };
  const setFilter = (filterId: string, optionId: string | null) => {
    const { [filterId]: _removed, ...rest } = current;
    setValues(optionId === null ? rest : { ...rest, [filterId]: optionId });
  };

  // Removing a chip unmounts the focused button; after the re-render, hand
  // focus to the next chip, else to the search input.
  const refocus = useRef(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!refocus.current) return;
    refocus.current = false;
    const root = rootRef.current;
    (root?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-filter-chip-remove]') ?? root?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('input'))?.focus();
  });

  const active = filters.flatMap((filter) => {
    const option = filter.options.find((o) => o.id === current[filter.id]);
    return option ? [{ filter, option }] : [];
  });
  const trimmed = search.trim();
  const hasActive = active.length > 0 || trimmed.length > 0;

  const clearAll = () => {
    refocus.current = true;
    setValues(EMPTY);
    setSearch('');
  };

  return (
    <div ref={rootRef} className={cx('flex w-full flex-col gap-3', className)}>
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 lg:flex-row lg:items-center lg:justify-between">
        {resultCount !== undefined ? (
          <div className="flex shrink-0 flex-col justify-center">
            <p className="text-body-medium whitespace-nowrap text-text-tertiary">{totalLabel}</p>
            <p aria-live="polite" aria-atomic className="text-body-medium whitespace-nowrap text-text-primary tabular-nums">
              {resultCount.toLocaleString()} {resultLabel}
            </p>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2.5 lg:justify-end">
          {filters.map((filter) => (
            <Select
              key={filter.id}
              aria-label={`Filter by ${filter.label.toLowerCase()}`}
              className="shrink-0"
              popoverClassName="w-auto min-w-44"
              selectedKey={current[filter.id] ?? ALL}
              onSelectionChange={(key: Key | null) => setFilter(filter.id, key === null || key === ALL ? null : String(key))}
            >
              <SelectItem id={ALL} textValue={filter.allLabel}>
                {filter.allLabel}
              </SelectItem>
              {filter.options.map((option) => (
                <SelectItem key={option.id} id={option.id} textValue={option.label}>
                  {option.label}
                </SelectItem>
              ))}
            </Select>
          ))}
          <SearchField
            aria-label={searchPlaceholder}
            placeholder={searchPlaceholder}
            value={search}
            onChange={setSearch}
            className="w-full sm:w-[200px]"
          />
        </div>
      </div>

      {showActiveFilters && hasActive ? (
        <div role="group" aria-label="Active filters" className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
          {active.map(({ filter, option }) => (
            <Chip key={filter.id} color="soft" variant="caption" className="gap-1 rounded-full py-0.5 ps-2.5 pe-0.5">
              <span>
                {filter.label}: <span className="text-text-primary">{option.label}</span>
              </span>
              <button
                type="button"
                data-filter-chip-remove
                aria-label={`Remove ${filter.label} filter: ${option.label}`}
                onClick={() => {
                  refocus.current = true;
                  setFilter(filter.id, null);
                }}
                className={cx(
                  'inline-flex size-5 cursor-pointer items-center justify-center rounded-full text-foreground-icon-tertiary outline-none',
                  'transition-colors duration-150 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none',
                  'hover:bg-background-tertiary-hover hover:text-foreground-icon-primary focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring',
                )}
              >
                <RiCloseLine aria-hidden className="size-3.5" />
              </button>
            </Chip>
          ))}
          {trimmed ? (
            <Chip color="soft" variant="caption" className="gap-1 rounded-full py-0.5 ps-2.5 pe-0.5">
              <span>
                Search: <span className="text-text-primary">&ldquo;{trimmed}&rdquo;</span>
              </span>
              <button
                type="button"
                data-filter-chip-remove
                aria-label={`Clear search: ${trimmed}`}
                onClick={() => {
                  refocus.current = true;
                  setSearch('');
                }}
                className={cx(
                  'inline-flex size-5 cursor-pointer items-center justify-center rounded-full text-foreground-icon-tertiary outline-none',
                  'transition-colors duration-150 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none',
                  'hover:bg-background-tertiary-hover hover:text-foreground-icon-primary focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring',
                )}
              >
                <RiCloseLine aria-hidden className="size-3.5" />
              </button>
            </Chip>
          ) : null}
          <Button variant="ghost" size="xs" leadingIcon={RiFilterOffLine} onClick={clearAll}>
            {clearLabel}
          </Button>
        </div>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers or listeners of its own; the refocus effect only reads a ref. The kit Select owns its outside-press listener.

**Reduced motion.** Only colour transitions are used (motion-reduce:transition-none on the chip remove buttons); the kit Select popover drops its scale entry under reduced motion.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not store the "All" choice as a value: chips and filtering would treat __all__ as an active filter. Delete the key instead.
- Removing a chip unmounts the focused button; without the refocus effect keyboard focus drops to <body>.
- The bar does not filter anything itself; pass the post-filter length as resultCount or the live count will be stale.

## Notes

- Set showActiveFilters={false} when the selects alone are enough, e.g. in a narrow card.
- Option and filter labels feed both the chips and the accessible names ("Filter by product", "Remove Product filter: Laptop").

## Definition of done

Choosing "Laptop" in "All products" narrows the demo list to 3 orders, shows a "Product: Laptop" chip and announces "3 orders"; typing "clark" in search narrows it to 1 order; Clear all removes every chip, resets the selects to "All ..." and restores 10 orders.

# Build: Tabs

Two tab styles from one kit. The underline tabs wrap React Aria `Tabs`, so arrow keys, roving focus and tab/panel wiring come for free, and a single absolutely positioned 2px bar glides to whichever tab is selected. The pill switcher is a plain row of toggle buttons for local view state, with a shared rounded thumb that slides under the active pill and overshoots slightly before it settles.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

React Aria underline tabs with a measured 2px indicator that slides between tabs, plus a pill switcher whose thumb settles with a spring.

- Category: navigation
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `Tabs`, `TabList`, `Tab` and `TabPanel` spread their props onto the React Aria primitives, which handle roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, automatic activation and the `aria-controls` link between a tab and its panel. Every `className` accepts a string or React Aria's state function and is merged through `cx`. `Tabs` is a `flex-col gap-4` stack that flips to `flex-row` when `orientation` is vertical.
2. `TabList` wraps the Aria list in a `relative w-full` div. The list itself is `flex items-center gap-1 border-b border-separator-border`, the 1px baseline every tab sits on. The selected tab is not underlined by its own border: an `aria-hidden` span (`absolute bottom-0 left-0 h-0.5 bg-accent-600`) is drawn once and moved.
3. A layout effect (`useLayoutEffect` on the client, `useEffect` on the server to avoid the SSR warning) queries `[role='tab'][data-selected]` and stores its `offsetLeft` and `offsetWidth`. The bar is rendered with `transform: translateX(left px)` and `width`, and `transition-[transform,width] duration-200` animates both, so it slides and resizes in one motion between tabs of different widths.
4. Measurement re-runs on three triggers: a `ResizeObserver` on the strip and on every tab (labels and web fonts change tab widths without resizing the strip), and a `MutationObserver` on the subtree filtered to `data-selected`, which fires when React Aria moves the selection. The MutationObserver also re-observes tabs when children change. The effect depends on `useDirection()`, so switching between LTR and RTL re-measures from the new layout.
5. `Tab` renders the label in `text-body-medium text-accent-600` when selected and `text-body-regular text-text-primary` otherwise, with an optional 16px leading `icon` that inherits the colour. A `count` badge (`rounded-sm px-1 py-px text-caption-1-medium`) uses `bg-tab-count-selected-background text-accent-600` when selected, and `bg-black/10 text-text-primary opacity-50` when not.
6. `PillTabList` is a `role="group"` row (`relative inline-flex gap-1`). It finds the `[data-pill-selected]` button and stores its `left`, `top`, `width`, `height` and variant (read from `data-pill-variant`), then paints one thumb with `translate(left, top)` plus width and height, transitioned over 300ms on `cubic-bezier(0.34,1.2,0.64,1)`. The same Resize/Mutation observer pair keeps it aligned.
7. `PillTab` is a `<button type="button" aria-pressed>` at `z-10` above the thumb. Variant `blue` is `rounded-full` with an accent-50 thumb and `text-accent-500` label. Variant `gray` is `rounded-2lg` with `bg-background-tertiary-default`. An unselected pill fades in its own hover layer (`opacity-0` to `group-hover:opacity-100`, 200ms), so hover never moves the shared thumb.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `underline = h-0.5 (2px), 200ms, transform + width`
  Figma draws a 2px blue rule over the 1px baseline. Transitioning only `transform` and `width` keeps the slide on the compositor-friendly path, and 200ms is short enough that rapid arrow-key presses never leave the bar lagging two tabs behind.
- `pill thumb easing = 300ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.2, 0.64, 1)`
  The second control point at 1.2 overshoots by a few percent, which reads as a small spring settle without a JS spring. It is longer than the underline because the thumb moves a filled surface and the overshoot needs time to read.
- `tab padding = px-2.5 py-2, gap-2.5 label to count`
  10px by 8px and the 10px label-to-count gap are the Figma tab spec (node 3793:2942). The indicator width is measured from the tab box, so changing padding also changes how wide the underline is.
- `pill padding = px-2 py-[5px], icon size-5`
  8px by 5px around a 20px icon and 20px line height gives a 30px pill, the height of the AI chat panel switcher it came from.

## API

```ts
function Tabs(props: AriaTabsProps & { ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function TabList<T extends object>(props: AriaTabListProps<T> & { ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function Tab(props: Omit<AriaTabProps, "children"> & { children?: ReactNode; icon?: IconComponent; count?: ReactNode; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function TabPanel(props: AriaTabPanelProps & { ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function PillTabList(props: HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function PillTab(props: { variant?: "blue" | "gray"; icon?: IconComponent; isSelected: boolean; onSelect: () => void; children: ReactNode; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `Tabs.selectedKey / defaultSelectedKey: Key`
  Controlled or uncontrolled selection, straight from React Aria. Pair with `onSelectionChange`.
- `Tabs.orientation: "horizontal" | "vertical"` — default `"horizontal"`
  Vertical switches the outer stack to `flex-row`. The underline measures `offsetLeft` only, so it is designed for horizontal strips.
- `TabList.aria-label: string`
  Accessible name for the tab list. Required when there is no visible heading.
- `Tab.id: Key`
  Key that matches the `id` of the `TabPanel` it controls.
- `Tab.icon: ComponentType<{ className?: string }>`
  16px leading icon component. Inherits the label colour.
- `Tab.count: ReactNode`
  Trailing badge, accent-tinted when the tab is selected and muted otherwise. Omitted when null.
- `PillTab.variant: "blue" | "gray"` — default `"blue"`
  Blue is fully rounded with an accent thumb; gray is a 10px radius with a neutral thumb.
- `PillTab.isSelected / onSelect: boolean / () => void`
  Controlled selection. The selected pill carries `data-pill-selected`, which the list measures.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
type Underline = { left: number; width: number };

export function TabList<T extends object>({ className, ref, ...props }: TabListProps<T>) {
  const direction = useDirection();
  const wrapperRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const [underline, setUnderline] = useState<Underline | null>(null);

  useIsomorphicLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = wrapperRef.current;
    if (!el) return;
    const measure = () => {
      const selected = el.querySelector<HTMLElement>("[role='tab'][data-selected]");
      if (selected) {
        setUnderline({ left: selected.offsetLeft, width: selected.offsetWidth });
      }
    };
    measure();
    const ro = new ResizeObserver(measure);
    ro.observe(el);
    // Labels and fonts can change width without resizing the full tab strip.
    const observeTabs = () => el.querySelectorAll("[role='tab']").forEach(tab => ro.observe(tab));
    observeTabs();
    const mo = new MutationObserver(() => { observeTabs(); measure(); });
    mo.observe(el, { attributes: true, childList: true, characterData: true, subtree: true, attributeFilter: ["data-selected"] });
    return () => {
      mo.disconnect();
      ro.disconnect();
    };
  }, [direction]);

  return (
    <div ref={wrapperRef} className="relative w-full">
      <AriaTabList
        ref={ref}
        {...props}
        className={(state) =>
          cx(
            "flex w-full items-center gap-1 border-b border-separator-border",
            typeof className === "function" ? className(state) : className,
          )
        }
      />
      {underline && (
        <span
          aria-hidden
          className="pointer-events-none absolute bottom-0 left-0 h-0.5 bg-accent-600 transition-[transform,width] duration-200 ease"
          style={{
            transform: `translateX(${underline.left}px)`,
            width: underline.width,
          }}
        />
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Each list disconnects its `ResizeObserver` and `MutationObserver` in the layout effect cleanup, on unmount and whenever the direction changes. There are no timers or animation frames.

**Reduced motion.** The component does not check `prefers-reduced-motion` itself. The underline (200ms) and pill thumb (300ms) slides and the colour fades are plain CSS transitions, so a global reduced-motion rule that zeroes transition durations makes them jump straight to the new tab.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not draw the active underline with a border on each `Tab`. It cannot animate between tabs, and it doubles up with the strip's own `border-b`. The single measured span is what slides.
- Do not measure in a plain `useEffect`. The first paint would show the bar at its old position, or missing, for one frame. The isomorphic layout effect measures before paint.
- Do not drop the `ResizeObserver` on the individual tabs. A web font that loads after mount widens the labels without resizing the strip, and the underline is then left short of the text.
- Do not use `PillTab` for routed content panels. It is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`, not a `role="tab"`, so it has no arrow-key navigation and no panel association. Use the React Aria `Tabs` for that.
- Do not forget `aria-label` on `TabList`. React Aria warns at runtime when a tab list has no accessible name.

## Notes

- `PillTab` is controlled only: it takes `isSelected` and `onSelect`, and the parent owns which one is active. Several pills can be selected at once, but the thumb only follows the first `[data-pill-selected]` it finds.
- The thumb picks up the variant of the selected pill, so a row can mix blue and gray pills and the surface colour and radius switch as the selection moves.

## Definition of done

An underline strip with three tabs shows a 2px accent bar under the selected tab only. Click or arrow-key to another tab and the bar slides and resizes to the new tab in about 200ms, while the label turns accent and medium weight. Count badges are tinted on the selected tab and faded on the others. In a pill row, selecting another pill slides one shared thumb under it with a small overshoot, and hovering an unselected pill tints only that pill.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Tag Group

A set of tags to filter by, pick from or prune: topics, labels on a ticket, recipients. `TagGroup` wraps React Aria's `TagGroup` and `TagList` with the kit Label, hint text and an optional empty state; `Tag` wraps React Aria's `Tag` in Chip's colour pairs at 28px, or 24px with `size="small"`. Give the group a `selectionMode` and tags toggle, a selected tag filling with the accent colour; give it `onRemove` and every tag grows a small close button, while Backspace or Delete removes the focused tag. Because it is a React Aria grid, Tab enters once and the arrow keys move between tags.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Selectable or removable tags in Chip's colours, with grid keyboard navigation and an empty state, on React Aria's TagGroup.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `TagGroup` renders `AriaTagGroup` (`flex flex-col items-start gap-1.5`) with every React Aria prop passed through, then the kit `Label`, an `AriaTagList` (`flex flex-wrap gap-1.5`) and an optional `HintText`.
2. The list takes `items` for data-driven tags, and `renderEmptyState` is set only when `emptyState` is given, rendering it as `text-body-regular text-text-tertiary`.
3. The group's `size` goes into a `SizeContext`, so each `Tag` reads it without a prop: medium is `h-7 px-2 text-body-medium`, small is `h-6 px-1.5 text-caption-1-medium`.
4. `Tag` styles itself from React Aria's render props. `isSelected` swaps the Chip colour for `bg-accent-500 text-white`; a selectable, unselected tag on hover darkens (`bg-background-tertiary-hover` for neutral, `brightness-95` for the colours); `isFocusVisible` adds a 2px focus ring; `isDisabled` drops to 50%.
5. When `allowsRemoving` is true (the group has `onRemove`), the tag trims its end padding and renders an `AriaButton slot="remove"` with `RiCloseLine` at 60% opacity, lifting to 100% with a `bg-current/15` wash on hover.
6. `textValue` defaults to the children when they are a plain string, so typeahead and screen readers get a label without extra props.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `tag height = medium h-7 (28px) px-2; small h-6 (24px) px-1.5`
  Matches Chip, so a tag and a static chip in the same row line up.
- `selected fill = bg-accent-500 text-white`
  One accent fill for every selected tag, whatever its resting colour, so selection reads the same across a coloured set.
- `transition = background-color, color, box-shadow, filter over 150ms ease-out`
  Covers the selection fill, the hover brightness and the focus ring without animating layout.
- `remove button = size-5 (size-4 small), opacity 0.6 → 1 on hover`
  Quiet until pointed at, so a row of removable tags still reads as labels first.

## API

```ts
type TagSize = "medium" | "small"
interface TagGroupProps<T extends object> extends Omit<AriaTagGroupProps, "className" | "children"> { label?: ReactNode; hint?: ReactNode; emptyState?: ReactNode; size?: TagSize; items?: Iterable<T>; children: ReactNode | ((item: T) => ReactNode); className?: string }
interface TagProps extends Omit<AriaTagProps, "className" | "children"> { color?: ChipColor; icon?: ComponentType<{ className?: string }>; className?: string; children: ReactNode }
function TagGroup<T extends object>(props: TagGroupProps<T>): JSX.Element
function Tag(props: TagProps): JSX.Element
```

- `label: ReactNode`
  TagGroup: visible label above the tags.
- `hint: ReactNode`
  TagGroup: helper text under the tags.
- `emptyState: ReactNode`
  TagGroup: shown in place of the tags when the list is empty.
- `size: "medium" | "small"` — default `"medium"`
  TagGroup: 28px or 24px tags.
- `items: Iterable<T>`
  TagGroup: data for a children render function.
- `selectionMode: "none" | "single" | "multiple"` — default `"none"`
  TagGroup: lets tags toggle (React Aria).
- `selectedKeys / defaultSelectedKeys: Iterable<Key> | "all"`
  TagGroup: controlled or uncontrolled selection (React Aria).
- `onRemove: (keys: Set<Key>) => void`
  TagGroup: turns on remove buttons and Backspace/Delete (React Aria).
- `color: ChipColor` — default `"neutral"`
  Tag: one of Chip's colour pairs.
- `icon: ComponentType`
  Tag: Remix Icon before the label.
- `id: Key`
  Tag: key used for selection and removal.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function Tag({ color = "neutral", icon: Icon, className, children, ...props }: TagProps) {
  const size = useContext(SizeContext);

  return (
    <AriaTag
      {...props}
      textValue={props.textValue ?? (typeof children === "string" ? children : undefined)}
      className={({ isSelected, selectionMode, allowsRemoving, isHovered, isFocusVisible, isDisabled }) => {
        const allowsSelection = selectionMode !== "none";
        return cx(
          "inline-flex max-w-full items-center gap-1 rounded-lg outline-none",
          "transition-[background-color,color,box-shadow,filter] duration-150 ease-out",
          size === "small" ? "h-6 px-1.5 text-caption-1-medium" : "h-7 px-2 text-body-medium",
          allowsRemoving && (size === "small" ? "pe-0.5" : "pe-1"),
          isSelected ? "bg-accent-500 text-white" : CHIP_COLORS[color],
          allowsSelection ? "cursor-pointer" : "cursor-default",
          allowsSelection && !isSelected && isHovered && (color === "neutral" ? "bg-background-tertiary-hover" : "brightness-95"),
          isFocusVisible && "ring-2 ring-border-focus-ring",
          isDisabled && "cursor-not-allowed opacity-50",
          className,
        );
      }}
    >
      {({ allowsRemoving }) => (
        <>
          {Icon ? <Icon aria-hidden className={cx("shrink-0", size === "small" ? "size-3.5" : "size-4")} /> : null}
          <span className="truncate">{children}</span>
          {allowsRemoving ? (
            <AriaButton
              slot="remove"
              className={cx(
                "flex shrink-0 cursor-pointer items-center justify-center rounded-md opacity-60 outline-none",
                "transition-[opacity,background-color] duration-150 ease-out hover:bg-current/15 hover:opacity-100",
                size === "small" ? "size-4" : "size-5",
              )}
            >
              <RiCloseLine aria-hidden className={size === "small" ? "size-3" : "size-3.5"} />
            </AriaButton>
          ) : null}
        </>
      )}
    </AriaTag>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up. React Aria owns focus, selection and keyboard handling; the component adds no listeners or timers.

**Reduced motion.** Only colour, shadow and filter transition, over 150ms, and nothing moves. There is no reduced-motion branch because there is no spatial motion to remove.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Give the group a `label` or an `aria-label`. React Aria's TagGroup is a grid and needs an accessible name.
- When tags are not plain strings (an icon plus text in a fragment, a formatted value), pass `textValue` so typeahead and screen readers have text.
- Removing is your state change. `onRemove` hands you the keys; filter them out of your list, or nothing disappears.
- With `items`, give each item an `id` (or a `key`) so React Aria can track it.
- Do not nest your own buttons or links in a tag. The only control inside is the remove button React Aria wires up.

## Notes

- Colours come straight from Chip's exported `CHIP_COLORS`, so tags and chips stay one palette.
- Selection is React Aria's: `selectionMode` "single" or "multiple" with `selectedKeys` / `defaultSelectedKeys` and `onSelectionChange`.

## Definition of done

A "Topics" group with `selectionMode="multiple"` and Design and Engineering selected shows two accent-filled tags among neutral ones. Clicking Marketing fills it; Tab focuses the group once and the arrow keys walk the tags with a visible ring. A group with `onRemove` shows a faint close icon in each tag that brightens on hover; clicking it, or pressing Delete on a focused tag, calls `onRemove` with that key. When the last tag is removed the empty state text appears in its place. `size="small"` renders 24px tags.

# Build: Task List

Renders what an agent did as a list of tasks, each a clickable header with a nested list of steps that can carry file chips. Every header and every step is one reveal unit paced by the Agent Log ticker, so the log grows row by row with a blur-in and a curved tree guide. A running task shimmers its title; once its last step lands it switches to doneTitle and, with collapseOnComplete, folds away while the header stays clickable.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A streaming agent log: task headers and their steps blur in one unit at a time down a curved guide, then each task settles and folds.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: motion@^12.43.0, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. countTaskUnits sums 1 + steps.length per task; useRevealTicker from agent-log returns how many units have landed, from its own timer (startDelay, then stepInterval) or from the controlled revealed prop.
2. One pass over the tasks hands each its slice: the header is visible once revealed passes its start offset, shown = clamp(revealed - start - 1, 0, steps.length) steps are rendered, and done means all of its units are in.
3. Headers mount as motion.li with the shared UNIT_INITIAL/UNIT_ANIMATE blur-and-height reveal; steps are agent-log LogRow items, each drawing its own curved branch, and a GuideBridge drops 6px from the 16px header glyph to the trunk at ms-2.
4. Open state is overrides[id] ?? !autoClosed, where autoClosed is done (collapseOnComplete true) or the whole run being complete ("all"); the region collapses with a grid-template-rows 1fr to 0fr transition and is inert while closed.
5. Until the last unit lands a WorkingRow (Agent Thinking stars plus elapsed timer) sits at the tail; onComplete fires once through the ticker when revealed reaches the total.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `startDelay = 320ms`
  Keeps the first row from landing on the same frame as the user turn that started the run.
- `stepInterval = 850ms (demo 700ms)`
  One unit per beat reads as work happening; faster reads as a list being printed.
- `GuideBridge height = 6px`
  Header row is 28px (20px line + 4px padding each side) and the 16px glyph ends at 22px, so 6px joins it to the nested trunk.
- `collapse transition = 300ms ease-out`
  Folding a task should finish before the next unit lands at 700-850ms intervals.

## API

```ts
<TaskList key={turnId} tasks={tasks} startDelay={320} stepInterval={850} collapseOnComplete onComplete={() => setPhase("answered")} />
```

- `tasks: readonly TaskItem[]`
  Tasks with id, title, optional doneTitle and icon, and steps ({ label, chips? }).
- `run: boolean` — default `true`
  Pauses and resumes the internal ticker.
- `startDelay: number` — default `320`
  Milliseconds before the first unit lands.
- `stepInterval: number` — default `850`
  Milliseconds between units.
- `revealed: number`
  Units landed, when driven from real events; disables the timer.
- `collapseOnComplete: boolean | "all"` — default `false`
  Fold each task when its steps land, or all tasks when the run completes.
- `working: string | false` — default `"Working"`
  Tail indicator label while running; false hides it.
- `onComplete: () => void`
  Fires once when the final unit lands.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Agent tasks"`
  Accessible name of the log.
- `className: string`
  Classes on the root.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Walk the tasks once, handing each its slice of the revealed units: the
// first unit shows the header, the rest land its steps in order. A task is
// done once all of its units are in, which settles its title and, with
// collapseOnComplete, folds it (or waits for the whole run with "all").
let offset = 0;
const blocks = tasks.map((task) => {
  const start = offset;
  offset += taskUnits(task);
  const visible = revealed > start;
  const shown = Math.max(0, Math.min(task.steps.length, revealed - start - 1));
  const done = revealed >= start + taskUnits(task);
  const autoClosed =
    collapseOnComplete === "all" ? complete : collapseOnComplete ? done : false;
  const open = overrides[task.id] ?? !autoClosed;
  return { task, visible, shown, done, open };
});
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The ticker clears its pending timeout whenever revealed, run or pacing changes and on unmount; the Working row timer interval is cleared on unmount. No other listeners are attached.

**Reduced motion.** Rows and headers appear without the blur, lift or height animation, the guide is drawn immediately, the title shimmer and star twinkle stop, and folding happens instantly. Units still arrive on the same schedule.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Key the list on the turn: changing tasks in place keeps the revealed count, so a fresh run needs a new key.
- Appending tasks to a finished list resumes the ticker and fires onComplete again when the new units land.
- Give every task a stable id; open overrides are stored by id.

## Notes

- Chip icons are ReactNodes sized to 14px by the chip; colour them with theme tokens.
- Pass working={false} to drop the tail indicator, or a string to relabel it.

## Definition of done

The log starts with "Searching project files" shimmering and its steps landing one by one with file chips; when the fourth step lands the title reads "Found project files" and the task folds; after the last task the Working row disappears and onComplete shows the reply. Clicking a folded header sets aria-expanded to true and shows its steps; Add task appends a follow-up that streams in; Replay restarts from the first task.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Tech Badges Row

The row of technologies under a landing-page hero: a small glyph tile, the name and a muted version per entry, separated by dots. Glyphs are simple monogram tiles drawn inline (a rounded square and one or two letters in a tone), never brand logos, so any stack can be listed. Hovering or tabbing onto a badge lifts it onto a bordered surface and opens the kit Tooltip with the name, version and a one-line description. An `icon` variant drops the labels for tight spaces and lets the tooltip carry the name.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A "built with" strip of monogram glyphs, names and versions; each badge lifts on hover or focus and names itself in a tooltip.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Render a `ul` (`aria-label` "Built with") of `li`s that wrap and centre; in the `label` variant a dot separator precedes every badge after the first, hidden below 640px where the row wraps.
2. Each badge is a `span role="img"` with `aria-label` "<name> <version>" inside react-aria `Focusable`, which gives it a tab stop and lets the kit `TooltipTrigger` attach hover, focus and `aria-describedby` to a non-button element.
3. Draw the glyph as a 20×20 SVG: a tile in the badge `tone` (rx 5.5), a 1px white inner stroke at 18% so dark tiles still read on a dark page, and the monogram centred with `dy="0.36em"` — 11px for one letter, 8.5px with tighter tracking for two.
4. The lift is CSS: on `hover:` and `focus-visible:` the badge translates up 2px (4px for icon tiles) and gains `bg-background-primary-default`, a `border-button-default` border and `shadow-md`, over 200ms ease-out. `motion-reduce` keeps the surface change and cancels the translate and transition.
5. The kit `Tooltip` (placement top, 8px offset, no delay) shows the name and version in semibold caption type, with the description on a second, secondary line.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `lift = -2px label · -4px icon, 200ms ease-out`
  Enough to read as picked up without the row looking jumpy when the pointer sweeps across it.
- `glyph = 16px in the label row, 20px on a 40px tile`
  The label glyph matches the cap height of 13px body-2 text; the icon tile stays a comfortable 40px pointer target.
- `monogram size = 11px (1 letter) · 8.5px, -0.3 tracking (2 letters)`
  Two-letter monograms must fit the 20-unit tile with side bearing to spare.

## API

```ts
function TechBadgesRow(props: { badges?: TechBadge[]; variant?: "label" | "icon"; label?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type TechBadge = { id: string; name: string; version?: string; monogram: string; tone: string; description?: string }
```

- `badges: TechBadge[]` — default `DEFAULT_TECH_BADGES`
  Entries: id, name, optional version, a 1–2 letter monogram, a tile tone and an optional tooltip description.
- `variant: "label" | "icon"` — default `"label"`
  `label` shows glyph, name and version with dot separators; `icon` shows 40px glyph tiles only.
- `label: string` — default `"Built with"`
  Accessible name of the list.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the list.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** A rounded tile with a 1px inner highlight and the monogram centred on it. */
function MonogramGlyph({ monogram, tone, className }: { monogram: string; tone: string; className?: string }) {
  const small = monogram.length > 1;
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden className={cx("shrink-0", className)}>
      <rect width="20" height="20" rx="5.5" fill={tone} />
      <rect x="0.5" y="0.5" width="19" height="19" rx="5" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" strokeOpacity="0.18" />
      <text
        x="10"
        y="10"
        dy="0.36em"
        textAnchor="middle"
        fill="#ffffff"
        fontSize={small ? 8.5 : 11}
        fontWeight={700}
        letterSpacing={small ? -0.3 : 0}
        style={{ fontFamily: "inherit" }}
      >
        {monogram}
      </text>
    </svg>
  );
}

/*
 * The lift: on hover or focus-visible the badge rises 2px (4px for icon
 * tiles) and picks up a surface, border and shadow, over 200ms ease-out.
 * Under reduced motion the surface still appears but nothing moves.
 */
const LIFT =
  "transition-[translate,background-color,border-color,box-shadow] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none " +
  "hover:shadow-md hover:bg-background-primary-default hover:border-border-button-default " +
  "focus-visible:shadow-md focus-visible:bg-background-primary-default focus-visible:border-border-button-default " +
  "outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring";

function Badge({ badge, variant }: { badge: TechBadge; variant: "label" | "icon" }) {
  const full = badge.version ? `${badge.name} ${badge.version}` : badge.name;
  return (
    <TooltipTrigger>
      <Focusable>
        <span
          role="img"
          aria-label={full}
          className={cx(
            "inline-flex cursor-default items-center border select-none",
            LIFT,
            variant === "label"
              ? "gap-1.5 rounded-full border-transparent px-2.5 py-1 hover:-translate-y-0.5 focus-visible:-translate-y-0.5 motion-reduce:hover:translate-y-0 motion-reduce:focus-visible:translate-y-0"
              : "size-10 justify-center rounded-xl border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default shadow-xs hover:-translate-y-1 focus-visible:-translate-y-1 motion-reduce:hover:translate-y-0 motion-reduce:focus-visible:translate-y-0",
          )}
        >
          <MonogramGlyph monogram={badge.monogram} tone={badge.tone} className={variant === "label" ? "size-4" : "size-5"} />
          {variant === "label" && (
            <>
              <span className="text-body-2-medium whitespace-nowrap text-text-primary">{badge.name}</span>
              {badge.version && (
                <span className="text-caption-1-regular whitespace-nowrap text-text-tertiary">v{badge.version}</span>
              )}
            </>
          )}
        </span>
      </Focusable>
      <Tooltip placement="top" offset={8}>
        <span className="text-caption-1-semibold">{full}</span>
        {badge.description && <span className="block text-caption-2-regular text-text-secondary">{badge.description}</span>}
      </Tooltip>
    </TooltipTrigger>
  );
}

export function TechBadgesRow({
  badges = DEFAULT_TECH_BADGES,
  variant = "label",
  label = "Built with",
  className,
}: TechBadgesRowProps) {
  return (
    <ul
      aria-label={label}
      className={cx(
        "flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center",
        variant === "label" ? "gap-x-1 gap-y-2" : "gap-2",
        className,
      )}
    >
      {badges.map((b, i) => (
        <li key={b.id} className="flex items-center gap-1">
          {variant === "label" && i > 0 && (
            <span aria-hidden className="hidden px-1 text-text-disabled sm:inline">
              ·
            </span>
          )}
          <Badge badge={b} variant={variant} />
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up: hover lift is CSS and react-aria owns the tooltip timers and listeners.

**Reduced motion.** Badges still gain their surface, border and shadow on hover and focus, but `motion-reduce` cancels the translate and the transition, so nothing moves; the kit Tooltip appears without its scale and blur.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Shipping traced brand logos as glyphs: they carry trademark rules and break the row's visual rhythm. Monogram tiles in a tone are neutral and extensible.
- Putting tooltips on plain non-focusable spans: keyboard and screen-reader users never get them. `Focusable` plus an `img` role makes each badge reachable and described.
- Relying on the tooltip for the name in the `icon` variant without an `aria-label`: tooltips are descriptions, the badge itself still needs a name.

## Notes

- `DEFAULT_TECH_BADGES` covers Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, Motion and React Aria; pass `badges` to add or replace entries.
- Tones are SVG fills, so any CSS colour works; the white inner stroke keeps near-black tiles visible in dark mode.

The row reads "Next.js v16 · React v19.2 · Tailwind CSS v4 · TypeScript v5.9 · Motion v12 · React Aria v1.17", each with a monogram tile. Hovering "React" lifts that badge 2px and opens a tooltip reading "React 19.2 / UI runtime". Tabbing onto a badge does the same. In the icon card, hovering the "TT" tile shows "TanStack Table 8.21".
