# Build: Tree View

A nested folder tree on React Aria `Tree`, which supplies the treegrid roles, expansion and selection state, typeahead and locale-aware arrow keys. On top of it the kit draws connected trunk lines with a rounded elbow into each child, swaps the folder icon to an open folder when a branch is expanded, and replaces the collection renderer so rows unfold with a height, fade and blur animation instead of popping in.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

React Aria file tree with curved guide lines, folder icons that open, and rows that unfold and blur in as branches expand.

- Category: navigation
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, motion@^12.43.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. `TreeView` renders `AriaTree` with `selectionMode` defaulting to `"single"`, a `data-size` and `data-show-guides` attribute, and a bordered `rounded-3xl p-2` card. It also provides a custom renderer through `CollectionRendererContext`: `TREE_VIEW_RENDERER` is `DefaultCollectionRenderer` with `CollectionRoot` swapped for `AnimatedTreeCollection`. The swap only happens when the parent renderer is the default and the tree has no `dragAndDropHooks`, so virtualizers and drag-and-drop keep working.
2. `AnimatedTreeCollection` reads `TreeStateContext` and maps the flattened collection (skipping `content` nodes) into `AnimatedTreeRow`s inside `<AnimatePresence initial={false}>`, keyed by node key. Each row is a `motion.div` that animates from `height: 0, opacity: 0, y: -4, blur(4px)` to `height: auto`, 1px vertical padding, `opacity: 1, y: 0, blur(0)` over 0.28s with ease `[0.22, 1, 0.36, 1]`, and reverses on exit. Because of `initial={false}`, rows present on first render do not animate.
3. An exiting row has already left React Aria's collection, so `AnimatedTreeRow` keeps the last `state` it saw while `useIsPresent()` was true and re-provides it through `TreeStateContext`. That lets the row keep rendering its label and guides while it collapses. It is marked `inert`, `aria-hidden` and `data-tree-view-exiting`, so it cannot be focused or announced.
4. `TreeViewItem` indents with `paddingInlineStart: calc(0.5rem + (level − 1) × 1.25rem)` and uses `min-h-9` rows (`min-h-8` and `text-body-2-regular` when the tree is `size="sm"`). Hover, press, keyboard focus and selection all paint `MENU_ITEM_ACTIVE` (`bg-dropdown-item-hover-background`), and focus adds an inset 2px ring. Branches get a `slot="chevron"` Aria button whose `RiArrowRightSLine` rotates 90° when open over 150ms. Leaves get a spacer (`w-5` at the root, `w-2` when nested).
5. The icon defaults to `RiFolder3Line` / `RiFolderOpenLine` for branches and `RiFileLine` for leaves, at `size-4 opacity-50`. `icon={null}` hides it, `expandedIcon` overrides the open state and `iconClassName` tints it.
6. `TreeGuides` draws the lines in an `aria-hidden` absolute layer. It walks up `parentKey` and adds a full-height 1px trunk for every ancestor level that still has a `nextKey` sibling, so lines run unbroken through expanded subtrees. A nested row then draws its own elbow: a vertical stub to 6px above centre, then an SVG `M0.5 0 Q0.5 6 6.5 6 H…` quadratic curve into the row (12px wide for branches, 16px for leaves). It adds a tail below when the row has a next sibling, and a bridge down from the icon when the row itself is expanded. Each axis sits at `calc(1.125rem + depth × 1.25rem)`.
7. A capture-phase `onKeyDownCapture` on a `display: contents` wrapper completes Right Arrow (Left Arrow in RTL) on an already-expanded row: it finds the next row in DOM order with a deeper `aria-level`, skips disabled and exiting rows, and focuses it. React Aria handles expanding closed branches and every other key.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `indent step = 1.25rem (20px) per level, from a 0.5rem base`
  The guide axes use the same 1.25rem step offset by 1.125rem, which centres each trunk under its parent's chevron. Change one and the lines stop lining up with the icons.
- `row animation = 0.28s, ease [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1], y −4px, blur 4px`
  A strong ease-out lets the height open quickly and settle softly. The small upward offset and blur make children look as if they slide out from under the parent rather than being inserted.
- `row heights = min-h-9 (36px) md, min-h-8 (32px) sm`
  Matches the kit's menu item heights, so a tree in a sidebar lines up with menus and nav items next to it.
- `elbow = quadratic curve, 6px radius; branch 12px wide, leaf 16px`
  Branches have a 20px chevron button before the icon and leaves only a spacer, so the elbow length differs to land right at each icon.

## API

```ts
function TreeView<T extends object>(props: AriaTreeProps<T> & { size?: "sm" | "md"; showGuides?: boolean; onKeyDownCapture?: KeyboardEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function TreeViewItem<T extends object = object>(props: Omit<AriaTreeItemProps<T>, "textValue" | "children"> & { label: string; textValue?: string; icon?: IconComponent | null; expandedIcon?: IconComponent; iconClassName?: string; trailingContent?: ReactNode; children?: ReactNode; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
export { Collection as TreeViewCollection } from "react-aria-components"
```

- `size: "sm" | "md"` — default `"md"`
  36px or 32px rows. Small also drops the label to the 13px body-2 style.
- `showGuides: boolean` — default `true`
  Draws trunk lines and curved branches beside nested rows.
- `selectionMode: "none" | "single" | "multiple"` — default `"single"`
  React Aria selection mode. Selected rows use the same tint as hover.
- `defaultExpandedKeys / expandedKeys: Iterable<Key>`
  Uncontrolled or controlled set of open branches.
- `TreeViewItem.label: string`
  Visible label, also the default `textValue` for typeahead and accessible naming.
- `TreeViewItem.icon: IconComponent | null`
  Defaults to folder for branches and file for leaves. `null` hides it.
- `TreeViewItem.iconClassName: string`
  Extra classes for the icon, typically a colour such as `text-accent-700`.
- `TreeViewItem.trailingContent: ReactNode`
  Metadata at the end of the row in caption type, such as a size or count.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const TREE_VIEW_RENDERER = {
  ...DefaultCollectionRenderer,
  CollectionRoot: AnimatedTreeCollection,
};

function AnimatedTreeCollection({ collection, ...props }: ComponentProps<typeof DefaultCollectionRenderer.CollectionRoot>) {
  const state = useContext(TreeStateContext);
  if (!state) return <DefaultCollectionRenderer.CollectionRoot collection={collection} {...props} />;

  return (
    <AnimatePresence initial={false}>
      {Array.from(collection).filter((node) => node.type !== "content").map((node) => (
        <AnimatedTreeRow key={node.key} state={state}>
          {node.render?.(node)}
        </AnimatedTreeRow>
      ))}
    </AnimatePresence>
  );
}

type TreeState = NonNullable<ContextType<typeof TreeStateContext>>;

function TreeGuides({ state, id, level, expanded, branchWidth, direction }: {
  state: TreeState;
  id: Key;
  level: number;
  expanded: boolean;
  branchWidth: number;
  direction: "ltr" | "rtl";
}) {
  const node = state.collection.getItem(id);
  if (!node) return null;

  // A descendant carries an outer trunk only when its ancestor has a sibling
  // still to come. This keeps the line connected through an expanded subtree,
  // while the final child's elbow closes that level of the tree.
  const continuingLevels: number[] = [];
  let ancestor = node.parentKey != null ? state.collection.getItem(node.parentKey) : null;
  let ancestorLevel = level - 1;
  while (ancestor) {
    if (ancestor.type === "item") {
      if (ancestorLevel > 1 && ancestor.nextKey != null) continuingLevels.push(ancestorLevel - 2);
      ancestorLevel--;
    }
    ancestor = ancestor.parentKey != null ? state.collection.getItem(ancestor.parentKey) : null;
  }

  const axis = (depth: number) => `calc(1.125rem + ${depth} * 1.25rem)`;

  return (
    <span aria-hidden data-tree-view-guides className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 text-foreground-icon-quaternary group-data-[show-guides=false]/tree-view:hidden">
      {continuingLevels.map((depth) => (
        <span key={depth} data-tree-view-trunk className="absolute -inset-y-px w-px bg-current" style={{ insetInlineStart: axis(depth) }} />
      ))}
      {level > 1 && (
        <span data-tree-view-branch className="absolute -inset-y-px" style={{ insetInlineStart: axis(level - 2), width: branchWidth }}>
          <span className="absolute start-0 top-0 w-px bg-current" style={{ bottom: "calc(50% + 6px)" }} />
          <svg
            width={branchWidth}
            height="7"
            viewBox={`0 0 ${branchWidth} 7`}
            fill="none"
            className={cx("absolute start-0", direction === "rtl" && "-scale-x-100")}
            style={{ top: "calc(50% - 6px)" }}
          >
            <path d={`M0.5 0 Q0.5 6 6.5 6 H${branchWidth - 0.5}`} stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="1" />
          </svg>
          {node.nextKey != null && (
            <span data-tree-view-tail className="absolute start-0 bottom-0 w-px bg-current" style={{ top: "calc(50% - 6px)" }} />
          )}
        </span>
      )}
      {expanded && (
        <span data-tree-view-bridge className="absolute -bottom-px w-px bg-current" style={{ insetInlineStart: axis(level - 1), top: "calc(50% + 8px)" }} />
      )}
    </span>
  );
}

function AnimatedTreeRow({ state, children }: { state: TreeState; children: ReactNode }) {
  const isPresent = useIsPresent();
  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();
  const [lastPresentState, setLastPresentState] = useState(state);
  if (isPresent && lastPresentState !== state) setLastPresentState(state);

  // Preserve the row's last collection while it fades out. The live tree has
  // already removed it from keyboard navigation; the retained visual is inert.
  return (
    <motion.div
      role="presentation"
      className="relative min-w-0 shrink-0 overflow-hidden"
      data-tree-view-exiting={!isPresent || undefined}
      aria-hidden={!isPresent || undefined}
      inert={!isPresent}
      initial={reduceMotion ? false : { height: 0, paddingTop: 0, paddingBottom: 0, opacity: 0, y: -4, filter: "blur(4px)" }}
      animate={{ height: "auto", paddingTop: 1, paddingBottom: 1, opacity: 1, y: 0, filter: "blur(0px)" }}
      exit={{ height: 0, paddingTop: 0, paddingBottom: 0, opacity: 0, y: reduceMotion ? 0 : -4, filter: reduceMotion ? "blur(0px)" : "blur(4px)" }}
      transition={{ duration: reduceMotion ? 0 : 0.28, ease: [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1] }}
    >
      <TreeStateContext.Provider value={isPresent ? state : lastPresentState}>
        {children}
      </TreeStateContext.Provider>
    </motion.div>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to release manually. `AnimatePresence` unmounts exiting rows when their exit animation finishes, and motion stops any running animation when the tree unmounts. There are no listeners outside React.

**Reduced motion.** With `useReducedMotion()` true the rows skip the entry animation (`initial={false}`), exit with no offset or blur, and the transition duration becomes 0, so branches open and close instantly. The chevron rotation and colour transitions have `motion-reduce:transition-none`.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not animate rows with CSS `height` transitions on the Aria items. A collapsed child is removed from the collection immediately, so there is nothing left to animate. The exit only works because `AnimatePresence` keeps the motion wrapper and the row keeps its last tree state.
- Do not leave exiting rows focusable. Without `inert` and `aria-hidden`, arrow keys and screen readers would land on rows that are already gone from the tree.
- Do not reuse ids across the tree. React Aria keys expansion, selection and the guide walk on `id`, so duplicates confuse all three.
- Do not forget `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on `TreeView`. React Aria warns when a tree has no accessible name.
- Do not force the custom renderer when using drag and drop or a virtualizer. The component already falls back to the parent renderer in those cases.

## Notes

- For data-driven trees, pass `items` and render recursively with the re-exported `TreeViewCollection` (React Aria `Collection`).
- Set `showGuides={false}` to hide every line with one `group-data-[show-guides=false]` rule, leaving plain indentation.
- The tree grows with its content and does not scroll itself. Wrap it in a scroll container if it lives in a fixed-height sidebar.

## Definition of done

With `src` and `components` expanded, nested rows are indented 20px per level and joined to their parent by thin lines with rounded elbows. The last child's elbow closes its level with no tail. Collapsing a folder makes its children shrink, fade and blur out over about 0.3s while the open-folder icon switches back to a closed folder and the chevron rotates back. Expanding animates them in. Clicking a row selects it with a tinted background. Arrow keys move between rows, Right on a closed folder opens it and Right on an open folder moves to its first child.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Trend Badge

The small change pill beside the big numbers on the BoardUI dashboard KPI cards ("+5.3%", "-2.1%", "0.00%"). The direction comes from the sign of the value after rounding, so a tiny change never shows as a red "-0.0%". Up is lime and down is rose, swapped with invert for metrics where lower is better. A single arrow rotates between up, sideways and down, so a live value turns it smoothly instead of swapping icons. Screen readers hear "Up 5.3% vs last month" instead of a bare "+5.3".

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Up, down or flat change pill for dashboard KPIs: one rotating arrow, a signed percent, lime, rose or grey, in three sizes.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The value is rounded to the shown decimals first; the sign of that rounded number picks up, down or flat (direction overrides it), and a rounded -0 is folded to 0.
2. Tone reuses the kit Chip colours: CHIP_COLORS.lime for good, CHIP_COLORS.rose for bad and CHIP_COLORS.neutral (tertiary background, secondary text) for flat; invert flips which direction counts as good.
3. The glyph is always RiArrowUpLine, rotated 0, 90 (mirrored under rtl) or 180 degrees with transition-[rotate], and the pill fades its colours with transition-colors, both 200 to 300ms ease-out and off under motion-reduce.
4. Intl.NumberFormat with signDisplay exceptZero prints "+5.3%" and "0.0%"; that visible text is aria-hidden and an sr-only span reads the direction word, the unsigned percent and the optional context.
5. A fixed locale (en-US by default) keeps the server and client text identical, so the badge hydrates cleanly.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `sizes = sm h-5 / md h-6 / lg h-7`
  sm fits table cells, md sits beside body text and lg matches the 28px pills next to the KPI numbers.
- `radius = rounded-md (sm, md), rounded-lg (lg)`
  The reference pills are squared-off rectangles, not full capsules.
- `rotate = 0 / 90 / 180deg, 300ms ease-out`
  One glyph that turns reads as the same metric changing, not a new icon popping in.
- `decimals = 1 by default`
  Matches "+5.3%"; pass 2 for "0.00%" as on the Orders card.

## API

```ts
export function TrendBadge({ value, direction, invert, decimals, size, icon, context, locale, className }: TrendBadgeProps): JSX.Element
```

- `value: number`
  Change in percent, e.g. 5.3 or -2.1.
- `direction: 'up' | 'down' | 'flat'`
  Overrides the direction taken from the rounded value.
- `invert: boolean` — default `false`
  Down is good: down turns lime and up rose.
- `decimals: number` — default `1`
  Fraction digits shown and used for rounding.
- `size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` — default `'md'`
  Pill height, padding and type size.
- `icon: boolean` — default `true`
  Show the rotating arrow.
- `context: string`
  Appended to the screen-reader text, e.g. "vs last month".
- `locale: string` — default `'en-US'`
  Number formatting locale.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function TrendBadge({
  value,
  direction,
  invert = false,
  decimals = 1,
  size = 'md',
  icon = true,
  context,
  locale = 'en-US',
  className,
}: TrendBadgeProps) {
  // Round first, so -0.04 at one decimal reads "0.0%" and counts as flat
  // instead of showing a red "-0.0%".
  const factor = 10 ** decimals;
  const rounded = Math.round(value * factor) / factor || 0;
  const dir: TrendDirection = direction ?? (rounded > 0 ? 'up' : rounded < 0 ? 'down' : 'flat');
  const tone = dir === 'flat' ? TONE.flat : (dir === 'up') !== invert ? TONE.good : TONE.bad;

  const format = (n: number, signDisplay: 'exceptZero' | 'never') =>
    new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { minimumFractionDigits: decimals, maximumFractionDigits: decimals, signDisplay }).format(n);
  const s = SIZE[size];

  return (
    <span
      data-direction={dir}
      className={cx(
        'inline-flex shrink-0 items-center whitespace-nowrap tabular-nums',
        'transition-colors duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none',
        s.pill,
        tone,
        className,
      )}
    >
      {icon ? (
        <RiArrowUpLine
          aria-hidden
          className={cx(
            'shrink-0 transition-[rotate] duration-300 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none',
            s.icon,
            ROTATE[dir],
          )}
        />
      ) : null}
      <span aria-hidden>{format(rounded, 'exceptZero')}%</span>
      <span className="sr-only">
        {`${WORD[dir]} ${format(Math.abs(rounded), 'never')}%${context ? ` ${context}` : ''}`}
      </span>
    </span>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Stateless span: no timers, listeners or effects.

**Reduced motion.** Under prefers-reduced-motion the arrow snaps to its new angle and the colours switch at once; nothing else moves.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Pass the change in percent (5.3), not as a ratio (0.053); the badge only formats, it does not multiply.
- Without context the screen-reader text is just "Up 5.3%"; add context ("vs last month") when the comparison period is not read out nearby.
- For cost, churn or latency set invert, or a drop shows rose although it is good news.

## Notes

- icon={false} gives the arrowless pills of the reference KPI cards; the arrow is on by default for tables and lists.
- It renders a plain span with no hooks, so it works in server components.

## Definition of done

The KPI cards show +5.3% lime, -2.1% rose and 0.00% grey; stepping the conversion change from +1.0% down through 0.0% to -0.5% turns its arrow from up to sideways to down and its colour from lime to grey to rose; the churn badge reads -0.6% in lime.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Tweened Cursor Uniform

A full-quad fragment shader draws a procedural grid and pulls its UVs toward a lens centred on the pointer. The lens position is not assigned into the uniform — GSAP tweens it onto a plain object, and the render loop copies that object across each frame, so the distortion trails the cursor and then comes fully to rest under it. Presence is a second, independent tween, so leaving the container dims the lens where it stands rather than dragging it away.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A shader grid with a lens under the pointer, whose position is tweened into the uniform so it settles instead of chasing.

- Category: cursor
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1, gsap@^3.15.0

## How it works

1. A `pointermove` handler converts client coordinates into NDC against the live container rect: `x = ((e.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width) * 2 - 1` and `y = -(((e.clientY - rect.top) / rect.height) * 2 - 1)`, y negated because NDC counts upward and CSS counts downward.
2. That NDC pair is tweened onto a plain `{ x, y }` object with `gsap.to(pos, { x, y, duration: 0.6, ease: "power3.out", overwrite: true })`. This is the smoothing. Nothing else damps: the uniform copy in the rAF loop is a straight assignment.
3. The contrast with `useSmoothPointer` is the point. `damp` closes a fixed fraction of the remaining gap per second — always moving, always behind, asymptotic. A tween has a duration and an end, so `power3.out` decelerates the lens into a hard stop exactly under the cursor when the hand stops.
4. Presence is a separate scalar tweened to 1 over 0.4s on move and back to 0 over 0.6s on `pointerleave`, multiplied into the falloff in the shader. Splitting it from position is what makes the lens fade out in place instead of sliding off toward a parked coordinate.
5. The fragment shader works in aspect-corrected centre space, computes a Gaussian `fall = exp(-d² / r²)` from the cursor, and displaces the sampling point with `warped = p - normalize(p - c) * fall * uStrength * uAmount` before the grid function reads it — so the grid compresses toward the cursor like glass rather than smearing.
6. Anti-aliasing of the grid lines is derived from `uResolution` (`w = widthPx * cells / res`) instead of `fwidth`, so the same source compiles on a WebGL1 context with no derivatives extension pragma.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `PARKED_NDC = 999`
  Initial value of the tweened cursor object. Far outside the -1..1 NDC range, so `exp(-d²/r²)` underflows to exactly 0 and the very first frame is guaranteed lens-free. Initialising at (0,0) puts a full-strength bulge dead centre before the pointer has ever moved.
- `followDuration = 0.6`
  Seconds for the lens to reach the pointer. This is long for a cursor effect and deliberately so — the lens reads as heavy glass being dragged. Under ~0.25 it is welded to the pointer and the trailing quality disappears.
- `PRESENCE_IN / PRESENCE_OUT = 0.4 / 0.6`
  Asymmetric on purpose. Arrival must beat the eye to the pointer; departure is slower so the lens reads as dissipating rather than being switched off.
- `radius = 0.28`
  Gaussian sigma in centre space, where the short edge spans 1.0. So the lens core is a bit over a quarter of the container height. Past ~0.45 the falloff no longer reaches zero inside the frame and the whole grid warps.
- `amount = 0.22`
  Peak UV displacement toward the cursor, in centre-space units. Above ~0.35 the pull exceeds the local grid spacing and lines fold back through each other, which reads as a rendering fault.
- `pixelRatio cap = 2`
  Fill-rate is quadratic in DPR. On a 3x display an uncapped full-container fragment shader costs 2.25x more per frame for no visible gain.

## API

```ts
function TweenedCursorUniform(props: { followDuration?: number; radius?: number; amount?: number; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `followDuration: number` — default `0.6`
  Seconds for the lens to catch the pointer.
- `radius: number` — default `0.28`
  Gaussian sigma of the lens, in centre-space units where the short edge is 1.
- `amount: number` — default `0.22`
  Peak UV displacement toward the cursor at full strength.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root container via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const FOLLOW_EASE = 'power3.out';
const PRESENCE_IN = 0.4;
const PRESENCE_OUT = 0.6;
/** Far outside NDC, so `exp(-d²/r²)` underflows to 0 before the first move. */
const PARKED_NDC = 999;

export function TweenedCursorUniform({
  followDuration = 0.6,
  radius = 0.28,
  amount = 0.22,
  className,
}: TweenedCursorUniformProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const api = useRef<Scene | null>(null);

  /* The two tween targets. Plain objects, not uniforms: GSAP writes numbers
     onto them and the loop copies them across once per frame. Tweening the
     uniform's `.value` vector directly works too, but this keeps the tween
     alive across a material rebuild. */
  const smooth = useRef({ x: PARKED_NDC, y: PARKED_NDC });
  const presence = useRef({ value: 0 });

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const { inView } = useInView(host, { rootMargin: '128px' });
  const visible = useVisibility();

  /* Build once. Never in the resize effect — recreating a WebGLRenderer on
     every resize leaks contexts, and Chromium kills the OLDEST live context
     when the ~16-per-process ceiling is hit, so an unrelated canvas
     elsewhere on the page goes black. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !hasWebGL()) return;

    /* three owns its canvas and it is appended here, per effect run. Handing
       the constructor a React-rendered `<canvas ref>` was the bug: cleanup
       calls `forceContextLoss()`, and `getContext` on an element that has been
       through that returns the same dead context, so the next construction
       threw straight into the catch below and the component stayed blank. The
       preview host hides components with `<Activity mode="hidden">` — effects
       unmount, the DOM does not — so that cycle is ordinary scrolling here,
       not just StrictMode in development. */
    let renderer: THREE.WebGLRenderer;
    try {
      renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({
        antialias: false,
        alpha: false,
        powerPreference: 'low-power',
      });
    } catch {
      // A context can still be refused between the probe and the construction —
      // the tab may have hit the browser's live-context ceiling in between. three
      // throws rather than returning null, and an uncaught throw here takes the
      // page with it.
      return;
    }
    renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio(2));
    renderer.domElement.className = 'block h-full w-full';
    el.append(renderer.domElement);

    const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader,
      fragmentShader,
      uniforms: {
        uResolution: { value: new THREE.Vector2(1, 1) },
        uCursor: { value: new THREE.Vector2(PARKED_NDC, PARKED_NDC) },
        uStrength: { value: 0 },
        uTime: { value: 0 },
        uRadius: { value: radius },
        uAmount: { value: amount },
        uInk: { value: new THREE.Color(0.08, 0.09, 0.11) },
        uPaper: { value: new THREE.Color(0.04, 0.04, 0.05) },
        uAccent: { value: new THREE.Color(0.95, 0.55, 0.2) },
      },
    });

    const geometry = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(2, 2);
    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material));

    // A 2x2 plane under an identity-ish ortho camera is a full-screen quad
    // with no projection maths and no camera to keep in sync on resize.
    const camera = new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0, 1);

    api.current = { renderer, camera, scene, geometry, material };

    return () => {
      api.current = null;
      // `dispose()` alone frees GPU objects but leaves the context alive;
      // only `forceContextLoss()` hands it back, which is what this does.
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      geometry.dispose();
      material.dispose();
      renderer.domElement.remove();
    };
    // Deliberately empty. `radius` and `amount` are uniform values and used to
    // sit here, which meant changing either tore the renderer down and built a
    // whole new context for what is one float. The effect below writes them
    // onto the live material instead.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  /* Uniform values, not construction inputs. Written straight onto the live
     material so a prop change costs one assignment rather than a context. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const s = api.current;
    if (!s) return;
    const r = s.material.uniforms.uRadius;
    if (r) r.value = radius;
    const a = s.material.uniforms.uAmount;
    if (a) a.value = amount;
  }, [radius, amount]);

  /* Size in its own effect so a resize never touches the renderer's lifetime. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const s = api.current;
    if (!s || width === 0 || height === 0) return;
    s.renderer.setSize(width, height, false);
    const res = s.material.uniforms.uResolution;
    if (res) (res.value as THREE.Vector2).set(width, height);
    // Render once so a resize while paused still repaints, rather than
    // stretching the previous framebuffer until the pointer moves again.
    s.renderer.render(s.scene, s.camera);
  }, [width, height]);

  /* Pointer -> tween. The tween is the smoothing; nothing else damps. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || reduced || !hasWebGL()) return;
    // A coarse pointer only produces events during a drag, so the lens would
    // pop into existence under a finger and vanish on release.
    if (!window.matchMedia('(pointer: fine)').matches) return;

    const pos = smooth.current;
    const pres = presence.current;

    const onMove = (e: PointerEvent) => {
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;
      const x = ((e.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width) * 2 - 1;
      const y = -(((e.clientY - rect.top) / rect.height) * 2 - 1);

      // `overwrite: true` (not 'auto'): each move must kill the whole previous
      // tween, including the half of it that has not started easing yet.
      gsap.to(pos, { x, y, duration: followDuration, ease: FOLLOW_EASE, overwrite: true });
      gsap.to(pres, { value: 1, duration: PRESENCE_IN, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto' });
    };

    const onLeave = () => {
      // Fade presence only. Leaving position alone means the lens dims where
      // it stands; tweening it to a corner instead drags a visible streak.
      gsap.to(pres, { value: 0, duration: PRESENCE_OUT, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto' });
    };

    el.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove, { passive: true });
    el.addEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);

    return () => {
      el.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
      el.removeEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);
      gsap.killTweensOf([pos, pres]);
    };
  }, [followDuration, reduced]);

  useRaf(
    (_dt, elapsed) => {
      const s = api.current;
      if (!s) return;
      const u = s.material.uniforms;
      const cursor = u.uCursor;
      const strength = u.uStrength;
      const time = u.uTime;
      if (cursor) (cursor.value as THREE.Vector2).set(smooth.current.x, smooth.current.y);
      if (strength) strength.value = presence.current.value;
      if (time) time.value = elapsed;
      s.renderer.render(s.scene, s.camera);
    },
    inView && visible && !reduced,
  );

  /* Reduced motion still gets a picture — a single frame with the lens parked
     off-centre — rather than an empty box. One render, then nothing. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const s = api.current;
    if (!s || !reduced || width === 0 || height === 0) return;
    const cursor = s.material.uniforms.uCursor;
    const strength = s.material.uniforms.uStrength;
    if (cursor) (cursor.value as THREE.Vector2).set(-0.25, 0.15);
    if (strength) strength.value = 1;
    s.renderer.render(s.scene, s.camera);
  }, [reduced, width, height]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes both pointer listeners and kills the tweens on the two plain objects. The build effect nulls its handle, calls `disposeRenderer` (which stops the animation loop, disposes, forces context loss, and zeroes the backing store), then disposes the geometry and the material. The rAF subscription is released by `useRaf`.

**Reduced motion.** The rAF loop and the pointer listeners never attach. A single frame is rendered with the lens parked slightly off-centre at full strength, so the component is a static composed image of the effect rather than an empty box. It repaints once on resize and never again.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Assigning the pointer straight into the uniform and smoothing in the shader instead. The shader has no memory between frames without a render target, so the usual workaround is to lerp a JS variable per frame with a fixed alpha — which is frame-rate dependent and converges twice as fast at 120Hz.
- Tweening position and presence together. On `pointerleave` the lens then slides toward its parked coordinate at full strength, dragging a bright streak across the whole canvas on the way out.
- Leaving the tweened cursor at (0, 0) on mount. A full-strength bulge sits dead centre from the first painted frame until the user moves, which looks like a baked-in artefact rather than an interaction.
- Using `overwrite: "auto"` on the position tween. Auto only retires *rendered* conflicts; a burst of moves inside one frame can leave the earlier tween partly live. `overwrite: true` kills the previous tween outright, which is what you want when every event supersedes the last.
- Recreating the `WebGLRenderer` inside the resize effect. Each resize leaks a context, and Chromium silently kills the oldest of its ~16 per-process contexts, so an unrelated canvas elsewhere on the page goes black.
- Calling `renderer.dispose()` and stopping there. That frees GPU objects but not the context itself; `forceContextLoss()` — what `disposeRenderer` does — is the call that actually hands it back.
- Not repainting after a resize while the loop is paused. The framebuffer keeps the old dimensions and the browser stretches the last frame, so an off-screen preview reappears visibly smeared.

## Notes

- Gated on `(pointer: fine)`. On touch the listeners never attach, so the canvas renders the idle grid with the lens parked outside NDC — a tap cannot pop a bulge under the finger and leave it there on release.
- Guarded with `hasWebGL()`: on a blocklisted GPU or with hardware acceleration off, nothing is constructed and the container is simply an empty dark panel rather than a permanently blank canvas.
- The loop is gated on `useInView` plus `useVisibility`, so an off-screen or backgrounded instance costs zero GPU time.

## Definition of done

Move across the panel and the grid compresses under a soft circular lens that arrives about half a second behind the pointer, then settles precisely under it when you stop. Leave the panel and the lens fades out where it stands without sliding. Resize the container and the lens stays circular rather than becoming an ellipse. Unmount and the WebGL context count in about:gpu goes back down.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Typewriter Install

The install line of a landing page: a small card with package-manager tabs on top and a monospace command below that appears one character at a time behind an accent caret, then idles with the caret blinking. Switching tabs swaps the command and types it again from the start; the copy button copies the whole command at any moment and confirms with a check. Screen readers get the full command at once, and reduced motion shows it fully typed.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

An install command that types itself behind a caret; pnpm, npm, yarn and bun tabs restart the typing and a copy button takes the full line.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: react-aria-components@^1.22.1, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Render a react-aria `Tabs` with one `Tab` and one `TabPanel` per command (`installCommands(pkg)` builds pnpm add / npm install / yarn add / bun add). Only the selected panel is mounted, so a tab change unmounts the old line and mounts a fresh one: the typing restarts without any reset logic.
2. Inside the panel, `TypedLine` runs a `setTimeout` chain: after `startDelay` (320ms) it bumps a character count, then schedules the next one with `charDelay` — `speed` (42ms) times a deterministic ±20% jitter from the index, ×2.4 after a space and ×1.6 after `@` or `/`. The effect cleanup clears the pending timer.
3. Stack two layers in one grid cell: the full command `invisible` underneath (it fixes the final width and wrapping, so the card never grows) and `text.slice(0, count)` plus the caret on top. Both are `aria-hidden`; an `sr-only` copy of the full command is what assistive tech reads.
4. The caret is a 2px accent bar held solid while typing; once the count reaches the end it gets `data-idle="true"` and a step-end blink keyframe (on 55%, off 45% of 1.06s), emitted once through React 19 `<style href precedence>`.
5. The copy button calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText` with the selected command, crossfades the copy icon into a success check for 1.6s and announces "Copied to clipboard" through a `role="status"` region; the reset timer is cleared on re-click and unmount.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `speed = 42ms per character, ±20% jitter`
  A 24-character command lands in about a second: slow enough to read as typing, fast enough that nobody waits to copy.
- `word beat = ×2.4 after a space, ×1.6 after @ or /`
  People type in words; a pause between words is what makes uniform per-key timing stop looking mechanical.
- `startDelay = 320ms`
  Shows the empty prompt and caret for a beat after a tab change, so the restart is visible as a restart.
- `copied state = 1.6s`
  Long enough to see the check after the pointer leaves the button, short enough that a second copy gets fresh feedback.

## API

```ts
function TypewriterInstall(props: { packageName?: string; commands?: InstallCommand[]; value?: string; defaultValue?: string; onChange?: (id: string) => void; speed?: number; startDelay?: number; prompt?: string; label?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
type InstallCommand = { id: string; label: string; command: string }
```

- `packageName: string` — default `"motion"`
  Package used to build the default pnpm, npm, yarn and bun commands.
- `commands: InstallCommand[]`
  Replaces the default commands: { id, label, command } per tab.
- `value: string`
  Controlled selected tab id.
- `defaultValue: string` — default `commands[0].id`
  Initial tab id when uncontrolled.
- `onChange: (id: string) => void`
  Called with the newly selected tab id.
- `speed: number` — default `42`
  Base milliseconds per character.
- `startDelay: number` — default `320`
  Milliseconds before the first character after mount or a tab change.
- `prompt: string` — default `"$"`
  Glyph shown before the command.
- `label: string` — default `"Package manager"`
  Accessible name of the tab list.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the card.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * Delay before character `i`. Deterministic, so server and client agree and
 * every replay has the same rhythm: ±20% around `speed` from the index, a
 * longer beat after a space (the eye reads word by word) and after `@`/`/`.
 */
function charDelay(text: string, i: number, speed: number) {
  const jitter = 0.8 + ((i * 37) % 9) / 20;
  const prev = text[i - 1];
  const beat = prev === " " ? 2.4 : prev === "@" || prev === "/" ? 1.6 : 1;
  return speed * jitter * beat;
}

/** One typed line. Mounted per tab, so a tab change restarts it. */
function TypedLine({ text, speed, startDelay, prompt }: { text: string; speed: number; startDelay: number; prompt: string }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (reduced) return;
    let i = 0;
    let timer = window.setTimeout(function step() {
      i += 1;
      setCount(i);
      if (i < text.length) timer = window.setTimeout(step, charDelay(text, i, speed));
    }, startDelay);
    return () => window.clearTimeout(timer);
  }, [text, speed, startDelay, reduced]);

  // Derived, not stored: reduced motion shows the whole line on the same
  // render the preference is known, with no typing frame in between.
  const shown = reduced ? text.length : Math.min(count, text.length);
  const done = shown >= text.length;

  return (
    <div className="flex min-w-0 items-baseline gap-2.5 font-mono text-body-2-regular">
      <span aria-hidden className="shrink-0 select-none text-text-tertiary">
        {prompt}
      </span>
      {/* The full line sits invisibly underneath to hold the final width and
          wrap, so the card never grows while the line types. */}
      <span className="grid min-w-0 flex-1 break-all">
        <span aria-hidden className="invisible col-start-1 row-start-1">
          {text}
          <span className="inline-block w-[2px]" />
        </span>
        <span aria-hidden className="col-start-1 row-start-1 text-text-primary">
          {text.slice(0, shown)}
          <span
            data-idle={done ? "true" : "false"}
            data-typewriter-caret=""
            className="ms-px inline-block h-[1em] w-[2px] rounded-full bg-accent-500 align-[-0.14em]"
          />
        </span>
        <span className="sr-only">{text}</span>
      </span>
    </div>
  );
}

/** Copies the whole command; the icon swaps to a check for 1.6s. */
function CopyCommandButton({ text }: { text: string }) {
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<"idle" | "copied" | "failed">("idle");
  const timer = useRef<number | undefined>(undefined);

  useEffect(() => () => window.clearTimeout(timer.current), []);

  const copy = async () => {
    window.clearTimeout(timer.current);
    try {
      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
      setStatus("copied");
    } catch {
      setStatus("failed");
    }
    timer.current = window.setTimeout(() => setStatus("idle"), COPIED_MS);
  };

  const copied = status === "copied";
  return (
    <>
      <button
        type="button"
        onClick={copy}
        aria-label={copied ? "Copied" : "Copy command"}
        className={cx(
          "relative -my-1 flex size-8 shrink-0 cursor-pointer items-center justify-center rounded-lg text-foreground-icon-secondary",
          "transition-colors duration-150 ease-out hover:bg-background-secondary-default hover:text-foreground-icon-primary",
          "outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
          "active:bg-background-secondary-hover",
        )}
      >
        <RiFileCopyLine
          aria-hidden
          className={cx(
            "absolute size-4 transition-[opacity,scale] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
            copied ? "scale-50 opacity-0" : "scale-100 opacity-100",
          )}
        />
        <RiCheckLine
          aria-hidden
          className={cx(
            "absolute size-4 text-state-success-text transition-[opacity,scale] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
            copied ? "scale-100 opacity-100" : "scale-50 opacity-0",
          )}
        />
      </button>
      <span role="status" className="sr-only">
        {status === "copied" ? "Copied to clipboard" : status === "failed" ? "Copy failed, select the command instead" : ""}
      </span>
    </>
  );
}

export function TypewriterInstall({
  packageName = "motion",
  commands,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onChange,
  speed = 42,
  startDelay = 320,
  prompt = "$",
  label = "Package manager",
  className,
}: TypewriterInstallProps) {
  const list = commands ?? installCommands(packageName);
  const [inner, setInner] = useState(defaultValue ?? list[0]?.id ?? "");
  const selected = value ?? inner;
  const current = list.find((c) => c.id === selected) ?? list[0];

  const select = (key: Key) => {
    const id = String(key);
    setInner(id);
    onChange?.(id);
  };

  return (
    <Tabs
      selectedKey={current?.id}
      onSelectionChange={select}
      className={cx(
        "w-full max-w-[560px] overflow-hidden rounded-2xl border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default shadow-card",
        className,
      )}
    >
      <style href="kinetic-typewriter-install" precedence="medium">
        {CARET_CSS}
      </style>
      <div className="flex items-center border-b border-border-button-default px-2 py-1.5">
        <TabList aria-label={label} className="flex items-center gap-0.5">
          {list.map((c) => (
            <Tab
              key={c.id}
              id={c.id}
              className={cx(
                "cursor-pointer rounded-md px-2.5 py-1 font-mono text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary outline-none",
                "transition-colors duration-150 ease-out hover:text-text-primary",
                "data-selected:bg-background-secondary-default data-selected:text-text-primary",
                "data-focus-visible:ring-2 data-focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring",
              )}
            >
              {c.label}
            </Tab>
          ))}
        </TabList>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3 px-4 py-3.5">
        {list.map((c) => (
          <TabPanel key={c.id} id={c.id} className="min-w-0 flex-1 rounded-sm outline-none data-focus-visible:ring-2 data-focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring">
            <TypedLine text={c.command} speed={speed} startDelay={startDelay} prompt={prompt} />
          </TabPanel>
        ))}
        {current && <CopyCommandButton text={current.command} />}
      </div>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The typing effect clears its pending timeout on unmount, tab change or prop change; the copy button clears its reset timeout on unmount and before each new copy.

**Reduced motion.** With prefers-reduced-motion the timer chain never starts and the full command renders on the first client render; the caret stays solid without blinking and the copy icon swap has no transition.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Copying the typed slice instead of the full command: a click halfway through would put half a command on the clipboard.
- Letting the typed text drive layout. Without the invisible full-width layer the card grows a line at a time on narrow screens as the text wraps.
- Pausing the caret blink with `animation-play-state: paused` — it can freeze on the invisible frame. Drop the animation while typing instead.
- Exposing the typing to screen readers. Each character change in a live tree is noise; hide the animated layer and give them the whole line once.

## Notes

- `commands` replaces the defaults for anything that is not a package install, e.g. a CLI `add` command.
- Clicking the already-selected tab does not retype; the panel only remounts when the selection changes.

## Definition of done

On load the pnpm tab is selected and "pnpm add @remixicon/react" types out in about a second, then the caret blinks. Clicking "npm" shows "npm install @remixicon/react" typing from the start and the caption reads "Package manager: npm". Clicking "Copy command" turns the icon into a check and the button name into "Copied". With reduced motion the full command shows immediately.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Typography

A docs specimen for the kit composite text utilities (`text-{family}-{weight}`). Each family gets a heading with its size, line height and tracking, a one-line usage note, and a bordered card with one row per weight: the sample sentence on the left, and the class name and weight on the right. The numbers are not typed into the component. They are read with `getComputedStyle` from the rendered rows, so the specimen always shows what the theme CSS resolves to. Clicking a class name copies it.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Type-scale specimen of the 13 kit text families in four weights, with size and line height read from the live CSS and copyable class names.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. `TYPE_SCALE` lists the 13 families from Large Title to Caption 2. Each has its four class names written out in full (`text-body-medium`, not `text-body-${w}`), because Tailwind only emits utilities it finds as literal strings in the source.
2. `TypeFamilySection` renders one `<li>` per requested weight. The sample `<p>` gets the composite class and a callback ref stored in `sampleRefs[i]`.
3. After mount, and again whenever the family or the weight list changes, an effect runs `readTypeMetrics` on every sample element. It turns `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing` and `fontWeight` into numbers and stores them in state. A window `resize` listener re-reads them, because zoom and responsive root sizes arrive that way.
4. `formatFamilyMetrics` builds the header string from the measured rows, for example `18px / 24–26px` for Title 3. It shows a range when the weights have different line heights, and adds `· tracking 0.15px` when letter spacing is not zero. Each row shows its own measured weight number next to the weight name.
5. `TokenCopy` is a mono button holding the class name. It copies through `useCopyToClipboard` and shows a lime check for 1.4s. `Typography` stacks one section per family id with a 40px gap.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `families = 13 × 4 weights = 52 utilities`
  This mirrors the `@theme` block in boardui-theme.css. A family missing from `TYPE_SCALE` would never be emitted, because its class names would appear nowhere in the source.
- `row = px-4 py-4, 1px border-button-default between rows, rounded-2xl card`
  This matches the reference card. The divider and corner radius are the same ones the code block and install box use.
- `metric header = font-mono caption-1, text-tertiary`
  Measured numbers read as data next to the title-2 family name, the same as the reference "64px / 80px".
- `copy reset = 1400 ms`
  The check only needs to confirm the click, and many class names get copied in a row.

## API

```ts
type TypeWeight = "regular" | "medium" | "semibold" | "bold";
function Typography(props: { families?: readonly string[]; weights?: readonly TypeWeight[]; sample?: string; headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4; className?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement> }): JSX.Element
function TypeFamilySection(props: { family: TypeFamily; weights?: readonly TypeWeight[]; sample?: string; headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function readTypeMetrics(element: Element): { fontSize: number; lineHeight: number; letterSpacing: number; fontWeight: number }
const TYPE_SCALE: readonly TypeFamily[]
```

- `families: readonly string[]` — default `all 13`
  Family ids to show (`large-title`, `display-1` … `caption-2`), kept in scale order.
- `weights: readonly TypeWeight[]` — default `["regular", "medium", "semibold", "bold"]`
  Weights shown in each family card.
- `sample: string` — default `"The five boxing wizards jump quickly."`
  Sentence rendered in every row.
- `headingLevel: 2 | 3 | 4` — default `3`
  Heading level of each family name.
- `className: string`
  Extra classes on the outer stack.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Metrics come from getComputedStyle on the rendered sample, not from a
// table in this file, so the specimen always shows what the theme CSS
// really resolves to (including a rem change or an overridden token).
useEffect(() => {
  const read = () =>
    setMetrics(
      weightKey.split(",").map((_, i) => {
        const el = sampleRefs.current[i];
        return el ? readTypeMetrics(el) : null;
      }),
    );
  read();
  // Page zoom and responsive root sizes arrive as a resize; re-read then.
  window.addEventListener("resize", read);
  return () => window.removeEventListener("resize", read);
}, [family.id, weightKey]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Each family section adds one window `resize` listener in its effect and removes it on unmount or before the next run. The copy reset timer in `useCopyToClipboard` is cleared on unmount.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing moves. Only the copy button hover colour transitions, and it has `motion-reduce:transition-none`.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Building class names with template strings (`text-${family}-${weight}`). Tailwind never sees them, the utilities are not generated, and every row renders in the inherited body size.
- Measuring in render or during SSR. `getComputedStyle` only exists after layout. Measuring in an effect means the server and the first client render both show a placeholder, so hydration still matches.
- Trusting a hard-coded metrics table. Title 3 uses a 24px line height for regular and 26px for heavier weights, and a table drifts as soon as a token changes. Reading the CSS keeps the specimen correct.

## Notes

- `readTypeMetrics` and `formatFamilyMetrics` are exported for other token docs, for example a size badge next to a heading in a design review.
- Pass `families={["body", "body-2"]}` and `weights={["regular", "medium"]}` to show a focused subset in a component page.

## Definition of done

Rendering `<Typography families={["title-3"]} />` shows a "Title 3" heading followed by `18px / 24–26px`, and four rows whose samples are visibly 18px regular, medium, semibold and bold. The rows are labelled `text-title-3-regular` … `text-title-3-bold` with "Regular · 400" … "Bold · 700". Caption 1 shows `12px / 16px · tracking 0.15px`. Clicking a class name puts that exact string on the clipboard and shows a check. Changing `sample` updates every row, and switching families re-measures the header.

# Build: Users Access Card

The "Users with access" panel of a workspace settings page. Each member row shows a tinted initials avatar, name, email and a compact role select, with a round × button to remove them; the owner row is locked and shows its role as text. An invite form at the bottom checks the email (empty, malformed, already a member), derives a name from the address and appends an "Invited" row with the chosen role. Every change is announced through a polite live region.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Workspace members with initials, email and a role select per row, a remove button, and an invite field that validates before adding a row.

- Category: form
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. Hold the list controlled-or-uncontrolled: local state seeds from `defaultUsers`, `users` wins when passed, and every change goes through `commit(next)` which sets local state and calls `onUsersChange(next)`.
2. Render each member as an `li` with the kit `Avatar` (initials from the first letters of the first two words, `aria-hidden`), name plus optional `Badge` "Invited", the email, then either the role as text (`locked`) or a kit `Select` (`aria-label` "Role for <name>") and a kit `CloseButton` (24px) "Remove <name>".
3. On invite submit, `preventDefault`, trim and lowercase the draft, and test in order: empty, the `EMAIL` regex, and duplicates (case-insensitive). A failure sets the kit `Input`'s `isInvalid` + `errorMessage` and refocuses the field; typing clears the error.
4. A valid address becomes a row: `nameFromEmail` splits the local part on `.`, `_` and `-` (dropping a `+tag`) and title-cases it, the colour cycles blue, lime, pink, neutral by list length, `invited: true` adds the badge, and the draft is cleared.
5. Removing stores the next non-locked neighbour (after, then before) in a ref; an effect keyed on the list focuses that row's remove button, or the invite field when none is left, so keyboard users never lose focus to `<body>`.
6. New rows fade and slide 4px down into place with a CSS `@starting-style` transition (`starting:opacity-0 starting:-translate-y-1`, 200ms ease-out), off under `motion-reduce`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `EMAIL = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]{2,}$/`
  Catches the common typos (missing @, missing TLD, spaces) without rejecting real addresses the way a strict RFC pattern would.
- `role select width = 104px`
  Fits the longest default label ("Editor"/"Viewer") plus the chevron; locked rows span 140px (select + 12px gap + 24px close button) with 8px start padding so "Owner" lines up with the select labels.
- `row entry = 200ms, translate-y -4px → 0, opacity 0 → 1`
  Long enough to show where the invited row landed, short enough not to delay a second invite.
- `invite row breakpoint = @sm container query`
  Below ~384px card width the field takes its own line and the role select and Invite button share the next one.

```ts

type AccessUser = { id: string; name: string; email: string; role: string; initials?: string; color?: "neutral" | "blue" | "lime" | "pink"; locked?: boolean; invited?: boolean }
```

  Controlled member list.
- `defaultUsers: AccessUser[]` — default `[]`
  Initial members when uncontrolled.

  Called with the new list after a role change, removal or invite.

  Options of every role select ({ id, label }).
- `defaultInviteRole: string` — default `roles[1].id`
  Role preselected in the invite form.

  Card heading and the list's accessible name.

  Merged onto the card.

## Reference implementation of the core

the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function UsersAccessCard({
  users,
  defaultUsers = [],
  onUsersChange,
  roles = DEFAULT_ACCESS_ROLES,
  defaultInviteRole,
  title = "Users with access",
  invitePlaceholder = "Invite by email",
  inviteLabel = "Invite",
  className,
}: UsersAccessCardProps) {
  const [own, setOwn] = useState(defaultUsers);
  const list = users ?? own;
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("");
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [inviteRole, setInviteRole] = useState(defaultInviteRole ?? roles[1]?.id ?? roles[0]?.id ?? "");
  const [announcement, setAnnouncement] = useState("");

  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const removeRefs = useRef(new Map<string, HTMLButtonElement>());
  // After a removal, focus lands on the next row's remove button (or the
  // invite field) once the new list has rendered.
  const pendingFocus = useRef<string | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const id = pendingFocus.current;
    if (id === null) return;
    pendingFocus.current = null;
    (removeRefs.current.get(id) ?? inputRef.current)?.focus();
  }, [list]);

  const commit = (next: AccessUser[]) => {
    setOwn(next);
    onUsersChange?.(next);
  };
  const roleLabel = (id: string) => roles.find((r) => r.id === id)?.label ?? id;

  const invite = (e: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const email = draft.trim().toLowerCase();
    let problem: string | null = null;
    if (!email) problem = "Enter an email address.";
    else if (!EMAIL.test(email)) problem = "Enter a valid email, like name@company.com.";
    else if (list.some((u) => u.email.toLowerCase() === email)) problem = `${email} already has access.`;
    if (problem) {
      setError(problem);
      inputRef.current?.focus();
      return;
    }
    const name = nameFromEmail(email);
    commit([
      ...list,
      {
        id: `invite:${email}`,
        name,
        email,
        role: inviteRole,
        color: COLORS[list.length % COLORS.length],
        invited: true,
      },
    ]);
    setDraft("");
    setAnnouncement(`Invited ${name} as ${roleLabel(inviteRole)}.`);
  };

  const remove = (id: string) => {
    const i = list.findIndex((u) => u.id === id);
    const gone = list[i];
    if (!gone) return;
    const next = list.filter((u) => u.id !== id);
    const neighbour = [...next.slice(i), ...next.slice(0, i).reverse()].find((u) => !u.locked);
    pendingFocus.current = neighbour?.id ?? "";
    commit(next);
    setAnnouncement(`Removed ${gone.name}.`);
  };

  const setRole = (id: string, role: string) => {
    commit(list.map((u) => (u.id === id ? { ...u, role } : u)));
    const who = list.find((u) => u.id === id);
    if (who) setAnnouncement(`${who.name} is now ${roleLabel(role)}.`);
  };

  return (
    <section
      className={cx(
        "@container flex w-full min-w-0 flex-col rounded-2xl border border-border-button-default bg-background-primary-default p-1.5 shadow-xs",
        className,
      )}
    >
      <header className="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3 px-2.5 pt-1.5 pb-1">
        <h3 className="text-body-medium text-text-secondary">{title}</h3>
        <span className="text-caption-1-medium text-text-tertiary tabular-nums">
          {list.length} {list.length === 1 ? "person" : "people"}
        </span>
      </header>

      <ul aria-label={title} className="flex flex-col">
        {list.map((u) => (
          <li
            key={u.id}
            className="flex items-center gap-3 rounded-2lg px-2.5 py-2 transition-[opacity,translate] duration-200 ease-out starting:-translate-y-1 starting:opacity-0 motion-reduce:transition-none"
          >
            <Avatar size="md" color={u.color ?? "neutral"} initials={u.initials ?? initialsOf(u.name)} aria-hidden />
            <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col">
              <span className="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-1.5">
                <span className="truncate text-body-medium text-text-primary">{u.name}</span>
                {u.invited ? <Badge className="shrink-0">Invited</Badge> : null}
              </span>
              <span className="truncate text-caption-1-medium text-text-tertiary">{u.email}</span>
            </div>
            {u.locked ? (
              <span className="w-[140px] shrink-0 ps-2 text-body-2-medium text-text-secondary">
                {roleLabel(u.role)}
              </span>
            ) : (
              <>
                <Select
                  aria-label={`Role for ${u.name}`}
                  size="sm"
                  value={u.role}
                  onChange={(k) => k != null && setRole(u.id, String(k))}
                  className="w-[104px] shrink-0"
                  popoverClassName="w-40"
                >
                  {roles.map((r) => (
                    <SelectItem key={r.id} id={r.id} textValue={r.label}>
                      {r.label}
                    </SelectItem>
                  ))}
                </Select>
                <CloseButton
                  ref={(el) => {
                    if (el) removeRefs.current.set(u.id, el);
                    else removeRefs.current.delete(u.id);
                  }}
                  size="sm"
                  aria-label={`Remove ${u.name}`}
                  onClick={() => remove(u.id)}
                />
              </>
            )}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>

      <form
        noValidate
        onSubmit={invite}
        className="mt-1 grid grid-cols-[1fr_auto] items-start gap-2 border-t border-border-button-default px-2.5 pt-3 pb-2 @sm:grid-cols-[1fr_auto_auto]"
      >
        <Input
          ref={inputRef}
          aria-label="Invite by email"
          type="email"
          size="small"
          leadingIcon={RiMailLine}
          placeholder={invitePlaceholder}
          value={draft}
          onChange={(v) => {
            setDraft(v);
            setError(null);
          }}
          isInvalid={error !== null}
          errorMessage={error}
          validationBehavior="aria"
          className="col-span-2 min-w-0 @sm:col-span-1"
        />
        <Select
          aria-label="Role for new member"
          size="sm"
          value={inviteRole}
          onChange={(k) => k != null && setInviteRole(String(k))}
          className="w-[104px] @sm:mt-px"
          popoverClassName="w-40"
        >
          {roles.map((r) => (
            <SelectItem key={r.id} id={r.id} textValue={r.label}>
              {r.label}
            </SelectItem>
          ))}
        </Select>
        <Button type="submit" variant="primary" size="small" className="justify-self-end">
          {inviteLabel}
        </Button>
      </form>

      <p className="sr-only" aria-live="polite">
        {announcement}
      </p>
    </section>
  );

```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up: no timers, listeners or observers. The remove-button ref map deletes an entry when its button unmounts.

**Reduced motion.** Rows carry `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so an invited row appears in place without the fade and slide; the kit Select popover follows its own reduced-motion rule.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Letting focus fall to <body> after removing a row: the button that had focus is gone, so focus must move to a neighbour explicitly after the re-render.
- Using native constraint validation on the email input: the browser bubble ignores the kit styling and fires before the duplicate check. Use `noValidate` and `validationBehavior="aria"` and show your own message.
- Comparing emails case-sensitively, which lets "Jon.Park@" and "jon.park@" both in.

## Notes

- `locked` accepts any role label (e.g. "Owner") that is not in `roles`; it is shown as text.
- The demo is controlled and counts admins under the card, so a role change updates the caption.

## Definition of done

The card lists 4 people with Ava Lindqvist as a locked Owner. Submitting an empty invite shows "Enter an email address."; "bad@x" shows the valid-email message; "jon.park@example.com" says it already has access. Inviting "dana.kim@example.com" appends "Dana Kim" with an Invited badge and the count becomes 5 people. Clicking "Remove Jon Park" drops the row and moves focus to the next remove button; changing a role through its select updates the admin count under the card.
