# Build: Vitals Chart Card

One vital sign over a short period, drawn like the medical profile's steps card: a column per reading, each a full-height grey track filled from the bottom. A dashed band marks the normal range, readings outside it turn pink, and an inner tile under the chart spells the range out next to an in-range count. Hovering, focusing or selecting a column swaps the headline for that reading; a "range" variant floats each bar from a low to a high value for blood pressure.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A weekly vital-sign card: track-and-fill columns, a dashed normal-range band, pink out-of-range bars and a period stepper.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @remixicon/react@^4.9.0

## How it works

1. The value axis is `domain` or, when omitted, the min and max of every value, low and normal-range bound padded by 25% of the spread. `pct(v)` maps a value into 0-100% of the plot height and clamps it.
2. Each reading is a `<button>` track (`bg-chart-track`, 10px radius) in a CSS grid of `repeat(n, minmax(0, 1fr))` columns, positioned `absolute inset-0` inside the flex-1 plot box. Its fill is an absolutely positioned span with `bottom` 0 (bars) or `pct(low)` (range) and `height` `pct(value) - bottom`, so a new period animates through a 500ms CSS transition of `height` and `bottom`.
3. `vitalStatus` compares `value` with `normalRange` (and, when `value` is normal, `low` with `lowNormalRange`) and returns low, normal or high. Normal fills use the `color` prop's chart token, anything else uses `bg-chart-3`, and the dashed `bg-chart-7/10` band (one per range) is laid over the tracks with the same `pct` mapping.
4. The active column is the hovered one, else the selected one. Clicking toggles selection (controlled `selectedIndex` or uncontrolled `defaultSelectedIndex`), other fills dim to 40%, and the headline re-keys so the kit `animate-number-fade` replays with that day's value, detail label and a Normal, High or Low chip.
5. Columns use a roving tabindex: Arrow keys, Home and End move focus and preview the reading (a focus that matches `:focus-visible` previews, a mouse focus does not), Enter or Space toggles it, and Escape clears the selection.
6. With no active column the headline shows the `summary` (average, latest, max or min; range readings print as value/low) and the chip reads "n/total in range", lime when every reading is normal and orange otherwise. The optional `period` prop renders a bordered stepper whose arrows call `onPrevious` and `onNext`.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `card min height = 330px`
  Matches the medical profile row of cards, so it lines up with Patient Info Card.
- `domain padding = 25% of the data spread`
  Keeps the tallest bar and the normal band clear of the top and bottom of the track.
- `fill transition = 500ms ease-out`
  Long enough to read the change when stepping periods, short enough not to delay hovering.
- `dimmed fill opacity = 40%`
  Keeps the other readings visible while the active one is read.
- `track radius = 10px`
  The rounded column shape of the steps chart.

## API

```ts
export function VitalsChartCard({ title, unit, icon, readings, normalRange, lowNormalRange, domain, variant = "bars", color = "teal", summary = "average", decimals = 0, period, selectedIndex, defaultSelectedIndex = null, onSelectedIndexChange, className }: VitalsChartCardProps): JSX.Element
```

- `title: string`
  Card label, e.g. "Heart rate".
- `unit: string`
  Unit printed after the headline and in the range hint.
- `icon: ComponentType`
  Optional icon before the title.
- `readings: VitalReading[]`
  One column per reading: label, optional detail, value and optional low.
- `normalRange: readonly [number, number]`
  Inclusive normal range for value; drawn as the dashed band.
- `lowNormalRange: readonly [number, number]`
  Inclusive normal range for low in the range variant; draws a second band.
- `domain: readonly [number, number]`
  Value axis floor and ceiling; derived from the data when omitted.
- `variant: "bars" | "range"` — default `"bars"`
  Fill from the floor, or float from low to value.
- `color: "teal" | "lime" | "sky" | "purple" | "blue" | "emerald" | "indigo"` — default `"teal"`
  Chart token for in-range fills.
- `summary: "average" | "latest" | "max" | "min"` — default `"average"`
  Headline when no column is active.
- `decimals: number` — default `0`
  Fraction digits for printed values.
- `period: VitalsPeriod`
  Label plus onPrevious/onNext and disabled flags for the header stepper.
- `selectedIndex: number | null`
  Controlled selected column.
- `defaultSelectedIndex: number | null` — default `null`
  Initial selected column when uncontrolled.
- `onSelectedIndexChange: (index: number | null) => void`
  Called when a column is selected or cleared.
- `className: string`
  Classes on the card.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function VitalsChartCard({
  title,
  unit,
  icon: Icon,
  readings,
  normalRange,
  lowNormalRange,
  domain,
  variant = "bars",
  color = "teal",
  summary = "average",
  decimals = 0,
  period,
  selectedIndex,
  defaultSelectedIndex = null,
  onSelectedIndexChange,
  className,
}: VitalsChartCardProps) {
  const [innerSelected, setInnerSelected] = useState<number | null>(defaultSelectedIndex);
  const [hoverIndex, setHoverIndex] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const [focusIndex, setFocusIndex] = useState(Math.max(0, readings.length - 1));
  const barRefs = useRef<(HTMLButtonElement | null)[]>([]);

  const isRange = variant === "range";
  const selectedRaw = selectedIndex !== undefined ? selectedIndex : innerSelected;
  const selected = selectedRaw !== null && selectedRaw < readings.length ? selectedRaw : null;
  const hovered = hoverIndex !== null && hoverIndex < readings.length ? hoverIndex : null;
  const activeIndex = hovered ?? selected;
  const active = activeIndex !== null ? readings[activeIndex] : undefined;
  const rovingIndex = Math.min(focusIndex, Math.max(0, readings.length - 1));

  const select = (index: number | null) => {
    if (selectedIndex === undefined) setInnerSelected(index);
    onSelectedIndexChange?.(index);
  };

  const [d0, d1] = domain ?? autoDomain(readings, normalRange, lowNormalRange);
  const span = d1 - d0 || 1;
  const pct = (v: number) => clampPct(((v - d0) / span) * 100);

  const fmt = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
    minimumFractionDigits: decimals,
    maximumFractionDigits: decimals,
  });
  const print = (r: Pick<VitalReading, "value" | "low">) =>
    isRange && r.low !== undefined ? `${fmt.format(r.value)}/${fmt.format(r.low)}` : fmt.format(r.value);

  // Headline when nothing is active: the summary of the whole period.
  let summaryReading: Pick<VitalReading, "value" | "low"> | undefined;
  if (readings.length > 0) {
    if (summary === "latest") summaryReading = readings[readings.length - 1];
    else if (summary === "max") summaryReading = readings.reduce((a, b) => (b.value > a.value ? b : a));
    else if (summary === "min") summaryReading = readings.reduce((a, b) => (b.value < a.value ? b : a));
    else {
      const mean = (xs: number[]) => xs.reduce((s, x) => s + x, 0) / xs.length;
      const lows = readings.flatMap((r) => (r.low === undefined ? [] : [r.low]));
      summaryReading = {
        value: mean(readings.map((r) => r.value)),
        low: lows.length > 0 ? mean(lows) : undefined,
      };
    }
  }

  const statuses = readings.map((r) => vitalStatus(r, normalRange, lowNormalRange));
  const inRange = statuses.filter((s) => s === "normal").length;
  const activeStatus = activeIndex !== null ? statuses[activeIndex] : undefined;
  const chip = activeStatus
    ? STATUS_CHIP[activeStatus]
    : {
        label: `${inRange}/${readings.length} in range`,
        color: inRange === readings.length ? ("lime" as const) : ("orange" as const),
      };

  const headline = active ?? summaryReading;
  const caption = active
    ? (active.detail ?? active.label)
    : `${SUMMARY_LABEL[summary]}${period ? ` · ${period.label}` : ""}`;

  const rangeText = (r: readonly [number, number]) => `${fmt.format(r[0])}–${fmt.format(r[1])}`;
  const normalText =
    isRange && lowNormalRange
      ? `${rangeText(normalRange)}/${rangeText(lowNormalRange)}`
      : `${rangeText(normalRange)} ${unit}`;

  const bands = [normalRange, ...(isRange && lowNormalRange ? [lowNormalRange] : [])];

  const moveFocus = (index: number) => {
    const next = (index + readings.length) % readings.length;
    setFocusIndex(next);
    setHoverIndex(next);
    barRefs.current[next]?.focus();
  };

  const onBarKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLButtonElement>, index: number) => {
    if (event.key === "ArrowRight" || event.key === "ArrowUp") moveFocus(index + 1);
    else if (event.key === "ArrowLeft" || event.key === "ArrowDown") moveFocus(index - 1);
    else if (event.key === "Home") moveFocus(0);
    else if (event.key === "End") moveFocus(readings.length - 1);
    else if (event.key === "Escape" && selected !== null) select(null);
    else return;
    event.preventDefault();
  };

  return (
    <section
      aria-label={title}
      className={cx(
        "flex min-h-[330px] w-full min-w-0 flex-col gap-4 rounded-[20px] bg-background-secondary-default px-4 pt-4 pb-3",
        className,
      )}
    >
      {/* Header: label, headline figure + unit, caption; period stepper on the right */}
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-start justify-between gap-x-3 gap-y-2">
        <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-[1_1_9rem] flex-col gap-0.5">
          <p className="flex items-center gap-1.5 text-body-medium text-text-secondary">
            {Icon ? <Icon className="size-4 shrink-0" aria-hidden /> : null}
            <span className="truncate">{title}</span>
          </p>
          <p className="flex items-baseline gap-1.5">
            <span
              key={activeIndex ?? "summary"}
              className="animate-number-fade text-title-1-medium whitespace-nowrap text-text-primary tabular-nums motion-reduce:animate-none"
              data-vital-value=""
            >
              {headline ? print(headline) : "–"}
            </span>
            <span className="text-body-2-medium text-text-secondary">{unit}</span>
          </p>
          <p className="truncate text-caption-1-medium text-text-tertiary" data-vital-caption="">
            {caption}
          </p>
        </div>
        {period ? <PeriodStepper period={period} title={title} /> : null}
      </div>

      {/* Plot: one track per reading, fills from the floor (bars) or floats low → value (range) */}
      <div className="flex min-h-[140px] flex-1 flex-col gap-2">
        <div className="relative min-h-0 flex-1">
          <div
            role="group"
            aria-label={`${title} readings`}
            className="absolute inset-0 grid gap-2"
            style={{ gridTemplateColumns: `repeat(${Math.max(1, readings.length)}, minmax(0, 1fr))` }}
            onPointerLeave={() => setHoverIndex(null)}
          >
            {readings.map((reading, index) => {
              const status = statuses[index] ?? "normal";
              const bottom = isRange && reading.low !== undefined ? pct(reading.low) : 0;
              const height = Math.max(pct(reading.value) - bottom, 0);
              const isSelected = selected === index;
              const dimmed = activeIndex !== null && activeIndex !== index;
              return (
                <button
                  key={`${reading.label}-${index}`}
                  ref={(node) => {
                    barRefs.current[index] = node;
                  }}
                  type="button"
                  tabIndex={index === rovingIndex ? 0 : -1}
                  aria-pressed={isSelected}
                  aria-label={`${reading.detail ?? reading.label}: ${print(reading)} ${unit}, ${STATUS_CHIP[status].label.toLowerCase()}`}
                  className={cx(
                    "relative h-full min-w-0 cursor-pointer overflow-hidden rounded-[10px] bg-chart-track outline-none",
                    "focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-background-secondary-default",
                    isSelected && "ring-2 ring-text-primary ring-offset-2 ring-offset-background-secondary-default",
                  )}
                  onPointerEnter={() => setHoverIndex(index)}
                  onFocus={(event) => {
                    setFocusIndex(index);
                    if (event.currentTarget.matches(":focus-visible")) setHoverIndex(index);
                  }}
                  onBlur={() => setHoverIndex((current) => (current === index ? null : current))}
                  onKeyDown={(event) => onBarKeyDown(event, index)}
                  onClick={() => select(isSelected ? null : index)}
                >
                  <span
                    aria-hidden
                    data-status={status}
                    className={cx(
                      "absolute inset-x-0 min-h-1.5 rounded-[10px] transition-[height,bottom,opacity] duration-500 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
                      status === "normal" ? FILL[color] : OUT_OF_RANGE_FILL,
                      dimmed && "opacity-40",
                    )}
                    style={{ bottom: `${bottom}%`, height: `${height}%` }}
                  />
                </button>
              );
            })}
          </div>
          {bands.map((band, i) => (
            <div
              key={i}
              aria-hidden
              className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-x-0 border-y border-dashed border-chart-7-active bg-chart-7/10"
              style={{ bottom: `${pct(band[0])}%`, height: `${Math.max(pct(band[1]) - pct(band[0]), 0)}%` }}
            />
          ))}
        </div>
        <div
          aria-hidden
          className="grid gap-2"
          style={{ gridTemplateColumns: `repeat(${Math.max(1, readings.length)}, minmax(0, 1fr))` }}
        >
          {readings.map((reading, index) => (
            <span
              key={`${reading.label}-${index}`}
              className={cx(
                "truncate text-center text-caption-1-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none",
                activeIndex === index ? "text-text-primary" : "text-text-tertiary",
              )}
            >
              {reading.label}
            </span>
          ))}
        </div>
      </div>

      {/* Normal-range hint */}
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 rounded-2lg bg-background-inner-default px-2.5 py-2">
        <div className="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-1.5">
          <span
            aria-hidden
            className="h-2.5 w-3.5 shrink-0 rounded-[3px] border border-dashed border-chart-7-active bg-chart-7/15"
          />
          <span className="text-body-regular whitespace-nowrap text-text-secondary">Normal</span>
          <span className="truncate text-body-medium text-text-primary tabular-nums">{normalText}</span>
        </div>
        <Chip variant="caption" color={chip.color} className="shrink-0" data-vital-status="">
          {chip.label}
        </Chip>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** No timers, listeners or observers; hover state lives in React state and the column refs are plain arrays.

**Reduced motion.** The fill height transition, the label colour fade and the headline fade are removed with motion-reduce:transition-none and motion-reduce:animate-none; values change instantly.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Do not use pink (`chart-3`) as the card colour: it is reserved for out-of-range readings, so the `color` prop excludes it.
- Do not let a mouse focus preview the column; only keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`) should, or the headline sticks after the pointer leaves.
- Do not size the column grid with h-full inside a flex-1 box whose parent only has a min-height: the percentage resolves to auto and the tracks collapse to zero. Position the grid absolute inset-0 inside the relative plot box instead.

## Notes

- Values print with `Intl.NumberFormat("en-US")` and `decimals` fraction digits; range readings print as "118/76", and the range variant's hint drops the unit ("90–120/60–80") so it fits a third-width card.
- The period stepper is display-only: the parent owns which readings are shown and passes new `readings` plus the period label.

## Definition of done

Clicking a column sets aria-pressed and shows that day's value, detail and status chip in the header; Escape clears it; the previous-period arrow swaps the readings and the label, and readings outside normalRange render with the pink fill.

and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Web Audio Scheduling Kit

Two clocks, one job each. `AudioContext.currentTime` is a sample counter and never drifts, but it cannot wake you up; `setInterval` can wake you up, but only when the main thread is free. The scheduler runs a 90 ms timer whose only responsibility is to ask which beats fall inside the next 300 ms and hand each one an exact audio time. The timer can fire late, early, or twice in a row and the notes still land in the same place.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A lookahead sequencer: a coarse timer queues beats onto the sample-accurate audio clock, so tempo never drifts.

- Category: primitive
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. `nextTime` holds the audio-clock time of the next unqueued beat, initialised to `ctx.currentTime + START_LEAD` when `start()` runs. Every timer tick loops `while (nextTime < ctx.currentTime + lookahead)`, calls `onBeat({ time: nextTime, beat, step, ctx })`, and advances `nextTime += 60 / bpm`.
2. The advance accumulates from the previous beat time, never from `ctx.currentTime`. Re-basing on the clock each pass folds the timer's jitter into the tempo, and a sequence that re-bases runs measurably sharp inside a minute.
3. It is a `while` and not an `if` because one tick may have to cover several beats — the timer was throttled, the tempo is faster than the interval, or the tab just came back to the foreground.
4. `scheduleTone` builds an oscillator and a gain node per beat, ramps `gain` from its peak to 0.001 over `decay`, stops the oscillator `TAIL` seconds after the ramp ends, and disconnects both nodes in `onended` so the graph does not accumulate dead nodes.
5. The visual step index comes from a second, independent pass: a rAF loop reads `ctx.currentTime` once per frame and pops every queued beat whose time has passed, so the highlighted step is the step you can hear rather than the step that was most recently queued 300 ms ago.
6. `phase` is derived in the same loop as `1 - (nextQueuedBeat.time - now) / secondsPerBeat`, clamped to 0-1, and written to a ref rather than to state — a playhead needs a value every frame and state would re-render the whole sequencer 60 times a second.
7. On `visibilitychange` to hidden the lookahead widens to 1.5s, because a hidden tab clamps `setInterval` to roughly one call per second and a 0.3s window would leave gaps of missed beats.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `intervalMs = 90`
  How often the scheduler wakes. It only has to beat the lookahead window, not the tempo — at 96 bpm a beat is 625 ms, so the timer gets about seven chances to queue each one. Dropping to ~10 ms burns main-thread time for nothing; going past ~250 ms leaves too few chances inside a 300 ms window.
- `lookahead = 0.3`
  Seconds queued in advance. Must exceed the worst-case gap between timer calls, which under main-thread contention is several times `intervalMs` — 0.3s over a 0.09s interval is a 3x margin. Larger windows make a tempo or pattern change take longer to take effect, because beats already queued cannot be un-queued.
- `HIDDEN_LOOKAHEAD = 1.5`
  Seconds queued while the tab is hidden. Chrome and Firefox clamp background timers to about one call per second, so the window has to be over 1s or the sequence develops audible holes; 1.5s leaves margin over the clamp.
- `START_LEAD = 0.08`
  Seconds before the first beat. Covers constructing the context, resuming it, and the first `drain()` — all of which happen inside the click handler. Scheduling the downbeat at exactly `currentTime` means its attack is already partly in the past.
- `SILENCE = 0.001`
  The ramp target, -60 dB. `exponentialRampToValueAtTime` is undefined at 0 and throws a RangeError; ramping to a literal 0 is the single most common Web Audio mistake.
- `TAIL = 0.05`
  Seconds between the end of the decay ramp and `osc.stop()`. Stopping exactly at the end of the ramp truncates the waveform mid-cycle, which is an audible click on a triangle or square wave.
- `gain default = 0.14`
  Peak per tone. Three simultaneous rows sum to 0.42, which leaves headroom for their overlapping tails; at 0.4 each the same chord clips the destination.

## API

```ts
function useWebAudioScheduler(options?: { bpm?: number; steps?: number; lookahead?: number; intervalMs?: number; onBeat?: (beat: { time: number; beat: number; step: number; ctx: AudioContext }) => void }): { start: () => void; stop: () => void; running: boolean; step: number | null; phase: RefObject<number> }
function scheduleTone(ctx: AudioContext, options: { frequency: number; at: number; gain?: number; decay?: number; type?: OscillatorType }): void
```

- `bpm: number` — default `96`
  Tempo. One beat is `60 / bpm` seconds on the audio clock.
- `steps: number` — default `8`
  Beats per bar. Only affects the wrapped `step` index handed to `onBeat`.
- `lookahead: number` — default `0.3`
  Seconds of beats queued in advance. Must exceed the worst-case timer gap.
- `intervalMs: number` — default `90`
  How often the scheduling timer runs. Independent of the tempo.
- `onBeat: (beat: ScheduledBeat) => void`
  Called once per beat, `lookahead` seconds early. Schedule audio against `beat.time`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** `exponentialRampToValueAtTime` is undefined at 0, so silence is -60 dB. */
const SILENCE = 0.001;
/** Seconds after the ramp before `stop()`, so the cut is inaudible. */
const TAIL = 0.05;
/** Seconds before the first beat, absorbing the cost of `start()` itself. */
const START_LEAD = 0.08;
/** Lookahead used while the tab is hidden, in seconds. */
const HIDDEN_LOOKAHEAD = 1.5;

interface QueuedBeat {
  time: number;
  step: number;
}

/**
 * One decaying tone, scheduled and self-disposing.
 *
 * The oscillator and its gain node disconnect themselves in `onended`. A
 * sequencer that omits that leaks two nodes per beat — at 120 bpm that is
 * 7200 dead nodes an hour, all still attached to the destination.
 */
export function scheduleTone(ctx: AudioContext, options: ToneOptions): void {
  const { frequency, at, gain = 0.14, decay = 0.28, type = 'triangle' } = options;

  const osc = ctx.createOscillator();
  const env = ctx.createGain();
  osc.type = type;
  osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(frequency, at);
  env.gain.setValueAtTime(gain, at);
  env.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(SILENCE, at + decay);
  osc.connect(env);
  env.connect(ctx.destination);
  osc.start(at);
  osc.stop(at + decay + TAIL);
  osc.onended = () => {
    osc.disconnect();
    env.disconnect();
  };
}

export function useWebAudioScheduler(
  options: UseWebAudioSchedulerOptions = {},
): WebAudioScheduler {
  const { bpm = 96, steps = 8, lookahead = 0.3, intervalMs = 90 } = options;
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();

  const [running, setRunning] = useState(false);
  const [step, setStep] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const phase = useRef(0);

  const ctxRef = useRef<AudioContext | null>(null);
  const timer = useRef<number | null>(null);
  const queue = useRef<QueuedBeat[]>([]);
  /** Audio time of the next beat to be scheduled. */
  const nextTime = useRef(0);
  /** Monotonic beat counter, so `step` survives a change of `steps`. */
  const counter = useRef(0);
  /** Widened while the tab is hidden, where timers are clamped to ~1 Hz. */
  const window_ = useRef(lookahead);

  const config = useRef({ bpm, steps, lookahead, intervalMs, reduced, options });
  config.current = { bpm, steps, lookahead, intervalMs, reduced, options };

  /** Queue every beat that falls inside the lookahead window. */
  const drain = useCallback(() => {
    const ctx = ctxRef.current;
    if (!ctx) return;
    const cfg = config.current;
    const secondsPerBeat = 60 / cfg.bpm;
    const horizon = ctx.currentTime + window_.current;

    // A `while`, not an `if`: one call may have to cover several beats when the
    // timer was throttled, and a fast tempo can put two beats in one window.
    while (nextTime.current < horizon) {
      const beat = counter.current;
      const at = nextTime.current;
      const index = wrapIndex(beat, cfg.steps);

      cfg.options.onBeat?.({ time: at, beat, step: index, ctx });
      queue.current.push({ time: at, step: index });

      // Accumulate from the previous beat time, never from `currentTime`.
      // Re-basing on the clock each pass folds the timer's jitter into the
      // tempo and the sequence drifts sharp within a minute.
      nextTime.current = at + secondsPerBeat;
      counter.current = beat + 1;
    }
  }, []);

  const stop = useCallback(() => {
    if (timer.current !== null) {
      clearInterval(timer.current);
      timer.current = null;
    }
    queue.current.length = 0;
    phase.current = 0;
    setRunning(false);
    setStep(null);
  }, []);

  const start = useCallback(() => {
    if (timer.current !== null) return;
    const cfg = config.current;

    let ctx = ctxRef.current;
    if (!ctx) {
      // Built inside the gesture handler that called `start`. Anywhere else
      // and the autoplay policy hands back a suspended context whose notes
      // are dropped silently.
      ctx = new AudioContext();
      ctxRef.current = ctx;
    }
    if (ctx.state === 'suspended') void ctx.resume();

    counter.current = 0;
    queue.current.length = 0;
    window_.current = document.visibilityState === 'hidden' ? HIDDEN_LOOKAHEAD : cfg.lookahead;
    nextTime.current = ctx.currentTime + START_LEAD;

    setRunning(true);
    drain();
    timer.current = window.setInterval(drain, cfg.intervalMs);
  }, [drain]);

  // The visual clock. Reading `ctx.currentTime` once per frame and popping the
  // beats that have passed keeps the highlight on the note you can hear; a
  // separate rAF counter of its own would slide out of step over a few bars.
  useRaf(() => {
    const ctx = ctxRef.current;
    if (!ctx) return;
    const now = ctx.currentTime;
    const q = queue.current;

    let current: QueuedBeat | null = null;
    while (q.length > 0) {
      const head = q[0];
      if (head === undefined || head.time > now) break;
      q.shift();
      current = head;
    }
    if (current) setStep(current.step);

    if (config.current.reduced) {
      phase.current = 0;
      return;
    }
    const secondsPerBeat = 60 / config.current.bpm;
    const head = q[0];
    // Time until the next queued beat, turned into progress through this one.
    phase.current =
      head === undefined ? 0 : clamp(1 - (head.time - now) / secondsPerBeat, 0, 1);
  }, running);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!running) return;
    // A hidden tab clamps `setInterval` to roughly one call per second, so a
    // 0.3s window drops entire bars. Widening the window instead of stopping
    // means the bar plays through unbroken while the tab is in the background.
    const onVisibility = () => {
      window_.current =
        document.visibilityState === 'hidden' ? HIDDEN_LOOKAHEAD : config.current.lookahead;
      drain();
    };
    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility);
    return () => document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility);
  }, [running, drain]);

  useEffect(
    () => () => {
      if (timer.current !== null) clearInterval(timer.current);
      timer.current = null;
      queue.current.length = 0;
      const ctx = ctxRef.current;
      ctxRef.current = null;
      // close() cancels every note already scheduled in the future. Without
      // it a bar keeps playing after the component has gone.
      if (ctx && ctx.state !== 'closed') void ctx.close();
    },
    [],
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The unmount cleanup clears the scheduling interval, empties the pending-beat queue, and calls `ctx.close()`, which cancels every note already committed to the audio thread. The `visibilitychange` listener is removed with its effect, and the rAF subscription is released by `useRaf` when `running` goes false. Each tone disconnects its own oscillator and gain node in `onended`.

**Reduced motion.** `step` still advances — a step index is information about the sound, not decoration — but `phase` is pinned to 0, so a playhead bound to it jumps from step to step in place of sliding continuously between them. The demo's playhead therefore renders as a static line on the current step.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Driving the sequence with one `setTimeout` per note. Every note then inherits main-thread jitter, and a single 80 ms layout pass puts that note 80 ms off the beat — clearly audible at any tempo.
- Advancing the beat time from `ctx.currentTime` instead of from the previous beat time. The timer never fires exactly on schedule, so each re-base rounds the interval down and the tempo creeps upward; a sequence started against a metronome is noticeably ahead within a minute.
- Using `if` instead of `while` in the drain. When the tab returns to the foreground, or the tempo is faster than the timer interval, one tick has several beats to queue — an `if` queues one and silently drops the rest.
- Setting the lookahead smaller than the worst-case timer gap. The window is the entire safety margin: at a 0.05s lookahead a single long frame means the beat is already in the past when the timer finally runs, and `osc.start(pastTime)` plays immediately, so the note is late *and* off-grid.
- Constructing the `AudioContext` at mount. The autoplay policy hands back a `suspended` context, `osc.start(at)` neither throws nor sounds, and the failure looks like a silent bug with a clean console.
- Ramping the gain to 0. `exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0, t)` throws — the target must be strictly positive.
- Leaving each beat's oscillator and gain connected. At 120 bpm that is two dead nodes a beat, 7200 an hour, all still attached to the destination; CPU climbs and the output eventually distorts.
- Counting the visual step with its own rAF counter rather than reading `ctx.currentTime`. The two clocks tick at different rates, so the highlight slides out of step with the sound over a few bars — the classic "my metronome light is not on the beat" bug.
- Highlighting the step at the moment it was *queued*. That is `lookahead` seconds before it sounds, so the playhead runs a third of a second ahead of the audio and looks broken.
- Publishing the beat phase as React state. Sixty re-renders a second of the whole sequencer to move one line; a ref plus a rAF write to a CSS custom property costs nothing.
- Never calling `ctx.close()`. Notes already queued keep playing after the component unmounts, and Chrome throws once about six contexts exist in one document.

## Notes

- A change to the pattern takes effect at most `lookahead` seconds later, because beats inside the window are already committed to the audio thread. That is inherent to lookahead scheduling, not a defect — shrink the window if you need a tighter response and accept the reduced timing margin.
- `onBeat` receives the context so the caller schedules its own nodes; the hook deliberately does not own the sound. Sequencing and synthesis are separate concerns and pairing them makes both untestable.
- For sub-millisecond scheduling with no main-thread involvement at all, the same shape moves into an `AudioWorklet` that posts beat messages. The lookahead pattern is identical; only the timer changes.

## Definition of done

Press Play: the highlight lands on a cell at the same instant you hear that cell, and stays in step after a minute of playing. Toggle a cell while it runs and the change is audible on the next pass. Switch to another tab for ten seconds and come back — the pattern is still on the grid with no gap or double-trigger. Press Stop and the step counter clears with no trailing note. Unmount while playing and nothing keeps sounding. With reduced motion on, the playhead line sits still on the current step instead of sweeping.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Web Search

Shows where an agent looked while it researched. Headings open a level and the searches under them land one row at a time on the Agent Log guide; a step with sources branches once more into a Sources row whose site marks overlap like a stack, each with its title and domain on hover. The row expands into a list of titles and domains, past six marks the rest collapse into a count, and per-step dwell makes slow searches hold longer than cached ones.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

The research half of an agent log: each query lands on a curved guide, and a step that found something branches into overlapping site marks.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: dom
- Dependencies: motion@^12.43.0, @remixicon/react@^4.9.0, react-aria-components@^1.22.1

## How it works

1. Steps flatten into reveal units: one per step plus one for its Sources row. useRevealTicker from agent-log counts them, paced by a delayFor callback: startDelay first, sourceBeat between a step and its Sources row, then that step's dwell (or stepInterval) before the next step.
2. A memoised tree groups plain steps under the heading before them, with each node's unit offset; a node renders once revealed passes its offset, and its Sources row once revealed passes offset + 1.
3. The step the trail is holding on is the one owning unit revealed - 1, and it shimmers through ShimmerText until the next unit lands.
4. Top-level rows mount as motion.li with the shared blur-and-height reveal; nested steps and Sources rows are agent-log LogRow items with their own curved branch, and a GuideBridge drops 6px from each 16px glyph to the nested trunk at ms-2.
5. Site marks reuse the social-button glyph set: the path is drawn in the brand colour, black brands take text-primary so they invert with the theme, and anything else gets a globe. Each mark is a react-aria Focusable trigger for the kit Tooltip, rendered as a link when the source has an href.
6. The Sources list collapses with a grid-template-rows 1fr to 0fr transition and is inert while closed.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `startDelay = 320ms`
  The first row should not land on the same frame as the user turn that started the search.
- `sourceBeat = 450ms`
  Long enough to read the step before its sources branch off, short enough that the two still read as one find.
- `stepInterval = 850ms (demo 800ms)`
  Default hold for a step with no dwell; dwell overrides it per step.
- `maxMarks = 6`
  Six overlapping 20px marks fit beside "Sources" at 360px; the rest become a +N count.
- `mark overlap = 20px bordered tiles, -6px overlap`
  Each tile carries its own border and fill, so the stack reads as separate sites on any surface in either theme.

## API

```ts
<WebSearch key={turnId} steps={[{ label: "Ran 3 searches", icon: RiSearchLine, heading: true }, { label: "Searched Reddit for", query: "design tokens", brand: "reddit", meta: "5 results", dwell: 1400, sources }]} onComplete={() => reply()} />
```

- `steps: readonly WebSearchStep[]`
  Steps with label, optional query, icon or brand, heading, meta, dwell and sources ({ title, domain, brand?, href? }).
- `run: boolean` — default `true`
  Pauses and resumes the internal timer.
- `startDelay: number` — default `320`
  Milliseconds before the first row lands.
- `stepInterval: number` — default `850`
  Hold on a step that has no dwell, in milliseconds.
- `sourceBeat: number` — default `450`
  Milliseconds between a step and its Sources row.
- `revealed: number`
  Rows landed, when driven from real events; disables the timer.
- `maxMarks: number` — default `6`
  Marks drawn before the rest collapse into a count.
- `working: string | false` — default `"Working"`
  Tail indicator label while running; false hides it.
- `onComplete: () => void`
  Fires once when the last row lands.
- `aria-label: string` — default `"Web search"`
  Accessible name of the log.
- `className: string`
  Classes on the root.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
// Reveal order: every step is one row and a step with sources is two, the
// step then its Sources row. Pacing is per row: the Sources row lands a beat
// after its step, and the trail then holds for that step's dwell (or the
// interval) before the next step, so slow searches look slow.
const units = useMemo(() => {
  const out: { step: number; sources: boolean }[] = [];
  steps.forEach((step, i) => {
    out.push({ step: i, sources: false });
    if (searchStepUnits(step) === 2) out.push({ step: i, sources: true });
  });
  return out;
}, [steps]);

const delayFor = useCallback(
  (index: number) => {
    if (index === 0) return startDelay;
    if (units[index]?.sources) return sourceBeat;
    const prev = units[index - 1];
    const step = prev ? steps[prev.step] : undefined;
    return step?.dwell ?? stepInterval;
  },
  [units, steps, startDelay, stepInterval, sourceBeat],
);

// Headings open a level; plain steps after one nest under it, and plain
// steps before any heading sit at the top level.
const tree = useMemo(() => {
  const top: SearchNode[] = [];
  let parent: SearchNode | null = null;
  let offset = 0;
  steps.forEach((step, index) => {
    const node: SearchNode = { index, step, start: offset, children: [] };
    offset += searchStepUnits(step);
    if (step.heading) {
      top.push(node);
      parent = node;
    } else if (parent) {
      parent.children.push(node);
    } else {
      top.push(node);
    }
  });
  return top;
}, [steps]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The ticker clears its pending timeout whenever the revealed count, run flag or pacing changes and on unmount; the Working row clears its timer on unmount; tooltips are owned by react-aria and close with their trigger.

**Reduced motion.** Rows appear without the blur, lift or height animation, the guide is drawn at once, the shimmer and star twinkle stop, marks no longer lift on hover, and the Sources list opens and closes instantly. Rows still arrive on the same schedule.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Key the component on the turn: a new question needs a new key, or the reveal count carries over.
- Pass steps as a stable array; the pacing callback depends on it and a new array every render restarts the pending timer.
- A step with sources counts as two units when you drive revealed yourself.
- The marks sit inside the log's clipping edge, so their tooltips portal out through the kit Tooltip rather than rendering inline.

## Notes

- brand accepts any of the 24 social-button providers; pass href on a source to make its mark and list entry links.
- Pass working={false} to hide the tail indicator or a string to relabel it.

## Definition of done

After the user turn, "Ran 3 searches" lands, then the first search shimmers and its Sources row branches off with five marks; the Reddit search shows six marks and +2; the X search lands last, the Working row leaves and the answer appears. Clicking Sources sets aria-expanded to true and lists titles with domains; clicking again folds it; sending the message again replays the trail from the top.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Week View Grid

A week calendar in the template style: a grey frame holding seven white rounded day columns, a 52px hour gutter and a sticky header with the weekday and date, today in an accent pill. Timed events are absolutely positioned from their start and duration with the kit event chip; events that overlap share the column in equal slices. All-day events span their days in a row under the header. A red now-line and time pill mark the fixed `now` you pass in. The body scrolls inside its own box, opening at `scrollToHour`, and on narrow screens it scrolls sideways with the gutter pinned. `renderEvent` lets each chip be wrapped, for example in an EventDetailPopover.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Seven-day time grid: hour gutter, day columns, events placed by start and duration, overlaps side by side, a fixed now-line.

- Category: display
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: @internationalized/date@^3.12.4

## How it works

1. The seven days come from `startOfWeek(week, locale, firstDayOfWeek)`, so en-US starts on Sunday unless you override it. One CSS grid template, `52px repeat(7, minmax(0, 1fr))`, is shared by the header, the all-day row and the body, so the columns line up.
2. `layoutDayEvents` clips each timed event to the day with a UTC day difference (minutes from midnight, negative before the day) and the visible hours, then sorts by start, longer first. It walks the list once: an event that starts after the cluster has ended closes it; inside a cluster the event takes the first column that is free, or opens a new one. Every member of a cluster then gets `columns` equal to the cluster width.
3. Each block is `top = (start − startHour·60) × hourHeight / 60`, height its duration in px (at least 22px; blocks under 40px switch to the one-line compact chip so a 15 minute stand-up still shows its title and time), left `col / cols` of the column plus 2px and width `1 / cols` minus 4px. Overlap is judged on the drawn height, so padded short events never cover the next one.
4. The header row is `position: sticky; top: 0` inside the scroll box and the gutter cells are `sticky; left: 0`, both on the frame colour, so the hours and day names stay put in either scroll direction. Hour lines are absolutely placed 1px borders behind the events.
5. When `now` falls in the week and inside the hour range, its column gets a 2px red line with a dot at the start edge and the gutter shows the time in a red pill at the same offset. A single effect sets `scrollTop` to `scrollToHour` on mount.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `hourHeight = 48px`
  Half an hour is 24px, enough for a one-line title; a full working day (8–18) fits a 480px box.
- `minimum block height = 22px`
  The compact chip height, so 15 minute events stay legible and clickable.
- `compact threshold = 40px`
  Under this the full chip cannot fit a title line and the time line, so short blocks render the one-line compact chip.
- `gutter = 52px`
  Holds "10:42" in the now pill and "11 PM" in 12-hour mode without wrapping.
- `min width = 640px`
  Below this the seven columns get too narrow for titles, so the body scrolls sideways instead.
- `scrollToHour = 8`
  Opens on the working day instead of midnight.

## API

```ts
function WeekViewGrid(props: { events: CalendarEvent[]; week: CalendarDate; firstDayOfWeek?: DayOfWeek; startHour?: number; endHour?: number; hourHeight?: number; scrollToHour?: number; now?: CalendarDateTime; height?: number; selectedEventId?: string | null; onEventClick?: (event: CalendarEvent) => void; renderEvent?: (event: CalendarEvent, chip: ReactElement) => ReactNode; locale?: string; hourCycle?: 12 | 24; "aria-label"?: string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
function layoutDayEvents(events: CalendarEvent[], day: CalendarDate, options: { startHour: number; endHour: number; hourHeight: number; minHeight: number }): WeekEventLayout[]
```

- `events: CalendarEvent[]`
  Timed and all-day events; any outside the week are ignored.
- `week: CalendarDate`
  Any day of the week to show.
- `firstDayOfWeek: 'sun' | 'mon' | … | 'sat'` — default `locale`
  First column.
- `startHour / endHour: number` — default `0 / 24`
  Visible hour range.
- `hourHeight: number` — default `48`
  Pixels per hour.
- `scrollToHour: number` — default `8`
  Hour scrolled to the top on mount.
- `now: CalendarDateTime`
  Draws the now-line and highlights today. Never read from the clock inside.
- `height: number` — default `520`
  Height of the scrolling box in px.
- `selectedEventId: string | null`
  Rings the matching chip.
- `onEventClick: (event) => void`
  Called when a chip is pressed.
- `renderEvent: (event, chip) => ReactNode`
  Wrap each chip, for example in an EventDetailPopover.
- `hourCycle: 12 | 24` — default `24`
  Hour labels and chip times.
- `locale: string` — default `"en-US"`
  Weekday names, first day of week, times.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * Places one day's timed events. Events are clipped to the day and the hour
 * range, sorted by start (longer first), and walked once: an event that starts
 * after everything so far has ended opens a new cluster; inside a cluster each
 * event takes the first column whose last event has ended, or a new column.
 * Every event in a cluster then shares its width by the cluster's column count.
 */
export function layoutDayEvents(events: CalendarEvent[], day: CalendarDate, options: LayoutOptions): WeekEventLayout[] {
  const { startHour, endHour, hourHeight, minHeight } = options;
  const perMinute = hourHeight / 60;
  const from = startHour * 60;
  const to = endHour * 60;
  const total = (to - from) * perMinute;

  const items = events
    .filter((event) => !event.allDay)
    .map((event) => ({
      event,
      start: Math.max(minutesInto(day, event.start), from),
      end: Math.min(minutesInto(day, event.end), to),
    }))
    .filter((item) => item.end > item.start)
    .sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start || b.end - a.end);

  const placed: WeekEventLayout[] = [];
  let cluster: WeekEventLayout[] = [];
  let columnEnds: number[] = [];
  let clusterEnd = -Infinity;
  const closeCluster = () => {
    for (const item of cluster) item.columns = columnEnds.length;
    cluster = [];
    columnEnds = [];
  };

  for (const item of items) {
    const height = Math.max((item.end - item.start) * perMinute, minHeight);
    const top = Math.min((item.start - from) * perMinute, total - height);
    // Overlap is judged on the drawn block, so short events padded to
    // minHeight never cover the next one.
    const drawnEnd = item.start + height / perMinute;
    if (item.start >= clusterEnd) closeCluster();
    let column = columnEnds.findIndex((end) => end <= item.start);
    if (column === -1) {
      column = columnEnds.length;
      columnEnds.push(drawnEnd);
    } else {
      columnEnds[column] = drawnEnd;
    }
    const layout = { event: item.event, top, height, column, columns: 1 };
    cluster.push(layout);
    placed.push(layout);
    clusterEnd = Math.max(clusterEnd, drawnEnd);
  }
  closeCluster();
  return placed;
}

export interface WeekViewGridProps {
  events: CalendarEvent[];
  /** Any day in the week to show. */
  week: CalendarDate;
  /** First column; defaults to the locale's first day of the week (Sunday in en-US). */
  firstDayOfWeek?: DayOfWeek;
  /** First and last hour rows. Default 0 and 24. */
  startHour?: number;
  endHour?: number;
  /** Pixel height of one hour. Default 48. */
  hourHeight?: number;
  /** Hour scrolled to the top on mount. Default 8. */
  scrollToHour?: number;
  /** Draws the now-line and highlights today. Pass a fixed value; the grid never reads the clock. */
  now?: CalendarDateTime;
  /** Height of the scrolling area in px. Default 520. */
  height?: number;
  selectedEventId?: string | null;
  onEventClick?: (event: CalendarEvent) => void;
  /** Wrap each chip, for example in an EventDetailPopover. */
  renderEvent?: (event: CalendarEvent, chip: ReactElement) => ReactNode;
  locale?: string;
  hourCycle?: HourCycle;
  "aria-label"?: string;
  className?: string;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>;
}

const GRID_COLUMNS = "grid grid-cols-[52px_repeat(7,minmax(0,1fr))] gap-x-1.5";
/** Below this height (px) a block has no room for the time line, so it uses the compact chip. */
const SHORT_BLOCK = 40;
/**
 * Slices of an overlap cluster are narrow: tighter padding and a one-line
 * caption-size title with an ellipsis, so "Planning" reads "Plann…" instead of
 * wrapping mid-word to "Plannin / g". The popover shows the full title.
 */
const NARROW_CHIP =
  "ps-1 pe-0.5 [&>span:first-child]:block [&>span:first-child]:truncate [&>span:first-child]:text-caption-1-medium";

export function WeekViewGrid({
  events,
  week,
  firstDayOfWeek,
  startHour = 0,
  endHour = 24,
  hourHeight = 48,
  scrollToHour = 8,
  now,
  height = 520,
  selectedEventId = null,
  onEventClick,
  renderEvent,
  locale = "en-US",
  hourCycle = 24,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel,
  className,
  ref,
}: WeekViewGridProps) {
  const scrollRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const first = startOfWeek(week, locale, firstDayOfWeek);
  const days = Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, i) => first.add({ days: i }));
  const last = days[6] ?? first;
  const hours = Array.from({ length: Math.max(endHour - startHour, 1) }, (_, i) => startHour + i);
  const bodyHeight = hours.length * hourHeight;
  const todayIndex = now ? daysBetween(now, first) : -1;
  const nowMinutes = now ? now.hour * 60 + now.minute : 0;
  const showNow = todayIndex >= 0 && todayIndex < 7 && nowMinutes >= startHour * 60 && nowMinutes <= endHour * 60;
  const nowTop = ((nowMinutes - startHour * 60) * hourHeight) / 60;

  // Scroll the working hours into view once the grid mounts (and when the
  // target hour changes). Plain scrollTop: no listener, nothing to clean up.
  useEffect(() => {
    const el = scrollRef.current;
    // 12px of slack keeps the target hour's label clear of the sticky header.
    if (el) el.scrollTop = Math.max(0, (scrollToHour - startHour) * hourHeight - 12);
  }, [scrollToHour, startHour, hourHeight]);

  const allDay = events
    .filter((event) => event.allDay)
    .map((event) => ({
      event,
      from: Math.max(daysBetween(event.start, first), 0),
      to: Math.min(daysBetween(lastDayOf(event), first), 6),
    }))
    .filter((span) => span.to >= span.from && span.from <= 6 && span.to >= 0)
    .sort((a, b) => a.from - b.from || b.to - a.to);

  const chipFor = (event: CalendarEvent, variant: "compact" | "full", chipClassName?: string) => {
    const chip = (
      <CalendarEventChip
        variant={variant}
        className={chipClassName}
        title={event.title}
        color={event.color}
        start={event.start}
        end={event.end}
        allDay={event.allDay}
        selected={selectedEventId === event.id}
        locale={locale}
        hourCycle={hourCycle}
        onClick={onEventClick ? () => onEventClick(event) : undefined}
      />
    );
    return renderEvent ? renderEvent(event, chip) : chip;
  };

  const label =
    ariaLabel ??
    `Week of ${formatDay(first, locale, { month: "long", day: "numeric" })} – ${formatDay(last, locale, {
      month: "long",
      day: "numeric",
      year: "numeric",
    })}`;

  return (
    <section
      ref={ref}
      aria-label={label}
      className={cx("flex w-full flex-col overflow-hidden rounded-[20px] bg-background-secondary-default", className)}
    >
      <div ref={scrollRef} className="relative overflow-auto overscroll-contain" style={{ height }}>
        <div className="min-w-[640px] px-2 pb-2">
          <div className="sticky top-0 z-20 bg-background-secondary-default pt-2 pb-1.5">
            <div className={GRID_COLUMNS}>
              <div aria-hidden className="sticky left-0 z-10 bg-background-secondary-default" />
              {days.map((day, i) => {
                const isToday = i === todayIndex;
                return (
                  <div key={day.toString()} aria-hidden className="flex flex-col items-center gap-0.5 py-0.5">
                    <span className="text-caption-1-medium text-text-secondary">
                      {formatDay(day, locale, { weekday: "short" })}
                    </span>
                    <span
                      className={cx(
                        "flex size-7 items-center justify-center rounded-full text-body-2-medium tabular-nums",
                        isToday ? "bg-accent-500 text-text-white" : "text-text-primary",
                      )}
                    >
                      {day.day}
                    </span>
                  </div>
                );
              })}
            </div>
            {allDay.length > 0 ? (
              <div className={cx(GRID_COLUMNS, "mt-1.5")}>
                <div className="sticky left-0 z-10 flex items-start justify-end bg-background-secondary-default pe-2 pt-1 text-caption-2-medium text-text-tertiary">
                  All day
                </div>
                <ul className="col-span-7 grid grid-flow-row-dense grid-cols-7 gap-x-1.5 gap-y-1">
                  {allDay.map(({ event, from, to }) => (
                    <li key={event.id} className="min-w-0" style={{ gridColumn: `${from + 1} / ${to + 2}` }}>
                      {chipFor(event, "compact")}
                    </li>
                  ))}
                </ul>
              </div>
            ) : null}
          </div>

          <div className={GRID_COLUMNS} style={{ height: bodyHeight }}>
            <div aria-hidden className="sticky left-0 z-10 bg-background-secondary-default">
              {hours.slice(1).map((hour, i) => (
                <span
                  key={hour}
                  className="absolute end-2 -translate-y-1/2 text-caption-2-regular tabular-nums text-text-tertiary"
                  style={{ top: (i + 1) * hourHeight }}
                >
                  {formatEventTime({ hour, minute: 0 }, { locale, hourCycle })}
                </span>
              ))}
              {showNow && now ? (
                <span
                  className="absolute end-1 z-[1] -translate-y-1/2 rounded-[5px] bg-text-error-primary px-1 text-caption-2-semibold tabular-nums text-text-white"
                  style={{ top: nowTop }}
                >
                  {formatEventTime(now, { locale, hourCycle })}
                </span>
              ) : null}
            </div>

            {days.map((day, i) => (
              <div
                key={day.toString()}
                role="group"
                aria-label={`${formatDay(day, locale, { weekday: "long", month: "long", day: "numeric" })}${i === todayIndex ? ", today" : ""}`}
                className="relative rounded-xl bg-background-primary-default"
              >
                <div aria-hidden className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0">
                  {hours.slice(1).map((hour, h) => (
                    <div
                      key={hour}
                      className="absolute inset-x-0 border-t border-border-table dark:border-border-button-group"
                      style={{ top: (h + 1) * hourHeight }}
                    />
                  ))}
                </div>
                {layoutDayEvents(events, day, { startHour, endHour, hourHeight, minHeight: 22 }).map((item) => {
                  const style: CSSProperties = {
                    top: item.top,
                    height: item.height,
                    insetInlineStart: `calc(${(item.column / item.columns) * 100}% + 2px)`,
                    width: `calc(${100 / item.columns}% - 4px)`,
                  };
                  return (
                    // Blocks too short for title and time fall back to the one-line chip;
                    // in a narrow slice it drops the time so the title keeps the room.
                    <div key={item.event.id} className="absolute z-[1] flex" style={style}>
                      {item.height < SHORT_BLOCK
                        ? chipFor(item.event, "compact", cx("h-full", item.columns > 1 && "px-1 [&>span+span]:hidden"))
                        : chipFor(item.event, "full", item.columns > 1 ? NARROW_CHIP : undefined)}
                    </div>
                  );
                })}
                {showNow && i === todayIndex ? (
                  <div
                    aria-hidden
                    className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-x-0 z-[2] h-0.5 -translate-y-1/2 bg-text-error-primary"
                    style={{ top: nowTop }}
                  >
                    <span className="absolute -start-1 top-1/2 size-2 -translate-y-1/2 rounded-full bg-text-error-primary" />
                  </div>
                ) : null}
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** One mount effect assigns `scrollTop` and returns nothing; there are no listeners, timers or observers. Formatters are cached in a module-level map.

**Reduced motion.** Nothing moves. The grid opens already scrolled to `scrollToHour` with an instant `scrollTop`, never a smooth scroll; the only transition is the kit chip's 150ms hover brightness and selection ring, which changes no position or size.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Reading the clock for the now-line during render. Server and client disagree by the time they hydrate; take `now` as a prop and update it from a timer in the caller if it should move.
- Measuring overlap on raw times when short events are padded to a minimum height. Two back-to-back 10 minute events would draw on top of each other; compare the drawn end instead.
- Wrapping chips in a popover inside the scroll box. React Aria closes an open popover when an ancestor of its trigger scrolls, which is the right behaviour but means scrolling the grid dismisses it.
- Giving each day its own grid. Columns drift as content changes; share one grid template for header, all-day row and body.

## Notes

- `layoutDayEvents` is exported for custom day or resource views.
- An event that ends exactly at midnight belongs to the day it started for the all-day row, so a one-day all-day event can be stored as midnight to midnight.
- Pass `startHour` / `endHour` to show only working hours; events outside are clipped to the edges.

## Definition of done

The week of August 16 2026 opens scrolled to 08:00 with Sun 16 to Sat 22 in the header and 20 in an accent pill. Planning and Design crit on Monday sit side by side at half width; Retro, Demo day and Wrap-up on Friday split three ways where they overlap. Payday spans Wednesday and Holidays spans Friday and Saturday in the all-day row. A red line and a "10:42" pill mark Thursday. Clicking Stand-up opens its details popover; Delete removes the block, lowers the count and offers Undo. At 360px the body scrolls sideways with the hour gutter pinned.

and where, so I can check them.
